Jim Prussak, CEO of Applause Home Care, said generational differences are changing how seniors view caregiving and could reshape the future of the home care industry. "As a non-medical home care agency owner, I've seen how the generational differences in caregiving can shape the way we support older adults in their homes," Prussak said. According to Prussak, many members of the Greatest Generation grew up valuing independence, privacy and self-reliance, making it difficult for some to accept outside assistance. "Many members of the Greatest Generation grew up valuing independence, privacy and self-reliance, so accepting help can sometimes feel like giving up control," he said. items.t: 68 dead in high-speed train collision, Spain’s 2nd deadly rail crash this year
items.x: URDA, Spain (AP) — A high-speed train slammed into another that had stopped on the tracks in Spain on Wednesday, killing at least 68 people and injuring dozens in the second deadly rail collision this year. The regional government of Castilla La Mancha confirmed the death toll and said another 58 people were receiving medical treatment at hospitals. Rescue workers searched the wreckage through the day for survivors and bodies. Freeways expand, transit systems improve, and technology promises more efficient journeys. Yet travelling across the city can still take a remarkable amount of time. A British aerospace company believes part of the solution might be above the roads rather than on them. Vertical Aerospace has demonstrated an electric aircraft capable of taking off vertically, transitioning into conventional forward flight, and landing without a runway. items.t: Dry October continues as northern Illinois sees near-record warmth
items.x: Dry October: October has been living up to its reputation as a dry fall month across the region. In fact, the Rockford area hasn't seen any measurable rainfall in the past 12 days, and the last time we picked up an inch or more was way back on October 1st. While the extended stretch of mild weather has been enjoyable, it has also allowed dry conditions to take hold. While dry and unseasonably mild conditions remain in place, rain chances will begin to slowly creep back in tonight as our next system glides into the Great Lakes. Near-Record Warmth: When we say "unseasonably mild", we're talking about temperatures that will approach record territory for late October. With sunshine returning and a warm, organized southerly wind in place, afternoon highs will climb into the low, possibly mid 70s. Similar to Sunday, we'll come up just shy of our record high of 77 degrees, set back in 1950. Still, temperatures will run 10 to 15 degree above average. These clouds have been the result of a weak low-pressure system (upper-level disturbance, really) moving through the Midwest. It's pulled in a little more moisture which has led to the increase in cloud cover. items.t: Cause of death revealed for ‘Office Space’ actor Richard Riehle: Reports
items.x: (NEXSTAR) – The cause of death for longtime actor Richard Riehle has been revealed, according to reports. The 78-year-old died earlier this month in Los Angeles, friends told TMZ , which was the first to report the news. The outlet and People , citing his death certificate, reported Tuesday that the "Office Space" actor experienced a stroke and had oropharyngeal cancer. He had been in a rehabilitation center at the time of his death in mid-October, according to People. Oropharyngeal cancer , which can be asymptomatic, impacts the middle portion of your throat, including the base of your tongue and the tonsils. While there are multiple types of oropharyngeal cancers, Johns Hopkins Medicine says the majority are squamous cell carcinomas, which are further divided into HPV-related and HPV-unrelated. The former is caused by HPV, while the latter is commonly caused by tobacco or alcohol. Details about Riehle's condition were not released. items.t: Heavy fire breaks out at Rockford home causing $60,000 in damages
items.x: ROCKFORD, Ill. (WTVO) — A fire at a home in Rockford late Tuesday morning caused approximately $60,000 in damages, officials reported. According to the Rockford Fire Department, firefighters were called to the 3400 block of Elm Street around 11:32 a.m. and found heavy fire coming from the front of the home. Officials said the fire was brought under control through the effort of 19 firefighters in under 15 minutes. No injuries were reported, and the Illinois State Fire Marshal's Office and Nicor Gas personnel were called in to assist with the investigation. The cause of the fire is undetermined, officials said.

items.t: Byron Generating Station will get more capacity from U.S. loan
items.x: BYRON, Ill. (WTVO) — The Byron Generating Station will bring more capacity online thanks to a taxpayer-funded loan from the U.S. Department of Energy that will add 1.1 gigawatts to the Midwestern power grid. On Tuesday, an announcement was made at Constellation's Byron Generating Station in Ogle County, where U.S. Rep. Darin LaHood and Energy Secretary Chris Wright highlighted plans to modernize existing reactors rather than build new plants. The funding commitment, first announced by the U.S. Department of Energy, would support upgrades at the Byron, Braidwood, Clinton, Dresden, LaSalle and Quad Cities nuclear stations in Illinois. NOW PLAYING Illinois produces more nuclear energy than any other state, and LaHood described nuclear power as a key part of the state's energy future. He said the facilities provide thousands of jobs while supplying reliable electricity to homes and businesses. Wright framed the project as part of the Trump administration's effort to increase domestic energy production and expand nuclear generation nationwide. He said the administration has set a goal of adding 5 gigawatts of capacity through reactor restarts and upgrades at existing nuclear facilities.

Following the assault, Dismuke reportedly drove her to his house, although the victim could not identify where it was. Later, she was able to describe the residence to police. items.t: Wynonna Judd will bring ‘The Hard Truths Tour’ to Hard Rock Casino Rockford
items.x: ROCKFORD, Ill. (WTVO) — Country music star Wynonna Judd is bringing her “The Hard Truths Tour” to Hard Rock Live at Hard Rock Casino Rockford on Sunday, March 7, 2027. The concert is scheduled to begin at 7 p.m. at the casino, located at 7801 E. State St. near the Interstate 90 State Street exit. Tickets are available through Hard Rock Casino Rockford. Judd has spent more than four decades in country music, first finding success as one half of the Grammy Award-winning duo The Judds alongside her mother, Naomi Judd. items.t: Electrical fire triggers evacuation at Harlem Middle School
items.x: LOVES PARK, Ill. (WTVO) — Harlem Middle School students were evacuated Tuesday afternoon due to an electrical fire in the girls' locker room, according to fire officials. First responders were called to the school, located at 735 Windsor Road, around 2:15 p.m. According to a letter sent to parents by Principal Jerry Harris, the fire occurred in an electrical panel. Emergency responders cleared the building for students and staff to return at approximately 2:35 p.m., Harris said. "We are pleased to report that all students and staff are safe," he wrote. "We appreciate the quick response of our students and staff, who followed our emergency procedures and evacuated the building safely."

items.t: Police: Rockford man arrested for aggravated DUI with three underage passengers in vehicle
items.x: ROCKFORD, Ill (WTVO) — A Rockford man was arrested and charged with aggravated DUI after Illinois State Police said he was driving with three underage passengers early Monday morning. According to police, troopers were on patrol around 3:43 a.m. on Alpine Road near Linden Road when they observed a vehicle with a suspended registration pull into a gas station. Investigators identified the driver as 25-year-old William Harris, who allegedly had a strong odor of alcohol on his breath. Authorities said a 17-year-old male, a 16-year-old male, and a 15-year-old female were passengers in the vehicle. During the stop, troopers found an unsealed bottle of Don Julio liquor on the floorboard. Using the Law Enforcement Agency Data System (LEADS), authorities determined Harris driver's license had been revoked following a previous DUI violation. Harris was arrested and charged with aggravated DUI with passengers under 16, driving on a revoked license, and endangering the life of a child. He is being held in the Winnebago County Jail. Officials said the 15-year-old and 16-year-old were released to their parents. The 17-year-old was arrested on an outstanding robbery warrant from Texas.

items.t: Recalled butter sold in 10 states receives risk warning: FDA
items.x: NEW JERSEY ( WPIX ) A popular plant-based butter has been recalled due to yeast, mold and E. coli, and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has now assigned it a risk level . The recall, which was initiated by Prosperity Organic Foods, Inc., headquartered in Boise, Idaho, involves 1,304 cases of Miyoko's Creamery European Style Salted Plant Milk Butter. The FDA assigned the recall as a Class II risk level on Friday, meaning a product may cause “temporary or medically reversible adverse health consequences.” The recall was initially announced Sept. 11. The affected butter, which is perishable and stored refrigerated or frozen, comes in six-packs of 8-ounce units, which can be identified with the following information: UPC 857554005773 Lot number and best-by on SBS carton: 07871, Nov. 5, 2026 Lot number and best-by date on the corrugated case for shipment: 1007871, Nov. 5, 2026 The affected products were also sold in Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Iowa, Illinois, Indiana, Maryland, New Jersey, New Hampshire and Wisconsin.

Johnson explained that his decision came from recognizing when the demands of his work began to outweigh the enjoyment he found in it. Sunny Hostin wants Jay-Z to use his NFL partnership to push for more Black leadership, even as she supports his confirmed Super Bowl performance . The View cohost questioned whether his 2019 Roc Nation deal with the league has brought enough change beyond the halftime stage. During Wednesday’s episode of ABC’s “The View,” Hostin called Jay-Z a “perfectly valid choice” to headline next year’s halftime show but said he could do more to improve racial equity in the NFL, Entertainment Weekly reported on Oct. 28. Jay-Z’s Roc Nation partnered with the NFL in 2019 to advise on entertainment and support the league’s Inspire Change initiative. The deal arrived amid continuing criticism of the NFL’s treatment of Colin Kaepernick, whose national anthem protests drew attention to racial injustice and police brutality. Hostin credited Jay-Z with making some progress but raised concerns about the number of Black coaches and team owners. She cited a league with “70 percent Black players,” “only three Black head coaches” and no Black majority owners.

Barkley discussed the decision with Front Office Sports in an interview published Wednesday, October 28, 2026. The running back said the league informs players before each season about the companies and industries they may endorse or invest in, and that prediction markets are now off-limits under its gambling policy. “I was in it before, but no bueno,” Barkley told the publication. The situation highlights the growing tension between professional sports leagues and prediction-market platforms, which allow users to trade contracts tied to the outcomes of real-world events, including sporting competitions. According to ESPN, a spokesperson for the NFL Players Association said earlier this year that the league considers prediction markets gambling entities. Angela Rye is warning that online disinformation campaigns are fueling divisions within Black communities by exploiting racial tensions and personal trauma. items.t: Is the ‘Thriller’ dance derived from the cake walk? The theory examined
items.x: We unpack the theory that keeps haunting the “Thriller” dance and its origins year after year during spooky season. Each spooky season, much like the living dead themselves, the infamous dance from Michael Jackson’s “Thriller” music video rises once again. Our timelines become awash in all manner of people recreating the choreography in increasingly elaborate ways, giving us their best renditions of the King of Pop, his unsuspecting date, or any one of the undead dancers who famously surrounded him. What also doesn’t seem to die, year after year, is the comparison between the iconic routine and another famous dance, the cakewalk. And we have to admit, the two do bear some resemblance. The infamous “Thriller” dance, which debuted in the groundbreaking short film on MTV on Dec. 2, 1983, was choreographed by Jackson alongside Michael Peters, incorporating elements ranging from jazz and street dance to the stiff, unnatural movements of movie monsters. Meanwhile, the cakewalk, a dance dating back to slavery, has its own complex history, as its influence can still be felt today. items.x: Christopher Alexander is Mamdani's pick to lead the commission tasked with addressing racial inequities across city government and studying potential reparations. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has named his pick to chair the New York City Commission on Racial Equity . TheGrio has scooped that Christopher Alexander, executive director of the NAACP New York State Conference, has been selected to lead the commission next year. The commission, established by ballot measure in 2022, is tasked with studying reparations and recommending policies to address racial inequities across city agencies. “From the release of the City’s first racial equity plan to delivering critical investments like childcare and housing to historically underserved communities, racial equity has been and remains a cornerstone of our administration,” Mayor Mamdani said in a statement. “New Yorkers not only deserve a City government where they can see themselves reflected in the people who serve them, but also one where their struggles are both recognized and met with action." When the legend Aretha Franklin died in 2018 at the age of 76, she left behind four sons, an extraordinary musical legacy, an estate worth millions, and no formal plan for what to do with it. As many may recall, two handwritten wills surfaced months later in her Michigan home, including one found tucked inside a notebook beneath her living room couch cushions, per the Washington Post . If it could happen to the Queen of Soul, it could certainly happen to you. Or at least that’s what Jehan Crump-Gibson , a Michigan-based estate-planning attorney, hopes more families realize. items.t: New SC law requires restaurants to disclose imported shrimp starting Wednesday
items.x: SOUTH CAROLINA (WCBD) A new South Carolina law aimed at increasing transparency for seafood consumers takes effect Wednesday, requiring restaurants and other food service establishments to disclose when they serve imported shrimp. The law , signed by Gov. Henry McMaster on June 30, requires establishments that serve imported shrimp to post notices on menus and at their main entrances informing customers that they may serve imported shrimp. The measure took effect 120 days after the governor signed it. Under the law, businesses that serve both domestic and imported shrimp must display a notice stating: "Some items served at this establishment may contain foreign imported shrimp. Ask for more information." Establishments that serve only imported shrimp must post a notice stating that some menu items contain foreign imported shrimp. The requirements apply to food service establishments including restaurants, cafeterias, food stands and food trucks. The law defines domestic shrimp as shrimp caught and landed in U.S. waters and foreign imported shrimp as shrimp imported into the United States. items.t: AAA advises drivers about daylight saving time

And even though we're on the easier end of the time transition (from daylight saving time to standard time), the switch still takes its toll. Nexstar's WAVY went to AAA Tidewater Virginia to see what commuters can expect. "Well, the biggest thing for drivers will be the change in daylight when we leave work or school," said Holly Dalby with AAA. "At the end of the day, gone will be the bright sunshine, and we will find ourselves either driving into the glare from the setting sun or driving home in the dark. So it's a time to be particularly careful on the roads." Days will get way shorter in November: How much daylight will we lose? While lawmakers have tried to get rid of the time switch altogether, it doesn't appear to be going anywhere anytime soon, so your circadian rhythm will have to dance to a different beat for a while. "It just messing with our sleep schedule can really add to our fatigue very quickly. And when we're fatigued, we can make mistakes," Dalby said. items.t: RFK Jr. eases access to unproven peptides despite opposition from FDA scientists
items.x: WASHINGTON (AP) — The Trump administration on Wednesday acted to ease access to unproven peptide drugs favored by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr . Food and Drug Administration scientific staffers had little input on the decision and opposed the changes, according to six people familiar with its development. The draft policy posted online by Kennedy’s Department of Health and Human Services covers a handful of injectable peptides promoted within the wellness industry for uses such as building muscle, healing injuries and boosting energy. The government will take comments for two weeks before finalizing the measure. The document, primarily written by officials at HHS, faced overwhelming pushback among FDA drug staffers who warned it could undermine the agency’s long-standing mission of keeping unsafe health products off the U.S. market, according to the people familiar with its development. items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. Gasoline and energy costs have risen in six of nine months this year, as the Iran war sparked oil price shocks via the Islamic Republic's restrictions on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Persistent inflation , which has remained above the Fed's 2 percent target for five-and-a-half years, spurred central bank officials to hike interest rates by a quarter point in mid-September. items.t: DoorDash to buy Instacart in $17 billion grocery delivery deal
items.x: DoorDash is gobbling up Instacart in a $17 billion acquisition that will supercharge its grocery delivery business. DoorDash said the Instacart brand name and app will remain, and Instacart shoppers can continue fulfilling orders for Instacart. Grocers can also choose to work with Instacart or DoorDash. Instacart customers will now have access to 50,000 additional stores covered by DoorDash, the company said. Instacart, founded in 2012, specializes in grocery and convenience store delivery in the U.S. and Canada. Its 600,000 “shoppers” — who are independent contractors — completed 338 million orders last year, according to company filings. Instacart has a market value of $14 billion. DoorDash, founded in San Francisco in 2013, began as a restaurant delivery business but has expanded to pet food and electronics. Operating in 40 countries, it completed more than 3 billion orders last year using a network of 9 million independent delivery workers. It has a market value of $73 billion. DoorDash began delivering groceries in 2020 amid a surge in pandemic-era demand. Grocers were initially cautious. items.x: SAVANNAH, Ga. (WSAV) The Savannah Police Department is investigating a stabbing that injured one person Thursday morning near the intersection of Abercorn Street and Largo Drive. items.t: South Georgia State Fair returns with family fun, community support

items.t: Savannah River Site declared a site area emergency
items.x: AIKEN, S.C. (WSAV) — The Savannah River Site (SRS) declared a site area emergency at 5:39 p.m. Wednesday, said a spokesperson. Savannah River National Laboratory reported a fire; it has been extinguished. There hasn't been any report of contamination outside the affected facility. The site entrance has been closed off; rail, river, and air traffic in the vicinity of SRS is also being restricted. For more information, you can go to the SRS website or their Facebook .

items.t: Long County softball earns walk-off win to start state softball tournament
items.x: SAVANNAH, Ga. (WSAV) — The Long County softball team advanced in the winners' bracket of the Class AAAA state softball tournament after an extra-innings win, 4-3, over Pickens in the opening round Wednesday. Long County, the top team in the bracket according to the PSR system used by the GHSA, won after a Pickens made a throwing error after Long County laid down a bunt in the bottom of the ninth. The game-defining inning started with a base hit for the Blue Tide, then the runner stole second to get into scoring position. Long County plays North Hall at 2:45 p.m. tomorrow on Field 5.

items.t: Groves boys’ basketball ready to take next step
items.x: GARDEN CITY, Ga. (WSAV) — After coming within a game of making the playoffs during the 2025-26 season, the Groves boys' basketball team hopes to earn a spot in the state playoffs this year. Last season, the Rebels went 9-20 and needed to beat Calvary Day in the Region 3-AAA tournament to make the playoffs. Groves lost three of their top five scorers from a year ago to graduation, but they return junior Kyje Davis and senior Kavalee Godboltee. Head coach Kevin Evans also talked about some young and new faces who might step up, including a freshman. This year, Groves transitions up to Class AAAAA, but Coach Evans says they are used to the competition. "One thing about us, we're not scared to play anybody," Evans said. "We're going to play hard every possession. We are going to be scrappy. We are going to get after it, but we don't really worry about the classification because just like we have to go them, they have to come to us, too." Groves opens the season on the road at 3:30 p.m. against Richmond Hill.

items.t: Harris advises Democrats against attempting to impeach Trump
items.x: ( The Hill ) Former Vice President Kamala Harris on Tuesday urged Democrats against making a third attempt to impeach President Trump if they win back the House after next week's midterm elections. "I think that going in the direction of impeachment is not a good idea, just to be honest with you," Harris told MeidasTouch's Aaron Parnas in an interview. "Just because we have limited resources and I think the energy and the resources need to put into accountability, need to be put into investigations." "And that's where the time should be spent," she added. "Remember, I was in the Senate for the last go-around, and the votes aren't there. "So, that's how I feel. But also, I think after the election, we all have to just also agree that our attitude has to be to get stuff done." Harris said Democrats should be "uncompromising" and "not sit around, you know, being genteel about the relationships," but maintain accountability when it comes to cuts to healthcare and oversight on the Iran war. items.t: Hayden Panettiere death ruled accidental by police in South Carolina
items.x: GREENVILLE, S.C. ( WSPA ) – Police in South Carolina have officially closed the investigation into the death of Hayden Panettiere, according to a Wednesday news release. Greenville Police Department officials said that Panettiere's death has been ruled accidental, based on findings in the investigation and the medical examiner's determination. On August 16, Panettiere was found unresponsive in an apartment at the Judson Mill Lofts on Easley Bridge Road. Police said that Brian Hickerson, Panettiere's on-and-off boyfriend, along with his brother, Zach Hickerson, were at the residence. EMS attempted life-saving measures before pronouncing Panettiere dead at 2:31 p.m. According to the Greenville County Coroner's Office, Panettiere had died from an accidental overdose of fentanyl, 4-ANPP, Alprazolam, Methocarbamol and Quetiapine. Panettiere had spoken openly about challenges in her personal life, including emotional scars from her childhood fame, postpartum depression after giving birth to her daughter, and struggles with alcohol addiction. items.t: Ribbon cutting held for archeological lab at Historic Mitchelville
items.x: HILTON HEAD ISLAND, S.C. (WSAV) — Local and state leaders gathered for a historic day on Hilton Head Island to celebrate a new chapter of Historic Mitchelville Freedom Park. Hundreds of people came out for the ribbon cutting for the park's new Archeology Research Facility. An important part of American history, Mitchelville is better known as the first town self-governed by formerly enslaved people. The new facility will allow historians and scientists to better analyze any artifacts found on site. "The research is part and parcel of the foundation of this organization and what we're trying to do," explained Ahmad Ward, Executive Director, Historic Mitchelville Freedom Park. "So it is fitting that a lab and an educational facility are the first things that are here on the site. And we're going to do a lot of great things here. And until the big building is built, it's going to basically serve as our de facto visitor center." "I said in my remarks that we stand on the shoulders of many people, and we certainly are," said Board Chair of the Freedom Park, Shirley "Peaches" Peterson. items.t: Law to allow UTVs on certain public roads takes effect in November
items.x: COLUMBIA, S.C. (WSPA) – A law passed earlier this year to allow utility terrain vehicles on some public roads will soon take effect in South Carolina. Starting Nov. 18, UTVs will be allowed on secondary highways and streets where the posted speed limit is 55 mph or less. While operating on public roads, UTV drivers must follow the same laws as drivers of regular vehicles, including registering their vehicles with the Department of Motor Vehicles, having working lights and carrying liability insurance. “We need to kind of treat it just like we do our car. We need to be mindful of what our speed is when we’re operating it, making sure we’re wearing our seat belt, making sure that we’re eliminating distractions behind the wheel, and of course, we don’t want people to get behind the wheel impaired,” said South Carolina Highway Patrol’s Troop 1 community relations officer Master Trooper William Bennett. The bill was introduced by Democratic state Sen. Russell Ott about six years ago. items.t: Chatham County Tax Commissioner explains Nov. 3 school tax referendum
items.x: CHATHAM COUNTY, Ga. (WSAV) — The Chatham County Tax Commissioner, Sonya L. Jackson, released information on the Chatham County School Board Ad Valorem Tax Referendum appearing on the ballot on Wednesday. This referendum will be on the Nov. 3, 2026 Ballot. The Chatham County School Board Ad Valorem Tax Referendum amendment adjusts the base-year assessed values used for the homestead exemption and applies them to Savannah-Chatham Public School System property tax. “Our responsibility is to help residents understand property tax terminology and the measures that may affect them,” said Tax Commissioner Sonya L. Jackson. If approved, the adjusted base-year assessed value will be under the exemption for qualifying homesteads and won't increase property taxes for tax year 2025. This would limit the value used under the school tax homestead exemption to the 2025 level, as opposed to having an adjusted base-year value that can continue to increase. If rejected, the applicable exemption would continue to be governed by the existing law. items.t: New SNAP rules for South Carolina start Nov. 1
items.x: SOUTH CAROLINA (WJBF) Beginning November 1st, South Carolina will update the definition of SNAP-eligible foods. Candy, energy drinks, soft drinks, and other sweetened beverages will no longer be allowed for purchase with SNAP benefits. Diet and zero sugar soft drinks are allowed. This is all part of the Healthy Food SC project, a two-year initiative designed to help households receiving SNAP benefits make healthier food choices. The goal of this project is to promote healthier food choices among participants by encouraging the purchase of more nutritious foods while reducing the purchase of items with limited nutritional value. All South Carolina SNAP approved retailers will participate in this project, and SNAP households in South Carolina will not have the option to opt out of these food restrictions. For more information on the new program, please visit the Healthy Food SC website .

items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war , creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle . items.t: Savannah Fire responding to residential fire in 100 block of Painted Lady Loop

items.t: Two SC polls show different pictures of Graham-Andrews Senate race
items.x: CHARLESTON, S.C. (WCBD) With voters already casting ballots ahead of Election Day, two South Carolina-based polls released this week show a closely contested U.S. Senate race but offer different snapshots of where the contest stands. Polls released by The Citadel and the South Carolina Policy Council both found Republican Sen. Darline Graham ahead of Democrat Annie Andrews, but by significantly different margins. Both surveys also found Republican Alan Wilson maintaining a larger lead in the governor's race. The Citadel's survey of 1,009 registered voters found Graham leading Andrews by 4 percentage points statewide. Pollsters described the race as close, noting that independent voters largely favored Andrews and that some voters remained undecided. According to The Citadel, 14% of voters who expect to participate in the election said they still do not know which Senate candidate they will support. The poll also found 2% of respondents said they may write in U.S. Rep. Ralph Norman, a factor researchers said could bring the race within the survey's margin of error. items.t: Sugary foods to lose SNAP-eligibility on Nov. 1: SCDSS
items.x: SOUTH CAROLINA (WCBD) The South Carolina Department of Social Services on Wednesday announced that its new program, Healthy Food SC, will take effect on Sunday. Healthy Food SC project is a two-year initiative beginning on Nov. 1, updating the definition of Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP)-eligible foods by removing candy, energy drinks, soft drinks, and other sweetened beverages. Diet and zero-sugar soft drinks will still be SNAP-eligible after the new definitions take effect. This change will affect all South Carolina SNAP-approved retailers. SNAP households will not have the option to opt out of the restrictions. More information about the program can be found on dss.sc.gov .

items.t: Georgia surpasses 2 million in early voting at the polls
items.x: ATLANTA (WSAV) — Georgia voters are continuing to break records in early voting turnout with 2,000,452 in-person ballots cast as of Tuesday evening, a spokesperson for the Secretary of State reported. In addition, 97,382 absentee ballots had been accepted by 4:30 p.m. on Tuesday, Oct. 27. “Georgia voters deserve the highest praise,” said Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger. “They are shattering in-person turnout records because they trust our election process. Our county election directors are delivering for their communities and bringing a free, fair, and fast election to every corner of our state." Compared to 2022, Georgia has seen a 22% increase in early in-person voting over the course of 15 days. Overall, statewide turnout is reported to be 28% seven days before Election Day. Georgians can participate in early voting through Friday, Oct. 30. You can find early voting locations and hours closest to you on Georgia's My Voter Page .

items.t: The Odd Savannah: Uncovering the city’s haunted history
items.x: SAVANNAH, Ga. (WSAV) — Savannah is known for its beautiful weeping willow trees and historic charm. But beneath the beauty lies something odd! The Odd Savannah is a show that focuses on everything odd in the spookiest city in the South. In its premiere episode, host Elliot Rosenblatt sits down with paranormal investigators Micah Watkins and Courtney Knight as they untangle nearly 209 years of history and haunts of the Savannah Theatre. From stories about its connection to renowned 19th-century actor Edwin Booth, brother of Abraham Lincoln’s assassin, John Wilkes Booth, to urban legends about the ethereal tenants that roam the theatre, this interview will unravel stories that go beyond the history books.

items.t: Chatham County Sheriff’s Office receives highway safety grant
items.x: CHATHAM COUNTY, Ga. (WSAV) The Chatham County Sheriff's Office (CCSO) announced Wednesday that it has been given a Highway Visibility Enforcement (HVE) grant. The grant will assist in providing new equipment and funding around Chatham County in an effort to reduce crashes and prevent injuries. This $67,760 grant is funded by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration and is awarded to recipients by the Governor's Office of Highway Safety (GOHS). items.t: 68 dead in high-speed train collision, Spain’s 2nd deadly rail crash this year
items.x: URDA, Spain (AP) — A high-speed train slammed into another that had stopped on the tracks in Spain on Wednesday, killing at least 68 people and injuring dozens in the second deadly rail collision this year. The regional government of Castilla La Mancha confirmed the death toll and said another 58 people were receiving medical treatment at hospitals. Rescue workers searched the wreckage through the day for survivors and bodies. The collision came just nine months after another deadly crash involving high-speed trains operated by the same two companies in southern Spain in January. “Today all of Spain is grieving,” Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said from the crash site, where he announced that his government would declare three days of national mourning. The MV Odyssey set sail two years ago on a voyage to the seven continents marketed as combining long-term living at sea with global travel. Its operator had offered to “make the Odyssey your permanent home,” with the purchase price of a suite for the lifetime of the vessel starting around $230,000. The ship has been carrying 203 passengers, mostly Americans, along with 156 crew members, according to Cambodian officials. It has a a 650-passenger capacity. Its Florida-based operator, Villa Vie Residences, said monthly fuel expenses per cabin that historically averaged $1,800 have reached an estimated $6,000 to $8,000 in parts of Asia due to the war in Iran. The drugs may result in "fullness and fewer serves" in pubs and bars. “We see some changes in consumption behaviour among (GLP-1) users and will continue to monitor how these behaviours evolve in 2027," a Heineken spokesperson told the publication. The report noted that the company’s research found consumers increasingly choosing smaller servings, lower-alcohol beverages and premium products and that these shifts also align with broader trends focused on health, wellness and moderation. One option Heineken advised customers to pursue is half-pints and low- and no-alcohol options, according to the publication. items.t: Flying taxis could carry passengers by 2030
items.x: (TestMiles) A British aerospace company has demonstrated an electric flying taxi that could eventually offer a new way to escape crowded city roads. The Flying Car Is Moving Beyond Science Fiction Los Angeles has spent decades trying to solve its traffic problems. Freeways expand, transit systems improve, and technology promises more efficient journeys. Yet travelling across the city can still take a remarkable amount of time. A British aerospace company believes part of the solution might be above the roads rather than on them. Vertical Aerospace has demonstrated an electric aircraft capable of taking off vertically, transitioning into conventional forward flight, and landing without a runway. The technology was publicly displayed at the Farnborough International Airshow in Britain, marking an important development in the company's plans to introduce commercial passenger flights. The aircraft is part of a growing category known as electric vertical takeoff and landing, or eVTOL. Unlike a conventional airplane, it does not require a runway for every departure. items.t: ECSO awarded over $300,000 in grants through the GOHS
items.x: EFFINGHAM COUNTY, Ga. (WSAV) – The Effingham County Sheriff’s Office (ECSO) has been awarded two traffic safety grants from the Governor's Office of Highway Safety (GOHS) in Atlanta, the ECSO spokesperson said. The ECSO has been awarded $289,692 for a Highway Enforcement of Aggressive Traffic (H.E.A.T.) grant and over $35,000 for a Traffic Enforcement grant. “I am proud to announce that the Effingham County Sheriff’s Office has been awarded $289,692 through the Governor’s Office of Highway Safety H.E.A.T. Grant," said Sheriff Jimmy McDuffie. "Our goal is not simply to write more citations, but to change dangerous driving behavior and prevent crashes before they happen. items.t: ‘There is a grieving family behind the headlines’: GoFundMe launched for woman fatally shot in Toombs County
items.x: TOOMBS COUNTY, Ga (WSAV) — The family of a woman fatally shot in a residence on McNatt Falls Road recently has launched a fundraiser to cover her funeral expenses. Pamela Cook, 40, was shot and killed on Oct.19 alongside Wallace Truman Edge, 75, by Wallace's former spouse, Grace Edge, 76. Cook's 55-year-old mother also received a non-life-threatening gunshot wound and is recovering from surgery. Edge was arrested shortly after and charged with two counts of murder and three counts of aggravated assault. Per the GoFundMe: "Pamela was more than the tragedy that took her life. She was our sister, our mother's daughter, and someone whose absence will be felt by our family for the rest of our lives. While the circumstance of her passing have received public attention, we ask that people remember there is a grieving family behind the headlines." The fundraiser, set up by Cook's sister, will help cover the family's unexpected expenses that come with laying her to rest. You can find the link to the family's GoFundMe here.

items.t: Recalled butter sold in 10 states receives risk warning: FDA
items.x: NEW JERSEY ( WPIX ) A popular plant-based butter has been recalled due to yeast, mold and E. coli, and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has now assigned it a risk level . The recall, which was initiated by Prosperity Organic Foods, Inc., headquartered in Boise, Idaho, involves 1,304 cases of Miyoko's Creamery European Style Salted Plant Milk Butter. The FDA assigned the recall as a Class II risk level on Friday, meaning a product may cause “temporary or medically reversible adverse health consequences.” The recall was initially announced Sept. 11. The affected butter, which is perishable and stored refrigerated or frozen, comes in six-packs of 8-ounce units, which can be identified with the following information: UPC 857554005773 Lot number and best-by on SBS carton: 07871, Nov. 5, 2026 Lot number and best-by date on the corrugated case for shipment: 1007871, Nov. 5, 2026 The affected products were also sold in Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Iowa, Illinois, Indiana, Maryland, New Jersey, New Hampshire and Wisconsin.

items.t: Drought worsens across central North Carolina as lake levels continue to fall

( WNCN ) The latest U.S. Drought Monitor, released Thursday, shows more than 30 percent of North Carolina experiencing severe drought or worse, including Wake and Johnston counties. Drought has also expanded across the Coastal Plain and northern Piedmont, with some communities seeing conditions deteriorate after recent weeks of improvement elsewhere in the state. The concern extends beyond brown lawns and dry fields. Prolonged rainfall deficits are reducing streamflow and putting pressure on water resources that communities rely on for drinking water and other needs. What happens next? The immediate concern is that continued dry weather will allow lake levels and streamflows to fall further. While Raleigh's current water supply remains above its October planning threshold, prolonged drought can put additional pressure on local water systems if the dry pattern persists. Residents should check with their local water provider for current conservation guidance and any water-use restrictions. items.t: NC early voting numbers top 2 million, a large increase from 2022 midterms
items.x: RALEIGH, N.C. ( WNCN ) Early voting ends Saturday in North Carolina, but so far the turnout has been huge. As of Thursday, more than 2.1 million ballots have been cast in the two weeks of early voting, including absentee ballots. That's a 36 percent increase compared to this point in the 2022 midterms. The early voting numbers so far represent 27.3 percent of registered voters. Early voting numbers nearly doubled in just a week on October 22 more than 1.1 million ballots had been cast. The numbers this week show that the edge Democrats had in early voting is shrinking although they still have a large lead. RELATED: NC early voting surges during first week, but will overall turnout result? A week ago, registered Democrats accounted for 43% of ballots cast early, compared with nearly 22.5% for Republicans and 34.2% for unaffiliated voters. Now, the Democratic early votes are at 39.8 percent while Republicans are at 25.2 percent, with unaffiliated voters at 34.6 percent. Republican and Democratic registration in North Carolina is nearly even at 29.53 percent and 29.65 percent, respectively, with unaffiliated registration at 40.1 percent.

The Senate battleground map has steadily expanded throughout the 2026 midterm election cycle as political handicappers have shifted seats that were thought to be in solidly Republican territory — such as Alaska, Iowa, Kansas and Texas — to the “toss-up" category. items.t: World Stroke Day: raising awareness and saving lives
items.x: RALEIGH, N.C. ( WNCN ) — Today marks World Stroke Day, a critical occasion dedicated to raising awareness about strokes, which rank as the fourth leading cause of death and a significant contributor to disability in the United States. Each year, nearly 800,000 Americans experience a stroke, with the condition affecting individuals regardless of age, race, or gender. This year’s observance emphasizes recognizing warning signs and taking swift action to save lives. Dr. Wayne Feng, the Board President of the American Heart Association of the Triangle and Division Chief of Stroke and Vascular Neurology at Duke University School of Medicine, highlights the urgency of stroke awareness. “Every minute counts,” he explains. “With every delay, we're losing about 2 million neurons.” This stark reality underscores why immediate recognition and treatment are crucial. The American Stroke Association encourages everyone to remember the acronym B.E. F.A.S.T. when identifying the common warning signs of a stroke: B Balance: Sudden loss of balance or coordination; dizziness or trouble walking. items.t: Central NC cold front for Halloween and the eventual return of rain
items.x: It will be a warm end to the work and school week with highs warmer than average, even flirting with 80-degrees! It's also a warmer start to our morning with temperatures Thursday morning mainly in the 50s. Some patchy fog is possible, but once the fog and our lingering clouds start to clear by the afternoon, we will enjoy mainly sunny skies by the afternoon. The sunshine will make our temperatures warmer than average in the mid-70s, but it will still be a pleasant day. A dry cold front will move through the region late Friday night, bringing slightly cooler air for Halloween. Saturday looks dry, with highs in the upper 60s and temperatures falling into the 50s during the evening. Some clouds may build later in the day, but rain is not expected for trick-or-treating, or any other Halloween plans. While our chances for rain have gone down early in the week, it still looks like the better opportunity for rain will arrive by the end of next week as a potentially stronger storm system approaches. items.t: Fort Bragg plans free on-demand ride service for soldiers, military families
items.x: FAYETTEVILLE, N.C. ( WNCN ) — Getting around Fort Bragg without a personal vehicle could soon become easier for soldiers and military families. The City of Fayetteville’s FAST Transit is helping Fort Bragg develop a new, free on-demand transportation service called the Bragg Connector, expected to launch next summer. The service will allow people on the installation to request rides through a mobile app instead of relying on traditional bus routes. Riders could use the service to travel from their homes or barracks to Womack Army Medical Center, dining facilities, childcare centers, and other destinations across the installation. “Potentially a game changer,” said Adam DiGaudio, the City of Fayetteville’s intergovernmental military manager. DiGaudio said the service could be especially helpful for service members who do not have their own vehicles and families who share one car. “A family could use this service to go from their residence to Womack Army Medical Center, or a service member could use this service to get from their barracks to the new campus style dining facility,” DiGaudio said. items.t: Raleigh woman changes lives, one lasagna at a time
items.x: RALEIGH, N.C. ( WNCN ) There's something about a home-cooked meal that feeds the heart as well as the body, and Dorea prepares dozens of homemade meals every week. She doesn’t do it for recognition; in fact, she asked us not to use her last name, but her neighbors know she’s making a difference, and she’s being honored for her efforts. Dorea started "Lasagna Wednesdays" early this year to help others who may need a meal. “I’m not asking anything back. I'm not asking you to explain why you need the meals,” she noted. “Just ask, and I'm going to give it to you.” Sometimes she cooks 100 meals. She buys ingredients on Monday, wakes up at 6 a.m. on Tuesday and cooks until midnight, then portions everything out on Wednesday before people pick up their meals or have them delivered. items.t: NC judges question dismissal of voter ID, income tax cap lawsuit days before North Carolinians vote on new amendments
items.x: RALEIGH, N.C. ( WNCN ) — North Carolina voters are being asked to tighten the state's voter ID requirement and income tax cap next week, even as an eight-year legal battle over the amendments they approved in 2018 remains unresolved. On Wednesday, NC appeals court judges questioned whether the NAACP should get another chance to make its case, while also raising the possibility that Tuesday's election could change the course of the lawsuit. "If the constitutional amendments currently on the ballot were to pass, wouldn't that render this moot?" one judge asked. "Yes. Simply, it would," said Martin Warf, an attorney representing Republican legislative leaders. "I assure you that if those amendments pass…we will move to dismiss this case." Next Tuesday, voters will decide whether to expand the state's constitutional photo ID requirement to all voting, including absentee ballots, and cap the state income tax rate from 7% to 3.5%. Photo ID is already required for absentee voting under state law, but the proposed amendment would enshrine that requirement in the state constitution. items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war , creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle . items.t: Medical imaging company to invest $230 million in Sanford for first US plant
items.x: SANFORD, N.C. ( WNCN ) — A medical imaging company will open its first U.S. facility in Lee County, the governor's office said Tuesday. According to the North Carolina Governor's Office, Italian company Bracco will invest $230 million to open a contrast media manufacturing plant in Sanford. The manufacturing plant will create 200 new jobs such as manufacturing, engineering, and technical roles, in addition to support operations, quality, warehousing, and administrative positions, according to the governor's office. Officials said the new jobs could create an annual payroll impact of more than $20.6 million for the region. "I am pleased to welcome Bracco and its investment to North Carolina," Gov. Josh Stein said in a statement. "Our longstanding strengths in manufacturing, innovation, and workforce development have created a robust ecosystem that gives companies like Bracco the confidence to invest here."

items.t: Woman dead after being hit by pickup truck on Rock Pillar Road in Johnston County: NCSHP
items.x: CLAYTON, N.C. ( WNCN ) — A woman is dead after being hit by a pickup truck in Johnston County Tuesday morning, the North Carolina State Highway Patrol said. According to the NCSHP, 33-year-old Ashley Fuller of Johnston County was walking east on Rock Pillar Road near Clayton with her brother just before 9 a.m. when she was hit by a westbound pickup truck. Fuller was pronounced dead at the scene, according to the NCSHP. Troopers said Fuller and her brother were walking in the direction of the pickup truck at the time of the crash. Fuller's brother managed to avoid the vehicle, according to the NCSHP. According to the NCSHP, Fuller had just left her home and the crash happened near where she lived. The pickup truck was also just leaving a neighborhood before the incident. Troopers said the driver of the pickup truck remained at the scene. The crash remains under investigation. No charges have been filed as of Wednesday morning.

items.t: After weeks, bedbug infestation cleared from Raleigh’s Oberlin library, Wake County officials say
items.x: RALEIGH, N.C. ( WNCN ) — A bedbug infestation that lasted for more than a month in a Raleigh library has been cleared out, according to Wake County officials. Nearly two weeks ago — on Oct. 16 — a bedbug cleanup had already been underway for more than four weeks at the Oberlin Regional Library in the 1900 block of Clark Avenue in the Village District shopping area, according to a manager at the facility, which is part of the Wake County Public Library system. After the cleanup, according to Wake County officials, a follow-up inspection was held three days later, on Oct. 19, that confirmed the library was cleared of bedbugs. Wake County officials also said there were reports of bedbugs at other library locations, but those were unconfirmed. PREVIOUS: Bedbug infestation cleanup underway at Oberlin library in Raleigh, officials say "On Oct. 16, out of an abundance of caution, the county’s pest control company treated the entire Oberlin Regional Library facility," Alice S. Avery, a communications manager for Wake County, told CBS 17 on Wednesday. " A follow-up inspection found no further evidence of bed bugs." A library branch manager said they suspected the sources of the infestation.

items.t: Candy Corn: A sweet debate among Americans this Halloween season
items.x: As Halloween approaches, one treat continues to spark debate among candy lovers: candy corn. According to recent research conducted by the National Confectioners Association, the iconic triangular candy remains a polarizing symbol of the spooky season. The survey reveals that a significant majority of Americans—60%—prefer to eat the entire piece of candy corn at once. However, consumption methods vary widely: 28% of candy corn fans start with the narrow white end, while 12% start with the wide yellow end. This split shows how personal the enjoyment of candy corn can be. No matter how you eat it, candy corn undeniably holds a special place in Halloween festivities. It continues to rank among the season's top treats, alongside beloved favorites like chocolate bars, gummy candies, and hard candies. Carly Schildhaus, the senior director of communications for the National Confectioners Association, commented on candy corn's enduring legacy. "Candy corn has been around for generations and is an iconic part of the Halloween season. items.t: Flying taxis could carry passengers by 2030
items.x: (TestMiles) A British aerospace company has demonstrated an electric flying taxi that could eventually offer a new way to escape crowded city roads. The Flying Car Is Moving Beyond Science Fiction Los Angeles has spent decades trying to solve its traffic problems. Freeways expand, transit systems improve, and technology promises more efficient journeys. Yet travelling across the city can still take a remarkable amount of time. A British aerospace company believes part of the solution might be above the roads rather than on them. Vertical Aerospace has demonstrated an electric aircraft capable of taking off vertically, transitioning into conventional forward flight, and landing without a runway. The technology was publicly displayed at the Farnborough International Airshow in Britain, marking an important development in the company's plans to introduce commercial passenger flights. The aircraft is part of a growing category known as electric vertical takeoff and landing, or eVTOL. Unlike a conventional airplane, it does not require a runway for every departure. items.t: Raleigh Police Department prepares for a safe Halloween celebration
items.x: RALEIGH, N.C. ( WNCN ) —As Halloween approaches, the Raleigh Police Department (RPD) is preparing for a festive yet safe evening for families and community members. For those planning to go trick-or-treating, the department emphasizes the importance of safety. Parents and guardians are encouraged to accompany their children, use reflective gear, and carry flashlights to enhance visibility. Officers also remind community members to stay alert for motorists, as costumes and excitement can distract drivers.

items.t: Cameron Art Museum unveils new exhibition: “With A Southern Accent” showcasing the rich heritage of eastern North Carolina
items.x: Wilmington, N.C. ( WNCN ) —The Cameron Art Museum (CAM) is thrilled to announce its latest exhibition, "With A Southern Accent: Sporting Art and Fine Art of Eastern North Carolina," on view through August 15, 2027. Curated by renowned expert Robbie Smith, this exhibition tells a unique story rooted in Eastern North Carolina's culture and traditions. "We are excited to explore the interconnectedness of people, wildlife, and landscapes through the lens of sporting art, folk art, and fine art," said CAM representatives. The exhibition aims to bridge the rich local traditions with broader narratives in American art history, highlighting how these elements have shaped the region. At the heart of the exhibition lies CAM's esteemed collection of American duck decoys, originally assembled by Wilmington businessman, philanthropist, and outdoorsman Bruce Cameron Jr. More than 300 hand-carved decoys make up the collection, with about 40 on display in this exhibition. These intricate pieces are more than functional objects; they reflect incredible craftsmanship and artistic expression, inviting visitors to see them as sculptural art. items.t: Wake County-led workplace board wins over $ 5 million to help laid-off workers
items.x: RALEIGH, N.C. ( WNCN ) — The Capital Area Workforce Development Board has been awarded a $5.8 million federal grant to help dislocated job seekers in Wake County and surrounding areas return to work. The 36-month initiative targets 628 laid-off workers across 15 North Carolina counties. Funded through the U.S. Department of Labor's Rapid Reskill Dislocated Worker grant program, the initiative focuses on employers rebuilding the regional industrial base. The effort concentrates on high-growth sectors, including advanced manufacturing and construction companies that adopt new technology. Wake County Commissioner Shinica Thomas emphasized the importance of supporting dislocated workers through local training and industry partnerships. “Losing a job can create real uncertainty for individuals and families and we want to help people get back on their feet as quickly as possible,” Thomas said. “This grant will connect workers with the training, skills and employer partnerships they need to move into good-paying jobs and build a strong future.” The initiative features four primary components designed to streamline employment recovery. items.t: Tarboro man charged after guns discovered in truck outside elementary school, Police say

Jimmy Laughter, of Tarboro, faces multiple firearm charges linked to incidents at both the elementary school and nearby Tarboro High School. School personnel reported a suspicious vehicle inside the perimeter of Stocks Elementary School shortly before 3 p.m. Tuesday. Police took Laughter into custody at the scene without incident, uncovering three weapons in his truck and linking him to another school property incident from the previous day. Staff members at Stocks Elementary School, located at 400 W. Hope Lodge Street in Tarboro, alerted authorities around 2:50 p.m. Tuesday after noticing a white vehicle parked near a tree line inside the school's fenced perimeter. Responding officers located the truck approximately 250 feet from the school building and arrested Laughter while he was seated inside. Officers seized three firearms from the vehicle during the arrest. items.t: Halloween cooler, still dry in central NC
items.x: The dry streak is now at 11 days in a row for central North Carolina and will last through the weekend, but it will get a little cooler Saturday and Sunday. Clouds Wednesday help keep temperatures a little cooler, but with more sunshine expected Thursday and Friday, temperatures will warm up again. There's still no sign of significant rain through the end of the month, and while that’s good for Halloween plans, it's bad for our ongoing drought . The pattern looks to flip with the calendar, as rain becomes a little more likely the first week of November. In terms of temperatures, our warmest afternoon will be Friday as highs climb into the upper 70s. A weak cold front will move through the area early Saturday morning and while it won't have any rain, it will bring slightly cooler temperatures this weekend. Rain chances return Monday due to Pacific tropical moisture, but the chances are very good. Another round of showers is possible late in the week, mainly Thursday and Friday. Don’t forget to turn your clocks back an hour when you go to bed on Saturday, with Daylight Saving Time coming to an end at 2 a.m. Sunday morning. That’ll make the sunset on Sunday at 5:19 in the evening. FOR

items.x: DURHAM, N.C. ( WNCN ) — In August, an 18-year-old Durham woman was accused of trying to kill her baby by taking abortion pills while she was 31 weeks pregnant. Now, those charges have been dropped. In August, the Durham Police Department alleged that Syeisha Johnson took mifepristone and misoprostol in an attempt to terminate her pregnancy early. Investigators said that caused her child to be born at 31 weeks with a weight under five and a half pounds. Johnson was charged with assault inflicting serious bodily injury on an unborn child and assault with a deadly weapon with intent to kill, along with negligent child abuse inflicting serious bodily injury. The child's father, 19-year-old Elijah Speight, was also facing charges of negligent child abuse. Court filings from Tuesday show all charges against Johnson and Speight have been dropped. According to the dismissal paperwork, the district attorney's office said they were not going to prosecute the case. A specific reason was not given in the dismissal document as to why they are not following through with prosecuting the case. items.t: Former UNC basketball coach Davis lands new job
items.x: CHAPEL HILL, N.C. ( WNCN ) — Hubert Davis, the former North Carolina men's basketball player and most recently the program's head coach, has a new job just in time for the new season. Davis has been hired by TNT Sports to be a studio and game analyst for the 2026-27 season, according to CBS Sports. He will make his debut in the studio on Nov. 5 during the network's Big East and Big 12 tripleheader, the outlet said. It marks a return to the media side of the business for Davis, who spent seven years as a college basketball analyst with ESPN following the end of his NBA playing career in 2004. The Carolina alum was let go in late March after the Tar Heels lost in overtime in the first round of the NCAA Tournament to VCU. Davis, who became an assistant coach at UNC in 2012, had been handpicked by legendary coach Roy Williams to be his successor after the Hall of Famer retired in 2021. In his five seasons at the helm of his alma mater, Davis racked up a record of 125-54. During his first season, the Tar Heels made a somewhat surprising run through the NCAA Tournament, ending up in the championship final. items.t: Lengthy dry stretch continues in central NC, with another rain-free week ahead
items.x: RALEIGH, N.C. ( WNCN ) — Our very dry pattern isn't letting up, now sitting at 10 straight days without rain at Raleigh-Durham International Airport. The double-digit number comes after a trend of every weekend this month seeing measurable rain through October 17 — the last time rain fell in the area. Only a few days remain until Halloween on Saturday, but we're expecting more zeros through the end of the month. That would bring our rain-free stretch to 14 days — a full two weeks. The last time we had a dry streak that long was back from May 26 to June 17 of this year, when we tallied 23 days with no rain. But even that isn't close to the all-time consecutive dry day record, which stands at 38 straight days from late September through early November in 2000. Right in the middle was the driest month the Triangle has ever seen, with just a trace of rain all of that October. So this month won't be anywhere near the driest October on record, even with the dry second half. Thankfully, the pattern of no rain looks to be about to change with the turning of the calendar. The first few days of November show signs of a more unsettled pattern, with the entire month looking wetter than average

Volunteers and students recently spent days restoring some of the wooden windows that are nearly 75 years old. The building once served as home to one of North Carolina’s first African American Catholic congregations. Originally completed in the early 1950s, NCCU later purchased the structure and moved it to campus. NCCU Archivist Andre Vann was there in 2010 when the school rededicated the building, formerly known as Holy Cross Church, as Centennial Chapel. Photo courtesy of Jordan Abdur-Raoof. Photo courtesy of Jordan Abdur-Raoof. "It helps to anchor this neighborhood and anchor this community," Vann said. "And we called it, after we moved it here, Centennial Chapel." This month, volunteers, students and craftspeople worked to restore decades-old wood windows of the Centennial Chapel that's located along Fayetteville Street. Organizers hosted a training event to give participants experience in fixing up a piece of local history. items.x: RALEIGH, N.C. (WNCN) — The North Carolina Republican Party is calling for an investigation into allegations of illegal electioneering by supporters of Democratic Congressman Don Davis at an early voting site in Edgecombe County. The formal complaint, filed Monday with the NC State Board of Elections, alleges Davis supporters wore campaign shirts and engaged in political activity inside the designated buffer zone at the polling site. “North Carolina’s election laws apply to everyone, including Congressman Don Davis and his campaign,” said Jason Simmons, Chairman of the North Carolina Republican Party. “Voters deserve to cast their ballots without improper political activity at the polls. There cannot be one set of rules for Democrats and another for everyone else.” State law prohibits electioneering within designated buffer zones at voting sites. items.t: Fayetteville moves forward with elevator for downtown parking garage after years of delays
items.x: FAYETTEVILLE, N.C. ( WNCN ) — After years of complaints about accessibility at a downtown Fayetteville parking garage, city leaders are moving forward with plans to install an elevator. The five-story public parking garage next to Segra Stadium opened in 2018 alongside the Fayetteville Woodpeckers stadium. But the developer never completed several parts of the project, including the elevator. The unfinished development was originally supposed to include a hotel and high-rise apartments above the garage, with retail space on the ground floor. Today, some storefronts remain unfinished, with no flooring and weeds growing inside. The lack of an elevator has frustrated people who use the garage, including Woodpeckers fans who park there for games. Fayetteville City Council voted to move forward with installing an elevator, and the city is now accepting bids for the work. Mayor Mitch Colvin said the developer struggled to get the larger development off the ground, leaving the city without a completed project. “The city did not necessarily put money into that. items.t: North Carolina joins 19 other states and FTC in suing Dollar General over pricing practices
items.x: RALEIGH, N.C. ( WNCN ) — North Carolina is joining 19 other states and the Federal Trade Commission , in a lawsuit accusing Dollar General of deceptive pricing practices. The Attorney General announced the move today and says the company has a history of charging customers more than what is advertised on the shelves. "For me personally, my experience hasn't been that, but I feel like a Dollar General is pretty fair,” one shopper who wanted to remain anonymous told CBS 17 on Tuesday, outside of the Dollar General location in Cary. She and other shoppers we spoke with told us they’re surprised the retail giant is accused of bad pricing practices. "As far as I know, the savings are what they say, the discounts are what they're supposed to be, and the prices usually." Dollar General's price tags are under scrutiny by the Federal Trade Commission and 20 states, including North Carolina, which has more than one thousand store locations. "They are illegally overcharging families, and they have been, we believe, for years,” said North Carolina Attorney General Jeff Jackson on Tuesday. items.t: Legacy ‘Lake Myra Christmas Light Show’ prepares for its final season in Wendell after almost 30 years
items.x: WENDELL, N.C. ( WNCN ) — One of Wake County’s beloved Christmas light displays is preparing for its final season. The owner of the Lake Myra Christmas Light Show said this year will be the last after nearly three decades of holiday magic in Wendell. “It’s hard for me to say no because I’ve been doing it for so many years,” said Don Williams. Williams was emotional as he told CBS 17 News this was his last year setting up. "I do it for the kids, families and the people from all over the world that come out to see this,” Williams said. Williams said he started in 1997 with some lights right outside his home. Now it has expanded to a large site in downtown Wendell. This light show was one of the first and largest computerized Christmas light shows in North Carolina. He believes he made an everlasting impact. “It’s hard to describe the experience that I’ve had while I’ve been here. It’s all been positive and the town has been behind me 100%,” Williams said. It is free for anyone who wants to enjoy the scenery. They do however, take donations to help keep the event going. items.t: NC’s State Health Plan taps retiree funds amid cash crisis, reaches deal with Atrium Health
items.x: RALEIGH, N.C. ( WNCN ) — North Carolina's State Health Plan could run out of money by the end of the year, prompting its Board of Trustees to vote Tuesday to dip into retiree health funds to keep the plan afloat for its 750,000 members. The decision comes as the plan struggles to keep up with rising healthcare costs, with more members needing expensive medical care. "We have more folks that are sicker, utilizing more things and fewer people that are healthier utilizing less things," said State Health Plan Executive Administrator Tom Friedman The plan is counting on its new multitier provider network to help control costs. On Tuesday, it reached a deal bringing Atrium Health into that network, ending a legal battle between the two. Atrium rolled out its own affordability program after being designated as a non-preferred provider, sparking Treasurer Brad Briner to file the lawsuit . After the judge sided with Atrium, the hospital was moved out-of-network altogether . Under the new contract, Atrium will be an access provider, meaning members can expect to pay the same as they do now. "It resolves our litigation, eliminates the affordability program. items.t: ‘I’ll always be cheering for the Wolfpack’: Ex-NC State football head coach Dave Doeren talks publicly for the first time since firing
items.x: RALEIGH, N.C. ( WNCN ) — For the first time since being fired from the head coaching job at North Carolina State University, the winningest coach in the school's football program history spoke publicly. Dave Doeren was relieved of his duties over the weekend following a 31-28 loss to Stanford. Earlier this week, Athletic Director Boo Corrigan thanked Doeren for his tenure with the program, saying he represented the university with pride. On Tuesday afternoon, Doeren addressed the media at a press conference at NC State. He thanked several people at the university, including Corrigan, as well as his wife, Sara. He also said it was different to not have a packed schedule during the fall months. "I've coached 32 years and I've never been unemployed," Doeren said. "Waking up in October and not having to think about a game is different." The former Wolfpack head coach emphasized his love for the school, even though he was ultimately unable to reach his goal. "I wanted to win a championship so bad," said Doeren. "This isn't how I wanted to go out but that's not how it works. This is a great job. It's also a very hard job." items.t: EXCLUSIVE: Faith Evans Loses As Judge Awards Biggie's Mother's Trust $12.5M
items.x: Faith Evans lost a $12.5 million court fight over money owed to Biggie's late mother's trust, with a Delaware judge ruling that the trust was entitled to the payouts plus interest. The October 27 decision set the amount at $12,518,336. The money came from distributions tied to Voletta Wallace's interest in Notorious B.I.G., LLC, the company Evans manages that holds rights to the late rapper's intellectual property. Judge Kathaleen St. J. McCormick of the Delaware Court of Chancery rejected an effort to limit the trust's payout to $48,612 while a separate family dispute plays out in Pennsylvania. The key issue was when the trust gained the right to receive money. It was formally admitted as an LLC member months after Wallace's death, but that delay did not erase its claim to earlier payouts. Judge McCormick wrote: "The short answers to the remaining questions are that the Trust did not become a member until December 12, 2025, when it executed the instrument required under the LLC Agreement, but the Trust is entitled to distributions made prior to that time in the amount of $12,518,336." A Florida judge ordered Kemp to remain at least 500 feet from 14-year-old Sire, according to court documents reviewed by TMZ . The order forbids direct or indirect contact, including messages or posts aimed at the teenager through social media. items.t: Why Digital Culture Has Become Essential to Modern Hip-Hop
items.x: Hip-hop has always reflected the way people communicate, create music, and express their experiences. Its early development relied on local communities, live performances, radio broadcasts, and physical recordings. Today, digital technology plays a central role in nearly every part of the culture. Artists share new tracks through online platforms, fans discuss music across social networks, and independent creators reach audiences without relying entirely on traditional industry structures. This shift extends beyond music. Digital entertainment now connects hip-hop with gaming, fashion, video production, and interactive services. Audiences who follow rap culture often explore other online activities, including streaming communities, virtual events, and gaming platforms such as spinsahara . These connections reflect broader changes in how people use technology during their free time. For hip-hop, digital culture now influences both artistic production and everyday interaction between musicians and listeners. With a thoughtfully planned Los Angeles Party Rental setup and an engaging Karaoke DJ , an ordinary gathering can become the kind of night guests keep talking about long after the final song. The key is creating an environment that feels comfortable enough for people to relax but exciting enough to encourage participation. From arranging furniture around the performance area to setting up lighting that gives singers their moment in the spotlight, small decisions can completely change the energy of the event. The performance area should be visible from most parts of the venue without blocking walkways or creating congestion. items.t: The One Creative Format AI Can't Replace Yet With Shane Ginsberg of Street Poller Media
items.x: Nearly every advertising category is currently having some version of the same anxious conversation about generative AI: how much of this work can be automated, how quickly, and what happens to the people currently doing it. Most creative formats have already received at least a partial answer, and for the humans involved it has rarely been reassuring. Product photography, voiceover, script writing, and increasingly the on-camera talent itself have all proven susceptible to synthetic replacement at a fraction of the cost. Street Poller Media founder Shane Ginsberg believes the unpredictability and authenticity of street interviews will be the last frontier for generative AI to crack. His argument starts with a direct comparison. A user-generated content creator filming a product review from their kitchen is, in Ginsberg's assessment, a scene AI can already fake convincingly. The lighting is controlled, the background is static and generic, the performance is scripted, and even the person delivering the pitch can now be synthesized well enough that most viewers would not detect the substitution. items.t: What to Change When Your First Song Demo Doesn't Sound Right
items.x: You play the first version of your song. One line rushes past, the chorus sounds angrier than you meant, or the guitar makes the words hard to hear. Where do you start? Pick the first passage that bothers you and replay it. Before rewriting anything, work out whether the problem is the words, the way they're sung, or what's playing underneath them. When the words feel rushed Try singing the line over the existing tune. Where do you have to squeeze words in or cut a word short? Mark that spot. Suppose the line is “Today I'm going to take the long way home.” Try “I'll take the long way home.” You've kept the decision to take a longer route and removed the lead-in. Sing both versions over the same phrase. Does the shorter one leave room to finish “home” comfortably? Don't shorten every line just to make them match. A fast delivery may be exactly what you want. Change the line when the pace makes it hard to understand or sing as intended. If you're stuck, describe the moment in plain speech: a runner taking the long route home, in no hurry to get back.
