The hometown show remains set for November 24 at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Fans outside Philly will also get stops in Boston and Chicago, with Ticketmaster listing December shows in both cities. Boston's date is December 5 at MGM Music Hall at Fenway. The show starts at 8 p.m., with doors opening an hour earlier. The event is open to all ages. Chicago follows on December 18 at Aragon Ballroom, also with a 7 p.m. door time and an 8 p.m. performance. That stop is an all-ages show with general admission standing room. For Chicago, artist and Citi cardmember presales began October 27 at noon Central time and run through October 29 at 10 p.m. Central. A Live Nation presale starts October 29 at 10 a.m. Central. Those sale times apply to the Chicago date. The expansion follows another arena show earlier this year. Meek played Total Mor

items.t: Neil Young Sues Donald Trump Committee For $10 Million Over Rally Song
items.x: Neil Young sued a Trump political committee for $10 million after he said "Rockin' in the Free World" played at another rally without his permission. The singer-songwriter filed his copyright lawsuit against Trump 47 Committee Inc. on Monday, October 26, in Virginia federal court, according to Courthouse News Service . His complaint pointed to the song playing before President Donald Trump took the stage at an October 12 midterm campaign event in Youngstown, Ohio. The committee faced the claim, while Trump was not named as an individual defendant, Rolling Stone reported . Young also said the dispute carried a cost beyond the use of a recording: he claimed the association hurt his reputation by suggesting he backed Trump, according to TheWrap . His lawyers argued that the message of the song, with its focus on people left behind, conflicted with the politics of the president using it. "In short, the song is the opposite of everything that Donald J. Trump stands for," the filing stated, as quoted by TheWrap. Young had already taken the Trump campaign to court in 2020 over "Rockin' in the Free World" and "Devil's Sidewalk." That case ended in December 2020 after a settlement that incl

items.t: Boosie Badazz Set To Perform With Full Orchestra In Little Rock
items.x: Boosie Badazz is taking "The Black Tie Experience" to Little Rock, Arkansas, with a January 2, 2027, date booked at Robinson Center. The Saturday night show will pair his Southern Hip-Hop catalog with The Signature Orchestra, giving fans a chance to hear his music backed by a live ensemble. The production draws on a recording career that spans more than two decades. "The Black Tie Experience was created to give audiences a different way to experience Boosie live," a Stage View Presents spokesperson said in an announcement published by SWARK Today . Robinson Center's performance hall seats 2,222. The venue dates to 1939 and underwent a $70 million renovation, according to its website. For the Little Rock concert, doors are scheduled to open at 7 p.m., an hour before the 8 p.m. show. The ticket seller limits purchases to nine tickets per person and per credit card. Ticketmaster lists October 23, 2026, as the start of the general sale. The spokesperson said the production's size makes touring difficult and limits the number of cities it can reach. Bringing it to Little Rock, the organizer said, would give fans across Arkansas and nearby areas access to the show in a theater setting. T

items.t: Nolan Wells March Brings Oxford Students Out For Answers
items.x: Nolan Wells name was back on signs at the University of Mississippi on October 25 as students and Oxford residents marched for answers about his death. University of Mississippi freshmen Christopher Burnett and Avah Trevino organized the event, The Daily Mississippian reported. They walked from Fulton Chapel past the Walk of Champions, the Circle and James Meredith's statue before returning. "We just want, simply, for the family's questions to be answered in further investigation," Burnett said. The demand had also reached Rider University, where its NAACP college chapter held an October 22 walk, according to The Rider News . President E'miija Eccles brought campus Black organizations into the event and contacted Public Safety three weeks ahead. Participants made at least three laps around Centennial Lake. Founding chapter president Naa'san S.J. Carr, a 2024 graduate, returned to speak. "We gather because remembrance matters, but so does the pursuit of truth and repair," Carr said. The marches followed the September 22 Jackson County grand jury decision to bring no criminal charges . Jurors found insufficient evidence to accuse anyone of a crime in the death of the 18-year-old, who

items.t: Loe Shimmy Adds Brent Faiyaz To Halloween "Zombieland" Concert
items.x: Loe Shimmy is bringing Brent Faiyaz into his Halloween plans, adding the singer to the lineup for his "Zombieland" concert in South Florida. Faiyaz joins BigXthaPlug, Sexyy Red and Rob49 for the October 31 show at Miramar Regional Park Amphitheater in Miramar, Florida. The concert starts at 8 P.M. Saturday, giving Shimmy a close-to-home stage to bring his rap and R&B collaborators together. The costumes could pay off, too. A $5,000 cash prize is at stake in the night's costume contest. The night also includes a haunted house, and Shimmy's team says the Halloween attractions will include a zombie invasion. A bigger plan is behind the party. The venue describes "Zombieland" as the start of Shimmy's push to build an annual Halloween event. It cites Tyler, The Creator's Camp Flog Gnaw and Travis Scott's Astroworld as inspirations for that goal. The concert's name also runs through Shimmy's catalog. He released Zombieland 2 in March 2024 and expanded it with Zombieland 2.6 that June. The Halloween show turns that recurring theme into a night of music and haunted attractions. Faiyaz has already been part of Shimmy's music for years. The pair released "For Me (Remix)" in November 2024, wi

items.t: French Montana & D-Block Europe's Copenhagen Concert Is Canceled Too
items.x: French Montana and D-Block Europe canceled their November 4 show in Copenhagen. The Danish stop joins the other dates fans will miss on their European run. The rappers were booked to play Store VEGA on Wednesday, November 4. VEGA's event page now carries a cancellation notice. The venue says ticket buyers will receive more information from the ticket provider. It gives no reason for the cancellation. The notice does not lay out a refund process for buyers. The page lists a price of 495 Danish kroner, including fees. Ticketmaster also marks the Copenhagen event as canceled under its listing for the "Worldwide Wave Tour." The bill paired the British duo with French, the Moroccan-American rapper. They had already made music together. French appeared on "If I Was Rich Enough" from D-Block Europe's PTSD 2 . They also teamed up on "Fully Loaded," a collaboration VEGA highlighted when promoting the concert. The planned night paired the duo's melodic UK rap with French's American catalog, bringing their studio connection to a shared live bill. Copenhagen joins two other canceled joint dates AllHipHop previously reported : October 30 at AFAS Live in Amsterdam and November 6 at Raiffeisen Ha

items.t: Yella Beezy Trial: MO3's Girlfriend Testifies
items.x: Yella Beezy faced testimony from MO3's girlfriend Tuesday (October 27) as his lawyers challenged the cash trail behind the state's murder-for-hire case. The Dallas rapper, legally named Markies Conway, pleaded not guilty to capital murder. He denied paying Kewon White to kill MO3 and faced life in prison if convicted. MO3's legal name was Melvin Noble. Jocylynn Jackson told jurors she suspected her address had reached others after MO3 was killed shortly after leaving her apartment, according to FOX 4 . She said Devin Brown, her children's father and a co-defendant, had asked their son whether MO3 was there. Brown denied involvement in a message shown in court. Phone records presented to jurors showed Brown repeatedly calling the boy that morning. Jackson said she had been subpoenaed and did not want to testify. Defense lawyer Toby Shook argued the bills Yella Beezy withdrew differed from cash recovered from convicted gunman White. He also accused investigators of overlooking Brown's personal dispute with MO3. The testimony followed Monday's jury selection in Dallas , where Judge Chika Anyiam questioned 75 potential jurors about whether news coverage would affect their judgment. The

items.t: Drake's "Janice STFU" Accuser Withdraws Copyright Lawsuit
items.x: Drake saw the copyright lawsuit over "Janice STFU" withdrawn less than two weeks after a songwriter accused him of copying its chorus. Rolling Stone reported that Aviel Calev Hirschfield voluntarily dismissed the lawsuit barely 10 days after filing it. The publication cited a recent court filing. The Portland producer, known professionally as GoodbyeCalev, had sued Drake on October 16 in California federal court. The complaint also named OVO Sound LLC, UMG Recordings Inc. and Universal Music Publishing Inc. Drake's team had denied the claims and called the lawsuit "manufactured and baseless." His representatives maintained that he wrote the song himself. GoodbyeCalev's complaint described a chorus he said he developed with Drake in mind over music from production duo FnZ. He alleged that he completed his demo around January 25, 2026, sent it to producers who worked with Drake and heard nothing back. "Janice STFU's chorus is literally identical to the Copyrighted Work in lyrics, melody, and cadence," the complaint alleged. The dispute involved more than what listeners heard. items.t: EXCLUSIVE: Lil Durk Offers Up Music Income To Get Out Of Jail, Lul Pab's Mom Doesn't Object
items.x: Lil Durk put his future music income on the line in a new bond push, offering earnings he could lose if he fled. His lawyers filed the proposal asking Judge Michael W. Fitzgerald to reconsider keeping the Chicago rapper behind bars after his recent acquittal. The filing offered future royalties, publishing income, money tied to his name and image, touring earnings and cash and property from supporters. "In support of his release, we offer a bond package so robust that should Mr. Banks violate his release conditions, both he and his family would be left destitute indefinitely," his lawyers wrote. Drew Findling, Marissa Goldberg, Brian Steel and Christy O'Connor submitted the brief, which said that while prosecutors opposed release, the slain man's family did not. In an attached September 28 letter, Andrea Robinson, mother of Saviay'a "Lul Pab" Robinson, left that decision to the judge considering the rapper's request. "On behalf of the family of Saviay'a Robinson, we do not object to Durk Banks being granted a bond if it is deemed appropriate by the Honorable Court," she wrote. The federal case grew out of an August 19, 2022 shooting near Los Angeles' Beverly Center that killed Pab.

items.t: Romeo Miller Joins Hulu's "The Mob"
items.x: Romeo Miller joined Hulu's "The Mob," putting the rapper in a villa with 11 other celebrities with up to $250,000 in cash prizes at stake. The reality competition premiered Monday, October 26. Parker Posey hosts and also serves as an executive producer. According to Hulu , the group picks a don who controls who gets paid, stays or leaves. The others can overthrow that leader. Each episode brings jobs drawn from mob movies, with the cast competing in an Italian villa. Some of Miller's castmates have played their own parts in crime families on screen. Aida Turturro played Tony Soprano's sister Janice on "The Sopranos." Debi Mazar's credits include "Goodfellas," "Entourage," and "Younger." Their acting careers put them alongside reality stars from dating shows and Bravo. Joe Gorga, of "The Real Housewives of New Jersey," is Melissa Gorga's husband and Teresa Giudice's brother. Harry Jowsey has appeared on "Too Hot to Handle," "Dancing With the Stars," and "Let's Marry Harry." Maria Georgas entered "The Bachelor" during Season 28, when Joey Graziadei was the lead, before joining this cast. items.t: Megan Thee Stallion Explains How Silence Over Her Contract Led To Regret & Legal War
items.x: Megan Thee Stallion said she once feared questioning her record deal. She spoke at Overcoming Impossible Live at 1 Hotel Brooklyn Bridge in New York City. Entrepreneur and Robert Irvine organized the event for business owners. The program paired small-group work with afternoon talks from Megan, Gary Vaynerchuk and Irvine. "I was a little bit nervous about asking questions," she told Entrepreneur . What followed were years of fights over her music. As AllHipHop previously reported, Megan signed with Carl Crawford's 1501 Certified Entertainment in 2018 and sued the label in 2020. In October 2023, the two sides settled and parted ways. They kept the terms private. During that dispute, Megan accused 1501 of blocking releases and keeping her under contract after she had fulfilled its terms. She also sought outside oversight of the label's finances to ensure it could pay a potential judgment. Crawford disputed that request and accused her of using it to harass the label. "I started realizing I'm not making as much money as I should be making because I kind of just gave my life away to somebody else,” Megan Thee Stallion said. items.t: Hit-Boy Turns Roblox Players Into Remix Rivals In "Beat Battle"
items.x: Hit-Boy is bringing his music to Roblox's Beat Battle, letting fans build beats with his vocals and go head-to-head with other players. The month-long season lets players pull apart 10 tracks from his album HITStory 2: Success is a Dirty Word . The game's first artist collaboration offers drums, bass, synths and vocals for remixing. The competition puts players on the clock. Battles use changing vocal clips that run 25 seconds. Players present their mixes, vote and earn Season Tickets, which unlock Hit-Boy beat packs, clothes and DJ decks. Some packs can be earned through play, while players can also buy music and merchandise in the game, the report said. Those tools have a limit: Roblox won't let players export raw audio or separate vocal stems. The official Beat Battle page lists the Hit-Boy season as live. Overtune, the game's developer, describes a setup where players can remix loops or make their own music with a piano roll. Friends can battle onstage and vote on performances. Players can also unlock stages and effects, grow their music collections and share tracks with friends. The game puts making music, performing it and judging other players' work in the same space. items.t: NE-YO Takes World Series Stage For Game 4 National Anthem
items.x: NE-YO will sing the national anthem before World Series Game 4 on Tuesday, October 27, bringing the R&B star to Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Florida. Hailey Riggs will provide American Sign Language interpretation during the performance, according to WFLA . Major League Baseball confirmed his appearance , with FOX's coverage set to begin at 7 p.m. ET. The booking comes in a year that marks two decades since his debut album, In My Own Words . The 2006 release topped the Billboard 200. Since then, the three-time Grammy winner has built a career both at the microphone and behind other artists' songs. His catalog includes "So Sick," "Sexy Love," "Closer," and "Miss Independent." Beyond his own records, he has written Beyoncé's "Irreplaceable" and Rihanna's "Unfaithful," "Russian Roulette," and "Take a Bow." He also earned his first diamond-certified song through "Give Me Everything," his collaboration with Pitbull and Afrojack. This summer, he took his music toward country with Highway 79 . Released July 10, the 11-song album was recorded in Nashville and included "Thinking What I'm Thinking," "Up Out & Gone" and "Ms. Tundra." Apple Music's album notes describe a project that bro

items.t: Krayzie Bone's Youth Foundation To Benefit From Ohio Hip Hop Awards Reunion
items.x: Krayzie Bone s push to help young people find work in music will get support from a Cleveland reunion this weekend. The Ohio Hip Hop Awards will mark its 20th anniversary with a dinner that will raise money for his Spread the Love Foundation and DJ Johnny O's Nerve DJ Institute. The event is set for Sunday, November 1, at Music Box Supper Club, 1148 Main Avenue in Cleveland. Doors and the red carpet open at 4 p.m., and the main program starts at 6 P.M. Organizers say a portion of the proceeds will go to each nonprofit. Spread the Love focuses on youth career training and arts education. The Nerve DJ Institute helps aspiring DJs and other young music professionals build skills through training and mentorship. For Krayzie, that work has already reached young people in detention. As AllHipHop previously reported , his foundation brought its Interest 2 Income program to the Cuyahoga County Juvenile Detention Center, teaching participants about music careers and creative work. The foundation's program goes beyond trying to make students the next star onstage. Its youth track serves ages 13 to 17 and introduces the business and creative jobs that keep music moving. items.t: GloRilla Renews Steelers Anthem Pledge
items.x: GloRilla still wants to give the Pittsburgh Steelers a song of their own, and she renewed that pledge ahead of her upcoming Pittsburgh concert. The Memphis rapper told Pittsburgh City Paper she planned to follow through on an anthem for her favorite NFL team. "I keep saying I'm going to do it, but I am," she said. "I need to shout out the Steelers." Her loyalty dates to age 3. She said her father told her that her grandmother, who died before GloRilla was born, also supported the team. The song idea has been around for a while. In April 2024, SteelerNation reported that she discussed making a Steelers record on "The Pivot." She pointed to Wiz Khalifa's "Black And Yellow" as the model and stressed that she wanted to find the right song. That comparison comes with some real Pittsburgh history. Wiz Khalifa performed "Black And Yellow" before the Steelers' January 2011 AFC Championship game against the New York Jets, where he joined actor Billy Gardell for the Terrible Towel Twirl before kickoff. items.t: EXCLUSIVE: RBX Loses Spotify Bot Lawsuit Again After Judge Rejects Latest Attempt
items.x: RBX lost his Spotify bot lawsuit after a federal judge rejected his revised claims and wouldn't let him refile. U.S. District Judge Josephine L. Staton dismissed the West Coast rapper's negligence and California Unfair Competition Law claims with prejudice in an order AllHipHop reviewed. That closed the door to another amended complaint in this case. The dispute centered on who loses money when fake plays inflate an artist's share of Spotify streams. RBX, whose legal name is Eric Dwayne Collins, claimed bots boosted major acts, including Drake, while shrinking the royalty shares of other music rights holders. Drake was not a defendant. RBX filed suit on November 2, 2025. Judge Staton dismissed his first complaint on June 22 but let him try again. As AllHipHop previously reported , his revised suit accused Spotify of using stricter fraud controls against smaller artists while letting bigger names escape the same scrutiny. That new argument did not save the case. The order said RBX failed to identify a specific fraud-control rule that Spotify enforced against some artists but ignored for others. items.t: Jakarta Government Reveals Massive Economic Impact Of Ye's Concert
items.x: Ye s Jakarta concert generated an estimated $25 million in economic activity, according to Governor Pramono Anung. The governor shared that estimate Monday, October 26, following the rapper's Saturday performance at Gelora B### Karno Main Stadium. The official report also put ticket sales at about $18 million, while Pramono said hotels, shops, transport and tourism benefited. That account offered no detailed breakdown of how officials arrived at the broader estimate of the concert's economic impact. Before the show, promoter Raw Vision Collective said 20,500 people outside Indonesia had bought tickets, according to Indonesia Expat . Karen Tjahja, who led marketing and communications for the promoter, gave that sales update at an October 22 press conference. Among buyers abroad, Australia ranked first, with Singapore and Malaysia following it in the promoter's count of international ticket sales. Those figures captured purchases ahead of the concert, leaving them separate from a final tally of fans inside the stadium. items.t: 50 Cent Sues Rick Ross' Ex Tia Kemp For $6M Over Posts About Sire Jackson
items.x: 50 Cent sought at least $6 million from Tia Kemp in a new federal lawsuit over posts about his son, Sire, according to Billboard . The outlet obtained the complaint, filed in Los Angeles on October 26. Curtis Jackson sued Tiallondra "Tia" Kemp on behalf of 14-year-old Sire, identified as S.J., alleging defamation, invasion of privacy and intentional infliction of emotional distress. His lawyers accused Kemp of inventing a medical diagnosis and sexually degrading claims involving Sire's mother, Daphne Joy. They alleged she kept posting after a cease-and-desist letter. "But autism is not shameful," the lawyers wrote in the filing quoted by Billboard. The federal case followed a separate Florida petition seeking an injunction against Kemp over alleged cyberstalking, first reported by TMZ. The dispute had already drawn a public response from Sire's father. As AllHipHop previously reported , he shared news of the restraining-order request on Instagram and objected to using claims about a child's health as an insult. "This is the greatest example of bullying a minor saying he is on the spectrum," 50 wrote. He also said he had friends whose children were on the spectrum and said the subje

items.t: America Prepares Military Bases For Catastrophe As Other Nations Warn Citizens To Prepare
items.x: America is preparing its military to survive a potential national catastrophe for 90 days, but a troubling question remains: Is anybody making sure ordinary Americans are equally prepared? The Pentagon has launched a sweeping initiative called FORTRESS , which stands for Federal Operations for Resilience, Troop Resources, Energy, Supply, and Survivability. Announced September 30 by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth , the program aims to make American military installations less dependent on civilian infrastructure. READ ALSO: Military Discipline Crumbles After Hegseth Protects Kid Rock According to an October 25 Fox News report, military bases are being prepared to operate independently for at least 90 days if war, cyberattacks or infrastructure failures disrupt electricity, fuel supplies and transportation networks. The plan includes nuclear microreactors, independent power systems and strategic reserves. That sounds like serious business. And it is. Meanwhile, governments across Europe are delivering increasingly explicit preparedness messages to their citizens. items.t: Donald Trump Offers $1M Voter Fraud Reward
items.x: President Donald Trump offered $1 million for voter fraud tips on October 26, eight days before the midterm election, while leaving the source of the money unanswered. His Truth Social post covered both past elections and the coming 2026 vote. The promised payment depended on an arrest and a conviction. Tipsters would be paid "upon the arrest and conviction of those that created the Fraud!" he wrote. The White House provided no further details about the offer, according to ABC News . The outlet reported that it was unclear where the reward money would come from. The post itself did not name an agency that would run the program or explain how someone should submit a claim. It followed another cash promise. Last week, Trump announced a separate whistleblower program offering people who successfully exposed fraud a share of money recovered by the government. ABC reported that the proposed cut was 1% and that Trump said he would decide whether someone received an award. The president also pushed the SAVE America Act, which would require voter identification at the polls and proof of citizenship to register. The House passed that measure, but it failed repeatedly in the Senate, ABC repo

items.t: Jimmy Kimmel Grosses Himself Out Copying "Horny" Donald Trump Lusting Over Nicki Minaj
items.x: Jimmy Kimmel tried out Donald Trump's moves after the president's comments about Nicki Minaj's backside, then admitted the impression was making him uncomfortable. During his October 26 monologue on "Jimmy Kimmel Live!," the host copied Trump's lip licking, air punch and pursed mouth as his studio audience laughed. The gestures followed Trump's remarks about Minaj at a rally in Port Huron, Michigan. "Honestly, I'm grossing myself out even doing it. Horny Donald is my least favorite Donald of all of them." Kimmel also questioned how Fox News would have reacted if Joe Biden had made the same comments about the rapper. His routine turned the president's words and physical reaction into material for Monday's show. The Port Huron exchange happened Sunday, October 25. Trump called Minaj's backside "one hell of a beautiful ass" and added, "That's hard to miss." He brought up Minaj while explaining why he had looked over Ohio Sen. Jon Husted. Trump tied that earlier moment to learning about Husted's college football career and his reputation for hard tackles. His remarks about Husted at an October 12 rally in Youngstown had drawn coverage before the Michigan stop. Nicki Minaj had traveled

items.t: Man indicted in deadly stabbing of shelter resident in Washington Heights
items.x: NEW YORK (PIX11) A 29-year-old man has been indicted in the deadly stabbing of a person at a Washington Heights men’s homeless shelter in September, according to the Manhattan District Attorney. Javed Tyghter is accused of stabbing 33-year-old Nicholas Ahmad on Sept. 27. He faces charges of second-degree murder and criminal possession of a weapon, District Attorney Alvin Bragg announced Wednesday. According to court documents, both men lived at a shelter near West 168th Street and Fort Washington Avenue. Get ongoing crime and safety coverage on our homepage Tyghter allegedly shoved Ahmad and argued with him in the shelter’s lobby before returning to his room. Tyghter then allegedly came back to the lobby and repeatedly stabbed Ahmad in the torso, causing him to collapse, according to court documents. He was arrested nearby and was allegedly wearing the same clothes seen during the stabbing, according to the DA. Ahmad was taken to a hospital, where he was pronounced dead. “As alleged, Nicholas Ahmad was brutally murdered by Javed Tyghter in a senseless act of violence,” Bragg said. No trial date has been announced.

items.t: Democrats see battleground map expand to South Carolina, Florida, Mississippi
items.x: Democrats are giddy about the possibility of a bigger blue wave than expected in the battle for the Senate as polls show that South Carolina , Florida and Mississippi — three seats that were long seen as safe Republican holds — are now competitive races. Democrats view the Republican candidates running in those states as mediocre political talents who must fight historic headwinds caused by President Trump’s unpopularity, voter anger over inflation and the war in Iran, and burgeoning Democratic voter enthusiasm. The Senate battleground map has steadily expanded throughout the 2026 midterm election cycle as political handicappers have shifted seats that were thought to be in solidly Republican territory — such as Alaska, Iowa, Kansas and Texas — to the “toss-up" category. But now Republicans have to worry about losing Senate seats in states that were unthinkable as realistic Democratic pickup opportunities at the start of the election cycle, most notably South Carolina, which last elected a Democrat, Fritz Hollings, to the Senate in 1998. A New York Times/Siena poll of 707 voters in South Carolina published Wednesday showed Sen. Darline Graham (R-S.C.) tied with Democrat Annie Andre

items.t: Teen killed in Bronx shooting: NYPD
items.x: CLAREMONT, The Bronx (PIX11) A teenager has died after being shot in the Bronx on Thursday morning, police say. The 15-year-old died at the hospital after he was shot near the intersection of Third Avenue and East 171st Street just before 9:30 a.m., according to authorities. Get ongoing crime and safety coverage on our homepage Sources told PIX11 the teen had been shot in the abdomen and was found in and out of consciousness. Sources say police are looking for three men who were last seen wearing all black, two of whom were wearing surgical masks. They were last seen running down Fulton Avenue. Dominique Jack is a digital content producer from Brooklyn with more than five years of experience covering news. She joined PIX11 in 2024. More of her work can be found here .

items.t: DoorDash to buy Instacart in $17 billion grocery delivery deal
items.x: DoorDash is gobbling up Instacart in a $17 billion acquisition that will supercharge its grocery delivery business. DoorDash said the Instacart brand name and app will remain, and Instacart shoppers can continue fulfilling orders for Instacart. Grocers can also choose to work with Instacart or DoorDash. Instacart customers will now have access to 50,000 additional stores covered by DoorDash, the company said. For more on what’s happening in your area, head to our homepage Instacart, founded in 2012, specializes in grocery and convenience store delivery in the U.S. and Canada. Its 600,000 “shoppers” — who are independent contractors — completed 338 million orders last year, according to company filings. Instacart has a market value of $14 billion. DoorDash, founded in San Francisco in 2013, began as a restaurant delivery business but has expanded to pet food and electronics. Operating in 40 countries, it completed more than 3 billion orders last year using a network of 9 million independent delivery workers. It has a market value of $73 billion. DoorDash began delivering groceries in 2020 amid a surge in pandemic-era demand. Grocers were initially cautious. Kroger partnered with the

items.t: Brooklyn woman struck and killed by DSNY truck: police
items.x: BROOKLYN, NY (PIX11) A 30-year-old woman was struck and killed by a Department of Sanitation truck Wednesday evening in Brooklyn, according to police. The woman was crossing from the corner of Bay Parkway when she was hit by the truck near the intersection of Cropsey Avenue and Bay Parkway, police said. More Local News The truck was operated by a 41-year-old man, according to authorities. The woman was taken to a nearby hospital, where she was pronounced dead after suffering trauma to her body. The driver remained at the scene. No arrests have been made.

items.t: Tractor-trailer crash in Newark under investigation
items.x: NEW JERSEY (PIX11) A massive crash on I-280 in Newark Wednesday afternoon caused major delays for evening commuters. According to New Jersey State Police, troopers responded to a crash around 2:28 p.m. on the I-280 East in Newark. According to a preliminary investigation, a Freightliner tractor-trailer, a Honda vehicle, an Acura vehicle and a Mazda SUV were traveling east on I-280 when the Freightliner driver lost control and struck all three vehicles. More New Jersey News The Freightliner continued to move forward when it struck the left concrete barrier, traveled up the barrier and came to a stop on top of it. The driver of the Acura sustained minor injuries and was transported to an area hospital, according to NJSP. No other injuries were reported at the scene. The crash left three lanes on the eastbound side of I-280 and two lanes on the westbound side of the highway closed west of Exit 13 for Orange Street and First Street. All lanes had reopened by about 9:10 p.m. Wednesday. The crash remains under investigation, and no additional information was made immedately available.

items.t: Teen shot in the Bronx: sources

The teen of unknown age was shot just before 9:30 a.m. near the intersection of Third Avenue and East 171st Street in the Claremont neighborhood, sources say. CitizenApp video from the scene appears to show the shooting happened just steps from a community center and a park. More Local News What led up to the shooting and further information on the victim and suspect were not immediately made known. items.t: Can You Get That Bread? Oroweat® Brings a $50,000 Sandwich Hunt to NYC
items.x: What if chasing down a giant sandwich could put you in the running for a chance to win $50,000? Just in time for the TCS New York City Marathon, Oroweat® Bread is bringing its “Get That Bread” campaign to the streets of New York City with a life-sized sandwich and a playful citywide hunt! Ben Aaron joined marathon runner, actor and self-proclaimed bread enthusiast Dylan Efron to get in on the fun and find out how New Yorkers can join the chase. On Friday, October 30, keep an eye out around Union Square for a chance to spot the Oroweat® Running Sandwich. On Saturday, check out Chelsea Triangle to it. Corsini claims she was pressured into giving permission to harvest his skin, bone grafts, corneas and heart valves. Court documents say she will serve anywhere from four to 12 years. Get ongoing crime and safety coverage on our homepage Tiffany Howell, 48, of Warwick in Orange County, was driving south in the northbound lanes of the Taconic State Parkway in Westchester County at more than 50 mph when she struck a car driven by Manuel Boitel on Jan. 22, 2026, according to the attorney general’s office. Boitel was taken to a local hospital, where he was pronounced dead shortly after midnight. Howell pleaded guilty to aggravated vehicular homicide and manslaughter, according to James. Her driver’s license has been revoked, and she has waived her right to appeal, according to the attorney general’s office.

items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war , creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle . items.t: Dolores Huerta, influential labor leader, feminist and civil rights icon, dies at 96
items.x: Dolores Huerta, who co-founded the United Farm Workers union to improve working conditions in the nation's fruit and vegetable fields and coined the phrase “Sí, se puede!” that became a widespread rallying cry, has died. She was 96. Huerta's family said in a statement through her foundation that she died Wednesday at home. She kept a busy schedule well into her 90s, marching in protests and speaking in cities across the country about race, poverty, LGBTQ+ and women’s rights on behalf of her Bakersfield, California-based foundation. Huerta’s resolve cemented her place in history as one of the nation’s most influential labor leaders, civil rights icons and feminist activists. Her three-word Spanish-language slogan — which translates to “Yes, it can be done” — was grounded in the belief that people could affect change. Her work over the decades earned her a number of accolades, including the Presidential Medal of Freedom, the nation’s highest civilian honor. When then-President Barack Obama presented the award in 2012, he praised Huerta as a tenacious leader and joked that he had stolen her slogan for his 2008 campaign. Allegheny County had the most ballot requests with 161,188; Philadelphia was second with 128,032. As of 8 a.m. on Oct. 28, there have been 933,707 ballots returned to county boards of election, a 71% return rate with less than a week until Election Day. Only 14 counties have a return rate below the state average; Lehigh County has the lowest return rate at 59%. items.t: ‘To whom is it going to benefit?’ Residents express concerns about subway expansion
items.x: HARLEM, Manhattan (PIX11) Harlem residents are speaking out about an ambitious new plan to expand the New York City subway down 125 th Street. MTA officials got an earful at a public hearing Tuesday at the Adam Clayton Powell Office Building about the most expensive subway construction project of all time. Discover more local reporting on our homepage "I believe in supporting local businesses, mom and pop, so I want to make sure they're protected,” Harlem resident Niachloe Bowman told PIX11 News. She wants to see small businesses receive subsidies to offset the decreased foot and vehicle traffic caused by a years-long construction project. "To whom is it going to benefit is the question?” Bowman asked. “Is it going to benefit people who are already living in Harlem or people who want to come to Harlem? I think that’s the overall question." The final phase of the original Second Avenue extension is now getting underway, with a boring machine ready to be put in place. The MTA wants to keep it there and continue digging down 125th, connecting several subway lines and Metro-North while also easing congestion on crosstown buses. items.t: Flying taxis could carry passengers by 2030
items.x: (TestMiles) A British aerospace company has demonstrated an electric flying taxi that could eventually offer a new way to escape crowded city roads. The Flying Car Is Moving Beyond Science Fiction Los Angeles has spent decades trying to solve its traffic problems. Freeways expand, transit systems improve, and technology promises more efficient journeys. Yet travelling across the city can still take a remarkable amount of time. A British aerospace company believes part of the solution might be above the roads rather than on them. Vertical Aerospace has demonstrated an electric aircraft capable of taking off vertically, transitioning into conventional forward flight, and landing without a runway. The technology was publicly displayed at the Farnborough International Airshow in Britain, marking an important development in the company's plans to introduce commercial passenger flights. The aircraft is part of a growing category known as electric vertical takeoff and landing, or eVTOL. Unlike a conventional airplane, it does not require a runway for every departure. items.t: New York State Unified Court System issues official guidance to prevent AI hallucinations
items.x: ALBANY, N.Y. (NEXSTAR) — The New York State Unified Court System warned lawyers on Monday to fact-check artificial intelligence tools before submitting legal papers to judges. The Advisory Committee on Artificial Intelligence and the Courts published a guide for attorneys to prevent fake cases and citations from entering the legal record. “The Risks of Using Artificial Intelligence in Preparing Court Papers: What Every Attorney Should Know” builds on previous rules adopted by the state court system . It tells lawyers using generative AI—computer programs like large language models that write text—to understand how the technology works and independently verify every fact, quote, and claim the software offers. items.t: Neighbors celebrate Bronx mural as the nation’s tallest
items.x: BRONX, N.Y. [PIX11] A towering new mural in the Bronx is drawing attention around the country and creating a colorful new symbol of neighborhood pride. The artwork spans the side of a 29-story building in the Morrisania Air Rights Development along East 158th Street between Morris and Park avenues. Standing nearly 300 feet tall, the mural is visible across the surrounding community and it is being called the tallest in the nation. Neighbors gathered Tuesday for a ribbon-cutting ceremony. The piece was created through a collaboration between residents, tenant leaders and the nonprofit organization ArtBridge. Neighbors participated in workshops throughout the year, helping shape the imagery and themes featured in the artwork. Beatrice Jeane Richardson, who has lived in the neighborhood for decades, said the mural’s depiction of a woman holding a child at the top of the piece resonates deeply with her. “It means a lot,” Richardson said. Her daughter, Beatrice E., who also lives in the neighborhood, visited the mural Tuesday and said it reflects the struggles and achievements of the community. “It’s wonderful. items.x: NORTH BERGEN, N.J. [PIX11] Residents in Bergen County, New Jersey, say loud, low-flying planes coming in to Alma at Teterboro Airport are having a significant impact on their quality of life. “We actually joke around. We look up and we wave, thinking we can almost see the pilot and the people flying in the planes,” said Woodcliff Lake resident Jacqueline Gadaleta. “That’s how low they usually are.” “We have to pause everything that we’re doing because of the airplanes,” said Woodcliff Lake resident Stephanie Huang. Residents say a solution already exists. In 2021, the Federal Aviation Authority approved an alternate route that flies over Route 21 instead of residential neighborhoods. The route is barely used. “Teterboro Airport has an alternate path for plane arrivals, and they never use it,” said Hackensack Mayor Caseen Gaines. “In 2024, the alternate approach was used less than 0.2% of the time.” Hackensack recently passed a resolution asking the FAA to mandate the use of the alternate approach. items.t: New York Dollar General stores found overcharging shoppers in state investigation
items.x: NEW YORK (PIX11) Dollar General shoppers in New York will see changes aimed at preventing overcharging after a state investigation found customers were often charged with incorrect prices. The news comes as the discount retailer faces a separate federal lawsuit over similar allegations. New York Attorney General Letitia James announced a settlement with Dollar General on Oct. 15. The company must donate $1.875 million worth of food and personal items to Foodlink, a Rochester-based nonprofit, and make changes to prevent customers from being overcharged. The state investigation found pricing problems at Dollar General stores across New York. The attorney general’s office reviewed more than 900 store inspection reports from 2021 to 2023. About 43% showed price accuracy failures above the state’s allowed limit. More US and World News Investigators also visited 11 Dollar General stores in Western New York. They found they were charged more than the listed price for about 14% of the items they bought. Under the settlement, Dollar General must train employees on pricing rules, make sure shelf prices match register prices and update its receipts to show discounts more clearly. The company

Fagbemi was on the Manhattan-bound side of the bridge around 3:30 a.m. when his minivan broke down, police said. He got out and opened the hood to check what was wrong. About 16 minutes later, a tractor-trailer hit the minivan from behind, pushing it onto the man, who was standing in front of the open hood, according to police. More Local News Officers called FDNY and EMS, who took the man to a nearby hospital. He was pronounced dead at 4:42 a.m. Police said a review of video footage found no signs of criminal activity. The investigation is ongoing, and officials are still working to determine how fast the tractor-trailer was going. No summonses have been issued. More Transit News The crash forced officials to close all lanes in both directions of the RFK Bridge. One lane began reopening intermittently at 5:21 a.m. before all lanes reopened at 8:28 a.m.

items.t: Zip Code Shouldn’t Be Destiny: Save the Children’s Push to Get Every Rural Kid Reading by Third Grade
items.x: For millions of children in rural America, the odds are stacked before the first school bell rings. Save the Children is fighting back with Learn Without Limits , a national movement to close the rural literacy gap, and author Lauren Neumer Whitehurst just put 50,000 books into the hands of kids who need them most. A child’s zip code should not determine whether they can read, learn and succeed. That’s the conviction behind Save the Children , the world’s first and leading independent children’s organization, and it’s the reason the group launched Learn Without Limits , a national effort to help every child read by grade three . On New York Living , Save the Children President & CEO Janti Soeripto and author Lauren Neumer Whitehurst joined Marysol Castro to talk about the hidden disparities facing rural kids and what one bookshelf can change. items.t: Penn State linebacker Rojas anchoring Nittany Lion defense through losing streak
items.x: Tony Rojas stuck around at Penn State because he believed the Nittany Lions could compete for a conference championship. The team’s star linebacker now knows a Big Ten title is out of reach, but he still believes the Nittany Lions (3-4, 0-4 Big Ten) can win. They’ll need to win three of their final five to salvage a bowl appearance. “I just want to win out,” Rojas said. “I think winning is my biggest thing and all those accolades and whatever, it doesn’t really do anything good for me. I just want to win.” Mired in a four-game losing streak, Penn State will try for its first conference win of the Matt Campbell era when Purdue (3-4, 2-2) visits Beaver Stadium on Saturday. Rojas has played inspired football since returning from a knee injury that cost him nearly all of last season. He’s anchored a defense that has often been hung out to dry by an offense averaging just 18.5 points per conference game with just three second-half touchdowns. The junior leads the team in tackles, tackles for loss and sacks. items.t: PA residents reminded to check smoke alarms during time change
items.x: PENNSYLVANIA (WTAJ) As Pennsylvanians turn their clocks back this weekend, the Shapiro Administration is urging residents to replace the batteries in their smoke and carbon monoxide alarms. The reminder comes as Pennsylvania reported 153 home fire deaths in 2025, the highest total in the nation. State officials say working smoke alarms can cut the risk of dying in a home fire by half, while missing or non-functioning alarms remain a common factor in fatal fires. State Fire Commissioner Thomas Cook encourages residents to test alarms regularly, replace old batteries, and make sure every level of their home is protected. Officials also recommend creating and practicing a home fire escape plan, including two ways out of each room and a designated outdoor meeting place. Residents are also encouraged to check carbon monoxide alarms. The odorless, colorless gas can be produced by fireplaces, gas appliances, generators, and vehicles, and exposure can cause symptoms including headaches, dizziness, and nausea. items.t: Transferring Power of Attorney || The Law and You
items.x: Sponsored by Gieg and Jancula In this segment of The Law and You, we ask: According to attorney Mike Gieg, every power of attorney document includes a "triggering event" that outlines when a backup power of attorney takes over. Many power of attorney documents state that a successor agent may step in when the primary agent is unable or unwilling to serve. In those cases, the backup power of attorney would assume the role. Because every situation is different, the process depends on the circumstances. If the father still has capacity despite his dementia diagnosis, he may be able to sign a resignation, allowing the daughter to become the acting power of attorney. The daughter would then need to provide both the resignation and the power of attorney documents to third parties, so there is a clear record of the transition. If the father no longer has capacity, there are other options. If the mother remains competent, she can simply execute a new power of attorney naming her daughter as the primary agent. If neither parent is competent, the daughter may be able to obtain certification from the father's doctor stating that he lacks capacity, depending on the language of the power of att

items.t: Mexican citizen found trafficking fentanyl on Pennsylvania Turnpike pleads guilty
items.x: JOHNSTOWN, Pa. (WTAJ) A citizen of Mexico, who officials said was illegally in the United States, has pleaded guilty to trafficking drugs through Pennsylvania on his way to New York, United States Attorney Troy Rivetti announced. Ramiro Cisneros Hernandez, 48, pleaded guilty Oct. 28 to one count of conspiring to possess with intent to distribute more than 400 grams of fentanyl and one count of possessing with intent to distribute. According to Rivetti, Hernandez was traveling from California to New York City Nov. 21, 2022. Pennsylvania State Police pulled over the vehicle he was a passenger in for a traffic violation on the PA Turnpike in Somerset County. After a search of the vehicle, troopers found three kilograms (more than 6.5 pounds) of fentanyl under the cushion of the rear seat. Judge Stephanie Haines scheduled Hernandez's sentencing for March 16, 1017. He faces up to life in prison and a fine of up to $10 million. Pending sentencing, he remains in the custody of the U.S. Marshals Service.

items.x: HARRISBURG, Pa. — State Representative Tarik Khan and colleagues have introduced a bill that would ban PFAS, also known as "forever chemicals", in pesticides. H.B 2883 follows a PennEnvironment report that found perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances in 96% of 88 Pennsylvania waterways tested and implemented a "Do Not Eat" advisory for fish caught in the Wissahickon Creek basin due to perfluorooctane sulfonate, or PFOS, contamination. "It's incredibly sad that we can't even eat the fish in the Wissahickon because they're contaminated with toxic forever chemicals," said Khan. "As a nurse, I know these chemicals can harm our health, affect children's development and even pass from mothers to their unborn babies. And these waterways ultimately feed into the rivers we rely on for drinking water. We need to stop PFAS pollution at its source so our families and future generations have clean water that's safe to drink and fish in." The bill would prohibit the sale and use of pesticides containing PFAS when safer alternatives are available, as PFAS have been connected to certain cancers, immune system problems and reproductive risks. items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war , creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle . items.x: NEW YORK (AP) — U.S. stocks are drifting Wednesday as the countdown ticks toward this afternoon’s announcement from the Federal Reserve on what it will do with interest rates . The S&P 500 rose 0.2% and pulled within 1% of its all-time high , which was set earlier this month. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 176 points, or 0.3%, as of 11:45 a.m. Eastern time, and the Nasdaq composite was virtually unchanged. The day’s highlight will likely be what the Federal Reserve says, if anything, about where interest rates are heading. The Fed raised its main interest rate last month for the first time in three years in hopes of slowing the high inflation that’s squeezing the economy and discouraging Americans . The widespread expectation on Wall Street is that the Fed will leave the federal funds rate alone at this meeting, and the question is whether it will give hints about what may happen at later meetings. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh, though, has been adamant since taking over the Fed about wanting it to give fewer indications about its future moves. items.t: Avoiding Health Insurance Scams || Wellness Wednesday
items.x: Sponsored by The Health Insurance Place Are you receiving phone calls claiming that you're missing out on benefits? During Medicare open enrollment, which runs from Oct. 15 through Dec. 7, you may notice an increase in phone calls promising free benefits or extra money. We sat down with Kate McKnight, an insurance specialist with The Health Insurance Place, to separate spoofs from truths. Some callers may claim you are missing out on benefits, Social Security money, or grocery allowances. Kate said only a small percentage of Medicare recipients qualify for many of these additional benefits, which are often available to people with chronic health conditions or those who qualify for both Medicare and Medicaid. If you're unsure whether you qualify for certain benefits, Kate recommends hanging up or ignoring calls from unfamiliar numbers. Never provide personal information, such as your date of birth, Medicare number or Social Security number, over the phone. If a caller claims to be your insurance agent, hang up and contact your agent directly using their verified business number. You can also call the member services number listed on your Medicare card. items.t: 1.3 million Pennsylvanians request absentee, mail ballots
items.x: (WHTM) More than 1.3 million Pennsylvania voters requested an absentee or mail ballot for the 2026 general election before the October 27 deadline, according to the Pennsylvania Department of State. Registered Democrats requested 840,881 ballots (64%), registered Republicans requested 324,944 ballots (25%), and Independent/Third Party voters requested 147,604 ballots (11%). Allegheny County had the most ballot requests with 161,188; Philadelphia was second with 128,032. As of 8 a.m. on Oct. 28, there have been 933,707 ballots returned to county boards of election, a 71% return rate with less than a week until Election Day. More than 72% of the returned ballots have come from registered Democrats (610,617). Republicans have returned 233,986 ballots, and the Independent/Third Party voters have returned 89,104 ballots. Only 14 counties have a return rate below the state average; Lehigh County has the lowest return rate at 59%. Other counties below 71% are (in order) Blair, Montgomery, Huntingdon, Monroe, Fulton, Luzerne, McKean, Chester, Berks, Northampton, Philadelphia, and Delaware. items.t: Johnson says there will be ‘peaceful transfer of power’ on Jan 3
items.x: ( The Hill ) House Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.) said Tuesday that there will be a “peaceful transfer of power” when new House members are set to join the lower chamber next year. “Of course, we'll have a peaceful transfer of power, but it will not be transferring because we are going to keep the majority, and I'm going to be the Speaker of the House, and I will keep steady hands with at wheel, okay?” Johnson said, responding to MS NOW reporter Mychael Schnell in a clip she posted to the social platform X Tuesday. “Look, you know my background. I'm a constitutional attorney. We're going to follow the Constitution. The Constitution says when a state certifies the election of members of Congress, then they are administered the oath. That's what I'll be doing on January 3 to everybody who's there,” the speaker added. Officials in states throughout the country have recently played defense against election fraud claims from President Trump, with the president doubling down ahead of this year’s midterms. The MV Odyssey set sail two years ago on a voyage to the seven continents marketed as combining long-term living at sea with global travel. Its operator had offered to “make the Odyssey your permanent home,” with the purchase price of a suite for the lifetime of the vessel starting around $230,000. items.t: Poll: PA voters support data centers prioritizing local jobs, energy conservation
items.x: PENNSYLVANIA (WTAJ) — A new statewide poll found that support for data centers increases sharply when developers meet clear safety standards to protect communities and ratepayers. The survey, conducted by Susquehanna Polling and research and commissioned by the American Infrastructure Alliance (AIA), found that 36% of Pennsylvania likely voters initially support new data center construction, while 50% oppose it. However, 80% said they would support construction after hearing about commitments to pay the full cost of energy infrastructure, conserve water, forgo special tax breaks, help reduce electricity bills, strengthen the electric grid, create good-paying union jobs and generate revenue for schools and local services. Only 13% said they would continue to oppose it. "Pennsylvanians are telling us that the debate is not simply whether data centers should be built. They want to know whether development will be responsible and whether companies will meet clear expectations," said President and CEO of Susquehanna Polling and Research Jim Lee. items.t: Flying taxis could carry passengers by 2030
items.x: (TestMiles) A British aerospace company has demonstrated an electric flying taxi that could eventually offer a new way to escape crowded city roads. The Flying Car Is Moving Beyond Science Fiction Los Angeles has spent decades trying to solve its traffic problems. Freeways expand, transit systems improve, and technology promises more efficient journeys. Yet travelling across the city can still take a remarkable amount of time. A British aerospace company believes part of the solution might be above the roads rather than on them. Vertical Aerospace has demonstrated an electric aircraft capable of taking off vertically, transitioning into conventional forward flight, and landing without a runway. The technology was publicly displayed at the Farnborough International Airshow in Britain, marking an important development in the company's plans to introduce commercial passenger flights. The aircraft is part of a growing category known as electric vertical takeoff and landing, or eVTOL. Unlike a conventional airplane, it does not require a runway for every departure. As the parade was nearing its conclusion on Main Street downtown, Johnstown police said a large group of juveniles started fighting near the intersection of Main and Franklin Street. Officers intervened to break up the scuffle, which led to more altercations. Officers used stun guns and pepper spray to maintain order and disperse the crowd. Firefighters were also seen escorting people away from the scene. Police said anyone seen fighting was detained for public disorderly conduct. Johnstown Police Captain Dan Price told WTAJ that multiple people were arrested and at least one officer was injured in the scuffle but did not elaborate on the officer’s condition or how the officer sustained the injury. items.t: Rep. Joyce seeks answers after 100 railcars derail in Blair County
items.x: BLAIR COUNTY, Pa. (WTAJ) A total of 100 railcars have derailed in Blair County this year, prompting U.S. Representative Dr. John Joyce to seek answers from federal officials and Norfolk Southern. On Monday, Joyce sent letters to the Federal Railroad Administration and Norfolk Southern following Friday's derailment, requesting information about the incidents and what steps can be taken to prevent future derailments. “When you have that many in such a short order, I think that the concerns are heightened, but I think the concerns are appropriate from the community,” Joyce said. While the four derailments in Blair County this year have not resulted in reported leaks or injuries, Joyce said the incidents raise concerns about community safety. He pointed to Friday's derailment, which involved 11 additional railcars, including cars carrying toxic materials. Joyce's letters request the findings from investigations into all four derailments and ask what federal support may be needed to prevent future incidents. Emergency responders are also raising concerns about communication during Friday's derailment. The Logan Township United Fire Department responded to the incident. Chief Rusty Shoen

items.t: New PA bill increases required school bus stopping distance for drivers
items.x: HARRISBURG, Pa. (WTAJ) — Gov. Josh Shapiro has signed legislation into law that aims to improve school bus safety by increasing the required stopping distance for drivers. Senate Bill 65 , now Act 89 of 2026, strengthens Pennsylvania's School Bus Stopping Law by increasing the required stopping distance from 10 feet to 15 feet when a bus is stopped, with its red lights flashing and side stop arm deployed. The bill also expands school bus safety education by assigning new responsibilities to PennDOT and school districts. "Every child deserves to get to and from school safely, and motorists have a responsibility to stop when a school bus is loading or unloading students," said Sen. Lisa Baker (R-Luzerne, Pike, Susquehanna, Wayne & Wyoming). "Act 89 is about changing driver behavior and holding repeat offenders accountable. We ow it to our children and their families to take this responsibility seriously." In 2024, PennDOT's Automated Bus Enforcement Program recorded 76,413 violations, which was significantly higher than the 24,085 violations in 2023. items.t: New personal care center proposed in Centre County
items.x: BENNER TOWNSHIP, Pa. (WTAJ) — A new personal care center is being proposed near Bellefonte, adding 30 beds for seniors. The Fountains at State College is a 18,536 square foot nursing facility proposed in Benner Township at the corner of Penntech Drive and Progress Drive. The Fountains Group has other locations around Central Pennsylvania. "The Fountains at DuBois and The Fountains in Indiana really show a nice facility for the type of skilled nursing," Chris Schnure, a planner with the county, said. Commissioners hope the 30 extra beds the facility would add will serve the county's aging population. According to Chair Mark Higgins, they expect the number of seniors 85 or older to double by 2050. "At a certain age, you're like, yeah, I'm not into maintaining a home, maybe not even a condo or townhome. And this [facility] might be a potential fit for some of those seniors," Higgins said. Higgins said none of the 30 beds will be for Medicaid. Commissioners have voiced their support for Medicaid beds before, notably with Centre Care. He says the number of Medicaid beds the county does have is limited. "If Centre Care were to close, those 170 beds will disappear forever," Higgins said.

items.x: CENTRE COUNTY, Pa. (WTAJ) A Centre Hall man is behind bars after police allege he shot a gun close to a one-year-old and a woman. Lukas Lawrence Evans, 42, was arraigned Tuesday on multiple charges, including felony discharge of a firearm into an occupied structure, misdemeanor terroristic threats, and recklessly endangering another person, among others, after an Oct. 26 incident. According to a criminal complaint, troopers were called to a report of a physical altercation along Lower Brush Valley Road in Potter Township around 9:30 p.m. A victim reported to police that Evans had allegedly been drinking alcohol and became agitated by another taking a long shower. An altercation ensued, with one victim escaping the home through an open window. Another victim alleged that following the incident, Evans grabbed a loaded 9mm handgun, shooting it just mere feet from a female victim and her one-year-old son into a nearby wall inside the home. Troopers saw a small hole in the wall consistent with her story and a tan Taurus GX4 9mm handgun in a nearby drawer in the room, the affidavit notes. items.t: PA senator proposes legislation banning use of AI for student mental health services
items.x: HARRISBURG, Pa. (WTAJ) — Sen. Nick Miller (D-Lehigh & Northampton) has proposed legislation that would ban the use of artificial intelligence for student mental health services. In a memo circulated to House members, Miller argues that artificial intelligence can generate inaccurate or unsafe advice and lacks the professional judgement necessary to properly recognize and respond to a student in a mental health crisis. "When a student is struggling, they should be able to rely on trusted adults at school. Technology should support, not substitute, those relationships at the heart of student's mental health care," said Miller. Senate Bill 1505 , a companion to upcoming House legislation by Rep. Shusterman, would prohibit schools from using artificial intelligence to provide mental or behavioral health services that are otherwise performed by mental health professionals. However, the bill would not restrict mental health professionals from using artificial intelligence for administrative functions such as scheduling, organizing records and managing files. items.x: Pepper and Penny are 5–6-week-old kittens at the Huntingdon Humane Society. Could their fur-ever home be with you? Pepper (and Devyn) The Huntingdon Humane Society is nearing capacity as it cares for more than 80 cats and kittens at its shelter and is seeking adopters, foster volunteers and community support. Among the animals currently receiving care are Pepper and Penny, two kittens that were brought to the shelter after being found about four weeks ago. items.t: Clearfield County residents warned to lock homes, buildings after string of burglaries
items.x: CLEARFIELD COUNTY, Pa. (WTAJ) Pennsylvania State Police are investigating a burglary that occurred in the Bells Landing area of Greenwood Township, Clearfield County. According to police, the incident was reported around 12:16 p.m. on Oct. 24 at a residence along Camp Corbly Road. Police reported that cash and approximately three gallons of gasoline were stolen from the property. The total value of the stolen items was estimated at about $55. State police noted that this is one of several recent burglaries reported in the area. Investigators are asking residents to secure their homes and outbuildings by keeping them locked and to contact Pennsylvania State Police with any information that could assist the investigation.

items.x: Spooky season is in full swing at Home and Harvest ! Co-owner Maura Cruse stopped by the studio to share the shop’s Halloween drink menu and show us how to make a Boo-Berry Refresher. The drink features sparkling water and blueberry syrup, but the real star is the adorable marshmallow ghosts decorating the cup. Creating the ghosts is simple. With a spoon, add a few dabs of the marshmallow topping in a clear cup, then draw little ghost faces on the outside of the cup with markers for a cute and spooky finishing touch. Maura explained that Home and Harvest uses a marshmallow dessert topping, not marshmallow fluff, because it’s creamier and easier to spread. items.t: PA ranks 21st nationwide for spam call complaints
items.x: PENNSYLVANIA (WTAJ) Pennsylvania residents filed more than 555,000 spam call complaints over the past five years, ranking the state 21st in the nation. According to a new study from SMSPool , Pennsylvanians submitted 555,463 complaints to the Federal Trade Commission between October 2020 and September 2025. That works out to 4,253 complaints per 100,000 residents, about 6.7% higher than the national average. After several years of declining reports, spam call complaints increased in the most recent fiscal year. Pennsylvania recorded 85,798 complaints in fiscal year 2025, up 33.1% from 64,441 the year before. Despite that increase, complaints remain well below the peak seen in fiscal year 2021, when nearly 197,000 complaints were filed. Overall, Pennsylvania's 2025 total was down 56.4% from that high point. The state ranked seventh nationwide for the total number of spam call complaints and accounted for 3.7% of all complaints filed across the country during the five years. Nationally, the FTC received more than 14.8 million spam call complaints. Delaware had the highest complaint rate, while North Dakota had the lowest, according to the study. items.t: Resolution aims to make November ‘Carbon Monoxide Awareness Month’ honoring two PA teens
items.x: PENNSYLVANIA (WTAJ) A resolution is being proposed in the state senate to recognize November as Carbon Monoxide Awareness Month. According to a memo by Senator Carolyn Comitta (D-Chester), the resolution aims to bring greater awareness to the dangers of carbon monoxide poisoning and what residents can look out for to protect themselves as colder weather brings multiple heating options. Carbon Monoxide is a colorless and odorless poisonous gas that is produced by the incomplete combustion of carbon-based fuels. Stoves, fireplaces, boilers, water heaters, and gas or oil-burning furnaces are common sources found in the home. Poisoning can be deadly if carbon monoxide builds up in the home, causing symptoms such as headaches, dizziness, fatigue, confusion, nausea, and vomiting, among others. UGI urges safety, prevent carbon monoxide exposure as cooler weather begins Residents should always make sure carbon monoxide detectors are working correctly and have furnaces, water heaters, and other appliances checked professionally to ensure they are working as they should, lessening the chance of exposure. "Just because we have limited resources and I think the energy and the resources need to put into accountability, need to be put into investigations." "And that's where the time should be spent," she added. "Remember, I was in the Senate for the last go-around, and the votes aren't there. "So, that's how I feel. Harris said Democrats should be "uncompromising" and "not sit around, you know, being genteel about the relationships," but maintain accountability when it comes to cuts to healthcare and oversight on the Iran war. items.t: Two fined thousands for illegal deer hunting in Fayette County
items.x: MEMPHIS, Tenn. Two men who illegally hunted deer in Fayette County were ordered to pay back thousands in fines and restitution, according to the U.S. District Attorney's Office in the Western District of Tennessee. A federal judge ordered Austin Elrod, 30, of Somerville, Tennessee, to surrender his hunting license for five years and pay $40,000 in fines and $20,000 for an illegal deer hunting operation, the office said. He will also be on probation for a year. Thomas Boswell, 39, of Barnesville, Georgia was sentenced in July and ordered to pay $15,000 in fines and $11,000 in restitution. He will not be able to hunt for 18 months, prosecutors said. During an investigation, Elrod was found to be guiding white-tailed deer hunts in the Fayette County area without a required guiding license, according to the U.S. District Attorney's Office. Man receives guilty verdict in 2023 fatal shooting Prosecutors said that the hunts were advertised on Facebook and resulted in the illegal hunt of seven deer throughout the 2021 and 2022 hunting seasons. Lee approved an increase the state reward for information leading to Morley's arrest to $10,000, from the initial $2,500 reward. Meanwhile, the U.S. Marshals also offered a $5,000 reward Wednesday. Truck stolen by escaped inmate found, manhunt continues Morley, 28, was serving a life sentence for a 2022 murder. Along the way, he stole a truck, which was found abandoned Tuesday in southern Illinois. Morley is still at large and is considered armed and dangerous. items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war , creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle . items.x: ( KTLA ) – Activist Dolores Huerta, who helped co-found the National Farm Workers Association with César Chavez, has died. She was 96. Huerta's family said in a statement through her foundation that she died Wednesday at home. "We are deeply saddened to announce that our beloved mother, Dolores Huerta, has passed away today at the age of 96," her family said in a statement posted on social media. "As you can imagine, this is an incredibly difficult time for us, and we ask for privacy as we grieve this incredible loss to our family," the statement continued. "We know that many of you around the world share in our mourning, and we will be following up on plans to recognize and celebrate her incredible life and legacy." items.t: 68 dead in high-speed train collision, Spain’s 2nd deadly rail crash this year
items.x: URDA, Spain (AP) — A high-speed train slammed into another that had stopped on the tracks in Spain on Wednesday, killing at least 68 people and injuring dozens in the second deadly rail collision this year. The regional government of Castilla La Mancha confirmed the death toll and said another 58 people were receiving medical treatment at hospitals. Rescue workers searched the wreckage through the day for survivors and bodies. The collision came just nine months after another deadly crash involving high-speed trains operated by the same two companies in southern Spain in January. “Today all of Spain is grieving,” Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said from the crash site, where he announced that his government would declare three days of national mourning. items.t: Flying taxis could carry passengers by 2030
items.x: (TestMiles) A British aerospace company has demonstrated an electric flying taxi that could eventually offer a new way to escape crowded city roads. The Flying Car Is Moving Beyond Science Fiction Los Angeles has spent decades trying to solve its traffic problems. Freeways expand, transit systems improve, and technology promises more efficient journeys. Yet travelling across the city can still take a remarkable amount of time. A British aerospace company believes part of the solution might be above the roads rather than on them. Vertical Aerospace has demonstrated an electric aircraft capable of taking off vertically, transitioning into conventional forward flight, and landing without a runway. The technology was publicly displayed at the Farnborough International Airshow in Britain, marking an important development in the company's plans to introduce commercial passenger flights. The aircraft is part of a growing category known as electric vertical takeoff and landing, or eVTOL. Unlike a conventional airplane, it does not require a runway for every departure. Investigators allege the organization moved cocaine from Mexico through El Paso before transporting it across the country in commercial trucks. El Paso police and Homeland Security Investigations assisted Florida detectives, authorities said. Prosecutors described the operation as a Juárez-based branch of the Sinaloa cartel that supplied Florida with monthly cocaine shipments from at least December 2025 through July 2026. Investigators say traffickers used inoperable truck tractors as cover to transport cocaine from El Paso to Florida as part of an alleged Sinaloa cartel-linked network. Slavich, who was not having much luck catching fish at the time, typically keeps his phone accessible to film his daily catch. But this time, it allowed him to record his frightening shark encounter. items.t: Utah authorities connect 1974 cold case to serial killer Ted Bundy
items.x: SUMMIT COUNTY, Utah ( KTVX ) — Investigators in Summit County, Utah closed the 1974 cold case homicide of Melissa Ann Smith Tuesday, linking her murder to prominent serial killer Ted Bundy. Using DNA and other evidence, the Summit County Sheriff's Office and Summit County Attorney's Office formally closed the cold-case murder, saying that the evidence conclusively proves that Ted Bundy murdered 17-year-old Melissa Ann Smith. Bundy has long been considered a suspect in several cold cases in Utah, and Smith's murder was one of them. Hunters found her remains in Summit County on Oct. 27, 1974, 52 years ago today. "The work began with the investigators who handled the case in 1974, and it continued through the dedication and perseverance of those who carried it forward," Summit County Sheriff Kacey Bates said. "After 50 years, we have reached a point that so many have worked toward." items.t: Memphis mother shares story to aid youth drug prevention
items.x: MEMPHIS, Tenn. A mother is sharing her story to encourage other parents whose children are struggling with drug use. Samantha Brown was among several families and community organizations discussing ways to prevent drug problems among the youth. The Youth Overdose Opioid Task Force held Tuesday's meeting. The task force is a collaboration of several organizations working to help young people dealing with drug problems. It also provides resources to help people struggling with drug use and prevent overdoses. According to the Shelby County Health Department, 137 people under the age of 30 have visited emergency rooms for suspected drug overdoses in 2026. Brown says her 15-year-old son has faced challenges involving drugs. She has a message for other parents dealing with a similar situation. “Don’t give up. Keep showing up. Remain curious for their sake. Trying to reach them, trying to hear them, but also reach out. We’re just one person away from maybe finding the resource that our family needs,” said Samantha Brown, a mother. If you or someone you know is struggling with substance abuse, you can call 988 for help.
