items.t: Over 125,000 have voted early in Shelby County
items.x: MEMPHIS, Tenn. It's the final push of early voting this week, and so far in Shelby County, more than 125,000 people have voted early. That's more than 20% of registered voters, according to numbers from the state. Tennessee's Elections coordinator estimates that by the end of Tuesday, 1 million people in the state will have voted early, as voters WREG talked with said it's crucial to make their voice heard. It's a big day for 23-year-old Alisha Malone. "This was my first time voting, so I'm excited," said Alisha Malone, a first-time voter. "It was a little nerve-wracking, but I was prepared." "It was important because I have children and I'm a Black woman in America and I really care about my rights," said Malone. This early voting cycle is seeing higher numbers across the state of Tennessee. "Shelby County is averaging between 12,000 to 15,000 a day, which is a pretty strong number when you think about it," said Mark Goins, Tennessee Elections Coordinator. State numbers show where the county sits right now is 60% higher than numbers at this point in 2022. What to know before heading to the polls for early voting Shelby County has been putting up some big early voting numbers. WREG

items.t: FEC electronic filing system hit with hours-long outage
items.x: The Federal Election Commission's electronic filing system has been down for hours on Tuesday, according to a spokesperson who confirmed the agency's IT teams are working to restore the service. According to the FEC's incident update page, the agency said Monday night it is "investigating this issue," stating the FEC filing system is down. An update shortly after 9:30 a.m. EDT Tuesday said the agency is "continuing to investigate this issue." "At this time, we can point to the status update posted to the FEC’s website that the electronic filing system is currently offline and our IT staff are actively working to restore service," the spokesperson said in a statement to The Hill. The FEC's website search function used to find campaign donations, recipients and political action committee information is not impacted by the outage. It is not clear what caused the outage, though Reuters , citing an email, reported the FEC website was targeted by a hacker or hackers. The incident comes just over a week until voters across the country will head to the polls for the midterm elections. The FEC's functions should not impact the electoral process. DEVELOPING

items.t: Democrats see battleground map expand to South Carolina, Florida, Mississippi
items.x: Democrats are giddy about the possibility of a bigger blue wave than expected in the battle for the Senate as polls show that South Carolina , Florida and Mississippi — three seats that were long seen as safe Republican holds — are now competitive races. Democrats view the Republican candidates running in those states as mediocre political talents who must fight historic headwinds caused by President Trump’s unpopularity, voter anger over inflation and the war in Iran, and burgeoning Democratic voter enthusiasm. The Senate battleground map has steadily expanded throughout the 2026 midterm election cycle as political handicappers have shifted seats that were thought to be in solidly Republican territory — such as Alaska, Iowa, Kansas and Texas — to the “toss-up" category. But now Republicans have to worry about losing Senate seats in states that were unthinkable as realistic Democratic pickup opportunities at the start of the election cycle, most notably South Carolina, which last elected a Democrat, Fritz Hollings, to the Senate in 1998. items.t: AAA advises drivers about daylight saving time
items.x: ( WAVY ) – It's only a few days until we trade one extra hour of sleep for months of darkness as we leave work to drive home. Days will get way shorter in November: How much daylight we’ll lose And even though we're on the easier end of the time transition (from daylight saving time to standard time), the switch still takes its toll. Nexstar's WAVY went to AAA Tidewater Virginia to see what commuters can expect. "Well, the biggest thing for drivers will be the change in daylight when we leave work or school," said Holly Dalby with AAA. "At the end of the day, gone will be the bright sunshine, and we will find ourselves either driving into the glare from the setting sun or driving home in the dark. So it's a time to be particularly careful on the roads." While lawmakers have tried to get rid of the time switch altogether, it doesn't appear to be going anywhere anytime soon, so your circadian rhythm will have to dance to a different beat for a while. "It just messing with our sleep schedule can really add to our fatigue very quickly. And when we're fatigued, we can make mistakes," Dalby said. "We can be distracted more easily. items.t: Is it legal to take a ‘ballot selfie’ in Colorado?
items.x: DENVER (KDVR) — The midterm elections are just days away, and while some have already cast their ballots, there are still plenty who haven't, and some who may be wondering — can I take a ballot selfie? Well, the emphatic answer is — yes — you can take a ballot selfie in Colorado, but it wasn’t always allowed. In fact, it was illegal as recently as 2016, but a revised statute and a ruling by a judge in 2017 made it legal. Wildlife rescue group holding largest fundraiser of the year According to Colorado Revised Statute § 1-13-712 , voters are allowed to take a photo of their ballot after completing it; however, there are still guidelines surrounding it. "Any voter who makes available an image of the voter’s own ballot through electronic means after it is prepared for voting is deemed to have consented to the transmittal of that image," the revised statute states. So if a voter takes a photo of their own ballot and shares it, that’s OK as long as it's not done in violation of other election laws. Some polling places can monitor activity or place "reasonable restrictions" on the use of photography as necessary.

items.x: GREENVILLE, S.C. ( WSPA ) – Police in South Carolina have officially closed the investigation into the death of Hayden Panettiere, according to a Wednesday news release. Greenville Police Department officials said that Panettiere's death has been ruled accidental, based on findings in the investigation and the medical examiner's determination. On August 16, Panettiere was found unresponsive in an apartment at the Judson Mill Lofts on Easley Bridge Road. Police said that Brian Hickerson, Panettiere's on-and-off boyfriend, along with his brother, Zach Hickerson, were at the residence. EMS attempted life-saving measures before pronouncing Panettiere dead at 2:31 p.m. According to the Greenville County Coroner's Office, Panettiere had died from an accidental overdose of fentanyl, 4-ANPP, Alprazolam, Methocarbamol and Quetiapine. Panettiere had spoken openly about challenges in her personal life, including emotional scars from her childhood fame, postpartum depression after giving birth to her daughter, and struggles with alcohol addiction. items.t: Suspicious device at Capitol building deemed non-threat
items.x: DENVER ( KDVR ) — A suspicious device found at the Colorado State Capitol building on Wednesday morning was determined not to be a threat, according to a press release from the Colorado State Patrol. At 10:34 a.m., CSP found a suspicious device that was reportedly designed to look like an explosive on a windowsill outside the east entrance to the Capitol building. Worker injured after explosion at Loveland construction site The building was evacuated as a precaution around 11:12 a.m., and the area was secured by law enforcement. Lincoln Street and 14th Avenue were closed during the incident. By 11:14 a.m., the Denver Police Department Bomb Squad arrived and tested the device, which was determined not to be a threat to the public. CSP said a 32-year-old man was arrested at 11:29 a.m. in connection with the incident. The Denver Police Department assumed custody of the suspect. The evacuation order was lifted at 11:49 a.m. CSP said it has identified a person of interest who it believes has information about the device.

items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war , creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle . items.t: Denver water bills will cost you more next year
items.x: DENVER ( KDVR ) — Denver Board of Water Commissioners announced Denver water bills will cost $3.25 to $4.50 more per month starting Jan. 1, 2027, because of this year's historic drought. The biggest price hike is for water used outside your home, which aligns with Denver Water restrictions on watering lawns and washing cars that cut down water use significantly . Commissioners also increased drought rates , which apply if the current dry weather conditions continue, and they need to restrict water use to one or two days a week. "This year the big change is because of the drought," Todd Hartman, a spokesperson for Denver Water, said. "We are really focused on reducing outdoor water use, so the change is the indoor water use cost will go down, but [residents will] be charged more for water being used outside." Tim Smith with Loveland Fire Rescue Authority says this was likely a gas explosion. "We're not sure exactly how much gas had been flowing in there or for how long, but there were workers in there," he said. Xcel Energy crews responded to the scene. The company says the issue was on the customer side of the meter and it was not an Xcel Energy issue. "Xcel Energy does not have a natural gas leak in the area. items.x: OURAY COUNTY, Colo. ( KREX ) The Colorado Department of Transportation is requesting $6.5 million in initial federal emergency relief funds following severe flooding that caused an estimated $65 million in damage to highways across Southwest Colorado. The request to the Federal Highway Administration asks for a quick-release distribution equal to 10% of the total damage to start repairs immediately, while the Colorado Transportation Commission has approved $5 million in state emergency funds to assist with urgent work. The funding request follows severe storms that struck the region from Oct. 22 through Oct. 25, delivering rainfall totals of up to seven inches in areas such as Pagosa Springs. Peak floodwaters topped 4 feet on some federal-aid roadways, forcing widespread road closures. Gov. items.t: US cruise ship suspends voyage in Asia due to fuel costs, stranding 200 passengers
items.x: SIHANOUKVILLE, Cambodia (AP) — A U.S. cruise ship on an around-the-world voyage that touted its cabins as floating homes suspended its three-year voyage in Cambodia due to fuel costs, forcing hundreds of passengers to disembark. The MV Odyssey set sail two years ago on a voyage to the seven continents marketed as combining long-term living at sea with global travel. Its operator had offered to “make the Odyssey your permanent home,” with the purchase price of a suite for the lifetime of the vessel starting around $230,000. This photo attained as part of the press kit by the Odyssey shows the U.S. cruise ship in Japan. (Odyssey via AP) For now, it is docked at the Cambodian port of Sihanoukville on the Gulf of Thailand, with no certain departure date. The ship has been carrying 203 passengers, mostly Americans, along with 156 crew members, according to Cambodian officials. It has a a 650-passenger capacity. Using DNA and other evidence, the Summit County Sheriff's Office and Summit County Attorney's Office formally closed the cold-case murder, saying that the evidence conclusively proves that Ted Bundy murdered 17-year-old Melissa Ann Smith. items.t: North Carolina flags to fly at half-staff in honor of civil rights icon Dolores Huerta
items.x: RALEIGH, N.C. (WGHP) Governor Josh Stein ordered all U.S. and North Carolina flags at state facilities to be flown at half-staff from sunrise on Thursday until sunset Monday in honor of labor activist and civil rights icon Dolores Huerta . Huerta died on Wednesday at her home in Bakersfield, California. The 96-year old civil rights activist spent decades championing equal rights for women, immigrants and workers. She is widely remembered for cofounding the United Farm Workers of America in the mid-1960s. "Dolores Huerta made America a better place for workers and women, moving our nation forward," Stein said. items.t: Bond denied for man accused in random deadly Chesnee attacks
items.x: CHESNEE, S.C. (WSPA)—A 24-year-old man facing murder and attempted murder charges following a series of violent attacks across Chesnee has been denied bond. The Spartanburg County Sheriff's Office and the Chesnee Police Department arrested Noah Ashton Kowalewsky Tuesday after responding to reports of a shooting and assault before 7 a.m. Law enforcement officers originally responded to the Food Lion grocery store parking lot on South Alabama Avenue following reports that a gunman had shot one person and struck a woman in the head with a handgun. A subsequent investigation revealed that the violence spanned three locations, including the Chesnee Car Wash and a nearby Hardee's parking lot. The Spartanburg County Coroner's Office reported that 39-year-old Lenny James Presnell, Jr., was fatally shot at the Chesnee Car Wash. Kowalewsky was located by law enforcement in the Food Lion parking lot. During a bond hearing Wednesday morning, the Seventh Circuit Solicitor's Office revealed that the attacks were completely random and the victims did not know the suspect. Kowalewsky remains in custody at the Spartanburg County Detention Center.

items.t: AAA advises drivers about daylight saving time

"At the end of the day, gone will be the bright sunshine, and we will find ourselves either driving into the glare from the setting sun or driving home in the dark. items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: ( The Hill ) Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. Gasoline and energy costs have risen in six of nine months this year, as the Iran war sparked oil price shocks via the Islamic Republic's restrictions on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Persistent inflation , which has remained above the Fed's 2 percent target for five-and-a-half years, spurred central bank officials to hike interest rates by a quarter point in mid-September. items.t: DOJ’s California ballot fight rejected by another judge

U.S. District Judge David Carter ruled California can continue to accept the questioned ballots like any other. “This request violates longstanding constitutional principles mandating that states have control over their elections,” Carter wrote. “If Plaintiff’s last-minute request for relief were granted, either party could create chaos for their own political purposes to disrupt the election process,” he continued. “Over 20,000 registered Californians would potentially lose the right that generations of Americans have fought to preserve.” California has raised eyebrows at the veracity of the administration's list and says it's not obligated to verify voters’ citizenship in response. items.x: YORK COUNTY, S.C. (QUEEN CITY NEWS) A York County couple is being charged with several counts of unlawfully placing a child at risk of harm, according to the South Carolina Law Enforcement Division (SLED). Joel Snipes II, 42, and Sabrinia Skidmore, 28, were charged with six counts each of unlawfully placing a child at risk of harm on Saturday, Oct. 24. The York County Sheriff’s Office requested the SLED investigation. Parts of the court documents were redacted, but they allege that Snipes and Skidmore exposed children to "deplorable living conditions" that affected the child's physical health and well-being. "I think that going in the direction of impeachment is not a good idea, just to be honest with you," Harris told MeidasTouch's Aaron Parnas in an interview. "Just because we have limited resources and I think the energy and the resources need to put into accountability, need to be put into investigations." "And that's where the time should be spent," she added. "Remember, I was in the Senate for the last go-around, and the votes aren't there. "So, that's how I feel. Harris said Democrats should be "uncompromising" and "not sit around, you know, being genteel about the relationships," but maintain accountability when it comes to cuts to healthcare and oversight on the Iran war. items.x: GREENVILLE COUNTY, S.C. ( WSPA ) One person has been referred to their healthcare provider after being exposed to a rabid bat in Greenville County, state health officials said Wednesday. The South Carolina Department of Public Health said the bat was found near Bessie and North Flat Rock roads in Piedmont. The bat was submitted to the SCDPH laboratory for testing on Oct. 23 and came back positive for rabies on Monday. What to do Officials urge residents never to handle a bat or any wild or stray animal with bare hands. Bats that could have had contact with people, pets, or livestock should be kept in a sealed container and not touched, SCDPH added. Bats exposed to a person or pet should never be released, as it cannot be tested for rabies. The winged mammals are known to carry the rabies virus, but not every bat is infected with the virus. Rabies program manager Terri McCollister said bats have tiny teeth, making bites easy to miss. "Bats are an important part of South Carolina's ecosystems and deserve a healthy degree of respect just like all wild animals,” McCollister said. items.t: Law to allow UTVs on certain public roads takes effect in November
items.x: COLUMBIA, S.C. (WSPA) – A law passed earlier this year to allow utility terrain vehicles on some public roads will soon take effect in South Carolina. Starting Nov. 18, UTVs will be allowed on secondary highways and streets where the posted speed limit is 55 mph or less. While operating on public roads, UTV drivers must follow the same laws as drivers of regular vehicles, including registering their vehicles with the Department of Motor Vehicles, having working lights and carrying liability insurance. “We need to kind of treat it just like we do our car. We need to be mindful of what our speed is when we’re operating it, making sure we’re wearing our seat belt, making sure that we’re eliminating distractions behind the wheel, and of course, we don’t want people to get behind the wheel impaired,” said South Carolina Highway Patrol’s Troop 1 community relations officer Master Trooper William Bennett. The bill was introduced by Democratic state Sen. Russell Ott about six years ago. Greenville Police Department officials said that Panettiere's death has been ruled accidental, based on findings in the investigation and the medical examiner's determination. On August 16, Panettiere was found unresponsive in an apartment at the Judson Mill Lofts on Easley Bridge Road. Police said that Brian Hickerson, Panettiere's on-and-off boyfriend, along with his brother, Zach Hickerson, were at the residence. EMS attempted life-saving measures before pronouncing Panettiere dead at 2:31 p.m. According to the Greenville County Coroner's Office, Panettiere had died from an accidental overdose of fentanyl, 4-ANPP, Alprazolam, Methocarbamol and Quetiapine. Panettiere had spoken openly about challenges in her personal life, including emotional scars from her childhood fame, postpartum depression after giving birth to her daughter, and struggles with alcohol addiction. items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war , creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle . items.t: Judge overseeing Maduro trial dies
items.x: ( The Hill ) Alvin Hellerstein, a longtime federal judge who was set to oversee the criminal trial of deposed Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro, has passed away, according to a court official. He was 92. Nominated by then-President Bill Clinton in 1998, Hellerstein oversaw many high-profile disputes during his nearly three decades on the bench in New York City. He was back in the national limelight presiding over the proceedings for Maduro , who was captured and brought to the U.S. earlier this year over accusations of narco-terrorism. Maduro and his wife were in the judge's courtroom less than two weeks ago to plead not guilty to a new set of criminal charges. Before the Maduro operation, Hellerstein had long clashed with President Donald Trump in court. The judge at one point agreed that Trump’s fixer-turned-foe, Michael Cohen, could be released from prison to home confinement. Cohen has cast his prosecution as retribution by Trump. Separately, Hellerstein repeatedly denied Trump's efforts to move his hush money criminal prosecution into federal court, forcing the president to try his luck in New York's state system. items.t: CBP evaluates military ‘heat ray’ for potential use at US-Mexico border
items.x: EL PASO, Texas (Border Report) — U.S. Customs and Border Protection is evaluating a military weapon that creates an intense heating sensation on the skin for potential use along the U.S.-Mexico border, but the agency has not disclosed a testing location or confirmed its deployment in the El Paso region. The weapon, called the Active Denial System and commonly known as a “heat ray,” is designed to repel people by directing an invisible beam of electromagnetic energy at them. The Pentagon authorized a seven-month loan of the system to the Department of Homeland Security beginning in September, according to a memorandum first reported by CNN. The arrangement lets DHS test the equipment and develop procedures for potential border operations. In a statement to Border Report, a CBP spokesperson said: “CBP is continually evaluating new technology, especially technology that can save lives while simultaneously enhancing national security effectiveness.” The statement provided to Border Report did not identify where testing would occur, what circumstances would justify using the weapon, or what safeguards would govern its operation. items.t: US stocks hold steady as the countdown ticks to a Federal Reserve decision on interest rates
items.x: NEW YORK (AP) — U.S. stocks are drifting Wednesday as the countdown ticks toward this afternoon’s announcement from the Federal Reserve on what it will do with interest rates . The S&P 500 rose 0.2% and pulled within 1% of its all-time high , which was set earlier this month. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 176 points, or 0.3%, as of 11:45 a.m. Eastern time, and the Nasdaq composite was virtually unchanged. The day’s highlight will likely be what the Federal Reserve says, if anything, about where interest rates are heading. The Fed raised its main interest rate last month for the first time in three years in hopes of slowing the high inflation that’s squeezing the economy and discouraging Americans . The widespread expectation on Wall Street is that the Fed will leave the federal funds rate alone at this meeting, and the question is whether it will give hints about what may happen at later meetings. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh, though, has been adamant since taking over the Fed about wanting it to give fewer indications about its future moves. items.t: Sugary foods to lose SNAP-eligibility on Nov. 1: SCDSS
items.x: SOUTH CAROLINA (WCBD) The South Carolina Department of Social Services on Wednesday announced that its new program, Healthy Food SC, will take effect on Sunday. Healthy Food SC project is a two-year initiative beginning on Nov. 1, updating the definition of Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP)-eligible foods by removing candy, energy drinks, soft drinks, and other sweetened beverages. Diet and zero-sugar soft drinks will still be SNAP-eligible after the new definitions take effect. This change will affect all South Carolina SNAP-approved retailers. SNAP households will not have the option to opt out of the restrictions. More information about the program can be found on dss.sc.gov .

items.t: $39K Home Depot Boom Lift sold on Facebook Marketplace in Tennessee, police say
items.x: NASHVILLE, Tenn. ( WKRN ) — A 23-year-old woman is set to appear in Nashville court after allegedly helping a man flip a $39,000 piece of Home Depot equipment on Facebook Marketplace. Arrest documents show Rebecca Walpole and a male suspect entered the Madison, Tennessee, Home Depot on May 26 and rented a boom lift, which is commonly known as a cherry picker or basket crane. The equipment was towed using a silver Dodge Ram. According to court documents, the property was never returned. Nashville Super 8 sued over almost $150K in unpaid repair bills The male suspect was arrested in Michigan on Sept. 23, according to arrest documents. Investigators said he admitted to selling rented construction equipment to buyers on Facebook Marketplace. Walpole faces a felony theft of property charge, and she was recently booked in Davidson County. Her bond was set at $10,000.

items.t: Dolores Huerta, labor leader and activist, dies at 96
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Activist Dolores Huerta, who helped co-found the National Farm Workers Association with César Chavez, has died. She was 96. Huerta's family said in a statement through her foundation that she died Wednesday at home. "We are deeply saddened to announce that our beloved mother, Dolores Huerta, has passed away today at the age of 96," her family said in a statement posted on social media. "As you can imagine, this is an incredibly difficult time for us, and we ask for privacy as we grieve this incredible loss to our family," the statement continued. "We know that many of you around the world share in our mourning, and we will be following up on plans to recognize and celebrate her incredible life and legacy." items.t: Two accused of robbing victim at gunpoint at Upstate credit union ATM
items.x: ANDERSON COUNTY, S.C. (WSPA) Two people are accused of robbing someone at gunpoint at an ATM outside an Upstate credit union. According to the Anderson County Sheriff's Office, the armed robbery happened at the State Credit Union on Pearman Dairy Road around 6:25 p.m. on October 15. According to warrants, the two armed 18-year-old suspects approached the victim from behind and forced the victim to hand over their wallet and $100 in cash. The two suspects, identified as Ja'Marion Vontrell Davis and Kamaria Zy'Tavious Lee-Henry, were arrested Tuesday and were each charged with armed robbery, kidnapping, financial transaction card theft, and possession of a weapon during a violent crime. Both are being held in the Anderson County Detention Center.

Kotlikoff after allegations of a 2024 gang rape at a campus fraternity that resulted in no criminal charges caused uproar around the country. The more than 75 members of the body will have their second meeting debating the resolution and the timing of a vote on it. A motion could be introduced to delay the no-confidence vote and set another meeting. But if that motion is not introduced or fails, members of the Faculty Senate will begin the no-confidence vote after Wednesday's meeting is over, and they typically have a week to cast their choice online. While a no-confidence vote has no authority to remove an official, its passing would show deep dissatisfaction from faculty with how Cornell leadership has handled accusations from Jane Doe that seven members of the Chi Phi fraternity raped her . What does the no-confidence vote entail? items.t: Sabato’s Crystal Ball moves 16 House races toward Democrats
items.x: ( The Hill ) – Nonpartisan election forecaster Sabato’s Crystal Ball is shifting more than a dozen House races toward Democrats in the final week of the campaign , another sign of a worsening political environment for Republicans. Crystal Ball, a division of the University of Virginia’s Center for Politics, has moved dozens of races toward Democrats in recent weeks, including nearly 50 races in the month of October alone. The race changes include moving a few deep-red seats into the “toss up” column. Open congressional districts in Kentucky and Montana, as well as seats with GOP incumbents in Missouri, Virginia, Colorado and Pennsylvania moved into coin flip territory. Many of the seats Crystal Ball rates as a toss-up were places Trump carried by double digits in 2024. Trump says he made the mistake' of studying' GOP senator's anatomy' One notable race that moved from toss-up to “leans Democratic” is Texas’s 15th Congressional District, where Rep. Monica de la Cruz (R) is facing a tough challenge from Tejano music star Bobby Pulido (D). items.x: GREENWOOD, S.C. (WSPA)— A shooting early Wednesday morning in Greenwood has resulted in an officer-involved incident and injuries. Around 4:30 a.m., officers with the Greenwood Police Department responded to a home on Hunter Street for a report of an individual who had been shot. Upon arrival, officers forced entry into the home and reportedly heard loud shouting coming from the back of the residence. As officers moved towards the situation, they found a 76-year-old man suffering from a gunshot wound. Subsequently, authorities encountered a 51-year-old man armed with a handgun in the same room. During the encounter, the armed suspect supposedly pointed the weapon toward officers, prompting law enforcement to discharge their firearm. The suspect fled to another room, where he sustained what police said appeared to be a self-inflicted gunshot wound. Both individuals were taken to a nearby hospital, where their conditions remain unknown. Officers said the suspect's identity is being withheld at this time pending further investigative and charging decisions. items.t: Man jailed for presenting gun at Upstate gas station
items.x: LAURENS COUNTY, S.C. (WSPA) One person was taken into custody Wednesday morning after an incident at a gas station in Laurens County. The Laurens County Sheriff's Office announced that Conell Bernard Terry III, of Piedmont, was arrested and charged with Pointing and Presenting a Firearm at Another Person and Breach of Peace Aggravated in Nature. An investigator arrived on scene quickly and took the man into custody without incident. Terry remains in the Laurens County Detention Center.

The MV Odyssey set sail two years ago on a voyage to the seven continents marketed as combining long-term living at sea with global travel. Its operator had offered to “make the Odyssey your permanent home,” with the purchase price of a suite for the lifetime of the vessel starting around $230,000. The ship has been carrying 203 passengers, mostly Americans, along with 156 crew members, according to Cambodian officials. It has a a 650-passenger capacity. Its Florida-based operator, Villa Vie Residences, said monthly fuel expenses per cabin that historically averaged $1,800 have reached an estimated $6,000 to $8,000 in parts of Asia due to the war in Iran. items.x: SPARTANBURG, S.C. (WSPA) Chuck-or-Treat returns to Fifth Third Park Wednesday, with gates opening at 5 p.m. and ending at 7:30 p.m. Here's what you need to know before you go! According to Reuters , Heineken presented a document to U.K. hospitality customers earlier this month advising that the medications could potentially change drinking habits among users. The drugs may result in "fullness and fewer serves" in pubs and bars. “We see some changes in consumption behaviour among (GLP-1) users and will continue to monitor how these behaviours evolve in 2027," a Heineken spokesperson told the publication. The report noted that the company’s research found consumers increasingly choosing smaller servings, lower-alcohol beverages and premium products and that these shifts also align with broader trends focused on health, wellness and moderation. One option Heineken advised customers to pursue is half-pints and low- and no-alcohol options, according to the publication. items.t: 68 dead in high-speed train collision, Spain’s 2nd deadly rail crash this year
items.x: URDA, Spain (AP) — A high-speed train slammed into another that had stopped on the tracks in Spain on Wednesday, killing at least 68 people and injuring dozens in the second deadly rail collision this year. The regional government of Castilla La Mancha confirmed the death toll and said another 58 people were receiving medical treatment at hospitals. Rescue workers searched the wreckage through the day for survivors and bodies. The collision came just nine months after another deadly crash involving high-speed trains operated by the same two companies in southern Spain in January. “Today all of Spain is grieving,” Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said from the crash site, where he announced that his government would declare three days of national mourning. items.t: Two SC polls show different pictures of Graham-Andrews Senate race
items.x: CHARLESTON, S.C. (WCBD) With voters already casting ballots ahead of Election Day, two South Carolina-based polls released this week show a closely contested U.S. Senate race but offer different snapshots of where the contest stands. Polls released by The Citadel and the South Carolina Policy Council both found Republican Sen. Darline Graham ahead of Democrat Annie Andrews, but by significantly different margins. Both surveys also found Republican Alan Wilson maintaining a larger lead in the governor's race. The Citadel's survey of 1,009 registered voters found Graham leading Andrews by 4 percentage points statewide. items.t: Democrats see battleground map expand to South Carolina, Florida, Mississippi
items.x: Democrats are giddy about the possibility of a bigger blue wave than expected in the battle for the Senate as polls show that South Carolina , Florida and Mississippi — three seats that were long seen as safe Republican holds — are now competitive races. Democrats view the Republican candidates running in those states as mediocre political talents who must fight historic headwinds caused by President Trump’s unpopularity, voter anger over inflation and the war in Iran, and burgeoning Democratic voter enthusiasm. The Senate battleground map has steadily expanded throughout the 2026 midterm election cycle as political handicappers have shifted seats that were thought to be in solidly Republican territory — such as Alaska, Iowa, Kansas and Texas — to the “toss-up" category. But now Republicans have to worry about losing Senate seats in states that were unthinkable as realistic Democratic pickup opportunities at the start of the election cycle, most notably South Carolina, which last elected a Democrat, Fritz Hollings, to the Senate in 1998. McCuskey alleges that TikTok "violated numerous West Virginia consumer protection laws through the design and operation of its app, ultimately harming kids." TikTok created a platform that puts West Virginia kids at risk by encouraging continuous use, targeting younger users with its recommendation systems that select what content children see, and failing to disclose safety gaps to parents and caregivers. items.t: Ohio man supplied urine to help another person qualify for jail release, found guilty

Robert Givens, 35, was found guilty of tampering with evidence following an Oct. 22 jury trial. The case began when a person at the Muskingum County Jail requested a drug test to qualify for release on a personal recognizance bond. Corrections Officer Troy Pontius collected the sample and found it measured 90 degrees. That was within the accepted range but below the typical temperature of 98 degrees for a new sample. The test was negative, though the person had tested positive for several substances days earlier. Surveillance video showed Givens and the person talking and walking together before exchanging an unidentified item. Givens placed the item in his pocket and went to a restroom urinal. The other person then approached the same urinal before going to Pontius for the drug test. Cameras did not show the urinals. items.t: Former West Virginia bus driver guilty of transporting child sexual abuse videos, photos, sentenced for crimes
items.x: CLARKSBURG, W.Va. (WTRF) — A former bus driver in West Virginia has been sentenced to 20 years in federal prison for transporting child sexual abuse material. Arlin James Fleckenstein, 36, of Belington, was also ordered to pay $83,500 in restitution to victims depicted in the material. According to the U.S. Attorney’s Office, Fleckenstein worked as a bus driver and lived on the grounds of a resort in 2023 when he uploaded thousands of files containing child sexual abuse material to an online file-sharing service. The uploads led to a cyber tip and an investigation. Investigators later received a second cyber tip from Instagram involving an adult having an explicit conversation with a minor in another state. Authorities traced both tips to Fleckenstein. A search of his electronic devices uncovered more than 1,000 images and videos containing child sexual abuse material. Investigators also found conversations with other victims on social media platforms. The FBI and West Virginia State Police investigated the case as part of Project Safe Childhood. Assistant U.S. Attorney David Perri prosecuted it, and Chief U.S. District Judge Thomas S. Kleeh presided.

items.t: Earlier sunsets return to the Ohio Valley as clocks fall back this weekend
items.x: WHEELING, W.Va. (WTRF) — As October comes to an end and November approaches, the Ohio Valley is preparing for another seasonal change. While temperatures have remained warmer than average, one thing will certainly change this weekend: the time the sun sets. Daylight saving time officially comes to an end Sunday, Nov. 1, at 2 a.m., when clocks will move backward one hour to 1 a.m. This means an extra hour of sleep for many residents, but it also means the sun will begin setting much earlier in the evening. On Halloween, Saturday, Oct. 31, the sun is expected to set in Wheeling around 6:21 p.m. Just one day later, on Sunday, Nov. 1, sunset will occur around 5:20 p.m. While the change may feel dramatic, the Ohio Valley is not actually losing an entire hour of daylight overnight. Instead, moving the clocks backward shifts an hour of daylight from the evening to the morning. Sunrise on Saturday will occur around 7:51 a.m., while Sunday morning's sunrise will be around 6:52 a.m. As we continue through the fall season, the Northern Hemisphere is tilted farther away from the sun. Owner Ashley Moore says Pull Out is a "chill place for everybody to come hangout and just relax after a hard day's work." The restaurant is open every day starting at 9 a.m. and it closes around 1 a.m. or 2 a.m. depending on the crowd, according to Moore. items.t: Glen Dale officials outline pool renovation plans

Officials and engineers gathered at the Glen Dale Pool to go over plans for the renovations Wednesday. The upgrades have been separated into two phases. Phase one concentrates on the pool house, which includes a renovated snack bar area, ADA improvements to bathrooms, and a new mechanical room for the baby pool. City of Glen Dale Park and Recreation Board member Betsy Frohnapfel says pools play an important part in communities and she is excited to see the plan through. I think it's very exciting. I'm always under the belief that if you lose your municipal pool, you lose your community. So my role as a rec board member, I am here to support the city of Glen Dale in their quest for getting grants and contributions to do the project. And I'll see that project through to the end of phase two." Betsy Frohnapfel, City of Glen Dale Park and Recreation Board Chairperson The cost of phase one is $424,800 and is marked for completion on March 15, 2027. The night was busy for care coordinators Andrea Andrusewicz and Taylor Nemick, who sparked conversations with interested families about what OhioRISE can do. They also met parents who were familiar with the program’s benefits. items.t: Mike Hawkins Jr. added to Maxwell Award watch list
items.x: MORGANTOWN, W.Va. — West Virginia quarterback Mike Hawkins Jr. has been added to the Maxwell Award watch list, the Maxwell Football Club announced Wednesday. The Maxwell Award, first presented in 1937, is given annually to the college player of the year. Hawkins has shone during his first year with the Mountaineers, throwing for 1,598 yards, rushing for 836 yards and accounting for 27 total touchdowns with just two interceptions. His 16 rushing touchdowns are tied for the most in the nation this season. Other players added to the Maxwell Award watch list on Wednesday were Missouri's Jamal Roberts, UCLA's Wayne Knight, Wake Forest's Gio Lopez and Oregon State's Braden Atkinson and Jesse Legree. items.t: WVU’s ZaZa Walton named to Cheryl Miller Award watch list
items.x: MORGANTOWN, W.Va. — West Virginia senior Zahirah "ZaZa" Walton has been named to the Cheryl Miller Award watch list, the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame announced Wednesday. The Cheryl Miller Award, in its 10th year, honors the top small forward in NCAA Division I women's college basketball. It is named after the three-time Naismith Player of the Year and Class of 1995 Hall of Famer. Walton transferred to WVU this offseason from George Mason, where she played the first three seasons of her college career. A three-time Atlantic 10 All-Conference selection, Walton averaged a career-best 18.1 points and 6.1 rebounds per game last season. Other Big 12 players named to the Cheryl Miller Award watch list are Arizona State's McKinna Brackens, Texas Tech's Jalynn Bristow, Oklahoma State's Stailee Heard and Baylor's Skylar Jones. items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war , creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle . items.t: Ohio mom who microwaved baby asks for clemency
items.x: Editor's Note: The video above is previous coverage of China Arnold s third trial. DAYTON, Ohio ( WDTN ) China Arnold. It's a name many Daytonians remember from the 2000s. The Dayton Branch of the NAACP is holding a press conference at 1 p.m. "urging the release of China Arnold." According to the organization, Arnold is asking Ohio Gov. Mike DeWine for clemency. Taking a brief look back On Aug. 30, 2005, Arnold had an argument with her boyfriend, Terrell Talley. Arnold caused the death of her 28-day-old child, Paris Talley, by burning her in a microwave. Paris Talley | WDTN File Photo A judge declared a mistrial during Arnold's first trial. She was found guilty in a second trial, but the verdict was later overturned. In the third trial, Arnold was found guilty and sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole. The death penalty for Arnold had been on the table, but jury members chose prison instead. Arnold attempted to get a fourth trial, but the U.S. Supreme Court declined to hear her appeal. She is currently an inmate at Dayton Correctional Institution.

items.t: Driver shortage forces Indian Creek to cut six bus routes
items.x: WINTERSVILLE, OH (WTRF) — Indian Creek Local School District has cut six bus routes as it works to transport about 1,200 students each day with fewer drivers. Transportation Director Brenda Staffilino said the district has increased wages, offered signing bonuses and combined routes to maintain service across its 75-square-mile area. The district has 11 route drivers, one substitute handling routes and trips, two substitutes who only cover trips and one substitute in training. Staffilino said she would like to add at least four drivers. “If I had more drivers, I can add more routes,” Staffilino said. Substitute drivers earn $17.41 per hour and can receive a $1,000 signing bonus at the end of the school year. Full-time drivers earn between $18.41 and $23.83 per hour based on experience, not including overtime. Staffilino said mechanics have also worked as substitute drivers for routes and athletic trips. Some drivers are nearing retirement, which could create more openings. The shortage led the district to eliminate open-enrollment transportation and courtesy busing. items.t: West Virginia #9 for grocery store shoplifting incidents in United States
items.x: WEST VIRGINIA (WTRF) — West Virginia had the ninth-highest rate of reported grocery store shoplifting incidents in the country, according to an analysis by H&P Law . The state recorded 6,350 incidents from 2021 through 2025, averaging 1,270 per year. That equals 71.64 incidents for every 100,000 residents. The analysis used FBI Crime Data Explorer figures and U.S. Census Bureau population estimates. West Virginia’s number of incidents rose 42.7% between the first and final years studied. Kentucky recorded a 25.4% increase during the same period. The state’s rate was 2.4 times Pennsylvania’s rate of 29.50 incidents per 100,000 people. West Virginia also ranked above Ohio at 61.52 and Virginia at 60.22. New Mexico ranked first with 156.53 incidents per 100,000 residents, more than twice West Virginia’s rate. items.t: “We don’t give up” 2-day manhunt ends after K9 Odin finds domestic violence suspect hiding in Ohio woods
items.x: MONROE COUNTY, OH (WTRF) — An Ohio man has been arrested after deputies searched for him for two days following a reported domestic violence incident. Monroe County sheriff’s deputies responded to the incident in Clarington on Oct. 26. The Sheriff’s Office said Danzig K. Williams, 30, fled from the residence into a wooded area before deputies arrived. Monroe County Sheriff's Office Deputies used a thermal drone and K9 Odin during the search but did not locate Williams. On the evening of Oct. 27 and into Oct. 28, deputies received information that Williams was near Brey Hollow Road in the Sardis area. Deputies saw him while responding, but he again ran into the woods. A thermal drone located Williams hiding near a roadside ditch. Deputies then deployed K9 Odin, and Williams surrendered. Williams was taken to the Monroe County Jail on charges of violating a temporary protection order, domestic violence and strangulation. Sheriff Derek Norman credited the deputies involved in the search and thanked the Monroe County commissioners for funding equipment, technology and training used by the department. Williams is presumed innocent unless proven guilty in court.

items.t: Fentanyl, methamphetamine, cocaine trafficking in Ohio, man sentenced for crimes

A Muskingum County jury found Vintrel Cloud, 26, guilty of multiple drug trafficking and possession charges during a trial in September. He was also convicted of possessing criminal tools for using a cellphone to conduct drug transactions. Evidence showed Cloud operated two drug houses in Columbus. Investigators found messages and records detailing his customers, money owed to him, drugs available for sale and his suppliers. Cloud’s attorney said he suffered from drug addiction, while supporters cited mental health issues connected to a previous incarceration. The defense asked for a five-year sentence. Prosecutors requested consecutive maximum sentences and presented Cloud’s criminal record from Franklin County. It included aggravated robbery with firearm specifications, burglary, aggravated assault involving a firearm and weapons offenses. It's about $5 cheaper than last year's basket and includes six additional items. "The Holiday Meal Basket has become one of our favorite traditions at Walmart. This year's basket includes a Butterball turkey (selling for 97 cents per pound and estimated at 13.5 lbs), Stove Top stuffing, dinner rolls, and ingredients for other holiday meal staples like sweet potato casserole and pumpkin pie, according to Walmart. The basket will be available in stores, and all of the items can be purchased online with one click. Walmart said the deal will be available through Christmas Eve. items.t: Ohio K9 Sadie receives protective vest through donation
items.x: HARRISON COUNTY, OH (WTRF) — Harrison County Sheriff’s Office K9 Sadie has received a vest designed to protect her from bullets and stab wounds. The vest was donated through Vested Interest in K9s Inc. and sponsored by Amy Leber of Vernon Hills, Illinois. It is embroidered with the message, “In honor of all four-pawed heroes.” Founded in 2009, Vested Interest in K9s is a nonprofit organization that provides protective vests and other assistance to dogs serving law enforcement and related agencies. The custom-fitted vests are made in the United States and certified by the National Institute of Justice. The organization has provided more than 6,677 vests valued at $6.9 million to K9s in all 50 states through private and corporate donations. The program serves certified working dogs that are at least 20 months old. K9s with expired vests may also qualify. An estimated 30,000 law enforcement K9s serve across the country. Each vest is valued at $1,800, weighs an average of 4 to 5 pounds and comes with a five-year warranty. A $1,050 donation sponsors one vest, but the organization accepts tax-deductible donations in any amount. More information is available at vik9s.org or by calling 508

An employee told them the person with a firearm, an adult woman, had already left the scene, according to the incident report. Police spoke to one man, who said he was pepper-sprayed by the woman, and various others claimed they were also impacted by the pepper spray. Medical crews were called to the scene to care for them, and the man was taken to the hospital due to eye pain from the pepper spray, while others were cleared on the scene. One witness told police he was driving in the area with his family when he witnessed a group of people run from a nearby skating rink toward the WRTA bus stop on Walmart property. The witness said he honked his horn at the group "in an attempt to prevent an altercation from starting" when an adult woman in the group pepper-sprayed his face, reports state. Kimbi's plea agreement says that he supported a separatist group in Cameroon known as the Ambazonia Defense Forces (ADF) for more than three years through financial support and acting as an intermediary between ground commanders and individuals who approved purchases for weapons. items.t: Flying taxis could carry passengers by 2030
items.x: (TestMiles) A British aerospace company has demonstrated an electric flying taxi that could eventually offer a new way to escape crowded city roads. The Flying Car Is Moving Beyond Science Fiction Los Angeles has spent decades trying to solve its traffic problems. Freeways expand, transit systems improve, and technology promises more efficient journeys. Yet travelling across the city can still take a remarkable amount of time. A British aerospace company believes part of the solution might be above the roads rather than on them. Vertical Aerospace has demonstrated an electric aircraft capable of taking off vertically, transitioning into conventional forward flight, and landing without a runway. The technology was publicly displayed at the Farnborough International Airshow in Britain, marking an important development in the company's plans to introduce commercial passenger flights. The aircraft is part of a growing category known as electric vertical takeoff and landing, or eVTOL. Unlike a conventional airplane, it does not require a runway for every departure. items.x: OHIO COUNTY, W.Va. (WTRF) Spooky season is in full swing, which means the return of trunk or treating. The Newbridge Church held a massive Trunk or Treat celebration tonight out at Wheeling Park. Hundreds of kids came out in costume to enjoy a wide variety of Halloween fun. The event is put on entirely by the congregation of Newbridge Church. People decorated their cars and handed out 100k pieces of candy that were donated for the kids. Myron Jellison, a pastor at Newbridge, says the Church loves throwing one of the largest trick or treat events in the Ohio Valley. "Just trying to bring the light and shine the light and be a blessing to the families of the Ohio Valley by throwing such a great event. We give away free hot chocolate and free popcorn. We've got carnival games because the line is like an hour wait to get to our trunks, so we love to just let the kids have fun in a safe environment, get a lot of candy, and like I said, just be a blessing and shine a light." Myron Jellison Next Gen Pastor, Newbridge Church We're told about 2,500 people showed up total, with about 1,000 kids enjoying the spooky holiday.

And with construction beginning next door, it allows the bridge to be put on full display to bask in its historical glory. The Director of the Wheeling/Ohio County Convention and Visitors Bureau Frank O’Brien said to have this local monument built by local people is simply remarkable. For 150 years, we've never seen the bridge. You didn't even know that it was there because some kind of building was blocking that. Well, today we’ve knocked that building down. We think people will come to see." Frank O'Brien, Director of the Wheeling/Ohio County Convention and Visitors Bureau The suspension bridge was designated as a U.S. National Historic Landmark back in May of 1975. items.t: Weirton ranks #3, Wheeling #27 as best places to retire in United States
items.x: WEIRTON, W.Va. (WTRF) — Two Ohio Valley cities are among the top 30 places to retire in the United States, according to U.S. News & World Report’s 2027 rankings. Weirton ranked No. 3 in the country, receiving high marks for affordability, retiree taxes and quality of life. Wheeling, known as the Friendly City, ranked No. 27. U.S. News evaluated more than 850 cities and published rankings for the top 250. The rankings considered affordability, health care, quality of life, retiree taxes, the job market and population trends among people ages 55 and older. The weight of each category was based on a survey of people ages 45 and older. Affordability received more weight in the 2027 rankings to reflect concerns about the cost of retirement. Midland, Michigan, remained No. 1 for the second year. Homosassa Springs, Florida, ranked second, followed by Weirton. items.t: Toby Mawer named Sun Belt, national Player of the Week
items.x: Redshirt sophomore goalkeeper Toby Mawer of the West Virginia University men’s soccer team has been named the Sun Belt Defensive Player of the Week as well as the Top Drawer Soccer National Player of the Week. In two games, Mawer made 13 saves while registering two shutouts. He began the week with six saves against UCF in a 3-0 victory before notching a career-high seven saves on the road at Georgia Southern. In the 1-0 win against the Eagles, he saved a penalty and also managed a defense that was down a man for the final 81 minutes of the game. It is the first time in his career that Mawer has taken home conference player of the week honors. It is the third time this season that a Mountaineer has earned Sun Belt weekly honors after senior Pablo Pozos was named Offensive Player of the Week on Sept. 15, and Jacob Redenfors was named Defensive Player of the Week on Sept. 29. Mawer is the first WVU goalkeeper to earn Top Drawer Soccer Player of the Week and the first Mountaineer since Marcus Caldeira on Oct. 24, 2023. The Mountaineers will be back in action on Thursday, Oct. 29, for a contest against Coastal Carolina. Kickoff from Dick Dlesk Soccer Stadium is set for 7 p.m.

items.x: COLUMBUS, Ohio ( WCMH ) – More than four decades ago, Franklin County sheriff’s deputies responded to a complaint about loud music coming from an apartment, where they found the body of 21-year-old Wanda Line. Her death was ruled a homicide. Now, her sister, Jacqueline Line, is hoping to find answers for their aging parents as the Franklin County Sheriff’s Office takes another look at the case. “Somebody lost their life here,” Jacqueline said. “Somebody was murdered and it's been unsolved, and if the person hasn't died yet, there's a killer walking amongst us out there who's gotten away with this for over 42 years, and Wanda's gotten no justice whatsoever – nothing.” North Linden man to face murder charge after girlfriend dies in hospital Jacqueline was a baby when Wanda was killed, so she has no memories of her. But Jacqueline said she has heard from others that Wanda was a kind person with an infectious laugh. “She loved elephants, I do know that, and she loved music,” Jacqueline said. “I know a few little tidbits here and there.” Wanda Line. Shelley Moore Capito joined officials for the ceremony. The 23,173-square-foot building will be set back from the Wheeling Suspension Bridge. Its position is designed to preserve views of the bridge from Main Street, inside the building and outdoor areas. The first phase will connect the Suspension Bridge with the Wheeling Heritage Trail and waterfront. Plans include an elevator tower that will take visitors 40 feet down from the bridge elevation to the trail and riverfront. Crews will also stabilize the hillside, prepare foundations and complete the building enclosure. This phase is expected to take 16 months. Funding comes from federal and state partners, including the Abandoned Mine Land Economic Revitalization program. The West Virginia Department of Environmental Protection manages that funding. Department Secretary Harold Ward attended the ceremony and discussed how the funding will support the hillside work and site infrastructure. Future phases will complete the building’s interior. items.t: Democrats see battleground map expand to South Carolina, Florida, Mississippi
items.x: Democrats are giddy about the possibility of a bigger blue wave than expected in the battle for the Senate as polls show that South Carolina , Florida and Mississippi — three seats that were long seen as safe Republican holds — are now competitive races. Democrats view the Republican candidates running in those states as mediocre political talents who must fight historic headwinds caused by President Trump’s unpopularity, voter anger over inflation and the war in Iran, and burgeoning Democratic voter enthusiasm. The Senate battleground map has steadily expanded throughout the 2026 midterm election cycle as political handicappers have shifted seats that were thought to be in solidly Republican territory — such as Alaska, Iowa, Kansas and Texas — to the “toss-up" category. But now Republicans have to worry about losing Senate seats in states that were unthinkable as realistic Democratic pickup opportunities at the start of the election cycle, most notably South Carolina, which last elected a Democrat, Fritz Hollings, to the Senate in 1998. items.t: DoorDash to buy Instacart in $17 billion grocery delivery deal
items.x: DoorDash is gobbling up Instacart in a $17 billion acquisition that will supercharge its grocery delivery business. DoorDash said the Instacart brand name and app will remain, and Instacart shoppers can continue fulfilling orders for Instacart. Grocers can also choose to work with Instacart or DoorDash. Instacart customers will now have access to 50,000 additional stores covered by DoorDash, the company said. Instacart, founded in 2012, specializes in grocery and convenience store delivery in the U.S. and Canada. Its 600,000 “shoppers” — who are independent contractors — completed 338 million orders last year, according to company filings. Instacart has a market value of $14 billion. DoorDash, founded in San Francisco in 2013, began as a restaurant delivery business but has expanded to pet food and electronics. Operating in 40 countries, it completed more than 3 billion orders last year using a network of 9 million independent delivery workers. It has a market value of $73 billion. DoorDash began delivering groceries in 2020 amid a surge in pandemic-era demand. Grocers were initially cautious. items.t: Recalled butter sold in 10 states receives risk warning: FDA
items.x: NEW JERSEY (WPIX) A popular plant-based butter has been recalled due to yeast, mold and E. coli, and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has now assigned it a risk level. The recall, which was initiated by Prosperity Organic Foods, Inc., headquartered in Boise, Idaho, involves 1,304 cases of Miyoko's Creamery European Style Salted Plant Milk Butter. The FDA assigned the recall as a Class II risk level on Friday, meaning a product may cause “temporary or medically reversible adverse health consequences.” The recall was initially announced Sept. 11. The affected butter, which is perishable and stored refrigerated or frozen, comes in six-packs of 8-ounce units, which can be identified with the following information: UPC 857554005773 Lot number and best-by on SBS carton: 07871, Nov. 5, 2026 Lot number and best-by date on the corrugated case for shipment: 1007871, Nov. 5, 2026 The affected products were also sold in Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Iowa, Illinois, Indiana, Maryland, New Jersey, New Hampshire and Wisconsin.

items.t: Heavy rain washes out portion of Arcadia Lake trail project, delays opening
items.x: EDMOND, Okla. ( KFOR ) A new trail in Edmond that was just weeks away from completion has hit a setback. The Northwest Connector Trail will extend the Arcadia Lake Trail network by 1.8 miles, starting from Midwest Blvd and connecting to the existing Spring Creek Trail. The project was originally expected to be completed in November with a ribbon cutting already planned, but heavy rain earlier this month caused significant damage to an unfinished low-water crossing. "We didn't have the trail in place and I think not having that in there with as much water as we had, it coming around the sides of everything and unfortunately did a lot of damage to this structure," said Rick Howland, Division 4 Urban Construction and Maintenance Engineer, Oklahoma Department of Transportation (ODOT). Howland says the crossing was designed to allow water to flow over the top during periods of heavy rainfall. However, because construction was not complete when the storm hit, rushing water eroded the soil surrounding the structure, leaving portions of the concrete without support and causing them to collapse. items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war , creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle . items.t: Third Times A Charm? Chicken Shack tackles state park restaurant at Lake Murray
items.x: OKLAHOMA CITY ( KFOR ) A popular metro restaurant is expanding. The Chicken Shack will operate a new restaurant at Lake Murray State Park Lodge. The restaurant is expected to open at the end of the year. Chicken Shack owner, Eddy Gochenour said, “Lake Murray is already a place where families come together, spend time outdoors and make memories, so it feels like a natural fit for Chicken Shack.” The Chicken Shack was selected through a competitive bidding process which allowed operators to bid on one or multiple state park locations. The Chicken Shack agreement will operate through October 31, 2027 with the option to renew the contract yearly for the next 4 years. This is the third restaurant to operate at Lake Murray in the past 5 years. The Lookout Kitchen there was closed by the State Department of Tourism after the operator failed to make payments. Before that, Swadley's Foggy Bottom operated in the space. It was shuttered after the state accused operator, Brent Swadley of defrauding the state. He was later convicted and order to pay restitution.

items.t: What to do if poll workers say you aren’t registered to vote

Road to the Midterms: Is Texas in play? Check before you go Check your registration status online before you go to vote and make sure you have the correct address for your polling place. Update your registration If you have recently moved, your registration may still reflect your old address. Ask a poll worker if you can update your registration on site and vote, or if you'll need to go to your old polling place to cast a ballot. Same-day registration Election laws vary by state, but 25 states and the District of Columbia offer some form of same-day registration . items.t: Dolores Huerta, labor leader and activist, dies at 96
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Activist Dolores Huerta, who helped co-found the National Farm Workers Association with César Chavez, has died. She was 96. Huerta's family said in a statement through her foundation that she died Wednesday at home. "We are deeply saddened to announce that our beloved mother, Dolores Huerta, has passed away today at the age of 96," her family said in a statement posted on social media. "As you can imagine, this is an incredibly difficult time for us, and we ask for privacy as we grieve this incredible loss to our family," the statement continued. "We know that many of you around the world share in our mourning, and we will be following up on plans to recognize and celebrate her incredible life and legacy." items.t: 68 dead in high-speed train collision, Spain’s 2nd deadly rail crash this year
items.x: URDA, Spain (AP) — A high-speed train slammed into another that had stopped on the tracks in Spain on Wednesday, killing at least 68 people and injuring dozens in the second deadly rail collision this year. The regional government of Castilla La Mancha confirmed the death toll and said another 58 people were receiving medical treatment at hospitals. Rescue workers searched the wreckage through the day for survivors and bodies. The collision came just nine months after another deadly crash involving high-speed trains operated by the same two companies in southern Spain in January. “Today all of Spain is grieving,” Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said from the crash site, where he announced that his government would declare three days of national mourning. items.t: Flying taxis could carry passengers by 2030
items.x: (TestMiles) A British aerospace company has demonstrated an electric flying taxi that could eventually offer a new way to escape crowded city roads. The Flying Car Is Moving Beyond Science Fiction Los Angeles has spent decades trying to solve its traffic problems. Freeways expand, transit systems improve, and technology promises more efficient journeys. Yet travelling across the city can still take a remarkable amount of time. A British aerospace company believes part of the solution might be above the roads rather than on them. Vertical Aerospace has demonstrated an electric aircraft capable of taking off vertically, transitioning into conventional forward flight, and landing without a runway. The technology was publicly displayed at the Farnborough International Airshow in Britain, marking an important development in the company's plans to introduce commercial passenger flights. The aircraft is part of a growing category known as electric vertical takeoff and landing, or eVTOL. Unlike a conventional airplane, it does not require a runway for every departure. items.t: Caught on camera: Man stashes drugs at an Airbnb
items.x: EDMOND, Okla. (KFOR) — A surprise delivery at an Airbnb leaves a host shocked, guests locked out, and the police stepping in. A man was caught on camera stashing drugs in a grill at an Edmond Airbnb on Friday, and it was all caught on camera. "When I opened that bag, I was in complete shock," said Elise Hobbs, the Airbnb host. Hobbs got an alert on her phone about someone outside the home. "I was sitting in my car doing some work when I got camera notifications going off," said Hobbs. "We allow early check-in at this Airbnb. So I was like, oh, no, are they showing up early? They didn't tell me the house isn't ready." But what she saw next was not the family who rented the house for the weekend. "I'm watching this gentleman who showed up at the house he parked in our driveway, comes to the front door," said Hobbs. "He's looking in. He doesn't try the door handle or anything. And then he starts circling the house, and I was like, okay, well, that's very strange. That's not normal." The man eventually goes back to his car, where he can be seen grabbing a bag, then walking to the back of the house. On camera, he lifts the grill cover and stashes the bag. items.x: OKLAHOMA CITY ( KFOR ) — Our state attorney general has joined 19 other state attorneys general and The Federal Trade Commission in a lawsuit against Dollar General. Oklahoma joins multi-state lawsuit against Dollar General They accuse the retail giant for years of engaging in deceptive pricing practices, knowing about it, and still doing it. Those we spoke with say they were disappointed to hear about the allegations. "That could be very bad, because we don't have a lot of money," said one shopper. "That is why we shop here in the first place." Shoppers at a Dollar General in Oklahoma City weighed in on the lawsuit toward Dollar General. The lawsuit states the store has charged customers more at the register than the prices displayed on shelves, price tags and advertisements. "I pray that is not true," said one shopper. "Why would you do that? You're supposed to be for the people." The complaint alleges Dollar General has, for years, repeatedly mislabeled prices, overcharged consumers, and failed to correct the issue despite knowing about it. items.t: Florida cocaine case exposes alleged Sinaloa cartel route through El Paso
items.x: EL PASO, Texas (Border Report) — Florida authorities announced charges Tuesday against 10 people accused of participating in a Sinaloa cartel-linked cocaine network that used El Paso as a transportation hub for shipments to the Tampa Bay area. Investigators allege the organization moved cocaine from Mexico through El Paso before transporting it across the country in commercial trucks. El Paso police and Homeland Security Investigations assisted Florida detectives, authorities said. Prosecutors described the operation as a Juárez-based branch of the Sinaloa cartel that supplied Florida with monthly cocaine shipments from at least December 2025 through July 2026. Investigators say traffickers used inoperable truck tractors as cover to transport cocaine from El Paso to Florida as part of an alleged Sinaloa cartel-linked network. (Photo: Courtesy of Pinellas County Sheeriff's Office) Authorities identified Jorge Ramiro Zamonsett as an alleged logistics coordinator in El Paso who arranged trucks and accompanying vehicles for the trips to Florida. items.t: OKC approves zoning for first mega-data center
items.x: OKLAHOMA CITY (KFOR) In an Oklahoma City Council Meeting on Tuesday, Beltline Energy won a huge battle in its efforts to build the first mega-data center in Oklahoma City. According to The Oklahoman, the news comes after Beltline Energy agreed to terms which the company's attorney described as the most restrictive, regulated zoning for such a project in city history. Mayor David Holt warned approval of the zoning is not setting a precedent for other data centers and asked that the current moratorium, which expires at the end of 2026, be extended by six months. "How people vote today should not be interpreted as to how they vote in the future," Holt warned. "There won't be anything like this coming again soon." The location of the data center is on both sides of Interstate 40 west of Frisco Road, with 110 acres north of I-40 and 184 acres south of I-40 in far west Oklahoma City. Beltline Energy has already obtained zoning for additional land in Yukon immediately west of the Oklahoma City site.

items.t: Toyota recalls more than 228,000 vehicles over risk of injury
items.x: (NewsNation) — Toyota is recalling more than 228,000 vehicles due to an issue with the second-row seat backs that could increase the risk of injury, according to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration. A notice by NHTSA says if a crash happens, the second-row seat backs may fail to remain secured. According to the notice, around 228,367 vehicles from the Toyota Sienna Hybrid 2022-26 are impacted. Dealers plan to update the supplemental restraint system electronics control unit software. For vehicles equipped with the “Mobility as a Service” package, dealers plan to replace the two second-row seat backs free of charge, according to NHTSA. Owners should expect to receive notification letters in the mail around Dec. 7, according to the notice.

items.t: Can you actually be scared to death? OMRF explains
items.x: OKLAHOMA CITY ( KFOR ) — Halloween is synonymous with spooky, chilling, and frightening events and movies. But could you actually be scared to death? Haunted houses, spirits from beyond the grave, creepy clowns, wild witches, and spooky skeletons can cause terror, or, as Dr. Hal' Scofield explains, it's a rush of adrenaline. "It's what is called the fight-or-flight reaction," said Dr. Scofield, with the Oklahoma Medical Research Foundation. "That causes all that your heart to race. Breathe fast. Sweating. It's all caused by that." In rare cases, all those strong emotions can trigger Takotsubo cardiomyopathy or Broken Heart Syndrome.' The stress temporarily weakens the heart, making it more difficult to pump blood. PHOTOS: OKCFD, OU Police rescue dog stuck in pipe "There are some estimates that maybe up to 5% of all women who are thought to have a heart attack instead have this. No blockage of their arteries in their heart," said Dr. Scofield. The Journal of the American Heart Association found nearly 200,000 diagnosed cases in the US between 2016 and 2020. Transportation Secretary Tim Gatz says heavy highway construction costs have gone up about 60% since 2020. And with that money not going as far as it used to, it could bring challenges. "That's much higher than what the consumer price index has. So it's hit heavy highway construction uniquely," said Gatz. ODOT to replace I-35 bridges, add pedestrian bridge over Oklahoma River Gatz says that in the multiple decades ODOT has been tracking the heavy highway construction cost index, they've never seen a trend like this. Construction costs have risen much faster than the money available to pay for the work, meaning the state can't fix as many miles of road with the same amount of money.
