items.t: Paycom employees donate $35,000 to expand access to service dogs
items.x: OKLAHOMA CITY (KFOR) The Canine Companions' Strategic Growth Fund received a big donation thanks to Paycom employees on Monday. The employees donated $35,000 to the fund. The donation will be used to help expand the organization's footprint nationally, including in Oklahoma through a new prison puppy raising program at the Federal Correctional Institution in El Reno, Oklahoma, puppy raising clubs at the University of Oklahoma and Oklahoma State University, and the expansion of its medical alert dog program. “A service dog can make a meaningful difference in someone’s daily life,” said Tanner Bergman, senior manager of well-being at Paycom. “We’re proud to join our employees in supporting Canine Companions as it expands its programs and helps more people gain greater independence.” Paycom has proudly supported Canine Companions through its employee giving program since 2023.

items.t: OSBI investigates cryptocurrency scam, multiple victims identified
items.x: NORMAN, Okla. ( KFOR ) The Norman Police Department (NPD) says it has requested the assistance of the Oklahoma State Bureau of Investigation (OSBI) regarding a cybercrime scam. NPD says a victim was told there was a transaction on her bank account related to the purchase of Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM). Police say the scammers impersonated bank employees and told the victim she must send them cryptocurrency or authorities would be contacted. OSBI investigates cryptocurrency scam, Image: OSBI's "X" platform Authorities in Norman say the cryptocurrency transactions traced back to multiple victims across Oklahoma, surrounding states and Canada. Investigators say dozens of victims have been identified with reported losses of over $70,000 dollars. OSBI says special agents obtained a warrant and seized more than $581,000 in cryptocurrency stored in the scammers' accounts and are working with the Oklahoma Attorney General's Office to return the stolen funds to the victims. Swift added another honor to her trophy wall with her second hall of fame induction this year and was celebrated at the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame Gala on Monday in a crowded ballroom full of artists, writers and country music elite. “I knew from the time I wrote my first song that even if it couldn’t be my career, it would be my passion," Swift said. items.t: Days will get way shorter in November: How much daylight we’ll lose
items.x: (NEXSTAR) – With daylight saving time coming to an end this weekend , many of us are about to see our latest sunsets until February. In some parts of the country, the last sunset at 6 p.m. or later will happen before our clocks even fall back. Our clocks being set back an hour early Sunday morning will, of course, cause early sunsets. That's the trademark of standard time , shifting sunlight toward the morning and away from the evening. But the natural tilt and orbit of Earth as we glide toward winter are also contributing to days feeling shorter , at least in terms of the sunlight we get to experience. The 3 approaches to daylight saving time considered this year, and what happened to them As part of that, many in the U.S. recently had their final sunset after 6 p.m. until well into 2027. Nashville, Tennessee, saw sunsets shift into the 5 o'clock hour over the weekend, while Providence, Rhode Island, last saw a sunset after 6 p.m. on Oct. 17. New York City and Panama City, Florida, will see their final 6 o'clock sunset on Monday, while Birmingham, Alabama, will make the shift on Tuesday. items.t: Claude AI reportedly bypassed paywall to access Georgia voter data
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — Anthropic’s Claude AI model reportedly accessed publicly available Georgia election data without human authorization, raising fresh questions about AI security and human oversight ahead of the midterm elections. The company told Axios that Claude accessed aggregate vote counts as part of an internal statistics project, bypassing a paywall to retrieve information that Georgia typically makes available for a fee. An Anthropic spokesperson told the outlet that the model didn't access the state’s voter registration system, retrieve individual voter records or alter any voting records. According to The Guardian , Claude exploited a loophole in an older version of the Georgia agency’s website, which issued digital access tokens that allowed users to reach the data. The outlet reported that the model requested a token without being instructed to do so. items.t: Cause of death revealed for ‘Office Space’ actor Richard Riehle: Reports
items.x: (NEXSTAR) – The cause of death for longtime actor Richard Riehle has been revealed, according to reports. The 78-year-old died earlier this month in Los Angeles, friends told TMZ, which was the first to report the news. The outlet and People, citing his death certificate, reported Tuesday that the "Office Space" actor experienced a stroke and had oropharyngeal cancer. He had been in a rehabilitation center at the time of his death in mid-October, according to People. Oropharyngeal cancer, which can be asymptomatic, impacts the middle portion of your throat, including the base of your tongue and the tonsils. While there are multiple types of oropharyngeal cancers, Johns Hopkins Medicine says the majority are squamous cell carcinomas, which are further divided into HPV-related and HPV-unrelated. The former is caused by HPV, while the latter is commonly caused by tobacco or alcohol. Details about Riehle's condition were not released. The Wisconsin native's prolific acting career dates back to the 1970s, though some of his biggest roles happened in the 1990s, including Tom Smykowski in "Office Space" and Charlie Clark in "Casino." 19-year-old sentenced for possessing handgun with a machine gun conversion device
items.x: OKLAHOMA CITY ( KFOR ) A 19-year-old has been sentenced for possessing a handgun with a machine gun conversion device (MCD). According to the United States Department of Justice, 19-year-old Catrayvion Houston was arrested on April 1, 2026, on an outstanding felony warrant. When he was taken into custody, officers found a handgun with an MCD, also known as a switch, that converts semiautomatic weapons into fully automatic. Police also found videos and photos on Houston's phone of him handling the gun. Officials say possessing MCDs violates federal law. On April 20, Houston was charged by Information with unlawful possession of a machine gun. He pleaded guilty on May 11 and admitted he knowingly had a handgun modified by an MCD. Houston was sentenced on October 22 to three years and one month in federal prison, followed by three years of supervised release.

items.t: Democrats see battleground map expand to South Carolina, Florida, Mississippi
items.x: Democrats are giddy about the possibility of a bigger blue wave than expected in the battle for the Senate as polls show that South Carolina , Florida and Mississippi — three seats that were long seen as safe Republican holds — are now competitive races. Democrats view the Republican candidates running in those states as mediocre political talents who must fight historic headwinds caused by President Trump’s unpopularity, voter anger over inflation and the war in Iran, and burgeoning Democratic voter enthusiasm. The Senate battleground map has steadily expanded throughout the 2026 midterm election cycle as political handicappers have shifted seats that were thought to be in solidly Republican territory — such as Alaska, Iowa, Kansas and Texas — to the “toss-up" category. But now Republicans have to worry about losing Senate seats in states that were unthinkable as realistic Democratic pickup opportunities at the start of the election cycle, most notably South Carolina, which last elected a Democrat, Fritz Hollings, to the Senate in 1998. The Madison County Journal reported the 5th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals scheduled oral arguments for November 4, 2026, for Warnock and co-defendant Cleveland Anderson, the former chairman of the Canton Municipal Utilities commission. Former Canton aldermen sentenced for roles in bribery scheme Warnock was sentenced to 144 months in prison on December 10, 2025. He was found guilty on multiple counts of bribery and wire fraud during a federal bribery trial . Warnock was charged with bribery and wire fraud that occurred during his time at Canton Municipal Utilities (CMU) after he was fired by Madison County. He worked at CMU from 2016 to 2017. Rudy Warnock (Courtesy: Forrest County Jail) In his appeal, Warnock argued that the jury instructions were flawed and that payments and perks he gave to Canton officials were lawful gratuities. items.t: Mississippi State looks to return to NCAA Tournament form after slipping a season ago
items.x: Mississippi State (13-19, 5-13 SEC) It’s a “prove it” year in Starkville for coach Chris Jans. He became the head coach ahead of the 2022-23 season and the Bulldogs incrementally improved from there, reaching the First Four that season and the Round of 64 the next two. However, State took a step backward last season, missing March Madness entirely and finishing the year with a losing record. Josh Hubbard has established himself as one of the better shooters in America and one of the better players in the SEC, but the challenge for MSU is finding the cast to support their top producer. Players to watch Hubbard, a senior from Madison, Mississippi, was named by the SEC as a preseason all-conference player. His 22.1 points per game not only led the maroon and white, but were also the second most in the SEC. He did so while averaging three 3-pointers a game last season. His 311 career 3-pointers are already a program record — tied for the ninth most in conference history. items.t: Ole Miss and coach Chris Beard look to bounce back with a transfer-heavy roster
items.x: Mississippi (15-20, 4-14 SEC) With the exception of a strong closing kick in the SEC Tournament, the Rebels suffered through a disappointing 2025-26 season. It was coach Chris Beard’s first losing season in 15 years — one season after a Sweet 16 appearance in the 2025 NCAA Tournament. A transfer-heavy roster and one returning starter never consistently meshed for sustained success. But Beard asserts that a return to postseason tournament play is not out of reach for this revamped team, which is predicted to finish 14th in the 16-team SEC. Players to watch Guard Ilias Kamardine and forward Patton Pinkins return to starting roles. Reserve guard Zach Day had positive moments last season. The remainder of the roster has been overhauled with transfers and freshmen. Kamardine, a combo guard, and Pinkins, with 42 percent accuracy from 3-point range, played well in last season’s surprising surge into the semifinals of the SEC Tournament. The duo combined for more than 20 points per game and must have strong campaigns if Ole Miss is to have a bounce-back season. items.t: AAA advises drivers about daylight saving time
items.x: ( WAVY ) – It's only a few days until we trade one extra hour of sleep for months of darkness as we leave work to drive home. And even though we're on the easier end of the time transition (from daylight saving time to standard time), the switch still takes its toll. Nexstar's WAVY went to AAA Tidewater Virginia to see what commuters can expect. "Well, the biggest thing for drivers will be the change in daylight when we leave work or school," said Holly Dalby with AAA. "At the end of the day, gone will be the bright sunshine, and we will find ourselves either driving into the glare from the setting sun or driving home in the dark. So it's a time to be particularly careful on the roads." While lawmakers have tried to get rid of the time switch altogether, it doesn't appear to be going anywhere anytime soon, so your circadian rhythm will have to dance to a different beat for a while. "It just messing with our sleep schedule can really add to our fatigue very quickly. And when we're fatigued, we can make mistakes," Dalby said. "We can be distracted more easily. Lose focus, inattention. Fatigue has a lot of impact on how we drive. And even though we are gaining an hour, you may find th

items.t: One issue, different bills: Energy costs shape key midterm races
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Higher energy costs have helped make affordability a top issue in the 2026 midterms , but voters aren't all worried about the same bills. Diesel prices are squeezing Midwest farmers , while homeowners in the Northeast face soaring heating oil costs . Others in data center hotspots like Texas and Ohio are worried about their electricity bills . Democrats have tried to tie those issues to President Trump , pointing to the war in Iran and his embrace of AI . As of Wednesday, Decision Desk HQ gave Democrats an 80% chance of winning the House and a 58% chance of controlling the Senate . Some Republicans have called for an end to the Iran war, while others have blamed high prices on Ukraine's war with Russia and Democrats' energy policies. To win the Senate, Democrats will have to break through on Republican turf . Of the Cook Political Report's seven toss-ups , five are in states Trump won by double digits in 2024. items.t: ‘Gut punch’: 2 college students found dead in Colorado after going missing on mountain hike
items.x: ( WJW ) – Two missing Colorado college students were found dead Wednesday after they left campus for a weekend trip up a nearly 14,000-foot peak and encountered a heavy snowstorm, police said. Kaden Matsuda, 19, from Ridgway, Colorado, and Jackson Donlon, 20, from New York, left Colorado Mountain College Leadville’s campus on Friday and didn’t return. They told family and friends they planned to go up Ice Mountain, which requires technical climbing, according to the county sheriff’s office. On Wednesday night, the sheriff's office confirmed that the students were found dead around 3:30 p.m. in a basin of the West Apostle Mountain. Authorities do not believe foul play was involved. The investigation is now being handled by the Chaffee County Coroner’s Office. “Our heart aches for Kaden and Jackson’s family and friends. We are very proud of our team’s efforts to find them before this weekend’s coming storm," Sheriff Andy Rohrich wrote on Facebook. "Although this is a gut punch, our prayers were answered that we would find Kaden and Jackson, allowing some closure for the family. We ask that everyone give time and distance to family members and friends as they mourn their loss.” Kaden

items.t: Cruise ship passenger says warning signs were there long before Cambodia
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — Kit Cassingham and her husband, Randy, sold their home and nearly everything they owned to live aboard a cruise ship for years. Now, she says she doesn't expect to see that money again. Cassingham told NewsNation's Jesse Weber on Wednesday that the couple paid about $370,000 to $380,000 for their cabin on the Villa Vie Odyssey, plus $7,000 a month in expenses. Asked if they will get it back, she said, "No, no, no, no." More than 200 passengers were told Tuesday to leave the Odyssey in Cambodia within hours after the cruise company suspended operations. In a news release , Villa Vie blamed soaring fuel costs tied to the war in Iran, saying the monthly fuel cost per cabin jumped from about $1,800 to as much as $8,000. Villa Vie Odyssey: How did passengers find out they had to leave? Cassingham and her husband had already gotten off the ship for a hotel so they could work online when a short message arrived saying the ship couldn't get more fuel . “You have till two o’clock to get off the ship,” she said. The news wasn't a total shock. “We’d seen red flags all along,” Cassingham said. More than 200 passengers, including Kit Cassingham, were told to leave the Villa Vie

items.t: Wendy’s gets buyout offer while struggling with beef prices and growing competition
items.x: Wendy’s shares jumped more than 14% Wednesday after noted investor Nelson Peltz made an offer to buy the chain, which has been struggling with high beef prices and aging stores. Peltz’s Trian Fund Management and several partners are offering Wendy’s $7.35 per share in cash, or a premium of nearly 19% over the stock’s closing price on Tuesday, in a deal that would take the company private. The offer values Wendy's at $1.4 billion. Wendy's, which is based in Dublin, Ohio, confirmed receipt of the unsolicited proposal in a statement Wednesday and said its board has formed an independent committee to evaluate it. At the end of last year, Wendy's had 5,969 restaurants in the U.S. and 1,428 outlets in 38 countries. Wendy's, founded in 1969 by Dave Thomas and named after his daughter, is known for its square burgers and Frosty desserts. The fast-growing chain introduced the drive-thru window in 1970 and went public in 1976. In the 1980s, as it jockeyed for sales with McDonald's and Burger King, Wendy's launched salad bars and ran its iconic “Where's the beef?” ad campaign. items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: ( The Hill ) Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. Gasoline and energy costs have risen in six of nine months this year, as the Iran war sparked oil price shocks via the Islamic Republic's restrictions on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Persistent inflation , which has remained above the Fed's 2 percent target for five-and-a-half years, spurred central bank officials to hike interest rates by a quarter point in mid-September. items.t: DoorDash to buy Instacart in $17 billion grocery delivery deal
items.x: DoorDash is gobbling up Instacart in a $17 billion acquisition that will supercharge its grocery delivery business. DoorDash said the Instacart brand name and app will remain, and Instacart shoppers can continue fulfilling orders for Instacart. Grocers can also choose to work with Instacart or DoorDash. Instacart customers will now have access to 50,000 additional stores covered by DoorDash, the company said. Instacart, founded in 2012, specializes in grocery and convenience store delivery in the U.S. and Canada. Its 600,000 “shoppers” — who are independent contractors — completed 338 million orders last year, according to company filings. Instacart has a market value of $14 billion. DoorDash, founded in San Francisco in 2013, began as a restaurant delivery business but has expanded to pet food and electronics. Operating in 40 countries, it completed more than 3 billion orders last year using a network of 9 million independent delivery workers. It has a market value of $73 billion. DoorDash began delivering groceries in 2020 amid a surge in pandemic-era demand. Grocers were initially cautious. items.t: RFK Jr. eases access to unproven peptides despite opposition from FDA scientists
items.x: WASHINGTON (AP) — The Trump administration on Wednesday acted to ease access to unproven peptide drugs favored by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr . Food and Drug Administration scientific staffers had little input on the decision and opposed the changes, according to six people familiar with its development. The draft policy posted online by Kennedy’s Department of Health and Human Services covers a handful of injectable peptides promoted within the wellness industry for uses such as building muscle, healing injuries and boosting energy. The government will take comments for two weeks before finalizing the measure. The document, primarily written by officials at HHS, faced overwhelming pushback among FDA drug staffers who warned it could undermine the agency’s long-standing mission of keeping unsafe health products off the U.S. market, according to the people familiar with its development. items.t: Screwworm detected in dog in El Paso County
items.x: EL PASO, Texas (Border Report) The number of active New World screwworm cases rose to 18 on Wednesday, with several counties reporting their first case, including the populous El Paso County, Texas. According to the USDA, the five latest confirmed screwworm cases involved four dogs and a cat. Cochise County, Arizona, reported its first screwworm case on Wednesday, the first in that state. Texas state Rep. Mary Gonzalez, D-El Paso, issued a statement saying the screwworm was detected in a dog in the town of Socorro. She said her office has been in communication with the appropriate state agencies and will continue to monitor the situation. She urged the public to check on their pets and monitor them closely. "It is important that members of our community stay vigilant and go to their veterinarians if they believe their animal may have been impacted," she said. The border county of Luna, New Mexico, also confirmed its first screwworm case in a cow on Monday. The New World screwworm is a parasitic fly that lays eggs in open wounds. items.t: Midterm results could bring brewing student loan battle to a head
items.x: ( The Hill ) Student loan advocates see next week’s midterms as an opportunity for further oversight and potential reversals of policies from the Trump administration that have delayed or denied debt relief and increased monthly payments. Democrats have the potential Tuesday to retake the House and Senate, possibly creating a friendlier environment for student loan borrowers after two years of drastic changes to the system. items.t: Johnson signals he’ll remain atop GOP, scrambling leadership landscape
items.x: Speaker Mike Johnson’s (R-La.) recent hints that he intends to remain GOP leader even if Republicans lose the House have rattled the party’s leadership outlook and raised fresh new questions about the GOP’s future heading into the next Congress. Most House Speakers in recent decades have stepped out of Congress after losing the gavel. And Reps. Steve Scalise (R-La.), the majority leader, and Jim Jordan (R-Ohio), a conservative icon, are both expected to launch bids to lead House Republicans if Democrats flip the chamber, according to GOP lawmakers, aides and strategists. items.t: Obama knocks Trump’s response to Cheesecake Factory jab: ‘These are not serious people’
items.x: ( The Hill ) Former President Obama on Wednesday responded to uproar over a recent campaign trail jab at President Trump’s White House decorations, slamming Republicans for focusing more on the joke than on the economy. “They mobilized a whole-of-government response to that joke, not to inflation, but to that joke,” Obama said during a campaign rally in Georgia. “This is what I mean when I say these are not serious people. They don't have solutions to actual problems, so they'd rather have the media and you talking about the Cheesecake Factory.” Obama had quipped during a recent campaign stop in Cleveland, Ohio, that Trump’s taste in renovations worth a reported $900 million has the White House “looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory, it’s just gold everywhere,” referring to the Iraqi palaces that were famously adorned with gold decor. Trump hit back from the road as he makes his own midterm travel blitz, touting the restaurant chain as a “very successful company” and calling Obama “a lousy president.” “It’s not about money. items.t: Giannis Antetokounmpo has 24 points, 18 rebounds as the Heat beat the Hawks 129-117 for first win
items.x: ATLANTA (AP) — Giannis Antetokounmpo had 24 points and 18 rebounds in his first victory with the Heat, leading Miami over the Atlanta Hawks 129-117 on Wednesday night. Bam Adebayo also had 24 points and grabbed nine rebounds for the Heat, who lost their first four games after acquiring Antetokounmpo from Milwaukee in the offseason. Adebayo passed Udonis Haslem to become the Heat's career leader in rebounds . Andrew Wiggins scored 18 points and Pelle Larsson had 17 points, eight assists and six rebounds for the Heat, who shot 53% from the field and had a whopping 70 points in the paint. Rookie Kingston Flemings and Nickeil Alexander-Walker each scored 23 points for the Hawks, who have dropped three in a row after opening the season with consecutive wins. Jalen Johnson shot just 4 for 12 and finished with 12 points, 11 assists and nine rebounds. The Hawks were playing the first game of a home back-to-back. The start of their game against Cleveland on Thursday was pushed back an hour so that Game 6 of the WNBA Finals between Atlanta and Golden State could be played at State Farm Arena during the afternoon. items.t: Russell Co. deputy arrested after allegedly engaging in ‘inappropriate acts’ with a student
items.x: RUSSELL COUNTY, Ala. ( WRBL ) — A Russell County sheriff's deputy is now behind bars after being charged in what investigators describe as an "inappropriate relationship" with a student. In a press conference Wednesday morning, Russell County Sheriff Heath Taylor stated that 30-year-old Joseph Cooner has been terminated from his role with the Russell County School System and arrested on four charges of a school employee engaging in a sex act with a student under 19. Cooner was assigned to the Russell County Middle School. The victim attended the Russell County High School. Sheriff Taylor says the allegations came as a rumor. A student was able to provide more information that led the sheriffs to the victim and Cooner. "We believe that the evidence will show that in the last month there were four encounters with the deputy and student," Taylor says. Cooner is currently being held at the Tallapoosa County Jail. He appeared in front of a judge Wednesday morning. Cooner was given a total bond amount of $40,000, $10,000 for each charge. items.t: After two-year search, woman’s coworker turns out to be a match for kidney transplant
items.x: SALT LAKE CITY, Utah ( ABC4 ) — Katie Hood and Reina Child became fast friends five years ago when they met as coworkers at Charlie's Produce in Salt Lake City. Then two years ago, Katie, 41, was diagnosed with renal failure. Family, friends and even coworkers began getting tested to see if they were a match. Reina, 47, knew she needed to be tested. And guess what? She is a perfect match. Now, the bond the two ladies share will grow even stronger because on Tuesday they're scheduled for kidney transplant surgery. The women had a pre-operation appointment today ahead of their surgery next Tuesday. "She's an inspiration to so many because even though she's struggling, she's smiles and laughs with you," Reina said about Katie. It all started in October 2024. "I had been really swollen for a while, and it got to the point where walking upstairs was just hard," explained Katie. She decided to go to the doctor, which led to an emergency room visit. That visit changed Katie's life. She was diagnosed with heart and kidney failure. "And I've been doing dialysis for three times a week for two years and yeah, just kind of on this crazy journey." items.t: DOJ’s California ballot fight rejected by another judge
items.x: ( The Hill ) The Trump administration's bid to separate 20,000 mail ballots in California that it says are likely noncitizens met another defeat on Wednesday as a trial judge refused to intervene. U.S. District Judge David Carter ruled California can continue to accept the questioned ballots like any other. “This request violates longstanding constitutional principles mandating that states have control over their elections,” Carter wrote. “If Plaintiff’s last-minute request for relief were granted, either party could create chaos for their own political purposes to disrupt the election process,” he continued. “Over 20,000 registered Californians would potentially lose the right that generations of Americans have fought to preserve.” California has raised eyebrows at the veracity of the administration's list and says it's not obligated to verify voters’ citizenship in response. The state has conceded it's not feasible to segregate a ballot once it's processed. It would be counted even if later found to be fraudulent. items.t: San Diego delays data center after residents – including Lord Farquaad, Elmo – address City Council
items.x: SAN DIEGO ( KSWB/KUSI ) — San Diego City Council and community members – including two in character as "Shrek" s Lord Farquaad and "Sesame Street" s Elmo – weighed in Tuesday morning on a moratorium on developing and expanding artificial intelligence data centers in San Diego. The moratorium is an effort by the city to pause a potential federal plan to convert the Naval Information Warfare Systems Command (NAVWAR) site near Old Town into a 400-megawatt AI data center. The moratorium, which passed unanimously, will temporarily pause the project for 45 days, after which city leaders could vote to extend the moratorium for an additional 10 months and 15 days. items.t: Report: Off-duty border agent allegedly stabs, kills wife
items.x: EL PASO, Texas (Border Report) An off-duty U.S. Border Patrol agent allegedly stabbed and killed his wife early Wednesday morning in Laredo, Texas, according to the Laredo Morning Times. The newspaper reported that Abel Garza, 30, is charged with murder in the death of his wife, 28-year-old Mayra Alejandra Landeros. The newspaper also reported that U.S. Customs and Border Protection confirmed that Garza is a U.S. Border Patrol agent with the Laredo Sector, and that the agency’s Office of Professional Responsibility is reviewing the incident. items.t: Religious, community leaders urge voters to help end hunger in Rio Grande Valley
items.x: McALLEN, Texas (Border Report) The Humanitarian Respite Center in McAllen used to help thousands of migrants who crossed the border during the Biden administration. But since Trump took over it has largely been empty. But on Wednesday dozens of faith-based and community leaders were at the center to speak out against hunger and food insecurities that are plaguing this South Texas border region. And to urge voters to elect leaders who will help. “In this election year Bread for the World is urging people of faith to vote to end hunger," Felipe Salinas of the Christian-based nonprofit group Bread for the World told the group. He says there are too many people in the region who cannot afford food for their families and he believes more public assistance is needed by the government. “It is very much a policy choice because for every meal a food bank or food pantry provides, the federally-funded Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, or SNAP, provides 9. items.t: Cartels recruit legal border crossers to move stolen US vehicles through El Paso, feds say
items.x: EL PASO, Texas (Border Report) — Mexican cartels are recruiting U.S. citizens and others who can legally cross the border to deliver stolen American vehicles through El Paso, supplying criminal organizations with transportation for their operations, federal authorities say. The alleged recruitment strategy emerged during Operation Southbound Takedown, an investigation that has resulted in charges against 13 people and the recovery of 29 vehicles worth approximately $1.14 million. U.S Attorney Justin Simmons said the international ports of entry in El Paso are major crossing points for stolen vehicles from across the country. (Aracely Lazcano/Border Report) Eleven defendants are U.S. citizens. The other two are Mexican citizens — one a lawful permanent resident and the other a border crossing cardholder, according to federal prosecutors. items.t: Mississippi nonprofits face critical funding shortages
items.x: JACKSON, Miss. ( WJTV ) Nonprofits across Mississippi have been facing various challenges, from funding to staffing. Albert Wilson, with the Genesis and Light Center, said that nonprofits throughout the state, particularly ones dealing with childcare, have been in a slump since the COVID-19 pandemic. "Funding is the biggest challenge we have. You know, in our world, we depend on the kindness from people, from state and federal grants," Wilson said. He said that families have relied on the center for more than 30 years, and they have began feeling the affects of these challenges. Wilson said that donations are welcomed, but its voting for proper leadership throughout the state that is critical for the livelihood of many nonprofits throughout Mississippi. items.t: Harris advises Democrats against attempting to impeach Trump
items.x: ( The Hill ) Former Vice President Kamala Harris on Tuesday urged Democrats against making a third attempt to impeach President Trump if they win back the House after next week's midterm elections. "I think that going in the direction of impeachment is not a good idea, just to be honest with you," Harris told MeidasTouch's Aaron Parnas in an interview. "Just because we have limited resources and I think the energy and the resources need to put into accountability, need to be put into investigations." "And that's where the time should be spent," she added. "Remember, I was in the Senate for the last go-around, and the votes aren't there. "So, that's how I feel. items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war , creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle . The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 176 points, or 0.3%, as of 11:45 a.m. Eastern time, and the Nasdaq composite was virtually unchanged. The day’s highlight will likely be what the Federal Reserve says, if anything, about where interest rates are heading. The Fed raised its main interest rate last month for the first time in three years in hopes of slowing the high inflation that’s squeezing the economy and discouraging Americans . items.t: Fish sold in 3 states recalled due to botulism risk
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – A New York company is recalling more than 560 pounds of smoked fish over concerns about potential contamination with a bacterium that can cause life-threatening botulism. Haifa Smoked Fish of Queens, New York, has recalled Cold Smoked Sprats that were distributed in New Jersey, New York and Pennsylvania through retail stores, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration announced this week. Cold-smoked sprats from Haifa Smoked Fish Inc. are pictured in a photo distributed by the Food and Drug Administration. (FDA) The recall was initiated after an FDA inspection revealed that the firm "was producing cold-smoked sprats without required food safety controls to prevent Clostridium botulinum growth and toxin formation." Botulism is a potentially fatal form of food poisoning, the FDA added. It can cause general weakness, dizziness, double vision, trouble with speaking or swallowing, difficulty in breathing, weakness of other muscles, abdominal distension and constipation. Consumers should return the recalled product to the place of purchase for a refund, according to the FDA. They are also urged not to consume the product even if it doesn't look or smell spoiled. items.t: Ole Miss basketball resolves tampering case with no further NCAA penalties
items.x: OXFORD, Miss. (AP) — The NCAA has decided against penalizing Mississippi basketball coach Chris Beard, meaning his program faces no further penalties related to an infractions case involving a former assistant coach who committed tampering violations. Beard “was not personally involved in the violations, was not aware of the impermissible contact and promoted an atmosphere for compliance,” the NCAA announced in a statement Friday. “Thus, the parties agreed that he should not receive any penalties.” The NCAA found that former assistant Wes Flanigan had “impermissible recruiting conversations with the advisor of a student-athlete from another school who had not entered the transfer portal.” The player, who was not identified, subsequently entered the portal but never visited Ole Miss and wound up at another school. The NCAA has accepted penalties that Ole Miss had already agreed to serve in connection with the case during the past two seasons, including two years of probation, a $455,000 fine, a one-week ban on all recruiting communications for the men’s basketball program and a one-week prohibition on prospective player visits. The more than 75 members of the body will have their second meeting debating the resolution and the timing of a vote on it. A motion could be introduced to delay the no-confidence vote and set another meeting. But if that motion is not introduced or fails, members of the Faculty Senate will begin the no-confidence vote after Wednesday's meeting is over, and they typically have a week to cast their choice online. items.t: Sabato’s Crystal Ball moves 16 House races toward Democrats
items.x: ( The Hill ) – Nonpartisan election forecaster Sabato’s Crystal Ball is shifting more than a dozen House races toward Democrats in the final week of the campaign , another sign of a worsening political environment for Republicans. Crystal Ball, a division of the University of Virginia’s Center for Politics, has moved dozens of races toward Democrats in recent weeks, including nearly 50 races in the month of October alone. The race changes include moving a few deep-red seats into the “toss up” column. Open congressional districts in Kentucky and Montana, as well as seats with GOP incumbents in Missouri, Virginia, Colorado and Pennsylvania moved into coin flip territory. Many of the seats Crystal Ball rates as a toss-up were places Trump carried by double digits in 2024. One notable race that moved from toss-up to “leans Democratic” is Texas’s 15th Congressional District, where Rep. Monica de la Cruz (R) is facing a tough challenge from Tejano music star Bobby Pulido (D). Unlike the other South Texas districts where Democrats are trying to hold onto redrawn seats, the 15th is a Republican-held district that Trump won by nearly 20 points in 2024. items.t: Naked Mississippi man held at gunpoint after entering home with stolen fire extinguisher, police say
items.x: BATON ROUGE, La. ( Louisiana First ) — A Mississippi man is accused of stealing a fire extinguisher from a church and then entering a home naked in St. Francisville. Heath Alan Brumfield, 49, of Vicksburg, Mississippi, was charged with simple burglary, simple battery, and unauthorized entry of an inhabited dwelling. The St. Francisville Police Department was called to Royal Street just before 2 a.m. Tuesday, Oct. 20. Police stated that a caller said Brumfield was being held at gunpoint until officers arrived. Officers found Brumfield without clothes on and holding a fire extinguisher. Investigators determined that Brumfield took the fire extinguisher from the church hall at the St. Francisville United Methodist Church. According to police, he entered the home through an unlocked door. Brumfield was evaluated by the coroner and sent for a medical evaluation at Our Lady of the Lake. He was released from their care and booked into the East Baton Rouge Parish Prison as a fugitive before being transported to the West Feliciana Sheriff’s Office Detention Center. The Flying Car Is Moving Beyond Science Fiction Los Angeles has spent decades trying to solve its traffic problems. Freeways expand, transit systems improve, and technology promises more efficient journeys. Yet travelling across the city can still take a remarkable amount of time. A British aerospace company believes part of the solution might be above the roads rather than on them. Vertical Aerospace has demonstrated an electric aircraft capable of taking off vertically, transitioning into conventional forward flight, and landing without a runway. The technology was publicly displayed at the Farnborough International Airshow in Britain, marking an important development in the company's plans to introduce commercial passenger flights. items.t: Democrats see battleground map expand to South Carolina, Florida, Mississippi
items.x: Democrats are giddy about the possibility of a bigger blue wave than expected in the battle for the Senate as polls show that South Carolina , Florida and Mississippi — three seats that were long seen as safe Republican holds — are now competitive races. Democrats view the Republican candidates running in those states as mediocre political talents who must fight historic headwinds caused by President Trump’s unpopularity, voter anger over inflation and the war in Iran, and burgeoning Democratic voter enthusiasm. The Senate battleground map has steadily expanded throughout the 2026 midterm election cycle as political handicappers have shifted seats that were thought to be in solidly Republican territory — such as Alaska, Iowa, Kansas and Texas — to the “toss-up" category. But now Republicans have to worry about losing Senate seats in states that were unthinkable as realistic Democratic pickup opportunities at the start of the election cycle, most notably South Carolina, which last elected a Democrat, Fritz Hollings, to the Senate in 1998. items.t: Dartmouth official resigns over AI use
items.x: ( The Hill ) A top Dartmouth official has resigned from his position after allegations that he violated the school's AI use policy. The university announced Wednesday that Provost Santiago Schnell resigned from his position after a university committee released the results of its investigation into the matter it opened in September. "The Provost used AI to meaningfully alter his writing in violation of at least one publication’s AI use and/or disclosure requirement, failed to disclose his use of AI in clear violation of a national newspaper’s stated policy, was not forthcoming about his AI use, and fell short of the standards set forth by Dartmouth’s Code of Ethical Conduct, the Academic Honor Principle, and Geisel’s Policy on Expectations for Professionalism for Faculty, Non-Faculty Academics, and Staff," the committee concluded. Schnell was accused of using AI to alter his work by the student newspaper The Dartmouth and outlet Semafor, specifically pointing to an opinion piece the provost wrote for The Washington Post. items.t: 2 people hospitalized after 3-vehicle crash involving semi in Greene County
items.x: GREENE COUNTY, Ind. Authorities responded to a serious crash involving three vehicles that resulted in two people being hospitalized in Greene County on Thursday morning. Deputies with the Greene County Sheriff's Department responded around 7:53 a.m. to the intersection of W. State Road 54 and N. County Road 250 West in response to a reported three-vehicle crash. GCSD said preliminary information gathered at the scene indicates that a 2006 semi was waiting to turn left onto County Road 250 W. while a 2023 Kia Sorento was waiting behind it. Deputies believe that a 2011 Dodge Durango reportedly failed to stop, causing it to rear-end the Kia, which subsequently caused the Kia to strike the semi. The drivers of the Dodge Durango and Kia Sorento were transported from the scene to Greene County General Hospital for medical treatment. Officials had to briefly shut down State Road 54 to one lane as the investigation began.

items.t: Could healthy tissue help prevent breast cancer?
items.x: INDIANAPOLIS — Researchers at the Susan G. Komen Tissue Bank at the IU Simon Comprehensive Cancer Center are studying healthy breast tissue in hopes of gaining new insights into how breast cancer develops and how it might one day be prevented. The tissue bank is the only biorepository in the world dedicated to collecting and storing healthy breast tissue from people who have never had breast cancer, according to Dr. Michele Cote, director of the tissue bank. The donated tissue is used by researchers around the world. “It's so critical to understand what is going on in truly normal tissue and to compare it to tissues that have become cancerous, so we understand what the changes are so we can target those changes and maybe prevent the breast cancer from occurring,” Cote said. She continued, “I think moving forward. We as a field, it will change how we look to prevent and treat breast cancer.” The work relies on volunteer donors. “If we want to benefit from the research, we must participate in the research,” said Dr. Kathi Ridley-Merriweather, communications and outreach manager for the tissue bank. It’s all to say thank you to the incredible men and women who have given their all for this country. “I just love how there's a flag for every veteran, a flag for every hero,” said Michelle Schwindler with Sandy Beach Lighting and Design, who helped set up the display. “I think this is just a fabulous dedication. items.t: ‘Gut punch’: 2 college students found dead in Colorado after going missing on mountain hike
items.x: ( WJW ) – Two missing Colorado college students were found dead Wednesday after they left campus for a weekend trip up a nearly 14,000-foot peak and encountered a heavy snowstorm, police said. Kaden Matsuda, 19, from Ridgway, Colorado, and Jackson Donlon, 20, from New York, left Colorado Mountain College Leadville’s campus on Friday and didn’t return. They told family and friends they planned to go up Ice Mountain, which requires technical climbing, according to the county sheriff’s office. On Wednesday night, the sheriff's office confirmed that the students were found dead around 3:30 p.m. in a basin of the West Apostle Mountain. Authorities do not believe foul play was involved. The investigation is now being handled by the Chaffee County Coroner’s Office. “Our heart aches for Kaden and Jackson’s family and friends. We are very proud of our team’s efforts to find them before this weekend’s coming storm," Sheriff Andy Rohrich wrote on Facebook. "Although this is a gut punch, our prayers were answered that we would find Kaden and Jackson, allowing some closure for the family. items.t: AAA advises drivers on daylight saving time
items.x: (WAVY) It's just a few days until we trade one extra hour of sleep for months of darkness as we leave work to drive home. While we're on the easier end of the time transition from daylight saving time to standard time, the switch does take its toll on everyone in some shape or form. 10 On Your Side went to AAA Tidewater to see what commuters can look forward to. "Well, the biggest thing for drivers will be the change in daylight when we leave work or school" said Holly Dalby with AAA, "at the end of the day, gone will be the bright sunshine, and we will find ourselves either driving into the glare from the setting sun or driving home in the dark. So it's a time to be particularly careful on the roads." While lawmakers have tried to get rid of the time switch altogether, it doesn't appear to be going anywhere anytime soon, so you circadian rhythm is going to have to dance to a different beat for a while. "It just messing with our sleep schedule can really add to our fatigue very quickly. And when we're fatigued, we can make mistakes," says Dalby. items.t: Cruise ship passenger says warning signs were there long before Cambodia
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — Kit Cassingham and her husband, Randy, sold their home and nearly everything they owned to live aboard a cruise ship for years. Now, she says she doesn't expect to see that money again. Cassingham told NewsNation's Jesse Weber on Wednesday that the couple paid about $370,000 to $380,000 for their cabin on the Villa Vie Odyssey, plus $7,000 a month in expenses. Asked if they will get it back, she said, "No, no, no, no." Cruise ship suspends voyage over fuel costs, stranding 200 passengers More than 200 passengers were told Tuesday to leave the Odyssey in Cambodia within hours after the cruise company suspended operations. In a news release , Villa Vie blamed soaring fuel costs tied to the war in Iran, saying the monthly fuel cost per cabin jumped from about $1,800 to as much as $8,000. Villa Vie Odyssey: How did passengers find out they had to leave? Cassingham and her husband had already gotten off the ship for a hotel so they could work online when a short message arrived saying the ship couldn't get more fuel . “You have till two o’clock to get off the ship,” she said. items.t: Wendy’s gets buyout offer while struggling with beef prices and growing competition
items.x: Wendy’s shares jumped more than 14% Wednesday after noted investor Nelson Peltz made an offer to buy the chain, which has been struggling with high beef prices and aging stores. Peltz’s Trian Fund Management and several partners are offering Wendy’s $7.35 per share in cash, or a premium of nearly 19% over the stock’s closing price on Tuesday, in a deal that would take the company private. The offer values Wendy's at $1.4 billion. Wendy's, which is based in Dublin, Ohio, confirmed receipt of the unsolicited proposal in a statement Wednesday and said its board has formed an independent committee to evaluate it. At the end of last year, Wendy's had 5,969 restaurants in the U.S. and 1,428 outlets in 38 countries. Wendy's, founded in 1969 by Dave Thomas and named after his daughter, is known for its square burgers and Frosty desserts. The fast-growing chain introduced the drive-thru window in 1970 and went public in 1976. In the 1980s, as it jockeyed for sales with McDonald's and Burger King, Wendy's launched salad bars and ran its iconic “Where's the beef?” ad campaign. items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: ( The Hill ) Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. Gasoline and energy costs have risen in six of nine months this year, as the Iran war sparked oil price shocks via the Islamic Republic's restrictions on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Persistent inflation , which has remained above the Fed's 2 percent target for five-and-a-half years, spurred central bank officials to hike interest rates by a quarter point in mid-September. A survey reported that more than 60% of adults 18-25 reported feeling lonely, impacting their mental health. Healthcare company Two Bridges is now creating a space for college students to make connections and get out of the house. The Future Friends Campus Series travels to campuses across the country, and they tackle loneliness through music. The organization has worked with artists like Alex Warren, Dasha, and Folk singer-songwriter Corey Harper, who will be performing at Indiana University. While the loneliness epidemic is impacting many age groups, experts say college students are in a unique situation of mental overload. Founder Harris Schwartzberg said technology isn't the only thing to blame for the shift. He said today's culture being so divisive is also a major factor in the change. items.t: What to expect when getting a mammogram

Many women are nervous about what to expect, how it'll feel or what may be found. Inside Northwest Radiology Breast Center in Carmel, little touches like the warmed-up gowns make the experience more comfortable. Once in the exam room, it only takes a few minutes. There are four positions in total, and each image only takes a few seconds. (WXIN/WTTV) For many women, the end of the scan is where the hard part begins. Diagnostic Radiologist Dr. Caryn Anderson told Lindy many women get very nervous, especially if they don't get the all-clear right away. items.t: DoorDash to buy Instacart in $17 billion grocery delivery deal
items.x: DoorDash is gobbling up Instacart in a $17 billion acquisition that will supercharge its grocery delivery business. DoorDash said the Instacart brand name and app will remain, and Instacart shoppers can continue fulfilling orders for Instacart. Grocers can also choose to work with Instacart or DoorDash. Instacart customers will now have access to 50,000 additional stores covered by DoorDash, the company said. Instacart, founded in 2012, specializes in grocery and convenience store delivery in the U.S. and Canada. Its 600,000 “shoppers” — who are independent contractors — completed 338 million orders last year, according to company filings. Instacart has a market value of $14 billion. DoorDash, founded in San Francisco in 2013, began as a restaurant delivery business but has expanded to pet food and electronics. Operating in 40 countries, it completed more than 3 billion orders last year using a network of 9 million independent delivery workers. It has a market value of $73 billion. DoorDash began delivering groceries in 2020 amid a surge in pandemic-era demand. Grocers were initially cautious. items.t: RFK Jr. eases access to unproven peptides despite opposition from FDA scientists
items.x: WASHINGTON (AP) — The Trump administration on Wednesday acted to ease access to unproven peptide drugs favored by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr . Food and Drug Administration scientific staffers had little input on the decision and opposed the changes, according to six people familiar with its development. The draft policy posted online by Kennedy’s Department of Health and Human Services covers a handful of injectable peptides promoted within the wellness industry for uses such as building muscle, healing injuries and boosting energy. The government will take comments for two weeks before finalizing the measure. The document, primarily written by officials at HHS, faced overwhelming pushback among FDA drug staffers who warned it could undermine the agency’s long-standing mission of keeping unsafe health products off the U.S. market, according to the people familiar with its development. items.t: IU researchers lead world-first effort to study male breast cancer
items.x: INDIANAPOLIS — Pink ribbons, screening campaigns, and public awareness efforts have made breast cancer a familiar part of the national conversation. At Indiana University, Harikrishna Nakshatri, Ph.D., the Marian J. Morrison Professor of Breast Cancer Research at IU School of Medicine, is studying breast tissue to help scientists better understand the disease’s biology. But for many men, the possibility of developing the disease remains outside their frame of reference. Tony Pottorff noticed a lump in his breast. About a year passed before he sought medical attention. By June 2017, he had stage 4 breast cancer. He died in December 2020 at 49. His wife, Margie Pottorff, wants people to remember the man behind the diagnosis: a high school teacher, a track and cross-country coach, a father of two daughters and the husband who woke her each morning with coffee and a kiss on the forehead. “He was a very gentle, kind, patient soul,” she said. Pottorff’s story highlights a consequential gap in breast cancer awareness. items.t: Mother pleads for accountability 10 years after daughter’s unprosecuted murder
items.x: INDIANAPOLIS A central Indiana mother is calling for police and the public to remember her daughter, Angie Barlow . Barlow would have been 33 years old now. But this week marks 10 years since she disappeared in Indianapolis, later found dead. "She wanted to get out of dancing," Barlow's mother, Christina Kramer, told FOX59/CBS4. "I think she eventually would've had a boyfriend that was worth a damn. I'm just kidding all the ex-boyfriends out there." Kramer is able to laugh and smile imagining what her daughter's life might look like today. Would she be a mother now? Would she be running her own business like she dreamed? Those questions are often eclipsed by the darker ones that haunt her unrelentingly. Angie Barlow/photo provided "Why? Why did you take my daughter? Why did you take her away from us?" Kramer said to FOX59/CBS4 in 2017. She's now spent a decade without an arrest for the murder of her 23-year-old daughter, who disappeared in October 2016. An anonymous tip led police to her body eight grueling months later, buried behind an east side house. "I believe it was handled poorly from the beginning," Kramer said of the investigation. items.t: Man in serious condition after near east side shooting, reported burglary
items.x: INDIANAPOLIS – A man was seriously hurt in a shooting on the near east side of Indianapolis. According to the Indianapolis Metropolitan Police Department, officers received a call about a suspicious person on South Oakland Avenue at 3:34 a.m. Thursday. They didn’t initially find anyone. At 3:40 a.m., they received a report that a person had been shot in the same vicinity. Again, officers didn’t initially locate anyone. A few minutes later, at 3:46 a.m., police saw a man walking near English and Oakland avenues. He was taken to an area hospital in serious condition. IMPD said the man wouldn’t provide police with information about what happened. There were no witnesses to the shooting. Police also received an earlier report of a prowler and said it appeared someone tried to steal copper tubing from an air conditioner at a home in the area. Investigators are seeking witnesses or surveillance video. Anyone with information should call IMPD at 317-327-3475 or Crime Stoppers at 317-262-TIPS (8477).

By this afternoon, southwest winds (7-14 mph) will freshen, as temperatures warm under sun-filled skies. Highs today will reach the upper 70s, close to the record high of 81° set back in 1922. This pattern will hold through Wednesday night, before steadier rain and cooler air invades the region.

items.t: Siakam scores 26; Maxey’s late threes sink Pacers
items.x: INDIANAPOLIS (AP) — Tyrese Maxey scored 27 points, including two 3-pointers in the final 1 1/2 minutes, to lift the Philadelphia 76ers to a 114-109 victory over the Indiana Pacers on Wednesday night. Joel Embiid had 21 points and 11 rebounds for the 76ers, who rebounded from a dismal start to the second half. Jaylen Brown had 20 points and 10 boards, Anfernee Simons scored 20 points off the bench and LeBron James added 13 points and 10 assists. items.t: Hancock County conducts first large-scale training exercise
items.x: HANCOCK COUNTY, Ind. — This week emergency crews in Hancock County are going through their first large-scale training event. The event brought 28 crews from across the county together to test their response to a mass casualty event. The scenario they responded to Wednesday was a mass casualty incident involving a school bus crash with a semi-truck. The first responders dealt with multiple injuries, deaths and the chaos that erupted at the simulated scene. "We'd rather be proactive than reactive and that's what this put us in the first stage for," said EMS chief for Vernon Township Fire Department, Kiely Culberson. All 28 agencies were to work in tandem to make sure the wounded were being cared for. "If we're not all speaking the same language or are on different playing fields there's a big gap. When we have that gap, we have some problems with patient transportation and care," said Culberson. The preparation comes as the population in Hancock County continues to grow. Officials said they needed to be ready to handle anything. The agencies are also testing new technology like Pulsara. This allows first responders to track patients from the scene to the hospital. items.t: DOJ’s California ballot fight rejected by another judge
items.x: ( The Hill ) The Trump administration's bid to separate 20,000 mail ballots in California that it says are likely noncitizens met another defeat on Wednesday as a trial judge refused to intervene. U.S. District Judge David Carter ruled California can continue to accept the questioned ballots like any other. “This request violates longstanding constitutional principles mandating that states have control over their elections,” Carter wrote. “If Plaintiff’s last-minute request for relief were granted, either party could create chaos for their own political purposes to disrupt the election process,” he continued. “Over 20,000 registered Californians would potentially lose the right that generations of Americans have fought to preserve.” California has raised eyebrows at the veracity of the administration's list and says it's not obligated to verify voters’ citizenship in response. The state has conceded it's not feasible to segregate a ballot once it's processed. It would be counted even if later found to be fraudulent. items.t: 2 injured in stabbing incident downtown, suspect in custody
items.x: INDIANAPOLIS— Two men were located downtown with injuries consistent with trauma after a stabbing incident Wednesday. According to the Indianapolis Metropolitan Police Department, officers responded to the intersection of North Pennsylvania Street and East North Street for the report of a person with a knife. Upon arrival Wednesday night, officers located two men with non-life-threatening injuries consistent with trauma. Photo of stabbing scene North Pennsylvania Street and East North Street courtesy of FOX59/CBS4 crew The victims have been reported to be in stable condition. items.t: Marion County election officials detail DOJ’s plan to send monitors to polling sites on Election Day
items.x: INDIANAPOLIS— Wednesday, attorneys with the Marion County Clerk’s Office spoke with representatives from the U.S. Department of Justice’s Civil Rights Division about the DOJ’s plan to send election monitors to Marion County. According to Marion County Clerk Kate Sweeney Bell, up to 12 election monitors in plain clothes will visit the county on Election Day. It is not clear which polling sites the election monitors intend to visit. The monitors are not members of law enforcement and cannot enter polling sites. It is reported that they must stay at least 50 feet away from a polling location’s entrance. “They cannot impede or infringe on any voter who is going in to cast a ballot,” Sweeney Bell said. It is reported that the monitors must stay at least 50 feet away from a polling location’s entrance. items.t: Harris advises Democrats against attempting to impeach Trump
items.x: ( The Hill ) Former Vice President Kamala Harris on Tuesday urged Democrats against making a third attempt to impeach President Trump if they win back the House after next week's midterm elections. "I think that going in the direction of impeachment is not a good idea, just to be honest with you," Harris told MeidasTouch's Aaron Parnas in an interview. "Just because we have limited resources and I think the energy and the resources need to put into accountability, need to be put into investigations." "And that's where the time should be spent," she added. "Remember, I was in the Senate for the last go-around, and the votes aren't there. "So, that's how I feel. But also, I think after the election, we all have to just also agree that our attitude has to be to get stuff done." Harris said Democrats should be "uncompromising" and "not sit around, you know, being genteel about the relationships," but maintain accountability when it comes to cuts to healthcare and oversight on the Iran war. items.x: SPEEDWAY, Ind. — The Town of Speedway is now aiming to take control of the Wilshaw Hotel property via eminent domain. According to a release, the town filed an eminent domain action in Marion County Superior Court on Wednesday. If the court permits the condemnation process on the property to proceed, three independent appraisers will be assigned to assess the site's value and compensable interests. Once the property is evaluated, the Town can pay the county clerk to acquire the site. The Town will likely need to buy the site at the price established by the appraisers. The court can, however, set a different price than the one recommended by the appraisers. In the event the court disagrees with the appraisers' estimates, the price it sets will be the one the Town must buy the property for. The documents filed in court on Wednesday do not automatically transfer the property from its current owner — Wilshaw Hotel LLC — to the Town. The aforementioned eminent domain procedures outlined in Indiana law must be performed before the Town can take control of the site. Wednesday's action was set in motion in March. items.t: Anti-violence initiative expanding target age range to combat youth violence
items.x: INDIANAPOLIS — Starting next year, a national violence reduction initiative is lowering its target age range. TenPoint Coalition currently works with males of color ages 12 to 24, but that range will be lowered to 6 years old starting in January. Pastor Charles Harrison, who serves as board president of Indy’s TenPoint Coalition, said the incoming change has been years in the making following alarming national trends. “Kids are being recruited much younger, nationally, into gangs and into cliques,” Harrison said. “Sometimes these kids, by the time they reach 14 or 15 years old, they become hardened criminals.” Harrison said it’s not just gang violence that’s a concern for younger kids, but also drug trafficking and gun violence. items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war , creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle . items.t: Purdue studies cockroach milk for food-based research
items.x: HENDERSON, Ky. (WEHT) Purdue University is looking into the potential for cockroach milk to create food. Ramaswamy Subramanian is a professor in the Department of Biological Sciences and the Weldon School of Biomedical Engineering at Purdue University. Officials say a cockroach found in Hawaii, called the Pacific beetle cockroach, makes a highly nutritious substance that it feeds to its babies. This substance, dubbed "cockroach milk" by scientists, has twice the number of calories per unit weight as the milk from a water buffalo. Four moon sites identified for future research Officials note this makes cockroach milk one of the most nutritious substances ever discovered. Cockroach milk is densely packed with nutrients and exists in a crystallized form that slowly releases nutrients to the cockroach embryo as needed. Subramanian believes that with modern genetic engineering, cockroach milk could be used to create high-protein bread that could help feed the world or create stable, high-calorie food that could feed astronauts on future journeys to Mars.

The S&P 500 rose 0.2% and pulled within 1% of its all-time high , which was set earlier this month. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 176 points, or 0.3%, as of 11:45 a.m. Eastern time, and the Nasdaq composite was virtually unchanged. The day’s highlight will likely be what the Federal Reserve says, if anything, about where interest rates are heading. The Fed raised its main interest rate last month for the first time in three years in hopes of slowing the high inflation that’s squeezing the economy and discouraging Americans . The widespread expectation on Wall Street is that the Fed will leave the federal funds rate alone at this meeting, and the question is whether it will give hints about what may happen at later meetings. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh, though, has been adamant since taking over the Fed about wanting it to give fewer indications about its future moves. items.x: BOONE COUNTY, Ind. The Boone County Board of Commissioners has delayed a vote to decide whether to proceed with removing the county auditor amid allegations that she leaked the personal information of hundreds of employees. County officials have confirmed their decision to take more time on their final decision to remove Boone County Auditor Debbie Crum, who is accused of releasing sensitive information, including the Social Security numbers of 290 county employees. The decision was made after the commissioners and members of the Boone County Council met on Monday to conduct an executive session before the commissioners met for their separate special meeting. items.t: Democrats see battleground map expand to South Carolina, Florida, Mississippi
items.x: Democrats are giddy about the possibility of a bigger blue wave than expected in the battle for the Senate as polls show that South Carolina , Florida and Mississippi — three seats that were long seen as safe Republican holds — are now competitive races. Democrats view the Republican candidates running in those states as mediocre political talents who must fight historic headwinds caused by President Trump’s unpopularity, voter anger over inflation and the war in Iran, and burgeoning Democratic voter enthusiasm. The Senate battleground map has steadily expanded throughout the 2026 midterm election cycle as political handicappers have shifted seats that were thought to be in solidly Republican territory — such as Alaska, Iowa, Kansas and Texas — to the “toss-up" category. But now Republicans have to worry about losing Senate seats in states that were unthinkable as realistic Democratic pickup opportunities at the start of the election cycle, most notably South Carolina, which last elected a Democrat, Fritz Hollings, to the Senate in 1998. items.t: AAA advises drivers about daylight saving time
items.x: ( WAVY ) – It's only a few days until we trade one extra hour of sleep for months of darkness as we leave work to drive home. And even though we're on the easier end of the time transition (from daylight saving time to standard time), the switch still takes its toll. While lawmakers have tried to get rid of the time switch altogether, it doesn't appear to be going anywhere anytime soon, so your circadian rhythm will have to dance to a different beat for a while. items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: ( The Hill ) Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. Gasoline and energy costs have risen in six of nine months this year, as the Iran war sparked oil price shocks via the Islamic Republic's restrictions on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Persistent inflation , which has remained above the Fed's 2 percent target for five-and-a-half years, spurred central bank officials to hike interest rates by a quarter point in mid-September. items.t: DOJ’s California ballot fight rejected by another judge
items.x: ( The Hill ) The Trump administration's bid to separate 20,000 mail ballots in California that it says are likely noncitizens met another defeat on Wednesday as a trial judge refused to intervene. U.S. District Judge David Carter ruled California can continue to accept the questioned ballots like any other. “This request violates longstanding constitutional principles mandating that states have control over their elections,” Carter wrote. “If Plaintiff’s last-minute request for relief were granted, either party could create chaos for their own political purposes to disrupt the election process,” he continued. “Over 20,000 registered Californians would potentially lose the right that generations of Americans have fought to preserve.” California has raised eyebrows at the veracity of the administration's list and says it's not obligated to verify voters’ citizenship in response. The state has conceded it's not feasible to segregate a ballot once it's processed. It would be counted even if later found to be fraudulent. items.t: Harris advises Democrats against attempting to impeach Trump
items.x: ( The Hill ) Former Vice President Kamala Harris on Tuesday urged Democrats against making a third attempt to impeach President Trump if they win back the House after next week's midterm elections. "I think that going in the direction of impeachment is not a good idea, just to be honest with you," Harris told MeidasTouch's Aaron Parnas in an interview. "Just because we have limited resources and I think the energy and the resources need to put into accountability, need to be put into investigations." "And that's where the time should be spent," she added. "Remember, I was in the Senate for the last go-around, and the votes aren't there. "So, that's how I feel. But also, I think after the election, we all have to just also agree that our attitude has to be to get stuff done." Harris said Democrats should be "uncompromising" and "not sit around, you know, being genteel about the relationships," but maintain accountability when it comes to cuts to healthcare and oversight on the Iran war. items.t: Protect yourself from flu strains this November
items.x: BISMARCK, ( KXNET ) — November is approaching fast, and so is flu season, which can affect everyone in North Dakota. Local health clinics and pharmacies are offering flu vaccinations to protect against the virus. The flu shot is recommended for anyone over six months old. The highest risk for the flu is those under five years old and over 65. NDHHS encourages North Dakotans to learn about lead exposure The vaccine is updated each year to target specific strains of the virus that are expected to be circulating. "Typically, we protect against three strains, and I believe that's the case this year too," Dr. Jordan Barth with Sanford Health said. "One of those is the B strain, specifically. And then there's two different A strains as well." Millions of people receive the flu shot every year in the U.S. Health experts remind those who receive it that people can still get the flu after vaccination. However, flu shots decrease risk and can lessen the severity of the illness. Close Thanks for signing up! Watch for us in your inbox. Emerald ash borer (EAB) is an invasive species of beetle that has killed tens of millions of ash trees in North America since it was found in the continent in 2002. Over the next 4-5 years, the City will be removing about half of the of the ash trees located along boulevards and public rights of way. Trees in worse conditions and those with structural concerns will be prioritized for removal. Zebra mussels found in Lake Sakakawea The remaining trees will be treated with insecticide on a three-year cycle. This is meant to help preserve the canopy and slow tree loss. items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war , creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle . The day’s highlight will likely be what the Federal Reserve says, if anything, about where interest rates are heading. The Fed raised its main interest rate last month for the first time in three years in hopes of slowing the high inflation that’s squeezing the economy and discouraging Americans . Police say all of that data, pictures included, gets deleted after seven days. Councilmember Mike Blessum says he trusts Minot police to use the technology the right way, but he thinks many members of the public have already turned against it. Minot police seek driver in hit-and-run that injured 12-year-old He pointed to a federal case out of Oklahoma.
