items.t: 4 in 10 say personal finances worsening: Survey
items.x: ( The Hill ) Four in 10 Americans say their personal finances are deteriorating, according to a new poll released shortly before November's midterm elections. In the NPR/PBS News/Marist Poll , 40 percent of people said their “personal family finances” have declined in the last 12 months, while 16 percent said the opposite. Forty-one percent said their personal family finances have “stayed about the same” within the prior year. Less than 1 percent of poll respondents were not sure about the state of their personal family finances within the last year, while three percent didn’t give an answer. The NPR/PBS News/Marist Poll was conducted two weeks out from Election Day, with the rise in cost of living being a major concern in this election cycle. September saw an uptick in annual inflation for Americans, with the cost of energy, gas and electricity rising from August to September. Democrats have campaigned on targeting the Trump administration's tariffs and the war in Iran — two factors behind U.S. price hikes. items.t: Police: No stabbing outside of Trump’s Ohio rally
items.x: CHILLCOTHE, Ohio ( WCMH ) Despite social media posts and videos claiming there was a stabbing outside of President Donald Trump's rally at the Shoemaker Center Wednesday in Chillicothe, police stated no such incident occurred. According to Capt. Michael Short of Chillicothe police, a pocketknife got caught in an individuals' shirts during a fight. A viral post on X claimed that a "leftist democrat" stabbed a Trump supporter in the back. "There was no stabbing. The incident involved a fight, which an officer intervened to break up," Short said. "The retention clip securing the officer’s pocketknife became caught in one of the individuals’ shirts during the altercation. The pocketknife did not open." Two people were cited for disorderly conduct after the fight, Short said. No arrests were made. Inside the rally , Trump claimed a heckler was paid $250 to protest while the crowd rang out in chants of "USA". About two dozen protesters were gathered outside of the rally throughout the day and into the evening.

items.x: COLUMBUS, Ohio (WKBN) Ohio and Pennsylvania will share in a $220 million agreement between General Motors and 36 other states over allegations that GM sold consumers' driving behavior and location data to third parties. Ohio will receive just over $8 million, and Pennsylvania will get $8.6 million. The case surrounded GM's Smart Driver Program, which tracks driving habits for safety purposes. Many dealerships were signing customers up for Smart Driver as they were registering them for OnStar location services by using a single sign-up process, Wilson said. items.t: Cruise ship passenger says warning signs were there long before Cambodia
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — Kit Cassingham and her husband, Randy, sold their home and nearly everything they owned to live aboard a cruise ship for years. Now, she says she doesn't expect to see that money again. Cassingham told NewsNation's Jesse Weber on Wednesday that the couple paid about $370,000 to $380,000 for their cabin on the Villa Vie Odyssey, plus $7,000 a month in expenses. Asked if they will get it back, she said, "No, no, no, no." More than 200 passengers were told Tuesday to leave the Odyssey in Cambodia within hours after the cruise company suspended operations. In a news release , Villa Vie blamed soaring fuel costs tied to the war in Iran, saying the monthly fuel cost per cabin jumped from about $1,800 to as much as $8,000. Villa Vie Odyssey: How did passengers find out they had to leave? Cassingham and her husband had already gotten off the ship for a hotel so they could work online when a short message arrived saying the ship couldn't get more fuel . “You have till two o’clock to get off the ship,” she said. The news wasn't a total shock. “We’d seen red flags all along,” Cassingham said. More than 200 passengers, including Kit Cassingham, were told to leave the Villa Vie

items.t: Trumbull County shed builder settles consumer lawsuit with AG
items.x: WARREN, Ohio (WKBN) A shed builder in Trumbull County has entered into an agreement with the Ohio Attorney General's Office to settle a consumer violations lawsuit. The lawsuit was filed in October 2024 in Trumbull County Common Pleas Court by former Attorney General Dave Yost. The agreement that was filed this week establishes that Warren-based Timber Creek Structures owner Timothy Dotson would accept money for sheds and construction and allowed eight weeks or more to elapse without delivering promised goods or services, and failed to provide refunds. In some cases, he implemented excessive liquidation damage clauses and restocking fees, the agreement said. Since the lawsuit was filed, the Attorney General's Office received an additional 200 complaints about the business, alleging that Dotson routinely failed to deliver on time and didn't communicate with customers in a timely manner, the agreement said. Dotson was ordered to pay $104,506 in penalties, fees and restitution to settle the case and ordered to resolve all issues with his clients within 12 months. items.t: Brewers beat the Rays 4-1 to win the World Series

Hey, Milwaukee: grab a brat, raise a beer and prepare for that parade. Young ace Jacob Misiorowski threw 5 2/3 scoreless innings of two-hit ball, rookie Cooper Pratt got two more hits and two RBIs, and the Brewers beat the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 in Game 5 on Wednesday night to set off a long-awaited celebration among thousands of Brewers fans in attendance at Tropicana Field. Misiorowski left the game because of a right calf cramp. He got a standing ovation from the Brew-Crew fans, who took over the section behind Milwaukee's dugout for the last three games. The 22-year-old Pratt set a Series rookie record with six straight hits before a sacrifice fly in the sixth inning. Jackson Chourio set a five-game Series record with 11 hits. The World Series title comes in the 58th season for a franchise that began as the Seattle Pilots in 1969 and moved to Milwaukee the following year. After a year filled with highs and lows, Hubbard managed to secure a spot and will travel to West Geauga on Friday night for a first-round matchup. Head coach Brian Hoffman has been with the Eagles for 20 years, seeing a lot of success, but the opportunity to extend the season never gets old. "This has been an interesting season for us," Hoffman said. "We've had some highs, and we've had some lows. But the team overall has continued to play together. And you know, we have a chance to extend our season." Hoffman also believes his team's ability to stick together through adversity has helped them through the season and will continue to help them play meaningful football. For seniors like Dylan BuCher, the postseason brings an added sense of urgency an urgency to play at a high level for a chance at one more game each week. "I think the driving factor really is just for seniors and play for us. Just play for one another," BuCher said. "Being a senior, I don't want it to be over yet. So, I think just playing for each other."

items.t: Report: Off-duty border agent allegedly stabs, kills wife
items.x: EL PASO, Texas (Border Report) An off-duty U.S. Border Patrol agent allegedly stabbed and killed his wife early Wednesday morning in Laredo, Texas, according to the Laredo Morning Times. The newspaper reported that Abel Garza, 30, is charged with murder in the death of his wife, 28-year-old Mayra Alejandra Landeros. The newspaper also reported that U.S. Customs and Border Protection confirmed that Garza is a U.S. Border Patrol agent with the Laredo Sector, and that the agency’s Office of Professional Responsibility is reviewing the incident.

items.t: How historic is this dry stretch of weather?
items.x: YOUNGSTOWN, Ohio (WKBN) – We are in the midst of dry and quiet weather in the Valley. Our last day of rainfall was on Oct. 16. The only thing that has changed in the past few days is the addition of a few clouds back in the atmosphere. So how unprecedented are these dry days in a row? You may be surprised that the answer is that these strings of dry weather in the Autumn months are not as rare as you think. Wednesday's dry day in the Valley was the 12th day in a row without measurable precipitation. While impressive, there have been longer streaks in Youngstown's history. The longest dry stretch in Youngstown history was 25 days, from September 13, 1922 to October 7, 1922. There were two 23-day stretches of no measurable rainfall in history, in October 1920 and 1924. There were 22 days of dry weather in 1995, but earlier in the year, from Aug. 16 to Sept. 6. items.t: CBP evaluates military ‘heat ray’ for potential use at US-Mexico border
items.x: EL PASO, Texas (Border Report) — U.S. Customs and Border Protection is evaluating a military weapon that creates an intense heating sensation on the skin for potential use along the U.S.-Mexico border, but the agency has not disclosed a testing location or confirmed its deployment in the El Paso region. The weapon, called the Active Denial System and commonly known as a “heat ray,” is designed to repel people by directing an invisible beam of electromagnetic energy at them. The Pentagon authorized a seven-month loan of the system to the Department of Homeland Security beginning in September, according to a memorandum first reported by CNN. The arrangement lets DHS test the equipment and develop procedures for potential border operations. In a statement to Border Report, a CBP spokesperson said: “CBP is continually evaluating new technology, especially technology that can save lives while simultaneously enhancing national security effectiveness.” The statement provided to Border Report did not identify where testing would occur, what circumstances would justify using the weapon, or what safeguards would govern its operation. items.t: Pennsylvania man faces new charges in connection with Halloween attraction assault in Bucks County
items.x: ( WPHL ) – New charges were filed in connection with an alleged serial sexual predator who targeted girls in workplace and domestic settings, the Bucks County District Attorney's Office announced on Tuesday. According to DA Joe Khan, in a press release , Edward Eisenhard's new charges include strangulation and indecent assault of an employee at the Valley of Fear Halloween attraction in Lower Southampton Township, Bucks County, as well as the repeated abuse of a 12-year-old child. “Halloween is the time when we send our little ones out dressed as Dracula and Frankenstein’s monster to Trick-or-Treat, but unfortunately some monsters are real and want to do violence to our children and other loved ones,” said Khan. Eisenhard was initially arrested on Oct. 1 in connection with an aggravated indecent assault reported at a Five Below following an investigation by the Hilltown Township Police Department. According to the DA, after the initial arrest, two more victims came forward, including one whom Eisenhard allegedly assaulted at the Valley of Fear attraction. Eisenhard was a manager at Five Below and worked at the Halloween attraction for 10 seasons while being the victim's supervisor.

items.t: Right-wing activist James O’Keefe charged with unlawful voting, identity theft

Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty announced during a press conference the two men are facing felony unlawful voting and identity fraud charges. “Elections are the bedrock of democracy and their protection is one of our highest priorities,” Moriarty said in a statement . “Individuals engaging in unlawful conduct related to our elections will be held accountable.” On the state’s Aug. 11 primary election day, O’Keefe and Higby donned mock “ Muslim attire ,” spoke in fake accents at Minnesota polling places. The two men filmed their interactions and were attempting to showcase alleged weaknesses associated with a state law that permits Minnesota voters to vouch for people who have recently moved to an area and allow them to cast ballots if they are not yet registered to vote. items.t: Harris advises Democrats against attempting to impeach Trump
items.x: ( The Hill ) Former Vice President Kamala Harris on Tuesday urged Democrats against making a third attempt to impeach President Trump if they win back the House after next week's midterm elections. "I think that going in the direction of impeachment is not a good idea, just to be honest with you," Harris told MeidasTouch's Aaron Parnas in an interview. "Just because we have limited resources and I think the energy and the resources need to put into accountability, need to be put into investigations." "And that's where the time should be spent," she added. "Remember, I was in the Senate for the last go-around, and the votes aren't there. So, that's how I feel. But also, I think after the election, we all have to just also agree that our attitude has to be to get stuff done." Harris said Democrats should be "uncompromising" and "not sit around, you know, being genteel about the relationships," but maintain accountability when it comes to cuts to healthcare and oversight on the Iran war. The former vice president was days into her new role in 2021 when Democratic lawmakers impeached Trump in connection with the Jan. 6 Capitol Hill attack. items.t: Hazmat teams join national training drill
items.x: YOUNGSTOWN, Ohio (WKBN) Hazmat teams suited up Wednesday to take part in a national training. The instruction was part of the International Association of Firefighters training on hazardous materials. The crews train for 80 hours with instructors from some of America's biggest cities on hazmat response. The drills they ran Wednesday were with a chlorine kit that you would find in a wastewater treatment plant and how to safely contain leaking materials. Officials say they are shifting more training from disaster-focused incidents to preparing for technological attacks. "Attacks on certain industries such as water treatment plants—those types of technological disasters may have a component that requires materials response," said Captain Ben Esposito with the Youngstown Fire Department. Esposito says he's never seen this level of interest in being a part of the hazmat team from so many different municipalities. They have 30 local members.

items.t: St. Joseph Warren Hospital ending labor and delivery services
items.x: WARREN, Ohio (WKBN) St. Joseph Warren Hospital will be ending its labor and delivery services in December a move Mercy Health describes as "enhancing maternity care in the Mahoning Valley" by integrating the services with St. Elizabeth Boardman Hospital. "This enhanced model combines the strengths of the region's existing maternity programs and centralizes deliveries at a location equipped with advanced clinical resources, including maternal-fetal medicine specialists and a Level III neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) in partnership with Akron Children's Hospital," a release from Mercy Health states. The release states the decision follows an evaluation of the long-term healthcare needs of the region and ongoing OB-GYN physician workforce challenges affecting healthcare organizations nationwide. "After exploring a variety of options, Mercy Health determined that integrating deliveries at St. Elizabeth Boardman Hospital provides the strongest foundation for sustainable, coordinated maternity care while improving access to specialized resources," the Mercy Health spokesperson stated in the release. items.t: New sidewalk coming to Struthers before Halloween parade
items.x: STRUTHERS, Ohio (WKBN) Work is being done to help kids have a safer Halloween in Struthers. Bigley Landscaping is working to replace 30 concrete sidewalk blocks near the Struthers Elementary School. T C Redimix donated some of the materials. All of the work should be done in time for the school's Halloween parade. "My kids go to the elementary school. Both of them over the last three years—we've watched the parade—the kids are trying to walk around the block, they have masks on, and they trip quite a bit over the uneven sidewalks. We've seen an issue where we can help, and we decided to help." Dallas Bigley is also a Struthers Councilman at-large.

items.t: Trump rallies in Chillicothe, touts Husted, Ramaswamy ahead of Tuesday election
items.x: CHILLICOTHE, Ohio ( WCMH ) President Donald Trump made his third October visit to Ohio on Wednesday night, hosting a midterm rally in Chillicothe in support of Republican candidates, some of whom are struggling in public polling. Trump took the stage at the Shoemaker Center on Ohio University's Chillicothe campus, where he followed Sen. Jon Husted, candidate for governor Vivek Ramaswamy and other speakers. Watch President Trump respond to a protester in the video player above. The midterm is a major election in Ohio, with governor and several state executive offices on the ballot , in addition to a U.S. Senate special election to decide who will complete the term of Trump's vice president, JD Vance. Chillicothe highlights economic struggles in historically red city Husted was appointed to that seat in January 2025 and is being challenged by former Sen. Sherrod Brown. Recent polling has mostly put Brown ahead but within the margin of error . For governor, the race has turned increasingly bitter , with Ramaswamy using the estranged mother of his opponent, Dr. Amy Acton, in a recent attack ad . Trump has supported the move . Election Day is Tuesday, with early voting underway now .

items.t: Hayden Panettiere death ruled accidental by police in South Carolina
items.x: GREENVILLE, S.C. ( WSPA ) – Police in South Carolina have officially closed the investigation into the death of Hayden Panettiere, according to a Wednesday news release. Greenville Police Department officials said that Panettiere's death has been ruled accidental, based on findings in the investigation and the medical examiner's determination. On August 16, Panettiere was found unresponsive in an apartment at the Judson Mill Lofts on Easley Bridge Road. Police said that Brian Hickerson, Panettiere's on-and-off boyfriend, along with his brother, Zach Hickerson, were at the residence. EMS attempted life-saving measures before pronouncing Panettiere dead at 2:31 p.m. According to the Greenville County Coroner's Office, Panettiere had died from an accidental overdose of fentanyl, 4-ANPP, Alprazolam, Methocarbamol and Quetiapine. Panettiere had spoken openly about challenges in her personal life, including emotional scars from her childhood fame, postpartum depression after giving birth to her daughter, and struggles with alcohol addiction. items.t: Judge overseeing Maduro trial dies
items.x: ( The Hill ) Alvin Hellerstein, a longtime federal judge who was set to oversee the criminal trial of deposed Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro, has passed away, according to a court official. He was 92. Nominated by then-President Bill Clinton in 1998, Hellerstein oversaw many high-profile disputes during his nearly three decades on the bench in New York City. He was back in the national limelight presiding over the proceedings for Maduro , who was captured and brought to the U.S. earlier this year over accusations of narco-terrorism. Maduro and his wife were in the judge's courtroom less than two weeks ago to plead not guilty to a new set of criminal charges. Before the Maduro operation, Hellerstein had long clashed with President Donald Trump in court. The judge at one point agreed that Trump’s fixer-turned-foe, Michael Cohen, could be released from prison to home confinement. Cohen has cast his prosecution as retribution by Trump. Separately, Hellerstein repeatedly denied Trump's efforts to move his hush money criminal prosecution into federal court, forcing the president to try his luck in New York's state system. items.t: New pet ‘spaw’ opens in Boardman
items.x: BOARDMAN, Ohio (WKBN) A new chapter began Wednesday for a pet grooming business in Boardman. The location along 1122 Western Reserve Road is now called Blue Ribbon Pet Spaw LLC, and it has new owners. Christine Stacy is one of them. Her family owned Blue Ribbon Motors for many years, and the car lot closed in July. She wanted to carry on the name and her parents' legacy in some way. Her husband learned the previous owners' lease was up at this location, and she took that as a sign to do something for the community. He tells me his idea, I said You're crazy," Stacy said. "He said, We need to do this. You need something, and I think we can make a difference.' We love animals; my parents loved animals. I thought about it for about a day, we jumped online for the name Blue Ribbon Pet Spaw was available I took that as our sign. If there was anything my parents loved as much as that car lot, it was animals." Blue Ribbon Pet Spaw provides services for both dogs and cats. Stacy said she hopes to build relationships with every single customer. It is also a veteran-owned business, and they will be offering a discount to veterans and first responders through the month of November.

items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war , creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle . Warsh said Wednesday he has "started to see some changes" in financial and credit conditions since the Fed raised rates in September. "They have tightened

items.t: Brookfield man pleads guilty to injuring infant
items.x: WARREN, Ohio (WKBN) Sentencing will be at a later date for a Brookfield man who pleaded guilty Wednesday in Trumbull County Common Pleas Court for breaking the ribs of an infant. Daniel Sattler, 26, of Stewart Sharon Road, entered a guilty plea before Judge Sean O'Brien to a charge of child endangering a third-degree felony. A news release from the county prosecutor's office said Sattler was originally charged with felonious assault, a second-degree felony, following an investigation by investigators with the Trumbull County Sheriff's Office. The sheriff's office and Trumbull County Children Services were both involved after a child a little over a month old suffered broken ribs. No other specifics were given. A grand jury indicted Sattler in November. He is presently free on bond. The release said sentencing will take place after a presentence investigation.

items.x: WARREN, Ohio (WKBN) A city man pleaded guilty in Trumbull County Common Pleas Court to his sixth arrest for operating a motor vehicle while under the influence of drugs or alcohol. Sentencing will take place after a presentence investigation for Ryan S. Morris, 42, who entered his plea to the third-degree felony charge before Judge Sean O'Brien. The charge includes repeat offender and vehicle forfeiture specifications. The charge also requires a mandatory prison sentence. The maximum sentence for a third-degree felony is three years. A news release from the county prosecutors office said the latest charge stems from a Jan. 2 traffic stop by troopers with the Southington Barracks of the Ohio State Highway Patrol. Morris refused to take a breath test during that stop also, the release said. The release said Morris has previous convictions July 17, 2024, in common pleas court; Aug. 31, 2023 and March 30, 2022, in Warren Municipal Court; Sept. 15, 2021, in Central District Court; and Feb. 6, 2007, in Warren Municipal Court.

items.t: Mung beans sold in 22 states recalled after glass found
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — Shoppers of Natural Grocers stores, check your mung beans. Vitamin Cottage Natural Food Markets is recalling its organic mung bean products due to the potential presence of glass in its two-pound bulk bags. In a notice posted by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, the company warns of injury, including potential "damage to teeth, laceration of the mouth and throat, or perforation of the intestine." The company issued the recall after receiving customer complaints, though no injuries had been reported as of the Oct. 22 notice. Image courtesy of the U.S. FDA The affected product was sold in clear plastic bags with Natural Grocers labeling in the following states: Arkansas, Arizona, Colorado, Iowa, Idaho, Kansas, Louisiana, Minnesota, Missouri, Montana, North Dakota, Nebraska, New Mexico, Nevada, Oklahoma, Oregon, South Dakota, Texas, Utah, Washington, Wisconsin and Wyoming. The affected lots began shipping on June 10 of this year, and the recalled beans bear the UPC 000080112600. Consumers should immediately stop using the beans and either throw them away or return them for a full refund or credit, the company advises.

items.t: Man gets prison sentence for road rage stabbing in Newton Falls
items.x: WARREN, Ohio (WKBN)—A Newton Falls man was sentenced Wednesday to two years in prison following a guilty plea this summer to stabbing another man in the face during a road rage incident. Joseph Cales, 37, received the sentence from Judge Sean O'Brien following a guilty plea July 23 to a charge of attempted felonious assault, a third-degree felony. Cales is accused of stabbing a man about 11 p.m. April 13 on Newton Drive in Newton Falls in what police called a road rage incident. Cales was on a three-wheel bicycle when he confronted the victim, who was driving a car that Cales said was driving too fast, reports said. The two argued before a fight broke out, reports said. The victim was stabbed in the face during the fight and was later treated at a hospital in Ravenna, reports said. The victim was able to pick Cales out of a photo lineup, and Cales was arrested later by members of the U.S. Marshals Northern Ohio Fugitive Task Force at a home on Newton Falls-Bailey Road. Patty Coller contributed to this report.

items.t: US stocks hold steady as the countdown ticks to a Federal Reserve decision on interest rates
items.x: NEW YORK (AP) — U.S. stocks are drifting Wednesday as the countdown ticks toward this afternoon’s announcement from the Federal Reserve on what it will do with interest rates . The S&P 500 rose 0.2% and pulled within 1% of its all-time high , which was set earlier this month. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 176 points, or 0.3%, as of 11:45 a.m. Eastern time, and the Nasdaq composite was virtually unchanged. The day’s highlight will likely be what the Federal Reserve says, if anything, about where interest rates are heading. The Fed raised its main interest rate last month for the first time in three years in hopes of slowing the high inflation that’s squeezing the economy and discouraging Americans . The widespread expectation on Wall Street is that the Fed will leave the federal funds rate alone at this meeting, and the question is whether it will give hints about what may happen at later meetings. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh, though, has been adamant since taking over the Fed about wanting it to give fewer indications about its future moves. items.t: Ohio Auditor of State’s Office targeted by cyberattack: What to know
items.x: COLUMBUS (WJW) The Ohio Auditor of State's Office was targeted by a cyberattack over the weekend. In a statement shared with FOX 8 News on Tuesday, Ohio Auditor of State Keith Faber confirmed the office's web server was "attacked by overseas cybercriminals and potentially foreign state actors." Once they detected it, the state office quickly "quarantined the threat" and temporarily took the web server and online accounts offline as a precaution, the statement continued. Faber said his team notified state and federal authorities about the attack and is working with them through the investigation. The incident was not a ransomware attack, the statement emphasized. There's also no evidence to believe that Ohioans' financial information was put at risk. The auditor's office said Ohioans shouldn't have to take any extra measures due to the attack. The auditor's office said it will be offering a grace period for audit clients until further notice because they might face issues with online payments at this time. items.t: Fish sold in 3 states recalled due to botulism risk
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – A New York company is recalling more than 560 pounds of smoked fish over concerns about potential contamination with a bacterium that can cause life-threatening botulism. Haifa Smoked Fish of Queens, New York, has recalled Cold Smoked Sprats that were distributed in New Jersey, New York and Pennsylvania through retail stores, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration announced this week. Cold-smoked sprats from Haifa Smoked Fish Inc. are pictured in a photo distributed by the Food and Drug Administration. (FDA) The recall was initiated after an FDA inspection revealed that the firm "was producing cold-smoked sprats without required food safety controls to prevent Clostridium botulinum growth and toxin formation." Botulism is a potentially fatal form of food poisoning, the FDA added. It can cause general weakness, dizziness, double vision, trouble with speaking or swallowing, difficulty in breathing, weakness of other muscles, abdominal distension and constipation. Consumers should return the recalled product to the place of purchase for a refund, according to the FDA. They are also urged not to consume the product even if it doesn't look or smell spoiled. The former Eastern Gateway Community College property is being transformed into a new Mahoning County government center. The plan announced Thursday afternoon by representatives of the Western Reserve Port Authority is to start demolition of the former Eastern Gateway building and the adjoining parking deck on Nov. 30 two days after Youngstown's holiday parade. The entire project, demolition and construction, will take 2 and a half years, with completion expected in the spring of 2029. The Covelli Centre Community room was crowded with people interested in the project. Most of the demolition of the building will be from January to March 2027. The plan is to have minimal work being done during next summer's festival season. But the summer of 2028 will be full construction mode. The term "over-communication" was used in the meeting. items.t: Calumet City mayor suffers minor stroke
items.x: CALUMET CITY, Ill. — Calumet City mayor and Illinois state representative Thaddeus Jones is hospitalized after suffering a minor stroke. According to the city, Jones walked into an emergency room after experiencing physical complications while working from home. Tests determined that Jones suffered a minor strike and he will remain hospitalized over the next few days. Jones is walking, talking and performing light work duties, according to the city. Doctors told him he's expected to make a complete recovery. Jones is also an Illinois state representative and said he has spoken to Illinois Speaker of the House Chris Welch. He's been the subject of controversy this year. WGN Investigates reported that some city council members claim that Jones has misused his municipal credit card. Records show Jones charged tens of thousands of dollars over a two-year span on Uber rides, gas, travel, meals and more. items.t: Democrats see battleground map expand to South Carolina, Florida, Mississippi
items.x: Democrats are giddy about the possibility of a bigger blue wave than expected in the battle for the Senate as polls show that South Carolina , Florida and Mississippi — three seats that were long seen as safe Republican holds — are now competitive races. Democrats view the Republican candidates running in those states as mediocre political talents who must fight historic headwinds caused by President Trump’s unpopularity, voter anger over inflation and the war in Iran, and burgeoning Democratic voter enthusiasm. The Senate battleground map has steadily expanded throughout the 2026 midterm election cycle as political handicappers have shifted seats that were thought to be in solidly Republican territory — such as Alaska, Iowa, Kansas and Texas — to the “toss-up" category. But now Republicans have to worry about losing Senate seats in states that were unthinkable as realistic Democratic pickup opportunities at the start of the election cycle, most notably South Carolina, which last elected a Democrat, Fritz Hollings, to the Senate in 1998. With a focus on expanding in urban areas, Chicago, Boston and Philadelphia will also be home to Whole Foods Market daily shops. The company says its market shops are designed for the customer everyday customer needs and will offer fresh produce as well as grab n go items. The Bears are giving up their 2027 and 2028 first-round picks and a 2027 fourth-round pick. Simmons, who recently turned 29, will be around Halas Hall for the next several years. In June, he signed a 3-year, $105 million extension with the Titans. Simmons, 6'4 and 305 pounds, had 11 sacks last season and 17 tackles for loss. So far in Tennessee, he's had four sacks and six tackles for loss this season. Per analytics from Pro Football Focus, he has the fifth best rating for interior defensive lineman this year for pass rushing and is ranked 16th in run defense. Simmons, since he entered the league in 2019, is second in sacks, tied for first in forced fumbles and second in fumble recoveries among defensive tackles, according to ESPN research. items.x: CHICAGO — Authorities are investigating the death of a baby after a teen girl gave birth at an elementary school on the city's Far South Side on Wednesday, according to a report. The Chicago Sun-Times reported that the 15-year-old girl gave birth around 3 p.m. Wednesday at Aldridge Elementary School, located in the 600 block of East 131st Street in Riverdale. items.t: 14-year-old charged after loaded gun brought to suburban school
items.x: YORKVILLE, Ill. — A 14-year-old is facing several charges after allegedly bringing a loaded gun to Yorkville High School Academy. On Tuesday after 1 p.m., staff at Yorkville High School Academy, which teaches freshman, were alerted by students that a fellow student may have a loaded gun. A staff member separated the student and requested police and security. Both Yorkville High School and the academy were placed on lockdown. The school resource officer and security located a loaded handgun in the student's backpack. The student was taken into custody and is facing the following charges — unlawful possession of a weapon, aggravated unlawful possession of a weapon, possession of a stolen firearm, obstructing a peace officer. "This investigation remains ongoing and additional charges may be filed should evidence indicate further violations. Currently, our investigation indicates that the incident was isolated. We have not identified any evidence of other students being involved, nor have we identified a specific threat directed at other students. We will continue to evaluate all available information as the investigation proceeds," police said.

items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: ( The Hill ) Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. Gasoline and energy costs have risen in six of nine months this year, as the Iran war sparked oil price shocks via the Islamic Republic's restrictions on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Persistent inflation , which has remained above the Fed's 2 percent target for five-and-a-half years, spurred central bank officials to hike interest rates by a quarter point in mid-September. items.t: DoorDash to buy Instacart in $17 billion grocery delivery deal
items.x: DoorDash is gobbling up Instacart in a $17 billion acquisition that will supercharge its grocery delivery business. DoorDash said the Instacart brand name and app will remain, and Instacart shoppers can continue fulfilling orders for Instacart. Grocers can also choose to work with Instacart or DoorDash. Instacart customers will now have access to 50,000 additional stores covered by DoorDash, the company said. Instacart, founded in 2012, specializes in grocery and convenience store delivery in the U.S. and Canada. Its 600,000 “shoppers” — who are independent contractors — completed 338 million orders last year, according to company filings. Instacart has a market value of $14 billion. DoorDash, founded in San Francisco in 2013, began as a restaurant delivery business but has expanded to pet food and electronics. Operating in 40 countries, it completed more than 3 billion orders last year using a network of 9 million independent delivery workers. It has a market value of $73 billion. DoorDash began delivering groceries in 2020 amid a surge in pandemic-era demand. Grocers were initially cautious. items.t: Cruise ship passenger says warning signs were there long before Cambodia
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — Kit Cassingham and her husband, Randy, sold their home and nearly everything they owned to live aboard a cruise ship for years. Now, she says she doesn't expect to see that money again. Cassingham told NewsNation's Jesse Weber on Wednesday that the couple paid about $370,000 to $380,000 for their cabin on the Villa Vie Odyssey, plus $7,000 a month in expenses. Asked if they will get it back, she said, "No, no, no, no." Cruise ship suspends voyage over fuel costs, stranding 200 passengers More than 200 passengers were told Tuesday to leave the Odyssey in Cambodia within hours after the cruise company suspended operations. In a news release , Villa Vie blamed soaring fuel costs tied to the war in Iran, saying the monthly fuel cost per cabin jumped from about $1,800 to as much as $8,000. Villa Vie Odyssey: How did passengers find out they had to leave? Cassingham and her husband had already gotten off the ship for a hotel so they could work online when a short message arrived saying the ship couldn't get more fuel . “You have till two o’clock to get off the ship,” she said. The news wasn't a total shock. “We’d seen red flags all along,” Cassingham said. More than 200

items.t: RFK Jr. eases access to unproven peptides despite opposition from FDA scientists
items.x: WASHINGTON (AP) — The Trump administration on Wednesday acted to ease access to unproven peptide drugs favored by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr . Food and Drug Administration scientific staffers had little input on the decision and opposed the changes, according to six people familiar with its development. The draft policy posted online by Kennedy’s Department of Health and Human Services covers a handful of injectable peptides promoted within the wellness industry for uses such as building muscle, healing injuries and boosting energy. The government will take comments for two weeks before finalizing the measure. The document, primarily written by officials at HHS, faced overwhelming pushback among FDA drug staffers who warned it could undermine the agency’s long-standing mission of keeping unsafe health products off the U.S. market, according to the people familiar with its development. items.t: Disabled veterans claim they lost thousands to contractor
items.x: A group of disabled veterans are sharing their story as a warning to other homeowners. In all, the men claim they lost more than $300,000 to a suburban contractor who they say promised more than he delivered. “At the end by termination, we were out $220,000,” said Rob Schultz, one of the veterans. “We had a garage that leaked, [and] drywall that wasn’t finished,” he said. Two other veterans we interviewed shared similar stories. One paid to update his bathroom. Another paid for a new garage. Both men said they didn’t get what they paid for. “ My job was an abandonment,” said Willie James Forrest. “He never came back.” They men say the contractor was well-known among Lake County’s veteran community. He came to them with good recommendations. But a review of court records, by WGN Investigates, found the contractor also has been accused of wrongdoing in two unrelated lawsuits. When we reached him by phone, the contractor, Daniel Vojacek, denied cheating the veterans and promised to make good. But weeks later, the men were still waiting. Gurnee Police are now investigating. items.t: Harris advises Democrats against attempting to impeach Trump
items.x: ( The Hill ) Former Vice President Kamala Harris on Tuesday urged Democrats against making a third attempt to impeach President Trump if they win back the House after next week's midterm elections. "I think that going in the direction of impeachment is not a good idea, just to be honest with you," Harris told MeidasTouch's Aaron Parnas in an interview. "Just because we have limited resources and I think the energy and the resources need to put into accountability, need to be put into investigations." "And that's where the time should be spent," she added. "Remember, I was in the Senate for the last go-around, and the votes aren't there. "So, that's how I feel. But also, I think after the election, we all have to just also agree that our attitude has to be to get stuff done." Harris said Democrats should be "uncompromising" and "not sit around, you know, being genteel about the relationships," but maintain accountability when it comes to cuts to healthcare and oversight on the Iran war. items.t: Northwestern University research links Chicago tree canopy growth to lower mortality
items.x: The cooling benefit of trees. Turns out they provide more than just beauty. Where there is more shade, there is more life. Whether golden, red, or green, they're especially stunning this time of year. But Harrison Garcia, a Northwestern Medical student and researcher, says it doesn't take a scientist to realize how nice trees are. Still, Garcia and his Northwestern University colleagues examined the urban canopy – the protective leafy layer that helps cool city streets. More Coverage: WGN's Medical Watch "There's been a lot of studies on the urban heat island effects by which concrete can absorb heat and put people under more heat stress," Garcia said. "Between hotter and cooler neighborhoods, neighborhoods that were cooler and had an increase in canopy, had reduced mortality over time." The latest findings that combine satellite measurements and local death records shed light on a critical correlation between trees, temperature and health. items.t: A look inside V. Formusa Foods and its famous giardiniera

The peppers have a little attitude, and so does the family. V. Formusa Foods is home to the popular Marconi brand, where giardiniera has been a family affair for generations. Chicago Pulp brings traditional papermaking to life in South Side basement It started in 1898 with a Sicilian immigrant named Vincent Formusa. He brought Italian foods to Chicago while his son Peter helped build the business. It was Sue Formusa's pops that fine-tuned what is now known as Chicago giardiniera, smaller chopped vegetables packed in oil instead of the traditional vinegar brine. items.x: ( The Hill ) Conservative influencer James O’Keefe was charged in Minnesota Wednesday after he and fellow right-leaning commentator Cam Higby misrepresented themselves at a polling place during the state’s primary election earlier this year. Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty announced during a press conference the two men are facing felony unlawful voting and identity fraud charges. “Elections are the bedrock of democracy and their protection is one of our highest priorities,” Moriarty said in a statement . “Individuals engaging in unlawful conduct related to our elections will be held accountable.” On the state’s Aug. 11 primary election day, O’Keefe and Higby donned mock “ Muslim attire ,” spoke in fake accents at Minnesota polling places. O’Keefe and Higby began the state's unregistered voter vouching process under fake names but did not ultimately sign this oath or cast a vote, according to the county attorney. items.t: Hayden Panettiere death ruled accidental by police in South Carolina
items.x: GREENVILLE, S.C. ( WSPA ) – Police in South Carolina have officially closed the investigation into the death of Hayden Panettiere, according to a Wednesday news release. Greenville Police Department officials said that Panettiere's death has been ruled accidental, based on findings in the investigation and the medical examiner's determination. On August 16, Panettiere was found unresponsive in an apartment at the Judson Mill Lofts on Easley Bridge Road. Police said that Brian Hickerson, Panettiere's on-and-off boyfriend, along with his brother, Zach Hickerson, were at the residence. EMS attempted life-saving measures before pronouncing Panettiere dead at 2:31 p.m. According to the Greenville County Coroner's Office, Panettiere had died from an accidental overdose of fentanyl, 4-ANPP, Alprazolam, Methocarbamol and Quetiapine. Panettiere had spoken openly about challenges in her personal life, including emotional scars from her childhood fame, postpartum depression after giving birth to her daughter, and struggles with alcohol addiction. items.t: Maternity ward at Roseland Hospital faces shutdown in two days
items.x: CHICAGO — The maternity unit at Roseland Hospital is set to be shut down in just a couple of days. Elected leaders, doctors at the hospital, and new and expecting moms held a news conference Wednesday to express their concerns. Not only do they want to keep the maternity unit open, but they also want to pause any additional planned closures across the state. Roseland Hospital's maternity unit closure is not the only one in the Chicagoland area. Three other maternity wards at hospitals owned by Prime Healthcare, say the move comes after many years of financial distress, changes in ownership, and declining birth rates. With few other options on the Far South Side, the company plans to centralize maternal care at just a few designated hospitals, but staff at Roseland Hospital as well as the community have real concerns about that. The maternity ward is set to close October 31. The cuts also include five OB doctors and about 30 nurses here at Roseland. WGN News reached out to Roseland Hospital for comment, but have not yet heard back.

items.t: 21-year-old motorcyclist dead following Elmhurst crash
items.x: ELMHURST, Ill. — A 21-year-old man on a motorcycle died following a crash in Elmhurst Tuesday afternoon. Just before 4:30 p.m., authorities responded to reports of a serious crash at Grand Avenue and Lamont Road. At the scene, police found a box truck and a Honda motorcycle in the roadway. The driver of the motorcycle, a 21-year-old man from Glendale Heights, was pronounced dead at the scene. The road was closed until approximately 10:15 p.m. Police believe the motorcyclist was traveling westbound on Grand Avenue and the box truck was traveling the opposite way when they collided in the intersection. The box truck driver remained at the scene.

items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war , creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle . items.t: US stocks hold steady as the countdown ticks to a Federal Reserve decision on interest rates
items.x: NEW YORK (AP) — U.S. stocks are drifting Wednesday as the countdown ticks toward this afternoon’s announcement from the Federal Reserve on what it will do with interest rates . The S&P 500 rose 0.2% and pulled within 1% of its all-time high , which was set earlier this month. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 176 points, or 0.3%, as of 11:45 a.m. Eastern time, and the Nasdaq composite was virtually unchanged. The day’s highlight will likely be what the Federal Reserve says, if anything, about where interest rates are heading. The Fed raised its main interest rate last month for the first time in three years in hopes of slowing the high inflation that’s squeezing the economy and discouraging Americans . The widespread expectation on Wall Street is that the Fed will leave the federal funds rate alone at this meeting, and the question is whether it will give hints about what may happen at later meetings. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh, though, has been adamant since taking over the Fed about wanting it to give fewer indications about its future moves. items.t: Dolores Huerta, labor leader and activist, dies at 96
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Activist Dolores Huerta, who helped co-found the National Farm Workers Association with César Chavez, has died. She was 96. Huerta's family said in a statement through her foundation that she died Wednesday at home. "We are deeply saddened to announce that our beloved mother, Dolores Huerta, has passed away today at the age of 96," her family said in a statement posted on social media. "As you can imagine, this is an incredibly difficult time for us, and we ask for privacy as we grieve this incredible loss to our family," the statement continued. "We know that many of you around the world share in our mourning, and we will be following up on plans to recognize and celebrate her incredible life and legacy." items.t: Chicago’s REAL ID Supercenter downtown to close in December
items.x: CHICAGO — Chicago's REAL ID Supercenter downtown is set to close by the end of the year after Illinois Secretary of State Alexi Giannoulias announced that it had fulfilled its mission. According to Giannoulias, the supercenter, which served more than 175,000 Illinoisans, has fulfilled its mission of helping people navigate the federal REAL ID deadline and will now close its doors on Dec. 28. Read more: Latest Chicago news and headlines “The REAL ID Supercenter is an example of what government can accomplish when we recognize a challenge and act decisively to put people first,” Giannoulias said. “We faced an extraordinary moment at one of the busiest times in the office’s history and instead of allowing residents to face long lines, confusion and frustration, we developed an innovative and efficient solution that became a model for the nation.” The supercenter will remain open through Dec. 28. and pafdter it closes, employees will be reassigned to other DMV locations The supercenter was opened back in March of 2025 in order to meet the surge in demand for REAL IDs ahead of the enforcement deadline. items.t: ‘Artificial Intimacy: Who We Become When We Talk to Machines’
items.x: If social media came for our attention, artificial intelligence is now coming for our capacity for attachment. Chatbots that speak to us in a human voice offer themselves as best friends, lovers, and psychotherapists, and a growing share of teens and adults now turn to them for companionship and emotional support, many preferring these relationships to human ones. Psychologist Sherry Turkle draws on vivid stories as well as decades of experience as a chronicler and analyst of digital culture to present an urgent warning about what these “perfect” companions are doing to our minds and relationships. items.t: John Kass, longtime Chicago columnist for the Tribune and then his own website, says he’s calling it a career
items.x: EDITOR'S NOTE: The attached video player is from a recent sitdown interview that WGN Political Reporter Tahman Bradley did with John Kass for an episode of The Point. John Kass, the longtime Chicago columnist who once wrote for the Chicago Tribune before starting his own website five years ago, will soon call it a career, according to a column Kass posted on his website Sunday. In the column, titled "Winding Down," the 70-year-old Kass writes that five strokes over the last three years "convinced" him it was time to retire. Citing an interview Kass did with Dan Proft of WIND-AM 560, Tribune media reporter Robert Channick says Kass has a final column planned for Thanksgiving. "I’ve run my race. Now it is time for me to go. Past time," Kass writes in his "Winding Down" column. "I didn’t want to consider it once. I was afraid. I wouldn’t even dare brush up against it." Kass was a fixture on the Tribune's Page 2 for decades after taking over legendary columnist Mike Royko's spot after Royko died in 1997. I'm a constitutional attorney. We're going to follow the Constitution. The Constitution says when a state certifies the election of members of Congress, then they are administered the oath. That's what I'll be doing on January 3 to everybody who's there,” the speaker added. Officials in states throughout the country have recently played defense against election fraud claims from President Trump, with the president doubling down ahead of this year’s midterms. While details surrounding the shooting are currently unclear, officials confirmed that agents were involved in a shooting during court-authorized law enforcement activity in the area. Officials said one subject is dead following the shooting and no agents were injured. Village officials said that FBI agents had responded to the area in order to serve a federal search warrant. "The FBI takes all shooting incidents involving our agents or task force members seriously. In accordance with FBI policy, the shooting incident is under review by the FBI’s Inspection Division. As this is an ongoing matter, we have no further details to provide," an FBI Spokesperson said. Authorities have not yet identified the individual killed.

items.t: Man killed in early-morning crash in Palatine
items.x: PALATINE, Ill. — Authorities say a man is dead following an early-morning crash that unfolded in northwest suburban Palatine on Wednesday. According to Palatine police, the single-vehicle crash occurred near the intersection of East Dundee Road and North Denise Drive at around 4 a.m. Read more: Latest Chicago news and headlines Officers responded to the report of a crash in the area and found a black Nissan Altima that had crashed into a utility pole and a tree near the northeast corner of the intersection. The driver of the Altima, a 19-year-old man from Schaumburg, was pronounced dead on the scene. Officers said a witness later reported seeing the Nissan stopped in the left-turn lane on eastbound Dundee Road at North Hicks Road before it traveled east into the westbound lanes. items.t: Flying taxis could carry passengers by 2030
items.x: (TestMiles) A British aerospace company has demonstrated an electric flying taxi that could eventually offer a new way to escape crowded city roads. The Flying Car Is Moving Beyond Science Fiction Los Angeles has spent decades trying to solve its traffic problems. Freeways expand, transit systems improve, and technology promises more efficient journeys. Yet travelling across the city can still take a remarkable amount of time. A British aerospace company believes part of the solution might be above the roads rather than on them. Vertical Aerospace has demonstrated an electric aircraft capable of taking off vertically, transitioning into conventional forward flight, and landing without a runway. The technology was publicly displayed at the Farnborough International Airshow in Britain, marking an important development in the company's plans to introduce commercial passenger flights. The aircraft is part of a growing category known as electric vertical takeoff and landing, or eVTOL. Unlike a conventional airplane, it does not require a runway for every departure. items.t: Teacher of the Month: Jan O’Neil

"Like every day I walk into gym class, or I just see her in the halls, it always makes me smile because she's always so energetic and happy, nice," seventh grader Momen Omer said. O'Neil has been a fixture at her school for 26 years, building relationships that last long after students leave the gym. "She's like a second mother to me. When they make mistakes, she doesn't give up on them, but she helps them get it right. As the school softball coach, she's built teams that feel more like family. "I can go to her for anything, and she's not only a great PE teacher, she's a great coach," seventh grader Emma Tsiaims said. items.t: Instagram now testing videos up to 90 minutes long in major shift
items.x: ( KTLA ) Instagram is moving beyond its signature short-form videos, testing a new feature that allows creators to share content lasting up to 90 minutes, including podcasts, interviews and comedy shows. The Meta-owned platform announced Monday that it is testing a feature called "Features," which allows select creators to upload longer, horizontal videos that viewers can watch directly within the app. "For a long time, I have been against doing long-form video on Instagram," Instagram head Adam Mosseri said in a video posted Monday alongside Tessa Lyons, the company's vice president of product. "But we are actually gonna lean in for a bunch of different reasons." Lyons, who previously led product development for Instagram Reels, described the expansion as a new chapter for the platform. "It feels like a full-circle moment that we're here now talking about the beginning of our journey on long-form video," she said. items.t: Loyola’s Youth Climate Justice Summit educates local students on how to impact climate change
items.x: CHICAGO ( WGN ) — The Youth Climate Justice Summit (YCJS) brought together over 100 students from 30 area high schools to Loyola University Chicago's School of Environmental Sustainability to answer one simple question. How do we move beyond talks to actually implement better ways to live? "I think the summit, it’s an amazing opportunity for us kids to stand and get educational opportunities as well," said Ari Nsiah, a senior at King College Prep. "Students can discover, I would say, new pathways that they didn’t know about when they hear from adults who are currently working in a variety of fields related to climate change." The United Nations defines climate change as long term shifts in global temperatures, which lead to extreme weather — like flooding, blizzards or excessive heat. And while the Earth's climate has changed naturally over the years, modern climate change is happening at an unprecedented rate, and it's caused by human behavior. "I think climate change is something that affects each and every one of us," said Shivaani Sivaraman, a student at Adlai E. Stevenson High School. items.t: 4 in 10 say personal finances worsening: Survey
items.x: ( The Hill ) Four in 10 Americans say their personal finances are deteriorating, according to a new poll released shortly before November's midterm elections. In the NPR/PBS News/Marist Poll , 40 percent of people said their “personal family finances” have declined in the last 12 months, while 16 percent said the opposite. Forty-one percent said their personal family finances have “stayed about the same” within the prior year. Less than 1 percent of poll respondents were not sure about the state of their personal family finances within the last year, while three percent didn’t give an answer. The NPR/PBS News/Marist Poll was conducted two weeks out from Election Day, with the rise in cost of living being a major concern in this election cycle. September saw an uptick in annual inflation for Americans, with the cost of energy, gas and electricity rising from August to September. Democrats have campaigned on targeting the Trump administration's tariffs and the war in Iran — two factors behind U.S. price hikes. items.t: Democrats see battleground map expand to South Carolina, Florida, Mississippi
items.x: Democrats are giddy about the possibility of a bigger blue wave than expected in the battle for the Senate as polls show that South Carolina , Florida and Mississippi — three seats that were long seen as safe Republican holds — are now competitive races. Democrats view the Republican candidates running in those states as mediocre political talents who must fight historic headwinds caused by President Trump’s unpopularity, voter anger over inflation and the war in Iran, and burgeoning Democratic voter enthusiasm. The Senate battleground map has steadily expanded throughout the 2026 midterm election cycle as political handicappers have shifted seats that were thought to be in solidly Republican territory — such as Alaska, Iowa, Kansas and Texas — to the “toss-up" category. But now Republicans have to worry about losing Senate seats in states that were unthinkable as realistic Democratic pickup opportunities at the start of the election cycle, most notably South Carolina, which last elected a Democrat, Fritz Hollings, to the Senate in 1998. items.x: ( The Hill ) A top Dartmouth official has resigned from his position after allegations that he violated the school's AI use policy. The university announced Wednesday that Provost Santiago Schnell resigned from his position after a university committee released the results of its investigation into the matter it opened in September. "The Provost used AI to meaningfully alter his writing in violation of at least one publication’s AI use and/or disclosure requirement, failed to disclose his use of AI in clear violation of a national newspaper’s stated policy, was not forthcoming about his AI use, and fell short of the standards set forth by Dartmouth’s Code of Ethical Conduct, the Academic Honor Principle, and Geisel’s Policy on Expectations for Professionalism for Faculty, Non-Faculty Academics, and Staff," the committee concluded. Schnell was accused of using AI to alter his work by the student newspaper The Dartmouth and outlet Semafor, specifically pointing to an opinion piece the provost wrote for The Washington Post. According to a press release from the West Virginia Senate, the teens attended the Huntington High School Prom in 2005 before they were shot and killed later that night in front of a Huntington residence. The victims were Megan Poston, 16; Michael Dillon, 17; Eddrick Clark, 18; and Donté Ward, 19. items.t: AAA advises drivers about daylight saving time
items.x: ( WAVY ) – It's only a few days until we trade one extra hour of sleep for months of darkness as we leave work to drive home. And even though we're on the easier end of the time transition (from daylight saving time to standard time), the switch still takes its toll. Nexstar's WAVY went to AAA Tidewater Virginia to see what commuters can expect. "Well, the biggest thing for drivers will be the change in daylight when we leave work or school," said Holly Dalby with AAA. "At the end of the day, gone will be the bright sunshine, and we will find ourselves either driving into the glare from the setting sun or driving home in the dark. So it's a time to be particularly careful on the roads." Days will get way shorter in November: How much daylight will we lose? While lawmakers have tried to get rid of the time switch altogether, it doesn't appear to be going anywhere anytime soon, so your circadian rhythm will have to dance to a different beat for a while. "It just messing with our sleep schedule can really add to our fatigue very quickly. And when we're fatigued, we can make mistakes," Dalby said. Kaden Matsuda, 19, from Ridgway, Colorado, and Jackson Donlon, 20, from New York, left Colorado Mountain College Leadville’s campus on Friday and didn’t return. They told family and friends they planned to go up Ice Mountain, which requires technical climbing, according to the county sheriff’s office. On Wednesday night, the sheriff's office confirmed that the students were found dead around 3:30 p.m. in a basin of the West Apostle Mountain. Authorities do not believe foul play was involved. The investigation is now being handled by the Chaffee County Coroner’s Office. “Our heart aches for Kaden and Jackson’s family and friends. items.t: Wendy’s gets buyout offer while struggling with beef prices and growing competition
items.x: Wendy’s shares jumped more than 14% Wednesday after noted investor Nelson Peltz made an offer to buy the chain, which has been struggling with high beef prices and aging stores. Peltz’s Trian Fund Management and several partners are offering Wendy’s $7.35 per share in cash, or a premium of nearly 19% over the stock’s closing price on Tuesday, in a deal that would take the company private. The offer values Wendy's at $1.4 billion. Wendy's, which is based in Dublin, Ohio, confirmed receipt of the unsolicited proposal in a statement Wednesday and said its board has formed an independent committee to evaluate it. At the end of last year, Wendy's had 5,969 restaurants in the U.S. and 1,428 outlets in 38 countries. Wendy's, founded in 1969 by Dave Thomas and named after his daughter, is known for its square burgers and Frosty desserts. The fast-growing chain introduced the drive-thru window in 1970 and went public in 1976. In the 1980s, as it jockeyed for sales with McDonald's and Burger King, Wendy's launched salad bars and ran its iconic “Where's the beef?” ad campaign. items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: ( The Hill ) Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. Gasoline and energy costs have risen in six of nine months this year, as the Iran war sparked oil price shocks via the Islamic Republic's restrictions on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Persistent inflation , which has remained above the Fed's 2 percent target for five-and-a-half years, spurred central bank officials to hike interest rates by a quarter point in mid-September. items.t: DoorDash to buy Instacart in $17 billion grocery delivery deal
items.x: DoorDash is gobbling up Instacart in a $17 billion acquisition that will supercharge its grocery delivery business. DoorDash said the Instacart brand name and app will remain, and Instacart shoppers can continue fulfilling orders for Instacart. Grocers can also choose to work with Instacart or DoorDash. Instacart customers will now have access to 50,000 additional stores covered by DoorDash, the company said. Instacart, founded in 2012, specializes in grocery and convenience store delivery in the U.S. and Canada. Its 600,000 “shoppers” — who are independent contractors — completed 338 million orders last year, according to company filings. Instacart has a market value of $14 billion. DoorDash, founded in San Francisco in 2013, began as a restaurant delivery business but has expanded to pet food and electronics. Operating in 40 countries, it completed more than 3 billion orders last year using a network of 9 million independent delivery workers. It has a market value of $73 billion. DoorDash began delivering groceries in 2020 amid a surge in pandemic-era demand. Grocers were initially cautious. items.t: RFK Jr. eases access to unproven peptides despite opposition from FDA scientists
items.x: WASHINGTON (AP) — The Trump administration on Wednesday acted to ease access to unproven peptide drugs favored by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr . Food and Drug Administration scientific staffers had little input on the decision and opposed the changes, according to six people familiar with its development. The draft policy posted online by Kennedy’s Department of Health and Human Services covers a handful of injectable peptides promoted within the wellness industry for uses such as building muscle, healing injuries and boosting energy. The government will take comments for two weeks before finalizing the measure. The document, primarily written by officials at HHS, faced overwhelming pushback among FDA drug staffers who warned it could undermine the agency’s long-standing mission of keeping unsafe health products off the U.S. market, according to the people familiar with its development. items.t: DOJ’s California ballot fight rejected by another judge
items.x: ( The Hill ) The Trump administration's bid to separate 20,000 mail ballots in California that it says are likely noncitizens met another defeat on Wednesday as a trial judge refused to intervene. U.S. District Judge David Carter ruled California can continue to accept the questioned ballots like any other. “This request violates longstanding constitutional principles mandating that states have control over their elections,” Carter wrote. “If Plaintiff’s last-minute request for relief were granted, either party could create chaos for their own political purposes to disrupt the election process,” he continued. “Over 20,000 registered Californians would potentially lose the right that generations of Americans have fought to preserve.” California has raised eyebrows at the veracity of the administration's list and says it's not obligated to verify voters’ citizenship in response. The state has conceded it's not feasible to segregate a ballot once it's processed. It would be counted even if later found to be fraudulent. items.t: Mercer County Animal Shelter asking for donations of blankets
items.x: PRINCETON, WV (WVNS) As we creep closer to winter, we are all probably thinking about staying warm with our heat inside and thick coats for braving the elements. But what about our furry friends? Mercer County Animal Shelter seeks help getting blankets Yes, they have fur to keep them warm, but when temperatures drop to freezing conditions, the animals in shelters need some help. That is where donations of throw blankets come in. Stacey Harmon, the Director of the Mercer County Animal Shelter, said blankets are a vital item the shelter needs for the wintertime. "We usually do like a double layer in the wintertime. And of course, the dogs, a lot of them like to play with the blankets and they rip them up, so we're running short on them," said Harmon. Harmon said the shelter does have a good heat source, but giving the dogs blankets helps keep them that much warmer. She said they keep certain doors open at the shelter to ensure the dogs have fresh air. However, the colder air does slip through, so blankets are crucial for them.

items.t: Harris advises Democrats against attempting to impeach Trump
items.x: ( The Hill ) Former Vice President Kamala Harris on Tuesday urged Democrats against making a third attempt to impeach President Trump if they win back the House after next week's midterm elections. "I think that going in the direction of impeachment is not a good idea, just to be honest with you," Harris told MeidasTouch's Aaron Parnas in an interview. "Just because we have limited resources and I think the energy and the resources need to put into accountability, need to be put into investigations." "And that's where the time should be spent," she added. "Remember, I was in the Senate for the last go-around, and the votes aren't there. "So, that's how I feel. But also, I think after the election, we all have to just also agree that our attitude has to be to get stuff done." Harris said Democrats should be "uncompromising" and "not sit around, you know, being genteel about the relationships," but maintain accountability when it comes to cuts to healthcare and oversight on the Iran war. Panettiere had spoken openly about challenges in her personal life, including emotional scars from her childhood fame, postpartum depression after giving birth to her daughter, and struggles with alcohol addiction. items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war , creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle . items.t: Why does the DNR stock trout every fall?
items.x: GHENT, WV (WVNS) As fall trout stocking continues, we are taking a look at why it is so important that it happens annually. West Virginia trout stocking locations for October 26 Every October, for two weeks, the West Virginia Department of Natural Resources stocks dozens of lakes, ponds, rivers, and streams with trout. And the reasoning behind these stockings is very simple. Frank Williams, Interim Hatchery Program Manager for the DNR, said it is to provide one last recreational opportunity for folks in the Mountain State. "It's an additional recreational opportunity for the anglers. It's the time of year when the water temperatures are starting to cool down and right before our deer seasons pick up. So, it's creating another recreational opportunity for the anglers," said Williams. Williams said the DNR stocks bodies of water across the state but mostly in the northern and southern parts of the state, as well as the eastern panhandle. He said they do not stock very many waterways in the western part of the state because there are fewer cold-water streams in that area.

Police advised parents and their kids to stick to neighborhoods with which they are familiar. Fall colors continue to spread across the Mountain State ahead of Halloween Adam Justice, a Corporal with the Beckley Police Department, told 59News you should always trust your gut, and it is always a good idea to have an adult present for trick-or-treaters of all ages. "I would just trust your instincts, if you think a house may be unsafe, usually if folks don't want you trick or treating at their place the porch lights will be turned off so that's typically a sign of a house to avoid. If there's any house with their lights off and no outside lights on. It would probably be a good idea to avoid those residences," said Justice. Justice told 59News it is best to avoid dark side roads, and keep your children within eyesight at all times.

Kirkpatrick was suspended for the latter half of the 2025 season after his arrest on three counts of reckless endangerment and one count of attempting to elude and speeding. items.t: AAA says drivers and pedestrians need to be alert on Halloween Night
items.x: BECKLEY, WV (WVNS) With foot traffic expected to be heavy on Halloween Night 2026, AAA urged drivers to watch the road for children. Lori Weaver-Hawkins, a Public Affairs Manager for AAA told 59News drivers will need to pay attention to the road for pedestrians that will be out celebrating. Fall colors continue to spread across the Mountain State ahead of Halloween She said when driving in a residential area it is always best to drive under the speed limit, and it is especially important on Halloween. She added that it is a good idea to keep your car lights on during the evening, so pedestrians know you are coming. "[Kids] might get so excited moving on to the next house for some more candy that they forget to cross the road safely or they be running about and step off the sidewalk into the roadway, so drivers need to slow down, put those distractions like your phone and everything else away. items.t: Instagram now testing videos up to 90 minutes long in major shift
items.x: ( KTLA ) Instagram is moving beyond its signature short-form videos, testing a new feature that allows creators to share content lasting up to 90 minutes, including podcasts, interviews and comedy shows. The Meta-owned platform announced Monday that it is testing a feature called "Features," which allows select creators to upload longer, horizontal videos that viewers can watch directly within the app. "For a long time, I have been against doing long-form video on Instagram," Instagram head Adam Mosseri said in a video posted Monday alongside Tessa Lyons, the company's vice president of product. "But we are actually gonna lean in for a bunch of different reasons." Lyons, who previously led product development for Instagram Reels, described the expansion as a new chapter for the platform. "It feels like a full-circle moment that we're here now talking about the beginning of our journey on long-form video," she said.
