items.t: Utah authorities connect 1974 cold case to serial killer Ted Bundy
items.x: SUMMIT COUNTY, Utah ( KTVX ) — Investigators in Summit County, Utah closed the 1974 cold case homicide of Melissa Ann Smith Tuesday, linking her murder to prominent serial killer Ted Bundy. Using DNA and other evidence, the Summit County Sheriff's Office and Summit County Attorney's Office formally closed the cold-case murder, saying that the evidence conclusively proves that Ted Bundy murdered 17-year-old Melissa Ann Smith. Bundy has long been considered a suspect in several cold cases in Utah, and Smith's murder was one of them. Hunters found her remains in Summit County on Oct. 27, 1974, 52 years ago today. "The work began with the investigators who handled the case in 1974, and it continued through the dedication and perseverance of those who carried it forward," Summit County Sheriff Kacey Bates said. "After 50 years, we have reached a point that so many have worked toward." items.t: 4 in 10 say personal finances worsening: Survey
items.x: ( The Hill ) Four in 10 Americans say their personal finances are deteriorating, according to a new poll released shortly before November's midterm elections. In the NPR/PBS News/Marist Poll , 40 percent of people said their “personal family finances” have declined in the last 12 months, while 16 percent said the opposite. Forty-one percent said their personal family finances have “stayed about the same” within the prior year. Less than 1 percent of poll respondents were not sure about the state of their personal family finances within the last year, while three percent didn’t give an answer. The NPR/PBS News/Marist Poll was conducted two weeks out from Election Day, with the rise in cost of living being a major concern in this election cycle. September saw an uptick in annual inflation for Americans, with the cost of energy, gas and electricity rising from August to September. Democrats have campaigned on targeting the Trump administration's tariffs and the war in Iran — two factors behind U.S. price hikes. items.t: Cause of death revealed for ‘Office Space’ actor Richard Riehle: Reports
items.x: (NEXSTAR) – The cause of death for longtime actor Richard Riehle has been revealed, according to reports. The 78-year-old died earlier this month in Los Angeles, friends told TMZ , which was the first to report the news. The outlet and People , citing his death certificate, reported Tuesday that the "Office Space" actor experienced a stroke and had oropharyngeal cancer. He had been in a rehabilitation center at the time of his death in mid-October, according to People. Oropharyngeal cancer , which can be asymptomatic, impacts the middle portion of your throat, including the base of your tongue and the tonsils. While there are multiple types of oropharyngeal cancers, Johns Hopkins Medicine says the majority are squamous cell carcinomas, which are further divided into HPV-related and HPV-unrelated. The former is caused by HPV, while the latter is commonly caused by tobacco or alcohol. Details about Riehle's condition were not released. items.x: MORGANTOWN, W.Va. — West Virginia University volleyball freshman outside hitter Macie Smith has been named to the Big 12 Starting Seven of the Week following a record-breaking performance over the weekend. The Big 12 Starting Seven of the Week consists of the four players of the week and three additional student-athletes who receive the most votes. The Cicero, Indiana, native led the Big 12 and ranked No. 5 among Power Four players in hitting percentage last week, recording 15 kills with zero errors on 27 attempts. She became the first freshman in program history to record 15 or more kills with zero errors in a match and just the fifth player overall. Her .556 hitting percentage contributed to the team's .374 mark for the match, the best hitting percentage by any WVU team in a Big 12 match. Smith also tallied three service aces, tying for No. 4 in the conference, as the Mountaineers defeated Arizona for the first time in program history and earned their most conference wins since 2021. She recorded career highs in kills, hitting percentage, points, aces and digs, totaling nine digs. The match against Arizona marked her seventh this season with double-digit kills. items.t: Finley Bizjack named to Jerry West Award watch list
items.x: MORGANTOWN, W.Va. — West Virginia men's basketball senior Finley Bizjack was one of 20 players named to the Jerry West Award watch list by the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame on Tuesday. The annual Jerry West Award, named after the late Class of 1980 Hall of Famer and 1959 NCAA Final Four Most Valuable Player, celebrates its 13th year by highlighting the top shooting guard in NCAA Division I men’s college basketball. Bizjack transferred to WVU this offseason after three seasons at Butler. He averaged a career-high 17.1 points per game last season, shooting 42.6% from the floor and 34.9% from three. Other Big 12 players named to the Jerry West Award watch list include BYU's Collin Chandler, Arizona's Caleb Holt and Iowa State's Killyan Toure. items.t: AAA advises drivers about daylight saving time
items.x: ( WAVY ) – It's only a few days until we trade one extra hour of sleep for months of darkness as we leave work to drive home. Fogo de Chão coming to Legacy Village in 2027 Nexstar's WAVY went to AAA Tidewater Virginia to see what commuters can expect. "Well, the biggest thing for drivers will be the change in daylight when we leave work or school," said Holly Dalby with AAA. "At the end of the day, gone will be the bright sunshine, and we will find ourselves either driving into the glare from the setting sun or driving home in the dark. So it's a time to be particularly careful on the roads." While lawmakers have tried to get rid of the time switch altogether, it doesn't appear to be going anywhere anytime soon, so your circadian rhythm will have to dance to a different beat for a while. "It just messing with our sleep schedule can really add to our fatigue very quickly. And when we're fatigued, we can make mistakes," Dalby said. items.t: Democrats see battleground map expand to South Carolina, Florida, Mississippi
items.x: Democrats are giddy about the possibility of a bigger blue wave than expected in the battle for the Senate as polls show that South Carolina , Florida and Mississippi — three seats that were long seen as safe Republican holds — are now competitive races. Democrats view the Republican candidates running in those states as mediocre political talents who must fight historic headwinds caused by President Trump’s unpopularity, voter anger over inflation and the war in Iran, and burgeoning Democratic voter enthusiasm. The Senate battleground map has steadily expanded throughout the 2026 midterm election cycle as political handicappers have shifted seats that were thought to be in solidly Republican territory — such as Alaska, Iowa, Kansas and Texas — to the “toss-up" category. But now Republicans have to worry about losing Senate seats in states that were unthinkable as realistic Democratic pickup opportunities at the start of the election cycle, most notably South Carolina, which last elected a Democrat, Fritz Hollings, to the Senate in 1998. items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war , creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle . Whether it be personal stories, old legends, or visits by nationally-recognized paranormal investigators, Ohio is no stranger to reports of ghostly sightings and spooky spots. Here are some of the reportedly most haunted places in Northeast Ohio. Franklin Castle Settled in Cleveland's Ohio City neighborhood, Franklin Castle is believed to be one of the most haunted houses in the state. Also known as the Tiedemann House, the Victorian home stands out behind its black iron gate on Franklin Boulevard with its stone walls, red-lined door and windows and a sharp spire near the front. The historic house was built by German immigrant Hannes Tiedemann in the late nineteenth century in what was, at the time, among the most upscale areas of the city, according to Cleveland Historical. items.x: NEW YORK (AP) — A dinosaur that looks like a miniature T. rex is now one of the world's most expensive fossils. The rare skeleton of a Nanotyrannus — recently confirmed to be a distant cousin of Tyrannosaurus rex , not just a young specimen — sold for $47.3 million to a mystery buyer at auction in New York City on Tuesday, according to Sotheby’s. The auction house had expected it to fetch anywhere from $6 to $9 million. Police called for fight outside Walmart, allegedly involving gun and pepper spray The blockbuster price tag for “Jodi,” as the skeleton is nicknamed, makes it the second-priciest set of dinosaur bones ever sold. This summer, a T. rex fossil known as “Gus” sold for a record $50.1 million at Sotheby's. The new owner of “Jodi” has, for now, chosen to remain anonymous after outbidding five other prospective buyers online and by phone during the roughly 12-minute live auction, Sotheby’s said. items.t: What is Issue 3? Ohioans to decide on voter ID amendment in November election
items.x: COLUMBUS , Ohio ( WCMH ) – In just a few days, Ohio voters will decide whether to enshrine voter ID requirements in the state Constitution. Issue 3, appearing on the Nov. 3 ballot , would leave Ohio’s current photo ID requirements largely unchanged but would make them harder for legislators to alter in the future. Ohio governor race brings historic fundraising, ad revenue The requirements under the proposed amendment — and current state law — include showing a government-issued photo ID to vote in person. Accepted IDs include an unexpired Ohio driver’s license, a U.S. passport or a military ID card. Current Ohio law requires absentee voters to provide a copy of their photo ID, Ohio driver’s license number or the last four digits of their Social Security number. A signature is also required. items.t: New weight-loss drug delivers double Ozempic results
items.x: (WJW) — An experimental weight-loss drug from Eli Lilly led to more than twice the average weight loss of Ozempic in a clinical trial involving adults with Type 2 diabetes, according to new results released Wednesday . Participants taking retatrutide lost an average of 44.3 pounds on a 9-milligram dose and 47.4 pounds on a 12-milligram dose over 80 weeks, compared with 20.9 pounds among those taking Ozempic’s highest 2-milligram dose, according to information released from Eli Lilly . Police called for fight outside Walmart, allegedly involving gun and pepper spray The Phase 3 trial included more than 1,000 adults with Type 2 diabetes. Retatrutide also produced greater improvements in blood sugar levels, cholesterol and blood pressure, the report said. How does retatrutide work? Retatrutide is a once-weekly injection that targets three hormone receptors involved in regulating appetite and metabolism: GLP-1, GIP and glucagon, according to Eli Lilly . Ozempic, made by Novo Nordisk, targets GLP-1. Other medications, including Eli Lilly’s Mounjaro and Zepbound, target both GLP-1 and GIP. Democrats view the Republican candidates running in those states as mediocre political talents who must fight historic headwinds caused by President Trump’s unpopularity, voter anger over inflation and the war in Iran, and burgeoning Democratic voter enthusiasm. The Senate battleground map has steadily expanded throughout the 2026 midterm election cycle as political handicappers have shifted seats that were thought to be in solidly Republican territory — such as Alaska, Iowa, Kansas and Texas — to the “toss-up" category. But now Republicans have to worry about losing Senate seats in states that were unthinkable as realistic Democratic pickup opportunities at the start of the election cycle, most notably South Carolina, which last elected a Democrat, Fritz Hollings, to the Senate in 1998. "The Provost used AI to meaningfully alter his writing in violation of at least one publication’s AI use and/or disclosure requirement, failed to disclose his use of AI in clear violation of a national newspaper’s stated policy, was not forthcoming about his AI use, and fell short of the standards set forth by Dartmouth’s Code of Ethical Conduct, the Academic Honor Principle, and Geisel’s Policy on Expectations for Professionalism for Faculty, Non-Faculty Academics, and Staff," the committee concluded. Schnell was accused of using AI to alter his work by the student newspaper The Dartmouth and outlet Semafor, specifically pointing to an opinion piece the provost wrote for The Washington Post. items.t: Opelika teen injured after drive-by shooting Wednesday night
items.x: OPELIKA, Ala. (WRBL) — An Opelika teen is in the hospital after being shot in the area of South Long Street Wednesday night. Opelika Police say that at 7:17 p.m., officers responded to reports of a shooting near S. Long Street and Alabama Avenue. An unidentified 17-year-old was found at the scene, in the back seat of a vehicle, with a gunshot wound to the leg. According to OPD, witnesses say a dark-colored vehicle drove past and fired several shots at the teen's vehicle before speeding off. The teen was taken to Piedmont Columbus Regional for treatment. The shooting caused a heavy police presence and road closure in the area that remained until 9 p.m. The case remains under investigation. If you have any information, please contact the Opelika Police Department Detective Division at (334) 705-5220 or the Secret Witness Hotline at (334) 745-8665. Tips can also be submitted via the Opelika Police Mobile App. You can remain anonymous.

items.t: AAA advises drivers about daylight saving time
items.x: ( WAVY ) – It's only a few days until we trade one extra hour of sleep for months of darkness as we leave work to drive home. And even though we're on the easier end of the time transition (from daylight saving time to standard time), the switch still takes its toll. Nexstar's WAVY went to AAA Tidewater Virginia to see what commuters can expect. "Well, the biggest thing for drivers will be the change in daylight when we leave work or school," said Holly Dalby with AAA. "At the end of the day, gone will be the bright sunshine, and we will find ourselves either driving into the glare from the setting sun or driving home in the dark. So it's a time to be particularly careful on the roads." Days will get way shorter in November: How much daylight will we lose? While lawmakers have tried to get rid of the time switch altogether, it doesn't appear to be going anywhere anytime soon, so your circadian rhythm will have to dance to a different beat for a while. "It just messing with our sleep schedule can really add to our fatigue very quickly. And when we're fatigued, we can make mistakes," Dalby said. items.t: ‘Gut punch’: 2 college students found dead in Colorado after going missing on mountain hike
items.x: ( WJW ) – Two missing Colorado college students were found dead Wednesday after they left campus for a weekend trip up a nearly 14,000-foot peak and encountered a heavy snowstorm, police said. Kaden Matsuda, 19, from Ridgway, Colorado, and Jackson Donlon, 20, from New York, left Colorado Mountain College Leadville’s campus on Friday and didn’t return. They told family and friends they planned to go up Ice Mountain, which requires technical climbing, according to the county sheriff’s office. On Wednesday night, the sheriff's office confirmed that the students were found dead around 3:30 p.m. in a basin of the West Apostle Mountain. Authorities do not believe foul play was involved. The investigation is now being handled by the Chaffee County Coroner’s Office. “Our heart aches for Kaden and Jackson’s family and friends. We are very proud of our team’s efforts to find them before this weekend’s coming storm," Sheriff Andy Rohrich wrote on Facebook. "Although this is a gut punch, our prayers were answered that we would find Kaden and Jackson, allowing some closure for the family. items.t: Cruise ship passenger says warning signs were there long before Cambodia
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — Kit Cassingham and her husband, Randy, sold their home and nearly everything they owned to live aboard a cruise ship for years. Now, she says she doesn't expect to see that money again. Cassingham told NewsNation's Jesse Weber on Wednesday that the couple paid about $370,000 to $380,000 for their cabin on the Villa Vie Odyssey, plus $7,000 a month in expenses. Asked if they will get it back, she said, "No, no, no, no." Cruise ship suspends voyage over fuel costs, stranding 200 passengers More than 200 passengers were told Tuesday to leave the Odyssey in Cambodia within hours after the cruise company suspended operations. In a news release , Villa Vie blamed soaring fuel costs tied to the war in Iran, saying the monthly fuel cost per cabin jumped from about $1,800 to as much as $8,000. Villa Vie Odyssey: How did passengers find out they had to leave? Cassingham and her husband had already gotten off the ship for a hotel so they could work online when a short message arrived saying the ship couldn't get more fuel . “You have till two o’clock to get off the ship,” she said. items.t: Wendy’s gets buyout offer while struggling with beef prices and growing competition
items.x: Wendy’s shares jumped more than 14% Wednesday after noted investor Nelson Peltz made an offer to buy the chain, which has been struggling with high beef prices and aging stores. Peltz’s Trian Fund Management and several partners are offering Wendy’s $7.35 per share in cash, or a premium of nearly 19% over the stock’s closing price on Tuesday, in a deal that would take the company private. The offer values Wendy's at $1.4 billion. Wendy's, which is based in Dublin, Ohio, confirmed receipt of the unsolicited proposal in a statement Wednesday and said its board has formed an independent committee to evaluate it. At the end of last year, Wendy's had 5,969 restaurants in the U.S. and 1,428 outlets in 38 countries. Wendy's, founded in 1969 by Dave Thomas and named after his daughter, is known for its square burgers and Frosty desserts. The fast-growing chain introduced the drive-thru window in 1970 and went public in 1976. In the 1980s, as it jockeyed for sales with McDonald's and Burger King, Wendy's launched salad bars and ran its iconic “Where's the beef?” ad campaign. items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: ( The Hill ) Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. Gasoline and energy costs have risen in six of nine months this year, as the Iran war sparked oil price shocks via the Islamic Republic's restrictions on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Persistent inflation , which has remained above the Fed's 2 percent target for five-and-a-half years, spurred central bank officials to hike interest rates by a quarter point in mid-September. items.t: DoorDash to buy Instacart in $17 billion grocery delivery deal
items.x: DoorDash is gobbling up Instacart in a $17 billion acquisition that will supercharge its grocery delivery business. DoorDash said the Instacart brand name and app will remain, and Instacart shoppers can continue fulfilling orders for Instacart. Grocers can also choose to work with Instacart or DoorDash. Instacart customers will now have access to 50,000 additional stores covered by DoorDash, the company said. Instacart, founded in 2012, specializes in grocery and convenience store delivery in the U.S. and Canada. Its 600,000 “shoppers” — who are independent contractors — completed 338 million orders last year, according to company filings. Instacart has a market value of $14 billion. DoorDash, founded in San Francisco in 2013, began as a restaurant delivery business but has expanded to pet food and electronics. Operating in 40 countries, it completed more than 3 billion orders last year using a network of 9 million independent delivery workers. It has a market value of $73 billion. DoorDash began delivering groceries in 2020 amid a surge in pandemic-era demand. Grocers were initially cautious. items.t: RFK Jr. eases access to unproven peptides despite opposition from FDA scientists
items.x: WASHINGTON (AP) — The Trump administration on Wednesday acted to ease access to unproven peptide drugs favored by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr . Food and Drug Administration scientific staffers had little input on the decision and opposed the changes, according to six people familiar with its development. The draft policy posted online by Kennedy’s Department of Health and Human Services covers a handful of injectable peptides promoted within the wellness industry for uses such as building muscle, healing injuries and boosting energy. The government will take comments for two weeks before finalizing the measure. The document, primarily written by officials at HHS, faced overwhelming pushback among FDA drug staffers who warned it could undermine the agency’s long-standing mission of keeping unsafe health products off the U.S. market, according to the people familiar with its development. items.t: DOJ’s California ballot fight rejected by another judge
items.x: ( The Hill ) The Trump administration's bid to separate 20,000 mail ballots in California that it says are likely noncitizens met another defeat on Wednesday as a trial judge refused to intervene. U.S. District Judge David Carter ruled California can continue to accept the questioned ballots like any other. “This request violates longstanding constitutional principles mandating that states have control over their elections,” Carter wrote. “If Plaintiff’s last-minute request for relief were granted, either party could create chaos for their own political purposes to disrupt the election process,” he continued. “Over 20,000 registered Californians would potentially lose the right that generations of Americans have fought to preserve.” California has raised eyebrows at the veracity of the administration's list and says it's not obligated to verify voters’ citizenship in response. The state has conceded it's not feasible to segregate a ballot once it's processed. It would be counted even if later found to be fraudulent. items.t: Harris advises Democrats against attempting to impeach Trump
items.x: ( The Hill ) Former Vice President Kamala Harris on Tuesday urged Democrats against making a third attempt to impeach President Trump if they win back the House after next week's midterm elections. "I think that going in the direction of impeachment is not a good idea, just to be honest with you," Harris told MeidasTouch's Aaron Parnas in an interview. "Just because we have limited resources and I think the energy and the resources need to put into accountability, need to be put into investigations." "And that's where the time should be spent," she added. "Remember, I was in the Senate for the last go-around, and the votes aren't there. "So, that's how I feel. But also, I think after the election, we all have to just also agree that our attitude has to be to get stuff done." Harris said Democrats should be "uncompromising" and "not sit around, you know, being genteel about the relationships," but maintain accountability when it comes to cuts to healthcare and oversight on the Iran war. items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war , creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle . The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 176 points, or 0.3%, as of 11:45 a.m. Eastern time, and the Nasdaq composite was virtually unchanged. items.t: 68 dead in high-speed train collision, Spain’s 2nd deadly rail crash this year
items.x: URDA, Spain (AP) — A high-speed train slammed into another that had stopped on the tracks in Spain on Wednesday, killing at least 68 people and injuring dozens in the second deadly rail collision this year. The regional government of Castilla La Mancha confirmed the death toll and said another 58 people were receiving medical treatment at hospitals. Rescue workers searched the wreckage through the day for survivors and bodies. The collision came just nine months after another deadly crash involving high-speed trains operated by the same two companies in southern Spain in January. “Today all of Spain is grieving,” Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said from the crash site, where he announced that his government would declare three days of national mourning. items.t: Russell County officials prepare for Election Day
items.x: RUSSELL COUNTY, Ala. ( WRBL )— Preparations for the November 3rd General Election are underway in Alabama. Election workers packed the Russell County Commission Chambers on Tuesday for Election Worker Training. This training focused on operating machines, procedures during polling hours, safety, and unexpected incidents. Russell County Probate Judge Belinda Strickland focused heavily on provisional ballots. Strickland said the number of provisional voters in Russell County has dropped significantly, but poll workers must be prepared. Strickland explained that the county has seen voters attempt to cast ballots at the wrong precincts out of convenience. "One of the things that we're doing now is we stop as soon as they are not showing up in the system," Strickland explained. "We call the registrars and find out why." Strickland emphasized that workers are not permitted to issue provisional ballots unless authorized by the registrar's office first. Safety concerns were addressed at the training. items.t: Utah authorities connect 1974 cold case to serial killer Ted Bundy
items.x: SUMMIT COUNTY, Utah ( KTVX ) — Investigators in Summit County, Utah closed the 1974 cold case homicide of Melissa Ann Smith Tuesday, linking her murder to prominent serial killer Ted Bundy. Using DNA and other evidence, the Summit County Sheriff's Office and Summit County Attorney's Office formally closed the cold-case murder, saying that the evidence conclusively proves that Ted Bundy murdered 17-year-old Melissa Ann Smith. Bundy has long been considered a suspect in several cold cases in Utah, and Smith's murder was one of them. Hunters found her remains in Summit County on Oct. 27, 1974, 52 years ago today. "The work began with the investigators who handled the case in 1974, and it continued through the dedication and perseverance of those who carried it forward," Summit County Sheriff Kacey Bates said. "After 50 years, we have reached a point that so many have worked toward." items.t: 4 in 10 say personal finances worsening: Survey
items.x: ( The Hill ) Four in 10 Americans say their personal finances are deteriorating, according to a new poll released shortly before November's midterm elections. In the NPR/PBS News/Marist Poll , 40 percent of people said their “personal family finances” have declined in the last 12 months, while 16 percent said the opposite. Forty-one percent said their personal family finances have “stayed about the same” within the prior year. Less than 1 percent of poll respondents were not sure about the state of their personal family finances within the last year, while three percent didn’t give an answer. The NPR/PBS News/Marist Poll was conducted two weeks out from Election Day, with the rise in cost of living being a major concern in this election cycle. September saw an uptick in annual inflation for Americans, with the cost of energy, gas and electricity rising from August to September. Democrats have campaigned on targeting the Trump administration's tariffs and the war in Iran — two factors behind U.S. price hikes. items.t: Lee County Sheriff confirms resignation of deputy as internal investigation is initiated
items.x: OPELIKA, Ala. ( WRBL ) — Lee County Sheriff Jay Jones confirms to WRBL News 3 the recent resignation of one of his deputies, citing an ongoing internal investigation. Sheriff Jones says the deputy, whose name he is not releasing, "resigned recently as we were initiating an internal investigation into a violation of policy and procedure. We requested ALEA SBI to investigate allegations of inappropriate actions that have been alleged, as is standard procedure," Jones stated. Sheriff Jones referred to an "unauthorized" internal copy of a report, which was emailed to the WRBL newsroom. It detailed a situation taking place on Oct. 18, 2026, when a woman reported she was pulled over by a deputy sheriff around midnight. The woman claims the deputy took her phone number and entered it into his phone. The woman then claims the deputy called her within minutes, pulled her over, kissed her and put his hand under her dress. Jones would only confirm that the Alabama State Bureau of Investigation, which is the state's investigative arm of ALEA, is looking into allegations of inappropriate actions.

items.t: Cause of death revealed for ‘Office Space’ actor Richard Riehle: Reports
items.x: (NEXSTAR) – The cause of death for longtime actor Richard Riehle has been revealed, according to reports. The 78-year-old died earlier this month in Los Angeles, friends told TMZ , which was the first to report the news. The outlet and People , citing his death certificate, reported Tuesday that the "Office Space" actor experienced a stroke and had oropharyngeal cancer. He had been in a rehabilitation center at the time of his death in mid-October, according to People. Oropharyngeal cancer , which can be asymptomatic, impacts the middle portion of your throat, including the base of your tongue and the tonsils. While there are multiple types of oropharyngeal cancers, Johns Hopkins Medicine says the majority are squamous cell carcinomas, which are further divided into HPV-related and HPV-unrelated. The former is caused by HPV, while the latter is commonly caused by tobacco or alcohol. Details about Riehle's condition were not released. items.t: Georgia woman sentenced for mailing synthetic cannabinoids into Alabama correctional facilities
items.x: MONTGOMERY, Ala. ( WRBL ) — A Georgia woman was sentenced to prison for distributing controlled substances and unlawfully using the U.S. mail to distribute synthetic cannabinoids into Alabama correctional facilities. According to court documents and statements made during court proceedings, the Drug Enforcement Administration and the Alabama Department of Corrections began an investigation in July 2024 after discovering the packages containing synthetic cannabinoids mailed into Alabama correctional facilities. The investigation revealed that several of the intercepted packages were linked to 44-year-old Jinna Moore of Fairburn, Ga., and her business shipping account. Officials said evidence showed that she distributed synthetic cannabinoids to individuals outside the prison system. On January 30, 2026, Moore pleaded guilty to three counts of distribution of a controlled substance and three counts of unlawful use of a communication facility. She was sentenced to 78 months in prison, followed by three years of supervised release. Officials reminded everyone that the federal system has no parole.

Frost presented First Liberty as a Christian lender that helped small businesses. He told investors their money would go toward short-term loans and promised them monthly returns of 8% to 18%. items.t: Recalled butter sold in 10 states receives risk warning: FDA
items.x: NEW JERSEY ( WPIX ) A popular plant-based butter has been recalled due to yeast, mold and E. coli, and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has now assigned it a risk level . The recall, which was initiated by Prosperity Organic Foods, Inc., headquartered in Boise, Idaho, involves 1,304 cases of Miyoko's Creamery European Style Salted Plant Milk Butter. The FDA assigned the recall as a Class II risk level on Friday, meaning a product may cause “temporary or medically reversible adverse health consequences.” The recall was initially announced Sept. 11. The affected butter, which is perishable and stored refrigerated or frozen, comes in six-packs of 8-ounce units, which can be identified with the following information: UPC 857554005773 Lot number and best-by on SBS carton: 07871, Nov. 5, 2026 Lot number and best-by date on the corrugated case for shipment: 1007871, Nov. 5, 2026 The affected products were also sold in Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Iowa, Illinois, Indiana, Maryland, New Jersey, New Hampshire and Wisconsin.

items.t: Democrats see battleground map expand to South Carolina, Florida, Mississippi
items.x: Democrats are giddy about the possibility of a bigger blue wave than expected in the battle for the Senate as polls show that South Carolina , Florida and Mississippi — three seats that were long seen as safe Republican holds — are now competitive races. Democrats view the Republican candidates running in those states as mediocre political talents who must fight historic headwinds caused by President Trump’s unpopularity, voter anger over inflation and the war in Iran, and burgeoning Democratic voter enthusiasm. The Senate battleground map has steadily expanded throughout the 2026 midterm election cycle as political handicappers have shifted seats that were thought to be in solidly Republican territory — such as Alaska, Iowa, Kansas and Texas — to the “toss-up" category. But now Republicans have to worry about losing Senate seats in states that were unthinkable as realistic Democratic pickup opportunities at the start of the election cycle, most notably South Carolina, which last elected a Democrat, Fritz Hollings, to the Senate in 1998. items.t: AAA advises drivers about daylight saving time
items.x: ( WAVY ) – It's only a few days until we trade one extra hour of sleep for months of darkness as we leave work to drive home. And even though we're on the easier end of the time transition (from daylight saving time to standard time), the switch still takes its toll. Nexstar's WAVY went to AAA Tidewater Virginia to see what commuters can expect. "Well, the biggest thing for drivers will be the change in daylight when we leave work or school," said Holly Dalby with AAA. "At the end of the day, gone will be the bright sunshine, and we will find ourselves either driving into the glare from the setting sun or driving home in the dark. So it's a time to be particularly careful on the roads." Days will get way shorter in November: How much daylight will we lose? While lawmakers have tried to get rid of the time switch altogether, it doesn't appear to be going anywhere anytime soon, so your circadian rhythm will have to dance to a different beat for a while. "It just messing with our sleep schedule can really add to our fatigue very quickly. And when we're fatigued, we can make mistakes," Dalby said. The offer values Wendy's at $1.4 billion. Wendy's, which is based in Dublin, Ohio, confirmed receipt of the unsolicited proposal in a statement Wednesday and said its board has formed an independent committee to evaluate it. At the end of last year, Wendy's had 5,969 restaurants in the U.S. and 1,428 outlets in 38 countries. Wendy's, founded in 1969 by Dave Thomas and named after his daughter, is known for its square burgers and Frosty desserts. The fast-growing chain introduced the drive-thru window in 1970 and went public in 1976. In the 1980s, as it jockeyed for sales with McDonald's and Burger King, Wendy's launched salad bars and ran its iconic “Where's the beef?” ad campaign. items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: ( The Hill ) Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. Gasoline and energy costs have risen in six of nine months this year, as the Iran war sparked oil price shocks via the Islamic Republic's restrictions on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Persistent inflation , which has remained above the Fed's 2 percent target for five-and-a-half years, spurred central bank officials to hike interest rates by a quarter point in mid-September. Instacart customers will now have access to 50,000 additional stores covered by DoorDash, the company said. Instacart, founded in 2012, specializes in grocery and convenience store delivery in the U.S. and Canada. Its 600,000 “shoppers” — who are independent contractors — completed 338 million orders last year, according to company filings. Instacart has a market value of $14 billion. DoorDash, founded in San Francisco in 2013, began as a restaurant delivery business but has expanded to pet food and electronics. Operating in 40 countries, it completed more than 3 billion orders last year using a network of 9 million independent delivery workers. It has a market value of $73 billion. DoorDash began delivering groceries in 2020 amid a surge in pandemic-era demand. Grocers were initially cautious. items.t: RFK Jr. eases access to unproven peptides despite opposition from FDA scientists
items.x: WASHINGTON (AP) — The Trump administration on Wednesday acted to ease access to unproven peptide drugs favored by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr . Food and Drug Administration scientific staffers had little input on the decision and opposed the changes, according to six people familiar with its development. The draft policy posted online by Kennedy’s Department of Health and Human Services covers a handful of injectable peptides promoted within the wellness industry for uses such as building muscle, healing injuries and boosting energy. The government will take comments for two weeks before finalizing the measure. The document, primarily written by officials at HHS, faced overwhelming pushback among FDA drug staffers who warned it could undermine the agency’s long-standing mission of keeping unsafe health products off the U.S. market, according to the people familiar with its development. items.t: DOJ’s California ballot fight rejected by another judge
items.x: ( The Hill ) The Trump administration's bid to separate 20,000 mail ballots in California that it says are likely noncitizens met another defeat on Wednesday as a trial judge refused to intervene. U.S. District Judge David Carter ruled California can continue to accept the questioned ballots like any other. “This request violates longstanding constitutional principles mandating that states have control over their elections,” Carter wrote. “If Plaintiff’s last-minute request for relief were granted, either party could create chaos for their own political purposes to disrupt the election process,” he continued. “Over 20,000 registered Californians would potentially lose the right that generations of Americans have fought to preserve.” California has raised eyebrows at the veracity of the administration's list and says it's not obligated to verify voters’ citizenship in response. The state has conceded it's not feasible to segregate a ballot once it's processed. It would be counted even if later found to be fraudulent. items.t: Harris advises Democrats against attempting to impeach Trump
items.x: ( The Hill ) Former Vice President Kamala Harris on Tuesday urged Democrats against making a third attempt to impeach President Trump if they win back the House after next week's midterm elections. "I think that going in the direction of impeachment is not a good idea, just to be honest with you," Harris told MeidasTouch's Aaron Parnas in an interview. "Just because we have limited resources and I think the energy and the resources need to put into accountability, need to be put into investigations." "And that's where the time should be spent," she added. "Remember, I was in the Senate for the last go-around, and the votes aren't there. "So, that's how I feel. But also, I think after the election, we all have to just also agree that our attitude has to be to get stuff done." Harris said Democrats should be "uncompromising" and "not sit around, you know, being genteel about the relationships," but maintain accountability when it comes to cuts to healthcare and oversight on the Iran war. "We are deeply saddened to announce that our beloved mother, Dolores Huerta, has passed away today at the age of 96," her family said in a statement posted on social media. "As you can imagine, this is an incredibly difficult time for us, and we ask for privacy as we grieve this incredible loss to our family," the statement continued. Kotlikoff after allegations of a 2024 gang rape at a campus fraternity that resulted in no criminal charges caused uproar around the country. The more than 75 members of the body will have their second meeting debating the resolution and the timing of a vote on it. A motion could be introduced to delay the no-confidence vote and set another meeting. But if that motion is not introduced or fails, members of the Faculty Senate will begin the no-confidence vote after Wednesday's meeting is over, and they typically have a week to cast their choice online. While a no-confidence vote has no authority to remove an official, its passing would show deep dissatisfaction from faculty with how Cornell leadership has handled accusations from Jane Doe that seven members of the Chi Phi fraternity raped her . What does the no-confidence vote entail? items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war , creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle . items.t: Judge overseeing Maduro trial dies
items.x: ( The Hill ) Alvin Hellerstein, a longtime federal judge who was set to oversee the criminal trial of deposed Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro, has passed away, according to a court official. He was 92. Nominated by then-President Bill Clinton in 1998, Hellerstein oversaw many high-profile disputes during his nearly three decades on the bench in New York City. He was back in the national limelight presiding over the proceedings for Maduro , who was captured and brought to the U.S. earlier this year over accusations of narco-terrorism. Maduro and his wife were in the judge's courtroom less than two weeks ago to plead not guilty to a new set of criminal charges. Before the Maduro operation, Hellerstein had long clashed with President Donald Trump in court. The judge at one point agreed that Trump’s fixer-turned-foe, Michael Cohen, could be released from prison to home confinement. Cohen has cast his prosecution as retribution by Trump. Separately, Hellerstein repeatedly denied Trump's efforts to move his hush money criminal prosecution into federal court, forcing the president to try his luck in New York's state system. items.t: US stocks hold steady as the countdown ticks to a Federal Reserve decision on interest rates
items.x: NEW YORK (AP) — U.S. stocks are drifting Wednesday as the countdown ticks toward this afternoon’s announcement from the Federal Reserve on what it will do with interest rates . The S&P 500 rose 0.2% and pulled within 1% of its all-time high , which was set earlier this month. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 176 points, or 0.3%, as of 11:45 a.m. Eastern time, and the Nasdaq composite was virtually unchanged. The day’s highlight will likely be what the Federal Reserve says, if anything, about where interest rates are heading. The Fed raised its main interest rate last month for the first time in three years in hopes of slowing the high inflation that’s squeezing the economy and discouraging Americans . The widespread expectation on Wall Street is that the Fed will leave the federal funds rate alone at this meeting, and the question is whether it will give hints about what may happen at later meetings. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh, though, has been adamant since taking over the Fed about wanting it to give fewer indications about its future moves. The aircraft is part of a growing category known as electric vertical takeoff and landing, or eVTOL. Unlike a conventional airplane, it does not require a runway for every departure. items.t: AAA advises drivers about daylight saving time
items.x: ( WAVY ) – It's only a few days until we trade one extra hour of sleep for months of darkness as we leave work to drive home. And even though we're on the easier end of the time transition (from daylight saving time to standard time), the switch still takes its toll. Nexstar's WAVY went to AAA Tidewater Virginia to see what commuters can expect. "Well, the biggest thing for drivers will be the change in daylight when we leave work or school," said Holly Dalby with AAA. "At the end of the day, gone will be the bright sunshine, and we will find ourselves either driving into the glare from the setting sun or driving home in the dark. So it's a time to be particularly careful on the roads." Days will get way shorter in November: How much daylight will we lose? While lawmakers have tried to get rid of the time switch altogether, it doesn't appear to be going anywhere anytime soon, so your circadian rhythm will have to dance to a different beat for a while. items.t: Escaped inmate in Brinkley after assaulting jailer reported by police
items.x: BRINKLEY, Ark. – The Brinkley Police Department is asking the public to watch for an escaped inmate. Officials said 41-year-old Rodney Smith assaulted a jailer and a Brinkley police officer, then escaped on Thursday morning at approximately 7:15 a.m. after taking the officer's Taser. State police officials said Smith is a 5-foot-10-inch Black man weighing 260 pounds. He was last seen wearing a white T-shirt, yellow pants and white socks. He was not wearing shoes. Smith is listed as an Arkansas Department of Corrections inmate since January 2013. He was sentenced for firearms possession, two counts of drug possession, possession of a firearm by certain persons and forgery. Officials said he had a history of domestic battery. State police officials said Smith was being held in Brinkley pending bed space availability in the state prison system. Records show he had previously completed a two-year sentence for aggravated robbery. Smith should be considered armed and dangerous, officials said, adding that if anyone sees him, they should call 911, the Brinkley police at 870-734-3434 or Arkansas State Police Troop D at 870-633-1454. Brinkley is in Monroe County, in east Arkansas.

items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: ( The Hill ) Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. Gasoline and energy costs have risen in six of nine months this year, as the Iran war sparked oil price shocks via the Islamic Republic's restrictions on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Persistent inflation , which has remained above the Fed's 2 percent target for five-and-a-half years, spurred central bank officials to hike interest rates by a quarter point in mid-September. DoorDash, founded in San Francisco in 2013, began as a restaurant delivery business but has expanded to pet food and electronics. Operating in 40 countries, it completed more than 3 billion orders last year using a network of 9 million independent delivery workers. It has a market value of $73 billion. items.t: Cabot father wants accountability after daughter is severely injured in hit-and-run motorcycle crash
items.x: CABOT, Ark. — A Cabot father is calling on a driver to turn themselves in after his 32-year-old daughter was severely injured in a hit-and-run motorcycle crash Sunday night, leaving her hospitalized with extensive injuries and facing a long road to recovery. Mark Hudgings says his daughter, Jasmine Hudgings, was riding as a passenger on a motorcycle with her boyfriend around 9:45 p.m. Sunday when a white truck allegedly turned in front of them near Highway 5 and Quail Trail in Cabot. Hudgings says the couple attempted to avoid the truck but were unable to get out of its path before crashing into a ditch and being thrown from the motorcycle. The driver of the truck reportedly left the scene, according to Hudgings. “I was sitting at the house and at about 9:45 pm Sunday I get a call from my daughter she had been in a motorcycle accident,” Hudgings said. “I said, ‘Where are you at?’ and she said she was just down the street, so of course dad jumps in his truck and heads down here.” What he discovered when he arrived was something he says no parent should ever have to witness. “What I found was my daughter laying in a ditch, leg just about tore off her body at the knee,” Hudgings said.

items.t: Harris advises Democrats against attempting to impeach Trump
items.x: ( The Hill ) Former Vice President Kamala Harris on Tuesday urged Democrats against making a third attempt to impeach President Trump if they win back the House after next week's midterm elections. "I think that going in the direction of impeachment is not a good idea, just to be honest with you," Harris told MeidasTouch's Aaron Parnas in an interview. "Just because we have limited resources and I think the energy and the resources need to put into accountability, need to be put into investigations." "And that's where the time should be spent," she added. "Remember, I was in the Senate for the last go-around, and the votes aren't there. "So, that's how I feel. But also, I think after the election, we all have to just also agree that our attitude has to be to get stuff done." Harris said Democrats should be "uncompromising" and "not sit around, you know, being genteel about the relationships," but maintain accountability when it comes to cuts to healthcare and oversight on the Iran war. items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war , creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle . The MV Odyssey set sail two years ago on a voyage to the seven continents marketed as combining long-term living at sea with global travel. Its operator had offered to “make the Odyssey your permanent home,” with the purchase price of a suite for the lifetime of the vessel starting around $230,000. items.t: 68 dead in high-speed train collision, Spain’s 2nd deadly rail crash this year
items.x: URDA, Spain (AP) — A high-speed train slammed into another that had stopped on the tracks in Spain on Wednesday, killing at least 68 people and injuring dozens in the second deadly rail collision this year. The regional government of Castilla La Mancha confirmed the death toll and said another 58 people were receiving medical treatment at hospitals. Rescue workers searched the wreckage through the day for survivors and bodies. The collision came just nine months after another deadly crash involving high-speed trains operated by the same two companies in southern Spain in January. “Today all of Spain is grieving,” Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said from the crash site, where he announced that his government would declare three days of national mourning. items.t: Flying taxis could carry passengers by 2030
items.x: (TestMiles) A British aerospace company has demonstrated an electric flying taxi that could eventually offer a new way to escape crowded city roads. The Flying Car Is Moving Beyond Science Fiction Los Angeles has spent decades trying to solve its traffic problems. Freeways expand, transit systems improve, and technology promises more efficient journeys. Yet travelling across the city can still take a remarkable amount of time. A British aerospace company believes part of the solution might be above the roads rather than on them. Vertical Aerospace has demonstrated an electric aircraft capable of taking off vertically, transitioning into conventional forward flight, and landing without a runway. The technology was publicly displayed at the Farnborough International Airshow in Britain, marking an important development in the company's plans to introduce commercial passenger flights. The aircraft is part of a growing category known as electric vertical takeoff and landing, or eVTOL. Unlike a conventional airplane, it does not require a runway for every departure. The Pulaski County Quorum Court voted 10-4 to override County Judge Barry Hyde’s veto of a proposed ordinance regulating data centers, moving forward with new requirements for qualifying developments after months of debate. The woman began working at the zoo when she was 17 and spent nearly all of her 40-year career there. items.t: Cause of death revealed for ‘Office Space’ actor Richard Riehle: Reports
items.x: (NEXSTAR) – The cause of death for longtime actor Richard Riehle has been revealed, according to reports. The 78-year-old died earlier this month in Los Angeles, friends told TMZ , which was the first to report the news. The outlet and People , citing his death certificate, reported Tuesday that the "Office Space" actor experienced a stroke and had oropharyngeal cancer. He had been in a rehabilitation center at the time of his death in mid-October, according to People. Oropharyngeal cancer , which can be asymptomatic, impacts the middle portion of your throat, including the base of your tongue and the tonsils. While there are multiple types of oropharyngeal cancers, Johns Hopkins Medicine says the majority are squamous cell carcinomas, which are further divided into HPV-related and HPV-unrelated. The former is caused by HPV, while the latter is commonly caused by tobacco or alcohol. Details about Riehle's condition were not released. The AI system continuously analyzes patient data and alerts bedside caregivers when a mother’s or baby’s condition falls outside established safety parameters. items.x: LITTLE ROCK, Ark. Robinson Center marks a milestone this fall, celebrating 10 years since its restoration, renovation, and expansion reopened the venue to the public. The Little Rock Convention & Visitors Bureau (LRCVB) will host a free public celebration on Nov. 10 from 4 p.m. to 7 p.m. at Robinson Center, located at 426 W. Markham St. in downtown Little Rock. The event commemorates a decade since the venue reopened following a $70 million transformation that officials say modernized the facility while preserving its historic character. The recall, which was initiated by Prosperity Organic Foods, Inc., headquartered in Boise, Idaho, involves 1,304 cases of Miyoko's Creamery European Style Salted Plant Milk Butter. The FDA assigned the recall as a Class II risk level on Friday, meaning a product may cause “temporary or medically reversible adverse health consequences.” The recall was initially announced Sept. 11. The affected butter, which is perishable and stored refrigerated or frozen, comes in six-packs of 8-ounce units, which can be identified with the following information: UPC 857554005773 Lot number and best-by on SBS carton: 07871, Nov. 5, 2026 Lot number and best-by date on the corrugated case for shipment: 1007871, Nov. 5, 2026 The affected products were also sold in Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Iowa, Illinois, Indiana, Maryland, New Jersey, New Hampshire and Wisconsin.

items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war , creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle . According to court records, the teen was allegedly involved in at least seven incidents, including armed robbery, attempted robbery and carjackings between April 7 and July 17. Bebak Gurung will serve 40 years in prison for two counts of sexual exploitation of a minor-production of child pornography, the United States Attorney's Office District of Kansas announced Monday. Court records say he pretended to be female to "gain their trust." It was also discovered that Gurung had been engaging with the victim while he was stationed at Fort Riley. items.t: Democrats see battleground map expand to South Carolina, Florida, Mississippi
items.x: Democrats are giddy about the possibility of a bigger blue wave than expected in the battle for the Senate as polls show that South Carolina , Florida and Mississippi — three seats that were long seen as safe Republican holds — are now competitive races. Democrats view the Republican candidates running in those states as mediocre political talents who must fight historic headwinds caused by President Trump’s unpopularity, voter anger over inflation and the war in Iran, and burgeoning Democratic voter enthusiasm. The Senate battleground map has steadily expanded throughout the 2026 midterm election cycle as political handicappers have shifted seats that were thought to be in solidly Republican territory — such as Alaska, Iowa, Kansas and Texas — to the “toss-up" category. But now Republicans have to worry about losing Senate seats in states that were unthinkable as realistic Democratic pickup opportunities at the start of the election cycle, most notably South Carolina, which last elected a Democrat, Fritz Hollings, to the Senate in 1998. items.x: GRAND RAPIDS, Mich. (WOOD) — Perrigo Company is selling its infant formula business for up to $175 million. The company has entered into a definitive agreement with American contract manufacturing platform MeridianMade, it announced Thursday. Under the deal, MeridianMade — a company that's built around infant nutrition — is set to acquire Perrigo's infant formula business for $40 million cash at closing and up to $135 million more, based on future performance. The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027. Until then, the companies will continue to operate as they currently do. items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. Gasoline and energy costs have risen in six of nine months this year, as the Iran war sparked oil price shocks via the Islamic Republic's restrictions on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Persistent inflation , which has remained above the Fed's 2 percent target for five-and-a-half years, spurred central bank officials to hike interest rates by a quarter point in mid-September. items.t: Motorcyclist, 29, killed in Oshtemo Township crash: MSP
items.x: OSHTEMO TOWNSHIP, Mich. (WOOD) — A motorcyclist is dead after after colliding with a car in Oshtemo Township Wednesday evening, Michigan State Police say. The 29-year-old Lawton man was driving a motorcycle westbound on Stadium Drive when he was hit by an SUV that was attempting to turn northbound onto 8th Street from Stadium Drive, state police said in a statement . The motorcyclist, who was not wearing a helmet, was taken to a hospital with life-threatening injuries. He was later pronounced dead. The SUV's driver, a 75-year-old Kalamazoo man, was wearing a seatbelt and sustained minor injuries, according to state police. As of Thursday morning, authorities said they have not determined whether alcohol and drug use may have contributed to the crash, though excessive speed may have been a factor. In a statement, an MSP official warned drivers to "Obey posted speed limits, eliminate distractions, and look twice for motorcycles before turning or changing lanes." The crash remains under investigation.

They don't have solutions to actual problems, so they'd rather have the media and you talking about the Cheesecake Factory.” Obama had quipped during a recent campaign stop in Cleveland, Ohio, that Trump’s taste in renovations worth a reported $900 million has the White House “looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory, it’s just gold everywhere,” referring to the Iraqi palaces that were famously adorned with gold decor. items.t: RFK Jr. eases access to unproven peptides despite opposition from FDA scientists
items.x: WASHINGTON (AP) — The Trump administration on Wednesday acted to ease access to unproven peptide drugs favored by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr . Food and Drug Administration scientific staffers had little input on the decision and opposed the changes, according to six people familiar with its development. The draft policy posted online by Kennedy’s Department of Health and Human Services covers a handful of injectable peptides promoted within the wellness industry for uses such as building muscle, healing injuries and boosting energy. The government will take comments for two weeks before finalizing the measure. The document, primarily written by officials at HHS, faced overwhelming pushback among FDA drug staffers who warned it could undermine the agency’s long-standing mission of keeping unsafe health products off the U.S. market, according to the people familiar with its development. items.x: GRAND RAPIDS, Mich. (WOOD) — The city of Grand Rapids is asking residents to send in feedback on the proposed 2027-2032 Parks and Recreation Master Plan . The Department of Parks & Recreation master plan is updated every five years to address community needs and guide decisions about park improvements, natural spaces and recreational facilities in Grand Rapids. "Our parks and recreation facilities are more than just places to play," Director of Parks and Recreation Laura Cleypool wrote in a statement. "They're where our community comes together." The draft plan, if approved, could shape the future of the city's parks, trails and recreation centers for years to come. “This master plan gives us a framework for making strategic investments, caring for our existing spaces, and making sure those spaces continue to reflect the needs of the people who use them,” Cleypool wrote. “Community feedback is an important part of making sure we’re moving in the right direction.” Grand Rapids residents can submit comments by emailing parkinfo@grcity.us or writing a letter to the Department of Parks & Recreation (1500 Scribner Ave. NW, Grand Rapids, MI 49504) by 4:30 p.m. Nov. 30. items.t: Wendy’s gets buyout offer while struggling with beef prices and growing competition
items.x: Wendy’s shares jumped more than 14% Wednesday after noted investor Nelson Peltz made an offer to buy the chain, which has been struggling with high beef prices and aging stores. Peltz’s Trian Fund Management and several partners are offering Wendy’s $7.35 per share in cash, or a premium of nearly 19% over the stock’s closing price on Tuesday, in a deal that would take the company private. The offer values Wendy's at $1.4 billion. Wendy's, which is based in Dublin, Ohio, confirmed receipt of the unsolicited proposal in a statement Wednesday and said its board has formed an independent committee to evaluate it. At the end of last year, Wendy's had 5,969 restaurants in the U.S. and 1,428 outlets in 38 countries. Wendy's, founded in 1969 by Dave Thomas and named after his daughter, is known for its square burgers and Frosty desserts. The fast-growing chain introduced the drive-thru window in 1970 and went public in 1976. In the 1980s, as it jockeyed for sales with McDonald's and Burger King, Wendy's launched salad bars and ran its iconic “Where's the beef?” ad campaign. items.t: DoorDash to buy Instacart in $17 billion grocery delivery deal
items.x: DoorDash is gobbling up Instacart in a $17 billion acquisition that will supercharge its grocery delivery business. DoorDash said the Instacart brand name and app will remain, and Instacart shoppers can continue fulfilling orders for Instacart. Grocers can also choose to work with Instacart or DoorDash. Instacart customers will now have access to 50,000 additional stores covered by DoorDash, the company said. Instacart, founded in 2012, specializes in grocery and convenience store delivery in the U.S. and Canada. Its 600,000 “shoppers” — who are independent contractors — completed 338 million orders last year, according to company filings. Instacart has a market value of $14 billion. DoorDash, founded in San Francisco in 2013, began as a restaurant delivery business but has expanded to pet food and electronics. Operating in 40 countries, it completed more than 3 billion orders last year using a network of 9 million independent delivery workers. It has a market value of $73 billion. DoorDash began delivering groceries in 2020 amid a surge in pandemic-era demand. Grocers were initially cautious. The MV Odyssey set sail two years ago on a voyage to the seven continents marketed as combining long-term living at sea with global travel. Its operator had offered to “make the Odyssey your permanent home,” with the purchase price of a suite for the lifetime of the vessel starting around $230,000. This photo attained as part of the press kit by the Odyssey shows the U.S. cruise ship in Japan. (Odyssey via AP) For now, it is docked at the Cambodian port of Sihanoukville on the Gulf of Thailand, with no certain departure date. The ship has been carrying 203 passengers, mostly Americans, along with 156 crew members, according to Cambodian officials. It has a a 650-passenger capacity. Its Florida-based operator, Villa Vie Residences, said monthly fuel expenses per cabin that historically averaged $1,800 have reached an estimated $6,000 to $8,000 in parts of Asia due to the war in Iran. Most House Speakers in recent decades have stepped out of Congress after losing the gavel. And Reps. Steve Scalise (R-La.), the majority leader, and Jim Jordan (R-Ohio), a conservative icon, are both expected to launch bids to lead House Republicans if Democrats flip the chamber, according to GOP lawmakers, aides and strategists. items.x: GRAND RAPIDS, Mich. (WOOD) — Seasonal parking rules return to Grand Rapids on Nov. 1 as the city prepares to keep streets clean and accessible during the winter months. Each year, the rules take effect starting 12:01 a.m. Nov. 1 and continuing through 11:59 p.m. April 1. Odd-even parking limits street parking to only one side of a street from 1 a.m. to 6 a.m., alternating sides daily so that street sweepers and snowplows can clear the open side of leaves, branches and snow. On odd-numbered mornings, vehicles may park on the side with odd-numbered addresses; on even mornings, parking is allowed on the even side. Street signs indicate on what streets this rule will go into effect. Outside of the designated times, parking is allowed on either side of the street. Because odd-even parking takes place in the early morning, residents parking their car in the evening should choose which side to park on based on the next day’s date. For example, someone parking their car the evening of on Nov. 1 would park on the even side of the road because the rules would next go into effect from 1 a.m. to 6 a.m. on Nov. 2. items.t: How Forest Hills Public Schools’ new panic buttons work
items.x: ADA TOWNSHIP, Mich. (WOOD) — Forest Hills Public Schools is one of the first districts in the state to roll out a panic button system for emergencies. The buttons made by Centegix are wireless and carried by every staff member. They can be used to alert responders in the building and 911 directly. "The badge alert system is really quite simple for the user. There's not a lot for them to do. It's something that they wear,” Superintendent Ben Kirby said. “It's very small. It's like the size of a credit card." The district began using the system at the beginning of the school year. "The first week, we had seven engagements; six of those were medical," Kirby said. Based on what tap patterns staff use, the buttons can also trigger beacon lights, alerting people in the building of an emergency. "Pushing that button, it can be discreet — it can (also) be in the wide open — but there could be some time when you're having a face-to-face and you recognize that you have an issue and you can call for that help," Kirby said. The buttons can provide emergency responders a more detailed location of where the emergency is compared with a cellphone. Technology like this could eventually be mandated

items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war , creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle . items.t: What to know about Michigan’s two statewide ballot proposals
items.x: GRAND RAPIDS, Mich. (WOOD) — As voters go through their Nov. 3 ballots, after a slew of races for various offices and before local ballot questions, they will see two statewide proposals. Here's what you need to know about those proposals: PROPOSAL 1 Proposal 1 asks Michigan residents whether they the state to hold a constitutional convention. So what is a constitutional convention and why are we voting on it? In 1850 at a Michigan constitutional convention, it was agreed that the issue would come up for a vote automatically every 16 years. Voters usually decide against actually holding a so-called con-con: There have been only two since 1850. Con-Con? Michigan’s Proposal 1 If voters approve the ballot proposal this time around, another election would be held to select delegates to a convention. Those delegates would then discuss and debate what should be left alone, changed or done away with completely in the state Constitution. That process would apply to every single part of the Constitution, and for some who oppose Proposal 1, that is part of the problem. items.t: Helping kids adjust to the fall time change
items.x: GRAND RAPIDS, Mich. (WOOD) — The end of daylight saving time is right around the corner, and while gaining an extra hour sounds like a gift, many parents know the reality can feel a little different. After the clocks "fall back," some children suddenly start waking up before sunrise, while others have a hard time settling into their usual routines. The good news is that most kids adjust well with a little patience and consistency. According to the American Academy of Pediatrics, even a one-hour time change can affect a child's internal body clock, sometimes leading to temporary changes in sleep, mood, attention, and energy levels. Young children often notice the change the most, but school-age children and teens can feel the effects, too. The gradual shift strategy One simple way to make the transition easier is to start preparing a few days before the time change. Try shifting bedtime, wake-up time, meals, and naps about 10 to 15 minutes later every few days. These small adjustments can help children's bodies adapt gradually rather than all at once. That night, the restaurant got the "all clear" to reopen, it announced in a social media post . items.t: How to fix a harmful porn habit: 6 signs real help
items.x: Consumption of adult content is common, and for many individuals, it does not negatively impact their daily lives. However, a habit becomes problematic when an individual experiences a distinct loss of behavioral control alongside escalating real-world consequences. While pornography addiction is not listed as an official diagnosis in the American Psychiatric Association’s DSM-5, clinical frameworks recognize this pattern. The World Health Organization’s ICD-11 classifies it under Compulsive Sexual Behavior Disorder. This condition is defined by repeated, unsuccessful efforts to control intense sexual impulses, resulting in significant personal distress or impairment in social, work, or educational areas. Identifying the line between a casual habit and compulsive behavior is essential for regaining control. Below are six documented signs of problematic use, followed by evidence-based strategy options to help change the pattern. Repeated and unsuccessful efforts to cut back A primary indicator of compulsive behavior is the inability to reduce or halt the activity despite a conscious desire to do so.
