items.t: How to stop spoiling an adult child: 6 signs and limits
items.x: Providing financial assistance to family members is a natural extension of parental care. Research by the Pew Research Center indicates that a majority of parents with adult children have offered financial aid. In many instances, this support serves as a temporary safety net during legitimate hardships. However, a serious risk emerges when this assistance transforms from a temporary lifeline into a permanent lifestyle subsidy. When you routinely drain retirement savings or skip your own healthcare to cover a grown child's expenses, the dynamic is no longer sustainable. Recognizing the boundary between healthy support and financial exploitation is essential for protecting your future. Below are six distinct indicators that your generosity is being taken advantage of, followed by actionable steps to establish healthy financial boundaries. 1. They Only Call for Money A healthy parent-child relationship requires mutual connection. A child who completely disappears between financial emergencies and only resurfaces when rent or utility bills are due is showing a transactional view of the relationship. items.t: Cenecia Booker on the fitness lie women keep buying
items.x: Cenecia Booker is the founder of She Evolves Fitness LLC. At 19, fresh out of Air Force basic training, she became the primary caregiver for her two younger sisters after her mother was sentenced to state prison. She went on to spend 10 years in the Air Force Reserve and four years in law enforcement. In 2024, she chose to bet on herself and focus on empowering women as a certified fitness professional specializing in sustainable strength, functional movement and holistic health. You went from the Air Force and law enforcement to fitness. What led you to start She Evolves Fitness? Being in the Air Force and in law enforcement taught me structure and discipline. When I transitioned out, I knew I still wanted to serve and empower people, especially women, in a more proactive way than a reactive way. items.t: Smoking withdrawal symptoms and 7 ways to beat them
items.x: Smoking withdrawal is the set of symptoms your body and brain go through after you stop using nicotine, including strong cravings, irritability, anxiety, low mood, restlessness, trouble sleeping and difficulty concentrating. Symptoms are usually strongest in the first few days and ease over the next few weeks, according to federal health resources, though occasional cravings can pop up later. The good news is that they are temporary, and there are proven ways to make them easier to handle. Why does smoking withdrawal hit so hard? Nicotine reaches the brain within seconds and triggers dopamine, the chemical tied to reward. Over time, your brain adjusts to that steady supply. When it stops, your body protests. Many smokers mistake withdrawal symptoms for everyday stress, so a cigarette feels like relief when it is really just ending the withdrawal it caused. According to a review in JAMA by tobacco researcher Nancy Rigotti, about half of quit attempts fail within the first week, which is why having a plan matters. googletag.cmd.push(function() { var mapping_lb_1 = googletag.sizeMapping() .addSize([1084, 0], [[300, 250]]) .addSize([0, 0], [[300, 250]]) .build(); googletag.defineSlot('

items.t: Miami-Dade coastal flooding isn’t over as tides return tonight
items.x: Water at Miami’s Virginia Key tide gauge rose to 2.54 feet above the average higher high tide on Tuesday, Oct. 27. That is the third highest reading since steady records began there in 1994, according to the National Weather Service in Miami, which shared the milestone on X. Only Hurricane Wilma and Hurricane Irma pushed water higher. This time there was no hurricane. A king tide did it. A coastal flood warning remains in effect through 8 p.m. today for South Florida’s east coast, from Palm Beach County to the Florida Keys, including West Palm Beach, Fort Lauderdale, Miami and Homestead. A coastal flood advisory then runs from 8 p.m. today to 8 p.m. Thursday, with moderate flooding possible. items.t: Surrounded By People But Still Lonely? Here's Why It Happens — And Tips To Feel More Connected
items.x: Source: Vladimir Vladimirov / Getty Ever had a great time with friends, laughed until your stomach hurt, and still gone home feeling a little empty? You were surrounded by people, having fun, and technically doing everything you're supposed to do to feel connected. So, why does loneliness still creep in? If you've ever wondered, Why do I feel lonely even when surrounded by people?, you're not alone. And no, it doesn't mean there's something wrong with you. Between the chaos of social media, everyday pressures, and everything happening in the world socially and politically, it's easy to feel disconnected, even when your calendar is packed with plans. In fact, loneliness is more common than you might think. According to the World Health Organization , around 1 in 6 people worldwide experience loneliness. Research cited by the American Psychological Association (APA) also found that 54% of U.S. adults felt isolated, 50% felt left out, and 50% lacked companionship some or all of the time. items.t: The Soft Life Isn't Just About Spa Days – It's About Making Your Everyday Life Easier
items.x: Source: Cavan Images / Andrea Piacquadio / Getty Let’s be honest: between raising kids, managing a household, keeping up with work, supporting our partners, and trying to maintain some semblance of a social life, there are days when simply getting through the to-do list feels like a full-time job. Somewhere between preparing dinner, cleaning up the latest mess, and figuring out what everyone needs next, self care can easily fall to the bottom of the list. By the time we finally get home and settle in, all we want is a little peace, quiet, and time to breathe, the good old soft life. That’s why anything that makes everyday life easier deserves our attention. Self-care isn’t always about booking a spa day or escaping on a weekend getaway. Sometimes, it means spending less time cleaning, making meal prep less stressful, or having fresh drinking water ready at the touch of a button. After all, the less time we spend wrestling with household chores, the more time we have for the things that truly matter. The shooting took place near Florida A&M’s football stadium, where hundreds of people were celebrating the university’s homecoming weekend. The Tallahassee Police Department revealed in a statement that 15-year-old Anthony Rivers III is facing 11 counts of attempted second-degree murder and possession of a firearm by a delinquent. items.t: Chris Brown Receives Suspended Sentence In London Nightclub Brawl
items.x: Thaddaeus McAdams Chris Brown won't be going to jail despite pleading guilty in a London court following a 2023 nightclub brawl. The 37-year-old R&B star was sentenced to eight months in prison, suspended for 12 months, meaning he won't serve any time as long as he stays out of trouble. Brown was convicted of affray, which in the British justice system involves the use or threat of unlawful violence. He pleaded guilty on July 24 after denying more serious charges of attempting to cause grievous bodily harm and assault causing actual bodily harm, which prosecutors later dropped. Affray carries a maximum sentence of three years in prison. The charges stem from a 2023 incident at Tape, a private members' club in London's Mayfair neighborhood. Video footage showed Brown attacking producer and former friend Abraham Diaw on the dance floor, hitting him in the head twice with a bottle of tequila. Brown was shown continuing the assault as Diaw tried to get away. Diaw was later treated at a hospital for head and knee injuries. items.t: The Price of Play: Jalen Hurts And The Black QB Trap
items.x: Source: DeFodi Images / Getty America and the NFL have a problem with Black quarterbacks. Look at Jalen Hurts, the celebrated Black quarterback of the Philadelphia Eagles, whose recent health crisis has forced an undeniable hiccup for a league that prioritizes entertainment value over players' physical safety. After Hurts sustained a calf injury in early October, team doctors found a superficial blood clot ahead of a game in London. Doctors cleared him to play and to fly home afterward. A follow-up check back in Philadelphia revealed the clot had traveled to his lungs, resulting in a diagnosis of deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli, a potentially fatal condition. The diagnosis is expected to sideline him for the rest of the season . While the NFL cleared the Eagles medical staff of wrongdoing, the players’ union is now investigating the quality of care he was provided. For Black professionals, knowing that Hurts was pushing his body to the edge of survival is an all-too familiar reality. items.t: What We Need to Know: Midterms, Health Coverage, HBCU Homecoming and the NBA Tip-Off
items.x: The news moves fast, and keeping up can feel like a full-time job. Veteran broadcaster Sybil Wilkes helps by cutting through the noise. Her "What We Need to Know" segment delivers the stories that matter most to Black families, in clear and direct terms. This week's rundown covers voting, health, money, culture, and sports. Midterm Elections Are One Week Away The top story is the ballot box. The midterm elections take place on Tuesday, November 3. Early voting is already open in many states. Control of Congress, governors' offices, and local races are all at stake. School boards, judges, and city councils often shape daily life more directly than any national race. Voters should confirm their registration, check polling locations, and review sample ballots before heading out. Rules differ by state, so a quick visit to the local election office website can prevent surprises on Election Day. October Brings a Breast Cancer Wake-Up Call The focus then shifts from civic health to physical health. October is Breast Cancer Awareness Month, and the numbers remain sobering. items.t: Former Google engineer has stopped saving for retirement because he thinks AI will kill us
items.x: ( KRON ) A former Google AI safety expert is so confident artificial intelligence will destroy humanity he says he's stopped saving for retirement. Nate Soares worked at Google and Microsoft, spending more than 12 years working on AI alignment. Currently, he is the president of the Machine Intelligence Research Institute , a Berkeley nonprofit dedicated to identifying and mitigating the risks of AI. He is also the author of the book, "If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies," which warns of the existential risks of artificial intelligence. Speaking on an episode of the " The Most Interesting Thing in AI " podcast, Soares said that he stopped saving for retirement a decade ago. AI has delivered ‘zero’ payoff outside of tech, leading economist says "I do not save for retirement now," Soares told host Nicholas Thompson. "I have a 401K from when I worked at Google, but I haven't contributed to it for like a decade." "I guess right now it looks like we probably don't have a decade on the clock," Soares continued, adding that it's "More than 50% that we don't have a decade at this point." items.t: Democrats see battleground map expand to South Carolina, Florida, Mississippi
items.x: Democrats are giddy about the possibility of a bigger blue wave than expected in the battle for the Senate as polls show that South Carolina , Florida and Mississippi — three seats that were long seen as safe Republican holds — are now competitive races. Democrats view the Republican candidates running in those states as mediocre political talents who must fight historic headwinds caused by President Trump’s unpopularity, voter anger over inflation and the war in Iran, and burgeoning Democratic voter enthusiasm. The Senate battleground map has steadily expanded throughout the 2026 midterm election cycle as political handicappers have shifted seats that were thought to be in solidly Republican territory — such as Alaska, Iowa, Kansas and Texas — to the “toss-up" category. But now Republicans have to worry about losing Senate seats in states that were unthinkable as realistic Democratic pickup opportunities at the start of the election cycle, most notably South Carolina, which last elected a Democrat, Fritz Hollings, to the Senate in 1998. items.t: Dartmouth official resigns over AI use
items.x: ( The Hill ) A top Dartmouth official has resigned from his position after allegations that he violated the school's AI use policy. The university announced Wednesday that Provost Santiago Schnell resigned from his position after a university committee released the results of its investigation into the matter it opened in September. "The Provost used AI to meaningfully alter his writing in violation of at least one publication’s AI use and/or disclosure requirement, failed to disclose his use of AI in clear violation of a national newspaper’s stated policy, was not forthcoming about his AI use, and fell short of the standards set forth by Dartmouth’s Code of Ethical Conduct, the Academic Honor Principle, and Geisel’s Policy on Expectations for Professionalism for Faculty, Non-Faculty Academics, and Staff," the committee concluded. Schnell was accused of using AI to alter his work by the student newspaper The Dartmouth and outlet Semafor, specifically pointing to an opinion piece the provost wrote for The Washington Post. items.t: AAA advises drivers about daylight saving time
items.x: ( WAVY ) – It's only a few days until we trade one extra hour of sleep for months of darkness as we leave work to drive home. And even though we're on the easier end of the time transition (from daylight saving time to standard time), the switch still takes its toll. Nexstar's WAVY went to AAA Tidewater Virginia to see what commuters can expect. "Well, the biggest thing for drivers will be the change in daylight when we leave work or school," said Holly Dalby with AAA. "At the end of the day, gone will be the bright sunshine, and we will find ourselves either driving into the glare from the setting sun or driving home in the dark. So it's a time to be particularly careful on the roads." Days will get way shorter in November: How much daylight will we lose? While lawmakers have tried to get rid of the time switch altogether, it doesn't appear to be going anywhere anytime soon, so your circadian rhythm will have to dance to a different beat for a while. "It just messing with our sleep schedule can really add to our fatigue very quickly. And when we're fatigued, we can make mistakes," Dalby said. Two 12-year-olds reported the incident happened near Sequoia Station in the 1000 block of El Camino Real, the Redwood City Police Department said. Responding officers canvassed the area and obtained surveillance video showing the suspect. items.t: ‘Gut punch’: 2 college students found dead in Colorado after going missing on mountain hike
items.x: ( WJW ) – Two missing Colorado college students were found dead Wednesday after they left campus for a weekend trip up a nearly 14,000-foot peak and encountered a heavy snowstorm, police said. Kaden Matsuda, 19, from Ridgway, Colorado, and Jackson Donlon, 20, from New York, left Colorado Mountain College Leadville’s campus on Friday and didn’t return. They told family and friends they planned to go up Ice Mountain, which requires technical climbing, according to the county sheriff’s office. On Wednesday night, the sheriff's office confirmed that the students were found dead around 3:30 p.m. in a basin of the West Apostle Mountain. Authorities do not believe foul play was involved. The investigation is now being handled by the Chaffee County Coroner’s Office. “Our heart aches for Kaden and Jackson’s family and friends. We are very proud of our team’s efforts to find them before this weekend’s coming storm," Sheriff Andy Rohrich wrote on Facebook. "Although this is a gut punch, our prayers were answered that we would find Kaden and Jackson, allowing some closure for the family. We ask that everyone give time and distance to family members and friends as they mourn their loss.” Kaden

items.t: Cruise ship passenger says warning signs were there long before Cambodia
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — Kit Cassingham and her husband, Randy, sold their home and nearly everything they owned to live aboard a cruise ship for years. Now, she says she doesn't expect to see that money again. Cassingham told NewsNation's Jesse Weber on Wednesday that the couple paid about $370,000 to $380,000 for their cabin on the Villa Vie Odyssey, plus $7,000 a month in expenses. Asked if they will get it back, she said, "No, no, no, no." Cruise ship suspends voyage over fuel costs, stranding 200 passengers More than 200 passengers were told Tuesday to leave the Odyssey in Cambodia within hours after the cruise company suspended operations. In a news release , Villa Vie blamed soaring fuel costs tied to the war in Iran, saying the monthly fuel cost per cabin jumped from about $1,800 to as much as $8,000. Villa Vie Odyssey: How did passengers find out they had to leave? Cassingham and her husband had already gotten off the ship for a hotel so they could work online when a short message arrived saying the ship couldn't get more fuel . “You have till two o’clock to get off the ship,” she said. items.t: Wendy’s gets buyout offer while struggling with beef prices and growing competition
items.x: Wendy’s shares jumped more than 14% Wednesday after noted investor Nelson Peltz made an offer to buy the chain, which has been struggling with high beef prices and aging stores. Peltz’s Trian Fund Management and several partners are offering Wendy’s $7.35 per share in cash, or a premium of nearly 19% over the stock’s closing price on Tuesday, in a deal that would take the company private. The offer values Wendy's at $1.4 billion. Wendy's, which is based in Dublin, Ohio, confirmed receipt of the unsolicited proposal in a statement Wednesday and said its board has formed an independent committee to evaluate it. At the end of last year, Wendy's had 5,969 restaurants in the U.S. and 1,428 outlets in 38 countries. Wendy's, founded in 1969 by Dave Thomas and named after his daughter, is known for its square burgers and Frosty desserts. The fast-growing chain introduced the drive-thru window in 1970 and went public in 1976. In the 1980s, as it jockeyed for sales with McDonald's and Burger King, Wendy's launched salad bars and ran its iconic “Where's the beef?” ad campaign. items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: ( The Hill ) Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. Gasoline and energy costs have risen in six of nine months this year, as the Iran war sparked oil price shocks via the Islamic Republic's restrictions on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Persistent inflation , which has remained above the Fed's 2 percent target for five-and-a-half years, spurred central bank officials to hike interest rates by a quarter point in mid-September. items.t: Cloudy, cool Thursday in Bay Area
items.x: (BCN) Thursday in the Bay Area calls for mostly cloudy skies during the day, with patchy fog in some parts of the region, according to the National Weather Service. Daytime highs will be mostly in the mid 60s to low 70s. Overnight lows will be in the low to mid 50s. Forecasters say the Bay Area will see cloudy skies and cool temperatures on Thursday, with only a slight chance of light rain and a risk of minor coastal flooding during high tide. Winds are expected to remain light, with some breezier conditions in favored areas during the afternoon and evening. The weather service says a deep layer of dry air makes it unlikely that much rain will reach the ground. Any precipitation may evaporate before reaching the surface, a phenomenon known as virga. Forecasters do not rule out rain entirely, but any amounts are expected to be limited to a few sprinkles or hundredths of an inch, mainly on mountaintops. The weather service also warns of possible minor coastal flooding at high tide along the shores of San Pablo, San Francisco and Monterey bays, as well as the Pacific coast. items.t: DoorDash to buy Instacart in $17 billion grocery delivery deal
items.x: (AP) DoorDash is gobbling up Instacart in a $17 billion acquisition that will supercharge its grocery delivery business. DoorDash said the Instacart brand name and app will remain, and Instacart shoppers can continue fulfilling orders for Instacart. Grocers can also choose to work with Instacart or DoorDash. Instacart customers will now have access to 50,000 additional stores covered by DoorDash, the company said. Instacart, founded in 2012, specializes in grocery and convenience store delivery in the U.S. and Canada. Its 600,000 “shoppers” — who are independent contractors — completed 338 million orders last year, according to company filings. Instacart has a market value of $14 billion. DoorDash, founded in San Francisco in 2013, began as a restaurant delivery business but has expanded to pet food and electronics. Operating in 40 countries, it completed more than 3 billion orders last year using a network of 9 million independent delivery workers. It has a market value of $73 billion. items.t: RFK Jr. eases access to unproven peptides despite opposition from FDA scientists
items.x: WASHINGTON (AP) — The Trump administration on Wednesday acted to ease access to unproven peptide drugs favored by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr . Food and Drug Administration scientific staffers had little input on the decision and opposed the changes, according to six people familiar with its development. The draft policy posted online by Kennedy’s Department of Health and Human Services covers a handful of injectable peptides promoted within the wellness industry for uses such as building muscle, healing injuries and boosting energy. The government will take comments for two weeks before finalizing the measure. The document, primarily written by officials at HHS, faced overwhelming pushback among FDA drug staffers who warned it could undermine the agency’s long-standing mission of keeping unsafe health products off the U.S. market, according to the people familiar with its development. The game, originally scheduled for 5 p.m. Thursday, was moved to 9:30 a.m. because of a scheduling conflict at State Farm Arena in Atlanta, where the Atlanta Dream are hosting the game. The early start has frustrated some fans who say the change could make it difficult for people to watch a potentially championship-clinching game during the work and school day. “It's really embarrassing for the league, and they shouldn't do this to hurt their product,” one fan said. Detectives identified Jose Jesus Cornelio-Aguirre, 18, of San Pablo, as a prime suspect after "receiving an outpouring of cooperation, support, and information from the community," police officials wrote. "I think that going in the direction of impeachment is not a good idea, just to be honest with you," Harris told MeidasTouch's Aaron Parnas in an interview. "Just because we have limited resources and I think the energy and the resources need to put into accountability, need to be put into investigations." "And that's where the time should be spent," she added. "Remember, I was in the Senate for the last go-around, and the votes aren't there. "So, that's how I feel. But also, I think after the election, we all have to just also agree that our attitude has to be to get stuff done." Harris said Democrats should be "uncompromising" and "not sit around, you know, being genteel about the relationships," but maintain accountability when it comes to cuts to healthcare and oversight on the Iran war. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war , creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle . items.t: US stocks hold steady as the countdown ticks to a Federal Reserve decision on interest rates
items.x: NEW YORK (AP) — U.S. stocks are drifting Wednesday as the countdown ticks toward this afternoon’s announcement from the Federal Reserve on what it will do with interest rates . The S&P 500 rose 0.2% and pulled within 1% of its all-time high , which was set earlier this month. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 176 points, or 0.3%, as of 11:45 a.m. Eastern time, and the Nasdaq composite was virtually unchanged. The day’s highlight will likely be what the Federal Reserve says, if anything, about where interest rates are heading. The Fed raised its main interest rate last month for the first time in three years in hopes of slowing the high inflation that’s squeezing the economy and discouraging Americans . The widespread expectation on Wall Street is that the Fed will leave the federal funds rate alone at this meeting, and the question is whether it will give hints about what may happen at later meetings. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh, though, has been adamant since taking over the Fed about wanting it to give fewer indications about its future moves. items.t: Kawasaki motorcycle crash kills pedestrian in San Jose
items.x: (KRON) The San Jose Police Department is investigating a collision involving a motorcyclist that killed a pedestrian last Friday. The incident marks San Jose's 42nd fatal collision and 42nd traffic-related death of the year, as well as the city's 20th pedestrian death. SJPD responded at approximately 1:26 a.m. on Oct. 24 to the crash near South Bascom and Fruitdale avenues. "A 2024 Kawasaki motorcycle, occupied by an adult male driver, was traveling southbound on South Bascom Avenue north of its intersection with Fruitdale Avenue when it struck an adult male pedestrian who was crossing South Bascom Avenue in an unknown direction," said police. Both the motorcyclist and pedestrian were hospitalized with life-threatening injuries. The driver was later stabilized, but the pedestrian died from his injuries, according to police. The Santa Clara County Office of the Medical Examiner identified the pedestrian as Diego Armando Avila Tinoco, 29, of San Jose. Anyone with information tied to this case is urged to contact Detective Leslie of the SJPD Traffic Investigations Unit at 4264@sanjoseca.gov or call 408-277-4654.

items.t: Utah authorities connect 1974 cold case to serial killer Ted Bundy

Using DNA and other evidence, the Summit County Sheriff's Office and Summit County Attorney's Office formally closed the cold-case murder, saying that the evidence conclusively proves that Ted Bundy murdered 17-year-old Melissa Ann Smith. Bundy has long been considered a suspect in several cold cases in Utah, and Smith's murder was one of them. Hunters found her remains in Summit County on Oct. 27, 1974, 52 years ago today. "The work began with the investigators who handled the case in 1974, and it continued through the dedication and perseverance of those who carried it forward," Summit County Sheriff Kacey Bates said. "After 50 years, we have reached a point that so many have worked toward." September saw an uptick in annual inflation for Americans, with the cost of energy, gas and electricity rising from August to September. Democrats have campaigned on targeting the Trump administration's tariffs and the war in Iran — two factors behind U.S. price hikes. items.t: El Niño-linked waves push California water levels to historic highs
items.x: Ocean water levels along the California coast are reaching some of their highest readings in more than a century, with massive underwater waves linked to El Niño contributing to the unusually high seas, federal officials say. The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) reported Wednesday that tide stations across California have recorded new or broken water level records, including readings in Los Angeles, San Diego, La Jolla and Santa Barbara. The elevated levels are being driven by a combination of unusually high tides associated with the full moon and the moon's close approach to Earth, along with oceanic Kelvin waves moving north along the West Coast, according to NOAA. NOAA data shows unusually high water levels exceeding the minor flooding threshold in La Jolla, California, in October 2026. Erik Eduardo Navarro, 26, of Orange County, had been on the run since late August, the San Bernardino County Sheriff's Department said. It all began when Therese Garcia, 71, had welcomed Navarro into her Crestline home after she spotted him walking in his neighborhood. He told the woman a “heartbreaking” story about all of his belongings being stolen while he was camping nearby. Therese sympathized with him and agreed to let him stay at her house temporarily. items.t: North Korea targeting cash-strapped Americans in expanding job scam: FBI
items.x: The FBI is warning Americans about an expanding North Korean scheme that uses fake job opportunities, stolen identities and unsuspecting U.S. residents to infiltrate American companies and help finance the country's nuclear weapons program. In an Oct. 13 public safety alert , the agency said thousands of state-controlled North Korean information technology workers are using increasingly sophisticated tactics to secure remote jobs at Western companies while concealing their identities and locations. Federal investigators warned that the workers are now recruiting Americans, particularly those experiencing financial hardship, to help carry out the fraud, sometimes without realizing they are assisting a foreign government. The scheme has also escalated beyond employment fraud, with the FBI documenting instances of extortion, data theft and threats of physical violence. How North Korean operatives recruit Americans According to the FBI, North Korean operatives frequently advertise seemingly legitimate freelance opportunities on popular employment websites, offering payment for tasks that may initially appear harmless. items.t: Southern California sex trafficker sentenced to 74 years to life in prison
items.x: A Southern California man who fled from authorities while he was on trial for sex trafficking two victims, including a teen girl, was sentenced to 74 years to life in prison. Calvin Lane, 40, of Gardena, is also a convicted sex offender, according to the Los Angeles County District Attorney’s Office. The investigation began on July 9, 2023, when Long Beach police responded to reports of a “person in distress” near 67th Street and Long Beach Boulevard. At the location, officers found a teen girl who was a trafficking victim. During their investigation, detectives learned the suspect had driven the girl to Los Angeles to work as a commercial sex worker. “While the victim was being sex trafficked, she was physically and sexually assaulted,” police said. The trafficker later transported the girl to Long Beach, where she continued to work as a commercial sex worker. Calvin Lane, 40, of Gardena, a man who fled from authorities while he was on trial for sex trafficking a teen girl and a woman, was captured and sentenced to 74 years to life in prison. items.t: Russell Brand denies all charges as he takes the stand at his rape and sex assault trial
items.x: Russell Brand acknowledged in a London court on Wednesday that he had been obsessed with sex as a younger man, but denied multiple charges of rape and sexual assault , saying the claims have had a “devastating” impact on his life. The British actor-comedian entered Southwark Crown Court alongside his wife, Laura Gallacher, to testify in his own defense, telling reporters that “today is the day for truth and justice.” Brand, 51, stood in the witness box and took the oath, then gave his full name: Russell Edward Brand. He answered “no” to each charge as his lawyer, Ian Winter, asked whether he was guilty of three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault and one count of attempted indecent assault. Brand said the allegations had had a “devastating” impact, with friends and colleagues abandoning him. items.t: Murder suspect arrested in Mexico months after Santa Monica shooting
items.x: A 26-year-old Southern California man accused of fatally shooting another man during an altercation near Santa Monica High School earlier this year was arrested in Mexico and returned to the United States to face murder and attempted murder charges, authorities announced. Manuel Reyes, a resident of Adelanto in San Bernardino County, was arrested on Oct. 20 in Nayarit, Mexico, more than six months after the deadly shooting, according to the Santa Monica Police Department. Deadly shooting near Santa Monica High School The March 28 incident occurred around 10:30 p.m. near the intersection of 4th Street and Olympic Drive, less than a block from Santa Monica High School. Officers responding to reports of gunfire located a man suffering from a gunshot wound and began providing emergency medical care. Paramedics transported the victim to a local hospital, where he was later pronounced dead. During the confrontation, police said one of the occupants pulled out a firearm and fired at least one shot, striking the victim. Investigators determined that an altercation between occupants of two vehicles preceded the shooting. The shooter fled the area before officers arrived. The deadly March 28

items.t: Layoffs reach Disney’s theme parks division, at least 100 people impacted: LAT
items.x: Layoffs have reached the Happiest Place on Earth, affecting the company’s theme parks division, according to the Los Angeles Times. The report, citing a person familiar with the matter who was not authorized to comment publicly, said The Walt Disney Company is laying off between 100 and 200 people. The cuts to Disney’s Experiences segment stem from a regular evaluation of the division’s priorities, investments and project timelines, the person said. Disney Experiences includes the company’s parks, cruise line, and Aulani Resort and Spa in Hawaii. Disney will notify all affected employees by the end of the day Wednesday, according to the report. The layoffs are limited to the experiences division. items.t: Frontier Airlines airfare jumps 71% in third quarter
items.x: High fuel prices are squeezing just about all of us, and they're having a major impact on the transportation industry. Frontier Airlines, the country's largest budget carrier, just revealed in its third quarter, their fares jumped 71% because of soaring jet fuel costs. The carrier's fare revenue averaged almost $68 per passenger in that quarter, compared with about $40 a year earlier. Then you tack on fees for baggage and seating and other services, and suddenly total revenue per passenger was up 30% to $138. These higher fares illustrate how sky-high energy costs related to the war in Iran are slamming the economy, impacting consumers from the gas pump to the airline terminal. In another alarming example of this impact, it was reported that a luxury cruise line had to drop off hundreds of passengers in Cambodia as their round-the-world voyage came to a sudden halt because high-fuel costs were bringing everything to a stop on board. Higher energy prices are a key factor in rising inflation, which is impacting consumers across the board. While the Federal Reserve held interest rates steady on Wednesday, it's likely we're going to see either a quarter-point or a half-point rate hike

items.t: Press Pause: Find Your Zen at The Reset Room in South L.A.
items.x: Sometimes the best thing you can do for yourself is simply hit the reset button! In the heart of South L.A.'s Adams District, The Reset Room is creating a peaceful escape from the hustle and bustle of everyday life. Founded by certified yoga instructor Adriana Gasaway, this wellness experience combines breathwork, meditation, and sound healing to help guests relax, recharge, and learn techniques to regulate their nervous systems. Gasaway's journey into wellness began during the pandemic when she launched Ace Naturals, her skincare and body butter line. Today, she's expanding her mission from nourishing the body to nurturing the mind and spirit. LA Unscripted's Jasmine Simpkins stopped by Violet Noir, the event space where The Reset Room hosts classes every Tuesday and Thursday, to learn how a little intentional stillness can go a long way toward finding balance. For more information visit their instagram . This segment aired October 6, 2026.

items.t: It’s a Party with Party Goats LA
items.x: Party Goats La brings unforgettable fun, charm and a little farmyard magic to celebrations or brush clearings throughout Los Angeles. The friendly, lovable goats make unique guests at birthday parties, hikes, private events, school gatherings, yoga classes and special celebrations of all kinds. Beyond the parties, the hardworking goats also provide eco-friendly brush clearance in fire-prone areas. The goats help reduce excess vegetation and support wildfire prevention efforts through natural land management. For more information visit their website and Instagram . This segment aired October 8, 2026.

items.t: Magical Blooms: Where Flowers Meet a Little Magic
items.x: Located in Redondo Beach, Magical Blooms is more than just a flower shop — it's a celebration of beauty, creativity, and the joy that fresh flowers can bring to everyday life. Founded by Jenny Barker, also known as “The Flower Doctor,” this boutique florist creates handcrafted arrangements using fresh, carefully selected blooms, with an emphasis on color, texture, and the meaning behind each stem. From romantic bouquets and vibrant seasonal arrangements to weddings and special events, every design is created with a personal touch and plenty of love. But the magic doesn't stop at the flowers! Magical Blooms offers unique experiences designed to bring people together, including hands-on floral workshops and an enchanting afternoon tea surrounded by beautiful blooms. With a philosophy that flowers can uplift your mood, inspire connection, and transform a space, Jenny and her team are all about making life a little more beautiful. Whether you're sending a thoughtful gift or treating yourself to something special, Magical Blooms is a reminder that sometimes the simplest things can bring the greatest joy. Find out more on their website . This segment aired October 8,2026.

items.t: From Altadena to SoFi Stadium: Orla Floral’s Inspiring Journey
items.x: For Los Angeles native Renata Ortega, founder of Orla Floral, flowers have become a symbol of resilience and new beginnings. After losing her home and floral studio in the Altadena fire, Ortega relocated her business to North Hollywood, where she's continuing to blossom. LA Unscripted's Jasmine Simpkins visited her showroom to hear about her journey, which includes being selected for FIFA's small business supplier program to provide floral arrangements for SoFi Stadium during the World Cup. No stranger to large-scale projects, Ortega has delivered anywhere from 1,200 to 1,500 floral arrangements in a single week! From corporate clients to weddings, parties, and private events, she says no job is too big or too small. Her philosophy? Floral design is like cooking — the better the ingredients, the better the final product. She also shared a few expert tips for creating beautiful arrangements at home. For more visit Orla's website and Instagram. This story aired on October 8, 2026.

items.t: Your One-Stop Beauty Escape: Inside Milk + Honey Spa
items.x: A little milk, a little honey, and a whole lot of pampering! Inspired by Cleopatra, who was famously said to bathe in milk and honey to maintain her beautiful skin, Milk + Honey Spa is putting a modern twist on the royal treatment. Founded in Austin, Texas in 2006, the luxury day spa has expanded to 10 locations nationwide over the past two decades. LA Unscripted's Jasmine Simpkins stopped by the Brentwood location to chat with community manager Lexie Bennett about the brand's growth and its mission to create a one-stop destination for beauty and wellness. From massages and facials to waxing, nail services, and even injectables, Milk + Honey offers a full menu of treatments in a serene, Zen-inspired setting designed to help guests relax, recharge, and leave feeling like royalty. For more visit their website and instagram . This segment aired October 13, 2026.

items.t: From The Notebookto Outer Banks: Charleston’s Hollywood Connection
items.x: Lights, camera, ghosts! Charleston, South Carolina, is known for its Southern charm, rich history, and reputation as one of America's most haunted cities. But did you know it's also a Hollywood hot spot? As one of the oldest cities in the country, Charleston has provided the perfect backdrop for countless movies and television shows. LA Unscripted's Jasmine Simpkins headed to "The Holy City" to explore some of its most famous filming locations, including historic Boone Hall Plantation, featured in The Notebook , Alex Haley's Queen , North and South , Army Wives , and even American Idol . Then things took a spooky turn with Bulldog Tours' popular Ghosts and Graveyards tour, exploring some of Charleston's most haunted locations. And fans of Netflix's Outer Banks may recognize a few familiar sights, as much of the hit series is filmed in and around Charleston. From Hollywood history to haunted hideaways, this Southern city has plenty of stories to tell — both on and off screen. For more Hollywood happenings in Charleston visit their website and instagram This segment aired October 15, 2026.

items.t: FOXBLOOD: For Babes Who Wear Black author: Olivia de Bortoli
items.x: For those who love a little darkness in their wardrobe, FOXBLOOD is redefining alternative fashion with a modern, wearable twist. Founded in 2017 by former red-carpet stylist and stage wear designer Lindsay Hearts, the Los Angeles-based, female-owned brand specializes in minimalist, gothic-inspired clothing that blends edgy style with everyday comfort. From statement dresses and sleek black staples to accessories and footwear, FOXBLOOD offers size-inclusive pieces for anyone looking to embrace their darker side. With its gothic aesthetic and all-black everything, FOXBLOOD is a natural fit for Halloween season. Whether you're putting together a show-stopping costume, searching for a witchy look for a Halloween party, or simply want to bring a little spooky style into your everyday wardrobe, the brand has you covered. At FOXBLOOD, Halloween isn't just one day of the year — it's a whole vibe! Visit its Melrose Avenue storefront in Los Angeles or shop the collection online . This segment aired October 15, 2026.

items.t: Mystery, Magic and Thrills All Year Long at The Mystic Museum author: Dayna Devon
items.x: Step into the wonderfully weird world of The Mystic Museum in Burbank, a one-of-a-kind destination celebrating horror movies, the supernatural, the occult and all things delightfully macabre. Located in the eclectic Magnolia Park neighborhood, this immersive attraction combines unusual curiosities, vintage oddities, gothic treasures and ever-changing exhibits inspired by cult horror films and pop culture. Visitors can explore interactive installations, shop the unique collectibles and capture unforgettable photos in movie-inspired settings. Whether you’re a lifelong horror fan, a lover of the unusual or simply looking for an extraordinary Los Angeles experience, the Mystic Museum is your one-stop shop. For more information visit their website and Instagram . This segment aired October 15, 2026.

items.t: Get Connected with Community at The Aster
items.x: The Aster is more than just an award-winning boutique hotel, it’s an exclusive members’ club that fosters community, connection, creativity and more! Or for those simply needing a new workspace, consider the Club Lounge for your new office! But these amazing member benefits are also available for all hotel guests so book your day – or your stay – and consider The Aster your second home! Attorneys announced a federal civil rights complaint connected to the death of Eric Valencia, a father of two children. Surveillance video showed the 37-year-old leaving the Azusa police station on March 23 following a DUI arrest. Valencia then opened the door of an unlocked police cruiser parked in front of the station and climbed inside. Footage 37-year-old Eric Valencia following his arrest for DUI on March 20. (Azusa PD) His body was reportedly found in that car three days later, on March 26, by a civilian employee just before 5 a.m. Before his body was discovered, Valencia was reported missing by family members. "My son can't go to sleep without crying for his dad," said Justine, the mother of Valencia's children. "I'd never, ever imagine something like this could ever happen to us. I wish Eric was better taken care of when he was in custody, and I hope that we get the answers that we're looking for." items.t: Hayden Panettiere death ruled accidental by police in South Carolina
items.x: GREENVILLE, S.C. ( WSPA ) – Police in South Carolina have officially closed the investigation into the death of Hayden Panettiere, according to a Wednesday news release. Greenville Police Department officials said that Panettiere's death has been ruled accidental, based on findings in the investigation and the medical examiner's determination. On August 16, Panettiere was found unresponsive in an apartment at the Judson Mill Lofts on Easley Bridge Road. Police said that Brian Hickerson, Panettiere's on-and-off boyfriend, along with his brother, Zach Hickerson, were at the residence. EMS attempted life-saving measures before pronouncing Panettiere dead at 2:31 p.m. According to the Greenville County Coroner's Office, Panettiere had died from an accidental overdose of fentanyl, 4-ANPP, Alprazolam, Methocarbamol and Quetiapine. Panettiere had spoken openly about challenges in her personal life, including emotional scars from her childhood fame, postpartum depression after giving birth to her daughter, and struggles with alcohol addiction. items.t: TikTok launches Must Eat restaurant guide in L.A. Here are some of the restaurants featured
items.x: TikTok has launched a new restaurant discovery feature designed to help users find popular local dining spots. The feature, called Must Eat, debuted Wednesday in the Los Angeles, New York City, and San Francisco Bay Area regions. Here's how the new feature works TikTok said the tool expands on its existing local discovery efforts by highlighting restaurants that have gained attention from the platform's food-focused community. Users can browse restaurants by city and filter results by cuisine, location, price point, and score. Each restaurant listing includes neighborhood information, pricing details and related TikTok videos. Users can also save restaurants to their TikTok collections and build personalized lists of places they want to visit. The guide is accessible through TikTok's search function, Local feed, points-of-interest pages and location tags attached to videos associated with participating restaurants. The company said the feature launches as food discovery continues to play a growing role on the platform. items.t: Suspect arrested in Mexico for Inland Empire shooting; mother arrested for driving him there
items.x: A young man was arrested for a June shooting after authorities tracked him down to Mexico, and two other people, including his mother, have been arrested for accessory after the fact. The San Bernardino County Sheriff’s Department announced the update to the case on Wednesday . According to SBSD, the investigation began on June 8 at 2:26 a.m. when deputies from the Fontana Station were dispatched to the 2500 block of North Arctic Drive in San Antonio Heights on reports of a shooting. When the deputies got to the scene, they found a victim with multiple gunshot wounds, and he was taken to a hospital for treatment. No information regarding the victim’s condition or identity were released; however, preliminary information obtained by authorities indicated the shooting “stemmed from an argument.” Further investigation led to the identification of a suspect – 19-year-old Andres Cruz – and authorities were able to track his movements, learning that he was taken to the Metrolink station in Montclair “immediately” after the shooting by Gabriel Magana. items.t: Ernie Johnson reveals he’s leaving ‘Inside the NBA’ after this season: ‘It’s time’
items.x: It's the end of an era for sportscaster Ernie Johnson. On Wednesday morning, the longtime host of "Inside the NBA" announced that the 2026-2027 NBA season will be his last at the legendary anchor desk. "It's time," he wrote in the caption on Instagram . Decked out in his iconic three-piece suit and bowtie, he revealed to fans that after 37 years, he's ready to make a fast break into the next chapter. "I've long described it as a get-to job. (I'm) still amazed that I get to do this for a living. Now, as the years have gone by, and I turned 70 this past summer, folks have asked me, So, how long are you going to keep doing Inside?' Well, I want to take a couple of minutes of your time to answer that. This will be my last season," he explained. "Totally my decision. It's just time. It's been an honor to share so many nights, decades, actually, at the desk with my brothers Kenny, Charles, and Shaq, and with our production crews who are so talented and devoted, and I so appreciate the leadership at TNT and ESPN for allowing the show to continue." items.t: Prince Jackson hopes to finally make ‘Thriller’ hit No. 1
items.x: Michael Jackson's song "Thriller" was released over 40 years ago, and it remains a hit. While the "Thriller" album spent a record-breaking 37 weeks on the Billboard 200, the single itself only reached the No. 4 spot in 1984. Jackson's eldest son, Prince, and fans of the King of Pop want to change that with the "Thriller Challenge." "You've got the album that is stacked with incredible songs, right? So the goal is to try and get my father's song Thriller,' the single, to number one," he explained on the KTLA 5 Morning News. "The way that we encourage people to do that is to request the play from radio stations, buy the single, buy the vinyls, the albums, and stream it as much as you can, because we are trying to get my father another number one." Since it is spooky season, the single has become synonymous with Halloween. Over the weekend, Prince's Heal Los Angeles Foundation held an event at the iconic Palace Theatre in downtown Los Angeles, where part of the music video was filmed. Proceeds from the event go to the foundation, which supports young people in the greater L.A. area. items.t: Thousands in golf clubs stolen at religious charity event in Camarillo
items.x: A 45-year-old Camarillo resident has been arrested for allegedly stealing thousands of dollars' worth of golf clubs during a religious charity event at a Ventura County country club earlier this month. Investigators said Las Posas Country Club was hosting the charity event for a local religious organization when staff discovered someone had taken several thousand dollars' worth of golf clubs before fleeing the area. Responding deputies used surveillance footage and witness statements to develop a vehicle description and identify a possible suspect, according to a news release from the Ventura County Sheriff's Office. Despite not having a license plate number, authorities were able to use a feature of the Sheriff's Office Automated License Plate Reader system to search for the vehicle based on its description, ultimately identifying the vehicle and a suspected driver, Brian Banner. A search warrant was served Thursday at Banner's home in the 900 block of Sharon Drive. He was later arrested and booked on suspicion of grand theft. items.t: American naturalization rates have declined ‘sharply,’ new research finds
items.x: Naturalization rates have declined “sharply” across America, with California particularly affected, according to new research . The study, conducted by experts from UCLA’s Center for Neighborhood Knowledge, determined that becoming a United States citizen has “become increasingly more difficult” by analyzing changes in national and state rates of naturalization. The findings: there were 76% fewer legal immigrants gaining citizenship nationwide under the administration of President Donald Trump as compared to the administration of President Joe Biden. At a broader scope, UCLA experts say that annual naturalization rates grew “dramatically” between the 1990s and 2024, by which time the monthly average was over 70,000. For comparison, there were peaks of over a million people in 1996 and 2008. items.t: Southern California’s coastal flooding is a problem now. Expert warns it could get worse
items.x: From San Diego to Los Angeles, coastal communities are getting inundated as high tides have sent ocean water cascading over berms and boardwalks, flooding roads, homes and businesses . Newport Beach’s Balboa Peninsula and the International Boardwalk in Redondo Beach were among the areas that saw flooding on Tuesday, and more flooding is expected in the coming days. Experts say ocean water levels are shattering records this fall due to several factors converging all at once: long-term sea-level rise, normal tides caused by the pull of the sun and the moon, and the emerging effects of a “super” El Niño , a periodic warming of ocean temperatures in the tropical Pacific. A search-and-rescue operation was launched at the almost 8,600-foot summit in the Tahoe National Forest, with assistance requested from the Nevada County Sheriff's Search and Rescue Mountain Rescue Team and the Washoe County Sheriff's Office RAVEN helicopter. items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war , creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle . items.t: Could hackers shut off your water? SoCal agencies prepare
items.x: Cyberattacks don’t just put personal information at risk. They could also disrupt essential services, including the water systems we depend on every day. “So you could have a wastewater plant that’s completely down. You could have a water district that can no longer serve the 150,000 customers that they intended to serve, right? And then they could actually replicate that through different water districts or different agencies,” said Ephraim Gonzalez of TEC-Refresh. That’s why local water agencies are teaming up through a regional cybersecurity coalition called ERNIE. The goal is to share information, strengthen their defenses and practice how to respond if hackers get into their systems. One concern is the automation used to operate water systems. “So if they control the automation, then they can change chemical amounts. But there’s set points to stop that. There’s a series of set points, a series of procedures that we go through to try to stop anything that harms anyone,” said Angel Cisneros of the Inland Empire Utilities Agency. Freeways expand, transit systems improve, and technology promises more efficient journeys. Yet travelling across the city can still take a remarkable amount of time. A British aerospace company believes part of the solution might be above the roads rather than on them. Vertical Aerospace has demonstrated an electric aircraft capable of taking off vertically, transitioning into conventional forward flight, and landing without a runway. The technology was publicly displayed at the Farnborough International Airshow in Britain, marking an important development in the company's plans to introduce commercial passenger flights. items.t: Utah authorities connect 1974 cold case to serial killer Ted Bundy
items.x: Investigators in Summit County, Utah, closed the 1974 cold case homicide of Melissa Ann Smith Tuesday, linking her murder to prominent serial killer Ted Bundy. Using DNA and other evidence, the Summit County Sheriff's Office and Summit County Attorney's Office formally closed the cold-case murder, saying that the evidence conclusively proves that Ted Bundy murdered 17-year-old Melissa Ann Smith. Bundy has long been considered a suspect in several cold cases in Utah, and Smith's murder was one of them. Hunters found her remains in Summit County on Oct. 27, 1974, 52 years ago today. "The work began with the investigators who handled the case in 1974, and it continued through the dedication and perseverance of those who carried it forward," Summit County Sheriff Kacey Bates said. "After 50 years, we have reached a point that so many have worked toward." items.x: A 39-year-old inmate serving a sentence for assault with a deadly weapon in Los Angeles County was killed Monday night in an attack involving two other prisoners in Folsom. The deadly incident unfolded around 6:43 p.m. on Oct. 26 at California State Prison, Sacramento, when correctional officers witnessed two inmates attacking another prisoner on the upper tier of a housing unit, according to the California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation (CDCR). Authorities identified the victim as Carlos Montenegro and the alleged attackers as 47-year-old Justin Castro and 33-year-old Luis Mendoza. Correctional officers immediately responded to the attack, ordering the inmates to get down, but their commands were ignored, officials said. Officers then fired five less-lethal 40mm impact rounds to stop the assault. items.t: AAA advises drivers about daylight saving time
items.x: ( WAVY ) – It's only a few days until we trade one extra hour of sleep for months of darkness as we leave work to drive home. And even though we're on the easier end of the time transition (from daylight saving time to standard time), the switch still takes its toll. Nexstar's WAVY went to AAA Tidewater Virginia to see what commuters can expect. "Well, the biggest thing for drivers will be the change in daylight when we leave work or school," said Holly Dalby with AAA. "At the end of the day, gone will be the bright sunshine, and we will find ourselves either driving into the glare from the setting sun or driving home in the dark. So it's a time to be particularly careful on the roads." While lawmakers have tried to get rid of the time switch altogether, it doesn't appear to be going anywhere anytime soon, so your circadian rhythm will have to dance to a different beat for a while. "It just messing with our sleep schedule can really add to our fatigue very quickly. And when we're fatigued, we can make mistakes," Dalby said. items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: ( The Hill ) Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. Gasoline and energy costs have risen in six of nine months this year, as the Iran war sparked oil price shocks via the Islamic Republic's restrictions on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Persistent inflation , which has remained above the Fed's 2 percent target for five-and-a-half years, spurred central bank officials to hike interest rates by a quarter point in mid-September. items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war , creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle . items.t: New Mexico man breaks state record for giant pumpkin, again
items.x: NEW MEXICO (KRQE) — The average riding horse is just over 930 pounds. A grand piano weighs about 990 pounds. In growing this massive pumpkin, Clark broke the state record for giant pumpkin . That record, by the way, was set by Clark in 2025 with a 1,010-pound pumpkin. And in 2024, he grew the biggest pumpkin the New Mexico State Fair had seen at 947 pounds. It's all a labor of love that starts well before spooky season. "I started the seed about the first or second week of April. Planted it outside as soon as the temperature allowed, which was the first couple of weeks of May," said Clark, who describes himself as a gardening enthusiast. "And then the pollination took place late June. And so from late June until harvest, the pumpkin was maybe 110 days old. So all that growth happens in a very rapid three month or so period." items.x: NEW MEXICO (KRQE) – Dolores Huerta, the New Mexico-born activist who spent more than six decades fighting for farm workers, women, and civil rights, has died at the age of 96. Archuleta County officials reveal details of damages left behind by flooding Her life was defined by a simple message: “Sí, se puede” — yes, we can. Local leaders gathered Wednesday to remember Huerta and the lasting impact she had on New Mexico and the nation. “There’s some people that you just feel like they’re going to be around forever. They’re going to live forever,” New Mexico Lt. Gov. Howie Morales said. Huerta was born in the small mining town of Dawson, New Mexico, in 1930. After beginning her career as a teacher, Huerta turned to organizing in the 1960s. She joined César Chávez in the fight to organize farm workers, helping build what would become the United Farm Workers. Huerta helped organize workers, negotiate contracts, and advocate for safer working conditions for agricultural workers. She helped lead a consumer boycott of grapes that led to the California Agricultural Labor Relations Act of 1975, which allowed farm workers to form unions and negotiate for better working conditions and pay. The MV Odyssey set sail two years ago on a voyage to the seven continents marketed as combining long-term living at sea with global travel. Its operator had offered to “make the Odyssey your permanent home,” with the purchase price of a suite for the lifetime of the vessel starting around $230,000. This photo attained as part of the press kit by the Odyssey shows the U.S. cruise ship in Japan. (Odyssey via AP) For now, it is docked at the Cambodian port of Sihanoukville on the Gulf of Thailand, with no certain departure date. The ship has been carrying 203 passengers, mostly Americans, along with 156 crew members, according to Cambodian officials. It has a a 650-passenger capacity. Its Florida-based operator, Villa Vie Residences, said monthly fuel expenses per cabin that historically averaged $1,800 have reached an estimated $6,000 to $8,000 in parts of Asia due to the war in Iran. items.t: 68 dead in high-speed train collision, Spain’s 2nd deadly rail crash this year
items.x: URDA, Spain (AP) — A high-speed train slammed into another that had stopped on the tracks in Spain on Wednesday, killing at least 68 people and injuring dozens in the second deadly rail collision this year. The regional government of Castilla La Mancha confirmed the death toll and said another 58 people were receiving medical treatment at hospitals. Rescue workers searched the wreckage through the day for survivors and bodies. The collision came just nine months after another deadly crash involving high-speed trains operated by the same two companies in southern Spain in January. “Today all of Spain is grieving,” Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said from the crash site, where he announced that his government would declare three days of national mourning. items.t: Flying taxis could carry passengers by 2030
items.x: (TestMiles) A British aerospace company has demonstrated an electric flying taxi that could eventually offer a new way to escape crowded city roads. The Flying Car Is Moving Beyond Science Fiction Los Angeles has spent decades trying to solve its traffic problems. Freeways expand, transit systems improve, and technology promises more efficient journeys. Yet travelling across the city can still take a remarkable amount of time. A British aerospace company believes part of the solution might be above the roads rather than on them. Vertical Aerospace has demonstrated an electric aircraft capable of taking off vertically, transitioning into conventional forward flight, and landing without a runway. The technology was publicly displayed at the Farnborough International Airshow in Britain, marking an important development in the company's plans to introduce commercial passenger flights. The aircraft is part of a growing category known as electric vertical takeoff and landing, or eVTOL. Unlike a conventional airplane, it does not require a runway for every departure. items.t: La Plata residents who use private wells advised to use bottled water after flooding
items.x: Colorado (KRQE) – With extreme flooding often comes high levels of water contamination. In an effort to keep residents safe and healthy, La Plata County officials in southern Colorado are urging the use of bottled water. San Juan County communities begin long road to recovery after weekend flood The La Plata County Public Health Department said private wells in the Animas Valley may be damaged. Those wells could contain contaminants that cannot be removed with simple boiling. County officials are providing bottled water at the La Plata County Fairgrounds from 3 p.m. to 6 p.m. beginning on Wednesday. Each resident is allotted two cases of bottled water per day. They said they will also provide clean-up kits. According to the health department, well water should not be used if: Floodwater reached your well. There is standing water around the well. Your well cap or well casing looks damaged. You notice sediment in the water. Your water pressure suddenly changes.

items.t: Democrats see battleground map expand to South Carolina, Florida, Mississippi
items.x: Democrats are giddy about the possibility of a bigger blue wave than expected in the battle for the Senate as polls show that South Carolina , Florida and Mississippi — three seats that were long seen as safe Republican holds — are now competitive races. Democrats view the Republican candidates running in those states as mediocre political talents who must fight historic headwinds caused by President Trump’s unpopularity, voter anger over inflation and the war in Iran, and burgeoning Democratic voter enthusiasm. The Senate battleground map has steadily expanded throughout the 2026 midterm election cycle as political handicappers have shifted seats that were thought to be in solidly Republican territory — such as Alaska, Iowa, Kansas and Texas — to the “toss-up" category. But now Republicans have to worry about losing Senate seats in states that were unthinkable as realistic Democratic pickup opportunities at the start of the election cycle, most notably South Carolina, which last elected a Democrat, Fritz Hollings, to the Senate in 1998. In a Facebook post, the Ocala Police Department explained that the young men — ages 20, 19 and 18 — had removed a chair from a nearby restaurant to use during the challenge. But while the 18-year-old was seated and getting his hair cut, a traffic accident nearby sent a Chevrolet 3500 in their direction. The two other suspects were able to move out of the way, but the 18-year-old "was seated with his back to the oncoming truck" and was hit by the vehicle. Blake wasn’t just another bull rider who came through our gates,” wrote the rodeo. “He was our family, our friend and someone who meant so much to so many of us. His absence will be felt every time those gates open.” Local police seek help finding missing 15-year-old boy According to the rodeo, Saylor loved the sport, the animals and the community. A portion of Saturday night’s proceeds will be given to Saylor’s family. “The rodeo arena has always been a place that brings us together, and this Saturday will mean a little more than most. We know it won’t be easy without Blake there, but we also know how much he loved this sport, these animals, and the people who surrounded him,” wrote the rodeo. “Thank you to everyone who has reached out, offered support and kept Blake’s family in your thoughts

items.t: Hostage rescued, suspect dead in Oxford
items.x: OXFORD, Ohio ( WDTN ) A reported hostage situation early Thursday morning is under investigation in Oxford. Around 3:42 a.m., Oxford officers were sent to the 600 block of South College Avenue for a domestic dispute that turned into a hostage situation. Police determined a male was holding a female hostage against her will. When law enforcement arrived, they reportedly heard gunshots inside a building. Once they identified the specific apartment, officers tried making contact with the suspect, prompting him to call law enforcement. While talking to him, Butler County Regional SWAT was reportedly called to assist with the incident. During negotiations, SWAT coordinated a rescue operation of the hostage. Oxford police said two gunshots were heard "a short time later" from where the suspect was. Authorities cleared the residence and found the suspect deceased from an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound.

items.t: AAA advises drivers about daylight saving time
items.x: ( WAVY ) – It's only a few days until we trade one extra hour of sleep for months of darkness as we leave work to drive home. And even though we're on the easier end of the time transition (from daylight saving time to standard time), the switch still takes its toll. Nexstar's WAVY went to AAA Tidewater Virginia to see what commuters can expect. "Well, the biggest thing for drivers will be the change in daylight when we leave work or school," said Holly Dalby with AAA. "At the end of the day, gone will be the bright sunshine, and we will find ourselves either driving into the glare from the setting sun or driving home in the dark. So it's a time to be particularly careful on the roads." Days will get way shorter in November: How much daylight will we lose? While lawmakers have tried to get rid of the time switch altogether, it doesn't appear to be going anywhere anytime soon, so your circadian rhythm will have to dance to a different beat for a while. "It just messing with our sleep schedule can really add to our fatigue very quickly. And when we're fatigued, we can make mistakes," Dalby said. "We can be distracted more easily. lose focus, inattention. Fatigue has a lot of impact o

items.t: Old Wendy’s near Dayton Mall set for demolition
items.x: MIAMI TOWNSHIP, Ohio ( WDTN ) A former restaurant in front of the Dayton Mall is expected to be demolished. Records obtained by 2 NEWS show plans to demolish the defunct Wendy's restaurant at 2948 Miamisburg Centerville Road. On Wednesday, two yellow barricades and plastic mesh material were placed at the entrance and along the sides of the property to block people from entering the future construction site. Former Wendy's Miami Township | Carlos Mathis/Photo Former Wendy's Miami Township | Carlos Mathis/Photo Former Wendy's Miami Township | Carlos Mathis/Photo According to records, the space where the building sits will be filled and the lot will be graded. Wendy's operated for several decades at the site until its abrupt closure in December 2024 . WDTN.com is working to learn what's next for the site.

To win the Senate, Democrats will have to break through on Republican turf . Of the Cook Political Report's seven toss-ups , five are in states Trump won by double digits in 2024. items.t: Judge orders competency evaluation for quadruple homicide suspect
items.x: DAYTON, Ohio (WDTN) Judge Gerald Parker is ordering a new look at the mental state of a Butler Township quadruple homicide suspect. Stephen Marlow is accused of killing four of his neighbors in Aug. 2022 before fleeing to Kansas. Judge Parker took over the case in June after the previous judge retired. The judge recently ruled that the state and court must both conduct competency evaluations by the end of the year. Marlow's last competency hearing was completed in May 2025. Dayton NAACP sending DeWine letter requesting clemency for China Arnold We are working to learn what comes next.

items.t: ‘Gut punch’: 2 college students found dead in Colorado after going missing on mountain hike
items.x: ( WJW ) – Two missing Colorado college students were found dead Wednesday after they left campus for a weekend trip up a nearly 14,000-foot peak and encountered a heavy snowstorm, police said. Kaden Matsuda, 19, from Ridgway, Colorado, and Jackson Donlon, 20, from New York, left Colorado Mountain College Leadville’s campus on Friday and didn’t return. They told family and friends they planned to go up Ice Mountain, which requires technical climbing, according to the county sheriff’s office. On Wednesday night, the sheriff's office confirmed that the students were found dead around 3:30 p.m. in a basin of the West Apostle Mountain. Authorities do not believe foul play was involved. The investigation is now being handled by the Chaffee County Coroner’s Office. “Our heart aches for Kaden and Jackson’s family and friends. We are very proud of our team’s efforts to find them before this weekend’s coming storm," Sheriff Andy Rohrich wrote on Facebook. "Although this is a gut punch, our prayers were answered that we would find Kaden and Jackson, allowing some closure for the family. We ask that everyone give time and distance to family members and friends as they mourn their loss.” Kaden

items.t: Cruise ship passenger says warning signs were there long before Cambodia
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — Kit Cassingham and her husband, Randy, sold their home and nearly everything they owned to live aboard a cruise ship for years. Now, she says she doesn't expect to see that money again. Cassingham told NewsNation's Jesse Weber on Wednesday that the couple paid about $370,000 to $380,000 for their cabin on the Villa Vie Odyssey, plus $7,000 a month in expenses. Asked if they will get it back, she said, "No, no, no, no." Cruise ship suspends voyage over fuel costs, stranding 200 passengers More than 200 passengers were told Tuesday to leave the Odyssey in Cambodia within hours after the cruise company suspended operations. In a news release , Villa Vie blamed soaring fuel costs tied to the war in Iran, saying the monthly fuel cost per cabin jumped from about $1,800 to as much as $8,000. Villa Vie Odyssey: How did passengers find out they had to leave? Cassingham and her husband had already gotten off the ship for a hotel so they could work online when a short message arrived saying the ship couldn't get more fuel . “You have till two o’clock to get off the ship,” she said. The news wasn't a total shock. “We’d seen red flags all along,” Cassingham said. More than 200

items.t: Wendy’s gets buyout offer while struggling with beef prices and growing competition
items.x: Wendy’s shares jumped more than 14% Wednesday after noted investor Nelson Peltz made an offer to buy the chain, which has been struggling with high beef prices and aging stores. Peltz’s Trian Fund Management and several partners are offering Wendy’s $7.35 per share in cash, or a premium of nearly 19% over the stock’s closing price on Tuesday, in a deal that would take the company private. The offer values Wendy's at $1.4 billion. Wendy's, which is based in Dublin, Ohio, confirmed receipt of the unsolicited proposal in a statement Wednesday and said its board has formed an independent committee to evaluate it. At the end of last year, Wendy's had 5,969 restaurants in the U.S. and 1,428 outlets in 38 countries. Wendy's, founded in 1969 by Dave Thomas and named after his daughter, is known for its square burgers and Frosty desserts. The fast-growing chain introduced the drive-thru window in 1970 and went public in 1976. In the 1980s, as it jockeyed for sales with McDonald's and Burger King, Wendy's launched salad bars and ran its iconic “Where's the beef?” ad campaign.
