items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: ( The Hill ) Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. Gasoline and energy costs have risen in six of nine months this year, as the Iran war sparked oil price shocks via the Islamic Republic's restrictions on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Persistent inflation , which has remained above the Fed's 2 percent target for five-and-a-half years, spurred central bank officials to hike interest rates by a quarter point in mid-September. items.t: DoorDash to buy Instacart in $17 billion grocery delivery deal
items.x: DoorDash is gobbling up Instacart in a $17 billion acquisition that will supercharge its grocery delivery business. DoorDash said the Instacart brand name and app will remain, and Instacart shoppers can continue fulfilling orders for Instacart. Grocers can also choose to work with Instacart or DoorDash. Instacart customers will now have access to 50,000 additional stores covered by DoorDash, the company said. Instacart, founded in 2012, specializes in grocery and convenience store delivery in the U.S. and Canada. Its 600,000 “shoppers” — who are independent contractors — completed 338 million orders last year, according to company filings. Instacart has a market value of $14 billion. DoorDash, founded in San Francisco in 2013, began as a restaurant delivery business but has expanded to pet food and electronics. Operating in 40 countries, it completed more than 3 billion orders last year using a network of 9 million independent delivery workers. It has a market value of $73 billion. DoorDash began delivering groceries in 2020 amid a surge in pandemic-era demand. Grocers were initially cautious. items.t: RFK Jr. eases access to unproven peptides despite opposition from FDA scientists
items.x: WASHINGTON (AP) — The Trump administration on Wednesday acted to ease access to unproven peptide drugs favored by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr . Food and Drug Administration scientific staffers had little input on the decision and opposed the changes, according to six people familiar with its development. The draft policy posted online by Kennedy’s Department of Health and Human Services covers a handful of injectable peptides promoted within the wellness industry for uses such as building muscle, healing injuries and boosting energy. The government will take comments for two weeks before finalizing the measure. The document, primarily written by officials at HHS, faced overwhelming pushback among FDA drug staffers who warned it could undermine the agency’s long-standing mission of keeping unsafe health products off the U.S. market, according to the people familiar with its development. items.t: Giant tortoise located by Dayton humane society
items.x: The Humane Society of Greater Dayton is looking to return a sulcata tortoise to their home. The giant tortoise was located by the shelter and are thankful to have done so when they did. "With nighttime temperatures starting to drop, we’re glad we were able to get this big guy somewhere safe and warm," said the Humane Society of Greater Dayton via social media. items.t: 61-year-old dead after semi crash in Clark County
items.x: CLARK COUNTY, Ohio (WDTN) One person is dead after a single-vehicle crash involving a semi. The Springfield Patrol Post of OSP confirmed that the driver of the vehicle died. He was identified as Dennis Ault, 61, of Springfield. The vehicle was transporting milk before the crash. An initial investigation determined that the semi crashed into a tree after driving off the right side of I-70 East. Hazmat crews and CareFlight were each called to the scene to assist OSP. The crash happened around5:10 a.m. The right lane of I-70 E. beyond US-40 remains closed as of 10:09 a.m.

Steve Scalise (R-La.), the majority leader, and Jim Jordan (R-Ohio), a conservative icon, are both expected to launch bids to lead House Republicans if Democrats flip the chamber, according to GOP lawmakers, aides and strategists. They don't have solutions to actual problems, so they'd rather have the media and you talking about the Cheesecake Factory.” Obama had quipped during a recent campaign stop in Cleveland, Ohio, that Trump’s taste in renovations worth a reported $900 million has the White House “looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory, it’s just gold everywhere,” referring to the Iraqi palaces that were famously adorned with gold decor. items.t: Giannis Antetokounmpo has 24 points, 18 rebounds as the Heat beat the Hawks 129-117 for first win
items.x: ATLANTA (AP) — Giannis Antetokounmpo had 24 points and 18 rebounds in his first victory with the Heat, leading Miami over the Atlanta Hawks 129-117 on Wednesday night. Bam Adebayo also had 24 points and grabbed nine rebounds for the Heat, who lost their first four games after acquiring Antetokounmpo from Milwaukee in the offseason. Adebayo passed Udonis Haslem to become the Heat's career leader in rebounds . Andrew Wiggins scored 18 points and Pelle Larsson had 17 points, eight assists and six rebounds for the Heat, who shot 53% from the field and had a whopping 70 points in the paint. Rookie Kingston Flemings and Nickeil Alexander-Walker each scored 23 points for the Hawks, who have dropped three in a row after opening the season with consecutive wins. Jalen Johnson shot just 4 for 12 and finished with 12 points, 11 assists and nine rebounds. The Hawks were playing the first game of a home back-to-back. The start of their game against Cleveland on Thursday was pushed back an hour so that Game 6 of the WNBA Finals between Atlanta and Golden State could be played at State Farm Arena during the afternoon. items.t: After two-year search, woman’s coworker turns out to be a match for kidney transplant
items.x: SALT LAKE CITY, Utah ( ABC4 ) — Katie Hood and Reina Child became fast friends five years ago when they met as coworkers at Charlie's Produce in Salt Lake City. Then two years ago, Katie, 41, was diagnosed with renal failure. Family, friends and even coworkers began getting tested to see if they were a match. Reina, 47, knew she needed to be tested. And guess what? She is a perfect match. Now, the bond the two ladies share will grow even stronger because on Tuesday they're scheduled for kidney transplant surgery. The women had a pre-operation appointment today ahead of their surgery next Tuesday. "She's an inspiration to so many because even though she's struggling, she's smiles and laughs with you," Reina said about Katie. It all started in October 2024. "I had been really swollen for a while, and it got to the point where walking upstairs was just hard," explained Katie. She decided to go to the doctor, which led to an emergency room visit. That visit changed Katie's life. She was diagnosed with heart and kidney failure. "And I've been doing dialysis for three times a week for two years and yeah, just kind of on this crazy journey." items.t: Union officer recognized for helping elderly man
items.x: UNION, Ohio ( WDTN ) – The Union Police Department is recognizing Officer David Clarkston for helping a man with dementia back on Tuesday, Oct. 20. Clarkston received a report that an elderly man suffering from dementia had gotten lost while driving in the area. Although information suggested the vehicle was in another county, Clarkston remained on alert. Within minutes, he saw the car traveling through the city and conducted a traffic stop. Clarkston was able to ensure the man was safe and contact his son, who helped his father get home safely. “This is a great example of what policing is all about,” wrote the UPD. “It’s not always about making arrests or issuing citations. Sometimes, it’s simply about being in the right place, paying attention, and helping someone who needs it.”

items.t: DOJ’s California ballot fight rejected by another judge
items.x: ( The Hill ) The Trump administration's bid to separate 20,000 mail ballots in California that it says are likely noncitizens met another defeat on Wednesday as a trial judge refused to intervene. U.S. District Judge David Carter ruled California can continue to accept the questioned ballots like any other. “This request violates longstanding constitutional principles mandating that states have control over their elections,” Carter wrote. “If Plaintiff’s last-minute request for relief were granted, either party could create chaos for their own political purposes to disrupt the election process,” he continued. “Over 20,000 registered Californians would potentially lose the right that generations of Americans have fought to preserve.” California has raised eyebrows at the veracity of the administration's list and says it's not obligated to verify voters’ citizenship in response. The state has conceded it's not feasible to segregate a ballot once it's processed. It would be counted even if later found to be fraudulent. items.t: Visit Greater Springfield wins four OTA RUBY Awards
items.x: SPRINGFIELD, Ohio ( WDTN ) – Visit Greater Springfield received four Ohio Travel Association (OTA) RUBY Awards for statewide marketing excellence at the 2026 Conference on Travel. The RUBY Awards recognize outstanding achievement in tourism, marketing, advertising, and communication across Ohio’s hospitality and travel industry. Visit Greater Springfield was recognized in four categories: marketing campaign, travel guides & planners, website, and promotional video. “These awards reflect the story our community tells every day,” said Christopher Schutte, vice president of destination marketing communications for the Greater Springfield Partnership. “The visitor guide, our website, the video, and the Find Your Unwind campaign are all built to show travelers what makes Greater Springfield worth the trip—and it’s an honor to have our peers across the state recognize that work.”

items.t: Winter is coming: ODOT urges caution around snowplows
items.x: DAYTON, Ohio ( WDTN ) – Winter is coming, and ODOT is preparing for whatever may happen as the days get colder. This past season, crews drove more than 9 million miles and used over 800,000 tons of salt to plow Ohio roads. In preparation for the upcoming season, ODOT has already gathered 600,000 tons of salt, as well as nearly 2,000 plow trucks and around 3,000 full-time and seasonal drivers. However, when the snow rolls in, officials want drivers to remain extra careful around snowplows in order to make sure both you and their workers get home safely. “Leaving with extra time before you need to get to work or wherever your destination is, it’s giving yourself plenty of extra space between you and the driver in front of you,” said ODOT Public Information Officer Loryn Bryson. “Our big trucks, they don’t stop quickly, and so the more room you can give us, the better.” Last season, plows were hit nearly 60 times.

items.t: Failed Florida gubernatorial candidate announces 2028 White House bid

items.t: Springfield, governor officially welcome aircraft startup
items.x: An $850 million investment first announced this summer is now taking shape in Springfield. After announcing in July that Electra would build its new EL9 Ultra Short aircraft, Ohio Gov. Mike DeWine officially welcomed the company to the Miami Valley during a special event at Springfield-Beckley Municipal Airport Wednesday. The nine-passenger EL9 is designed to do things that most planes cannot, such as take off and land in only 150 feet. The hybrid-electric aircraft is meant for trips of less than 250 miles. "They're making flying taxis," said DeWine. The construction of a new facility and staffing is expected to create nearly 2,000 jobs in Clark County. "We see this as coming to the new neighborhood," said Electra CEO Marc Allen. "The neighbors have been so gracious and pull out a chair and offer a meal." "I think that going in the direction of impeachment is not a good idea, just to be honest with you," Harris told MeidasTouch's Aaron Parnas in an interview. "Just because we have limited resources and I think the energy and the resources need to put into accountability, need to be put into investigations." "And that's where the time should be spent," she added. "Remember, I was in the Senate for the last go-around, and the votes aren't there. "So, that's how I feel. Harris said Democrats should be "uncompromising" and "not sit around, you know, being genteel about the relationships," but maintain accountability when it comes to cuts to healthcare and oversight on the Iran war. items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war , creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle . The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 176 points, or 0.3%, as of 11:45 a.m. Eastern time, and the Nasdaq composite was virtually unchanged. The day’s highlight will likely be what the Federal Reserve says, if anything, about where interest rates are heading. The Fed raised its main interest rate last month for the first time in three years in hopes of slowing the high inflation that’s squeezing the economy and discouraging Americans . The widespread expectation on Wall Street is that the Fed will leave the federal funds rate alone at this meeting, and the question is whether it will give hints about what may happen at later meetings. items.t: Cornell preps for no-confidence vote against president after Jane Doe’s allegations: What to know
items.x: ( The Hill ) The Cornell University Faculty Senate is set to debate a no-confidence vote on Wednesday against President Michael I. Kotlikoff after allegations of a 2024 gang rape at a campus fraternity that resulted in no criminal charges caused uproar around the country. The more than 75 members of the body will have their second meeting debating the resolution and the timing of a vote on it. A motion could be introduced to delay the no-confidence vote and set another meeting. But if that motion is not introduced or fails, members of the Faculty Senate will begin the no-confidence vote after Wednesday's meeting is over, and they typically have a week to cast their choice online. While a no-confidence vote has no authority to remove an official, its passing would show deep dissatisfaction from faculty with how Cornell leadership has handled accusations from Jane Doe that seven members of the Chi Phi fraternity raped her . What does the no-confidence vote entail? items.t: Sabato’s Crystal Ball moves 16 House races toward Democrats
items.x: ( The Hill ) – Nonpartisan election forecaster Sabato’s Crystal Ball is shifting more than a dozen House races toward Democrats in the final week of the campaign , another sign of a worsening political environment for Republicans. Crystal Ball, a division of the University of Virginia’s Center for Politics, has moved dozens of races toward Democrats in recent weeks, including nearly 50 races in the month of October alone. The race changes include moving a few deep-red seats into the “toss up” column. Open congressional districts in Kentucky and Montana, as well as seats with GOP incumbents in Missouri, Virginia, Colorado and Pennsylvania moved into coin flip territory. Many of the seats Crystal Ball rates as a toss-up were places Trump carried by double digits in 2024. Trump says he made the mistake' of studying' GOP senator's anatomy' One notable race that moved from toss-up to “leans Democratic” is Texas’s 15th Congressional District, where Rep. Monica de la Cruz (R) is facing a tough challenge from Tejano music star Bobby Pulido (D). The election was widely seen as a referendum on Netanyahu , the country’s longest-serving prime minister, who gave a defiant speech to his supporters just after 3 a.m. on Wednesday in Jerusalem despite the unclear results. With around 70% of the votes counted on Wednesday afternoon, his party, Likud, appears to have gotten the most votes, capturing around 20% of the popular vote. This was a dip from the previous election in 2022, when Likud won 23.4% of the popular vote. items.x: The Neon is set to reopen in a major way on Friday. As Corner Store nears completion of principal photography , Dayton's independent theater will open with two indie bangers: "You Can See Everything" and "Wicker." The latter will feature special guest Darden Bradshaw, who will be at the theater doing basket weaving demonstrations in the lobby on Friday and Saturday showings of the film. ‘Who wants a full season?’: Trailer for Ohio comedy debuts Darden is a fiber artist and educator, who works primarily in weaving, felting and basketry. items.t: US cruise ship suspends voyage in Asia due to fuel costs, stranding 200 passengers
items.x: SIHANOUKVILLE, Cambodia (AP) — A U.S. cruise ship on an around-the-world voyage that touted its cabins as floating homes suspended its three-year voyage in Cambodia due to fuel costs, forcing hundreds of passengers to disembark. The MV Odyssey set sail two years ago on a voyage to the seven continents marketed as combining long-term living at sea with global travel. Its operator had offered to “make the Odyssey your permanent home,” with the purchase price of a suite for the lifetime of the vessel starting around $230,000. The ship has been carrying 203 passengers, mostly Americans, along with 156 crew members, according to Cambodian officials. It has a a 650-passenger capacity. Its Florida-based operator, Villa Vie Residences, said monthly fuel expenses per cabin that historically averaged $1,800 have reached an estimated $6,000 to $8,000 in parts of Asia due to the war in Iran. "FreeLance" follows a young filmmaker who moves in with an equally ambitious group of friends, all of whom take odd jobs to build their brands and pay the bills. items.t: Flying taxis could carry passengers by 2030
items.x: (TestMiles) A British aerospace company has demonstrated an electric flying taxi that could eventually offer a new way to escape crowded city roads. The Flying Car Is Moving Beyond Science Fiction Los Angeles has spent decades trying to solve its traffic problems. Freeways expand, transit systems improve, and technology promises more efficient journeys. Yet travelling across the city can still take a remarkable amount of time. A British aerospace company believes part of the solution might be above the roads rather than on them. Vertical Aerospace has demonstrated an electric aircraft capable of taking off vertically, transitioning into conventional forward flight, and landing without a runway. The technology was publicly displayed at the Farnborough International Airshow in Britain, marking an important development in the company's plans to introduce commercial passenger flights. The aircraft is part of a growing category known as electric vertical takeoff and landing, or eVTOL. Unlike a conventional airplane, it does not require a runway for every departure. items.t: 68 dead in high-speed train collision, Spain’s 2nd deadly rail crash this year
items.x: URDA, Spain (AP) — A high-speed train slammed into another that had stopped on the tracks in Spain on Wednesday, killing at least 68 people and injuring dozens in the second deadly rail collision this year. The regional government of Castilla La Mancha confirmed the death toll and said another 58 people were receiving medical treatment at hospitals. Rescue workers searched the wreckage through the day for survivors and bodies. The collision came just nine months after another deadly crash involving high-speed trains operated by the same two companies in southern Spain in January. “Today all of Spain is grieving,” Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said from the crash site, where he announced that his government would declare three days of national mourning. items.t: Trump and Talarico hold dueling Texas rallies
items.x: ( The Hill ) President Trump and Texas Senate candidate James Talarico (D) shared their competing visions Tuesday as the two held dueling rallies in the Lone Star State one week before the midterm elections. Trump did two rallies in Texas — the first in Corpus Christi and another in Lubbock . It’s his fourth trip to Texas to support Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton. Talarico held his own rally in Lubbock on Tuesday. He was in Corpus Christi on Saturday. The Texas race is one of the most contested and watched Senate races in the country. Talarico and Paxton remain close in the polls — Real Clear Polling calls the race a toss-up, with Talarico holding a slight lead. A Democrat winning the Senate seat would be a shock — none have won a U.S. Senate race in Texas since 1988, and Trump won the state by nearly 14 percentage points in the 2024 presidential election. Democrats are vying to take control of the House and the Senate. The party would need to win four seats to win control of the Senate. items.t: Kristina Knickerbocker holds rally at Wright State University
items.x: DAYTON, Ohio ( WDTN ) – Democrat Kristina Knickerbocker held a rally at Wright State University tonight alongside David Hogg, co-founder of Leaders We Deserve, and Nico Agosta, co-founder of the Political Integrity Project. Knickerbocker is running for Congress in Ohio’s 10 th Congressional District, which is currently held by Republican incumbent Mike Turner. Knickerbocker, a U.S. Air Force veteran and nurse practitioner, says she wants to challenge the status quo. “It has to be people in my generation, and generations to come, to say no, we do not have to think it’s okay,” said Knickerbocker. “We can bring better values and new ideas to make sure to solve a lot of the problems that we are seeing caused by this administration.” Over the weekend, Congressman Turner was knocking on doors in Belmont and Oakwood to talk with voters. Libertarian Tom McMasters is also running for the seat.

items.t: Wilberforce University wins $3 million grant for tech project
items.x: WILBERFORCE, Ohio ( WDTN ) – Wilberforce University has been awarded a $3 million grant from the Title III Strengthening Institutions Program to help the university implement its Technology and Rural Digital Equity Project. The project aims to modernize eight classrooms with interactive digital displays, 4K auto-tracking cameras, high-performance computers, and integrated hybrid-learning systems. An additional $550,000 of the grant will go toward transforming portions of the Rembert E. Stokes Library, and $667,000 will support adaptive learning platforms to identify students who may need additional academic support. The award is the school’s largest single-source federal grant outside regular Title III funding since 2023.

items.t: Ohio allocates $1.8M to reduce nutrient runoff
items.x: DAYTON, Ohio ( WDTN ) – Several counties across Ohio are receiving funds for water quality projects aimed at reducing nutrient soil run-off. The $1.8 million in H2Ohio funds will help nine soil and water conservation districts maintain healthy soil cover and prevent nutrient loss into waterways. According to leaders with the Ohio Department of Agriculture, implementing these practices benefits everyone in the state. “The agricultural community, as they have been for many years, are being part of the solution when it comes to water quality here in the state of Ohio,” said Director Brian Baldridge. “Everybody in Ohio cares about that.” Some of the counties receiving funds include Clermont, Brown, and Highland.

"It feels like a full-circle moment that we're here now talking about the beginning of our journey on long-form video," she said. items.t: Utah authorities connect 1974 cold case to serial killer Ted Bundy
items.x: SUMMIT COUNTY, Utah ( KTVX ) — Investigators in Summit County, Utah closed the 1974 cold case homicide of Melissa Ann Smith Tuesday, linking her murder to prominent serial killer Ted Bundy. Using DNA and other evidence, the Summit County Sheriff's Office and Summit County Attorney's Office formally closed the cold-case murder, saying that the evidence conclusively proves that Ted Bundy murdered 17-year-old Melissa Ann Smith. Bundy has long been considered a suspect in several cold cases in Utah, and Smith's murder was one of them. Hunters found her remains in Summit County on Oct. 27, 1974, 52 years ago today. "The work began with the investigators who handled the case in 1974, and it continued through the dedication and perseverance of those who carried it forward," Summit County Sheriff Kacey Bates said. "After 50 years, we have reached a point that so many have worked toward." items.t: Democrats see battleground map expand to South Carolina, Florida, Mississippi
items.x: Democrats are giddy about the possibility of a bigger blue wave than expected in the battle for the Senate as polls show that South Carolina , Florida and Mississippi — three seats that were long seen as safe Republican holds — are now competitive races. Democrats view the Republican candidates running in those states as mediocre political talents who must fight historic headwinds caused by President Trump’s unpopularity, voter anger over inflation and the war in Iran, and burgeoning Democratic voter enthusiasm. The Senate battleground map has steadily expanded throughout the 2026 midterm election cycle as political handicappers have shifted seats that were thought to be in solidly Republican territory — such as Alaska, Iowa, Kansas and Texas — to the “toss-up" category. But now Republicans have to worry about losing Senate seats in states that were unthinkable as realistic Democratic pickup opportunities at the start of the election cycle, most notably South Carolina, which last elected a Democrat, Fritz Hollings, to the Senate in 1998. (WFLA) — Video shows the moment a woman had a close encounter with a great white shark when she reached off of a fishing boat to pet it, causing the shark to lunge and thrash. items.t: Vigilando los Trópicos: ¿Qué esperar en noviembre? Atlántico sigue tranquilo mientras la humedad de Vance podría llevar más lluvia a EE.UU.
items.x: TAMPA, FLA. (WFLA-TAMPAHOY) — A poco más de un mes del cierre oficial de la temporada de huracanes, el Atlántico permanece sin ciclones tropicales. En el Pacífico, la tormenta tropical Vance se debilita frente a México, pero la humedad asociada al sistema se desplaza hacia el centro-sur y el suroeste de Estados Unidos. El Centro Nacional de Huracanes pronosticó que Vance se debilitaría durante el jueves y se convertiría en un remanente. Mientras tanto, la lluvia asociada al sistema podría provocar inundaciones y deslizamientos de tierra en el oeste de México, particularmente en Sinaloa, Durango y Nayarit. La humedad de Vance también podría contribuir a lluvias adicionales en algunas regiones de Estados Unidos al interactuar con otros sistemas. El Centro Nacional de Huracanes indicó que se extendería a partes del centro-sur y suroeste del país. En esta edición de Vigilando los Trópicos, nuestra meteoróloga Zuleika Soler repasa cómo va la temporada en el Atlántico, qué se puede esperar durante noviembre y dónde la humedad de Vance podría aumentar las lluvias y el riesgo de inundaciones. items.t: Florida missing boater found after being lost at sea for 3 days
items.x: Video above: See the week's top headlines in Tampa Bay MARCO ISLAND, Fla. (WFLA)— A missing boater who spent three days at sea in extremely rough conditions was rescued near Coon Key Pass, the Marco Island Police Department announced. The U.S. Coast Guard requested help from Marco Island Fire Rescue's Fireboat 50, the Collier County marine unit, and the Marco Island Police Department marine unit after losing communication with the boater on Oct. 27. According to officers, the Collier County marine unit located the missing boater on Wednesday around 16 miles southwest of Coon Key Pass. Credit: Marco Island Police Department Credit: Marco Island Police Department The boater reportedly spent three days at sea in extremely rough conditions, MIPD said. Fireboat 50 arrived and brought the boater aboard to provide medical attention. "This successful rescue highlights the importance of teamwork, communication, and coordination among our public safety partners. We are grateful for the dedication of everyone involved and the continued cooperation of the Collier County Marine Emergency Response Team in keeping our waterways safe," the Marco Island Police Department said.

items.t: Armed citizens hold knife-wielding woman at gunpoint at Polk County Dollar General: sheriff
items.x: POLK COUNTY, Fla. (WFLA) — A woman who threatened customers at a Polk County Dollar General with a knife was arrested after two armed citizens held her at gunpoint until deputies arrived, according to the sheriff's office. The Polk County Sheriff's Office shared surveillance video on Tuesday of Natalia Gaviria, 26, of Kissimmee entering the Dollar General while allegedly intoxicated. She then pulled out a knife and began waving it around while threatening customers. "One of the managers starts running out the back door because she's afraid she's going to stab some of them, and she stabs a soda bottle," Polk County Sheriff Grady Judd said. PCSO said employees helped customers evacuate the store and called 911. Credit: PCSO Two armed citizens then drew their "legally carried firearms" and held Gaviria at gunpoint until deputies arrived, PCSO said. "Way to got Polk County!" Judd said, praising the citizens for stepping in. Gaviria was arrested and charged with disorderly intoxication, theft involving the soda bottle and two counts of assault. items.t: Noah Kahan announces show at Raymond James Stadium in Tampa
items.x: TAMPA, Fla. (WFLA) Grammy-nominated artist Noah Kahan is stopping in Tampa on his stadium tour next year. Kahan, known for songs like "Stick Season" and "Northern Attitude," will perform at Raymond James Stadium on April 29, 2027. It is the only Florida show on his The Last of the Bugs tour. Artist presale tickets will be available on November 10 at noon. Fans must register on the Ticketmaster website by November 5 to participate. The Reserved by Spotify presale will take place on November 11 at 9 a.m. Tickets may be available to eligible U.S. Spotify Premium subscribers through Ticketmaster. These fans will be notified by Spotify via email and app notification, and will have the opportunity to purchase up to two tickets during the presale. The remaining tickets will go on sale to the general public on November 12. Tickets for the Tampa show will be priced between $59.95 and $399.95, according to Kahan's website . Kahan's last tour, The Great Divide World Tour, sold more than 1.8 million tickets worldwide.

items.t: RFK Jr. eases access to unproven peptides despite opposition from FDA scientists
items.x: WASHINGTON (AP) — The Trump administration on Wednesday acted to ease access to unproven peptide drugs favored by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr . Food and Drug Administration scientific staffers had little input on the decision and opposed the changes, according to six people familiar with its development. The draft policy posted online by Kennedy’s Department of Health and Human Services covers a handful of injectable peptides promoted within the wellness industry for uses such as building muscle, healing injuries and boosting energy. The government will take comments for two weeks before finalizing the measure. The document, primarily written by officials at HHS, faced overwhelming pushback among FDA drug staffers who warned it could undermine the agency’s long-standing mission of keeping unsafe health products off the U.S. market, according to the people familiar with its development. Jacksonville Fire Rescue Department firefighter Josue Garcia-Otero, a member of the critical care team, was traveling with his wife, Diamary, and their family when the train crashed into another. "We’re grateful they are safe and proud of their willingness to help in the midst of such a tragic event. We look forward to welcoming the Garcia-Otero family home safely," JFRD said in a post on Facebook. Credit: Jacksonville Fire Rescue Department Once their family was out of danger, Josue and Diamary turned to help others, providing care to critically injured passengers, JFRD said. "Earlier this month, for our Hispanic Heritage Month series, Josue shared how his grandparents instilled in him the importance of caring for others. items.t: 2 St. Petersburg police officers hospitalized after car collides with golf cart
items.x: ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. (WFLA)— Two St. Petersburg police officers were hospitalized after a crash in St. Petersburg Thursday morning. Officers were in a golf cart at the intersection of 38th Avenue North and 37th Avenue North when the crash occurred. According to SPPD, a Honda CRV was turning north on 37th ST N. when it collided with the golf cart, ejecting one of the officers. Both officers sustained non-life-threatening injuries and were taken to a nearby hospital. The roads have since been reopened, but the investigation continues. The driver of the Honda CRV stayed on scene and is cooperating with the investigation. This is a developing story. items.t: DoorDash to buy Instacart in $17B grocery delivery deal
items.x: DoorDash is gobbling up Instacart in a $17 billion acquisition that will supercharge its grocery delivery business. DoorDash said the Instacart brand name and app will remain, and Instacart shoppers can continue fulfilling orders for Instacart. Grocers can also choose to work with Instacart or DoorDash. Instacart customers will now have access to 50,000 additional stores covered by DoorDash, the company said. Instacart, founded in 2012, specializes in grocery and convenience store delivery in the U.S. and Canada. Its 600,000 “shoppers” — who are independent contractors — completed 338 million orders last year, according to company filings. Instacart has a market value of $14 billion. DoorDash, founded in San Francisco in 2013, began as a restaurant delivery business but has expanded to pet food and electronics. Operating in 40 countries, it completed more than 3 billion orders last year using a network of 9 million independent delivery workers. It has a market value of $73 billion. DoorDash began delivering groceries in 2020 amid a surge in pandemic-era demand. Grocers were initially cautious. items.t: Villa Vie Odyssey passenger says warning signs were there long before Cambodia
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — Kit Cassingham and her husband, Randy, sold their home and nearly everything they owned to live aboard a cruise ship for years. Now, she says she doesn't expect to see that money again. Cassingham told NewsNation's Jesse Weber on Wednesday that the couple paid about $370,000 to $380,000 for their cabin on the Villa Vie Odyssey, plus $7,000 a month in expenses. Asked if they will get it back, she said, "No, no, no, no." More than 200 passengers were told Tuesday to leave the Odyssey in Cambodia within hours after the cruise company suspended operations. In a news release , Villa Vie blamed soaring fuel costs tied to the war in Iran, saying the monthly fuel cost per cabin jumped from about $1,800 to as much as $8,000. Villa Vie Odyssey: How did passengers find out they had to leave? She and Randy had already gotten off the ship for a hotel so they could work online when a short message arrived saying the ship couldn't get more fuel . “You have till two o’clock to get off the ship,” she said. items.t: Big 12 fines UCF $100K for fan behavior aimed at BYU, Mormon church
items.x: IRVING, Texas (AP) — The Big 12 Conference has fined UCF $100,000 for fans' derogatory chants aimed at The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints at last weekend’s football game against BYU. The league also announced Wednesday it has established a conference-wide policy with “escalating consequences for discriminatory conduct” that it says “has no place in the Big 12.” The fine against UCF will be directed toward “student education initiatives,” the league said in a statement. It’s the latest fine against a Big 12 school over fan treatment of BYU, the flagship school for what’s widely known as the Mormon church. “After becoming aware of the conference’s decision, we will be reviewing our options,” UCF athletics spokesman Adam Widman said in a email Wednesday night. Video shared on social media showed UCF fans chanting “(expletive) the Mormons!” prior to kickoff Saturday. University security then removed some fans from the game, won by UCF in overtime . The Big 12's conduct policy at athletic events will now include an automatic minimum $100,000 fine and a warning after a first confirmed incident. items.t: Rays become 3rd team to lose first 3 World Series
items.x: ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. (AP) — Eyes red and voice soft, Drew Rasmussen stood in front of his locker. “Failure sucks. And to be this close, it's really, really hard,” the Tampa Bay Rays pitcher said. “That's the best team I've played at the major league level.” Predicted by many to finish at or near the bottom of the AL East, the Rays reached the World Series for the third time but remain without a title. Their year ended Wednesday night with a 4-1 loss to the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 5, leaving them among four teams without a title along with Colorado, San Diego and Seattle. “They’re banged up and hurting right now,” manager Kevin Cash said of his players. An expansion team that started in 1998, the Rays also lost in the World Series to Philadelphia in 2008 and to the Los Angeles Dodgers in 2020. The only other clubs to lose in their first three Series appearances were the Brooklyn Dodgers (0-7) and Detroit Tigers (0-4), according to the Elias Sports Bureau. “It hurts knowing that you got this close, you got this far," closer Bryan Baker said. items.t: Brewers beat the Rays 4-1 in Game 5 to win the first World Series title in franchise history
items.x: Previous coverage: New hope for Rays fans, businesses thankful for the extension ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. (AP) — The small-ball Milwaukee Brewers playing in the smallest market in the majors are World Series champions for the first time in franchise history. Hey, Milwaukee: grab a brat, raise a beer and prepare for that parade. Young ace Jacob Misiorowski threw 5 2/3 scoreless innings of two-hit ball, rookie Cooper Pratt got two more hits and two RBIs, and the Brewers beat the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 in Game 5 on Wednesday night to set off a long-awaited celebration among thousands of Brewers fans in attendance at Tropicana Field. Misiorowski left the game because of a right calf cramp. He got a standing ovation from the Brew-Crew fans, who took over the section behind Milwaukee’s dugout for the last three games. The 22-year-old Pratt set a Series rookie record with six straight hits before a sacrifice fly in the sixth inning. Jackson Chourio set a five-game Series record with 11 hits. The World Series title comes in the 58th season for a franchise that began as the Seattle Pilots in 1969 and moved to Milwaukee the following year. The report by Home Economics and Redfin, analysed the current housing market to identify the time of year where a home's original asking price saw a significant price drop or discount through negotiations between the buyer and seller. The data found early November, as winter approaches, to be the peak season for buying a home as homebuying slows with the upcoming holiday leaving sellers with fewer potential buyers. In Tampa, November shows to be the best time for buyers partially due to weather. "House hunters have a window of opportunity to negotiate on listings that have been lingering on the market since summer: Sellers want to close a deal before the new year, and there's often not much competition from out-of-towners yet." items.t: Hillsborough County Fire Rescue opens new fire station in Palm River
items.x: HILLSBOROUGH COUNTY, Fla. (WFLA) — Hillsborough County Fire Rescue celebrated the opening of Fire Station 15 on Wednesday, which will serve the Palm River area. Rob Herrin with HCFR told 8 On Your Side it replaces the old Palm River station just a few minutes away. "It was a 60, six zero, 60-year-old station. What this station provides is a more modern fire station for our firefighter safety and just for better response to the community we serve," he said. Construction cost $5.6 million and the county said ARPA funds were used to build the station. Herrin said at older fire stations, firefighters would bring in harmful carcinogens after a fire. But he said the new station comes with a decontamination area. "When they get out of the truck, they take their gear off, they clean that, they clean themselves in the shower before they take those carcinogens, now gone, into the fire station where they live," Herrin said. Herrin added at other stations, sleeping firefighters would be waken up for every call the station gets, but not this one. items.t: New device helps change stroke patients’ life
items.x: TAMPA, Fla. (WFLA) Thursday, October 29 is World Stroke Day, and a newer device that TGH is using is helping multiple stroke patients. In 2021, Jose M. Rivera Jr. had a stroke that changed his life. He couldn't do the things he was used to doing every single day. Then, he switched his care to TGH, and this August, he had a device implanted and said it has made all the difference. "I couldn't even cook, I couldn't pick up my arm, I couldn't walk, it was difficult for me," Rivera Jr. said. The stroke impacted his right side and his voice. For five years, he wasn't able to use his right arm until he got a Vivistim device implanted. "I'm doing things that I couldn't do before," Rivera Jr. said. The device was introduced a few years ago and helps stroke patients regain their movement. "It's connected to the vagus nerve that then helps with neuroplasticity for the brain. It helps make the connection stronger, the communication between the arm and the brain better," said occupational therapist with TGH, Kim Branagan. items.t: Harris advises Democrats against attempting to impeach Trump
items.x: ( The Hill ) Former Vice President Kamala Harris on Tuesday urged Democrats against making a third attempt to impeach President Trump if they win back the House after next week's midterm elections. "I think that going in the direction of impeachment is not a good idea, just to be honest with you," Harris told MeidasTouch's Aaron Parnas in an interview. "Just because we have limited resources and I think the energy and the resources need to put into accountability, need to be put into investigations." "And that's where the time should be spent," she added. "Remember, I was in the Senate for the last go-around, and the votes aren't there. "So, that's how I feel. But also, I think after the election, we all have to just also agree that our attitude has to be to get stuff done." Harris said Democrats should be "uncompromising" and "not sit around, you know, being genteel about the relationships," but maintain accountability when it comes to cuts to healthcare and oversight on the Iran war. items.t: Houdini death theory debunked? Author weighs in
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — A new theory surrounding the death of legendary magician Harry Houdini is reigniting debate nearly 100 years after his death, but magician and author Vince Wilson says he remains unconvinced by claims of a cover-up. Speaking with Jesse Weber, Wilson said he still believes the long-accepted explanation remains the most likely. “I would still probably stick to the original theory that he simply died of complications,” Wilson said, referring to Houdini's ruptured appendix and resulting infection. According to Hoodline , retired surgeon Larrian Gillespie argues in her 2026 book "Houdini: The Man Who Died Twice" that records surrounding Houdini's death may have been altered and that he may have died earlier than officially documented. items.t: BODY CAM: Man arrested in connection with fatal Tampa shooting
items.x: TAMPA, Fla. (WFLA) — A man was arrested on Wednesday in connection with a fatal shooting that occurred in Tampa a day prior. According to the Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office, at 11:19 p.m. on Tuesday, deputies responded to the 12000 block of Taliaferro Avenue following reports of shots being fired. At the scene, deputies said they found a man identified as 29-year-old Ronnie Sheppard, who appeared to be suffering from upper body trauma. He was taken to a nearby hospital where he was pronounced dead, HCSO reported. During an investigation, detectives learned that the shooting stemmed from an argument between the two men that quickly escalated. Detectives identified the shooter as 26-year-old Nathan Campbell. On Wednesday, the Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office arrested Campbell at his home in Gibsonton. He is charged with murder in the second degree involving a firearm, and felon in possession of a firearm.

The Polk County Sheriff's Office welcomed K-9 Vader, a 15-month-old German Shepherd, to its team last week. According to the sheriff's office, HBK-9 donated Vader to PCSO after hearing Deputy Natalie Oestreich and K-9 Ace's story. In August, K-9 Ace was shot in the chest. Due to the injury, his left front leg was amputated. WATCH: Florida homeowner holds armed car burglar at gunpoint, deputies say K-9 Ace recovered from the surgery, but he was forced to retire. Herb Bennett from HBK-9 said he reached out to the chain of command and offered to donate Oestreich's replacement dog. "We just went through the selection process, and I gave Natalie first choice out of all the dogs I showed, and she has selected her replacement dog," Bennett said. "After K9 Ace was forced to retire following being shot in the line of duty, Natalie is ready to begin this next chapter with her new partner!" the Polk County Sheriff's Office said.

items.t: Choque de trenes a alta velocidad en España causa al menos 68 muertes
items.x: URDA, España (AP) — Un tren de alta velocidad chocó contra otro que se había detenido en las vías en España el miércoles, causando al menos 68 muertos y decenas de heridos en la segunda colisión ferroviaria mortal de este año. El gobierno regional de Castilla La Mancha confirmó el número de muertos y dijo que otras 58 personas estaban recibiendo atención médica en hospitales. Los equipos de rescate registraron los restos durante el día en busca de supervivientes y cuerpos. La colisión se produjo apenas nueve meses después de otro accidente mortal que involucró trenes de alta velocidad operados por las mismas dos compañías en el sur de España en enero. "Hoy toda España está de luto", dijo el presidente del Gobierno español Pedro Sánchez desde el lugar del accidente, donde anunció que su gobierno declararía tres días de luto nacional. items.x: ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. (AP) — Drew Rasmussen will start for Tampa Bay on three days' rest in Game 5 of the World Series against the Milwaukee Brewers on Wednesday night, trying to stave off elimination for the Rays. A 31-year-old right-hander, Rasmussen threw 89 pitches over 3 2/3 innings in Game 2 on Saturday, getting no decision as Milwaukee rallied for a 5-4 victory and a 2-0 Series lead. items.x: ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. (WFLA) — As excitement for a Rays World Series victory picks back up, local businesses are seeing a major boost from baseball fans. According to Ferg's Sports Bar & Grill owner Mark Ferguson, the bar had a month's worth of sales during Game 3 of the World Series, which ended in the Tampa Bay Rays' third loss. Florida is one of the worst states for jobs, study shows Monday, Ferg's sold 24,000 Miller and Coors Light beers, which translates to 1,000 cases. The bar also had 23,000 orders for wings. During Game 4, Ferg's saw an even bigger sale of 26,000 beers, which would make up 1,100 cases. Game 4 ended in a Rays victory. Ferg's, which is located across the street from Tropicana Field, has been a popular spot for Rays fans to watch the games away and at home. The Rays face off against the Milwaukee Brewers again Wednesday night for Game 5, which could end in a Brewers total victory if the Rays do not fend them off again.

items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war , creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle . items.t: Judge overseeing Maduro trial dies
items.x: ( The Hill ) Alvin Hellerstein, a longtime federal judge who was set to oversee the criminal trial of deposed Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro, has passed away, according to a court official. He was 92. Nominated by then-President Bill Clinton in 1998, Hellerstein oversaw many high-profile disputes during his nearly three decades on the bench in New York City. He was back in the national limelight presiding over the proceedings for Maduro , who was captured and brought to the U.S. earlier this year over accusations of narco-terrorism. Maduro and his wife were in the judge's courtroom less than two weeks ago to plead not guilty to a new set of criminal charges. Before the Maduro operation, Hellerstein had long clashed with President Donald Trump in court. The judge at one point agreed that Trump’s fixer-turned-foe, Michael Cohen, could be released from prison to home confinement. Cohen has cast his prosecution as retribution by Trump. Separately, Hellerstein repeatedly denied Trump's efforts to move his hush money criminal prosecution into federal court, forcing the president to try his luck in New York's state system. The 38-page lawsuit, filed in federal court in Washington, D.C., centers on an Aug. 11 episode of “The Scott Jennings Show,” in which Jennings shared clips of Piker claiming he had said, “the USA should resume lynchings against Black people.” Piker, who threatened legal action in August over the claim and shared further context to the clips, alleges Jennings knowingly misrepresented sarcastic comments he made during his livestreams by turning it into an apparent endorsement of racial violence. “Mr. Jennings did not merely mischaracterize something Mr. Piker said,” the complaint reads. “He took a false, fabricated, and manipulated video of Mr. Piker, added a made-up quotation that Mr. Piker never uttered, and then made accusations that went beyond even what the manipulated footage purported to show.” During the August broadcast, Jennings warned Black voters to pay close attention before playing the clip, which included an on-screen c

items.t: Sabato’s Crystal Ball moves 16 House races, Florida Senate race toward Democrats
items.x: Nonpartisan election forecaster Sabato’s Crystal Ball is shifting more than a dozen House races toward Democrats in the final week of the campaign , another sign of a worsening political environment for Republicans. Sabato's Crystal Ball, a division of the University of Virginia’s Center for Politics, has moved dozens of races toward Democrats in recent weeks, including nearly 50 races in the month of October alone. The race changes include moving a few deep-red seats into the “toss-up” column. Open congressional districts in Kentucky and Montana, as well as seats with GOP incumbents in Missouri, Virginia, Colorado and Pennsylvania, moved into coin-flip territory. Many of the seats Crystal Ball rates as toss-ups were places President Trump carried by double digits in 2024. One notable race that moved from toss-up to “leans Democratic” is Texas’s 15th Congressional District, where Rep. Monica De la Cruz (R) is facing a tough challenge from Tejano music star Bobby Pulido (D). Unlike the other South Texas districts where Democrats are trying to hold on to redrawn seats, the 15th District is a Republican-held district that Trump won by nearly 20 points in 2024. items.x: TAMPA, FLA. (WFLA-TAMPAHOY) – Los vientos fuertes continuarán un día más. Será un día más bochornoso, con temperaturas máximas que rondarán los 84F y que se sentirán más altas esta tarde. items.t: Rays reignite World Series hopes after 4-3 victory
items.x: ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. (WFLA) Rays fans have renewed excitement about the team's chances in the World Series. Tuesday's win over the Brewers forces a fifth game in the series. Hundreds of fans spent Game 4 at Ferg's across the street from Tropicana Field. Cheers erupted throughout downtown St. Petersburg when the Rays claimed the 4-3 victory. "Sometimes we pray extra hard, and sometimes he listens. Tonight, he listened," said one Rays fan, "always believe." More than 40,000 fans are expected to fill the stadium during Game 5. If the Rays win Wednesday's game, any remaining games in the series will be played in Milwaukee. First pitch for Game 5 is at 8 p.m., and gates to the stadium open at 5 p.m.

items.t: US cruise ship suspends voyage in Asia due to fuel costs, stranding 200 passengers

The MV Odyssey set sail two years ago on a voyage to the seven continents marketed as combining long-term living at sea with global travel. Its operator had offered to “make the Odyssey your permanent home,” with the purchase price of a suite for the lifetime of the vessel starting around $230,000. This photo attained as part of the press kit by the Odyssey shows the U.S. cruise ship in Japan. (Odyssey via AP) For now, it is docked at the Cambodian port of Sihanoukville on the Gulf of Thailand, with no certain departure date. The ship has been carrying 203 passengers, mostly Americans, along with 156 crew members, according to Cambodian officials. It has a a 650-passenger capacity. Its Florida-based operator, Villa Vie Residences, said monthly fuel expenses per cabin that historically averaged $1,800 have reached an estimated $6,000 to $8,000 in parts of Asia due to the war in Iran. items.t: GLP-1s could cause beer sales to take a hit, report says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — One benefit reported by people taking GLP-1 medications is a reduction in alcohol cravings and consumption, but the drugs' growing popularity has created new challenges for beer companies. According to Reuters , Heineken presented a document to U.K. hospitality customers earlier this month advising that the medications could potentially change drinking habits among users. The drugs may result in "fullness and fewer serves" in pubs and bars. “We see some changes in consumption behaviour among (GLP-1) users and will continue to monitor how these behaviours evolve in 2027," a Heineken spokesperson told the publication. The report noted that the company’s research found consumers increasingly choosing smaller servings, lower-alcohol beverages and premium products and that these shifts also align with broader trends focused on health, wellness and moderation. One option Heineken advised customers to pursue is half-pints and low- and no-alcohol options, according to the publication. items.t: Two sewer main breaks send sewage into Henrico’s Gillies Creek
items.x: HENRICO COUNTY, Va. (WRIC) — Two sewer main breaks sent sewage into Henrico County's Gillies Creek, prompting officials to warn residents to stay out of the water as remediation efforts continued. Crews with the Henrico County Department of Public Utilities (DPU) were dispatched to Gillies Creek the evening of Friday, Oct. 23, and finished repairs to the water main, according to a Thursday press release. Wastewater flowed into a short section of the creek near Kemp Avenue as a result of the break. County leaders said the sewage discharge impacts are "minimal," though crews hold a large portion of the wastewater at the nearby Gillies Creek Pump Station and send it slowly to Henrico’s Water Reclamation Facility in eastern Henrico for treatment. The pump station and main are now functioning normally. DPU completed repairs to the sewer main the afternoon of Tuesday, Oct. 27. Crews continue to remove impacted soil near the break and investigate impacts from the discharge, according to the county. items.t: Laopakdee takes lead in bid for second Masters invitation
items.x: TOMARATA, New Zealand – A year after a historic breakthrough at the Asia-Pacific Amateur Championship, defending champion Fifa Laopakdee picked up where he left off with an eight-under 63 to take a three-stroke lead over New Zealand’s Joshua Bai after the first round at Te Arai Links’ South Course. Laopakdee, now a senior at Arizona State University, became the first player from Thailand to win the Asia-Pacific Amateur last fall with a victory on the third playoff hole in Dubai. He went on to compete in the Masters and The Open earlier this year before returning to defend his title at the 17th edition of the Asia-Pacific Amateur this week. “Couldn't ask for a better way to start the round,” said Laopakdee. “Before it started, I knew it was going to be windy out there and it was going to be tough… Eight under wasn’t on my bingo card today, but I was able to pull it off and it feels amazing.” Fifa Laopakdee of Thailand plays a tee stroke during the first round of the 2026 Asia-Pacific Amateur Championship being played at the Te Arai Links, South Course in Auckland, New Zealand on Thursday 29 October 2026. items.x: OCALA, Fla. The challenge, according to police, involved one of the men giving another a haircut "in the center of the road" on State Route 200 in Ocala. The third suspect was filming the stunt, authorities say. In a Facebook post, the Ocala Police Department explained that the young men — ages 20, 19 and 18 — had removed a chair from a nearby restaurant to use during the challenge. But while the 18-year-old was seated and getting his hair cut, a traffic accident nearby sent a Chevrolet 3500 in their direction. The two other suspects were able to move out of the way, but the 18-year-old "was seated with his back to the oncoming truck" and was hit by the vehicle. Ocala police indicated that the 18-year-old was hospitalized after the incident, but did not disclose the extent of his injuries. All three men were later arrested. items.t: Dartmouth official resigns over AI use
items.x: (The Hill) A top Dartmouth official has resigned from his position after allegations that he violated the school's AI use policy. The university announced Wednesday that Provost Santiago Schnell resigned from his position after a university committee released the results of its investigation into the matter it opened in September. "The Provost used AI to meaningfully alter his writing in violation of at least one publication’s AI use and/or disclosure requirement, failed to disclose his use of AI in clear violation of a national newspaper’s stated policy, was not forthcoming about his AI use, and fell short of the standards set forth by Dartmouth’s Code of Ethical Conduct, the Academic Honor Principle, and Geisel’s Policy on Expectations for Professionalism for Faculty, Non-Faculty Academics, and Staff," the committee concluded. Schnell was accused of using AI to alter his work by the student newspaper The Dartmouth and outlet Semafor, specifically pointing to an opinion piece the provost wrote for The Washington Post. items.t: AAA advises drivers about daylight saving time
items.x: (WAVY) – It's only a few days until we trade one extra hour of sleep for months of darkness as we leave work to drive home. And even though we're on the easier end of the time transition (from daylight saving time to standard time), the switch still takes its toll. Nexstar's WAVY went to AAA Tidewater Virginia to see what commuters can expect. "Well, the biggest thing for drivers will be the change in daylight when we leave work or school," said Holly Dalby with AAA. "At the end of the day, gone will be the bright sunshine, and we will find ourselves either driving into the glare from the setting sun or driving home in the dark. So it's a time to be particularly careful on the roads." While lawmakers have tried to get rid of the time switch altogether, it doesn't appear to be going anywhere anytime soon, so your circadian rhythm will have to dance to a different beat for a while. "It just messing with our sleep schedule can really add to our fatigue very quickly. And when we're fatigued, we can make mistakes," Dalby said. items.t: One issue, different bills: Energy costs shape key midterm races
items.x: (NewsNation) – Higher energy costs have helped make affordability a top issue in the 2026 midterms , but voters aren't all worried about the same bills. Diesel prices are squeezing Midwest farmers , while homeowners in the Northeast face soaring heating oil costs . Others in data center hotspots like Texas and Ohio are worried about their electricity bills . Democrats have tried to tie those issues to President Trump , pointing to the war in Iran and his embrace of AI . As of Wednesday, Decision Desk HQ gave Democrats an 80% chance of winning the House and a 58% chance of controlling the Senate . Some Republicans have called for an end to the Iran war, while others have blamed high prices on Ukraine's war with Russia and Democrats' energy policies. To win the Senate, Democrats will have to break through on Republican turf . Of the Cook Political Report's seven toss-ups , five are in states Trump won by double digits in 2024. items.t: Images of naked inmates found on Florida deputy’s agency computer: Sheriff’s office
items.x: DESOTO COUNTY, Fla. (WFLA) – A deputy in Florida's DeSoto County has been fired and charged with a felony after the sheriff's office IT department discovered troubling photos on an agency computer, the office said. Douglas Chirinos, 35, had been working as a detention deputy when a possible security breach was flagged on his computer. Initially, Chirinos was only suspected of downloading YouTube and streaming services onto the device, which is prohibited. But when the IT director started investigating, he found a folder containing "images of concern," Chirinos' arrest affidavit said. As officials continued reviewing the contents, they discovered Chirinos had been taking screenshots of naked or partially naked women from surveillance feeds inside the jail isolation cell. At least three different women were shown in the images, which were taken between April and October 2026. DCSO said Chirinos had only worked for the sheriff's office since 2025. The women were in varying stages of undress, some wearing nothing but underwear and some completely nude, the affidavit said. items.t: ‘Gut punch’: 2 college students found dead in Colorado after going missing on mountain hike
items.x: (WJW) – Two missing Colorado college students were found dead Wednesday after they left campus for a weekend trip up a nearly 14,000-foot peak and encountered a heavy snowstorm, police said. Kaden Matsuda, 19, from Ridgway, Colorado, and Jackson Donlon, 20, from New York, left Colorado Mountain College Leadville’s campus on Friday and didn’t return. They told family and friends they planned to go up Ice Mountain, which requires technical climbing, according to the county sheriff’s office . On Wednesday night, the sheriff's office confirmed that the students were found dead around 3:30 p.m. in a basin of the West Apostle Mountain. Authorities do not believe foul play was involved. The investigation is now being handled by the Chaffee County Coroner’s Office. “Our heart aches for Kaden and Jackson’s family and friends. We are very proud of our team’s efforts to find them before this weekend’s coming storm," Sheriff Andy Rohrich wrote on Facebook. "Although this is a gut punch, our prayers were answered that we would find Kaden and Jackson, allowing some closure for the family. items.t: Muzzleloader Deer Season Opens Oct. 31, Is Your Gun Ready?
items.x: NEW CASTLE, Va. (WFXR) Expect to hear the thunder of gunfire around Virginia soon. Deer muzzleloader season opens October 31. But, before you head into the woods, there is one very important thing to consider. "Is my gun ready?" The only way to tell is to fire it at a target to make sure the scope and gun are in synch, and that your aim is true. If not, you will need to make adjustments on the scope and possibly the gun. There are any number of things that can affect the scope. "Well, it's been been a whole year since we've done this, so bumping them in the closet or on the truck ride, you know, things happen," said expert deer hunter Randy Frango of Craig County. "It's a good practice to, you check your rifle prior to season." Having a gun dialed in can keep you from missing a deer, but it can also prevent something else, wounding a deer and not being able to track it. "You don't want to make a bad shot and wound an animal either," said Frango. "So yeah, check your rifle, whether it be a muzzleloader or rifle, rifle season is coming up, and make sure your firearm is hitting where it should." The other thing Frango emphasized is safety and especially avoiding double charging a gun.

items.t: Cruise ship passenger says warning signs were there long before Cambodia
items.x: (NewsNation) — Kit Cassingham and her husband, Randy, sold their home and nearly everything they owned to live aboard a cruise ship for years. Now, she says she doesn't expect to see that money again. Cassingham told NewsNation's Jesse Weber on Wednesday that the couple paid about $370,000 to $380,000 for their cabin on the Villa Vie Odyssey, plus $7,000 a month in expenses. Asked if they will get it back, she said, "No, no, no, no." More than 200 passengers were told Tuesday to leave the Odyssey in Cambodia within hours after the cruise company suspended operations. In a news release , Villa Vie blamed soaring fuel costs tied to the war in Iran, saying the monthly fuel cost per cabin jumped from about $1,800 to as much as $8,000. Villa Vie Odyssey: How did passengers find out they had to leave? Cassingham and her husband had already gotten off the ship for a hotel so they could work online when a short message arrived saying the ship couldn't get more fuel. “You have till two o’clock to get off the ship,” she said. items.x: HANOVER COUNTY, Va. (WRIC) Hanover County Public Schools broke ground Tuesday on the expansion of The Hanover Center for Trades and Technology. According to a release from the district, school officials, students, faculty and more celebrated the groundbreaking on Tuesday, Oct. 27. The expansion is set to open for the 2027-28 school year and will add welding and diesel equipment technology and expand the existing cosmetology program, the release said. “We are opening new doors for our students to explore their interests, discover their passions, develop valuable skills, and pursue meaningful and rewarding careers,” Superintendent of Schools Lisa Pennycuff said in the release. items.t: Democrats see battleground map expand to South Carolina, Florida, Mississippi
items.x: Democrats are giddy about the possibility of a bigger blue wave than expected in the battle for the Senate as polls show that South Carolina , Florida and Mississippi — three seats that were long seen as safe Republican holds — are now competitive races. Democrats view the Republican candidates running in those states as mediocre political talents who must fight historic headwinds caused by President Trump’s unpopularity, voter anger over inflation and the war in Iran, and burgeoning Democratic voter enthusiasm. The Senate battleground map has steadily expanded throughout the 2026 midterm election cycle as political handicappers have shifted seats that were thought to be in solidly Republican territory — such as Alaska, Iowa, Kansas and Texas — to the “toss-up" category. But now Republicans have to worry about losing Senate seats in states that were unthinkable as realistic Democratic pickup opportunities at the start of the election cycle, most notably South Carolina, which last elected a Democrat, Fritz Hollings, to the Senate in 1998. items.x: RICHMOND, Va. (WRIC) 8News is highlighting local authors as part of the first-ever Author Blitz, including local writer Jo Lily, courtesy of All About Books. 8News anchors Delaney Hall and Madison Moore talked with Lily about the experience of writing and publishing his first two novels after having a stroke. "I write romantasy and cozy mystery novels," Lily said. items.t: Virginia Elk Cam returns for ninth season
items.x: BUCHANAN COUNTY, Va. (WRIC) The Virginia Department of Wildlife Resources' (DWR) Elk Cam has returned for its ninth season. DWR announced the Virginia Elk Cam s return on Thursday, Oct. 29. Viewers can check it out to watch a restored elk herd on their phones, tablets or computers any time through December. The camera scans a field located on reclaimed mine land in Buchanan County, which is frequented by elk, especially during early morning, evening and nighttime hours, the department said. As the weather cools, elk are expected to become more active during the day. The herd also shares the landscape with other wildlife that appear on camera, including deer and turkeys, the occasional black bear or coyote, and more. The Virginia Elk Cam typically goes live in September each year, but this time around, DWR said the herd wasn't spending time in the fields within view of the camera until recently. Elk spotted on the DWR Elk Cam around 7 p.m. Sept. 13, 2023 (Photo: DWR) The herd has since resumed its previous patterns, according to the department, and is now frequently seen in view of the camera. items.t: RFK Jr. eases access to unproven peptides despite opposition from FDA scientists
items.x: WASHINGTON (AP) — The Trump administration on Wednesday acted to ease access to unproven peptide drugs favored by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. Food and Drug Administration scientific staffers had little input on the decision and opposed the changes, according to six people familiar with its development. The draft policy posted online by Kennedy’s Department of Health and Human Services covers a handful of injectable peptides promoted within the wellness industry for uses such as building muscle, healing injuries and boosting energy. The government will take comments for two weeks before finalizing the measure. The document, primarily written by officials at HHS, faced overwhelming pushback among FDA drug staffers who warned it could undermine the agency’s long-standing mission of keeping unsafe health products off the U.S. market, according to people familiar with its development. The people spoke to The Associated Press on the condition of anonymity to discuss confidential government deliberations. items.t: DoorDash to buy Instacart in $17 billion grocery delivery deal
items.x: DoorDash is gobbling up Instacart in a $17 billion acquisition that will supercharge its grocery delivery business. DoorDash said the Instacart brand name and app will remain, and Instacart shoppers can continue fulfilling orders for Instacart. Grocers can also choose to work with Instacart or DoorDash. Instacart customers will now have access to 50,000 additional stores covered by DoorDash, the company said. Instacart, founded in 2012, specializes in grocery and convenience store delivery in the U.S. and Canada. Its 600,000 “shoppers” — who are independent contractors — completed 338 million orders last year, according to company filings. Instacart has a market value of $14 billion. DoorDash, founded in San Francisco in 2013, began as a restaurant delivery business but has expanded to pet food and electronics. Operating in 40 countries, it completed more than 3 billion orders last year using a network of 9 million independent delivery workers. It has a market value of $73 billion. DoorDash began delivering groceries in 2020 amid a surge in pandemic-era demand. Grocers were initially cautious. items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5% last month and was up 3.6% relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5% month-over-month and 3.6% relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7in July to 3.4% in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2% from August to September, after increasing by 4.4% from July to August. Gasoline and energy costs have risen in six of nine months this year, as the Iran war sparked oil price shocks via the Islamic Republic's restrictions on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Persistent inflation , which has remained above the Fed's 2% target for five-and-a-half years, spurred central bank officials to hike interest rates by a quarter point in mid-September. The offer values Wendy's at $1.4 billion. Wendy's, which is based in Dublin, Ohio, confirmed receipt of the unsolicited proposal in a statement Wednesday and said its board has formed an independent committee to evaluate it. At the end of last year, Wendy's had 5,969 restaurants in the U.S. and 1,428 outlets in 38 countries. Wendy's, founded in 1969 by Dave Thomas and named after his daughter, is known for its square burgers and Frosty desserts. The fast-growing chain introduced the drive-thru window in 1970 and went public in 1976. In the 1980s, as it jockeyed for sales with McDonald's and Burger King, Wendy's launched salad bars and ran its iconic “Where's the beef?” ad campaign. items.t: Virginia sees early rise in flu activity ahead of peak flu season
items.x: CHESTERFIELD COUNTY, Va. (WRIC) — Flu activity is increasing in Virginia earlier than usual, according to data from the Virginia Department of Health (VDH). The uptick has prompted doctors to warn Virginians to take precautions ahead of peak flu season. According to the Virginia Department of Health, 1.24% of emergency department visits during the week ending Oct. 24 were diagnosed with the flu . This time in 2025, that rate was closer to 0.32%. Despite this early uptick, the VDH reports that overall respiratory illness activity in the commonwealth is low and stable. Dr. Trenée West, medical director at Patient First in Midlothian, said the increase is unusual for this early in the respiratory season. “We've seen an uptick in flu cases this year a little bit earlier than what we typically see," West said. "Usually we'll see flu numbers start to increase around November or December, especially after the holidays when people are gathering together,” She says patients have reported common symptoms like fever, chills, runny nose and body aches. items.t: Kickers promote Glen Allen native Brian Ownby to head coach
items.x: RICHMOND, Va. (WRIC) The Richmond Kickers have named Brian Ownby the ninth head coach in club history, Chairman and CEO Rob Ukrop announced Wednesday. Ownby, a Glen Allen native and former professional player, was named interim head coach on June 15. He led the team for the final 22 games of the 2026 season, winning two of his final three matches. The Kickers scored 16 goals in their final nine games, with Tarik Pannholzer and Lucca Dourado combining for eight goals during the final eight matches of the regular season. “I am honored and grateful to be named the ninth Head Coach of the Richmond Kickers,” Ownby said. “I would like to thank Rob Ulrop, Camp Peery, and everyone within the organization for their trust and confidence in me to bring my vision to life on the field. I am excited for what lies ahead and look forward to building something special together.” Ownby starred at Deep Run High School and the University of Virginia before beginning his professional career. At UVA, he scored 21 goals and recorded 10 assists in 72 appearances. He also helped the Cavaliers reach the NCAA College Cup national final. items.t: Judge overseeing Maduro trial dies
items.x: ( The Hill ) Alvin Hellerstein, a longtime federal judge who was set to oversee the criminal trial of deposed Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro, has passed away, according to a court official. He was 92. Nominated by then-President Bill Clinton in 1998, Hellerstein oversaw many high-profile disputes during his nearly three decades on the bench in New York City. He was back in the national limelight presiding over the proceedings for Maduro , who was captured and brought to the U.S. earlier this year over accusations of narco-terrorism. Maduro and his wife were in the judge's courtroom less than two weeks ago to plead not guilty to a new set of criminal charges. Before the Maduro operation, Hellerstein had long clashed with President Donald Trump in court. The judge at one point agreed that Trump’s fixer-turned-foe, Michael Cohen, could be released from prison to home confinement. Cohen has cast his prosecution as retribution by Trump. Separately, Hellerstein repeatedly denied Trump's efforts to move his hush money criminal prosecution into federal court, forcing the president to try his luck in New York's state system.
