items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: ( The Hill ) Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. items.t: Wendy’s gets buyout offer while struggling with beef prices and growing competition
items.x: Wendy’s shares jumped more than 14% Wednesday after noted investor Nelson Peltz made an offer to buy the chain, which has been struggling with high beef prices and aging stores. Peltz’s Trian Fund Management and several partners are offering Wendy’s $7.35 per share in cash, or a premium of nearly 19% over the stock’s closing price on Tuesday, in a deal that would take the company private. items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Kaden Matsuda, 19, from Ridgway, Colorado, and Jackson Donlon, 20, from New York, left Colorado Mountain College Leadville’s campus on Friday and didn’t return. They told family and friends they planned to go up Ice Mountain, which requires technical climbing, according to the county sheriff’s office. On Wednesday night, the sheriff's office confirmed that the students were found dead around 3:30 p.m. in a basin of the West Apostle Mountain. Authorities do not believe foul play was involved. The investigation is now being handled by the Chaffee County Coroner’s Office. “Our heart aches for Kaden and Jackson’s family and friends. We are very proud of our team’s efforts to find them before this weekend’s coming storm," Sheriff Andy Rohrich wrote on Facebook. "Although this is a gut punch, our prayers were answered that we would find Kaden and Jackson, allowing some closure for the family. items.t: Cruise ship passenger says warning signs were there long before Cambodia
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — Kit Cassingham and her husband, Randy, sold their home and nearly everything they owned to live aboard a cruise ship for years. Now, she says she doesn't expect to see that money again. Cassingham told NewsNation's Jesse Weber on Wednesday that the couple paid about $370,000 to $380,000 for their cabin on the Villa Vie Odyssey, plus $7,000 a month in expenses. Asked if they will get it back, she said, "No, no, no, no." Cruise ship suspends voyage over fuel costs, stranding 200 passengers More than 200 passengers were told Tuesday to leave the Odyssey in Cambodia within hours after the cruise company suspended operations. In a news release , Villa Vie blamed soaring fuel costs tied to the war in Iran, saying the monthly fuel cost per cabin jumped from about $1,800 to as much as $8,000. Villa Vie Odyssey: How did passengers find out they had to leave? Cassingham and her husband had already gotten off the ship for a hotel so they could work online when a short message arrived saying the ship couldn't get more fuel . “You have till two o’clock to get off the ship,” she said. The news wasn't a total shock. “We’d seen red flags all along,” Cassingham said. More than 200

items.t: One person dead after Fairfield crash on I-80 involving sport bike
items.x: (FOX40.COM) — One person is dead Thursday morning after a crash involving a sport bike in Fairfield, according to the California Highway Patrol. CHP said a person riding a BMW sport bike crashed around 4:22 a.m. on westbound Interstate 80 at the Manuel Campos Parkway onramp. The rider, identified as a 37-year-old man from Vacaville, was entering the onramp and failed to negotiate the curve due to his speed and crashed, CHP said. Officers arrived to find the man unconscious with shallow breathing. The Fairfield Fire Department began life-saving measures. Despite the efforts, the man was pronounced dead around 4:36 a.m. No other vehicles or people were involved. "The officers and staff of CHP Solano extend our deepest condolences to the family, friends, and everyone affected by this heartbreaking incident," a spokesperson with CHP said. The crash is under investigation.

items.t: Wendy’s gets buyout offer while struggling with beef prices and growing competition
items.x: Wendy’s shares jumped more than 14% Wednesday after noted investor Nelson Peltz made an offer to buy the chain, which has been struggling with high beef prices and aging stores. Peltz’s Trian Fund Management and several partners are offering Wendy’s $7.35 per share in cash, or a premium of nearly 19% over the stock’s closing price on Tuesday, in a deal that would take the company private. The offer values Wendy's at $1.4 billion. Wendy's, which is based in Dublin, Ohio, confirmed receipt of the unsolicited proposal in a statement Wednesday and said its board has formed an independent committee to evaluate it. At the end of last year, Wendy's had 5,969 restaurants in the U.S. and 1,428 outlets in 38 countries. Wendy's, founded in 1969 by Dave Thomas and named after his daughter, is known for its square burgers and Frosty desserts. The fast-growing chain introduced the drive-thru window in 1970 and went public in 1976. In the 1980s, as it jockeyed for sales with McDonald's and Burger King, Wendy's launched salad bars and ran its iconic “Where's the beef?” ad campaign. But as the fast-food market grew even more competitive and rival burger-focused chains like In-N-Out and Five Guys ex

items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: ( The Hill ) Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. Gasoline and energy costs have risen in six of nine months this year, as the Iran war sparked oil price shocks via the Islamic Republic's restrictions on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Persistent inflation , which has remained above the Fed's 2 percent target for five-and-a-half years, spurred central bank officials to hike interest rates by a quarter point in mid-September. items.t: Dutch Bros. location in Fair Oaks closed after drive-thru crash
items.x: (FOX40.COM) — A Dutch Bros. coffee stand in Fair Oaks is closed Thursday following an early-morning crash. Officials said a woman driving eastbound veered off the road and into the drive-thru of the business just before 3 a.m. on Madison and Kenneth Avenues. There were no employees working at the time of the crash, but the impact did damage a hot water container and cause items to spill and scatter inside. A pole, signage, two tables and several Halloween decorations outside were also damaged. The business is closed for damage assessment and to clean up glass, metal, plastic and other debris. Employees said multiple Dutch Bros. locations within five miles are still open. The business hopes to reopen Thursday but could be closed until Friday. Madison Avenue was closed for about two hours during the investigation but has since reopened.

items.t: DoorDash to buy Instacart in $17 billion grocery delivery deal
items.x: DoorDash is gobbling up Instacart in a $17 billion acquisition that will supercharge its grocery delivery business. DoorDash said the Instacart brand name and app will remain, and Instacart shoppers can continue fulfilling orders for Instacart. Grocers can also choose to work with Instacart or DoorDash. Instacart customers will now have access to 50,000 additional stores covered by DoorDash, the company said. Instacart, founded in 2012, specializes in grocery and convenience store delivery in the U.S. and Canada. Its 600,000 “shoppers” — who are independent contractors — completed 338 million orders last year, according to company filings. Instacart has a market value of $14 billion. DoorDash, founded in San Francisco in 2013, began as a restaurant delivery business but has expanded to pet food and electronics. Operating in 40 countries, it completed more than 3 billion orders last year using a network of 9 million independent delivery workers. It has a market value of $73 billion. DoorDash began delivering groceries in 2020 amid a surge in pandemic-era demand. Grocers were initially cautious. items.t: RFK Jr. eases access to unproven peptides despite opposition from FDA scientists
items.x: WASHINGTON (AP) — The Trump administration on Wednesday acted to ease access to unproven peptide drugs favored by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr . Food and Drug Administration scientific staffers had little input on the decision and opposed the changes, according to six people familiar with its development. The draft policy posted online by Kennedy’s Department of Health and Human Services covers a handful of injectable peptides promoted within the wellness industry for uses such as building muscle, healing injuries and boosting energy. The government will take comments for two weeks before finalizing the measure. The document, primarily written by officials at HHS, faced overwhelming pushback among FDA drug staffers who warned it could undermine the agency’s long-standing mission of keeping unsafe health products off the U.S. market, according to the people familiar with its development. items.x: SACRAMENTO, Calif. (KTXL) — Sacramento Republic FC forward Kyle Edwards has developed a reputation for delivering when his team needs him most. Whether it's a late-game goal, a burst of energy off the bench or a game-winning finish, Edwards has become one of Republic FC's most valuable weapons heading into the USL Championship playoffs. items.t: California ballot measure guide: Everything you need to know
items.x: (Inside California Politics) — Californians are already voting in high-profile elections across the state, from the gubernatorial race to congressional contests, along with dozens of other state and local races. On this special election-season edition of Inside California Politics , host Nikki Laurenzo and capitol correspondent Eytan Wallace break down each of those ballot measures, from the high-profile "billionaire tax" to lesser-discussed proposals like bonds for housing and health research. items.t: Stockton serial killing suspect found competent to stand trial
items.x: (FOX40.COM) — The man suspected of perpetrating a series of shootings in and around Stockton in 2021 and 2022 has been found competent to stand trial by a jury, the San Joaquin County District Attorney Ron Freitas announced Wednesday. Wesley Brownlee is charged with six counts of first-degree murder and one count of attempted murder. Brownlee was arrested on October 15, 2022, following five shootings that spanned from July 8 of that year to September 27. Brownlee is also suspected in two shootings, one of which was fatal, in April of 2021. Most of the fatal shootings he is charged with happened at night or in the morning as victims walked to or were in their cars. Police said at the time that they found him in the early morning with a gun and wearing a mask around his neck. “After years of delay, the victims’ families and this community deserve their day in court," Freitas said.

U.S. District Judge David Carter ruled California can continue to accept the questioned ballots like any other. “This request violates longstanding constitutional principles mandating that states have control over their elections,” Carter wrote. “If Plaintiff’s last-minute request for relief were granted, either party could create chaos for their own political purposes to disrupt the election process,” he continued. “Over 20,000 registered Californians would potentially lose the right that generations of Americans have fought to preserve.” California has raised eyebrows at the veracity of the administration's list and says it's not obligated to verify voters’ citizenship in response. The state has conceded it's not feasible to segregate a ballot once it's processed. It would be counted even if later found to be fraudulent. items.t: Santa Clara parolee arrested for West Sacramento business burglaries
items.x: (FOX40.COM) — A Santa Clara person was arrested in connection to a series of burglaries and vandalism in West Sacramento, officials announced Wednesday. At the beginning of October, six different West Sacramento businesses along West Capitol Avenue were burglarized and vandalized within a single week, the West Sacramento Police Department said. Officers and and detectives obtained surveillance footage that helped them identify a suspect. A person wearing similar clothing to the suspect in the footage was found along West Capitol Avenue and then arrested. This person was a wanted parolee from Santa Clara, with multiple outstanding felony warrants throughout the Bay Area, West Sacramento police said. Officers searched the location where the suspect was staying and found property believed to be connected to the burglaries.

items.t: Harris advises Democrats against attempting to impeach Trump
items.x: ( The Hill ) Former Vice President Kamala Harris on Tuesday urged Democrats against making a third attempt to impeach President Trump if they win back the House after next week's midterm elections. "I think that going in the direction of impeachment is not a good idea, just to be honest with you," Harris told MeidasTouch's Aaron Parnas in an interview. "Just because we have limited resources and I think the energy and the resources need to put into accountability, need to be put into investigations." "And that's where the time should be spent," she added. "Remember, I was in the Senate for the last go-around, and the votes aren't there. "So, that's how I feel. But also, I think after the election, we all have to just also agree that our attitude has to be to get stuff done." Harris said Democrats should be "uncompromising" and "not sit around, you know, being genteel about the relationships," but maintain accountability when it comes to cuts to healthcare and oversight on the Iran war. items.t: Stockton City Councilmember up for reelection detained by Political Corruption Unit
items.x: This story was updated Wednesday afternoon to include a statement from Brando Villapudua. (FOX40.COM) — Brando Villapudua, a Stockton City Councilmember up for reelection this November, was detained and later released by the San Joaquin County District Attorney's Office on Wednesday morning, the office said. Villapudua has represented District 5 since January 2023 — his first term on Stockton City Council. Prior to that, he served as Stockton Planning Commissioner for two years. The district attorney's office announced Tuesday in a news release that the Political Corruption Unit within its Bureau of Investigations detained the councilmember "for an investigation and service of search warrants." The unit later released him without filing charges and declined to comment on why. According to the county district attorney's office, the investigation into Villapudua is ongoing and anyone with information is encouraged to call the Bureau of Investigations at 209-468-2400. Hours after being detained, Villapudua gave a recorded statement in front of Stockton City Hall. In it, he thanked supporters and pledged to keep serving as a councilmember. "We're gonna fight this," Villapudua asserted.

items.t: ‘Hoarder conditions’ make for difficult firefight at Sacramento home
items.x: (FOX40.COM) — Firefighters had a challenging time battling flames at a Sacramento home with "hoarder conditions" late Wednesday morning, fire officials said. Around 10:41 a.m., the Sacramento Fire Department responded to a house fire in the 3100 block of 60th Street in the city's Tahoe Park community. Crews arrived to find a heavy fire burning through the single-story house, the fire department said. Although no one was home, fire officials said the hoarder conditions added additional challenges for crews. No one was in the home when firefighters arrived and no injuries resulted from the fire. Officials are currently investigating the cause.

Along with counsel, the inmate, 49-year-old Jose Romero of Fairfield, participated in a Sept. 4 hearing in which he was denied parole for three more years. The decision was based on arguments from counsel as well as the lasting impact that left Romero’s wife permanently scarred following a weeks-long assault she endured in 2011. On Aug. 11, 2011, Romero assaulted his then-19-year-old wife with the goal of framing his ex-girlfriend and mother of his child. According to his plan, framing his ex-girlfriend would result in her being deported to Mexico and therefore allow Romero to obtain custody of their child, the district attorney's office said in a Tuesday news release. Romero then went on to assault the victim by punching her, cutting her hair and stabbing her in the abdomen, leading to hospitalization and an emergency surgery procedure. Greenville Police Department officials said that Panettiere's death has been ruled accidental, based on findings in the investigation and the medical examiner's determination. On August 16, Panettiere was found unresponsive in an apartment at the Judson Mill Lofts on Easley Bridge Road. Police said that Brian Hickerson, Panettiere's on-and-off boyfriend, along with his brother, Zach Hickerson, were at the residence. EMS attempted life-saving measures before pronouncing Panettiere dead at 2:31 p.m. According to the Greenville County Coroner's Office, Panettiere had died from an accidental overdose of fentanyl, 4-ANPP, Alprazolam, Methocarbamol and Quetiapine. Panettiere had spoken openly about challenges in her personal life, including emotional scars from her childhood fame, postpartum depression after giving birth to her daughter, and struggles with alcohol addiction. items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war , creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle . items.t: Halloween pet safety: How to make sure your pets are comfortable
items.x: (FOX40.COM) — Halloween is just days away and officials with Sacramento County's Bradshaw Animal Shelter are sharing ways residents can ensure their pets are safe and comfortable. Pet owners are asked to keep candy out of reach of their furry friends. Chocolate, especially dark and baking chocolate, can be dangerous for dogs and cats. Meanwhile, xylitol, a sweetener found in some candies and gum, along with raisins, can be life-threatening and dangerous to dogs. Officials said swallowed wrappers can also cause blockages. Community members are asked to store treats in a closed cabinet and pick up wrappers. To include pets in Halloween celebrations, give them their usual treats. Before guests or trick-or-treaters arrive, pet owners can set up a comfortable room with water, bedding and familiar toys away from the front door. The door should be kept closed and guests should be advised that the room is off-limits. Pet owners should consider walking their dog before trick-or-treaters hit the streets. He was 92. Nominated by then-President Bill Clinton in 1998, Hellerstein oversaw many high-profile disputes during his nearly three decades on the bench in New York City. He was back in the national limelight presiding over the proceedings for Maduro , who was captured and brought to the U.S. earlier this year over accusations of narco-terrorism. Maduro and his wife were in the judge's courtroom less than two weeks ago to plead not guilty to a new set of criminal charges. Before the Maduro operation, Hellerstein had long clashed with President Donald Trump in court. The judge at one point agreed that Trump’s fixer-turned-foe, Michael Cohen, could be released from prison to home confinement. Cohen has cast his prosecution as retribution by Trump. Separately, Hellerstein repeatedly denied Trump's efforts to move his hush money criminal prosecution into federal court, forcing the president to try his luck in New York's state system. items.t: US stocks hold steady as the countdown ticks to a Federal Reserve decision on interest rates
items.x: NEW YORK (AP) — U.S. stocks are drifting Wednesday as the countdown ticks toward this afternoon’s announcement from the Federal Reserve on what it will do with interest rates . The S&P 500 rose 0.2% and pulled within 1% of its all-time high , which was set earlier this month. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 176 points, or 0.3%, as of 11:45 a.m. Eastern time, and the Nasdaq composite was virtually unchanged. The day’s highlight will likely be what the Federal Reserve says, if anything, about where interest rates are heading. The Fed raised its main interest rate last month for the first time in three years in hopes of slowing the high inflation that’s squeezing the economy and discouraging Americans . The widespread expectation on Wall Street is that the Fed will leave the federal funds rate alone at this meeting, and the question is whether it will give hints about what may happen at later meetings. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh, though, has been adamant since taking over the Fed about wanting it to give fewer indications about its future moves. items.t: Dolores Huerta, labor leader and civil rights icon, lived a life of ‘fearlessness’
items.x: BAKERSFIELD, Calif. (KGET) Dolores Huerta lived a long and remarkable life of service and controversy, conflict, achievement and fame. She was among the last of a generation of iconic civil rights leaders and advocates for change that included Robert F. Kennedy, Martin Luther King Jr., and her colleague and mentor, Cesar Chavez. But unlike those leaders Huerta lived a long, full life into her 90s — and she never retired. Huerta died Wednesday at age 96, her family announced on social media. Her cause of death has not been determined yet. "As you can imagine, this is an incredibly difficult time for us, and we ask for privacy as we grieve this incredible loss to our family," Huerta's family said. "We know that many of you around the world share in our mourning, and we will be following up on plans to recognize and celebrate her incredible life and legacy." Freeways expand, transit systems improve, and technology promises more efficient journeys. Yet travelling across the city can still take a remarkable amount of time. A British aerospace company believes part of the solution might be above the roads rather than on them. items.t: Man dead following attack at California State Prison in Sacramento, officials say
items.x: (FOX40.COM) — The death of an inmate at California State Prison, Sacramento located in Folsom on Monday is being investigated as a homicide, prison officials said. According to the California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation, around 6:43 p.m., prison staff saw inmates Justin Castro and Luis Mendoza attack Carlos Montenegro. Officers disrupted the attack using "less lethal 40mm direct impact rounds" and attempted life-saving measures on Montenegro. Two improvised weapons were found at the scene, the agency said. Paramedics arrived at the prison and pronounced the man dead at 7:24 p.m. Montenegro, 39, was a little over two years into a six-year sentence. items.t: Utah authorities connect 1974 cold case to serial killer Ted Bundy
items.x: SUMMIT COUNTY, Utah ( KTVX ) — Investigators in Summit County, Utah closed the 1974 cold case homicide of Melissa Ann Smith Tuesday, linking her murder to prominent serial killer Ted Bundy. Using DNA and other evidence, the Summit County Sheriff's Office and Summit County Attorney's Office formally closed the cold-case murder, saying that the evidence conclusively proves that Ted Bundy murdered 17-year-old Melissa Ann Smith. Bundy has long been considered a suspect in several cold cases in Utah, and Smith's murder was one of them. Hunters found her remains in Summit County on Oct. 27, 1974, 52 years ago today. "The work began with the investigators who handled the case in 1974, and it continued through the dedication and perseverance of those who carried it forward," Summit County Sheriff Kacey Bates said. "After 50 years, we have reached a point that so many have worked toward." items.t: 4 in 10 say personal finances worsening: Survey
items.x: ( The Hill ) Four in 10 Americans say their personal finances are deteriorating, according to a new poll released shortly before November's midterm elections. In the NPR/PBS News/Marist Poll , 40 percent of people said their “personal family finances” have declined in the last 12 months, while 16 percent said the opposite. Forty-one percent said their personal family finances have “stayed about the same” within the prior year. Less than 1 percent of poll respondents were not sure about the state of their personal family finances within the last year, while three percent didn’t give an answer. The NPR/PBS News/Marist Poll was conducted two weeks out from Election Day, with the rise in cost of living being a major concern in this election cycle. September saw an uptick in annual inflation for Americans, with the cost of energy, gas and electricity rising from August to September. Democrats have campaigned on targeting the Trump administration's tariffs and the war in Iran — two factors behind U.S. price hikes. items.t: Cause of death revealed for ‘Office Space’ actor Richard Riehle: Reports
items.x: (NEXSTAR) – The cause of death for longtime actor Richard Riehle has been revealed, according to reports. The 78-year-old died earlier this month in Los Angeles, friends told TMZ , which was the first to report the news. The outlet and People , citing his death certificate, reported Tuesday that the "Office Space" actor experienced a stroke and had oropharyngeal cancer. He had been in a rehabilitation center at the time of his death in mid-October, according to People. Oropharyngeal cancer , which can be asymptomatic, impacts the middle portion of your throat, including the base of your tongue and the tonsils. While there are multiple types of oropharyngeal cancers, Johns Hopkins Medicine says the majority are squamous cell carcinomas, which are further divided into HPV-related and HPV-unrelated. The former is caused by HPV, while the latter is commonly caused by tobacco or alcohol. Details about Riehle's condition were not released. "The Provost used AI to meaningfully alter his writing in violation of at least one publication’s AI use and/or disclosure requirement, failed to disclose his use of AI in clear violation of a national newspaper’s stated policy, was not forthcoming about his AI use, and fell short of the standards set forth by Dartmouth’s Code of Ethical Conduct, the Academic Honor Principle, and Geisel’s Policy on Expectations for Professionalism for Faculty, Non-Faculty Academics, and Staff," the committee concluded. Schnell was accused of using AI to alter his work by the student newspaper The Dartmouth and outlet Semafor, specifically pointing to an opinion piece the provost wrote for The Washington Post. items.t: AAA advises drivers about daylight saving time
items.x: ( WAVY ) – It's only a few days until we trade one extra hour of sleep for months of darkness as we leave work to drive home. And even though we're on the easier end of the time transition (from daylight saving time to standard time), the switch still takes its toll. Nexstar's WAVY went to AAA Tidewater Virginia to see what commuters can expect. "Well, the biggest thing for drivers will be the change in daylight when we leave work or school," said Holly Dalby with AAA. "At the end of the day, gone will be the bright sunshine, and we will find ourselves either driving into the glare from the setting sun or driving home in the dark. So it's a time to be particularly careful on the roads." Days will get way shorter in November: How much daylight will we lose? While lawmakers have tried to get rid of the time switch altogether, it doesn't appear to be going anywhere anytime soon, so your circadian rhythm will have to dance to a different beat for a while. "It just messing with our sleep schedule can really add to our fatigue very quickly. And when we're fatigued, we can make mistakes," Dalby said. items.t: TONIGHT: Man in the Sea Museum to Dive into Art with benefit show and sale
items.x: PANAMA CITY BEACH, Fla. ( WMBB ) – Happening Thursday, the Man in the Sea Museum will host its inaugural Dive into Art show and sale, benefiting the museum's efforts within the local diving community. From 5 p.m. until 9 p.m., the museum located at 17314 Panama City Beach Parkway will be full of creative moments alongside the rich underwater history present year-round. “If you've never been out to the museum, it’s a great opportunity to just come check it out and hopefully buy something while you're here to support the museum that's part of Bay County's history and of course support these artists as well,” said the Executive Director of the Man in the Sea Museum, Steve Mulholland. This one-night-only event will feature Deep Sea Dive Art by Rick Armstrong, Marsha Edmond Art, Harman Metal Art, and White Sands Woodwork. There will also be drinks & hors d'oeuvres available during the free admission event. For more information, click here .

Others in data center hotspots like Texas and Ohio are worried about their electricity bills . items.t: ‘Gut punch’: 2 college students found dead in Colorado after going missing on mountain hike
items.x: ( WJW ) – Two missing Colorado college students were found dead Wednesday after they left campus for a weekend trip up a nearly 14,000-foot peak and encountered a heavy snowstorm, police said. Kaden Matsuda, 19, from Ridgway, Colorado, and Jackson Donlon, 20, from New York, left Colorado Mountain College Leadville’s campus on Friday and didn’t return. They told family and friends they planned to go up Ice Mountain, which requires technical climbing, according to the county sheriff’s office. On Wednesday night, the sheriff's office confirmed that the students were found dead around 3:30 p.m. in a basin of the West Apostle Mountain. Authorities do not believe foul play was involved. The investigation is now being handled by the Chaffee County Coroner’s Office. “Our heart aches for Kaden and Jackson’s family and friends. We are very proud of our team’s efforts to find them before this weekend’s coming storm," Sheriff Andy Rohrich wrote on Facebook. "Although this is a gut punch, our prayers were answered that we would find Kaden and Jackson, allowing some closure for the family. items.t: Cruise ship passenger says warning signs were there long before Cambodia
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — Kit Cassingham and her husband, Randy, sold their home and nearly everything they owned to live aboard a cruise ship for years. Now, she says she doesn't expect to see that money again. Cassingham told NewsNation's Jesse Weber on Wednesday that the couple paid about $370,000 to $380,000 for their cabin on the Villa Vie Odyssey, plus $7,000 a month in expenses. Asked if they will get it back, she said, "No, no, no, no." Cruise ship suspends voyage over fuel costs, stranding 200 passengers More than 200 passengers were told Tuesday to leave the Odyssey in Cambodia within hours after the cruise company suspended operations. In a news release , Villa Vie blamed soaring fuel costs tied to the war in Iran, saying the monthly fuel cost per cabin jumped from about $1,800 to as much as $8,000. Villa Vie Odyssey: How did passengers find out they had to leave? Cassingham and her husband had already gotten off the ship for a hotel so they could work online when a short message arrived saying the ship couldn't get more fuel . “You have till two o’clock to get off the ship,” she said. The news wasn't a total shock. “We’d seen red flags all along,” Cassingham said. More than 200

items.t: Wendy’s gets buyout offer while struggling with beef prices and growing competition
items.x: Wendy’s shares jumped more than 14% Wednesday after noted investor Nelson Peltz made an offer to buy the chain, which has been struggling with high beef prices and aging stores. Peltz’s Trian Fund Management and several partners are offering Wendy’s $7.35 per share in cash, or a premium of nearly 19% over the stock’s closing price on Tuesday, in a deal that would take the company private. The offer values Wendy's at $1.4 billion. Wendy's, which is based in Dublin, Ohio, confirmed receipt of the unsolicited proposal in a statement Wednesday and said its board has formed an independent committee to evaluate it. At the end of last year, Wendy's had 5,969 restaurants in the U.S. and 1,428 outlets in 38 countries. Wendy's, founded in 1969 by Dave Thomas and named after his daughter, is known for its square burgers and Frosty desserts. The fast-growing chain introduced the drive-thru window in 1970 and went public in 1976. In the 1980s, as it jockeyed for sales with McDonald's and Burger King, Wendy's launched salad bars and ran its iconic “Where's the beef?” ad campaign. items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: ( The Hill ) Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. Gasoline and energy costs have risen in six of nine months this year, as the Iran war sparked oil price shocks via the Islamic Republic's restrictions on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Persistent inflation , which has remained above the Fed's 2 percent target for five-and-a-half years, spurred central bank officials to hike interest rates by a quarter point in mid-September. items.t: DoorDash to buy Instacart in $17 billion grocery delivery deal
items.x: DoorDash is gobbling up Instacart in a $17 billion acquisition that will supercharge its grocery delivery business. DoorDash said the Instacart brand name and app will remain, and Instacart shoppers can continue fulfilling orders for Instacart. Grocers can also choose to work with Instacart or DoorDash. Instacart customers will now have access to 50,000 additional stores covered by DoorDash, the company said. Instacart, founded in 2012, specializes in grocery and convenience store delivery in the U.S. and Canada. Its 600,000 “shoppers” — who are independent contractors — completed 338 million orders last year, according to company filings. Instacart has a market value of $14 billion. DoorDash, founded in San Francisco in 2013, began as a restaurant delivery business but has expanded to pet food and electronics. Operating in 40 countries, it completed more than 3 billion orders last year using a network of 9 million independent delivery workers. It has a market value of $73 billion. DoorDash began delivering groceries in 2020 amid a surge in pandemic-era demand. Grocers were initially cautious. items.t: RFK Jr. eases access to unproven peptides despite opposition from FDA scientists
items.x: WASHINGTON (AP) — The Trump administration on Wednesday acted to ease access to unproven peptide drugs favored by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr . Food and Drug Administration scientific staffers had little input on the decision and opposed the changes, according to six people familiar with its development. The draft policy posted online by Kennedy’s Department of Health and Human Services covers a handful of injectable peptides promoted within the wellness industry for uses such as building muscle, healing injuries and boosting energy. The government will take comments for two weeks before finalizing the measure. The document, primarily written by officials at HHS, faced overwhelming pushback among FDA drug staffers who warned it could undermine the agency’s long-standing mission of keeping unsafe health products off the U.S. market, according to the people familiar with its development. items.t: Obama knocks Trump’s response to Cheesecake Factory jab: ‘These are not serious people’
items.x: ( The Hill ) Former President Obama on Wednesday responded to uproar over a recent campaign trail jab at President Trump’s White House decorations, slamming Republicans for focusing more on the joke than on the economy. “They mobilized a whole-of-government response to that joke, not to inflation, but to that joke,” Obama said during a campaign rally in Georgia. “This is what I mean when I say these are not serious people. Bam Adebayo also had 24 points and grabbed nine rebounds for the Heat, who lost their first four games after acquiring Antetokounmpo from Milwaukee in the offseason. Andrew Wiggins scored 18 points and Pelle Larsson had 17 points, eight assists and six rebounds for the Heat, who shot 53% from the field and had a whopping 70 points in the paint. items.t: After two-year search, woman’s coworker turns out to be a match for kidney transplant
items.x: SALT LAKE CITY, Utah ( ABC4 ) — Katie Hood and Reina Child became fast friends five years ago when they met as coworkers at Charlie's Produce in Salt Lake City. Then two years ago, Katie, 41, was diagnosed with renal failure. Family, friends and even coworkers began getting tested to see if they were a match. Reina, 47, knew she needed to be tested. And guess what? She is a perfect match. Now, the bond the two ladies share will grow even stronger because on Tuesday they're scheduled for kidney transplant surgery. The women had a pre-operation appointment today ahead of their surgery next Tuesday. That visit changed Katie's life. She was diagnosed with heart and kidney failure. "And I've been doing dialysis for three times a week for two years and yeah, just kind of on this crazy journey." items.t: DOJ’s California ballot fight rejected by another judge
items.x: ( The Hill ) The Trump administration's bid to separate 20,000 mail ballots in California that it says are likely noncitizens met another defeat on Wednesday as a trial judge refused to intervene. U.S. District Judge David Carter ruled California can continue to accept the questioned ballots like any other. “This request violates longstanding constitutional principles mandating that states have control over their elections,” Carter wrote. “If Plaintiff’s last-minute request for relief were granted, either party could create chaos for their own political purposes to disrupt the election process,” he continued. “Over 20,000 registered Californians would potentially lose the right that generations of Americans have fought to preserve.” California has raised eyebrows at the veracity of the administration's list and says it's not obligated to verify voters’ citizenship in response. The state has conceded it's not feasible to segregate a ballot once it's processed. It would be counted even if later found to be fraudulent. items.t: Failed Florida gubernatorial candidate announces 2028 White House bid
items.x: ( The Hill ) Former Florida gubernatorial candidate James Fishback (R) said he plans to run for president in 2028. “Last night, someone asked me ‘What do you plan on doing next?’ I told them the truth. items.t: Over 5,600 mail-in ballots in Bay County still unreturned
items.x: PANAMA CITY, Fla. (WMBB) If you're planning to vote by mail, but haven't put the ballot in the mail yet, you need to consider an alternative method of delivery. Voters have until 7 p.m. on Election Night to get their ballots to the Supervisor of Elections Office. If you've waited this long, the U.S. Postal Service may not get it there in time. According to Bay County Supervisor of Elections Nina Ward, more than 5,600 mail-in ballots have not been returned yet. If you're holding one of those ballots and you want it to be counted on Tuesday, Ward strongly urges those voters to drop them off in person. “I would encourage voters that if they're able get out this week until Saturday at 6 p.m., visit us at any of our early voting locations and we have a secure ballot intake station, a drop box that they can just hand deliver their vote by mail ballot too. That way they know it gets to us and they don't have to worry about getting it into the mail,” Ward said. If you're waiting to vote in person, you still have plenty of time. items.t: Florida Panhandle Marine Institute releases Z-Boo
items.x: CAPE SAN BLAS, Fla. (WMBB) Through the summer, sea turtle releases are common in the Florida Panhandle, especially during sea turtle nesting season on the beaches. But as sea turtle nesting season dwindles down, the releases continue on. "The rehab side actually has no bearing on the nesting season. So we can release turtles any time throughout the year as long as the water temperature and weather conditions are right. Basically, it's all about when the turtle is medically ready for release and ready to thrive again in their natural environment," FPMI Stranding Coordinator Lauren Albrittain said. Dozens gathered for the last-minute release of Z-Boo in Cape San Blas. Z-Boo is a juvenile green sea turtle that has been a rehabilitation patient for a full year. The name Z-Boo comes from an original experience from over a year ago. items.t: Panama City approves downtown gateway infrastructure project
items.x: PANAMA CITY, Fla. (WMBB) Most consider the intersection of 6th Street and West Beach Drive to be one of the main gateways to Downtown Panama City. City leaders want to make it a smooth entrance. They've approved an infrastructure project that will cover the section of West Beach Drive from 6th Street to 4th Street, along with Mulberry Avenue from 6th Street to West Beach Drive. The project includes replacing infrastructure, improving vehicular travel, and pedestrian access. "It's a complete infrastructure project, redoing all of the water lines, the sewer lines, and certainly the storm water lines, which is where there is a lot of problems with that system throughout that stretch of road," City Manager Jonathan Hayes said. "Water and sewer have not been updated in this town since it was installed, that was about 80 years ago," Commissioner Robbie Hughes said. The project will be completed in three phases, with construction planned to help businesses remain open while the work is underway. items.t: Harris advises Democrats against attempting to impeach Trump
items.x: ( The Hill ) Former Vice President Kamala Harris on Tuesday urged Democrats against making a third attempt to impeach President Trump if they win back the House after next week's midterm elections. "I think that going in the direction of impeachment is not a good idea, just to be honest with you," Harris told MeidasTouch's Aaron Parnas in an interview. "Just because we have limited resources and I think the energy and the resources need to put into accountability, need to be put into investigations." "And that's where the time should be spent," she added. "Remember, I was in the Senate for the last go-around, and the votes aren't there. "So, that's how I feel. But also, I think after the election, we all have to just also agree that our attitude has to be to get stuff done." Harris said Democrats should be "uncompromising" and "not sit around, you know, being genteel about the relationships," but maintain accountability when it comes to cuts to healthcare and oversight on the Iran war. items.t: New Rooted in Holmes initiative aims to end local hunger
items.x: HOLMES COUNTY, Fla. (WMBB) Holmes County is home to around 20,000 people. About 60% of those are struggling with food insecurity or financial instability. The "Rooted in Holmes" initiative hopes to change that statistic by providing food for the community. The project began with Crosspoint church. The United Way of Northwest Florida later joined the mission. "This is our mission: nobody goes hungry. And what we mean by that is both spiritually and physically; it's always been our heart if somebody is hungry, we want to feed them. We might not can pay their light bill and their electric bill, but we'll find a way to give them some food," Crosspoint Church Lead Pastor Michael Tadlock said. The Florida Blue Foundation has also joined the mission, committing $400,000 over the next four years. "With the partnership with United Way and Florida Blue, this is affording that opportunity for us to be able to move what was, you know, every other month to once-a-quarter distributions to, you know, at least once a month and being able to meet the need as the need arises," Tadlock said. items.t: Right-wing activist James O’Keefe charged with unlawful voting, identity theft
items.x: ( The Hill ) Conservative influencer James O’Keefe was charged in Minnesota Wednesday after he and fellow right-leaning commentator Cam Higby misrepresented themselves at a polling place during the state’s primary election earlier this year. Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty announced during a press conference the two men are facing felony unlawful voting and identity fraud charges. “Elections are the bedrock of democracy and their protection is one of our highest priorities,” Moriarty said in a statement . “Individuals engaging in unlawful conduct related to our elections will be held accountable.” On the state’s Aug. 11 primary election day, O’Keefe and Higby donned mock “ Muslim attire ,” spoke in fake accents at Minnesota polling places. O’Keefe and Higby began the state's unregistered voter vouching process under fake names but did not ultimately sign this oath or cast a vote, according to the county attorney. items.t: Hayden Panettiere death ruled accidental by police in South Carolina
items.x: GREENVILLE, S.C. ( WSPA ) – Police in South Carolina have officially closed the investigation into the death of Hayden Panettiere, according to a Wednesday news release. Greenville Police Department officials said that Panettiere's death has been ruled accidental, based on findings in the investigation and the medical examiner's determination. On August 16, Panettiere was found unresponsive in an apartment at the Judson Mill Lofts on Easley Bridge Road. Police said that Brian Hickerson, Panettiere's on-and-off boyfriend, along with his brother, Zach Hickerson, were at the residence. EMS attempted life-saving measures before pronouncing Panettiere dead at 2:31 p.m. According to the Greenville County Coroner's Office, Panettiere had died from an accidental overdose of fentanyl, 4-ANPP, Alprazolam, Methocarbamol and Quetiapine. Panettiere had spoken openly about challenges in her personal life, including emotional scars from her childhood fame, postpartum depression after giving birth to her daughter, and struggles with alcohol addiction. items.t: Woman fights for life after crash kills unborn son
items.x: BAY COUNTY, Fla. ( WMBB ) A woman is fighting to recover after a car accident in Panama City killed her unborn child and left her in critical condition. A GoFundMe has been set up to support Audra and her family. According to the GoFundMe, Audra who is a registered nurse, was 34 weeks pregnant with her son, Henry Ellis Furber, when she was involved in a car crash a few days ago in Panama City. Sadly, Henry didn't survive the crash. Event organizers of the GoFundMe said Audra's recovery is uncertain and includes several surgeries. They also said her fiancé is reducing his work hours so he can stay by Audra's side in the hospital. "If you are unable to give, please continue to pray for Audra, her fiancé, and our entire family," wrote organizers. "Sharing this fundraiser would also mean so much to us." To donate to Audra’s GoFundMe, click here .

items.t: Trump approves FEMA assistance for Panhandle following Hurricane Isaias
items.x: ACROSS THE PANHANDLE, Fla. (WMBB) Following Hurricane Isaias, FEMA has announced that federal disaster assistance has been approved for our area. President Donald Trump approved the FEMA assistance on Wednesday for areas affected by Hurricane Isaias from Oct. 6 through 12. Public assistance and federal funding will be available for state, tribal, and local governments and certain non-profit organizations in Bay, Calhoun, Escambia, Franklin, Gadsden, Gulf, Holmes, Jackson, Jefferson, Liberty, Okaloosa, Santa Rosa, Wakulla, Walton, and Washington Counties. The funding will be used to provide emergency work and repairs for public facilities damaged in Hurricane Isaias.

items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war , creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle . items.t: Beachfront home fire displaces family in Miramar Beach
items.x: WALTON COUNTY, Fla. ( WMBB ) A beachfront home caught fire late Tuesday evening, leaving one family displaced. According to the South Walton Fire District, the fire occurred around 9:20 p.m. near the area of Beach Drive East in Miramar Beach. Responding crews began extinguishing the flames and worked to mitigate the incident and overhaul any hot spots. Most of the crews were released from the scene by midnight and were able to return to their stations. The residents were home during the time of the incident but were not injured and no firefighter injuries were reported. Firefighters said the fire caused significant damage to the home and resulted in the family being displaced. SWFD contacted the American Red Cross to assist the homeowners. A neighboring home was sustained broken windows due to the fire's heat. SWFD Fire Investigators and the State Fire Marshal's Office are conducting a joint investigation into the cause of the fire.

items.t: Judge overseeing Maduro trial dies
items.x: ( The Hill ) Alvin Hellerstein, a longtime federal judge who was set to oversee the criminal trial of deposed Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro, has passed away, according to a court official. He was 92. Nominated by then-President Bill Clinton in 1998, Hellerstein oversaw many high-profile disputes during his nearly three decades on the bench in New York City. He was back in the national limelight presiding over the proceedings for Maduro , who was captured and brought to the U.S. earlier this year over accusations of narco-terrorism. Maduro and his wife were in the judge's courtroom less than two weeks ago to plead not guilty to a new set of criminal charges. Before the Maduro operation, Hellerstein had long clashed with President Donald Trump in court. The judge at one point agreed that Trump’s fixer-turned-foe, Michael Cohen, could be released from prison to home confinement. Cohen has cast his prosecution as retribution by Trump. Separately, Hellerstein repeatedly denied Trump's efforts to move his hush money criminal prosecution into federal court, forcing the president to try his luck in New York's state system. items.t: Project 25 car show returns to support local children
items.x: BAY COUNTY, Fla. ( WMBB ) Cool cars, several vendors, and supporting children at Christmas are what the 25th Annual Project 25 Car Show is all about. The fundraiser put on by American Muscle Car Club will be on Sunday, Nov. 1 at the Bay County Fairgrounds in Panama City. The event is from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. and free to spectators. However, spectators are encouraged to bring an unwrapped toy. Registration is from 9 a.m. to 12 p.m. The registration fee is a $20 donation or a new, unwrapped toy. Nelson Foundation donates $500,000 for school prep program "We're probably gonna have about 150 cars there," American Muscle Car Club President Troy Brown said. Brown said there will be more than 20 vendors set up as well. This benefits Project 25, which supports Bay County children at Christmas. "Project 25 started in 1980 when two deputies saw a need for some kids to have toys because they weren't going to have any on Christmas," said Deputy Jake Navarro, Public Affairs Specialist for Bay County Sheriff's Office. "[They] went and bought some toys for these kids and kind of avalanched from there."

items.t: US stocks hold steady as the countdown ticks to a Federal Reserve decision on interest rates
items.x: NEW YORK (AP) — U.S. stocks are drifting Wednesday as the countdown ticks toward this afternoon’s announcement from the Federal Reserve on what it will do with interest rates . The S&P 500 rose 0.2% and pulled within 1% of its all-time high , which was set earlier this month. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 176 points, or 0.3%, as of 11:45 a.m. Eastern time, and the Nasdaq composite was virtually unchanged. The day’s highlight will likely be what the Federal Reserve says, if anything, about where interest rates are heading. The Fed raised its main interest rate last month for the first time in three years in hopes of slowing the high inflation that’s squeezing the economy and discouraging Americans . The widespread expectation on Wall Street is that the Fed will leave the federal funds rate alone at this meeting, and the question is whether it will give hints about what may happen at later meetings. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh, though, has been adamant since taking over the Fed about wanting it to give fewer indications about its future moves. Arrest documents show Rebecca Walpole and a male suspect entered the Madison, Tennessee, Home Depot on May 26 and rented a boom lift, which is commonly known as a cherry picker or basket crane. The equipment was towed using a silver Dodge Ram. According to court documents, the property was never returned. Nashville Super 8 sued over almost $150K in unpaid repair bills The male suspect was arrested in Michigan on Sept. 23, according to arrest documents. Investigators said he admitted to selling rented construction equipment to buyers on Facebook Marketplace. Walpole faces a felony theft of property charge, and she was recently booked in Davidson County. Her bond was set at $10,000.

items.t: Dolores Huerta, labor leader and activist, dies at 96
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Activist Dolores Huerta, who helped co-found the National Farm Workers Association with César Chavez, has died. She was 96. Huerta's family said in a statement through her foundation that she died Wednesday at home. "We are deeply saddened to announce that our beloved mother, Dolores Huerta, has passed away today at the age of 96," her family said in a statement posted on social media. "As you can imagine, this is an incredibly difficult time for us, and we ask for privacy as we grieve this incredible loss to our family," the statement continued. "We know that many of you around the world share in our mourning, and we will be following up on plans to recognize and celebrate her incredible life and legacy." Kotlikoff after allegations of a 2024 gang rape at a campus fraternity that resulted in no criminal charges caused uproar around the country. The more than 75 members of the body will have their second meeting debating the resolution and the timing of a vote on it. A motion could be introduced to delay the no-confidence vote and set another meeting. But if that motion is not introduced or fails, members of the Faculty Senate will begin the no-confidence vote after Wednesday's meeting is over, and they typically have a week to cast their choice online. While a no-confidence vote has no authority to remove an official, its passing would show deep dissatisfaction from faculty with how Cornell leadership has handled accusations from Jane Doe that seven members of the Chi Phi fraternity raped her . What does the no-confidence vote entail? items.t: Sabato’s Crystal Ball moves 16 House races toward Democrats

Crystal Ball, a division of the University of Virginia’s Center for Politics, has moved dozens of races toward Democrats in recent weeks, including nearly 50 races in the month of October alone. The race changes include moving a few deep-red seats into the “toss up” column. Open congressional districts in Kentucky and Montana, as well as seats with GOP incumbents in Missouri, Virginia, Colorado and Pennsylvania moved into coin flip territory. Many of the seats Crystal Ball rates as a toss-up were places Trump carried by double digits in 2024. The Flying Car Is Moving Beyond Science Fiction Los Angeles has spent decades trying to solve its traffic problems. Freeways expand, transit systems improve, and technology promises more efficient journeys. Yet travelling across the city can still take a remarkable amount of time. A British aerospace company believes part of the solution might be above the roads rather than on them. Vertical Aerospace has demonstrated an electric aircraft capable of taking off vertically, transitioning into conventional forward flight, and landing without a runway. The technology was publicly displayed at the Farnborough International Airshow in Britain, marking an important development in the company's plans to introduce commercial passenger flights. items.x: URDA, Spain (AP) — A high-speed train slammed into another that had stopped on the tracks in Spain on Wednesday, killing at least 68 people and injuring dozens in the second deadly rail collision this year. The regional government of Castilla La Mancha confirmed the death toll and said another 58 people were receiving medical treatment at hospitals. Rescue workers searched the wreckage through the day for survivors and bodies. items.x: PANAMA CITY, Fla. (WMBB) Panama City commissioners have approved a revised plan to rebid the Downtown Marina Project, this time leaving out the boat ramp. The updated plan focuses on rebuilding the marina in phases, starting with 50 boat slips in the west basin. The second phase calls for extending the existing breakwater That dock is designed to accommodate day to day use and visiting boats, giving more boaters a place to dock in downtown Panama City. "This area has amazing marine contractors, large and small. You have people building small docks that are 40 feet long. City officials will move forward, preparing the revised bid package and soliciting bids from qualified marine construction companies.

items.x: BAY COUNTY Fla. (WMBB) At Deane Bozeman, students have the opportunity to work with animals, but it's not just about the animals. items.t: Trump and Talarico hold dueling Texas rallies
items.x: ( The Hill ) President Trump and Texas Senate candidate James Talarico (D) shared their competing visions Tuesday as the two held dueling rallies in the Lone Star State one week before the midterm elections. Trump did two rallies in Texas — the first in Corpus Christi and another in Lubbock . It’s his fourth trip to Texas to support Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton. Talarico held his own rally in Lubbock on Tuesday. He was in Corpus Christi on Saturday. The Texas race is one of the most contested and watched Senate races in the country. Talarico and Paxton remain close in the polls — Real Clear Polling calls the race a toss-up, with Talarico holding a slight lead. A Democrat winning the Senate seat would be a shock — none have won a U.S. Senate race in Texas since 1988, and Trump won the state by nearly 14 percentage points in the 2024 presidential election. Democrats are vying to take control of the House and the Senate. The party would need to win four seats to win control of the Senate. items.t: City Clerk duties discussed, expected to solidify Nov. 10
items.x: LYNN HAVEN, Fla. (WMBB) Lynn Haven City Commissioners are working to nail down the role of the new city clerk position. They voted to create a clerk-treasurer position to work under the city, focusing primarily on budgetary matters. During tonight's discussions, two roles seemed to emerge. Commissioner Corey Langford believes the clerk should concentrate on the budget process, while commissioner Jamie Warrick wants the clerk to focus on the city's general financial work. "What they do is the city manager will handle operations, right? The day to day, the fixing of the pipes, the running of the city. But we have a totally separate bean counter and check book monitor, if you will. And both of these individuals are peers. So they work together. One handles," Mayor Dave Lowery said. Commissioners want to finalize the clerk's job duties by their November 10 commission meeting. Lowery says he hopes the city can hire a new city clerk within 30 days of posting the job.

items.t: Nelson Foundation donates $500,000 for school prep program
items.x: BAY COUNTY, Fla. (WMBB) Bay District School officials are using a $500,000 donation to help prepare youngsters for school. Bay County School Board members announced the new Kindergarten Preparatory Academy on Tuesday. The free eight-week summer program will begin next summer at six bay county schools, with up to 180 incoming kindergarteners attending. They'll focus on early literacy, math, STEM and social development, helping to build the skills and confidence they need before entering the classroom. The program will run weekdays from7:30 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. with free after school care available until 5:30. items.t: Couple and dogs safe after Panama City home caught fire
items.x: PANAMA CITY, Fla. (WMBB) Panama City Fire officials are still trying to determine the cause of a fire that destroyed a home Tuesday evening. The call came in about ten minutes before 6:00 at a home on Loyola Lane, north of 23rd Street off Harrison Ave. Firefighters arrived within five minutes and found heavy smoke coming from the home with flames spreading into the attic. A married couple and their two dogs had escaped safely. Authorities believe the fire started near the back porch and spread up the side of the house into the attic. Despite firefighters' best efforts, the home sustained heavy fire damage and is considered a total loss. The cause of the fire remains under investigation.

items.t: Florida cocaine case exposes alleged Sinaloa cartel route through El Paso

items.t: GoFundMe set up after South Walton man drowns in Gulf
items.x: WALTON COUNTY, Fla. (WMBB) Friends of a local family are asking you to help them after suffering an unthinkable tragedy. 31-year old Stone Romberg drowned in the Gulf. According to the GoFundMe page, Romberg was fishing near the inlet when he caught a seagull. He swam out to free the bird, but it got tangled-up around his hand. As he tried to swim back-in, the current carried him farther out and he drown. Romberg was well known in South Walton. He worked for La Dolce Vita Beach service. He leaves behind a wife and two young daughters ages 1 and 3. To donate, click here .

items.t: Franklin County man convicted in child sting operation
items.x: FRANKLIN COUNTY, Fla. (WMBB) A Franklin County man, arrested during a sex sting operation in Aug. 2025 is going to prison. A federal jury found 38-year-old William Jared Breski guilty of attempting to entice a minor to produce child sexual abuse material, attempting to transfer obscene material to a minor, and a penalty for registered sex offenders. Breski was arrested twice that month, once by Franklin County Sheriff's deputies for failure to register and providing false registration information. Then, Leon County Sheriff's Investigators arrested him for soliciting a minor, soliciting the performance of a sexual act by a child, harmful communication with a minor and trasmitting obscene material to a minor. The sex sting was called "Operation Summer Hurricane." From July 10 through the 12, undercover law enforcement officers spent hours staring at computer screens, posing as teenagers and talking to suspected child predators. It was the first-ever sting operation of it's kind in Franklin County. Breski faces a mandatory minimum of 10 years in prison, and up to life on each of the 3-counts. His sentencing is scheduled for January 28.

"The work began with the investigators who handled the case in 1974, and it continued through the dedication and perseverance of those who carried it forward," Summit County Sheriff Kacey Bates said. items.t: 4 in 10 say personal finances worsening: Survey
items.x: ( The Hill ) Four in 10 Americans say their personal finances are deteriorating, according to a new poll released shortly before November's midterm elections. In the NPR/PBS News/Marist Poll , 40 percent of people said their “personal family finances” have declined in the last 12 months, while 16 percent said the opposite. Forty-one percent said their personal family finances have “stayed about the same” within the prior year. Less than 1 percent of poll respondents were not sure about the state of their personal family finances within the last year, while three percent didn’t give an answer. The NPR/PBS News/Marist Poll was conducted two weeks out from Election Day, with the rise in cost of living being a major concern in this election cycle. September saw an uptick in annual inflation for Americans, with the cost of energy, gas and electricity rising from August to September. Democrats have campaigned on targeting the Trump administration's tariffs and the war in Iran — two factors behind U.S. price hikes. Amid the Iran war, the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway for the oil industry, has been closed. According to AAA , the average price of a regular gallon of gas in the U.S. has r

items.t: Bay County judge refuses to reduce Rebecca Falcon’s sentence
items.x: BAY COUNTY, Fla. (WMBB) A Bay County judge has made his decision in the case of a woman who was asking for a reduction in her sentence for murder. Judge Brantley Clark ruled he will not reduce Rebecca Falcon's life sentence. Falcon was only 15-years-old when she shot her cab driver, Richard Phillips, in the back of his head in 1997. Falcon was convicted on first-degree murder and was sentenced to life without parole in 1999. However, after the state passed a law in 2012 stating life without parole is unconstitutional for juveniles, Falcon was granted a new sentencing hearing in February. Judge Clark was considering Falcon's request in March, when the state introduced new evidence: 51 text messages between Falcon and her stepfather, Kent Kaneer. The messages from Falcon claimed Kaneer abused her, which played a role in her committing the murder. The new evidence led investigators to question Falcon's credibility. The state and defense submitted their written closing arguments in May. Judge Clark filed his decision on Tuesday.

The woman began working at the zoo when she was 17 and spent nearly all of her 40-year career there. items.t: Cause of death revealed for ‘Office Space’ actor Richard Riehle: Reports
items.x: (NEXSTAR) – The cause of death for longtime actor Richard Riehle has been revealed, according to reports. The 78-year-old died earlier this month in Los Angeles, friends told TMZ , which was the first to report the news. The outlet and People , citing his death certificate, reported Tuesday that the "Office Space" actor experienced a stroke and had oropharyngeal cancer. He had been in a rehabilitation center at the time of his death in mid-October, according to People. Oropharyngeal cancer , which can be asymptomatic, impacts the middle portion of your throat, including the base of your tongue and the tonsils. While there are multiple types of oropharyngeal cancers, Johns Hopkins Medicine says the majority are squamous cell carcinomas, which are further divided into HPV-related and HPV-unrelated. The former is caused by HPV, while the latter is commonly caused by tobacco or alcohol. Details about Riehle's condition were not released. items.x: BAY COUNTY, Fla. (WMBB) Last week, Bay County Sheriff's Office released security footage of am armed robbery at a Callaway gas station. Deputies asked the public's assistance in identifying the masked suspect in the footage. Tuesday, deputies announced they made two arrests in connection with the robbery. After reviewing the footage, deputies identified Robert Bowen as the possible suspect. On Oct. 22, deputies conducted a search warrant at Bowen's residence. items.t: Recalled butter sold in 10 states receives risk warning: FDA
items.x: NEW JERSEY ( WPIX ) A popular plant-based butter has been recalled due to yeast, mold and E. coli, and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has now assigned it a risk level . The recall, which was initiated by Prosperity Organic Foods, Inc., headquartered in Boise, Idaho, involves 1,304 cases of Miyoko's Creamery European Style Salted Plant Milk Butter. The FDA assigned the recall as a Class II risk level on Friday, meaning a product may cause “temporary or medically reversible adverse health consequences.” The recall was initially announced Sept. 11. The affected butter, which is perishable and stored refrigerated or frozen, comes in six-packs of 8-ounce units, which can be identified with the following information: UPC 857554005773 Lot number and best-by on SBS carton: 07871, Nov. 5, 2026 Lot number and best-by date on the corrugated case for shipment: 1007871, Nov. 5, 2026 The affected products were also sold in Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Iowa, Illinois, Indiana, Maryland, New Jersey, New Hampshire and Wisconsin.

items.t: Panama City Symphony to host Renaissance to Rock-N-Roll Halloween event
items.x: PANAMA CITY, Fla. ( WMBB ) The Panama City Symphony is excited to announce its annual Renaissance to Rock-N-Roll event, celebrating Halloween with a unique blend of music. This spooky event will take place from 6 p.m. to 9 p.m. on Friday, October 30, at the Captain Anderson’s Event Center in Panama City Beach. This year, the approach is distinctive: a combination of classical music from the Renaissance era and rock-n-roll. Principal Bassist David Goldflies has been tasked with creating the arrangements for the rock band participating in the show, the Will Thompson Band. "We're going to be doing some fun songs like "Ghostbusters", "Thriller", "I Put a Spell on You", and what turned out to be my favorite was "Don't Fear the Reaper", which are all sort of Halloween-themed, but they're just fun songs," said Principal Bassist David Goldflies. In the classical section, there will be pieces by Bach, Mozart, and selections from Phantom of the Opera, along with other virtuosic classical compositions. Costumes are optional but encouraged. For more information and tickets, click here .

items.x: ( The Hill ) The Trump administration's bid to separate 20,000 mail ballots in California that it says are likely noncitizens met another defeat on Wednesday as a trial judge refused to intervene. U.S. District Judge David Carter ruled California can continue to accept the questioned ballots like any other. “This request violates longstanding constitutional principles mandating that states have control over their elections,” Carter wrote. “If Plaintiff’s last-minute request for relief were granted, either party could create chaos for their own political purposes to disrupt the election process,” he continued. “Over 20,000 registered Californians would potentially lose the right that generations of Americans have fought to preserve.” California has raised eyebrows at the veracity of the administration's list and says it's not obligated to verify voters’ citizenship in response. items.t: Mild and dry weather continues into Halloween
items.x: Temperatures will continue to run above average this afternoon, with coastal highs in the mid to upper 70s and inland highs around 80. It will also be more humid than we’re used to this time of year, with dew points in the low to mid 60s near the coast. Tomorrow will feature very similar conditions to today, but we will cool down a bit closer to average for Halloween weekend. The Halloween forecast remains dry. Under partly to mostly cloudy skies, afternoon temperatures will reach the low to mid 70s, and during trick-or-treating hours, from 5 to 8 p.m., temperatures will begin falling into the 60s. We have been watching the potential for some rain to return to our area during the first few days of November, but those chances have really decreased over the past 24 hours. Some light scattered showers still cannot be ruled out on Sunday or early next week, so stay tuned as we monitor our chances.

items.t: AAA advises drivers about daylight saving time
items.x: ( WAVY ) – It's only a few days until we trade one extra hour of sleep for months of darkness as we leave work to drive home. And even though we're on the easier end of the time transition (from daylight saving time to standard time), the switch still takes its toll. Nexstar's WAVY went to AAA Tidewater Virginia to see what commuters can expect. "Well, the biggest thing for drivers will be the change in daylight when we leave work or school," said Holly Dalby with AAA. "At the end of the day, gone will be the bright sunshine, and we will find ourselves either driving into the glare from the setting sun or driving home in the dark. So it's a time to be particularly careful on the roads." Days will get way shorter in November: How much daylight will we lose? While lawmakers have tried to get rid of the time switch altogether, it doesn't appear to be going anywhere anytime soon, so your circadian rhythm will have to dance to a different beat for a while. items.x: Wendy’s shares jumped more than 14% Wednesday after noted investor Nelson Peltz made an offer to buy the chain, which has been struggling with high beef prices and aging stores. Peltz’s Trian Fund Management and several partners are offering Wendy’s $7.35 per share in cash, or a premium of nearly 19% over the stock’s closing price on Tuesday, in a deal that would take the company private. The offer values Wendy's at $1.4 billion. Wendy's, which is based in Dublin, Ohio, confirmed receipt of the unsolicited proposal in a statement Wednesday and said its board has formed an independent committee to evaluate it. At the end of last year, Wendy's had 5,969 restaurants in the U.S. and 1,428 outlets in 38 countries. Wendy's, founded in 1969 by Dave Thomas and named after his daughter, is known for its square burgers and Frosty desserts. The fast-growing chain introduced the drive-thru window in 1970 and went public in 1976. In the 1980s, as it jockeyed for sales with McDonald's and Burger King, Wendy's launched salad bars and ran its iconic “Where's the beef?” ad campaign. items.x: DESOTO COUNTY, Fla. ( WFLA ) – A deputy in Florida's DeSoto County has been fired and charged with a felony after the sheriff's office IT department discovered troubling photos on an agency computer, the office said. Douglas Chirinos, 35, had been working as a detention deputy when a possible security breach was flagged on his computer. Initially, Chirinos was only suspected of downloading YouTube and streaming services onto the device, which is prohibited. But when the IT director started investigating, he found a folder containing "images of concern," Chirinos' arrest affidavit said. As officials continued reviewing the contents, they discovered Chirinos had been taking screenshots of naked or partially naked women from surveillance feeds inside the jail isolation cell. At least three different women were shown in the images, which were taken between April and October 2026. DCSO said Chirinos had only worked for the sheriff's office since 2025. The women were in varying stages of undress, some wearing nothing but underwear and some completely nude, the affidavit said. "I think that going in the direction of impeachment is not a good idea, just to be honest with you," Harris told MeidasTouch's Aaron Parnas in an interview.
