items.t: New SC law requires restaurants to disclose imported shrimp
items.x: MURRELLS INLET, S.C. (WBTW) — A new South Carolina law requiring restaurants that serve imported shrimp to disclose that information to customers took effect Wednesday. Under the law, restaurants serving imported shrimp must post notices at their main entrances and include disclosures on their menus. The legislation follows genetic testing by an independent consulting firm that found only about a quarter of Grand Strand restaurants tested were serving wild-caught American shrimp. Bryan Jones, vice president of the South Carolina Shrimpers Association, said the law is intended to give customers more information about where their seafood comes from. “October 28th represents a culmination of all the work to bring this law into place, which is providing consumers with the ability to know where their shrimp is coming from,” Jones said. Jones said the legislation also addresses concerns about restaurants allegedly passing off imported, farm-raised shrimp as locally caught seafood. items.t: Myrtle Beach woman accused of shooting through bedroom door during argument with husband
items.x: MYRTLE BEACH, S.C. (WBTW) A 66-year-old woman is facing charges after allegedly firing a gun through a bedroom door during an argument with her husband at their Myrtle Beach home last week, according to police records. Pamela Garland Shanley was arrested Oct. 21 and charged with domestic violence of a high and aggravated nature and using a firearm while under the influence of alcohol or drugs, according to a Myrtle Beach Police Department arrest report. Officers responded to a reported shooting in the 600 block of Jennings Road around 8:40 p.m. on Oct. 21. According to an incident report, Shanley’s husband told police the couple had been arguing after she returned home around 8:30 p.m. He said Shanley was upset because he had left a water hose running in the front yard after watering a lemon tree. The man told police Shanley began questioning him about their relationship and where it was going. He said he did not know, then went into his bedroom and locked the door to prevent the argument from escalating. According to the report, Shanley banged on the bedroom door twice before allegedly firing a .380-caliber Smith & Wesson handgun through the closed door in her husband’s direction.

items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war , creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle . He was back in the national limelight presiding over the proceedings for Maduro , who was captured and brought to the U.S. earlier this year over accusations of narco-terrorism. Maduro and his wife were in the judge's courtroom less than two weeks ago to plead not guilty to a new set of criminal charges. Before the Maduro operation, Hellerstein had long clashed with President Donald Trump in court. The judge at one point agreed that Trump’s fixer-turned-foe, Michael Cohen, could be released from prison to home confinement. Cohen has cast his prosecution as retribution by Trump. items.t: $39K Home Depot Boom Lift sold on Facebook Marketplace in Tennessee, police say
items.x: NASHVILLE, Tenn. ( WKRN ) — A 23-year-old woman is set to appear in Nashville court after allegedly helping a man flip a $39,000 piece of Home Depot equipment on Facebook Marketplace. Arrest documents show Rebecca Walpole and a male suspect entered the Madison, Tennessee, Home Depot on May 26 and rented a boom lift, which is commonly known as a cherry picker or basket crane. The equipment was towed using a silver Dodge Ram. According to court documents, the property was never returned. The male suspect was arrested in Michigan on Sept. 23, according to arrest documents. Investigators said he admitted to selling rented construction equipment to buyers on Facebook Marketplace. Walpole faces a felony theft of property charge, and she was recently booked in Davidson County. Her bond was set at $10,000.

The S&P 500 rose 0.2% and pulled within 1% of its all-time high , which was set earlier this month. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 176 points, or 0.3%, as of 11:45 a.m. Eastern time, and the Nasdaq composite was virtually unchanged. items.t: Sugary foods to lose SNAP-eligibility on Nov. 1: SCDSS
items.x: SOUTH CAROLINA (WCBD) The South Carolina Department of Social Services on Wednesday announced that its new program, Healthy Food SC, will take effect on Sunday. Healthy Food SC project is a two-year initiative beginning on Nov. 1, updating the definition of Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP)-eligible foods by removing candy, energy drinks, soft drinks, and other sweetened beverages. Diet and zero-sugar soft drinks will still be SNAP-eligible after the new definitions take effect. This change will affect all South Carolina SNAP-approved retailers. items.t: Flying taxis could carry passengers by 2030
items.x: (TestMiles) A British aerospace company has demonstrated an electric flying taxi that could eventually offer a new way to escape crowded city roads. The Flying Car Is Moving Beyond Science Fiction Los Angeles has spent decades trying to solve its traffic problems. Freeways expand, transit systems improve, and technology promises more efficient journeys. Yet travelling across the city can still take a remarkable amount of time. A British aerospace company believes part of the solution might be above the roads rather than on them. Vertical Aerospace has demonstrated an electric aircraft capable of taking off vertically, transitioning into conventional forward flight, and landing without a runway. The technology was publicly displayed at the Farnborough International Airshow in Britain, marking an important development in the company's plans to introduce commercial passenger flights. items.t: Utah authorities connect 1974 cold case to serial killer Ted Bundy
items.x: SUMMIT COUNTY, Utah ( KTVX ) — Investigators in Summit County, Utah, closed the 1974 cold-case homicide of Melissa Ann Smith Tuesday, linking her murder to prominent serial killer Ted Bundy. Using DNA and other evidence, the Summit County Sheriff's Office and Summit County Attorney's Office formally closed the cold-case murder, saying that the evidence conclusively proves that Ted Bundy murdered 17-year-old Melissa Ann Smith. Bundy has long been considered a suspect in several cold cases in Utah, and Smith's murder was one of them. Hunters found her remains in Summit County on Oct. 27, 1974, 52 years ago today. "The work began with the investigators who handled the case in 1974, and it continued through the dedication and perseverance of those who carried it forward," Summit County Sheriff Kacey Bates said. In the NPR/PBS News/Marist Poll , 40 percent of people said their “personal family finances” have declined in the last 12 months, while 16 percent said the opposite. Forty-one percent said their personal family finances have “stayed about the same” within the prior year. Less than 1 percent of poll respondents were not sure about the state of their personal family finances within the last year, while three percent didn’t give an answer. items.t: Cause of death revealed for ‘Office Space’ actor Richard Riehle: Reports
items.x: (NEXSTAR) – The cause of death for longtime actor Richard Riehle has been revealed, according to reports. The 78-year-old died earlier this month in Los Angeles, friends told TMZ , which was the first to report the news. The outlet and People , citing his death certificate, reported Tuesday that the "Office Space" actor experienced a stroke and had oropharyngeal cancer. He had been in a rehabilitation center at the time of his death in mid-October, according to People. Oropharyngeal cancer , which can be asymptomatic, impacts the middle portion of your throat, including the base of your tongue and the tonsils. While there are multiple types of oropharyngeal cancers, Johns Hopkins Medicine says the majority are squamous cell carcinomas, which are further divided into HPV-related and HPV-unrelated. The former is caused by HPV, while the latter is commonly caused by tobacco or alcohol. Details about Riehle's condition were not released. items.t: Recalled butter sold in 10 states receives risk warning: FDA
items.x: NEW JERSEY ( WPIX ) A popular plant-based butter has been recalled due to yeast, mold and E. coli, and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has now assigned it a risk level . The recall, which was initiated by Prosperity Organic Foods, Inc., headquartered in Boise, Idaho, involves 1,304 cases of Miyoko's Creamery European Style Salted Plant Milk Butter. The FDA assigned the recall as a Class II risk level on Friday, meaning a product may cause “temporary or medically reversible adverse health consequences.” The recall was initially announced Sept. 11. The affected butter, which is perishable and stored refrigerated or frozen, comes in six-packs of 8-ounce units, which can be identified with the following information: UPC 857554005773 Lot number and best-by on SBS carton: 07871, Nov. 5, 2026 Lot number and best-by date on the corrugated case for shipment: 1007871, Nov. 5, 2026 The affected products were also sold in Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Iowa, Illinois, Indiana, Maryland, New Jersey, New Hampshire and Wisconsin.

But what happens if you head to the polls and you're told you aren't registered to vote? Whether you vote early or on Election Day, here's what to do if you're told you aren't eligible to vote. Check before you go Check your registration status online before you go to vote and make sure you have the correct address for your polling place. Update your registration If you have recently moved, your registration may still reflect your old address. Ask a poll worker if you can update your registration on site and vote, or if you'll need to go to your old polling place to cast a ballot. Same-day registration Election laws vary by state, but 25 states and the District of Columbia offer some form of same-day registration . Ask a poll worker how to register. You may be able to do so at the polling place or you may need to go to a specific location if you need to register. items.t: Video: Kayaker survives close encounter with great white shark
items.x: ( KRON ) – A fisherman captured video of a close encounter with a great white shark while fishing in a kayak off the coast of Half Moon Bay, California, on a Sunday. David Slavich was uninjured during the encounter as the shark swam past his kayak without attacking. Slavich was fishing when he found himself close to the predator. Prior to the sighting, a paddleboarder in the area had warned Slavich about a great white shark nearby. Slavich, who was not having much luck catching fish at the time, typically keeps his phone accessible to film his daily catch. But this time, it allowed him to record his frightening shark encounter. David Slavich had a close encounter with a great white off the California coast this weekend. (David Slavich) He recalled hearing a sound in the water before spotting the shark nearby. “I hear this woosh, and I look over my shoulder, and I see this massive, massive silhouette and the fin, the distinctive fin," Slavich said. "This is not a killer whale. This is not a dolphin. This is a great white." Before the sighting, Slavich doubted he would spot the predator despite the prior warning. items.t: Flock camera ordinance proposed in Spartanburg County: What to know
items.x: SPARTANBURG COUNTY, S.C. ( WSPA ) The use of Flock and other Automatic License Plate Readers (ALPR) by law enforcement agencies has undergone scrutiny nationwide as the number of police officers abusing the system continues to grow. As a result, some communities have voiced concerns for strict consequences for officers who misuse their access to Flock cameras or to take the cameras down altogether. With their limited power, Spartanburg County Council proposed an ordinance that controls who can access the cameras, the information stored in their systems, and the punishments for violating the rules. Cole Alverson, the County Administrator, said "The use of these systems, like the Flock system, is for bonified law enforcement purposes only." If a law enforcement officer is found guilty of misusing Flock, or an ALPR, there is a $500 fine for each individual violation. Sheriff Bill Rhyne added his own consequence on top of that: "Any misuse in any way, shape, or form, you will be terminated." items.t: Horry County firefighter wins world championship in Las Vegas
items.x: HORRY COUNTY, S.C. (WBTW) A Horry County Fire Rescue captain is celebrating a world championship victory after winning a competitive firefighting event in Las Vegas over the weekend. Capt. David Howell and his teammate, Mike Medeiros, won the Over 50 Tandem division at the Firefighter Challenge World Championships on Saturday, Oct. 24, according to HCFR. The pair finished the race in 1 minute, 34.59 seconds, defeating a team from Berlin and setting a South Carolina state record. "The firefighter challenge is called the toughest two minutes in sports," Howell said. "It's very unique because you have to complete an obstacle course, wearing full turnout gear and breathing on your SCBA, so it's exclusive only for firefighters." The competition tests skills firefighters use on the job, including carrying hoses up stairs, hoisting equipment, forcing entry, advancing hoses, and rescuing victims. Competitors complete the course while wearing full firefighting gear, including air packs. Howell joined HCFR in 2002, the same year he began competing in firefighter challenges. items.t: DOJ charges Comey for third time
items.x: Former FBI Director James Comey has been charged again by the Justice Department (DOJ) for allegedly disclosing sensitive national defense information in 2016, according to newly unsealed court documents . Comey was charged with two counts of transmitting information and conspiring to transmit information related to national defense matters on Oct. 5, but a federal judge granted his request to unseal the complaint Monday. The DOJ alleges that Comey “through one and more co-conspirators” directed an individual to share classified information with a reporter from a national news organization in October 2016, according to the charging document. The publication is identified in other court documents as The New York Times. Swift added another honor to her trophy wall with her second hall of fame induction this year and was celebrated at the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame Gala on Monday in a crowded ballroom full of artists, writers and country music elite. “I knew from the time I wrote my first song that even if it couldn’t be my career, it would be my passion," Swift said. She described soaking up the lessons from other writers like a sponge, learning how to push through writer's block and write about the human condition, even when her writing partner was hungover or going through a divorce. items.t: Florida man pleads guilty to shooting horse over money
items.x: TAMPA, Fla. ( WFLA ) — A Florida man is heading to prison after he shot a horse when he didn't get the money he demanded for work, the Hillsborough County State Attorney's Office announced. Joel Gutierrez was sentenced to one year in prison after pleading guilty to four felonies in connection with the death of a horse named Ms. Mo. Credit: Hillsborough SAO According to the attorney's office, in Sept. 2024, Gutierrez showed up at a home on North Turkey Creek Road in Lakeland and demanded payment for work he had allegedly done. Gutierrez shot Ms. Mo, and the bullet fractured her leg, leaving her with injuries so severe that she had to be euthanized, the attorney's office said. Gutierrez pleaded guilty to counts of aggravated animal cruelty to animals with a weapon, discharging a firearm from a vehicle, grand theft of an animal, and breaking or injuring fences containing animals "Animals cannot speak for themselves, but that doesn't mean they don't deserve justice. items.t: GM settles $220M lawsuit for allegedly selling private drivers’ data, Connecticut Attorney General says
items.x: HARTFORD, Conn. (WTNH) — Attorney General William Tong announced Thursday that General Motors will pay $220 million to settle allegations that it illegally sold consumers' private driver behavior data and location information to third parties. Tong said that General Motors sold the information to data brokers, who then sold the data to insurance companies. For many consumers, this data was used by insurance companies in part to set insurance rates, Tong said. According to Tong, Connecticut will receive more than $6 million through the settlement, which requires GM to obtain consent from consumers before collecting or disclosing consumer driving and location data. items.t: Florida man hit by truck while filming ‘haircut’ challenge on busy road
items.x: OCALA, Fla. (WFLA) — Three young men were arrested in Florida — and one was seriously injured — after attempting a "dangerous online challenge" in the middle of a busy road, the Ocala Police Department said. The challenge, according to police, involved one of the men giving another a haircut "in the center of the road" on State Route 200 in Ocala. The third suspect was filming the stunt, authorities say. Bridgeport man killed in Orlando DUI crash In a Facebook post, the Ocala Police Department explained that the young men — ages 20, 19 and 18 — had removed a chair from a nearby restaurant to use during the challenge. But while the 18-year-old was seated and getting his hair cut, a traffic accident nearby sent a Chevrolet 3500 in their direction. The two other suspects were able to move out of the way, but the 18-year-old "was seated with his back to the oncoming truck" and was hit by the vehicle. Ocala police indicated that the 18-year-old was hospitalized after the incident, but did not disclose the extent of his injuries. All three men were later arrested. They face charges of "unlawful assembly and dangerous use of public rights-of-way under city ordinance," according to police.

items.t: Democrats see battleground map expand to South Carolina, Florida, Mississippi
items.x: Democrats are giddy about the possibility of a bigger blue wave than expected in the battle for the Senate as polls show that South Carolina , Florida and Mississippi — three seats that were long seen as safe Republican holds — are now competitive races. Democrats view the Republican candidates running in those states as mediocre political talents who must fight historic headwinds caused by President Trump’s unpopularity, voter anger over inflation and the war in Iran, and burgeoning Democratic voter enthusiasm. The Senate battleground map has steadily expanded throughout the 2026 midterm election cycle as political handicappers have shifted seats that were thought to be in solidly Republican territory — such as Alaska, Iowa, Kansas and Texas — to the “toss-up" category. But now Republicans have to worry about losing Senate seats in states that were unthinkable as realistic Democratic pickup opportunities at the start of the election cycle, most notably South Carolina, which last elected a Democrat, Fritz Hollings, to the Senate in 1998. items.x: ROCKY HILL, Conn. (WTNH) — Rocky Hill fire officials said a cleaning solution was responsible for a shelter-in-place issued at Concierge Apartments on Wednesday. Fire crews were dispatched to the apartments at 100 Cold Spring Road around 4:15 p.m. for a report of a natural gas odor. New agreement offers more protections for tenants at Rocky Hill apartment complex On scene, they determined the odor was from a highly concentrated vinegar-based cleaning solution being used inside the complex. The smell prompted fire officials to order a shelter-in-place for residents, as a precaution. The Connecticut Department of Energy and Environmental Protection (DEEP) was also requested to assist. Firefighters ventilated the affected floors and stairwells and residents were able to return to their homes once they were determined to be clear of any chemical odors, fire officials said. items.t: AAA advises drivers about daylight saving time
items.x: ( WAVY ) – It's only a few days until we trade one extra hour of sleep for months of darkness as we leave work to drive home. And even though we're on the easier end of the time transition (from daylight saving time to standard time), the switch still takes its toll. Nexstar's WAVY went to AAA Tidewater Virginia to see what commuters can expect. "Well, the biggest thing for drivers will be the change in daylight when we leave work or school," said Holly Dalby with AAA. "At the end of the day, gone will be the bright sunshine, and we will find ourselves either driving into the glare from the setting sun or driving home in the dark. So it's a time to be particularly careful on the roads." While lawmakers have tried to get rid of the time switch altogether, it doesn't appear to be going anywhere anytime soon, so your circadian rhythm will have to dance to a different beat for a while. "It just messing with our sleep schedule can really add to our fatigue very quickly. And when we're fatigued, we can make mistakes," Dalby said. Democrats have tried to tie those issues to President Trump , pointing to the war in Iran and his embrace of AI . Some Republicans have called for an end to the Iran war, while others have blamed high prices on Ukraine's war with Russia and Democrats' energy policies. To win the Senate, Democrats will have to break through on Republican turf . Of the Cook Political Report's seven toss-ups , five are in states Trump won by double digits in 2024. Kaden Matsuda, 19, from Ridgway, Colorado, and Jackson Donlon, 20, from New York, left Colorado Mountain College Leadville’s campus on Friday and didn’t return. They told family and friends they planned to go up Ice Mountain, which requires technical climbing, according to the county sheriff’s office. On Wednesday night, the sheriff's office confirmed that the students were found dead around 3:30 p.m. in a basin of the West Apostle Mountain. Authorities do not believe foul play was involved. The investigation is now being handled by the Chaffee County Coroner’s Office. “Our heart aches for Kaden and Jackson’s family and friends. We are very proud of our team’s efforts to find them before this weekend’s coming storm," Sheriff Andy Rohrich wrote on Facebook. items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: ( The Hill ) Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. Gasoline and energy costs have risen in six of nine months this year, as the Iran war sparked oil price shocks via the Islamic Republic's restrictions on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Persistent inflation , which has remained above the Fed's 2 percent target for five-and-a-half years, spurred central bank officials to hike interest rates by a quarter point in mid-September. items.t: Harris advises Democrats against attempting to impeach Trump
items.x: ( The Hill ) Former Vice President Kamala Harris on Tuesday urged Democrats against making a third attempt to impeach President Trump if they win back the House after next week's midterm elections. "I think that going in the direction of impeachment is not a good idea, just to be honest with you," Harris told MeidasTouch's Aaron Parnas in an interview. "Just because we have limited resources and I think the energy and the resources need to put into accountability, need to be put into investigations." "And that's where the time should be spent," she added. "Remember, I was in the Senate for the last go-around, and the votes aren't there. "So, that's how I feel. But also, I think after the election, we all have to just also agree that our attitude has to be to get stuff done." Harris said Democrats should be "uncompromising" and "not sit around, you know, being genteel about the relationships," but maintain accountability when it comes to cuts to healthcare and oversight on the Iran war. Arrest documents show Rebecca Walpole and a male suspect entered the Madison, Tennessee, Home Depot on May 26 and rented a boom lift, which is commonly known as a cherry picker or basket crane. The equipment was towed using a silver Dodge Ram. According to court documents, the property was never returned. Nashville Super 8 sued over almost $150K in unpaid repair bills The male suspect was arrested in Michigan on Sept. 23, according to arrest documents. Investigators said he admitted to selling rented construction equipment to buyers on Facebook Marketplace. Walpole faces a felony theft of property charge, and she was recently booked in Davidson County. Her bond was set at $10,000.

items.t: CBP evaluates military ‘heat ray’ for potential use at US-Mexico border
items.x: EL PASO, Texas (Border Report) — U.S. Customs and Border Protection is evaluating a military weapon that creates an intense heating sensation on the skin for potential use along the U.S.-Mexico border, but the agency has not disclosed a testing location or confirmed its deployment in the El Paso region. The weapon, called the Active Denial System and commonly known as a “heat ray,” is designed to repel people by directing an invisible beam of electromagnetic energy at them. The Pentagon authorized a seven-month loan of the system to the Department of Homeland Security beginning in September, according to a memorandum first reported by CNN. The arrangement lets DHS test the equipment and develop procedures for potential border operations. In a statement to Border Report, a CBP spokesperson said: “CBP is continually evaluating new technology, especially technology that can save lives while simultaneously enhancing national security effectiveness.” The statement provided to Border Report did not identify where testing would occur, what circumstances would justify using the weapon, or what safeguards would govern its operation. items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war , creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle . items.t: Judge overseeing Maduro trial dies
items.x: ( The Hill ) Alvin Hellerstein, a longtime federal judge who was set to oversee the criminal trial of deposed Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro, has passed away, according to a court official. He was 92. Nominated by then-President Bill Clinton in 1998, Hellerstein oversaw many high-profile disputes during his nearly three decades on the bench in New York City. He was back in the national limelight presiding over the proceedings for Maduro , who was captured and brought to the U.S. earlier this year over accusations of narco-terrorism. Maduro and his wife were in the judge's courtroom less than two weeks ago to plead not guilty to a new set of criminal charges. Before the Maduro operation, Hellerstein had long clashed with President Donald Trump in court. The judge at one point agreed that Trump’s fixer-turned-foe, Michael Cohen, could be released from prison to home confinement. Cohen has cast his prosecution as retribution by Trump. Separately, Hellerstein repeatedly denied Trump's efforts to move his hush money criminal prosecution into federal court, forcing the president to try his luck in New York's state system. items.t: Cornell preps for no-confidence vote against president after Jane Doe’s allegations: What to know
items.x: ( The Hill ) The Cornell University Faculty Senate is set to debate a no-confidence vote on Wednesday against President Michael I. Kotlikoff after allegations of a 2024 gang rape at a campus fraternity that resulted in no criminal charges caused uproar around the country. The more than 75 members of the body will have their second meeting debating the resolution and the timing of a vote on it. A motion could be introduced to delay the no-confidence vote and set another meeting. But if that motion is not introduced or fails, members of the Faculty Senate will begin the no-confidence vote after Wednesday's meeting is over, and they typically have a week to cast their choice online. While a no-confidence vote has no authority to remove an official, its passing would show deep dissatisfaction from faculty with how Cornell leadership has handled accusations from Jane Doe that seven members of the Chi Phi fraternity raped her . What does the no-confidence vote entail? The resolution, led by Paul Ortiz, a professor of labor history, states the faculty has no confidence in Cornell's leadership to "address the ongoing crisis of sexual assault" at the school. "The boards help me talk to my friends." Those simple words mean so much for 9-year-old Colton McClain. Because for him, communication hasn't always come easy. Wednesday’s Warrior: Connecticut mom turns special moment into children’s book to help other military families "There was a point he was nonspeaking and didn't have the ability to verbally communicate," his mom, Ashley McClain, said. She is on a mission to make sure every child has the opportunity to be heard. "Because every child deserves a voice; every individual deserves a voice," she said. Advocacy, awareness, education and inclusion are the pillars of Beyond the Horizon, Inc., a nonprofit Ashley started with her family three years ago. One way she's putting that mission into action is helping children communicate one playground at a time. "So, these boards have simple images and simple language where the children can just come right up to them and point to various things," she said. items.t: 68 dead in high-speed train collision, Spain’s 2nd deadly rail crash this year
items.x: URDA, Spain (AP) — A high-speed train slammed into another that had stopped on the tracks in Spain on Wednesday, killing at least 68 people and injuring dozens in the second deadly rail collision this year. The regional government of Castilla La Mancha confirmed the death toll and said another 58 people were receiving medical treatment at hospitals. Rescue workers searched the wreckage through the day for survivors and bodies. The collision came just nine months after another deadly crash involving high-speed trains operated by the same two companies in southern Spain in January. “Today all of Spain is grieving,” Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said from the crash site, where he announced that his government would declare three days of national mourning. items.t: VSP: Man dies after striking VDOT contractor vehicle on I-64
items.x: YORK COUNTY, Va. (WAVY) A 52-year-old man died after striking a VDOT contractor vehicle Wednesday evening in York County, according to Virginia State Police. State police responded to I-64 East at mile marker 237 for a fatal two-vehicle crash at approximately 6:40 p.m. A preliminary investigation determined a VDOT contractor vehicle provided a safety net for a construction crew setting out warning signs for an overnight lane closure when it was crashed into by a 2025 Ford Mustang. The Mustang operator, 52-year-old Michael Ohman, of Newport News, suffered serious injuries and was taken to the hospital for treatment. He later died at the hospital. State police confirmed no VDOT contractors were harmed in the crash. The incident remains under investigation.

items.t: Muzzleloader Deer Season Opens Oct. 31, Is Your Gun Ready?
items.x: NEW CASTLE, Va. (WFXR) Expect to hear the thunder of gunfire around Virginia soon. Deer muzzleloader season opens October 31. But, before you head into the woods, there is one very important thing to consider. "Is my gun ready?" The only way to tell is to fire it at a target to make sure the scope and gun are in synch, and that your aim is true. If not, you will need to make adjustments on the scope and possibly the gun. There are any number of things that can affect the scope. "Well, it's been been a whole year since we've done this, so bumping them in the closet or on the truck ride, you know, things happen," said expert deer hunter Randy Frango of Craig County. "It's a good practice to, you check your rifle prior to season." Having a gun dialed in can keep you from missing a deer, but it can also prevent something else, wounding a deer and not being able to track it. "You don't want to make a bad shot and wound an animal either," said Frango. "So yeah, check your rifle, whether it be a muzzleloader or rifle, rifle season is coming up, and make sure your firearm is hitting where it should." The other thing Frango emphasized is safety and especially avoiding double charging a gun.

items.t: Cruise ship passenger says warning signs were there long before Cambodia
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — Kit Cassingham and her husband, Randy, sold their home and nearly everything they owned to live aboard a cruise ship for years. Asked if they will get it back, she said, "No, no, no, no." items.t: Wendy’s gets buyout offer while struggling with beef prices and growing competition
items.x: Wendy’s shares jumped more than 14% Wednesday after noted investor Nelson Peltz made an offer to buy the chain, which has been struggling with high beef prices and aging stores. Peltz’s Trian Fund Management and several partners are offering Wendy’s $7.35 per share in cash, or a premium of nearly 19% over the stock’s closing price on Tuesday, in a deal that would take the company private. The offer values Wendy's at $1.4 billion. Wendy's, which is based in Dublin, Ohio, confirmed receipt of the unsolicited proposal in a statement Wednesday and said its board has formed an independent committee to evaluate it. At the end of last year, Wendy's had 5,969 restaurants in the U.S. and 1,428 outlets in 38 countries. Wendy's, founded in 1969 by Dave Thomas and named after his daughter, is known for its square burgers and Frosty desserts. The fast-growing chain introduced the drive-thru window in 1970 and went public in 1976. In the 1980s, as it jockeyed for sales with McDonald's and Burger King, Wendy's launched salad bars and ran its iconic “Where's the beef?” ad campaign. items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: ( The Hill ) Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. Gasoline and energy costs have risen in six of nine months this year, as the Iran war sparked oil price shocks via the Islamic Republic's restrictions on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Persistent inflation , which has remained above the Fed's 2 percent target for five-and-a-half years, spurred central bank officials to hike interest rates by a quarter point in mid-September. items.x: WASHINGTON (AP) — The Trump administration on Wednesday acted to ease access to unproven peptide drugs favored by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr . Food and Drug Administration scientific staffers had little input on the decision and opposed the changes, according to six people familiar with its development. The draft policy posted online by Kennedy’s Department of Health and Human Services covers a handful of injectable peptides promoted within the wellness industry for uses such as building muscle, healing injuries and boosting energy. items.t: North Carolina flags to fly at half-staff in honor of civil rights icon Dolores Huerta
items.x: RALEIGH, N.C. (WGHP) Governor Josh Stein ordered all U.S. and North Carolina flags at state facilities to be flown at half-staff from sunrise on Thursday until sunset Monday in honor of labor activist and civil rights icon Dolores Huerta . Huerta died on Wednesday at her home in Bakersfield, California. The 96-year old civil rights activist spent decades championing equal rights for women, immigrants and workers. She is widely remembered for cofounding the United Farm Workers of America in the mid-1960s. "Dolores Huerta made America a better place for workers and women, moving our nation forward," Stein said. "Let us honor her legacy by continuing to extend the promise of this nation to all who call it home. May her memory be a blessing."

According to the USDA, the five latest confirmed screwworm cases involved four dogs and a cat. Cochise County, Arizona, reported its first screwworm case on Wednesday, the first in that state. Texas state Rep. Mary Gonzalez, D-El Paso, issued a statement saying the screwworm was detected in a dog in the town of Socorro. She said her office has been in communication with the appropriate state agencies and will continue to monitor the situation. She urged the public to check on their pets and monitor them closely. "It is important that members of our community stay vigilant and go to their veterinarians if they believe their animal may have been impacted," she said. The border county of Luna, New Mexico, also confirmed its first screwworm case in a cow on Monday. The New World screwworm is a parasitic fly that lays eggs in open wounds. items.t: DOJ’s California ballot fight rejected by another judge
items.x: ( The Hill ) The Trump administration's bid to separate 20,000 mail ballots in California that it says are likely noncitizens met another defeat on Wednesday as a trial judge refused to intervene. U.S. District Judge David Carter ruled California can continue to accept the questioned ballots like any other. “This request violates longstanding constitutional principles mandating that states have control over their elections,” Carter wrote. “If Plaintiff’s last-minute request for relief were granted, either party could create chaos for their own political purposes to disrupt the election process,” he continued. “Over 20,000 registered Californians would potentially lose the right that generations of Americans have fought to preserve.” California has raised eyebrows at the veracity of the administration's list and says it's not obligated to verify voters’ citizenship in response. The state has conceded it's not feasible to segregate a ballot once it's processed. It would be counted even if later found to be fraudulent. items.t: NNPD holds annual Domestic Violence Awareness Walk
items.x: NEWPORT NEWS, Va. (WAVY) — The Newport News Police Department held its annual Domestic Violence Awareness Walk in City Center Wednesday, as step-by-step, dozens of advocates on the Peninsula came together, sporting purple and holding candles, in the hope of ending domestic violence. "One of the first things that a lot of the victims go through is isolation and feeling like you're alone," said Noed, a domestic violence survivor. "But knowing that there are several community partners, that there are a lot of resources out here with familiar faces, it just feels supported." Noed is one of many survivors who joined in on the walk, and shared her own story. "There is hope on the other side. There's freedom. There's healing and restoration. And speak up. You may not have all the answers, and you won't have all the answers, but you do have community partners out here who we're willing to help out," Noed said. This is the fifth year in a row NNPD has held the walk with the goal of bringing more awareness to the issue. items.t: Religious, community leaders urge voters to help end hunger in Rio Grande Valley
items.x: McALLEN, Texas (Border Report) The Humanitarian Respite Center in McAllen used to help thousands of migrants who crossed the border during the Biden administration. But since Trump took over it has largely been empty. But on Wednesday dozens of faith-based and community leaders were at the center to speak out against hunger and food insecurities that are plaguing this South Texas border region. And to urge voters to elect leaders who will help. “In this election year Bread for the World is urging people of faith to vote to end hunger," Felipe Salinas of the Christian-based nonprofit group Bread for the World told the group. He says there are too many people in the region who cannot afford food for their families and he believes more public assistance is needed by the government. “It is very much a policy choice because for every meal a food bank or food pantry provides, the federally-funded Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, or SNAP, provides 9. items.t: Harris advises Democrats against attempting to impeach Trump
items.x: ( The Hill ) Former Vice President Kamala Harris on Tuesday urged Democrats against making a third attempt to impeach President Trump if they win back the House after next week's midterm elections. "I think that going in the direction of impeachment is not a good idea, just to be honest with you," Harris told MeidasTouch's Aaron Parnas in an interview. "Just because we have limited resources and I think the energy and the resources need to put into accountability, need to be put into investigations." "And that's where the time should be spent," she added. "Remember, I was in the Senate for the last go-around, and the votes aren't there. "So, that's how I feel. But also, I think after the election, we all have to just also agree that our attitude has to be to get stuff done." Harris said Democrats should be "uncompromising" and "not sit around, you know, being genteel about the relationships," but maintain accountability when it comes to cuts to healthcare and oversight on the Iran war. items.t: Hayden Panettiere death ruled accidental by police in South Carolina
items.x: GREENVILLE, S.C. ( WSPA ) – Police in South Carolina have officially closed the investigation into the death of Hayden Panettiere, according to a Wednesday news release. Greenville Police Department officials said that Panettiere's death has been ruled accidental, based on findings in the investigation and the medical examiner's determination. On August 16, Panettiere was found unresponsive in an apartment at the Judson Mill Lofts on Easley Bridge Road. Police said that Brian Hickerson, Panettiere's on-and-off boyfriend, along with his brother, Zach Hickerson, were at the residence. EMS attempted life-saving measures before pronouncing Panettiere dead at 2:31 p.m. According to the Greenville County Coroner's Office, Panettiere had died from an accidental overdose of fentanyl, 4-ANPP, Alprazolam, Methocarbamol and Quetiapine. Panettiere had spoken openly about challenges in her personal life, including emotional scars from her childhood fame, postpartum depression after giving birth to her daughter, and struggles with alcohol addiction. items.t: Judge overseeing Maduro trial dies
items.x: ( The Hill ) Alvin Hellerstein, a longtime federal judge who was set to oversee the criminal trial of deposed Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro, has passed away, according to a court official. He was 92. Nominated by then-President Bill Clinton in 1998, Hellerstein oversaw many high-profile disputes during his nearly three decades on the bench in New York City. He was back in the national limelight presiding over the proceedings for Maduro , who was captured and brought to the U.S. earlier this year over accusations of narco-terrorism. Maduro and his wife were in the judge's courtroom less than two weeks ago to plead not guilty to a new set of criminal charges. Before the Maduro operation, Hellerstein had long clashed with President Donald Trump in court. The judge at one point agreed that Trump’s fixer-turned-foe, Michael Cohen, could be released from prison to home confinement. Cohen has cast his prosecution as retribution by Trump. Separately, Hellerstein repeatedly denied Trump's efforts to move his hush money criminal prosecution into federal court, forcing the president to try his luck in New York's state system. "We are deeply saddened to announce that our beloved mother, Dolores Huerta, has passed away today at the age of 96," her family said in a statement posted on social media. "As you can imagine, this is an incredibly difficult time for us, and we ask for privacy as we grieve this incredible loss to our family," the statement continued. "We know that many of you around the world share in our mourning, and we will be following up on plans to recognize and celebrate her incredible life and legacy." items.t: US stocks hold steady as the countdown ticks to a Federal Reserve decision on interest rates
items.x: NEW YORK (AP) — U.S. stocks are drifting Wednesday as the countdown ticks toward this afternoon’s announcement from the Federal Reserve on what it will do with interest rates . The S&P 500 rose 0.2% and pulled within 1% of its all-time high , which was set earlier this month. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 176 points, or 0.3%, as of 11:45 a.m. Eastern time, and the Nasdaq composite was virtually unchanged. The day’s highlight will likely be what the Federal Reserve says, if anything, about where interest rates are heading. The Fed raised its main interest rate last month for the first time in three years in hopes of slowing the high inflation that’s squeezing the economy and discouraging Americans . The widespread expectation on Wall Street is that the Fed will leave the federal funds rate alone at this meeting, and the question is whether it will give hints about what may happen at later meetings. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh, though, has been adamant since taking over the Fed about wanting it to give fewer indications about its future moves. items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war , creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle . items.t: $39K Home Depot Boom Lift sold on Facebook Marketplace in Tennessee, police say
items.x: NASHVILLE, Tenn. ( WKRN ) — A 23-year-old woman is set to appear in Nashville court after allegedly helping a man flip a $39,000 piece of Home Depot equipment on Facebook Marketplace. Arrest documents show Rebecca Walpole and a male suspect entered the Madison, Tennessee, Home Depot on May 26 and rented a boom lift, which is commonly known as a cherry picker or basket crane. The equipment was towed using a silver Dodge Ram. According to court documents, the property was never returned. Nashville Super 8 sued over almost $150K in unpaid repair bills The male suspect was arrested in Michigan on Sept. 23, according to arrest documents. Investigators said he admitted to selling rented construction equipment to buyers on Facebook Marketplace. Walpole faces a felony theft of property charge, and she was recently booked in Davidson County. Her bond was set at $10,000.

The weapon, called the Active Denial System and commonly known as a “heat ray,” is designed to repel people by directing an invisible beam of electromagnetic energy at them. The Pentagon authorized a seven-month loan of the system to the Department of Homeland Security beginning in September, according to a memorandum first reported by CNN. The arrangement lets DHS test the equipment and develop procedures for potential border operations. In a statement to Border Report, a CBP spokesperson said: “CBP is continually evaluating new technology, especially technology that can save lives while simultaneously enhancing national security effectiveness.” The statement provided to Border Report did not identify where testing would occur, what circumstances would justify using the weapon, or what safeguards would govern its operation. items.x: ( The Hill ) The Cornell University Faculty Senate is set to debate a no-confidence vote on Wednesday against President Michael I. Kotlikoff after allegations of a 2024 gang rape at a campus fraternity that resulted in no criminal charges caused uproar around the country. The more than 75 members of the body will have their second meeting debating the resolution and the timing of a vote on it. A motion could be introduced to delay the no-confidence vote and set another meeting. But if that motion is not introduced or fails, members of the Faculty Senate will begin the no-confidence vote after Wednesday's meeting is over, and they typically have a week to cast their choice online. While a no-confidence vote has no authority to remove an official, its passing would show deep dissatisfaction from faculty with how Cornell leadership has handled accusations from Jane Doe that seven members of the Chi Phi fraternity raped her . What does the no-confidence vote entail? The resolution, led by Paul Ortiz, a professor of labor history, states the faculty has no confidence in Cornell's leadership to "address the ongoing crisis of sexual assault" at the school. items.t: Sabato’s Crystal Ball moves 16 House races toward Democrats
items.x: ( The Hill ) – Nonpartisan election forecaster Sabato’s Crystal Ball is shifting more than a dozen House races toward Democrats in the final week of the campaign , another sign of a worsening political environment for Republicans. Crystal Ball, a division of the University of Virginia’s Center for Politics, has moved dozens of races toward Democrats in recent weeks, including nearly 50 races in the month of October alone. The race changes include moving a few deep-red seats into the “toss up” column. Open congressional districts in Kentucky and Montana, as well as seats with GOP incumbents in Missouri, Virginia, Colorado and Pennsylvania moved into coin flip territory. Many of the seats Crystal Ball rates as a toss-up were places Trump carried by double digits in 2024. Monica de la Cruz (R) is facing a tough challenge from Tejano music star Bobby Pulido (D). items.t: No clear winner yet in Israel’s national elections: What happens now?
items.x: JERUSALEM (AP) — No clear winner has emerged in Israel’s national elections as vote-counting continues, and weeks of negotiations may lie ahead as Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his main rival, Gadi Eisenkot , will scramble to build a governing coalition. The election was widely seen as a referendum on Netanyahu , the country’s longest-serving prime minister, who gave a defiant speech to his supporters just after 3 a.m. on Wednesday in Jerusalem despite the unclear results. With around 70% of the votes counted on Wednesday afternoon, his party, Likud, appears to have gotten the most votes, capturing around 20% of the popular vote. This was a dip from the previous election in 2022, when Likud won 23.4% of the popular vote. items.x: ( NewsNation ) — One benefit reported by people taking GLP-1 medications is a reduction in alcohol cravings and consumption, but the drugs' growing popularity has created new challenges for beer companies. According to Reuters , Heineken presented a document to U.K. hospitality customers earlier this month advising that the medications could potentially change drinking habits among users. The drugs may result in "fullness and fewer serves" in pubs and bars. “We see some changes in consumption behaviour among (GLP-1) users and will continue to monitor how these behaviours evolve in 2027," a Heineken spokesperson told the publication. The report noted that the company’s research found consumers increasingly choosing smaller servings, lower-alcohol beverages and premium products and that these shifts also align with broader trends focused on health, wellness and moderation. One option Heineken advised customers to pursue is half-pints and low- and no-alcohol options, according to the publication. items.x: NORFOLK, Va. (WAVY) — For the past five years, the E. Palmer Supermarket has been serving as the go-to grocery store for Norfolk's Berkley community, with Esron Palmer and his father serving a community in need. "The community used to be a food desert," Palmer said. "I mean, I didn't have the access to fresh fruits, vegetables and other things like that just to stay alive. So a lot of the big chains didn't want to come into this neighborhood. So, the city of Norfolk put it out there that this is sorely needed in this area." Palmers estimates that about 35% of his customers are paying for groceries by using the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, or SNAP — a program that provides food benefits to low-income families to supplement their grocery budgets so they can afford the nutritious food essentials FOR health and well-being. "As far as trying to push the healthier options, they have different programs like we have in our store, where if you are using the EBT, you can get 50% off your fruits or vegetables," Palmer said. items.t: Five pets died, two people displaced by Norfolk house fire
items.x: NORFOLK, Va. (WAVY) — Three dogs and two cats died, and two adults have been displaced, as a result of a house fire Wednesday on Buckingham Street, just off of Chesapeake Boulevard. Norfolk Fire-Rescue responded to a reported structure fire at 8:30 a.m. and found heavy smoke and flames coming from a house. Firefighters initiated a fire attack, and a search confirmed that all occupants were outside the home. However, several pets were still inside. Photos courtesy of Norfolk Fire-Rescue The fire was brought under control at 9:12 a.m. Three dogs and two cats died as a result of the fire, while two adults were displaced and are requesting assistance from the American Red Cross, Norfolk Fire-Rescue said. The cause of the fire is still under investigation.

items.x: VIRGINIA BEACH, Va. (WAVY) A dumpster containing scrap metal caught on fire at the Virginia Beach City Landfill Tuesday morning. The Virginia Beach Fire Department responded to the landfill just after 8 a.m. and found a dumpster, attached to a tractor, actively on fire. The landfill is located at 1989 Jake Sears Road. Firefighters got the fire under control at 8:34 a.m. but didn't mark it officially out until 8:56 a.m. Crews removed the contents of the dumpster to control any hot spots. There were no injuries reported. VBFD provided these images from the scene. If you need to dispose of them, the following items are accepted at the City Landfill and Resource Recovery Center: automotive and all rechargeable batteries such as lithium-ion (Li-On), nickel-cadmium batteries (Ni-Cd or NiCad), or nickel-metal hydride (NiMH or Ni-MH). items.t: VBFD: 40-foot recreational boat runs aground near North Landing Bridge
items.x: VIRGINIA BEACH, Va. (WAVY) Two people required assistance after a recreational boat ran aground on a stump Tuesday afternoon near the North Landing Bridge, according to the Virginia Beach Fire Department. Units were dispatched to a report of a boat in distress near the North Landing Bridge at approximately 3:15 p.m. Upon arrival, crews located a 40-foot recreational boat that had run aground on a stump and was listing to the starboard side. Authorities said two people aboard reported they were not in distress but needed assistance getting off the boat. They safely took both individuals to shore. Neither reported needing medical assistance. Officials said the U.S. Coast Guard was notified, and the scene was turned over to Virginia Conservation Police after the incident was mitigated.

items.t: CPD: Man accused of strangulation of romantic partner at Chesapeake residence
items.x: CHESAPEAKE, Va. (WAVY) — Chesapeake resident Blair Hess, who has been the subject of ongoing complaints from his Tyre Neck Road neighbors about the condition of his yard, now faces domestic assault and strangulation charges following a dispute with his romantic partner at their shared residence, he told officers who responded to his residence Tuesday afternoon, according to court documents. Officers responded to a report of a domestic assault in progress, and when they got to the home, they spoke with a victim who reported that she had been assaulted and strangled by a suspect. items.t: Izzo talks after exhibition losses, previews season opener
items.x: LANSING, Mich. (WLNS) — The Michigan State men's basketball team officially begins the season on Monday, Nov. 2, against Quinnipiac. Tom Izzo spoke with the media on Thursday about the season opener and the two exhibition losses the Spartans suffered last week. "I've learned a lot during these past two exhibition games, some of it good and some of it not so good," said Izzo. MSU fell to UConn 78-70 and then lost on the road to Marquette 86-79 in the exhibition slate. Freshman Jasiah Jervis had a team-high 19 points in the loss to Marquette. "We've got a lot of great pieces and now it's putting the puzzle together. The puzzle is going to take a little time, as it always does," said Izzo. Izzo said he was most disappointed in the team's ability to push the ball and finish on the fast break, something past MSU units have been very effective at. "Our stamp on this basketball world is our fast break; we defend, we rebound, we run. It's been the same mantra for all my years," said Izzo. "Neither game did we do a very good job at that," he added. Izzo is entering his 32 nd season leading the program, and his team is ranked No. 6 in the preseason AP Top 25 poll.

items.t: Michigan awards MSU $400K to study PFAS in agriculture
items.x: LANSING, Mich. (WLNS) — The Michigan Department of Agriculture and Rural Development awarded a team of researchers and outreach specialists from Michigan State University and Purdue University $400,000 to study the impacts of PFAS. PFAS, also known as forever chemicals, are a large group of human-made, widely used, long-lasting chemicals that break down very slowly and can lead to harmful health effects. The teams will use the funds to study how PFAS impacts agricultural systems and develop mitigation strategies. Subhasis Giri, an assistant professor in the MSU Department of Biosystems and Agricultural Engineering, is leading the project, which began in September. "PFAS is a global health threat that requires additional research, particularly within agriculture as it relates to movement through fields and ultimately crop uptake. Our goal is to help affected farmers navigate an increasingly difficult situation while protecting public health and reducing environmental impact," said Giri in a news release.

The offer values Wendy's at $1.4 billion. Wendy's, which is based in Dublin, Ohio, confirmed receipt of the unsolicited proposal in a statement Wednesday and said its board has formed an independent committee to evaluate it. items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: ( The Hill ) Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. Gasoline and energy costs have risen in six of nine months this year, as the Iran war sparked oil price shocks via the Islamic Republic's restrictions on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Persistent inflation , which has remained above the Fed's 2 percent target for five-and-a-half years, spurred central bank officials to hike interest rates by a quarter point in mid-September. items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war , creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle . items.t: Box truck kills pedestrian on I-96 in Livingston County
items.x: LANSING, Mich. (WLNS) — A 28-year-old man from Fenton was killed after being hit by a box truck in Livingston County Wednesday morning. Michigan State Police Brighton Post said in a release that they responded to a pedestrian crash on westbound I-96 near the US-23 interchange before 3:30 a.m. Investigators say the 28-year-old man hit a deer and didn't move his Ford Escape to the shoulder. Instead, he stopped in the right lane and exited his vehicle to inspect the damage. A box truck traveling in the center lane switched into the right lane before noticing the Ford Escape. The box truck hit the driver. The 28-year-old man was pronounced dead at the scene. MSP says the driver of the box truck wasn't hurt. The Michigan Department of Transportation has reopened all lanes going westbound on I-96 in Livingston County near Pleasant Valley Rd. Exit 150 after several hours.

items.t: Utah authorities connect 1974 cold case to serial killer Ted Bundy
items.x: SUMMIT COUNTY, Utah ( KTVX ) — Investigators in Summit County, Utah closed the 1974 cold case homicide of Melissa Ann Smith Tuesday, linking her murder to prominent serial killer Ted Bundy. Using DNA and other evidence, the Summit County Sheriff's Office and Summit County Attorney's Office formally closed the cold-case murder, saying that the evidence conclusively proves that Ted Bundy murdered 17-year-old Melissa Ann Smith. Bundy has long been considered a suspect in several cold cases in Utah, and Smith's murder was one of them. Hunters found her remains in Summit County on Oct. 27, 1974, 52 years ago today. "The work began with the investigators who handled the case in 1974, and it continued through the dedication and perseverance of those who carried it forward," Summit County Sheriff Kacey Bates said. "After 50 years, we have reached a point that so many have worked toward." items.t: Getting too many texts reminding you to vote? How to get them to stop
items.x: LANSING, Mich. (WLNS) — Election Day is a week away, and with that comes more and more texts urging you to vote. These texts often include a name and address of someone who has not yet voted. Lansing City Clerk Chris Swope said he and his team haven't sent any texts yet this year, and more likely than not, the texts are coming from the campaign of each candidate. "We do occasional texts just to inform," said Swope. "The candidates obviously want to get their supporters out to vote." Voting Guide: What Michigan voters need to know ahead of the 2026 midterm election Campaigns gather information from public records sites and target numbers based on whether or not you have voted. Swope said your voter registration data is private and not shared by his office, so information can often be skewed. Swope said there is only one way to be sure to stop the texts before election day. "As soon as they vote, a lot of times they stop," he said. "The campaigns, they try to be smart with their money, so the texts, the mail will slow down, the phone calls. items.x: Democrats are giddy about the possibility of a bigger blue wave than expected in the battle for the Senate as polls show that South Carolina , Florida and Mississippi — three seats that were long seen as safe Republican holds — are now competitive races. Democrats view the Republican candidates running in those states as mediocre political talents who must fight historic headwinds caused by President Trump’s unpopularity, voter anger over inflation and the war in Iran, and burgeoning Democratic voter enthusiasm. The Senate battleground map has steadily expanded throughout the 2026 midterm election cycle as political handicappers have shifted seats that were thought to be in solidly Republican territory — such as Alaska, Iowa, Kansas and Texas — to the “toss-up" category. But now Republicans have to worry about losing Senate seats in states that were unthinkable as realistic Democratic pickup opportunities at the start of the election cycle, most notably South Carolina, which last elected a Democrat, Fritz Hollings, to the Senate in 1998. Schnell was accused of using AI to alter his work by the student newspaper The Dartmouth and outlet Semafor, specifically pointing to an opinion piece the provost wrote for The Washington Post. items.t: AAA advises drivers about daylight saving time
items.x: ( WAVY ) – It's only a few days until we trade one extra hour of sleep for months of darkness as we leave work to drive home. And even though we're on the easier end of the time transition (from daylight saving time to standard time), the switch still takes its toll. Nexstar's WAVY went to AAA Tidewater Virginia to see what commuters can expect. "Well, the biggest thing for drivers will be the change in daylight when we leave work or school," said Holly Dalby with AAA. "At the end of the day, gone will be the bright sunshine, and we will find ourselves either driving into the glare from the setting sun or driving home in the dark. So it's a time to be particularly careful on the roads." Days will get way shorter in November: How much daylight will we lose? While lawmakers have tried to get rid of the time switch altogether, it doesn't appear to be going anywhere anytime soon, so your circadian rhythm will have to dance to a different beat for a while. "It just messing with our sleep schedule can really add to our fatigue very quickly. And when we're fatigued, we can make mistakes," Dalby said. items.t: ‘Gut punch’: 2 college students found dead in Colorado after going missing on mountain hike
items.x: ( WJW ) – Two missing Colorado college students were found dead Wednesday after they left campus for a weekend trip up a nearly 14,000-foot peak and encountered a heavy snowstorm, police said. Kaden Matsuda, 19, from Ridgway, Colorado, and Jackson Donlon, 20, from New York, left Colorado Mountain College Leadville’s campus on Friday and didn’t return. They told family and friends they planned to go up Ice Mountain, which requires technical climbing, according to the county sheriff’s office. On Wednesday night, the sheriff's office confirmed that the students were found dead around 3:30 p.m. in a basin of the West Apostle Mountain. Authorities do not believe foul play was involved. The investigation is now being handled by the Chaffee County Coroner’s Office. “Our heart aches for Kaden and Jackson’s family and friends. We are very proud of our team’s efforts to find them before this weekend’s coming storm," Sheriff Andy Rohrich wrote on Facebook. "Although this is a gut punch, our prayers were answered that we would find Kaden and Jackson, allowing some closure for the family. Now, she says she doesn't expect to see that money again. Asked if they will get it back, she said, "No, no, no, no." Cruise ship suspends voyage over fuel costs, stranding 200 passengers More than 200 passengers were told Tuesday to leave the Odyssey in Cambodia within hours after the cruise company suspended operations. items.t: Wendy’s gets buyout offer while struggling with beef prices and growing competition
items.x: Wendy’s shares jumped more than 14% Wednesday after noted investor Nelson Peltz made an offer to buy the chain, which has been struggling with high beef prices and aging stores. Peltz’s Trian Fund Management and several partners are offering Wendy’s $7.35 per share in cash, or a premium of nearly 19% over the stock’s closing price on Tuesday, in a deal that would take the company private. The offer values Wendy's at $1.4 billion. Wendy's, which is based in Dublin, Ohio, confirmed receipt of the unsolicited proposal in a statement Wednesday and said its board has formed an independent committee to evaluate it. At the end of last year, Wendy's had 5,969 restaurants in the U.S. and 1,428 outlets in 38 countries. Wendy's, founded in 1969 by Dave Thomas and named after his daughter, is known for its square burgers and Frosty desserts. The fast-growing chain introduced the drive-thru window in 1970 and went public in 1976. In the 1980s, as it jockeyed for sales with McDonald's and Burger King, Wendy's launched salad bars and ran its iconic “Where's the beef?” ad campaign. items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: ( The Hill ) Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. Gasoline and energy costs have risen in six of nine months this year, as the Iran war sparked oil price shocks via the Islamic Republic's restrictions on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Persistent inflation , which has remained above the Fed's 2 percent target for five-and-a-half years, spurred central bank officials to hike interest rates by a quarter point in mid-September. items.t: DoorDash to buy Instacart in $17 billion grocery delivery deal
items.x: DoorDash is gobbling up Instacart in a $17 billion acquisition that will supercharge its grocery delivery business. DoorDash said the Instacart brand name and app will remain, and Instacart shoppers can continue fulfilling orders for Instacart. Grocers can also choose to work with Instacart or DoorDash. Instacart customers will now have access to 50,000 additional stores covered by DoorDash, the company said. Instacart, founded in 2012, specializes in grocery and convenience store delivery in the U.S. and Canada. Its 600,000 “shoppers” — who are independent contractors — completed 338 million orders last year, according to company filings. Instacart has a market value of $14 billion. DoorDash, founded in San Francisco in 2013, began as a restaurant delivery business but has expanded to pet food and electronics. Operating in 40 countries, it completed more than 3 billion orders last year using a network of 9 million independent delivery workers. It has a market value of $73 billion. DoorDash began delivering groceries in 2020 amid a surge in pandemic-era demand. Grocers were initially cautious. items.t: RFK Jr. eases access to unproven peptides despite opposition from FDA scientists
items.x: WASHINGTON (AP) — The Trump administration on Wednesday acted to ease access to unproven peptide drugs favored by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr . Food and Drug Administration scientific staffers had little input on the decision and opposed the changes, according to six people familiar with its development. The draft policy posted online by Kennedy’s Department of Health and Human Services covers a handful of injectable peptides promoted within the wellness industry for uses such as building muscle, healing injuries and boosting energy. The government will take comments for two weeks before finalizing the measure. The document, primarily written by officials at HHS, faced overwhelming pushback among FDA drug staffers who warned it could undermine the agency’s long-standing mission of keeping unsafe health products off the U.S. market, according to the people familiar with its development. (KNWA/KFTA) Arkansas head coach John Calipari along with freshmen Miikka Muurinen and Jordan Smith Jr. met with the media following the Razorbacks’ 93–81 exhibition win over Memphis at Bud Walton Arena. Calipari discussed his team’s defensive effort, struggles with physicality and free throw shooting, and the challenges of coaching a young roster. He also addressed Muurinen’s rebounding, Billy Richmond’s efficient performance, Davion Thompson’s development and the importance of preparing for a difficult non-conference schedule. NOW PLAYING Smith discussed his bounce-back performance after struggling against Gonzaga, the importance of playing aggressively and the team’s defensive mentality. Muurinen talked about getting comfortable with his new teammates, bringing energy to Bud Walton Arena through hustle plays and embracing the physicality of college basketball. Both players also shared their thoughts on Richmond’s leadership and Thompson’s development. For the full press conferences, click the videos above!

items.t: Giannis Antetokounmpo has 24 points, 18 rebounds as the Heat beat the Hawks 129-117 for first win
items.x: ATLANTA (AP) — Giannis Antetokounmpo had 24 points and 18 rebounds in his first victory with the Heat, leading Miami over the Atlanta Hawks 129-117 on Wednesday night. Bam Adebayo also had 24 points and grabbed nine rebounds for the Heat, who lost their first four games after acquiring Antetokounmpo from Milwaukee in the offseason. Adebayo passed Udonis Haslem to become the Heat's career leader in rebounds . Andrew Wiggins scored 18 points and Pelle Larsson had 17 points, eight assists and six rebounds for the Heat, who shot 53% from the field and had a whopping 70 points in the paint. Rookie Kingston Flemings and Nickeil Alexander-Walker each scored 23 points for the Hawks, who have dropped three in a row after opening the season with consecutive wins. Jalen Johnson shot just 4 for 12 and finished with 12 points, 11 assists and nine rebounds. The Hawks were playing the first game of a home back-to-back. The start of their game against Cleveland on Thursday was pushed back an hour so that Game 6 of the WNBA Finals between Atlanta and Golden State could be played at State Farm Arena during the afternoon.
