items.t: What does ‘Arkansas first’ look like? Sen. Cotton, Shoffner answer
items.x: FAYETTEVILLE, Ark. (KNWA/KFTA) — "Arkansas first" has become a familiar phrase on the campaign trail. KNWA/FOX24's Reagan Wynn asked two of the candidates for U.S. Senate, Republican incumbent Tom Cotton and Democrat Hallie Shoffner, what it would look like in practice. Each candidate was asked the same questions, in the same order, with about 30 seconds to answer. Wynn named an issue, and the candidate described what an "Arkansas first" approach to it would be. The topics: Each Arkansas ballot issue, explained What wins when what Arkansas wants conflicts with what their party wants Cost of living and housing Jobs and economic development, including data centers Taxes Social Security and Medicare Health care, rural hospitals and Medicaid Food assistance and SNAP Public education Immigration and the border Guns and public safety Foreign policy and war powers Watch the full segment in the video player next to the headline. KNWA/FOX24 will keep you up to date on state and local elections on air and through our Your Local Election Headquarters page .

items.t: After two-year search, woman’s coworker turns out to be a match for kidney transplant
items.x: SALT LAKE CITY, Utah ( ABC4 ) — Katie Hood and Reina Child became fast friends five years ago when they met as coworkers at Charlie's Produce in Salt Lake City. Then two years ago, Katie, 41, was diagnosed with renal failure. Family, friends and even coworkers began getting tested to see if they were a match. Reina, 47, knew she needed to be tested. And guess what? She is a perfect match. Now, the bond the two ladies share will grow even stronger because on Tuesday they're scheduled for kidney transplant surgery. The women had a pre-operation appointment today ahead of their surgery next Tuesday. "She's an inspiration to so many because even though she's struggling, she's smiles and laughs with you," Reina said about Katie. It all started in October 2024. "I had been really swollen for a while, and it got to the point where walking upstairs was just hard," explained Katie. She decided to go to the doctor, which led to an emergency room visit. That visit changed Katie's life. She was diagnosed with heart and kidney failure. "And I've been doing dialysis for three times a week for two years and yeah, just kind of on this crazy journey." items.t: DOJ’s California ballot fight rejected by another judge
items.x: ( The Hill ) The Trump administration's bid to separate 20,000 mail ballots in California that it says are likely noncitizens met another defeat on Wednesday as a trial judge refused to intervene. U.S. District Judge David Carter ruled California can continue to accept the questioned ballots like any other. “This request violates longstanding constitutional principles mandating that states have control over their elections,” Carter wrote. “If Plaintiff’s last-minute request for relief were granted, either party could create chaos for their own political purposes to disrupt the election process,” he continued. “Over 20,000 registered Californians would potentially lose the right that generations of Americans have fought to preserve.” California has raised eyebrows at the veracity of the administration's list and says it's not obligated to verify voters’ citizenship in response. The state has conceded it's not feasible to segregate a ballot once it's processed. It would be counted even if later found to be fraudulent. items.t: Benton, Washington county early voting still up from 2022 midterms
items.x: FAYETTEVILLE, Ark. (KNWA/KFTA) — More than halfway into early voting, turnout in Northwest Arkansas is exceeding figures from the 2022 midterms. Benton and Washington counties reported that early voter turnout on Wednesday surpassed voting numbers from this time four years ago. In Benton County, 5,292 voters cast their ballots on Thursday alone. This is up from 4,650 at this time in 2022, a 13.8% increase. Washington County voters showed up during the fourth day of early voting compared to 2022 at an even higher rate than Benton County voters. Washington County to not let DOJ election monitors in polling locations on Nov. 3 In Washington County, 3,945 residents voted on Thursday. This is up from 2,953 on the second Wednesday of 2022 early voting, a 33.6% increase. Total voter turnout numbers in Northwest Arkansas also continue to beat 2022 early voting figures up to this point. In Benton County, 46,893 residents have voted since the early voting period began last week. This is up from 34,858 in 2022, a 34.8% increase. In Washington County, 34,359 voters have cast their ballots through the end of the day Wednesday. This is up from 24,954 in 2022, a 37.7% increase.

items.t: Harris advises Democrats against attempting to impeach Trump
items.x: ( The Hill ) Former Vice President Kamala Harris on Tuesday urged Democrats against making a third attempt to impeach President Trump if they win back the House after next week's midterm elections. "I think that going in the direction of impeachment is not a good idea, just to be honest with you," Harris told MeidasTouch's Aaron Parnas in an interview. "Just because we have limited resources and I think the energy and the resources need to put into accountability, need to be put into investigations." "And that's where the time should be spent," she added. "Remember, I was in the Senate for the last go-around, and the votes aren't there. "So, that's how I feel. But also, I think after the election, we all have to just also agree that our attitude has to be to get stuff done." Harris said Democrats should be "uncompromising" and "not sit around, you know, being genteel about the relationships," but maintain accountability when it comes to cuts to healthcare and oversight on the Iran war. items.t: Subiaco Academy high school football team cancels rest of season
items.x: SUBIACO, Ark. (KNWA/KFTA) — Subiaco Academy's high school football team has opted to forfeit its remaining games in the 2026 season, the school announced on Monday. The team said in a social media post that it will not play its remaining two games on schedule, on Oct. 30 at Mena and on Nov. 6 vs. Lamar. "While this was a difficult decision, the safety and well-being of our student-athletes must always come first," the post said. The team said the decision to forfeit the remaining games came following its 41-0 loss to Waldron on Oct. 23. Subiaco currently sits with a record of 0-8, with two of those losses coming in forfeit fashion. The forfeited games were on Sept. 25 at Booneville and on Oct. 16 at Ozark . Both of those games were canceled by Subiaco "due to injuries and limited player availability." Subiaco joins Spiro High School as the two schools in the KNWA/FOX24 viewing area to cut their football seasons short.

items.t: Right-wing activist James O’Keefe charged with unlawful voting, identity theft
items.x: ( The Hill ) Conservative influencer James O’Keefe was charged in Minnesota Wednesday after he and fellow right-leaning commentator Cam Higby misrepresented themselves at a polling place during the state’s primary election earlier this year. Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty announced during a press conference the two men are facing felony unlawful voting and identity fraud charges. “Elections are the bedrock of democracy and their protection is one of our highest priorities,” Moriarty said in a statement . “Individuals engaging in unlawful conduct related to our elections will be held accountable.” On the state’s Aug. 11 primary election day, O’Keefe and Higby donned mock “ Muslim attire ,” spoke in fake accents at Minnesota polling places. O’Keefe and Higby began the state's unregistered voter vouching process under fake names but did not ultimately sign this oath or cast a vote, according to the county attorney. items.t: Arkansas Department of Finance and Administration urges caution about intoxicating Halloween candy look-alikes
items.x: LITTLE ROCK, Ark. – Arkansas Department of Finance and Administration officials is sounding a warning about potentially dangerous candy. Officials said substances like kratom and hallucinogenic mushrooms are frequently packaged in such a way as to resemble popular candy products. They worry that one of these intoxicating “candies” could end up in an unsuspecting child’s bag while out trick-or-treating. Boo!seum Bash taking place in Little Rock on Oct. 29 Parents and guardians are encouraged to inspect every candy package to make sure it is the real thing. If a child unwittingly consumes an intoxicating product, the Arkansas Poison Control Center is at 1-800-222-1222 and medical treatment should be sought immediately, officials said. The warning comes by way of the department’s regulatory division, which oversees medical marijuana, alcohol and tobacco permits. Officials there said they have previously seized candy look-alikes from tobacco and convenience stores.

items.t: Hayden Panettiere death ruled accidental by police in South Carolina
items.x: GREENVILLE, S.C. ( WSPA ) – Police in South Carolina have officially closed the investigation into the death of Hayden Panettiere, according to a Wednesday news release. Greenville Police Department officials said that Panettiere's death has been ruled accidental, based on findings in the investigation and the medical examiner's determination. On August 16, Panettiere was found unresponsive in an apartment at the Judson Mill Lofts on Easley Bridge Road. Police said that Brian Hickerson, Panettiere's on-and-off boyfriend, along with his brother, Zach Hickerson, were at the residence. EMS attempted life-saving measures before pronouncing Panettiere dead at 2:31 p.m. According to the Greenville County Coroner's Office, Panettiere had died from an accidental overdose of fentanyl, 4-ANPP, Alprazolam, Methocarbamol and Quetiapine. Panettiere had spoken openly about challenges in her personal life, including emotional scars from her childhood fame, postpartum depression after giving birth to her daughter, and struggles with alcohol addiction. items.t: Fort Smith Public Schools could see further enrollment decline
items.x: FORT SMITH, Ark. (KNWA/KFTA) — Fort Smith Public Schools could potentially see a decrease in more than 1,000 students by the 2036-37 school year. A presentation given by Hudson Huff of Zonda Education at Monday's school board meeting cited lack of people moving to the area, low birth rates, and the increase in alternate schooling options as reasons educators could see less students in the district. "Your overall enrollment is just going to struggle to increase," Huff said. According to Huff, current enrollment has dropped to 6.1% since the 2024-25 school year, leaving the student population at 12,851. Based on the projections, in the next 10 years, enrollment could be as low as 11,839 district wide. "We still see some, some enrollment, decline in the next few years and would be, recommending accounting for that in the, in the districts planning, strategies in the next year or two," Huff said. items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war , creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle . items.t: Utah authorities connect 1974 cold case to serial killer Ted Bundy
items.x: SUMMIT COUNTY, Utah ( KTVX ) — Investigators in Summit County, Utah closed the 1974 cold case homicide of Melissa Ann Smith Tuesday, linking her murder to prominent serial killer Ted Bundy. Using DNA and other evidence, the Summit County Sheriff's Office and Summit County Attorney's Office formally closed the cold-case murder, saying that the evidence conclusively proves that Ted Bundy murdered 17-year-old Melissa Ann Smith. Bundy has long been considered a suspect in several cold cases in Utah, and Smith's murder was one of them. Hunters found her remains in Summit County on Oct. 27, 1974, 52 years ago today. "The work began with the investigators who handled the case in 1974, and it continued through the dedication and perseverance of those who carried it forward," Summit County Sheriff Kacey Bates said. "After 50 years, we have reached a point that so many have worked toward." items.t: What voting equipment does your Tennessee county use?
items.x: NASHVILLE, Tenn. (WKRN) — From declaring votes by voice to making selections on an electronic machine, the way Americans exercise the democratic right to vote has changed a lot over the years. Nearly four million Tennesseans are registered to vote in the 2026 midterm election. The system each person will use depends on where they live, as each of Tennessee's 95 counties had the ability to select from a variety of approved methods. The machine Tennesseans are most likely to use is the Microvote Infinity, a type of machine that directly records votes using an electronic system. It's used in 44 counties and allows voters to select a candidate or referendum using a push button interface. In Tennessee, all direct recording electronic system, or DREs, are required to include a voter verified paper audit trail printer in case the county is selected for an audit. ES&S ExpressVote, ES&S Optical Scan, and Unisyn Optical Scan are other types of systems approved by Tennessee for use in elections. You can find the Secretary of State's list of approved machines and watch videos of how each one works by clicking here .

items.t: Purdue studies cockroach milk for food-based research
items.x: HENDERSON, Ky. (WEHT) Purdue University is looking into the potential for cockroach milk to create food. Ramaswamy Subramanian is a professor in the Department of Biological Sciences and the Weldon School of Biomedical Engineering at Purdue University. Officials say a cockroach found on Hawaii, called the Pacific beetle cockroach, makes a highly nutritious substance that it feeds to its babies. This substance, dubbed "cockroach milk" by scientists, has twice the number of calories per unit weight as the milk from a water buffalo. Four moon sites identified for future research Officals note this makes cockroach milk one of the most nutritious substances ever discovered. Cockroach milk is densely packed with nutrients and exists in a crystallized form that slowly releases nutrients to the cockroach embryo as needed. Subramanian believes that with modern genetic engineering, cockroach milk could be used to create high-protein bread that could help feed the world or create stable, high-calorie food that could feed astronauts on future journeys to Mars.

The offer values Wendy's at $1.4 billion. In the 1980s, as it jockeyed for sales with McDonald's and Burger King, Wendy's launched salad bars and ran its iconic “Where's the beef?” ad campaign. items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: ( The Hill ) Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. Gasoline and energy costs have risen in six of nine months this year, as the Iran war sparked oil price shocks via the Islamic Republic's restrictions on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Persistent inflation , which has remained above the Fed's 2 percent target for five-and-a-half years, spurred central bank officials to hike interest rates by a quarter point in mid-September. items.t: RFK Jr. eases access to unproven peptides despite opposition from FDA scientists
items.x: WASHINGTON (AP) — The Trump administration on Wednesday acted to ease access to unproven peptide drugs favored by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr . Food and Drug Administration scientific staffers had little input on the decision and opposed the changes, according to six people familiar with its development. The draft policy posted online by Kennedy’s Department of Health and Human Services covers a handful of injectable peptides promoted within the wellness industry for uses such as building muscle, healing injuries and boosting energy. The government will take comments for two weeks before finalizing the measure. The document, primarily written by officials at HHS, faced overwhelming pushback among FDA drug staffers who warned it could undermine the agency’s long-standing mission of keeping unsafe health products off the U.S. market, according to the people familiar with its development. "I think that going in the direction of impeachment is not a good idea, just to be honest with you," Harris told MeidasTouch's Aaron Parnas in an interview. items.t: Are prediction markets accurate when it comes to elections?
items.x: JOHNSON CITY, Tenn. (WJHL) Prediction markets such as Kalshi and Polymarket have become popular for many topics, including the upcoming midterm elections. However, there is a question about the accuracy of the markets. Looking at the Tennessee governor's race between Republican Marsha Blackburn, Democrat Jerri Green, and Independent David Hatley, both Kalshi and Polymarket show Blackburn taking a significant lead. How much are Tennessee’s gubernatorial candidates spending on their campaigns? In the District 1 House race between incumbent Republican candidate Diana Harshbarger and Democratic candidate Kristi Burke, Kalshi and Polymarket show the Republican Harshbarger taking a lead with over 90%. Robin Hanson, an economics professor at George Mason University , said that, based on past elections, the mechanisms of prediction markets are accurate. "When we've compared them head-to-head with other mechanisms like polls or poll aggregates or committees, these markets just consistently do about as well or substantially better," Hanson said. items.t: Reward for escaped inmate Jacob Morley up to $15,000
items.x: CARTER COUNTY, Tenn. (WJHL) — The reward for information leading to the arrest of escaped inmate and convicted murderer Jacob Morley has been increased to $15,000. The Tennessee Bureau of Investigation (TBI) announced on Wednesday that the reward had been increased. Previously, the TBI had offered a $2,500 reward of its own. items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war , creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle . He was 92. Nominated by then-President Bill Clinton in 1998, Hellerstein oversaw many high-profile disputes during his nearly three decades on the bench in New York City. He was back in the national limelight presiding over the proceedings for Maduro , who was captured and brought to the U.S. earlier this year over accusations of narco-terrorism. Maduro and his wife were in the judge's courtroom less than two weeks ago to plead not guilty to a new set of criminal charges. Before the Maduro operation, Hellerstein had long clashed with President Donald Trump in court. The judge at one point agreed that Trump’s fixer-turned-foe, Michael Cohen, could be released from prison to home confinement. Cohen has cast his prosecution as retribution by Trump. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 176 points, or 0.3%, as of 11:45 a.m. Eastern time, and the Nasdaq composite was virtually unchanged. The day’s highlight will likely be what the Federal Reserve says, if anything, about where interest rates are heading. The Fed raised its main interest rate last month for the first time in three years in hopes of slowing the high inflation that’s squeezing the economy and discouraging Americans . The widespread expectation on Wall Street is that the Fed will leave the federal funds rate alone at this meeting, and the question is whether it will give hints about what may happen at later meetings. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh, though, has been adamant since taking over the Fed about wanting it to give fewer indications about its future moves. items.t: Democrats see battleground map expand to South Carolina, Florida, Mississippi
items.x: Democrats are giddy about the possibility of a bigger blue wave than expected in the battle for the Senate as polls show that South Carolina , Florida and Mississippi — three seats that were long seen as safe Republican holds — are now competitive races. Democrats view the Republican candidates running in those states as mediocre political talents who must fight historic headwinds caused by President Trump’s unpopularity, voter anger over inflation and the war in Iran, and burgeoning Democratic voter enthusiasm. The Senate battleground map has steadily expanded throughout the 2026 midterm election cycle as political handicappers have shifted seats that were thought to be in solidly Republican territory — such as Alaska, Iowa, Kansas and Texas — to the “toss-up" category. But now Republicans have to worry about losing Senate seats in states that were unthinkable as realistic Democratic pickup opportunities at the start of the election cycle, most notably South Carolina, which last elected a Democrat, Fritz Hollings, to the Senate in 1998. (WSYR-TV) The 2026 Cortaca Jug football game between Ithaca College and SUNY Cortland will be broadcast live nationwide on the YES Network and streamed free on the DAZN app. The matchup takes place at Yankee Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14, at 1 p.m. Eastern. The broadcast agreement coincides with a four-year naming sponsorship from Visions Federal Credit Union, covering the annual rivalry game through 2029. The deal marks the first naming sponsorship in the history of the Cortaca Jug. Ithaca College President La Jerne Terry Cornish highlighted the significance of bringing the event to a national viewing audience. “Cortaca brings the Ithaca College community together across generations and across the country,” Cornish said. “We would love to have every Bomber fan join us at Yankee Stadium, but we know that isn't possible. Having the game on YES and DAZN means more of our alumni, families and friends nationwide can share in an afternoon that means so much to IC.” The upcoming 67th Cortaca Jug marks the second time the rivalry game will be held at Yankee Stadium. items.t: AAA advises drivers about daylight saving time
items.x: ( WAVY ) – It's only a few days until we trade one extra hour of sleep for months of darkness as we leave work to drive home. And even though we're on the easier end of the time transition (from daylight saving time to standard time), the switch still takes its toll. Nexstar's WAVY went to AAA Tidewater Virginia to see what commuters can expect. "Well, the biggest thing for drivers will be the change in daylight when we leave work or school," said Holly Dalby with AAA. "At the end of the day, gone will be the bright sunshine, and we will find ourselves either driving into the glare from the setting sun or driving home in the dark. So it's a time to be particularly careful on the roads." Days will get way shorter in November: How much daylight will we lose? While lawmakers have tried to get rid of the time switch altogether, it doesn't appear to be going anywhere anytime soon, so your circadian rhythm will have to dance to a different beat for a while. "It just messing with our sleep schedule can really add to our fatigue very quickly. And when we're fatigued, we can make mistakes," Dalby said. items.t: One issue, different bills: Energy costs shape key midterm races
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Higher energy costs have helped make affordability a top issue in the 2026 midterms , but voters aren't all worried about the same bills. Diesel prices are squeezing Midwest farmers , while homeowners in the Northeast face soaring heating oil costs . Others in data center hotspots like Texas and Ohio are worried about their electricity bills . Democrats have tried to tie those issues to President Trump , pointing to the war in Iran and his embrace of AI . As of Wednesday, Decision Desk HQ gave Democrats an 80% chance of winning the House and a 58% chance of controlling the Senate . Democrats narrowly favored to sweep House and Senate: DDHQ Some Republicans have called for an end to the Iran war, while others have blamed high prices on Ukraine's war with Russia and Democrats' energy policies. To win the Senate, Democrats will have to break through on Republican turf . Of the Cook Political Report's seven toss-ups , five are in states Trump won by double digits in 2024. items.t: ‘Gut punch’: 2 college students found dead in Colorado after going missing on mountain hike
items.x: ( WJW ) – Two missing Colorado college students were found dead Wednesday after they left campus for a weekend trip up a nearly 14,000-foot peak and encountered a heavy snowstorm, police said. Kaden Matsuda, 19, from Ridgway, Colorado, and Jackson Donlon, 20, from New York, left Colorado Mountain College Leadville’s campus on Friday and didn’t return. They told family and friends they planned to go up Ice Mountain, which requires technical climbing, according to the county sheriff’s office. On Wednesday night, the sheriff's office confirmed that the students were found dead around 3:30 p.m. in a basin of the West Apostle Mountain. Authorities do not believe foul play was involved. The investigation is now being handled by the Chaffee County Coroner’s Office. “Our heart aches for Kaden and Jackson’s family and friends. We are very proud of our team’s efforts to find them before this weekend’s coming storm," Sheriff Andy Rohrich wrote on Facebook. "Although this is a gut punch, our prayers were answered that we would find Kaden and Jackson, allowing some closure for the family. We ask that everyone give time and distance to family members and friends as they mourn their loss.” Kaden

items.t: Cruise ship passenger says warning signs were there long before Cambodia
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — Kit Cassingham and her husband, Randy, sold their home and nearly everything they owned to live aboard a cruise ship for years. Now, she says she doesn't expect to see that money again. Cassingham told NewsNation's Jesse Weber on Wednesday that the couple paid about $370,000 to $380,000 for their cabin on the Villa Vie Odyssey, plus $7,000 a month in expenses. Asked if they will get it back, she said, "No, no, no, no." Cruise ship suspends voyage over fuel costs, stranding 200 passengers More than 200 passengers were told Tuesday to leave the Odyssey in Cambodia within hours after the cruise company suspended operations. In a news release , Villa Vie blamed soaring fuel costs tied to the war in Iran, saying the monthly fuel cost per cabin jumped from about $1,800 to as much as $8,000. Villa Vie Odyssey: How did passengers find out they had to leave? Cassingham and her husband had already gotten off the ship for a hotel so they could work online when a short message arrived saying the ship couldn't get more fuel . “You have till two o’clock to get off the ship,” she said. The news wasn't a total shock. “We’d seen red flags all along,” Cassingham said. More than 200

items.t: Wendy’s gets buyout offer while struggling with beef prices and growing competition
items.x: Wendy’s shares jumped more than 14% Wednesday after noted investor Nelson Peltz made an offer to buy the chain, which has been struggling with high beef prices and aging stores. Peltz’s Trian Fund Management and several partners are offering Wendy’s $7.35 per share in cash, or a premium of nearly 19% over the stock’s closing price on Tuesday, in a deal that would take the company private. The offer values Wendy's at $1.4 billion. Wendy's, which is based in Dublin, Ohio, confirmed receipt of the unsolicited proposal in a statement Wednesday and said its board has formed an independent committee to evaluate it. At the end of last year, Wendy's had 5,969 restaurants in the U.S. and 1,428 outlets in 38 countries. Wendy's, founded in 1969 by Dave Thomas and named after his daughter, is known for its square burgers and Frosty desserts. The fast-growing chain introduced the drive-thru window in 1970 and went public in 1976. In the 1980s, as it jockeyed for sales with McDonald's and Burger King, Wendy's launched salad bars and ran its iconic “Where's the beef?” ad campaign. items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: ( The Hill ) Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. Gasoline and energy costs have risen in six of nine months this year, as the Iran war sparked oil price shocks via the Islamic Republic's restrictions on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Persistent inflation , which has remained above the Fed's 2 percent target for five-and-a-half years, spurred central bank officials to hike interest rates by a quarter point in mid-September. items.t: DoorDash to buy Instacart in $17 billion grocery delivery deal
items.x: DoorDash is gobbling up Instacart in a $17 billion acquisition that will supercharge its grocery delivery business. DoorDash said the Instacart brand name and app will remain, and Instacart shoppers can continue fulfilling orders for Instacart. Grocers can also choose to work with Instacart or DoorDash. Instacart customers will now have access to 50,000 additional stores covered by DoorDash, the company said. Instacart, founded in 2012, specializes in grocery and convenience store delivery in the U.S. and Canada. Its 600,000 “shoppers” — who are independent contractors — completed 338 million orders last year, according to company filings. Instacart has a market value of $14 billion. DoorDash, founded in San Francisco in 2013, began as a restaurant delivery business but has expanded to pet food and electronics. Operating in 40 countries, it completed more than 3 billion orders last year using a network of 9 million independent delivery workers. It has a market value of $73 billion. DoorDash began delivering groceries in 2020 amid a surge in pandemic-era demand. Grocers were initially cautious. items.t: RFK Jr. eases access to unproven peptides despite opposition from FDA scientists
items.x: WASHINGTON (AP) — The Trump administration on Wednesday acted to ease access to unproven peptide drugs favored by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr . Food and Drug Administration scientific staffers had little input on the decision and opposed the changes, according to six people familiar with its development. The draft policy posted online by Kennedy’s Department of Health and Human Services covers a handful of injectable peptides promoted within the wellness industry for uses such as building muscle, healing injuries and boosting energy. The government will take comments for two weeks before finalizing the measure. The document, primarily written by officials at HHS, faced overwhelming pushback among FDA drug staffers who warned it could undermine the agency’s long-standing mission of keeping unsafe health products off the U.S. market, according to the people familiar with its development. items.x: (NEXSTAR) – Walmart has stepped up to the table with its cheapest-ever holiday meal deal, preparing to face off against the other grocers who have also unveiled dinner specials ahead of Thanksgiving. The Arkansas-based retailer unveiled its "Holiday Meal Basket" on Wednesday, saying it can feed 10 for $35, the most affordable price since Walmart began offering such a deal. It's about $5 cheaper than last year's basket and includes six additional items. "The Holiday Meal Basket has become one of our favorite traditions at Walmart. It brings our purpose to life in such a meaningful way by helping families make the holidays special without stretching their budgets," said Walmart U.S. President and CEO David Guggina. This year's basket includes a Butterball turkey (selling for 97 cents per pound and estimated at 13.5 lbs), Stove Top stuffing, dinner rolls, and ingredients for other holiday meal staples like sweet potato casserole and pumpkin pie, according to Walmart. The basket will be available in stores, and all of the items can be purchased online with one click. Walmart said the deal will be available through Christmas Eve. items.x: ( The Hill ) Student loan advocates see next week’s midterms as an opportunity for further oversight and potential reversals of policies from the Trump administration that have delayed or denied debt relief and increased monthly payments. Democrats have the potential Tuesday to retake the House and Senate, possibly creating a friendlier environment for student loan borrowers after two years of drastic changes to the system. items.t: 82% of Syracuse pothole claims are denied, investigation reveals
items.x: SYRACUSE, N.Y. (WSYR-TV) — For drivers, hitting a pothole can mean more than an annoying bump in the road. In some cases, it can lead to hundreds of dollars in damage. Kimberly O’Brien knows that firsthand. In January, while driving her sister’s car on James Street in Syracuse, she hit a pothole near a sewer grate. “I hit it, and I heard that famous thump,” O’Brien said. After parking, O’Brien discovered two flat tires and a bent rim. The total repair bill came to $890.15. “It was not a small amount at all,” O’Brien said. O’Brien filed a claim with the City of Syracuse in March, hoping to be reimbursed for the damage. In June, the city denied her claim. The letter stated: “After a careful evaluation of the facts, we can only conclude that we are not liable for any damages.” O’Brien said she was frustrated by the decision. “I was like, you’ve gotta be kidding me?” she said. items.t: Mother killed in Union Springs fire, chief confirms
items.x: UNION SPRINGS, N.Y. (WSYR-TV) New York State Police and the Union Springs Fire Department confirmed to NewsChannel 9 that one woman is dead following an overnight fire in the village of Union Springs. State Police said the woman died from their injuries at the hospital. She was a mother of seven. Nine people lived in the home. All photos courtesy of Springport Fire District. The call for the fire went out around 8:30 p.m. last night, Oct. 29. The home was at the intersection of Routes 90 and 326, near the Lakeside Trading gas station and Dollar General. It's not clear as to how the fire started, but state police are leading the investigation, and say they will release more details later. items.t: Steps to lower your energy bills in CNY this winter
items.x: SYRACUSE, N.Y. (WSYR) As the cost of heating homes goes up during the winter, keeping cold air out and the heat inside is vital, and the federal Weatherization Assistance Program, around since 1976, can help lower-income families. "The work we do in the home stays there," Sally Ward, the director of Energy and Housing Services for Peace Inc., said. " It's permanent. The insulation doesn't disappear after five years. The work we do to save them money on their energy bill this season will help them next season, and so on." But the waiting list is lengthy, with approximately 300 people in line, and there are ways to cut costs in the meantime. Something as simple as replacing an incandescent light bulb with an LED is an effective way to reduce energy costs, Joe Maggiore, the executive director of the New York State Weatherization Directors Association, said. "It doesn't sound like a lot, but 20, 30 bucks a month just by switching out your light bulbs, you know that's two, three, four, 500 bucks a year," Maggiore said. Drunk driver in deadly 2019 Cayuga County crash to be released to ICE
items.x: WEEDSPORT, N.Y. (WSYR-TV) A man convicted of killing a Cayuga County resident in a drunk driving crash is set to be released to ICE. Heriberto Perez-Velasquez is scheduled to be released early from state prison on Friday, Nov. 6 to ICE's custody due to a decision from the New York State Board of Parole, a statement from the Cayuga County District Attorney's Office said. With a blood-alcohol content level of .21% almost three times the legal limit Perez-Velasquez hit a tractor driven by Mark Knapp, killing him, in the village of Weedsport on Nov. 10, 2019. Perez-Velasquez, a Guatemala native who was deported before reentering the United States illegally, pleaded guilty in Cayuga County Court to the class B felony of aggravated vehicular homicide, among other charges, on Sept. 24, 2020. He was sentenced that November to 7 to 24 years in state prison. Perez-Velasquez was arrested three weeks prior in Wayne County on an aggravated driving while intoxicated charge, the district attorney's office said. Bam Adebayo also had 24 points and grabbed nine rebounds for the Heat, who lost their first four games after acquiring Antetokounmpo from Milwaukee in the offseason. Andrew Wiggins scored 18 points and Pelle Larsson had 17 points, eight assists and six rebounds for the Heat, who shot 53% from the field and had a whopping 70 points in the paint. Rookie Kingston Flemings and Nickeil Alexander-Walker each scored 23 points for the Hawks, who have dropped three in a row after opening the season with consecutive wins. Jalen Johnson shot just 4 for 12 and finished with 12 points, 11 assists and nine rebounds. The Hawks were playing the first game of a home back-to-back. The start of their game against Cleveland on Thursday was pushed back an hour so that Game 6 of the WNBA Finals between Atlanta and Golden State could be played at State Farm Arena during the afternoon. And guess what? She is a perfect match. Now, the bond the two ladies share will grow even stronger because on Tuesday they're scheduled for kidney transplant surgery. The women had a pre-operation appointment today ahead of their surgery next Tuesday. items.t: DOJ’s California ballot fight rejected by another judge
items.x: ( The Hill ) The Trump administration's bid to separate 20,000 mail ballots in California that it says are likely noncitizens met another defeat on Wednesday as a trial judge refused to intervene. U.S. District Judge David Carter ruled California can continue to accept the questioned ballots like any other. “This request violates longstanding constitutional principles mandating that states have control over their elections,” Carter wrote. “If Plaintiff’s last-minute request for relief were granted, either party could create chaos for their own political purposes to disrupt the election process,” he continued. “Over 20,000 registered Californians would potentially lose the right that generations of Americans have fought to preserve.” California has raised eyebrows at the veracity of the administration's list and says it's not obligated to verify voters’ citizenship in response. The state has conceded it's not feasible to segregate a ballot once it's processed. It would be counted even if later found to be fraudulent. items.t: Cornell faculty senate to begin weeklong process for no-confidence vote for university administration
items.x: ITHACA, N.Y. (WSYR-TV) The Cornell University Faculty Senate opted to start a weeklong process for a no-confidence vote for the school's administrators. At a meeting Wednesday night , the faculty senate voted on a resolution to hold a no-confidence vote for the university's leadership in light of how an alleged 2024 gang rape was handled. The voting process, which will be held online, is expected to open Thursday, Oct. 29. The voting process will last until noon on Friday, Nov. 6. The senate meeting was extended three times once for 10 minutes, once for 30, and again for another 10 minutes. The meeting went 50 minutes longer than anticipated. The no-confidence vote would be symbolic, showing an overall distrust among faculty in the private school's ability to properly deal with sexual assault cases. The faculty turned in a resolution about three weeks ago calling for the no-confidence vote due to concerns over how university leaders dealt with accusations that a woman was raped by several men at the Chi Phi fraternity house in October 2024. items.t: Failed Florida gubernatorial candidate announces 2028 White House bid
items.x: ( The Hill ) Former Florida gubernatorial candidate James Fishback (R) said he plans to run for president in 2028. “Last night, someone asked me ‘What do you plan on doing next?’ I told them the truth. I’m running for president,” Fishback wrote Wednesday on social platform X , attaching a video of him announcing his presidential bid at an event. The 41 second video clip shows Fishback’s announcement followed by a round of applause. “My wife and I will soon visit Iowa, New Hampshire, and South Carolina to hold public TownHalls. Between November 2025 and June 2026, average daily school zone speed violations fell by 65%, dropping from approximately 1,275 to 441 per school day. items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war , creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle . The S&P 500 rose 0.2% and pulled within 1% of its all-time high , which was set earlier this month. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 176 points, or 0.3%, as of 11:45 a.m. Eastern time, and the Nasdaq composite was virtually unchanged. The day’s highlight will likely be what the Federal Reserve says, if anything, about where interest rates are heading. The Fed raised its main interest rate last month for the first time in three years in hopes of slowing the high inflation that’s squeezing the economy and discouraging Americans . The widespread expectation on Wall Street is that the Fed will leave the federal funds rate alone at this meeting, and the question is whether it will give hints about what may happen at later meetings. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh, though, has been adamant since taking over the Fed about wanting it to give fewer indications about its future moves. items.t: Recalled butter sold in 10 states receives risk warning: FDA
items.x: NEW JERSEY ( WPIX ) A popular plant-based butter has been recalled due to yeast, mold and E. coli, and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has now assigned it a risk level . The recall, which was initiated by Prosperity Organic Foods, Inc., headquartered in Boise, Idaho, involves 1,304 cases of Miyoko's Creamery European Style Salted Plant Milk Butter. The FDA assigned the recall as a Class II risk level on Friday, meaning a product may cause “temporary or medically reversible adverse health consequences.” The recall was initially announced Sept. 11. The affected butter, which is perishable and stored refrigerated or frozen, comes in six-packs of 8-ounce units, which can be identified with the following information: UPC 857554005773 Lot number and best-by on SBS carton: 07871, Nov. 5, 2026 Lot number and best-by date on the corrugated case for shipment: 1007871, Nov. 5, 2026 The affected products were also sold in Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Iowa, Illinois, Indiana, Maryland, New Jersey, New Hampshire and Wisconsin.

items.t: Watertown issues safety tips for Halloween celebrations
items.x: WATERTOWN, N.Y. (WWTI) – As residents prepare for Halloween celebrations on October 31, 2026, the City of Watertown has issued essential safety tips to help ensure a safe, enjoyable holiday for everyone. In a press release, city officials outlined several key recommendations for trick-or-treaters and parents: Choose a safe route: Stick to well-lit areas and utilize sidewalks. Stay visible: Wear bright colors and incorporate reflective tape into costumes, and carry a flashlight to improve nighttime visibility. Go in groups: Trick-or-treat with friends or family members, ensuring that an adult accompanies young children. Watch for traffic: Always look both ways and cross streets safely at corners. Keep pets indoors: Protect family pets by keeping them inside during the celebrations. Inspect treats: Have an adult thoroughly check all collected treats before anyone eats them. For emergencies, residents are reminded to dial 911; for non-emergency police matters, call 315-786-2601. Additional details can be found by visiting the official city website .

items.t: Utah authorities connect 1974 cold case to serial killer Ted Bundy
items.x: SUMMIT COUNTY, Utah ( KTVX ) — Investigators in Summit County, Utah closed the 1974 cold case homicide of Melissa Ann Smith Tuesday, linking her murder to prominent serial killer Ted Bundy. Using DNA and other evidence, the Summit County Sheriff's Office and Summit County Attorney's Office formally closed the cold-case murder, saying that the evidence conclusively proves that Ted Bundy murdered 17-year-old Melissa Ann Smith. Bundy has long been considered a suspect in several cold cases in Utah, and Smith's murder was one of them. Hunters found her remains in Summit County on Oct. 27, 1974, 52 years ago today. "The work began with the investigators who handled the case in 1974, and it continued through the dedication and perseverance of those who carried it forward," Summit County Sheriff Kacey Bates said. "After 50 years, we have reached a point that so many have worked toward." items.t: Cause of death revealed for ‘Office Space’ actor Richard Riehle: Reports
items.x: (NEXSTAR) – The cause of death for longtime actor Richard Riehle has been revealed, according to reports. The 78-year-old died earlier this month in Los Angeles, friends told TMZ , which was the first to report the news. The outlet and People , citing his death certificate, reported Tuesday that the "Office Space" actor experienced a stroke and had oropharyngeal cancer. He had been in a rehabilitation center at the time of his death in mid-October, according to People. Oropharyngeal cancer , which can be asymptomatic, impacts the middle portion of your throat, including the base of your tongue and the tonsils. While there are multiple types of oropharyngeal cancers, Johns Hopkins Medicine says the majority are squamous cell carcinomas, which are further divided into HPV-related and HPV-unrelated. The former is caused by HPV, while the latter is commonly caused by tobacco or alcohol. Details about Riehle's condition were not released. items.t: AAA advises drivers about daylight saving time
items.x: (WAVY) – It's only a few days until we trade one extra hour of sleep for months of darkness as we leave work to drive home. And even though we're on the easier end of the time transition (from daylight saving time to standard time), the switch still takes its toll. Nexstar's WAVY went to AAA Tidewater Virginia to see what commuters can expect. "Well, the biggest thing for drivers will be the change in daylight when we leave work or school," said Holly Dalby with AAA. There are any number of things that can affect the scope. "You don't want to make a bad shot and wound an animal either," said Frango. items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. Gasoline and energy costs have risen in six of nine months this year, as the Iran war sparked oil price shocks via the Islamic Republic's restrictions on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Persistent inflation , which has remained above the Fed's 2 percent target for five-and-a-half years, spurred central bank officials to hike interest rates by a quarter point in mid-September. items.t: Carroll hockey rallies past Leo in battle of defending state champs
items.x: FORT WAYNE, Ind. (WANE) In a battle between two of last year's state champions, Carroll stormed back from a 3-1 deficit to top Leo 5-3 on Wednesday at PSM Icehouse. The Chargers shut out Leo 3-0 in the final period, scoring the game-winning goal with 3:24 to go in regulation. Easton Harter netted the game-winning goal off of assists from Peyton MacDonald and Trentyn Vongphanchanh. Ryder Potts scored an insurance goal 30 seconds later to cap off a comeback win for the Chargers. Leo took a 2-1 lead to the end of the first period off of strikes from Bradley Kornmann and Asher Putt. Jackson Crawford added onto Leo's lead with a power play goal early in the second period. Jakob Pedersen ignited Carroll's comeback by scoring with 10 seconds left before the second intermission. Carroll (3-0) faces Homestead next Wednesday, while Leo (1-2) looks to bounce back against the Fort Wayne Vipers that same night.

items.t: Religious, community leaders urge voters to help end hunger in Rio Grande Valley
items.x: McALLEN, Texas (Border Report) The Humanitarian Respite Center in McAllen used to help thousands of migrants who crossed the border during the Biden administration. But since Trump took over it has largely been empty. But on Wednesday dozens of faith-based and community leaders were at the center to speak out against hunger and food insecurities that are plaguing this South Texas border region. And to urge voters to elect leaders who will help. “In this election year Bread for the World is urging people of faith to vote to end hunger," Felipe Salinas of the Christian-based nonprofit group Bread for the World told the group. He says there are too many people in the region who cannot afford food for their families and he believes more public assistance is needed by the government. “It is very much a policy choice because for every meal a food bank or food pantry provides, the federally-funded Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, or SNAP, provides 9. How we vote in this election can make a difference in ending hunger.” From a rabbi, to Christian ministers, to the Catholic bishop from Brownsville, speaker after speaker told stories of community members unable to pay for groceries

items.t: Failed Florida gubernatorial candidate announces 2028 White House bid
items.x: ( The Hill ) Former Florida gubernatorial candidate James Fishback (R) said he plans to run for president in 2028. “Last night, someone asked me ‘What do you plan on doing next?’ I told them the truth. I’m running for president,” Fishback wrote Wednesday on social platform X , attaching a video of him announcing his presidential bid at an event. The 41 second video clip shows Fishback’s announcement followed by a round of applause. “My wife and I will soon visit Iowa, New Hampshire, and South Carolina to hold public TownHalls. Soon after I will announce my final decision,” Fishback told The Hill in a statement Wednesday. The Florida Republican lost his gubernatorial bid to Rep. Byron Donalds (R-Fla.), who is running against Obama-endorsed Democratic nominee David Jolly in the upcoming elections. Fishback finished third in the Republican primary. Recently , Fishback said he and his wife were stopped from entering a Republican rally in Clearwater, Fla. Local news reports said the rally was hosted by Rep. Anna Paulina Luna (R-Fla.) and listed Donalds and Sen. Ashley Moody (R-Fla.) as special guests. Earlier this year, Fishback said his campaign was banned from Waffle House restaurants

items.t: Report: Off-duty border agent allegedly stabs, kills wife
items.x: EL PASO, Texas (Border Report) An off-duty U.S. Border Patrol agent allegedly stabbed and killed his wife early Wednesday morning in Laredo, Texas, according to the Laredo Morning Times. The newspaper reported that Abel Garza, 30, is charged with murder in the death of his wife, 28-year-old Mayra Alejandra Landeros. The newspaper also reported that U.S. Customs and Border Protection confirmed that Garza is a U.S. Border Patrol agent with the Laredo Sector, and that the agency’s Office of Professional Responsibility is reviewing the incident.

items.t: Marion County election officials detail DOJ’s plan to send monitors to polling sites on Election Day
items.x: INDIANAPOLIS— Wednesday, attorneys with the Marion County Clerk’s Office spoke with representatives from the U.S. Department of Justice’s Civil Rights Division about the DOJ’s plan to send election monitors to Marion County. According to Marion County Clerk Kate Sweeney Bell, up to 12 election monitors in plain clothes will visit the county on Election Day. It is not clear which polling sites the election monitors intend to visit. The monitors are not members of law enforcement and cannot enter polling sites. It is reported that they must stay at least 50 feet away from a polling location’s entrance. “They cannot impede or infringe on any voter who is going in to cast a ballot,” Sweeney Bell said. It is reported that the monitors must stay at least 50 feet away from a polling location’s entrance. While monitors cannot talk to voters as they head into polling sites, Sweeney Bell said the DOJ intends for the monitors to speak with voters as they exit the polls. “I want voters to know they are not required, nor will they face any penalty [in] any way, shape, or form if they just keep on walking once, they finish voting,” Sweeney Bell said. “They don’t have to stop and talk to anyone.”

Jacob Morley, 28, escaped Sunday night from the Northwest Correctional Complex in Tiptonville, Tennessee, where he was serving a life sentence for a 2022 murder. items.t: Harris advises Democrats against attempting to impeach Trump
items.x: ( The Hill ) Former Vice President Kamala Harris on Tuesday urged Democrats against making a third attempt to impeach President Trump if they win back the House after next week's midterm elections. "I think that going in the direction of impeachment is not a good idea, just to be honest with you," Harris told MeidasTouch's Aaron Parnas in an interview. "Just because we have limited resources and I think the energy and the resources need to put into accountability, need to be put into investigations." "And that's where the time should be spent," she added. "Remember, I was in the Senate for the last go-around, and the votes aren't there. "So, that's how I feel. But also, I think after the election, we all have to just also agree that our attitude has to be to get stuff done." Harris said Democrats should be "uncompromising" and "not sit around, you know, being genteel about the relationships," but maintain accountability when it comes to cuts to healthcare and oversight on the Iran war. The former vice president was days into her new role in 2021 when Democratic lawmakers impeached Trump in connection with the Jan. 6 Capitol Hill attack. In February 2021, the Senate acquitted Trump

Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty announced during a press conference the two men are facing felony unlawful voting and identity fraud charges. “Elections are the bedrock of democracy and their protection is one of our highest priorities,” Moriarty said in a statement . “Individuals engaging in unlawful conduct related to our elections will be held accountable.” On the state’s Aug. 11 primary election day, O’Keefe and Higby donned mock “ Muslim attire ,” spoke in fake accents at Minnesota polling places. O’Keefe and Higby began the state's unregistered voter vouching process under fake names but did not ultimately sign this oath or cast a vote, according to the county attorney. items.t: Trick or treat? Halloween weather history
items.x: FORT WAYNE, Ind. (WANE) – Over the years, our Halloween forecast has seen some tricks and treats, with snow or even a high temperature in the 80s. This years forecast doesn't look too spooky, although we've certainly seen some eerie happenings in our weather history. Our average high temperature on Halloween lands in the upper 50s and the average low is typically in the upper 30s. The overall average temperature for the days is in the upper 40s. Average Halloween temperatures range from the upper 30s to upper 50s. In the past five years, we've seen high temperatures ranging from the 70s to upper 30s. Four out of the past five years have seen some rain on the holiday, and in 2023 we saw a trace of snow! With data going back to 1897, we've seen eight years where at least a trace of snow has fallen. The highest total was 1.5 in 1917, which was also the coldest year on record with a high of only 35°. Snowfall totals higher than a trace ranged from 0.5 -0.2 . The second coldest year on record was 2023 with a high of 39°. Snow has fallen on Halloween in eight of the years on record. items.t: Man charged second time with murder found dead in Huntington County Jail
items.x: HUNTINGTON COUNTY, Ind. (WANE) A man has been found dead in his jail cell after charges related to a 2022 fatal shooting were refiled against him. The Huntington County Coroner announced in a press release that 32-year-old Quantae Jackson was found dead in his jail cell Wednesday morning in the Huntington County Jail. The coroner determined that Jackson's cause of death was asphyxia due to hanging, and his death was ruled a suicide. Man charged second time with murder, attempted murder in 2022 shooting case Jackson was being held in the Huntington County Jail on federal charges, though on Oct. 21, murder and attempted murder charges were refiled after additional witnesses came forward to provide investigators with more evidence. The charges were initially dismissed after prosecutors could not prove "beyond a reasonable doubt' that Jackson was involved in a shooting that killed 27-year-old Calvin Keys and severely injured another. Jackson's death remains under investigation by the Indiana State Police.

items.t: Huntington County Health Department backs effort to delay smartphones for kids
items.x: HUNTINGTON, Ind. (WANE)- The Huntington County Health Department is supporting a national initiative encouraging parents to wait until their children finish 8th grade before giving them a smart phone. The campaign, called Wait Until 8th, aims to reduce pressure on families by encouraging parents at the same school and grade level to make the commitment together. Dr. Matt Pflieger, Huntington County's public health officer, said concerns about mental health, suicide prevention and body image, along with reports of increased anxiety from school counselors and support staff, prompted the department to examine possible contributing factors. Pflieger pointed to research examining connections between smartphone and social media use and children’s mental health. He said waiting gives children more time to develop socially and engage in face-to-face interaction and imaginative play before introducing smartphones and social media. “They have had more face-to-face interactions. They’ve had more time for play-based childhood,” Pflieger said. “At that point, it’s a little easier to introduce how to use technology safely.” Pflieger emphasized that the initiative is not against technology. items.t: Enfranchising the Amish: A state representative helps get out the vote
items.x: NORTHEAST INDIANA (WANE) — Not many Amish people vote, but a local lawmaker is making sure those who want to cast their ballot can. "They're probably never going to take an elected position, but this is a way they can have a voice in this process," said State Representative Joanna King (R), who represents District 49, including much of Elkhart County, an area with an Amish population of about 10%. King also grew up Amish until she was in the third grade. "Deeply concerned": What's driving the Amish vote? Historically, government infringement or participation is not something the Amish want, according to King. Local bishops and church leaders determine the rules each community abides by, so issues like voting differ by area. However, when the pandemic struck in 2020 and those tight-knit communities were told they could not congregate in churches, that struck a chord with Amish everywhere. "I had a lot of phone calls from people saying, Can the government really do this to us?' and that's when they started getting more involved one of the things I told them was Voting is a great way to let your voice be heard.'" items.t: Russell Brand denies all charges as he takes the stand at his rape and sex assault trial
items.x: LONDON (AP) — Russell Brand acknowledged in a London court on Wednesday that he had been obsessed with sex as a younger man, but denied multiple charges of rape and sexual assault , saying the claims have had a “devastating” impact on his life. The British actor-comedian entered Southwark Crown Court alongside his wife, Laura Gallacher, to testify in his own defense, telling reporters that “today is the day for truth and justice.” Brand, 51, stood in the witness box and took the oath, then gave his full name: Russell Edward Brand. He answered “no” to each charge as his lawyer, Ian Winter, asked whether he was guilty of three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault and one count of attempted indecent assault. items.t: Judge orders 30-year prison sentence for key figure in Minnesota food fraud
items.x: MINNEAPOLIS (AP) — A man who played a major role in defrauding a federal food program in Minnesota was sentenced Wednesday to 30 years in prison, the latest punishment in a sprawling scheme to collect millions of dollars during the COVID-19 pandemic by claiming to have fed needy children. The depth of fraud in Minnesota — dozens of people have been convicted — has repeatedly drawn the attention of President Donald Trump, who ridiculed the Democratic governor for failing to stop it and partly cited it as grounds for an extraordinary immigration crackdown in the state's largest cities. Salim Said operated Safari Restaurant in Minneapolis, which specialized in dishes from Somalia. He was accused of vastly overstating the number of meals when seeking payment for providing food. The government said he was responsible for $44 million in fraud, some of which was committed by others he recruited. “You took more than taxpayers' dollars to enrich yourself. You took the reputation of our state down with you,” U.S. District Judge Nancy Brasel said. items.t: Hayden Panettiere death ruled accidental by police in South Carolina
items.x: GREENVILLE, S.C. ( WSPA ) – Police in South Carolina have officially closed the investigation into the death of Hayden Panettiere, according to a Wednesday news release. Greenville Police Department officials said that Panettiere's death has been ruled accidental, based on findings in the investigation and the medical examiner's determination. On August 16, Panettiere was found unresponsive in an apartment at the Judson Mill Lofts on Easley Bridge Road. Police said that Brian Hickerson, Panettiere's on-and-off boyfriend, along with his brother, Zach Hickerson, were at the residence. EMS attempted life-saving measures before pronouncing Panettiere dead at 2:31 p.m. According to the Greenville County Coroner's Office, Panettiere had died from an accidental overdose of fentanyl, 4-ANPP, Alprazolam, Methocarbamol and Quetiapine. Panettiere had spoken openly about challenges in her personal life, including emotional scars from her childhood fame, postpartum depression after giving birth to her daughter, and struggles with alcohol addiction. items.t: Huntington University student film celebrates successful first week in box office
items.x: HUNTINGTON, Ind. (WANE) Student film from Huntington University has solidified new school records after its opening-weekend box office debut. After winning awards at the Heartland International Film Festival, the film made by 40 Huntington University Forester Film students drew packed theaters during its opening weekend starting on Oct. 23. At the Los Angeles festival, the film won the Indiana Narrative Award and the Audience Choice Award. Huntington to Hollywood: Student-led film premiers, wins award in L.A. Titled SENIORS, the film follows a high schooler court-ordered to community service hours at a retirement home and his unlikely friendship with a war veteran. The film features John Rhys-Davies of Lord of the Rings fame and Paris Brosnan. According to a press release from Huntington University, the high attendance at these showings was attributed to word-of-mouth marketing. The distributor of the movie is expanding showtimes through a second week in theaters. More information about SENIORS is available on its website .

items.t: Parole Board announces decision for man convicted of murdering children in Vanderburgh County
items.x: HENDERSON, Ky. (WEHT) The Indiana Parole Board has submitted their recommendation following a clemency hearing with Jeffrey Weisheit, the man convicted of murdering 5-year-old Caleb Lynch and 8-year-old Alyssa Lynch in 2010. Weisheit submitted a request in September to commute his death sentence to a sentence of life in prison without the possibility of parole. The board conducted a hearing earlier this month with Weisheit and the public to provide testimony in favor and against the commutation of his sentence. items.t: Purdue studies cockroach milk for food-based research
items.x: HENDERSON, Ky. (WEHT) Purdue University is looking into the potential for cockroach milk to create food. Ramaswamy Subramanian is a professor in the Department of Biological Sciences and the Weldon School of Biomedical Engineering at Purdue University. Officials say a cockroach found on Hawaii, called the Pacific beetle cockroach, makes a highly nutritious substance that it feeds to its babies. This substance, dubbed "cockroach milk" by scientists, has twice the number of calories per unit weight as the milk from a water buffalo. Study: Indiana No. 1 state in US for blue-collar work Officials note this makes cockroach milk one of the most nutritious substances ever discovered. Cockroach milk is densely packed with nutrients and exists in a crystallized form that slowly releases nutrients to the cockroach embryo as needed. Subramanian believes that with modern genetic engineering, cockroach milk could be used to create high-protein bread that could help feed the world or create stable, high-calorie food that could feed astronauts on future journeys to Mars.

items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war , creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle . items.t: Judge overseeing Maduro trial dies
items.x: ( The Hill ) Alvin Hellerstein, a longtime federal judge who was set to oversee the criminal trial of deposed Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro, has passed away, according to a court official. He was 92. Nominated by then-President Bill Clinton in 1998, Hellerstein oversaw many high-profile disputes during his nearly three decades on the bench in New York City. He was back in the national limelight presiding over the proceedings for Maduro , who was captured and brought to the U.S. earlier this year over accusations of narco-terrorism. Maduro and his wife were in the judge's courtroom less than two weeks ago to plead not guilty to a new set of criminal charges. Before the Maduro operation, Hellerstein had long clashed with President Donald Trump in court. The judge at one point agreed that Trump’s fixer-turned-foe, Michael Cohen, could be released from prison to home confinement. Cohen has cast his prosecution as retribution by Trump. The weapon, called the Active Denial System and commonly known as a “heat ray,” is designed to repel people by directing an invisible beam of electromagnetic energy at them. items.x: NEW YORK (AP) — U.S. stocks are drifting Wednesday as the countdown ticks toward this afternoon’s announcement from the Federal Reserve on what it will do with interest rates . The S&P 500 rose 0.2% and pulled within 1% of its all-time high , which was set earlier this month. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 176 points, or 0.3%, as of 11:45 a.m. Eastern time, and the Nasdaq composite was virtually unchanged. The day’s highlight will likely be what the Federal Reserve says, if anything, about where interest rates are heading. The Fed raised its main interest rate last month for the first time in three years in hopes of slowing the high inflation that’s squeezing the economy and discouraging Americans . The widespread expectation on Wall Street is that the Fed will leave the federal funds rate alone at this meeting, and the question is whether it will give hints about what may happen at later meetings. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh, though, has been adamant since taking over the Fed about wanting it to give fewer indications about its future moves. I'm a constitutional attorney. We're going to follow the Constitution. The Constitution says when a state certifies the election of members of Congress, then they are administered the oath. That's what I'll be doing on January 3 to everybody who's there,” the speaker added. Officials in states throughout the country have recently played defense against election fraud claims from President Trump, with the president doubling down ahead of this year’s midterms. The Arkansas-based retailer unveiled its "Holiday Meal Basket" on Wednesday, saying it can feed 10 for $35, the most affordable price since Walmart began offering such a deal. It's about $5 cheaper than last year's basket and includes six additional items. "The Holiday Meal Basket has become one of our favorite traditions at Walmart. This year's basket includes a Butterball turkey (selling for 97 cents per pound and estimated at 13.5 lbs), Stove Top stuffing, dinner rolls, and ingredients for other holiday meal staples like sweet potato casserole and pumpkin pie, according to Walmart. items.t: 68 dead in high-speed train collision, Spain’s 2nd deadly rail crash this year
items.x: URDA, Spain (AP) — A high-speed train slammed into another that had stopped on the tracks in Spain on Wednesday, killing at least 68 people and injuring dozens in the second deadly rail collision this year. The regional government of Castilla La Mancha confirmed the death toll and said another 58 people were receiving medical treatment at hospitals. Rescue workers searched the wreckage through the day for survivors and bodies. The collision came just nine months after another deadly crash involving high-speed trains operated by the same two companies in southern Spain in January. “Today all of Spain is grieving,” Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said from the crash site, where he announced that his government would declare three days of national mourning. items.t: Flying taxis could carry passengers by 2030
items.x: (TestMiles) A British aerospace company has demonstrated an electric flying taxi that could eventually offer a new way to escape crowded city roads. The Flying Car Is Moving Beyond Science Fiction Los Angeles has spent decades trying to solve its traffic problems. Freeways expand, transit systems improve, and technology promises more efficient journeys. Yet travelling across the city can still take a remarkable amount of time. A British aerospace company believes part of the solution might be above the roads rather than on them. Vertical Aerospace has demonstrated an electric aircraft capable of taking off vertically, transitioning into conventional forward flight, and landing without a runway. The technology was publicly displayed at the Farnborough International Airshow in Britain, marking an important development in the company's plans to introduce commercial passenger flights. The aircraft is part of a growing category known as electric vertical takeoff and landing, or eVTOL. Unlike a conventional airplane, it does not require a runway for every departure. items.t: Final Honor Flight Northeast Indiana of 2026 takes veterans to Washington
items.x: FORT WAYNE, Ind. (WANE)— The final Honor Flight of 2026 took off Wednesday. Honor Flight Northeast Indiana has taken 4,495 veterans to Washington, D.C. The 59th flight has 85 veterans; two from the Cold War, 80 from the Vietnam War and three who served during other conflicts. When the flight landed, singer Lee Greenwood surprised the group with a quick rendition of "God Bless the USA." Organizers said he happened to be at the airport; he then made his way to the plane and sang the chorus over the speakerphone. "Welcome to the capital of the United States," Greenwood said. "It's free because of your service." Veterans are spending the day touring the monuments and memorials dedicated to their service. Veterans can apply online to be on a future flight. The public is invited to the welcome home on Wednesday at the Fort Wayne International Airport. People are asked to arrive at 8 p.m. and park in long-term parking.

items.t: Warming up again as Halloween approaches
items.x: More low clouds and patchy fog greeted some of us this morning, with most of the grey skies and lower visibility in the chillier locations to the west. All of that has cleared out, and plenty of sunshine is on tap for the rest of the day. We're warming up thanks to all of this sunshine, with only the foggiest locations from this morning lagging behind a bit. Highs will reach the low 70s for most of us, and it will be calm with high pressure still locked in. Calm winds and clear skies will remain in place tonight, but fog isn't likely with less moisture in the air and lows staying milder in the low to mid-50s. Friday is still setting up as the warmest day of the week, even as a dry cold front comes through. Cooler air will eventually roll in behind the front for the start of the weekend, but it will take some time. So, in the meantime, highs will hit the mid-to-upper 70s tomorrow under sunny skies. Breezy winds of 10-20 mph will be in the mix, but they won't impact the warmth. We will only top out in the mid-60s for Halloween as the cooler air settles in, but we'll still have enough sunshine that it should feel comfortable.
