items.t: Laopakdee takes lead in bid for second Masters invitation
items.x: TOMARATA, New Zealand – A year after a historic breakthrough at the Asia-Pacific Amateur Championship, defending champion Fifa Laopakdee picked up where he left off with an eight-under 63 to take a three-stroke lead over New Zealand’s Joshua Bai after the first round at Te Arai Links’ South Course. Laopakdee, now a senior at Arizona State University, became the first player from Thailand to win the Asia-Pacific Amateur last fall with a victory on the third playoff hole in Dubai. He went on to compete in the Masters and The Open earlier this year before returning to defend his title at the 17th edition of the Asia-Pacific Amateur this week. “Couldn't ask for a better way to start the round,” said Laopakdee. “Before it started, I knew it was going to be windy out there and it was going to be tough… Eight under wasn’t on my bingo card today, but I was able to pull it off and it feels amazing.” Fifa Laopakdee of Thailand plays a tee stroke during the first round of the 2026 Asia-Pacific Amateur Championship being played at the Te Arai Links, South Course in Auckland, New Zealand on Thursday 29 October 2026. items.t: 76-year-old man dies in I-295 crash after SUV crashed into wooded area
items.x: WASHINGTON ( DC News Now ) D.C. police said an SUV driver died after he lost control and crashed into a wooded area off of Interstate 295. The deadly collision happened minutes after 12:30 p.m. on Oct. 26 near Exit 2. When officers arrived on the scene, they found a Toyota 4Runner in an embankment and the driver, Baldwin Rudolph Robertson, unresponsive. Robertson died at the scene. DC police shoot armed man in parking lot on Minnesota Avenue: MPD The Metropolitan Police Department's investigation revealed that Robertson was driving the 4Runner North on I-295 at an "accelerated speed." He then reportedly lost control of the SUV and struck a guardrail. Police said the impact of the collision launched the SUV into the woods, where it landed against a tree. No other vehicles were involved in the crash. The collision remains under investigation. Anyone with information about the collision is asked to call 202-727-9099 or text MPD at 50411.

The challenge, according to police, involved one of the men giving another a haircut "in the center of the road" on State Route 200 in Ocala. The third suspect was filming the stunt, authorities say. In a Facebook post, the Ocala Police Department explained that the young men — ages 20, 19 and 18 — had removed a chair from a nearby restaurant to use during the challenge. But while the 18-year-old was seated and getting his hair cut, a traffic accident nearby sent a Chevrolet 3500 in their direction. The two other suspects were able to move out of the way, but the 18-year-old "was seated with his back to the oncoming truck" and was hit by the vehicle. items.t: Democrats see battleground map expand to South Carolina, Florida, Mississippi
items.x: Democrats are giddy about the possibility of a bigger blue wave than expected in the battle for the Senate as polls show that South Carolina , Florida and Mississippi — three seats that were long seen as safe Republican holds — are now competitive races. Democrats view the Republican candidates running in those states as mediocre political talents who must fight historic headwinds caused by President Trump’s unpopularity, voter anger over inflation and the war in Iran, and burgeoning Democratic voter enthusiasm. The Senate battleground map has steadily expanded throughout the 2026 midterm election cycle as political handicappers have shifted seats that were thought to be in solidly Republican territory — such as Alaska, Iowa, Kansas and Texas — to the “toss-up" category. But now Republicans have to worry about losing Senate seats in states that were unthinkable as realistic Democratic pickup opportunities at the start of the election cycle, most notably South Carolina, which last elected a Democrat, Fritz Hollings, to the Senate in 1998. items.t: West Virginia #9 for grocery store shoplifting incidents in United States
items.x: WEST VIRGINIA (WTRF) — West Virginia had the ninth-highest rate of reported grocery store shoplifting incidents in the country, according to an analysis by H&P Law . The state recorded 6,350 incidents from 2021 through 2025, averaging 1,270 per year. That equals 71.64 incidents for every 100,000 residents. The analysis used FBI Crime Data Explorer figures and U.S. Census Bureau population estimates. West Virginia’s number of incidents rose 42.7% between the first and final years studied. Kentucky recorded a 25.4% increase during the same period. The state’s rate was 2.4 times Pennsylvania’s rate of 29.50 incidents per 100,000 people. West Virginia also ranked above Ohio at 61.52 and Virginia at 60.22. New Mexico ranked first with 156.53 incidents per 100,000 residents, more than twice West Virginia’s rate. Now, the West Virginia State Police Cold Case Task Force is opening its own investigation into the devastating event now known as the "Prom Night Murders." According to a press release from the West Virginia Senate, the teens attended the Huntington High School Prom in 2005 before they were shot and killed later that night in front of a Huntington residence. The victims were Megan Poston, 16; Michael Dillon, 17; Eddrick Clark, 18; and Donté Ward, 19. items.t: AG McCuskey suing TikTok ‘for putting West Virginia kids at risk’
items.x: CHARLESTON, W.Va. (WBOY) — Attorney General JB McCuskey announced in a press release Thursday that he has filed a lawsuit against popular social media app TikTok. McCuskey alleges that TikTok "violated numerous West Virginia consumer protection laws through the design and operation of its app, ultimately harming kids." TikTok created a platform that puts West Virginia kids at risk by encouraging continuous use, targeting younger users with its recommendation systems that select what content children see, and failing to disclose safety gaps to parents and caregivers. The Consumer Protection Division of the Attorney General’s Office conducted testing using one account registered to an adult and another to a 13-year-old girl. The testing identified notable differences in the content delivered to each account: the child account repeatedly received sexually suggestive content while the adult account largely received content focused on ordinary interests like home improvement and local restaurants." items.t: AAA advises drivers about daylight saving time
items.x: ( WAVY ) – It's only a few days until we trade one extra hour of sleep for months of darkness as we leave work to drive home. And even though we're on the easier end of the time transition (from daylight saving time to standard time), the switch still takes its toll. Nexstar's WAVY went to AAA Tidewater Virginia to see what commuters can expect. "Well, the biggest thing for drivers will be the change in daylight when we leave work or school," said Holly Dalby with AAA. "At the end of the day, gone will be the bright sunshine, and we will find ourselves either driving into the glare from the setting sun or driving home in the dark. So it's a time to be particularly careful on the roads." Days will get way shorter in November: How much daylight we’ll lose While lawmakers have tried to get rid of the time switch altogether, it doesn't appear to be going anywhere anytime soon, so your circadian rhythm will have to dance to a different beat for a while. "It just messing with our sleep schedule can really add to our fatigue very quickly. And when we're fatigued, we can make mistakes," Dalby said. items.t: RFK Jr. eases access to unproven peptides despite opposition from FDA scientists
items.x: WASHINGTON (AP) — The Trump administration on Wednesday acted to ease access to unproven peptide drugs favored by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr . Food and Drug Administration scientific staffers had little input on the decision and opposed the changes, according to six people familiar with its development. The draft policy posted online by Kennedy’s Department of Health and Human Services covers a handful of injectable peptides promoted within the wellness industry for uses such as building muscle, healing injuries and boosting energy. The government will take comments for two weeks before finalizing the measure. The document, primarily written by officials at HHS, faced overwhelming pushback among FDA drug staffers who warned it could undermine the agency’s long-standing mission of keeping unsafe health products off the U.S. market, according to the people familiar with its development. items.t: ‘Gut punch’: 2 college students found dead in Colorado after going missing on mountain hike
items.x: ( WJW ) – Two missing Colorado college students were found dead Wednesday after they left campus for a weekend trip up a nearly 14,000-foot peak and encountered a heavy snowstorm, police said. Kaden Matsuda, 19, from Ridgway, Colorado, and Jackson Donlon, 20, from New York, left Colorado Mountain College Leadville’s campus on Friday and didn’t return. They told family and friends they planned to go up Ice Mountain, which requires technical climbing, according to the county sheriff’s office. On Wednesday night, the sheriff's office confirmed that the students were found dead around 3:30 p.m. in a basin of the West Apostle Mountain. Authorities do not believe foul play was involved. The investigation is now being handled by the Chaffee County Coroner’s Office. “Our heart aches for Kaden and Jackson’s family and friends. We are very proud of our team’s efforts to find them before this weekend’s coming storm," Sheriff Andy Rohrich wrote on Facebook. "Although this is a gut punch, our prayers were answered that we would find Kaden and Jackson, allowing some closure for the family. items.t: Cruise ship passenger says warning signs were there long before Cambodia

Now, she says she doesn't expect to see that money again. Asked if they will get it back, she said, "No, no, no, no." items.x: DoorDash is gobbling up Instacart in a $17 billion acquisition that will supercharge its grocery delivery business. DoorDash said the Instacart brand name and app will remain, and Instacart shoppers can continue fulfilling orders for Instacart. Grocers can also choose to work with Instacart or DoorDash. Instacart customers will now have access to 50,000 additional stores covered by DoorDash, the company said. Instacart, founded in 2012, specializes in grocery and convenience store delivery in the U.S. and Canada. Its 600,000 “shoppers” — who are independent contractors — completed 338 million orders last year, according to company filings. Instacart has a market value of $14 billion. items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: ( The Hill ) Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. US stocks hold steady as the countdown ticks to a Federal Reserve decision on interest rates The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. Gasoline and energy costs have risen in six of nine months this year, as the Iran war sparked oil price shocks via the Islamic Republic's restrictions on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. items.t: Wendy’s gets buyout offer while struggling with beef prices and growing competition
items.x: Wendy’s shares jumped more than 14% Wednesday after noted investor Nelson Peltz made an offer to buy the chain, which has been struggling with high beef prices and aging stores. Peltz’s Trian Fund Management and several partners are offering Wendy’s $7.35 per share in cash, or a premium of nearly 19% over the stock’s closing price on Tuesday, in a deal that would take the company private. The offer values Wendy's at $1.4 billion. Trader Joe’s Thanksgiving items are already hitting the shelves Wendy's, which is based in Dublin, Ohio, confirmed receipt of the unsolicited proposal in a statement Wednesday and said its board has formed an independent committee to evaluate it. At the end of last year, Wendy's had 5,969 restaurants in the U.S. and 1,428 outlets in 38 countries. Wendy's, founded in 1969 by Dave Thomas and named after his daughter, is known for its square burgers and Frosty desserts. The fast-growing chain introduced the drive-thru window in 1970 and went public in 1976. In the 1980s, as it jockeyed for sales with McDonald's and Burger King, Wendy's launched salad bars and ran its iconic “Where's the beef?” ad campaign. items.t: Obama knocks Trump’s response to Cheesecake Factory jab: ‘These are not serious people’
items.x: ( The Hill ) Former President Obama on Wednesday responded to uproar over a recent campaign trail jab at President Trump’s White House decorations, slamming Republicans for focusing more on the joke than on the economy. “They mobilized a whole-of-government response to that joke, not to inflation, but to that joke,” Obama said during a campaign rally in Georgia. “This is what I mean when I say these are not serious people. They don't have solutions to actual problems, so they'd rather have the media and you talking about the Cheesecake Factory.” Obama had quipped during a recent campaign stop in Cleveland, Ohio, that Trump’s taste in renovations worth a reported $900 million has the White House “looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory, it’s just gold everywhere,” referring to the Iraqi palaces that were famously adorned with gold decor. items.t: Screwworm detected in dog in El Paso County
items.x: EL PASO, Texas (Border Report) The number of active New World screwworm cases rose to 18 on Wednesday, with several counties reporting their first case, including the populous El Paso County, Texas. According to the USDA, the five latest confirmed screwworm cases involved four dogs and a cat. Cochise County, Arizona, reported its first screwworm case on Wednesday, the first in that state. Texas state Rep. Mary Gonzalez, D-El Paso, issued a statement saying the screwworm was detected in a dog in the town of Socorro. She said her office has been in communication with the appropriate state agencies and will continue to monitor the situation. She urged the public to check on their pets and monitor them closely. Screwworm spreads to US wildlife in Texas, USDA says "It is important that members of our community stay vigilant and go to their veterinarians if they believe their animal may have been impacted," she said. The border county of Luna, New Mexico, also confirmed its first screwworm case in a cow on Monday. The New World screwworm is a parasitic fly that lays eggs in open wounds. items.t: After two-year search, woman’s coworker turns out to be a match for kidney transplant
items.x: SALT LAKE CITY, Utah ( ABC4 ) — Katie Hood and Reina Child became fast friends five years ago when they met as coworkers at Charlie's Produce in Salt Lake City. Then two years ago, Katie, 41, was diagnosed with renal failure. Family, friends and even coworkers began getting tested to see if they were a match. Reina, 47, knew she needed to be tested. And guess what? She is a perfect match. Now, the bond the two ladies share will grow even stronger because on Tuesday they're scheduled for kidney transplant surgery. The women had a pre-operation appointment today ahead of their surgery next Tuesday. "She's an inspiration to so many because even though she's struggling, she's smiles and laughs with you," Reina said about Katie. It all started in October 2024. "I had been really swollen for a while, and it got to the point where walking upstairs was just hard," explained Katie. She decided to go to the doctor, which led to an emergency room visit. That visit changed Katie's life. She was diagnosed with heart and kidney failure. "And I've been doing dialysis for three times a week for two years and yeah, just kind of on this crazy journey." items.t: Tuch scores 2 more goals, Capitals beat Flyers 5-2
items.x: WASHINGTON (AP) — Alex Tuch scored his eighth and ninth goals in his first season with Washington, the second into an empty net to help the Capitals seal a 5-2 victory over the Philadelphia Flyers on Wednesday night. Tuch arrived in a trade from Buffalo and signed an eight-year, $84-million contract extension in June. On Wednesday, he became only the second player in Capitals history to score at least nine goals in his first 11 games for the team, joining Dino Ciccarelli, who scored 12 times in his first 11 Caps appearances to close the 1988-89 season. Jordan Kyrou also scored twice, and Aliaksei Protas added his first goal of the season as Washington completed a five-game homestand with four wins. Dylan Strome had three assists, and Jack St. Ivany and Pierre-Luc Dubois each had two. Logan Thompson made 23 saves after missing a victory Saturday against Buffalo because of a lower-body injury. Matvei Michkov scored his ninth goal of the season and fifth on the power play for Philadelphia, which lost its third straight after an overtime defeat to visiting Columbus on Tuesday night. "Sounds like a great idea to me," said Greg Biro. "What I can tell is it looks like they're obviously pretty invasive." Police and city leaders announced the cancellation of the program that's been in place since 2023, during Tuesday night's city council meeting. "I think it's a good idea, man," said Timothy Palmer. "You know, Flock cameras get a lot of people in trouble." Alexandria police release map of 61 Flock camera locations amid public scrutiny Alexandria joins the Fairfax County Board of Supervisors, the Arlington County School Board, and the Fairfax County School Board that have banned Flock cameras. "I don't know what they're supposed to be doing, to be honest with you," Palmer said. "I guess catch people speeding and things of that nature. But they're just in the way." City staff will go before the city council Nov. 10 as they begin discussions about the use of other surveillance technology. But even that has people concerned. items.t: DOJ’s California ballot fight rejected by another judge
items.x: ( The Hill ) The Trump administration's bid to separate 20,000 mail ballots in California that it says are likely noncitizens met another defeat on Wednesday as a trial judge refused to intervene. U.S. District Judge David Carter ruled California can continue to accept the questioned ballots like any other. “This request violates longstanding constitutional principles mandating that states have control over their elections,” Carter wrote. “If Plaintiff’s last-minute request for relief were granted, either party could create chaos for their own political purposes to disrupt the election process,” he continued. “Over 20,000 registered Californians would potentially lose the right that generations of Americans have fought to preserve.” California has raised eyebrows at the veracity of the administration's list and says it's not obligated to verify voters’ citizenship in response. The state has conceded it's not feasible to segregate a ballot once it's processed. It would be counted even if later found to be fraudulent. The Mountaineers used a 26-3 run in the second half to bust open a 43-point lead with five minutes to play. “I thought we really started guarding the ball better and put them in tough positions,” WVU coach Ross Hodge said. “They challenged us in some unique ways early to start the game. We haven’t played against a true five-out team.” The Cardinals shot the ball well in the first half, particularly early on. Wheeling made eight of its first 16 shots and 11 of its first 23. The alleged recruitment strategy emerged during Operation Southbound Takedown, an investigation that has resulted in charges against 13 people and the recovery of 29 vehicles worth approximately $1.14 million. U.S Attorney Justin Simmons said the international ports of entry in El Paso are major crossing points for stolen vehicles from across the country. (Aracely Lazcano/Border Report) Eleven defendants are U.S. citizens. The other two are Mexican citizens — one a lawful permanent resident and the other a border crossing cardholder, according to federal prosecutors. items.t: Report: Off-duty border agent allegedly stabs, kills wife
items.x: EL PASO, Texas (Border Report) An off-duty U.S. Border Patrol agent allegedly stabbed and killed his wife early Wednesday morning in Laredo, Texas, according to the Laredo Morning Times. The newspaper reported that Abel Garza, 30, is charged with murder in the death of his wife, 28-year-old Mayra Alejandra Landeros. The newspaper also reported that U.S. Customs and Border Protection confirmed that Garza is a U.S. Border Patrol agent with the Laredo Sector, and that the agency’s Office of Professional Responsibility is reviewing the incident.

items.t: Religious, community leaders urge voters to help end hunger in Rio Grande Valley
items.x: McALLEN, Texas (Border Report) The Humanitarian Respite Center in McAllen used to help thousands of migrants who crossed the border during the Biden administration. But since Trump took over it has largely been empty. But on Wednesday dozens of faith-based and community leaders were at the center to speak out against hunger and food insecurities that are plaguing this South Texas border region. And to urge voters to elect leaders who will help. “In this election year Bread for the World is urging people of faith to vote to end hunger," Felipe Salinas of the Christian-based nonprofit group Bread for the World told the group. He says there are too many people in the region who cannot afford food for their families and he believes more public assistance is needed by the government. “It is very much a policy choice because for every meal a food bank or food pantry provides, the federally-funded Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, or SNAP, provides 9. items.t: Commanders are feeling urgency to play a complete game as they enter an important stretch
items.x: ASHBURN, Va. (AP) — The Commanders have played six games so far this year. Yet it feels like their season could be on the line Sunday against the Eagles. After a bye week, the Commanders say there's a sense of urgency to improve quickly. If Washington doesn't start winning soon, the season could slip away far earlier than players or coaches anticipated. “Sometimes I’ll go big picture — in this case, it was just three weeks,” coach Dan Quinn said of team meetings this week. “I started the meeting Monday, ‘This is the next three weeks. items.t: Harris advises Democrats against attempting to impeach Trump
items.x: ( The Hill ) Former Vice President Kamala Harris on Tuesday urged Democrats against making a third attempt to impeach President Trump if they win back the House after next week's midterm elections. "I think that going in the direction of impeachment is not a good idea, just to be honest with you," Harris told MeidasTouch's Aaron Parnas in an interview. "Just because we have limited resources and I think the energy and the resources need to put into accountability, need to be put into investigations." "And that's where the time should be spent," she added. "Remember, I was in the Senate for the last go-around, and the votes aren't there. "So, that's how I feel. But also, I think after the election, we all have to just also agree that our attitude has to be to get stuff done." Harris said Democrats should be "uncompromising" and "not sit around, you know, being genteel about the relationships," but maintain accountability when it comes to cuts to healthcare and oversight on the Iran war. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 176 points, or 0.3%, as of 11:45 a.m. Eastern time, and the Nasdaq composite was virtually unchanged. The day’s highlight will likely be what the Federal Reserve says, if anything, about where interest rates are heading. The Fed raised its main interest rate last month for the first time in three years in hopes of slowing the high inflation that’s squeezing the economy and discouraging Americans . The widespread expectation on Wall Street is that the Fed will leave the federal funds rate alone at this meeting, and the question is whether it will give hints about what may happen at later meetings. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh, though, has been adamant since taking over the Fed about wanting it to give fewer indications about its future moves. items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war , creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle . items.t: Councilmember Robert White faces challenge in election for DC delegate
items.x: WASHINGTON ( DC News Now ) At-Large Councilmember Robert White (D) is facing a hurdle in the election to become Washington, D.C.'s next congressional delegate and could be ineligible for the role. White is predicted to win the race and assume the seat of longtime DC Delegate Eleanor Holmes Norton. Norton, a veteran of the Civil Rights Movement, has been the sole representative of the residents of the nation’s capital in Congress since 1991. Despite the likelihood that White could win, he may be ineligible for delegate unless he resigns from council. DC early voting begins: What to know before heading to the polls According to the District of Columbia Delegate Act , which was signed into law in 1970, a congressional delegate candidate may not hold any other paid public office at the time of their election. The statute also states that the individual can forfeit their office upon failure to maintain the qualifications. White has held a seat in the D.C. Council since 2016. He chairs the Council's Committee on Housing. With early voting underway and Election Day days away, White's next steps are unclear. The regional government of Castilla La Mancha confirmed the death toll and said another 58 people were receiving medical treatment at hospitals. Rescue workers searched the wreckage through the day for survivors and bodies. The Flying Car Is Moving Beyond Science Fiction Los Angeles has spent decades trying to solve its traffic problems. Freeways expand, transit systems improve, and technology promises more efficient journeys. Yet travelling across the city can still take a remarkable amount of time. A British aerospace company believes part of the solution might be above the roads rather than on them. Vertical Aerospace has demonstrated an electric aircraft capable of taking off vertically, transitioning into conventional forward flight, and landing without a runway. The technology was publicly displayed at the Farnborough International Airshow in Britain, marking an important development in the company's plans to introduce commercial passenger flights. The aircraft is part of a growing category known as electric vertical takeoff and landing, or eVTOL. Unlike a conventional airplane, it does not require a runway for every departure. items.t: Patchy AM fog to partly sunny Wednesday afternoon
items.x: Some patchy morning fog will greet us as we head out Wednesday morning before it gives way to a partly sunny Wednesday afternoon. It will make for some gorgeous photos, though with the fall foliage across the region and maybe even a bit spooky (on theme with Halloween right around the corner). We'll see highs on Wednesday reach into the mid to upper 60s while Thursday and Friday bring a late-week warmup. Highs on Thursday are back into the lower 70s under plenty of sunshine while Friday will be the warmest day out of the 7-day with highs into the mid to upper 70s, also under mainly sunny skies. We're back to around 70 on Halloween thanks to a dry cold front. We'll have increasing clouds though on Saturday ahead of our next weather maker that will bring our next best chance for rain later in the day on Sunday. Showers are back in the forecast as we start off the first week of November and highs are nearly back to normal, into the mid to upper 60s.

items.t: Utah authorities connect 1974 cold case to serial killer Ted Bundy
items.x: SUMMIT COUNTY, Utah ( KTVX ) — Investigators in Summit County, Utah closed the 1974 cold case homicide of Melissa Ann Smith Tuesday, linking her murder to prominent serial killer Ted Bundy. Using DNA and other evidence, the Summit County Sheriff's Office and Summit County Attorney's Office formally closed the cold-case murder, saying that the evidence conclusively proves that Ted Bundy murdered 17-year-old Melissa Ann Smith. Bundy has long been considered a suspect in several cold cases in Utah, and Smith's murder was one of them. Hunters found her remains in Summit County on Oct. 27, 1974, 52 years ago today. "The work began with the investigators who handled the case in 1974, and it continued through the dedication and perseverance of those who carried it forward," Summit County Sheriff Kacey Bates said. "After 50 years, we have reached a point that so many have worked toward." Democrats view the Republican candidates running in those states as mediocre political talents who must fight historic headwinds caused by President Trump’s unpopularity, voter anger over inflation and the war in Iran, and burgeoning Democratic voter enthusiasm. The Senate battleground map has steadily expanded throughout the 2026 midterm election cycle as political handicappers have shifted seats that were thought to be in solidly Republican territory — such as Alaska, Iowa, Kansas and Texas — to the “toss-up" category. In January 2022, the victim was hospitalized due to a medical event after a fire broke out at his home on Brinkman Avenue in Buffalo. Mayor Sean Ryan announced plans for a new Buffalo Animal Shelter on Thursday at 294 Louisiana St. as part of a $30 million project. The plan will need approval from the Buffalo Common Council as part of its annual budget. "Choosing the site is a major milestone, but that’s just the start of the journey," Ryan said. "It’s a major investment in the city of Buffalo, it’s a major investment in animal care, but it’s all subject to council approval. But we spent the time on this to get it right." The plan calls for planning in 2027, design work in 2027 and 2028, and construction in 2028 and 2029 though officials said the goal was to have the project completed by the end of 2028. Located near Father Conway Park as well as the proposed Seneca Nation One Stop gas station that is currently under dispute and undergoing construction on Miami Street the city plans on redeveloping and expanding the former police precinct so it can better take care of the animals it serves. items.t: Dartmouth official resigns over AI use
items.x: ( The Hill ) A top Dartmouth official has resigned from his position after allegations that he violated the school's AI use policy. The university announced Wednesday that Provost Santiago Schnell resigned from his position after a university committee released the results of its investigation into the matter it opened in September. "The Provost used AI to meaningfully alter his writing in violation of at least one publication’s AI use and/or disclosure requirement, failed to disclose his use of AI in clear violation of a national newspaper’s stated policy, was not forthcoming about his AI use, and fell short of the standards set forth by Dartmouth’s Code of Ethical Conduct, the Academic Honor Principle, and Geisel’s Policy on Expectations for Professionalism for Faculty, Non-Faculty Academics, and Staff," the committee concluded. Schnell was accused of using AI to alter his work by the student newspaper The Dartmouth and outlet Semafor, specifically pointing to an opinion piece the provost wrote for The Washington Post. items.t: Global manufacturer opens $319M facility in Genesee County
items.x: BUFFALO, N.Y. (WIVB) Construction is complete on a multimillion-dollar facility in Genesee County for global manufacturer Edwards Vacuum, which officials say will help strengthen the state's semiconductor supply chain. The $319 million manufacturing facility is located in the Town of Alabama. Leaders said it has the capacity to produce 10,000 dry pumps each year. “Edwards’ decision to choose New York means hundreds of good-paying jobs and millions of dollars in investment in the Upstate economy while helping to strengthen our domestic semiconductor supply chain and ensuring that New York remains a global hub of innovation and the epicenter of semiconductor manufacturing nationwide,” Gov. Kathy Hochul said in a release. The company said it will reduce carbon dioxide emissions and serve U.S. customers faster by expanding operations in New York State. Edwards Vacuum was founded in London and operates as part of the Atlas Copco Group, based in Sweden. items.t: AAA advises drivers about daylight saving time
items.x: ( WAVY ) – It's only a few days until we trade one extra hour of sleep for months of darkness as we leave work to drive home. And even though we're on the easier end of the time transition (from daylight saving time to standard time), the switch still takes its toll. Nexstar's WAVY went to AAA Tidewater Virginia to see what commuters can expect. "Well, the biggest thing for drivers will be the change in daylight when we leave work or school," said Holly Dalby with AAA. "At the end of the day, gone will be the bright sunshine, and we will find ourselves either driving into the glare from the setting sun or driving home in the dark. So it's a time to be particularly careful on the roads." Days will get way shorter in November: How much daylight will we lose? While lawmakers have tried to get rid of the time switch altogether, it doesn't appear to be going anywhere anytime soon, so your circadian rhythm will have to dance to a different beat for a while. "It just messing with our sleep schedule can really add to our fatigue very quickly. And when we're fatigued, we can make mistakes," Dalby said. items.t: ‘Gut punch’: 2 college students found dead in Colorado after going missing on mountain hike
items.x: ( WJW ) – Two missing Colorado college students were found dead Wednesday after they left campus for a weekend trip up a nearly 14,000-foot peak and encountered a heavy snowstorm, police said. Kaden Matsuda, 19, from Ridgway, Colorado, and Jackson Donlon, 20, from New York, left Colorado Mountain College Leadville’s campus on Friday and didn’t return. They told family and friends they planned to go up Ice Mountain, which requires technical climbing, according to the county sheriff’s office. On Wednesday night, the sheriff's office confirmed that the students were found dead around 3:30 p.m. in a basin of the West Apostle Mountain. Authorities do not believe foul play was involved. The investigation is now being handled by the Chaffee County Coroner’s Office. “Our heart aches for Kaden and Jackson’s family and friends. We are very proud of our team’s efforts to find them before this weekend’s coming storm," Sheriff Andy Rohrich wrote on Facebook. "Although this is a gut punch, our prayers were answered that we would find Kaden and Jackson, allowing some closure for the family. items.t: Cruise ship passenger says warning signs were there long before Cambodia
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — Kit Cassingham and her husband, Randy, sold their home and nearly everything they owned to live aboard a cruise ship for years. Now, she says she doesn't expect to see that money again. Cassingham told NewsNation's Jesse Weber on Wednesday that the couple paid about $370,000 to $380,000 for their cabin on the Villa Vie Odyssey, plus $7,000 a month in expenses. Asked if they will get it back, she said, "No, no, no, no." Cruise ship suspends voyage over fuel costs, stranding 200 passengers More than 200 passengers were told Tuesday to leave the Odyssey in Cambodia within hours after the cruise company suspended operations. In a news release , Villa Vie blamed soaring fuel costs tied to the war in Iran, saying the monthly fuel cost per cabin jumped from about $1,800 to as much as $8,000. Villa Vie Odyssey: How did passengers find out they had to leave? Cassingham and her husband had already gotten off the ship for a hotel so they could work online when a short message arrived saying the ship couldn't get more fuel . “You have till two o’clock to get off the ship,” she said. items.t: Wendy’s gets buyout offer while struggling with beef prices and growing competition
items.x: Wendy’s shares jumped more than 14% Wednesday after noted investor Nelson Peltz made an offer to buy the chain, which has been struggling with high beef prices and aging stores. Peltz’s Trian Fund Management and several partners are offering Wendy’s $7.35 per share in cash, or a premium of nearly 19% over the stock’s closing price on Tuesday, in a deal that would take the company private. The offer values Wendy's at $1.4 billion. Wendy's, which is based in Dublin, Ohio, confirmed receipt of the unsolicited proposal in a statement Wednesday and said its board has formed an independent committee to evaluate it. At the end of last year, Wendy's had 5,969 restaurants in the U.S. and 1,428 outlets in 38 countries. Wendy's, founded in 1969 by Dave Thomas and named after his daughter, is known for its square burgers and Frosty desserts. The fast-growing chain introduced the drive-thru window in 1970 and went public in 1976. In the 1980s, as it jockeyed for sales with McDonald's and Burger King, Wendy's launched salad bars and ran its iconic “Where's the beef?” ad campaign. items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: ( The Hill ) Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. Gasoline and energy costs have risen in six of nine months this year, as the Iran war sparked oil price shocks via the Islamic Republic's restrictions on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Persistent inflation , which has remained above the Fed's 2 percent target for five-and-a-half years, spurred central bank officials to hike interest rates by a quarter point in mid-September. items.t: DoorDash to buy Instacart in $17 billion grocery delivery deal
items.x: DoorDash is gobbling up Instacart in a $17 billion acquisition that will supercharge its grocery delivery business. DoorDash said the Instacart brand name and app will remain, and Instacart shoppers can continue fulfilling orders for Instacart. Grocers can also choose to work with Instacart or DoorDash. Instacart customers will now have access to 50,000 additional stores covered by DoorDash, the company said. Instacart, founded in 2012, specializes in grocery and convenience store delivery in the U.S. and Canada. Its 600,000 “shoppers” — who are independent contractors — completed 338 million orders last year, according to company filings. Instacart has a market value of $14 billion. DoorDash, founded in San Francisco in 2013, began as a restaurant delivery business but has expanded to pet food and electronics. Operating in 40 countries, it completed more than 3 billion orders last year using a network of 9 million independent delivery workers. It has a market value of $73 billion. DoorDash began delivering groceries in 2020 amid a surge in pandemic-era demand. Grocers were initially cautious. items.t: RFK Jr. eases access to unproven peptides despite opposition from FDA scientists
items.x: WASHINGTON (AP) — The Trump administration on Wednesday acted to ease access to unproven peptide drugs favored by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr . Food and Drug Administration scientific staffers had little input on the decision and opposed the changes, according to six people familiar with its development. The draft policy posted online by Kennedy’s Department of Health and Human Services covers a handful of injectable peptides promoted within the wellness industry for uses such as building muscle, healing injuries and boosting energy. The government will take comments for two weeks before finalizing the measure. The document, primarily written by officials at HHS, faced overwhelming pushback among FDA drug staffers who warned it could undermine the agency’s long-standing mission of keeping unsafe health products off the U.S. market, according to the people familiar with its development. Bam Adebayo also had 24 points and grabbed nine rebounds for the Heat, who lost their first four games after acquiring Antetokounmpo from Milwaukee in the offseason. Adebayo passed Udonis Haslem to become the Heat's career leader in rebounds . Andrew Wiggins scored 18 points and Pelle Larsson had 17 points, eight assists and six rebounds for the Heat, who shot 53% from the field and had a whopping 70 points in the paint. Rookie Kingston Flemings and Nickeil Alexander-Walker each scored 23 points for the Hawks, who have dropped three in a row after opening the season with consecutive wins. Jalen Johnson shot just 4 for 12 and finished with 12 points, 11 assists and nine rebounds. The Hawks were playing the first game of a home back-to-back. items.t: Lockport City Council votes to remove Flock cameras
items.x: BUFFALO, N.Y. (WIVB) On Wednesday, the City of Lockport Common Council voted to remove permission to use Flock cameras within city limits. The decision was made after Lockport residents became vocal on the issue, joining the growing pushback on Flock cameras over safety and privacy concerns. "I oppose AI-driven cameras operated by outside for-profit companies because of the concerns about data misuse, profit and stockpiling," one resident said while attending Wednesday's meeting. The council initially authorized the installation and use of two Flock cameras within city limits this past February. City of Lockport 4th Ward Alderman Kathryn Fogle brought forward Wednesday's resolution to remove the cameras. "It was really an urging from all my constituents," Fogle said. "I just listened to the people and brought it forth. And I feel like this is a really good thing for the city because I feel like the people think they were heard." An investigator with the Niagara County Sheriff's Office attended the meeting and spoke out, asking the council to take more time to consider the decision on the cameras before voting. items.t: Theodore Roosevelt Inaugural Site receives $400k
items.x: BUFFALO, N.Y. (WIVB) The Theodore Roosevelt Inaugural Site in Buffalo is getting $400,000, which will make it possible for more visitors to enjoy the facility. The site foundation says the cash will go toward development and the installation of a self-guided tour. Currently, full access requires being on a tour with a docent. Officials hope the change increases attendance and revenue for the historic site. National Park Service approves funding for Roosevelt site In August, the National Park Service approved about $300,000 of funding to cover the site's utilities, operating budget and staff salaries. The site commemorates the location where Roosevelt took the oath of office on Sept. 14, 1901, following the assassination of President William McKinley in Buffalo. items.t: DOJ’s California ballot fight rejected by another judge
items.x: ( The Hill ) The Trump administration's bid to separate 20,000 mail ballots in California that it says are likely noncitizens met another defeat on Wednesday as a trial judge refused to intervene. U.S. District Judge David Carter ruled California can continue to accept the questioned ballots like any other. “This request violates longstanding constitutional principles mandating that states have control over their elections,” Carter wrote. “If Plaintiff’s last-minute request for relief were granted, either party could create chaos for their own political purposes to disrupt the election process,” he continued. “Over 20,000 registered Californians would potentially lose the right that generations of Americans have fought to preserve.” California has raised eyebrows at the veracity of the administration's list and says it's not obligated to verify voters’ citizenship in response. The state has conceded it's not feasible to segregate a ballot once it's processed. It would be counted even if later found to be fraudulent. items.t: Harris advises Democrats against attempting to impeach Trump
items.x: ( The Hill ) Former Vice President Kamala Harris on Tuesday urged Democrats against making a third attempt to impeach President Trump if they win back the House after next week's midterm elections. "I think that going in the direction of impeachment is not a good idea, just to be honest with you," Harris told MeidasTouch's Aaron Parnas in an interview. "Just because we have limited resources and I think the energy and the resources need to put into accountability, need to be put into investigations." "And that's where the time should be spent," she added. "Remember, I was in the Senate for the last go-around, and the votes aren't there. "So, that's how I feel. But also, I think after the election, we all have to just also agree that our attitude has to be to get stuff done." Harris said Democrats should be "uncompromising" and "not sit around, you know, being genteel about the relationships," but maintain accountability when it comes to cuts to healthcare and oversight on the Iran war. items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war , creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle . He was back in the national limelight presiding over the proceedings for Maduro , who was captured and brought to the U.S. earlier this year over accusations of narco-terrorism. Maduro and his wife were in the judge's courtroom less than two weeks ago to plead not guilty to a new set of criminal charges. Before the Maduro operation, Hellerstein had long clashed with President Donald Trump in court. items.x: NEW YORK (AP) — U.S. stocks are drifting Wednesday as the countdown ticks toward this afternoon’s announcement from the Federal Reserve on what it will do with interest rates . The S&P 500 rose 0.2% and pulled within 1% of its all-time high , which was set earlier this month. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 176 points, or 0.3%, as of 11:45 a.m. Eastern time, and the Nasdaq composite was virtually unchanged. The day’s highlight will likely be what the Federal Reserve says, if anything, about where interest rates are heading. The Fed raised its main interest rate last month for the first time in three years in hopes of slowing the high inflation that’s squeezing the economy and discouraging Americans . The widespread expectation on Wall Street is that the Fed will leave the federal funds rate alone at this meeting, and the question is whether it will give hints about what may happen at later meetings. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh, though, has been adamant since taking over the Fed about wanting it to give fewer indications about its future moves. Using DNA and other evidence, the Summit County Sheriff's Office and Summit County Attorney's Office formally closed the cold-case murder, saying that the evidence conclusively proves that Ted Bundy murdered 17-year-old Melissa Ann Smith. Bundy has long been considered a suspect in several cold cases in Utah, and Smith's murder was one of them. Hunters found her remains in Summit County on Oct. 27, 1974, 52 years ago today. items.t: Cause of death revealed for ‘Office Space’ actor Richard Riehle: Reports
items.x: (NEXSTAR) – The cause of death for longtime actor Richard Riehle has been revealed, according to reports. The 78-year-old died earlier this month in Los Angeles, friends told TMZ , which was the first to report the news. The outlet and People , citing his death certificate, reported Tuesday that the "Office Space" actor experienced a stroke and had oropharyngeal cancer. He had been in a rehabilitation center at the time of his death in mid-October, according to People. Oropharyngeal cancer , which can be asymptomatic, impacts the middle portion of your throat, including the base of your tongue and the tonsils. While there are multiple types of oropharyngeal cancers, Johns Hopkins Medicine says the majority are squamous cell carcinomas, which are further divided into HPV-related and HPV-unrelated. The former is caused by HPV, while the latter is commonly caused by tobacco or alcohol. Details about Riehle's condition were not released. items.t: Recalled butter sold in 10 states receives risk warning: FDA
items.x: NEW JERSEY ( WPIX ) A popular plant-based butter has been recalled due to yeast, mold and E. coli, and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has now assigned it a risk level . The recall, which was initiated by Prosperity Organic Foods, Inc., headquartered in Boise, Idaho, involves 1,304 cases of Miyoko's Creamery European Style Salted Plant Milk Butter. The FDA assigned the recall as a Class II risk level on Friday, meaning a product may cause “temporary or medically reversible adverse health consequences.” The recall was initially announced Sept. 11. The affected butter, which is perishable and stored refrigerated or frozen, comes in six-packs of 8-ounce units, which can be identified with the following information: UPC 857554005773 Lot number and best-by on SBS carton: 07871, Nov. 5, 2026 Lot number and best-by date on the corrugated case for shipment: 1007871, Nov. 5, 2026 The affected products were also sold in Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Iowa, Illinois, Indiana, Maryland, New Jersey, New Hampshire and Wisconsin.

items.x: Democrats are giddy about the possibility of a bigger blue wave than expected in the battle for the Senate as polls show that South Carolina , Florida and Mississippi — three seats that were long seen as safe Republican holds — are now competitive races. Democrats view the Republican candidates running in those states as mediocre political talents who must fight historic headwinds caused by President Trump’s unpopularity, voter anger over inflation and the war in Iran, and burgeoning Democratic voter enthusiasm. The Senate battleground map has steadily expanded throughout the 2026 midterm election cycle as political handicappers have shifted seats that were thought to be in solidly Republican territory — such as Alaska, Iowa, Kansas and Texas — to the “toss-up" category. items.t: Muzzleloader Deer Season Opens Oct. 31, Is Your Gun Ready?
items.x: NEW CASTLE, Va. (WFXR) Expect to hear the thunder of gunfire around Virginia soon. Deer muzzleloader season opens October 31. But, before you head into the woods, there is one very important thing to consider. "Is my gun ready?" The only way to tell is to fire it at a target to make sure the scope and gun are in synch, and that your aim is true. If not, you will need to make adjustments on the scope and possibly the gun. There are any number of things that can affect the scope. "Well, it's been been a whole year since we've done this, so bumping them in the closet or on the truck ride, you know, things happen," said expert deer hunter Randy Frango of Craig County. "It's a good practice to, you check your rifle prior to season." Having a gun dialed in can keep you from missing a deer, but it can also prevent something else, wounding a deer and not being able to track it. "You don't want to make a bad shot and wound an animal either," said Frango. "So yeah, check your rifle, whether it be a muzzleloader or rifle, rifle season is coming up, and make sure your firearm is hitting where it should." The other thing Frango emphasized is safety and especially avoiding double charging a gun.

items.t: AAA advises drivers about daylight saving time
items.x: ( WAVY ) – It's only a few days until we trade one extra hour of sleep for months of darkness as we leave work to drive home. And even though we're on the easier end of the time transition (from daylight saving time to standard time), the switch still takes its toll. Nexstar's WAVY went to AAA Tidewater Virginia to see what commuters can expect. "Well, the biggest thing for drivers will be the change in daylight when we leave work or school," said Holly Dalby with AAA. "At the end of the day, gone will be the bright sunshine, and we will find ourselves either driving into the glare from the setting sun or driving home in the dark. So it's a time to be particularly careful on the roads." Days will get way shorter in November: How much daylight will we lose? While lawmakers have tried to get rid of the time switch altogether, it doesn't appear to be going anywhere anytime soon, so your circadian rhythm will have to dance to a different beat for a while. "It just messing with our sleep schedule can really add to our fatigue very quickly. And when we're fatigued, we can make mistakes," Dalby said. items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: ( The Hill ) Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. Gasoline and energy costs have risen in six of nine months this year, as the Iran war sparked oil price shocks via the Islamic Republic's restrictions on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Persistent inflation , which has remained above the Fed's 2 percent target for five-and-a-half years, spurred central bank officials to hike interest rates by a quarter point in mid-September. At 2 a.m. on Sunday, November 1, clocks across most of the United States will be turned back to 1 a.m. Since the current U.S. daylight saving schedule was adopted in 2007, Halloween has coincided with the clock change only a handful of times, including 2009, 2015 and 2020. As Halloween celebrations stretch an extra hour this year thanks to the end of daylight saving time, partygoers are being advised to plan ahead before heading out for the evening. "It's kind of a recipe for potential disaster on the roadway," said AAA Northeast Senior Spokesperson Mark Schieldrop. items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war , creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle . items.x: ( The Hill ) Alvin Hellerstein, a longtime federal judge who was set to oversee the criminal trial of deposed Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro, has passed away, according to a court official. He was 92. Nominated by then-President Bill Clinton in 1998, Hellerstein oversaw many high-profile disputes during his nearly three decades on the bench in New York City. He was back in the national limelight presiding over the proceedings for Maduro , who was captured and brought to the U.S. earlier this year over accusations of narco-terrorism. Maduro and his wife were in the judge's courtroom less than two weeks ago to plead not guilty to a new set of criminal charges. Before the Maduro operation, Hellerstein had long clashed with President Donald Trump in court. The judge at one point agreed that Trump’s fixer-turned-foe, Michael Cohen, could be released from prison to home confinement. Cohen has cast his prosecution as retribution by Trump. Separately, Hellerstein repeatedly denied Trump's efforts to move his hush money criminal prosecution into federal court, forcing the president to try his luck in New York's state system. items.x: NEW YORK (AP) — U.S. stocks are drifting Wednesday as the countdown ticks toward this afternoon’s announcement from the Federal Reserve on what it will do with interest rates . The S&P 500 rose 0.2% and pulled within 1% of its all-time high , which was set earlier this month. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 176 points, or 0.3%, as of 11:45 a.m. Eastern time, and the Nasdaq composite was virtually unchanged. The day’s highlight will likely be what the Federal Reserve says, if anything, about where interest rates are heading. The Fed raised its main interest rate last month for the first time in three years in hopes of slowing the high inflation that’s squeezing the economy and discouraging Americans . The widespread expectation on Wall Street is that the Fed will leave the federal funds rate alone at this meeting, and the question is whether it will give hints about what may happen at later meetings. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh, though, has been adamant since taking over the Fed about wanting it to give fewer indications about its future moves. items.t: Democrats see battleground map expand to South Carolina, Florida, Mississippi
items.x: Democrats are giddy about the possibility of a bigger blue wave than expected in the battle for the Senate as polls show that South Carolina , Florida and Mississippi — three seats that were long seen as safe Republican holds — are now competitive races. Democrats view the Republican candidates running in those states as mediocre political talents who must fight historic headwinds caused by President Trump’s unpopularity, voter anger over inflation and the war in Iran, and burgeoning Democratic voter enthusiasm. The Senate battleground map has steadily expanded throughout the 2026 midterm election cycle as political handicappers have shifted seats that were thought to be in solidly Republican territory — such as Alaska, Iowa, Kansas and Texas — to the “toss-up" category. But now Republicans have to worry about losing Senate seats in states that were unthinkable as realistic Democratic pickup opportunities at the start of the election cycle, most notably South Carolina, which last elected a Democrat, Fritz Hollings, to the Senate in 1998. items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: ( The Hill ) Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. Gasoline and energy costs have risen in six of nine months this year, as the Iran war sparked oil price shocks via the Islamic Republic's restrictions on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Persistent inflation , which has remained above the Fed's 2 percent target for five-and-a-half years, spurred central bank officials to hike interest rates by a quarter point in mid-September. items.t: Muzzleloader Deer Season Opens Oct. 31, Is Your Gun Ready?
items.x: NEW CASTLE, Va. (WFXR) Expect to hear the thunder of gunfire around Virginia soon. Deer muzzleloader season opens October 31. But, before you head into the woods, there is one very important thing to consider. "Is my gun ready?" The only way to tell is to fire it at a target to make sure the scope and gun are in synch, and that your aim is true. If not, you will need to make adjustments on the scope and possibly the gun. There are any number of things that can affect the scope. "Well, it's been been a whole year since we've done this, so bumping them in the closet or on the truck ride, you know, things happen," said expert deer hunter Randy Frango of Craig County. "It's a good practice to, you check your rifle prior to season." Having a gun dialed in can keep you from missing a deer, but it can also prevent something else, wounding a deer and not being able to track it. "You don't want to make a bad shot and wound an animal either," said Frango. "So yeah, check your rifle, whether it be a muzzleloader or rifle, rifle season is coming up, and make sure your firearm is hitting where it should." The other thing Frango emphasized is safety and especially avoiding double charging a gun.

items.t: AAA advises drivers about daylight saving time

Nexstar's WAVY went to AAA Tidewater Virginia to see what commuters can expect. "Well, the biggest thing for drivers will be the change in daylight when we leave work or school," said Holly Dalby with AAA. "At the end of the day, gone will be the bright sunshine, and we will find ourselves either driving into the glare from the setting sun or driving home in the dark. While lawmakers have tried to get rid of the time switch altogether, it doesn't appear to be going anywhere anytime soon, so your circadian rhythm will have to dance to a different beat for a while. items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. Gasoline and energy costs have risen in six of nine months this year, as the Iran war sparked oil price shocks via the Islamic Republic's restrictions on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Persistent inflation , which has remained above the Fed's 2 percent target for five-and-a-half years, spurred central bank officials to hike interest rates by a quarter point in mid-September. items.t: DOJ’s California ballot fight rejected by another judge
items.x: ( The Hill ) The Trump administration's bid to separate 20,000 mail ballots in California that it says are likely noncitizens met another defeat on Wednesday as a trial judge refused to intervene. U.S. District Judge David Carter ruled California can continue to accept the questioned ballots like any other. “This request violates longstanding constitutional principles mandating that states have control over their elections,” Carter wrote. “If Plaintiff’s last-minute request for relief were granted, either party could create chaos for their own political purposes to disrupt the election process,” he continued. “Over 20,000 registered Californians would potentially lose the right that generations of Americans have fought to preserve.” California has raised eyebrows at the veracity of the administration's list and says it's not obligated to verify voters’ citizenship in response. The state has conceded it's not feasible to segregate a ballot once it's processed. It would be counted even if later found to be fraudulent. items.t: Religious, community leaders urge voters to help end hunger in Rio Grande Valley
items.x: McALLEN, Texas (Border Report) The Humanitarian Respite Center in McAllen used to help thousands of migrants who crossed the border during the Biden administration. But since Trump took over it has largely been empty. But on Wednesday dozens of faith-based and community leaders were at the center to speak out against hunger and food insecurities that are plaguing this South Texas border region. And to urge voters to elect leaders who will help. “In this election year Bread for the World is urging people of faith to vote to end hunger," Felipe Salinas of the Christian-based nonprofit group Bread for the World told the group. He says there are too many people in the region who cannot afford food for their families and he believes more public assistance is needed by the government. “It is very much a policy choice because for every meal a food bank or food pantry provides, the federally-funded Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, or SNAP, provides 9. items.t: Acadia Parish Sheriff’s Office warns residents of scam phone calls
items.x: ACADIA PARISH, La . ( KLFY ) The Acadia Parish Sheriff’s Office is warning residents about a growing number of phone calls from individuals claiming to represent various government agencies and demanding money. According to the sheriff’s office, dispatchers have received numerous calls from citizens reporting suspicious phone calls in which callers claim the recipients owe money. Officials are urging residents to use caution and avoid sending money to anyone who contacts them unexpectedly and claims to be working for a government entity. The sheriff’s office warns that once money is sent to scammers, recovering those funds can be difficult or impossible, particularly when the individuals responsible are operating outside the country. Before sending money or providing financial information, residents are encouraged to contact their local law enforcement agency to verify whether the request is legitimate. Residents who have questions or concerns can contact Acadia Parish Sheriff’s Office dispatchers at 337-788-8772 . items.t: Harris advises Democrats against attempting to impeach Trump
items.x: ( The Hill ) Former Vice President Kamala Harris on Tuesday urged Democrats against making a third attempt to impeach President Trump if they win back the House after next week's midterm elections. "I think that going in the direction of impeachment is not a good idea, just to be honest with you," Harris told MeidasTouch's Aaron Parnas in an interview. "Just because we have limited resources and I think the energy and the resources need to put into accountability, need to be put into investigations." "And that's where the time should be spent," she added. "Remember, I was in the Senate for the last go-around, and the votes aren't there. "So, that's how I feel. But also, I think after the election, we all have to just also agree that our attitude has to be to get stuff done." Harris said Democrats should be "uncompromising" and "not sit around, you know, being genteel about the relationships," but maintain accountability when it comes to cuts to healthcare and oversight on the Iran war. "The main purpose is for them to collect any floating debris, to prevent that from getting into the intakes at the Sewerage and Water Board pump stations, so that it doesn't ultimately get into our waterways and lake,” Cory Miller, the Pontchartrain Conservancy's community engagement director, said. Officials said the goal is to engage residents in litter prevention, data collection and device maintenance. Litter booms and storm drain filters have been placed in three canals: St. Charles, Lower Ninth and Monticello. items.t: Purdue studies cockroach milk for food-based research
items.x: HENDERSON, Ky. (WEHT) Purdue University is looking into the potential for cockroach milk to create food. Ramaswamy Subramanian is a professor in the Department of Biological Sciences and the Weldon School of Biomedical Engineering at Purdue University. Officials say a cockroach found on Hawaii, called the Pacific beetle cockroach, makes a highly nutritious substance that it feeds to its babies. This substance, dubbed "cockroach milk" by scientists, has twice the number of calories per unit weight as the milk from a water buffalo. Officals note this makes cockroach milk one of the most nutritious substances ever discovered. Cockroach milk is densely packed with nutrients and exists in a crystallized form that slowly releases nutrients to the cockroach embryo as needed. Subramanian believes that with modern genetic engineering, cockroach milk could be used to create high-protein bread that could help feed the world or create stable, high-calorie food that could feed astronauts on future journeys to Mars. items.t: Judge overseeing Maduro trial dies
items.x: ( The Hill ) Alvin Hellerstein, a longtime federal judge who was set to oversee the criminal trial of deposed Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro, has passed away, according to a court official. He was 92. Nominated by then-President Bill Clinton in 1998, Hellerstein oversaw many high-profile disputes during his nearly three decades on the bench in New York City. He was back in the national limelight presiding over the proceedings for Maduro , who was captured and brought to the U.S. earlier this year over accusations of narco-terrorism. items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war , creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle . The S&P 500 rose 0.2% and pulled within 1% of its all-time high , which was set earlier this month. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 176 points, or 0.3%, as of 11:45 a.m. Eastern time, and the Nasdaq composite was virtually unchanged. The day’s highlight will likely be what the Federal Reserve says, if anything, about where interest rates are heading. The Fed raised its main interest rate last month for the first time in three years in hopes of slowing the high inflation that’s squeezing the economy and discouraging Americans . The widespread expectation on Wall Street is that the Fed will leave the federal funds rate alone at this meeting, and the question is whether it will give hints about what may happen at later meetings. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh, though, has been adamant since taking over the Fed about wanting it to give fewer indications about its future moves. Democrats view the Republican candidates running in those states as mediocre political talents who must fight historic headwinds caused by President Trump’s unpopularity, voter anger over inflation and the war in Iran, and burgeoning Democratic voter enthusiasm. The Senate battleground map has steadily expanded throughout the 2026 midterm election cycle as political handicappers have shifted seats that were thought to be in solidly Republican territory — such as Alaska, Iowa, Kansas and Texas — to the “toss-up" category. items.t: AAA advises drivers about daylight saving time
items.x: ( WAVY ) – It's only a few days until we trade one extra hour of sleep for months of darkness as we leave work to drive home. And even though we're on the easier end of the time transition (from daylight saving time to standard time), the switch still takes its toll. Nexstar's WAVY went to AAA Tidewater Virginia to see what commuters can expect. "Well, the biggest thing for drivers will be the change in daylight when we leave work or school," said Holly Dalby with AAA. "At the end of the day, gone will be the bright sunshine, and we will find ourselves either driving into the glare from the setting sun or driving home in the dark. So it's a time to be particularly careful on the roads." items.x: Wendy’s shares jumped more than 14% Wednesday after noted investor Nelson Peltz made an offer to buy the chain, which has been struggling with high beef prices and aging stores. Peltz’s Trian Fund Management and several partners are offering Wendy’s $7.35 per share in cash, or a premium of nearly 19% over the stock’s closing price on Tuesday, in a deal that would take the company private. The offer values Wendy's at $1.4 billion. Wendy's, which is based in Dublin, Ohio, confirmed receipt of the unsolicited proposal in a statement Wednesday and said its board has formed an independent committee to evaluate it. At the end of last year, Wendy's had 5,969 restaurants in the U.S. and 1,428 outlets in 38 countries. Wendy's, founded in 1969 by Dave Thomas and named after his daughter, is known for its square burgers and Frosty desserts. The fast-growing chain introduced the drive-thru window in 1970 and went public in 1976. In the 1980s, as it jockeyed for sales with McDonald's and Burger King, Wendy's launched salad bars and ran its iconic “Where's the beef?” ad campaign. items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: ( The Hill ) Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. Gasoline and energy costs have risen in six of nine months this year, as the Iran war sparked oil price shocks via the Islamic Republic's restrictions on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Persistent inflation , which has remained above the Fed's 2 percent target for five-and-a-half years, spurred central bank officials to hike interest rates by a quarter point in mid-September. items.x: DoorDash is gobbling up Instacart in a $17 billion acquisition that will supercharge its grocery delivery business. DoorDash said the Instacart brand name and app will remain, and Instacart shoppers can continue fulfilling orders for Instacart. Grocers can also choose to work with Instacart or DoorDash. Instacart customers will now have access to 50,000 additional stores covered by DoorDash, the company said. Instacart, founded in 2012, specializes in grocery and convenience store delivery in the U.S. and Canada. Its 600,000 “shoppers” — who are independent contractors — completed 338 million orders last year, according to company filings. Instacart has a market value of $14 billion. DoorDash, founded in San Francisco in 2013, began as a restaurant delivery business but has expanded to pet food and electronics. Operating in 40 countries, it completed more than 3 billion orders last year using a network of 9 million independent delivery workers. It has a market value of $73 billion. DoorDash began delivering groceries in 2020 amid a surge in pandemic-era demand. Grocers were initially cautious.
