items.t: RFK Jr. eases access to unproven peptides despite opposition from FDA scientists
items.x: WASHINGTON (AP) — The Trump administration on Wednesday acted to ease access to unproven peptide drugs favored by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr . Food and Drug Administration scientific staffers had little input on the decision and opposed the changes, according to six people familiar with its development. The draft policy posted online by Kennedy’s Department of Health and Human Services covers a handful of injectable peptides promoted within the wellness industry for uses such as building muscle, healing injuries and boosting energy. The government will take comments for two weeks before finalizing the measure. The document, primarily written by officials at HHS, faced overwhelming pushback among FDA drug staffers who warned it could undermine the agency’s long-standing mission of keeping unsafe health products off the U.S. market, according to the people familiar with its development. items.t: Young entrepreneur turns his passion for lemonade into a growing business

Brennan Williams, founder of Brennan’s Lemonade, turned his love for business and a passion for creating the perfect drink into an entrepreneurial journey that began when he was just 9 years old. Growing up around a family of business owners, Williams said he was inspired to follow in their footsteps and build something of his own. Rather than follow popular drink trends, he chose a different approach: focusing on a classic favorite, lemonade. His signature drink, “Premium Blend,” took years to perfect before he began bottling and selling it in 2021 at a local snowball shop. Customers quickly took notice, encouraging him to bring his product to grocery store shelves. Since then, Brennan’s Lemonade has expanded into 11 stores, marking a major milestone for the young business owner. Williams has even bigger plans for the future, including getting his lemonade into airports and introducing the brand to an even wider audience. items.t: Louisiana AG seeks dismissal of death row inmate’s execution lawsuit
items.x: BATON ROUGE, La. (Louisiana First) — The Attorney General's Office filed a reply to support the motion to dismiss a death row inmate's lawsuit against the state. According to court documents, AG Liz Murrill is asking a federal judge in the Middle District of Louisiana to dismiss Todd Wessinger's lawsuit challenging the state's method of execution. State attorneys argue that Wessinger's lawsuit should be dismissed since the state has agreed to allow him to choose lethal injection rather than the original method of nitrogen hypoxia if an execution warrant is issued. Officials confirmed that the state has secured a supplier and requested a deposit of 15 grams of Pentobarbital. State attorneys also accuse Wessinger of using the lawsuit to delay his execution. Wessinger was convicted of a double murder in Baton Rouge in 1995, killing Stephanie Guzzardo and David Breakwell during a robbery. Wessinger was a former employee of Calendar’s restaurant who shot Guzzardo and Breakwell and injured another. By 1997, Wessinger was sentenced to the death penalty. items.t: Harris advises Democrats against attempting to impeach Trump
items.x: ( The Hill ) Former Vice President Kamala Harris on Tuesday urged Democrats against making a third attempt to impeach President Trump if they win back the House after next week's midterm elections. "I think that going in the direction of impeachment is not a good idea, just to be honest with you," Harris told MeidasTouch's Aaron Parnas in an interview. "Just because we have limited resources and I think the energy and the resources need to put into accountability, need to be put into investigations." "And that's where the time should be spent," she added. "Remember, I was in the Senate for the last go-around, and the votes aren't there. "So, that's how I feel. But also, I think after the election, we all have to just also agree that our attitude has to be to get stuff done." Harris said Democrats should be "uncompromising" and "not sit around, you know, being genteel about the relationships," but maintain accountability when it comes to cuts to healthcare and oversight on the Iran war. ( Louisiana First ) A Donaldsonville man was arrested Wednesday, Oct. 28, after a three-vehicle crash near the Sunshine Bridge left three horses dead and another injured, according to a fundraiser organized by the horses' owners. Louisiana State Police confirmed the crash happened Saturday, Oct. 24, on LA 70 in Ascension Parish. Troopers with LSP Troop A arrested Carlo Phillips, 43, of Donaldsonville, in connection with the crash. Phillips was charged with hit-and-run, careless operation and driving under suspension. He was booked into the East Baton Rouge Parish Prison. According to a GoFundMe fundraiser organized by Situated Riderz, a horseback riding group, its horse trailer was struck from behind by a vehicle on a bridge. The group said four horses were involved in the crash. Two died at the scene, while a third died the following day from internal bleeding. Situated Riderz described the horses as family members, saying they had spent years caring for them and building their riding group. "These horses weren't just animals to us. items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war , creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle . items.t: Metro Council to talk about deconsolidating Baton Rouge from EBR Parish
items.x: BATON ROUGE, La. ( Louisiana First ) — Could the City of Baton Rouge deconsolidate from East Baton Rouge Parish? The East Baton Rouge Metro Council will meet at 4 p.m. on Wednesday, Oct. 28, to assess the financial implications for both the parish and the city. According to the meeting agenda, "The report should include, but not be limited to, a separation of East Baton Rouge Parish and City of Baton Rouge revenues and expenses, a sample annual budget for both the City of Baton Rouge and the Parish of East Baton Rouge." The report should also include an opinion on whether the city would have an independent tax base to cover its expenses. There are two other items that were requested to be a part of the report, and they were the sustainability of the parish and city if deconsolidation took place, and "the independent financial responsibility of the City of Baton Rouge and the Parish of East Baton Rouge as it relates to the constitutional office funding requirements," according to the agenda. items.t: Judge overseeing Maduro trial dies
items.x: ( The Hill ) Alvin Hellerstein, a longtime federal judge who was set to oversee the criminal trial of deposed Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro, has passed away, according to a court official. He was 92. Nominated by then-President Bill Clinton in 1998, Hellerstein oversaw many high-profile disputes during his nearly three decades on the bench in New York City. He was back in the national limelight presiding over the proceedings for Maduro , who was captured and brought to the U.S. earlier this year over accusations of narco-terrorism. Maduro and his wife were in the judge's courtroom less than two weeks ago to plead not guilty to a new set of criminal charges. Before the Maduro operation, Hellerstein had long clashed with President Donald Trump in court. The judge at one point agreed that Trump’s fixer-turned-foe, Michael Cohen, could be released from prison to home confinement. Cohen has cast his prosecution as retribution by Trump. Separately, Hellerstein repeatedly denied Trump's efforts to move his hush money criminal prosecution into federal court, forcing the president to try his luck in New York's state system. items.t: Cap City Beer Fest: Baton Rouge festivalgoers can sample craft beers, support animal shelter
items.x: BATON ROUGE, La. ( Louisiana First ) A downtown Baton Rouge beer festival benefiting a local animal shelter is back on Nov. 1. Cap City Beer Fest raises money for Companion Animal Alliance (CAA) each year. It features craft beer, food and live entertainment on Fourth Street, between North Street and Spanish Town Road. Breweries and homebrewers will offer samples. "Cap City Beer Fest is such a fun way for our community to come together and support the animals at CAA," CAA Executive Director JT Hackett said. "Every ticket, sponsorship, and partnership helps us continue providing the care and resources our animals need while giving people a great reason to spend the day downtown." Proceeds help support animal care, medical services, enrichment programs and adoption efforts for pets in need. "Whether this will be your first year attending or your 11th, we hope you'll buy a ticket and help raise a glass to the work of CAA and to our community and their pets,” said 2026 Committee Chair Tyler Hicks. Tickets are on sale now online . Three different options are available: $50 general admission, $15 designated driver and $100 VIP. People can also donate money or buy a T-shirt on the website.

items.t: US stocks hold steady as the countdown ticks to a Federal Reserve decision on interest rates
items.x: NEW YORK (AP) — U.S. stocks are drifting Wednesday as the countdown ticks toward this afternoon’s announcement from the Federal Reserve on what it will do with interest rates . The S&P 500 rose 0.2% and pulled within 1% of its all-time high , which was set earlier this month. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 176 points, or 0.3%, as of 11:45 a.m. Eastern time, and the Nasdaq composite was virtually unchanged. The day’s highlight will likely be what the Federal Reserve says, if anything, about where interest rates are heading. The Fed raised its main interest rate last month for the first time in three years in hopes of slowing the high inflation that’s squeezing the economy and discouraging Americans . The widespread expectation on Wall Street is that the Fed will leave the federal funds rate alone at this meeting, and the question is whether it will give hints about what may happen at later meetings. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh, though, has been adamant since taking over the Fed about wanting it to give fewer indications about its future moves. items.x: BATON ROUGE, La. (Louisiana First) The Louisiana Highway Safety Commission (LHSC) reminds all drivers to watch out for little ghosts and goblins on Halloween. LHSC urges drivers on the road during peak trick-or-treating hours to be on the lookout for children running into the streets while going door-to-door for treats, especially while driving through residential neighborhoods. “These children are looking for candy bars, not trucks and cars,” LHSC Executive Director Lisa Freeman said. “As drivers, we must look out for them.” Freeman also recommended that parents make their child as visible as possible. “Trick-or-treaters and their parents should have some type of flashlight with them to improve their visibility,” she said. “Bright colors, glowing bracelets and reflective tape on shoes make it much easier for oncoming traffic to see you.” Children aren't the only ones at risk on Halloween night. items.x: NASHVILLE, Tenn. ( WKRN ) — A 23-year-old woman is set to appear in Nashville court after allegedly helping a man flip a $39,000 piece of Home Depot equipment on Facebook Marketplace. Arrest documents show Rebecca Walpole and a male suspect entered the Madison, Tennessee, Home Depot on May 26 and rented a boom lift, which is commonly known as a cherry picker or basket crane. The equipment was towed using a silver Dodge Ram. According to court documents, the property was never returned. Nashville Super 8 sued over almost $150K in unpaid repair bills The male suspect was arrested in Michigan on Sept. 23, according to arrest documents. Investigators said he admitted to selling rented construction equipment to buyers on Facebook Marketplace. Walpole faces a felony theft of property charge, and she was recently booked in Davidson County. Her bond was set at $10,000.

items.t: Dolores Huerta, labor leader and activist, dies at 96
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Activist Dolores Huerta, who helped co-found the National Farm Workers Association with César Chavez, has died. She was 96. Huerta's family said in a statement through her foundation that she died Wednesday at home. "We are deeply saddened to announce that our beloved mother, Dolores Huerta, has passed away today at the age of 96," her family said in a statement posted on social media. "As you can imagine, this is an incredibly difficult time for us, and we ask for privacy as we grieve this incredible loss to our family," the statement continued. "We know that many of you around the world share in our mourning, and we will be following up on plans to recognize and celebrate her incredible life and legacy." (KTAL/KMSS) – Three federal judges heard arguments Tuesday in Shreveport over whether a lawsuit challenging Louisiana’s congressional map should be dismissed, a decision that could affect how Black voters are represented in Congress. The hearing took place at the Tom Stagg Federal Courthouse as attorneys debated whether the Louisiana v. Callais litigation should remain open following changes to the state’s congressional map. Voters take action during Louisiana v. Callais motion-to-dismiss hearing The dispute follows a U.S. Supreme Court ruling against Louisiana’s previous map. The state subsequently adopted a new map that eliminated its second Black-majority congressional district, prompting renewed debate over voting rights and representation. Outside the courthouse, civil rights advocates argued the case is about preserving Black voters’ ability to elect candidates of their choice. “We’re not here because the United States Supreme Court simply eliminated one Black opportunity district. Kotlikoff after allegations of a 2024 gang rape at a campus fraternity that resulted in no criminal charges caused uproar around the country. The more than 75 members of the body will have their second meeting debating the resolution and the timing of a vote on it. A motion could be introduced to delay the no-confidence vote and set another meeting. But if that motion is not introduced or fails, members of the Faculty Senate will begin the no-confidence vote after Wednesday's meeting is over, and they typically have a week to cast their choice online. While a no-confidence vote has no authority to remove an official, its passing would show deep dissatisfaction from faculty with how Cornell leadership has handled accusations from Jane Doe that seven members of the Chi Phi fraternity raped her . items.t: Sabato’s Crystal Ball moves 16 House races toward Democrats
items.x: ( The Hill ) – Nonpartisan election forecaster Sabato’s Crystal Ball is shifting more than a dozen House races toward Democrats in the final week of the campaign , another sign of a worsening political environment for Republicans. Crystal Ball, a division of the University of Virginia’s Center for Politics, has moved dozens of races toward Democrats in recent weeks, including nearly 50 races in the month of October alone. The race changes include moving a few deep-red seats into the “toss up” column. Open congressional districts in Kentucky and Montana, as well as seats with GOP incumbents in Missouri, Virginia, Colorado and Pennsylvania moved into coin flip territory. Many of the seats Crystal Ball rates as a toss-up were places Trump carried by double digits in 2024. Monica de la Cruz (R) is facing a tough challenge from Tejano music star Bobby Pulido (D). The request was included in a petition filed Tuesday in state district court in East Baton Rouge Parish, where Judge Ronald R. Johnson in late August granted a preliminary injunction against the NCAA , which has argued that Luis is ineligible to play. An SEC spokesman said Tuesday that the conference had no immediate comment on the new filing. The SEC already has accused LSU in a related federal case of exhibiting an “ongoing defiance of the conference’s professionalism rules” by trying to add Luis to its roster. The SEC has a long-established rule forbidding teams from adding players with major professional experience to their rosters. items.t: No clear winner yet in Israel’s national elections: What happens now?
items.x: JERUSALEM (AP) — No clear winner has emerged in Israel’s national elections as vote-counting continues, and weeks of negotiations may lie ahead as Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his main rival, Gadi Eisenkot, will scramble to build a governing coalition. The election was widely seen as a referendum on Netanyahu , the country’s longest-serving prime minister, who gave a defiant speech to his supporters just after 3 a.m. on Wednesday in Jerusalem despite the unclear results. This was a dip from the previous election in 2022, when Likud won 23.4% of the popular vote. items.t: Louisiana’s bond rating improves, which should save the state money
items.x: ( Louisiana Illuminator ) One of the three national credit rating agencies upgraded Louisiana’s bond rating at the end of last week. The state should now expect to pay less in interest when it borrows money for roadwork and other construction projects. Fitch Ratings moved Louisiana’s credit from “AA-” to “AA,” according to a statement released by the global agency Friday. It attributed the upgrade, in part, to new tax laws Gov. Jeff Landry and the Louisiana Legislature approved two years ago. “The upgrade reflects the state’s successful implementation of 2024 revenue policy changes, which reduces a projected structural gap,” said the Fitch report. Landry and state lawmakers skirted a major state budget deficit by eliminating an automatic sales tax cut before it took place in 2025. Instead, the governor and legislators raised the sales tax rate further to offset a new income tax reduction. They also freed up more money by shifting revenue dedicated to major transportation projects into accounts for expenses such as healthcare and higher education. items.t: Flying taxis could carry passengers by 2030
items.x: (TestMiles) A British aerospace company has demonstrated an electric flying taxi that could eventually offer a new way to escape crowded city roads. The Flying Car Is Moving Beyond Science Fiction Los Angeles has spent decades trying to solve its traffic problems. Freeways expand, transit systems improve, and technology promises more efficient journeys. Yet travelling across the city can still take a remarkable amount of time. A British aerospace company believes part of the solution might be above the roads rather than on them. Vertical Aerospace has demonstrated an electric aircraft capable of taking off vertically, transitioning into conventional forward flight, and landing without a runway. The technology was publicly displayed at the Farnborough International Airshow in Britain, marking an important development in the company's plans to introduce commercial passenger flights. The aircraft is part of a growing category known as electric vertical takeoff and landing, or eVTOL. Unlike a conventional airplane, it does not require a runway for every departure. items.t: 68 dead in high-speed train collision, Spain’s 2nd deadly rail crash this year
items.x: URDA, Spain (AP) — A high-speed train slammed into another that had stopped on the tracks in Spain on Wednesday, killing at least 68 people and injuring dozens in the second deadly rail collision this year. The regional government of Castilla La Mancha confirmed the death toll and said another 58 people were receiving medical treatment at hospitals. Rescue workers searched the wreckage through the day for survivors and bodies. The collision came just nine months after another deadly crash involving high-speed trains operated by the same two companies in southern Spain in January. “Today all of Spain is grieving,” Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said from the crash site, where he announced that his government would declare three days of national mourning. Trump did two rallies in Texas — the first in Corpus Christi and another in Lubbock . It’s his fourth trip to Texas to support Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton. Talarico held his own rally in Lubbock on Tuesday. He was in Corpus Christi on Saturday. The Texas race is one of the most contested and watched Senate races in the country. Talarico and Paxton remain close in the polls — Real Clear Polling calls the race a toss-up, with Talarico holding a slight lead. A Democrat winning the Senate seat would be a shock — none have won a U.S. Senate race in Texas since 1988, and Trump won the state by nearly 14 percentage points in the 2024 presidential election. Democrats are vying to take control of the House and the Senate. The party would need to win four seats to win control of the Senate. items.t: Southern University football needs outside help to win SWAC West after loss to Texas Southern
items.x: BATON ROUGE, La. (Louisiana First) — Southern University no longer controls its own destiny in the SWAC West title race following Saturday's loss to Texas Southern (24-21). The Jaguars sit at 1-3 in conference play and at the bottom of the SWAC West standings, but still have a chance to win the division. However, they'll need some outside help and must win their remaining games. Southern's final stretch begins Saturday against Florida A&M on the road, followed by home games against Bethune-Cookman and Alcorn State before closing out the regular season against Grambling in the Bayou Classic. Despite the challenging road ahead, head coach Marshall Faulk isn't focused on the standings. "I don't address standings at all," Faulk said. "We're still in the business of just those small wins." Freshman linebacker Hunter Schnakenberg echoed that message, saying the team's focus remains on executing its brand of football. "We know what we can be," Schnakenberg said. "We're going to work to execute who we are." items.x: ( KTLA ) Instagram is moving beyond its signature short-form videos, testing a new feature that allows creators to share content lasting up to 90 minutes, including podcasts, interviews and comedy shows. The Meta-owned platform announced Monday that it is testing a feature called "Features," which allows select creators to upload longer, horizontal videos that viewers can watch directly within the app. "For a long time, I have been against doing long-form video on Instagram," Instagram head Adam Mosseri said in a video posted Monday alongside Tessa Lyons, the company's vice president of product. "But we are actually gonna lean in for a bunch of different reasons." Lyons, who previously led product development for Instagram Reels, described the expansion as a new chapter for the platform. "It feels like a full-circle moment that we're here now talking about the beginning of our journey on long-form video," she said. items.t: Utah authorities connect 1974 cold case to serial killer Ted Bundy
items.x: SUMMIT COUNTY, Utah ( KTVX ) — Investigators in Summit County, Utah closed the 1974 cold case homicide of Melissa Ann Smith Tuesday, linking her murder to prominent serial killer Ted Bundy. Using DNA and other evidence, the Summit County Sheriff's Office and Summit County Attorney's Office formally closed the cold-case murder, saying that the evidence conclusively proves that Ted Bundy murdered 17-year-old Melissa Ann Smith. Bundy has long been considered a suspect in several cold cases in Utah, and Smith's murder was one of them. Hunters found her remains in Summit County on Oct. 27, 1974, 52 years ago today. "The work began with the investigators who handled the case in 1974, and it continued through the dedication and perseverance of those who carried it forward," Summit County Sheriff Kacey Bates said. "After 50 years, we have reached a point that so many have worked toward." In the NPR/PBS News/Marist Poll , 40 percent of people said their “personal family finances” have declined in the last 12 months, while 16 percent said the opposite. Forty-one percent said their personal family finances have “stayed about the same” within the prior year. Less than 1 percent of poll respondents were not sure about the state of their personal family finances within the last year, while three percent didn’t give an answer. The NPR/PBS News/Marist Poll was conducted two weeks out from Election Day, with the rise in cost of living being a major concern in this election cycle. September saw an uptick in annual inflation for Americans, with the cost of energy, gas and electricity rising from August to September. Democrats have campaigned on targeting the Trump administration's tariffs and the war in Iran — two factors behind U.S. price hikes. items.t: Anderson High School journalism class puts spotlight on larger class sizes
items.x: AUSTIN (KXAN) — Facing continued budget deficits, school districts around Central Texas have had to make many cuts over the years. Some of those cuts have also impacted teacher to student ratios. Anderson High School journalism students recently spotlighted class sizes and how more students in the classroom can impact learning. Journalism student Desirae Gutierrez decided to dig into the issue after hearing teachers and students talking about the topic. "There is definitely less one-on-one time with the teachers," said Gutierrez. "Since I knew about there being a lot of budget cuts, I was hearing about how teachers have more students." The Austin Independent School District said due to staff leveling after the finalization of the 2026-27 budget, most class sizes, across all departments, are larger than they have been in years before. At Anderson High School, there are 17 classes that are called "literature" classes. The smallest class size has 23 students and the largest has 39 students, with an average class size of 32 students. items.t: APD: 100K people expected to descend on Austin entertainment district for Halloween
items.x: AUSTIN (KXAN) Austin Police are preparing for large crowds ahead of a busy Halloween weekend in downtown Austin. APD expects an estimated 80,000 to 100,000 people to descend upon the city's entertainment district, which includes Rainey Street, East Sixth Street and West Sixth Street. An already popular weekend in Austin is expected to get even busier. Not only does Halloween fall on a Saturday this year, but Sunday morning marks the end of daylight saving time. It's the first time clocks have fallen back the Sunday after Halloween in several years. The Texas Longhorns also face off against the Mississippi State Bulldogs Saturday at DKR Texas Memorial Stadium at 6:30 p.m. "There's an extra hour for people to consume alcohol, so we think it's going to be a very busy weekend," APD's commander for downtown Austin Christopher Juusola said. APD plans to have extra officers stationed downtown, along with crews from the Austin Fire Department and Austin-Travis County EMS. Juusola said police will have anti-vehicle barriers to prevent drivers from making their way on Sixth Street, and will install gates purchased by the city to allow easy access for emergency vehicles. items.t: How dangerous are construction zones?
items.x: Bastrop County, TX (KXAN) Two construction workers died early Thursday morning while working on a project in Bastrop County after a vehicle crashed into the work zone on State Highway 71 near Tucker Hill Lane. This is the first time since December 2021 that a construction worker was killed in a work zone in the TxDOT Austin District. That crash, which occurred in southeast Austin, also killed two workers. Work zone safety campaigns are a part of the Texas Department of Transportation's awareness efforts for drivers, particularly because the vast majority of work zone crashes injure drivers or their passengers—not the workers. TxDOT: 2 contractors killed in construction zone of westbound SH 71 In 2025, Texas had 28,000 crashes in work zones. Of those, 203 were deadly, and only seven involved construction workers. Drivers on SH 71 east of Austin will have to navigate construction zones for several more years. TxDOT is working on a series of projects on East SH 71 between Austin and Bastrop. items.t: Democrats see battleground map expand to South Carolina, Florida, Mississippi
items.x: Democrats are giddy about the possibility of a bigger blue wave than expected in the battle for the Senate as polls show that South Carolina , Florida and Mississippi — three seats that were long seen as safe Republican holds — are now competitive races. Democrats view the Republican candidates running in those states as mediocre political talents who must fight historic headwinds caused by President Trump’s unpopularity, voter anger over inflation and the war in Iran, and burgeoning Democratic voter enthusiasm. The Senate battleground map has steadily expanded throughout the 2026 midterm election cycle as political handicappers have shifted seats that were thought to be in solidly Republican territory — such as Alaska, Iowa, Kansas and Texas — to the “toss-up" category. But now Republicans have to worry about losing Senate seats in states that were unthinkable as realistic Democratic pickup opportunities at the start of the election cycle, most notably South Carolina, which last elected a Democrat, Fritz Hollings, to the Senate in 1998. items.t: Noah Kahan bringing first major concert to DKR in over 30 years
items.x: AUSTIN (KXAN) He may not be a professional athlete, but Noah Kahan has been selling out baseball stadium shows this year and will soon bring his music to even bigger stadiums, including a historic show in Austin. Kahan is currently on his biggest tour to date, The Great Divide World Tour, which will wrap up in December. The tour has sold out several baseball stadiums across the U.S., including a record-breaking, sold-out, four-show run at Fenway. Noah Kahan plays surprise show in Austin after SXSW documentary premiere After a few months off, Kahan will hit the road again next spring with an even bigger tour, The Last Of The Bugs World Tour, where he'll do a 31-date stadium run at some of the biggest stadiums across North America, Europe, and the U.K. This tour will also bring a historic show to Austin. Kahan will bring his Last of The Bugs tour to the Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium on May 15, marking the venue's first major ticketed show in over 30 years, according to Texas Athletics . items.t: Inside the Torchy’s Tacos turnaround plan after store closures
items.x: AUSTIN (ABJ) — Torchy’s Tacos closed seven locations earlier this year. Shedding those stores was part of the company’s new growth plan. The Austin-based taco chain is sitting at about 120 locations and has new restaurants in the pipeline. But previously, Torchy’s Tacos grew into too many new markets at once and it opened stores that weren’t the right size, CEO Paul Macaluso said. The company closed restaurants that were losing money, causing a large drain on the business and preventing it from growing the right way, the CEO told the ABJ. The company closed seven stores in August 2025 and seven more in February 2026. Since February, Torchy’s Tacos has opened multiple locations. Read the rest of this story in the Austin Business Journal .

items.t: Russell Brand denies all charges as he takes the stand at his rape and sex assault trial
items.x: LONDON (AP) — Russell Brand acknowledged in a London court on Wednesday that he had been obsessed with sex as a younger man, but denied multiple charges of rape and sexual assault , saying the claims have had a “devastating” impact on his life. The British actor-comedian entered Southwark Crown Court alongside his wife, Laura Gallacher, to testify in his own defense, telling reporters that “today is the day for truth and justice.” Brand, 51, stood in the witness box and took the oath, then gave his full name: Russell Edward Brand. He answered “no” to each charge as his lawyer, Ian Winter, asked whether he was guilty of three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault and one count of attempted indecent assault. William Shatner pays tribute to Walter Koenig Brand denied forcing any of the six alleged victims to do anything against their will. “Consent is fundamental, essential, necessary, and indeed in many ways more important than sex itself,” Brand said. Brand said the allegations had had a “devastating” impact, with friends and colleagues abandoning him. items.t: Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation rose slightly in September
items.x: ( The Hill ) Inflation increased slightly in September after declining in August , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis showed Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index , the preferred inflation metric for the Federal Reserve, rose by 0.5 percent last month and was up 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation for last month at 0.5 percent month-over-month and 3.6 percent relative to September 2025. Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously dipped from 3.7 percent in July to 3.4 percent in August. The price of gas and other energy goods rose by 9.2 percent from August to September, after increasing by 4.4 percent from July to August. Gasoline and energy costs have risen in six of nine months this year, as the Iran war sparked oil price shocks via the Islamic Republic's restrictions on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Persistent inflation , which has remained above the Fed's 2 percent target for five-and-a-half years, spurred central bank officials to hike interest rates by a quarter point in mid-September. items.t: Obama knocks Trump’s response to Cheesecake Factory jab: ‘These are not serious people’
items.x: ( The Hill ) Former President Obama on Wednesday responded to uproar over a recent campaign trail jab at President Trump’s White House decorations, slamming Republicans for focusing more on the joke than on the economy. “They mobilized a whole-of-government response to that joke, not to inflation, but to that joke,” Obama said during a campaign rally in Georgia. “This is what I mean when I say these are not serious people. They don't have solutions to actual problems, so they'd rather have the media and you talking about the Cheesecake Factory.” Obama had quipped during a recent campaign stop in Cleveland, Ohio, that Trump’s taste in renovations worth a reported $900 million has the White House “looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory, it’s just gold everywhere,” referring to the Iraqi palaces that were famously adorned with gold decor. Trump hit back from the road as he makes his own midterm travel blitz, touting the restaurant chain as a “very successful company” and calling Obama “a lousy president.” “It’s not about money. items.t: DOJ’s California ballot fight rejected by another judge
items.x: ( The Hill ) The Trump administration's bid to separate 20,000 mail ballots in California that it says are likely noncitizens met another defeat on Wednesday as a trial judge refused to intervene. U.S. District Judge David Carter ruled California can continue to accept the questioned ballots like any other. “This request violates longstanding constitutional principles mandating that states have control over their elections,” Carter wrote. “If Plaintiff’s last-minute request for relief were granted, either party could create chaos for their own political purposes to disrupt the election process,” he continued. “Over 20,000 registered Californians would potentially lose the right that generations of Americans have fought to preserve.” California has raised eyebrows at the veracity of the administration's list and says it's not obligated to verify voters’ citizenship in response. The state has conceded it's not feasible to segregate a ballot once it's processed. It would be counted even if later found to be fraudulent. items.t: Failed Florida gubernatorial candidate announces 2028 White House bid
items.x: ( The Hill ) Former Florida gubernatorial candidate James Fishback (R) said he plans to run for president in 2028. “Last night, someone asked me ‘What do you plan on doing next?’ I told them the truth. I’m running for president,” Fishback wrote Wednesday on social platform X , attaching a video of him announcing his presidential bid at an event. The 41 second video clip shows Fishback’s announcement followed by a round of applause. “My wife and I will soon visit Iowa, New Hampshire, and South Carolina to hold public TownHalls. Soon after I will announce my final decision,” Fishback told The Hill in a statement Wednesday. The Florida Republican lost his gubernatorial bid to Rep. Byron Donalds (R-Fla.), who is running against Obama-endorsed Democratic nominee David Jolly in the upcoming elections. Fishback finished third in the Republican primary. items.x: ( The Hill ) Conservative influencer James O’Keefe was charged in Minnesota Wednesday after he and fellow right-leaning commentator Cam Higby misrepresented themselves at a polling place during the state’s primary election earlier this year. Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty announced during a press conference the two men are facing felony unlawful voting and identity fraud charges. “Elections are the bedrock of democracy and their protection is one of our highest priorities,” Moriarty said in a statement . “Individuals engaging in unlawful conduct related to our elections will be held accountable.” On the state’s Aug. 11 primary election day, O’Keefe and Higby donned mock “ Muslim attire ,” spoke in fake accents at Minnesota polling places. O’Keefe and Higby began the state's unregistered voter vouching process under fake names but did not ultimately sign this oath or cast a vote, according to the county attorney. items.t: Judge overseeing Maduro trial dies
items.x: ( The Hill ) Alvin Hellerstein, a longtime federal judge who was set to oversee the criminal trial of deposed Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro, has passed away, according to a court official. He was 92. Nominated by then-President Bill Clinton in 1998, Hellerstein oversaw many high-profile disputes during his nearly three decades on the bench in New York City. He was back in the national limelight presiding over the proceedings for Maduro , who was captured and brought to the U.S. earlier this year over accusations of narco-terrorism. Maduro and his wife were in the judge's courtroom less than two weeks ago to plead not guilty to a new set of criminal charges. Before the Maduro operation, Hellerstein had long clashed with President Donald Trump in court. The judge at one point agreed that Trump’s fixer-turned-foe, Michael Cohen, could be released from prison to home confinement. Cohen has cast his prosecution as retribution by Trump. Separately, Hellerstein repeatedly denied Trump's efforts to move his hush money criminal prosecution into federal court, forcing the president to try his luck in New York's state system. items.t: Screwworm detected in dog in El Paso County
items.x: EL PASO, Texas (Border Report) The number of active New World screwworm cases rose to 18 on Wednesday, with several counties reporting their first case, including the populous El Paso County, Texas. According to the USDA, the five latest confirmed screwworm cases involved four dogs and a cat. Cochise County, Arizona, reported its first screwworm case on Wednesday, the first in that state. Texas state Rep. Mary Gonzalez, D-El Paso, issued a statement saying the screwworm was detected in a dog in the town of Socorro. She said her office has been in communication with the appropriate state agencies and will continue to monitor the situation. She urged the public to check on their pets and monitor them closely. "It is important that members of our community stay vigilant and go to their veterinarians if they believe their animal may have been impacted," she said. The border county of Luna, New Mexico, also confirmed its first screwworm case in a cow on Monday. The New World screwworm is a parasitic fly that lays eggs in open wounds. items.t: Cartels recruit legal border crossers to move stolen US vehicles through El Paso, feds say
items.x: EL PASO, Texas (Border Report) — Mexican cartels are recruiting U.S. citizens and others who can legally cross the border to deliver stolen American vehicles through El Paso, supplying criminal organizations with transportation for their operations, federal authorities say. The alleged recruitment strategy emerged during Operation Southbound Takedown, an investigation that has resulted in charges against 13 people and the recovery of 29 vehicles worth approximately $1.14 million. U.S Attorney Justin Simmons said the international ports of entry in El Paso are major crossing points for stolen vehicles from across the country. (Aracely Lazcano/Border Report) Eleven defendants are U.S. citizens. The other two are Mexican citizens — one a lawful permanent resident and the other a border crossing cardholder, according to federal prosecutors. items.t: Religious, community leaders urge voters to help end hunger in Rio Grande Valley
items.x: McALLEN, Texas (Border Report) The Humanitarian Respite Center in McAllen used to help thousands of migrants who crossed the border during the Biden administration. But since Trump took over it has largely been empty. But on Wednesday dozens of faith-based and community leaders were at the center to speak out against hunger and food insecurities that are plaguing this South Texas border region. And to urge voters to elect leaders who will help. “In this election year Bread for the World is urging people of faith to vote to end hunger," Felipe Salinas of the Christian-based nonprofit group Bread for the World told the group. He says there are too many people in the region who cannot afford food for their families and he believes more public assistance is needed by the government. “It is very much a policy choice because for every meal a food bank or food pantry provides, the federally-funded Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, or SNAP, provides 9. items.t: Report: Off-duty border agent allegedly stabs, kills wife
items.x: EL PASO, Texas (Border Report) An off-duty U.S. Border Patrol agent allegedly stabbed and killed his wife early Wednesday morning in Laredo, Texas, according to the Laredo Morning Times. The newspaper reported that Abel Garza, 30, is charged with murder in the death of his wife, 28-year-old Mayra Alejandra Landeros. The newspaper also reported that U.S. Customs and Border Protection confirmed that Garza is a U.S. Border Patrol agent with the Laredo Sector, and that the agency’s Office of Professional Responsibility is reviewing the incident.

items.t: Austin ISD to vote on Marshall, Linder school boundary changes
items.x: AUSTIN (KXAN) — Austin ISD trustees are expected to vote Thursday on proposed attendance boundary changes affecting General Marshall Middle School and Linder Elementary School beginning in the 2027-28 school year. District leaders say the proposals are part of a broader effort to create clearer feeder patterns and address enrollment and space challenges at specific campuses. General Marshall would receive first official attendance zone When General Marshall opened in 2023, it did not receive a traditional attendance zone. Instead, students from seven different elementary schools were given the option to attend. According to district documents, AISD says the campus cannot accommodate all seven feeder schools long term and wants to create a permanent attendance pattern as the district continues its broader boundary realignment efforts . Under the proposal, students from Overton, Jordan, Harris and Blanton elementary schools, along with portions of the Andrews and Pecan Springs attendance areas, would feed into General Marshall Middle School. items.t: TxDOT: 2 contractors killed in construction zone of westbound SH 71
items.x: BASTROP COUNTY, Texas (KXAN) — The Texas Department of Transportation confirmed two contractors were killed early Thursday morning following the fatal crash on State Highway 71. A KXAN team at the scene confirmed the medical examiner arrived around 6:25 a.m. Crews also saw first responders investigating the two deaths. KXAN was working to confirm the status of the driver of the vehicle involved. Westbound SH 71 near Tucker Hill Lane was completely closed following the incident, but the highway has since reopened. The area is part of an ongoing TxDOT construction project. A new overpass is going up on SH 71 to replace the existing traffic light intersection there at Tucker Hill Lane. TxDOT said the project will also include new frontage roads and improved bicycle and pedestrian accommodations. TxDOT is deeply saddened by the loss of lives in this morning’s crash on SH 71 near Tucker Hill Lane, including two contractors working on a TxDOT project. Our thoughts are with their families and coworkers. Most House Speakers in recent decades have stepped out of Congress after losing the gavel. And Reps. Steve Scalise (R-La.), the majority leader, and Jim Jordan (R-Ohio), a conservative icon, are both expected to launch bids to lead House Republicans if Democrats flip the chamber, according to GOP lawmakers, aides and strategists. items.t: 1 dead in north Austin hit-and-run crash
items.x: AUSTIN (KXAN) — Austin Police were in north Austin investigating a deadly auto-pedestrian crash Thursday morning. According to APD, someone called 911 around 2:17 a.m. to report that a driver hit a person in the parking lot of a shopping center in the 9500 block of North Lamar Boulevard, which is at the corner of North Lamar Boulevard and Rutland Drive. When officers arrived, they found the man dead. APD has not identified the victim publicly yet. APD also told KXAN the driver was not at the scene when officers arrived. items.t: Shadow Force: Inside Texas’ ICE-powered police network
items.x: AUSTIN (KXAN) Texas has become the epicenter of ICE’s expanding 287(g) program , with hundreds of agencies signing on, more officers gaining federal immigration powers and new funding driving further growth . In partnership with ProPublica and The Texas Tribune , KXAN investigators found that expansion has come with limited transparency , as agencies withheld records, redirected requests to ICE or fought disclosure. KXAN identified hundreds of authorized officers in the state, including more than a dozen with criminal charges or state disciplinary histories, raising questions about how they are vetted. As Texas puts more money, officers and power behind 287(g), KXAN is pushing for answers about a program that remains largely in the shadows. App users, click here to explore the investigation.

items.x: AUSTIN (KXAN) — Police were in east Austin Wednesday night investigating a stabbing that occurred at a coffee shop, which was followed by a crash as the suspect left the scene. APD confirmed two people were stabbed and taken to local hospitals by Austin-Travis County EMS. One of the victims had life-threatening injuries and the second had non-life-threatening injuries, according to police. As of 10:30 a.m. Thursday, APD said both were in stable condition. The suspect involved was identified as 20-year-old Shankar Temple Grace. According to police, he was charged with two counts of Aggravated Assault with a Deadly Weapon. Mugshot of Shankar T Grace (APD photo) APD officers responded to the stabbing call around 8:55 p.m. at The Buzz Mill, located at 1505 Town Creek Drive. According to APD, Grace left the scene in a pickup truck at a high rate of speed and crashed into an unoccupied autonomous vehicle. He was subsequently arrested after being questioned at the scene. 2 stabbed at The Buzz Mill followed by crash involving robotaxi, Austin police say. items.t: Austin attorney joins lawsuit demanding transparency over SpaceX Terafab deal
items.x: AUSTIN (KXAN) — In the search for answers, Marie Egyed filed a public information request in June. The Grimes County resident struggled understanding what went into a local Commissioners Court approval for SpaceX's "Terafab" to be built in the community. "Everything is going to change," worries Egyed. Announced earlier this year , the 100 million square foot facility will be a "vertically integrated semiconductor manufacturing and advanced computing fabrication facility." Terafab's website describes it as the "most epic" chip-building effort ever and shows its purposes as supporting other Elon Musk projects like Tesla cars or the "Optimus" robot. "We've been asking the same questions from day one," said Egyed. For months, the director of operations for Grimes County Citizens for Responsible Development wanted to see records relating to a tax abatement, reinvestment zone and communications behind the deal. But Egyed has yet to see a document she requested. Instead, the effort to release records has descended into a legal labyrinth pitting SpaceX against Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, Grimes County and locals. items.t: Group behind trans mailers must answer questions under oath, Travis County judge rules
items.x: (The Texas Tribune) Siding with efforts to discover who is behind mailers offering support for transgender youths, a Travis County judge ordered those behind the pamphlets to answer questions under oath later this week. Travis County District Judge Jan Soifer late Tuesday ordered depositions to be taken from a representative of the Texas Transgender Student Union, which was registered last month in Wyoming and has a mailing address linked to a post office box in Houston. The Transgender Education Network of Texas, known as TENT, requested the deposition, saying the mailers were worded to appear to come from TENT, prompting a backlash that included threats of violence. TENT also is seeking to identify the sender of text messages that linked to TENT’s website but did not come from the organization. The texts, which started arriving on phones across Texas on Oct. 12, advertised guides on “bathrooms and beyond for trans kids at school” or offered to answer questions about gender-affirming care in Texas. items.t: UT Austin names 3 faculty committees to oversee new core curriculum
items.x: AUSTIN (KXAN) The University of Texas at Austin announced Wednesday three faculty committees that will review courses for its new core curriculum, the first overhaul of the University's general education requirements in more than 20 years. Provost William Inboden, the University’s executive vice president, and Devin Stauffer, dean-designate of the new University College, sent the announcement to faculty. The college, which begins operating in January 2027, will oversee the new core curriculum. "Faculty expertise has shaped the new Core from the beginning, and faculty guidance remains essential as we move from its design to the development and implementation of courses," Inboden and Stauffer wrote in the email. What the new core curriculum is Under the plan, students would take 36 credit hours in the core curriculum, down from the current 42. The new core is organized into three pillars: arts and humanities, social sciences, and STEM. Current students will not be required to complete the new core. At the time, President Donald Trump said his goal was "we pick up five seats." With less than a week until election day, it appears Texas Republicans are set to underperform that lofty goal — and possibly lose one of their own seats in the process. Texas Republicans targeted five districts: TX-09, held by Rep. Al Green in Houston TX-28, held by Henry Cuellar in the Rio Grande Valley TX-32, held by Julie Johnson in North Texas TX-34, held by Vicente Gonzalez in the southern Coastal Bend and TX-35, moved to San Antonio after being held by Greg Casar in Austin A year later, the results appear far more modest. According to the Cook Political Report, only TX-32 is rated "Solid Republican," while TX-09 is rated "Likely Republican." TX-28 remains "Likely Democratic," TX-34 is "Lean Democratic" and TX-35 is considered a toss-up. The other three targets are not as solid as Republicans would have hoped when they initial drew the map. TX-28 is rated as "Likely D," and TX-34 is labeled "Lean D." items.x: Studio 512’s Blake Haynes sits down with writer, director, and executive producer Peter Berg to discuss the powerful true story behind Mosquito Bowl, a new World War II drama featuring Nicholas Galitzine, Bill Skarsgård, Ray Nicholson, and Tom Francis. From acclaimed filmmaker Peter Berg comes Mosquito Bowl , an emotional World War II drama that follows four promising young football players whose lives are forever changed when they answer the call to serve as U.S. Marines during one of history’s deadliest conflicts. Based on Buzz Bissinger’s bestselling book, the film combines brotherhood, sacrifice, and historical authenticity to tell a story that Berg believes remains just as relevant today as it was more than 80 years ago. While speaking with Studio 512’s Blake Haynes in Los Angeles, Berg shared why bringing these young men’s stories to the screen felt so important, how real archival war footage influenced the film, and what he hopes audiences take away from the experience. items.x: Studio 512’s Blake Haynes sits down with the stars of Netflix’s new World War II drama Mosquito Bowl to discuss honoring real-life heroes, the lasting impact of loss, and the emotional weight of telling a true story. Few films capture both the camaraderie of friendship and the devastation of war quite like Mosquito Bowl . The new Netflix film tells the harrowing true story of four college football players who became Marines and found themselves fighting in World War II. Blending the excitement of athletics with the realities of combat, the film shines a light on a generation whose lives were forever changed by war. Studio 512’s Blake Haynes caught up with stars Nicholas Galitzine, Bill Skarsgård, Ray Nicholson, and Tom Francis while in Los Angeles to discuss the emotional experience of bringing these real-life figures to the screen. Galitzine portrays John McLaughry, Skarsgård takes on the role of Bob Baumann, Nicholson plays Tony Butkovich, and Francis stars as Dave Schreiner. items.t: Dispute over house listing rules could boil over into lawsuit against Central Texas service
items.x: AUSTIN (KXAN) A dispute between Central Texas real estate listing service Unlock MLS and real estate company Compass could lead to an antitrust lawsuit over a rule that imposes $100 fines if a home for sale isn't listed with the service. The rule requires realtors list a property they represent with the service when it goes up for sale. "Only the law and the homeowner should tell agents how to publicly market a home, and Unlock MLS is neither the law nor the homeowner," said a Compass spokesperson. Unlock MLS said in its letter to Compass that the "Clear Cooperation Policy," or CCP, is required by the National Association of Realtors. Compass told KXAN that sellers and agents should not be obligated to pay a fine "to publicly market as the homeowner wants." "Unlock MLS seems to agree that agents can and should be able to publicly market a property as the homeowner instructs without negatively impacting the MLS, but only if the agent pays Unlock MLS a $100 fine," said Compass, directly responding to the letter. items.t: Six injured in three-vehicle crash in Niederwald
items.x: AUSTIN (KXAN) — Six people were involved in a three-vehicle crash Wednesday on Highway 21 in Niederwald, Texas, Wednesday evening. According to Travis County Fire Rescue, emergency crews responded to the crash and found six patients that needed help. One patient with critical injuries was flown by STARFlight , while another was airlifted by Air Life in serious condition. Three additional patients were taken by ambulance to area hospitals. A sixth person declined medical transport, according to TCFR. Fire officials said all patients were successfully extricated from the vehicles. Several agencies assisted at the scene, including Travis County Fire Rescue, Hays County EMS, Caldwell County EMS, Buda Fire EMS, STARFlight and Air Life. Highway 21 is closed in both directions as crews worked the scene and investigators gathered information, according to Travis County Fire Rescue.

items.t: Hayden Panettiere death ruled accidental by police in South Carolina
items.x: GREENVILLE, S.C. ( WSPA ) – Police in South Carolina have officially closed the investigation into the death of Hayden Panettiere, according to a Wednesday news release. Greenville Police Department officials said that Panettiere's death has been ruled accidental, based on findings in the investigation and the medical examiner's determination. On August 16, Panettiere was found unresponsive in an apartment at the Judson Mill Lofts on Easley Bridge Road. Police said that Brian Hickerson, Panettiere's on-and-off boyfriend, along with his brother, Zach Hickerson, were at the residence. EMS attempted life-saving measures before pronouncing Panettiere dead at 2:31 p.m. According to the Greenville County Coroner's Office, Panettiere had died from an accidental overdose of fentanyl, 4-ANPP, Alprazolam, Methocarbamol and Quetiapine. Panettiere had spoken openly about challenges in her personal life, including emotional scars from her childhood fame, postpartum depression after giving birth to her daughter, and struggles with alcohol addiction. items.t: District attorney Jose Garza responds to Abbott campaign ad
items.x: TRAVIS COUNTY, Texas (KXAN) Travis County District Attorney Jose Garza responded Monday to a Greg Abbott campaign ad targeting him over the dismissal of a murder charge against a man whose 1992 conviction in the case had been overturned. In 1991, Anita Byington died by homicide and Allen Andre Causey was charged with murder. He was sentenced to 50 years imprisonment, but received paroled in 2022 and was exonerated in 2025. “The family of Anita Byington deserves justice, and Mr. Causey deserves peace,” Garza said in the release. "Mr. Causey was wrongfully convicted of a crime he did not commit." Abbott's campaign press secretary Eduardo Leal said in a statement about the ad that Abbott intends to hold "rogue district attorneys accountable" if reelected. "District Attorney Jose Garza has repeatedly failed to deliver justice for Texas families like Kristina Byington's. He has let out countless convicted criminals, including murders, back onto the streets in the name of social justice," Leal said. Kristina Byington, Anita's cousin, voices in the ad . items.t: After a Stage 4 breast cancer diagnosis at 29, Austin woman urges others to know their risk
items.x: AUSTIN (KXAN) — As she approached her 30th birthday, Jacquelyn Stamatedes thought she was entering a new chapter of life. She and her husband had purchased their first home and were beginning to plan for a family. Instead, she received life-changing news: she had Stage 4 breast cancer that had already spread to her liver. "It was pretty frustrating to get like such a far-along diagnosis," Stamatedes said. A lump she first noticed years earlier Now 35, Stamatedes said her diagnosis did not come out of nowhere. She remembers feeling a lump when she was 18 or 19 years old. But because she was young and had no family history of breast cancer or other cancers, she said concerns were often dismissed. "So for my patient history as a young patient, no genealogy that would have led to it, no family history of cancer in the family at all, not just for breast," Stamatedes said. "I had been seen either at 18 or 19 because I felt a lump." Looking back, she wishes she had pushed harder for more answers and encourages others to do the same. "I know it's tough for younger patients because oftentimes we either don't have insurance or our insurance isn't top tier and you're out of pocket," she said.

items.t: Trump announces more relief for flood survivors
items.x: AUSTIN (KXAN) — Families impacted by this year's flooding across Central Texas could be getting more FEMA aid, according to President Trump. Trump made the announcement during a rally in Corpus Christi on Tuesday. The announcement comes after many families who lost homes during the flooding have been outspoken over FEMA's denial of individual assistance. Last week, KXAN crews spoke with people who had lost homes during the flooding in Kerr County, they said without more help they could not rebuild. "At the request of Ken Paxton and Sen. Ted Cruz I am pleased to announce I will be making available more FEMA relief funds from this year's floods in the Texas Hill Country," said Trump. "So we will work that out on Monday." "Survivors are hopeful to hear those words, but really are expecting to see something in writing," said Allison Brim-Estelle with Rebuild: The National Disaster Survivors Association. She says President Trump's announcement is promising, but it will only mean something and help survivors once it happens. items.t: Pflugerville council unanimously approves ‘SAFE’ Technology AI oversight policy
items.x: AUSTIN (KXAN) Pflugerville city council members voted unanimously on Tuesday to adopt an artificial intelligence oversight policy. It's called "SAFE," which stands for the Secure, Accountable, Fair and Explainable (SAFE) Technology policy. According to a press release from the city, it "sets standards for reviewing and approving technology that could affect residents' rights or access to City services. It also limits how City data can be used and shared." Pflugerville cancels Flock contract, covers and turns off cameras “Technology helps us serve our community better, but that shouldn’t come at the expense of privacy, accountability or public trust,” Mayor Doug Weiss said in the release. “Our residents deserve to know how these tools are used and what we're doing to protect their information. This policy allows us to embrace new technology while keeping the people we serve at the center of every decision.” Under the policy, city technology will be classified as low, moderate, or high risk based on how it's used and potential impacts, according to the release. High-risk systems, like surveillance and biometric identification technology, will require city council review and approval

items.t: CAMPO launches I-35 carpool program connecting Austin, Buda and Kyle
items.x: AUSTIN (KXAN) — CAMPO has launched a new carpool program aimed at helping commuters travel between Kyle, Buda and Austin as construction continues along Interstate 35. The program, known as We Ride I-35, was announced Wednesday and is being offered through CAMPO's regional Transportation Demand Management program. The initiative is designed to connect commuters with similar schedules and destinations who are interested in sharing rides. In partnership with CTXGO, the program matches participants based on their travel routes and commuting schedules. Users can choose to drive, ride as a passenger or alternate between the two options. Once matched, commuters arrange their own meeting locations and travel times. Program participants also have access to CTXGO's Guaranteed Ride Home feature, which provides eligible carpoolers with a free ride home if an unexpected situation arises. Commuters may also qualify for incentives through the CTXGO Commute Rewards program, earning up to $5 per day and a maximum of $150 for logging carpool trips. items.t: Austin firefighters say raccoon stuck in tree is ‘alive and unharmed’
items.x: AUSTIN (KXAN) A raccoon was stuck in a sticky situation, and Austin firefighters came to the rescue. Austin Firefighters Association said on Monday a concerned neighbor reported the raccoon had its head stuck in the hallow of a tree. Crews arrived at the site and used a catch pole to safely free and lower the raccoon to the ground. Austin Firefighters said the raccoon was handed over to animal control after the rescue. While some concerned Austinites were worried for the raccoon, Austin Firefighters assured that the furry friend was "alive and unharmed." "This rescue is a great example of what makes Austin firefighters such an important part of our community. The job goes beyond fighting fires and responding to emergencies ," AFA said, in part.

items.t: McNeil junior’s self-defense club earns her a Girl Scout Gold Award
items.x: AUSTIN (KXAN) Nikita Devasthale is a junior at McNeil High School who just earned her Girl Scout Gold Award , the highest achievement a Girl Scout can earn. To earn that award, Devasthale had to complete a community project that makes the world a better place. For her project, she chose to incorporate one of her longtime passions, martial arts. Devasthale is a second-degree black belt who trains at Golden Hands Martial Arts with Holly Holt, head teacher at Golden Hands, who helped her with her Gold Award project. Devasthale, with Holt's help, launched a self-defense club at her school last year. "Initially, I wanted to bring self-defense to the community as part of my Gold Award, and I wanted to start with the club because I think mostly I wanted to focus on teenagers since after high school you go to college and most people say that college campuses are relatively unsafe, so I wanted to make sure that they were trained or at least had knowledge of the skill in high school," Devasthale explained. "It was also accessible to them. Because I think the main reason people might not do martial arts is because either transportation or money, or they might not have the accessibility to it.

items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years. Inflation has risen this year amid the Iran war , creating a difficult set of circumstances for President Trump and the GOP this midterm cycle . items.t: CBP evaluates military ‘heat ray’ for potential use at US-Mexico border

The weapon, called the Active Denial System and commonly known as a “heat ray,” is designed to repel people by directing an invisible beam of electromagnetic energy at them. The Pentagon authorized a seven-month loan of the system to the Department of Homeland Security beginning in September, according to a memorandum first reported by CNN. The arrangement lets DHS test the equipment and develop procedures for potential border operations. In a statement to Border Report, a CBP spokesperson said: “CBP is continually evaluating new technology, especially technology that can save lives while simultaneously enhancing national security effectiveness.” The statement provided to Border Report did not identify where testing would occur, what circumstances would justify using the weapon, or what safeguards would govern its operation. PAST COVERAGE | Pandemic loan frauds took over $15.3M in Texas, $245.3M nationwide: DOJ According to the U.S. Department of Justice, Mago repeatedly committed loan fraud during the COVID-19 pandemic that undermined the Paycheck Protection Program (PPP). “Mago applied for and received several fraudulent PPP loans and Economic Injury Disaster Loans (EIDL) for several business entities totaling nearly $1 million,” the DOJ said. “Bank records revealed that Mago transferred the funds into his personal bank account and used them for multiple real estate purchases.” In addition to the prison sentence, a judge also ordered Mago to pay more than $900,000 in restitution, as well as a $250,000 fine.

James is accused of killing four people and injuring three others in Austin in December of 2023. Police said the attacks were random and James did not know the victims. His attorneys plan to argue James was not guilty by reason of insanity. The defendant has been diagnosed with schizophrenia. Authorities said he killed his parents in Bexar County before coming to Austin. The Bexar County Sheriff's Office said he was arrested for misdemeanor assault of his parents in 2022 , and he was discharged from the Army after a "domestic violence" issue. He served from 2013 to 2015. A competency trial took place Monday , where a different set of jurors ruled James was competent to stand trial, despite concerns raised by his psychologist that his delusions may be impacting his thinking too much. The State's psychologist, who conducted an independent assessment of James as part of this process, said she believed James recognized his delusions and was capable of understanding what was going on, therefore fit for trial. items.x: AUSTIN (KXAN) New data from the city of Austin shows efforts to slow drivers down are paying off in a big way. The latest Vision Zero Speed Management report confirms fewer serious and deadly crashes have been reported on streets where safety measures have been implemented. Among the most effective are speed cushions, pedestrian islands, and lower speed limits. Vision Zero is a city initiative with a goal of reducing the number of people hurt or killed by traffic crashes in Austin to zero. Pedestrian island in Austin. Speeding is the leading factor in severe traffic crashes nationwide, according to the report. "The risk posed by speed is not linear: as velocity increases, a driver’s field of vision narrows, braking distances increase and the impact force of collisions rises. This effect is most lethal for vulnerable road users like people walking or biking," the report said. A look at the data The city analyzed data from nearly 30 traffic-calming projects, roughly 800 miles of neighborhood streets, and dozens of arterial roads, similar to busy roads like Lamar Blvd. and Congress Ave. Across all categories, the results show positive safety trends and speed reduction. Morley had been convicted in 2022 and was serving a life sentence for the murder of a man in Carter County. Jacob Allen Morley was reported missing from a correctional center in Tennessee on Sunday night. The win provided a much-needed boost, but Sarkisian’s message heading into the final stretch of the regular season is simple. Sarkisian is turning to the “Mamba mentality” popularized by late NBA legend Kobe Bryant, emphasizing relentless preparation, focus and the ability to move on quickly to the next challenge. “Now is not the time for relief syndrome,” Sarkisian said. “Now is the time for a Mamba mentality.” That mindset could be critical for a Texas team that remains in the thick of the SEC race but has little margin for error. The Longhorns are 5-2 overall and 2-2 in conference play, with Mississippi State coming to Austin on Saturday. Linebacker Rasheem Biles said the team views every remaining game as a must-win opportunity. "For me, I feel like our season is on the line every game now," Biles said. items.t: 68 dead in high-speed train collision, Spain’s 2nd deadly rail crash this year
items.x: URDA, Spain (AP) — A high-speed train slammed into another that had stopped on the tracks in Spain on Wednesday, killing at least 68 people and injuring dozens in the second deadly rail collision this year. The regional government of Castilla La Mancha confirmed the death toll and said another 58 people were receiving medical treatment at hospitals. Rescue workers searched the wreckage through the day for survivors and bodies. The collision came just nine months after another deadly crash involving high-speed trains operated by the same two companies in southern Spain in January. “Today all of Spain is grieving,” Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said from the crash site, where he announced that his government would declare three days of national mourning. items.t: 4 in 10 say personal finances worsening: Survey
items.x: ( The Hill ) Four in 10 Americans say their personal finances are deteriorating, according to a new poll released shortly before November's midterm elections. In the NPR/PBS News/Marist Poll , 40 percent of people said their “personal family finances” have declined in the last 12 months, while 16 percent said the opposite. Forty-one percent said their personal family finances have “stayed about the same” within the prior year. Less than 1 percent of poll respondents were not sure about the state of their personal family finances within the last year, while three percent didn’t give an answer. The NPR/PBS News/Marist Poll was conducted two weeks out from Election Day, with the rise in cost of living being a major concern in this election cycle. September saw an uptick in annual inflation for Americans, with the cost of energy, gas and electricity rising from August to September. Democrats have campaigned on targeting the Trump administration's tariffs and the war in Iran — two factors behind U.S. price hikes. items.t: 33% say second attempt should follow failed execution: Survey
items.x: ( The Hill ) A third of Americans think that the government should try a second time to put 50-year-old Christa Pike to death after she survived Tennessee’s attempt to execute her by lethal injection last month. A four-day Reuters/Ipsos poll found 33 percent of American adults said a second attempt should be made to execute inmates who survive the first time, while 39 percent supported life in prison instead. On Sept. 30, Pike received two doses of the state’s lethal injection drug pentobarbital and survived. She was taken to a Nashville area hospital in an ambulance, where she received medical care and regained consciousness five days after. She was later discharged from the hospital and is back at the Deborah K. Johnson Rehabilitation Center, the women’s prison where she was housed for 30 years. Pike was sentenced to death for the 1995 beating and stabbing death of classmate Colleen Slemmer. The latest poll showed 52 percent Republicans, compared to 24 percent Democrats, support a second execution attempt. items.x: ( The Hill ) President Trump and Texas Senate candidate James Talarico (D) shared their competing visions Tuesday as the two held dueling rallies in the Lone Star State one week before the midterm elections. Trump did two rallies in Texas — the first in Corpus Christi and another in Lubbock . It’s his fourth trip to Texas to support Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton. Talarico held his own rally in Lubbock on Tuesday. He was in Corpus Christi on Saturday. The Texas race is one of the most contested and watched Senate races in the country. Talarico and Paxton remain close in the polls — Real Clear Polling calls the race a toss-up, with Talarico holding a slight lead. A Democrat winning the Senate seat would be a shock — none have won a U.S. Senate race in Texas since 1988, and Trump won the state by nearly 14 percentage points in the 2024 presidential election. Democrats are vying to take control of the House and the Senate. The party would need to win four seats to win control of the Senate. items.t: Flying taxis could carry passengers by 2030
items.x: (TestMiles) A British aerospace company has demonstrated an electric flying taxi that could eventually offer a new way to escape crowded city roads. The Flying Car Is Moving Beyond Science Fiction Los Angeles has spent decades trying to solve its traffic problems. Freeways expand, transit systems improve, and technology promises more efficient journeys. Yet travelling across the city can still take a remarkable amount of time. A British aerospace company believes part of the solution might be above the roads rather than on them. Vertical Aerospace has demonstrated an electric aircraft capable of taking off vertically, transitioning into conventional forward flight, and landing without a runway. The technology was publicly displayed at the Farnborough International Airshow in Britain, marking an important development in the company's plans to introduce commercial passenger flights. The aircraft is part of a growing category known as electric vertical takeoff and landing, or eVTOL. Unlike a conventional airplane, it does not require a runway for every departure. items.t: Toyota recalls more than 228,000 vehicles over risk of injury
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — Toyota is recalling more than 228,000 vehicles due to an issue with the second-row seat backs that could increase the risk of injury, according to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration. A notice by NHTSA says if a crash happens, the second-row seat backs may fail to remain secured. According to the notice, around 228,367 vehicles from the Toyota Sienna Hybrid 2022-26 are impacted. Dollar General sued by FTC, 20 states for allegedly overcharging customers Dealers plan to update the supplemental restraint system electronics control unit software. For vehicles equipped with the “Mobility as a Service” package, dealers plan to replace the two second-row seat backs free of charge, according to NHTSA. Owners should expect to receive notification letters in the mail around Dec. 7, according to the notice.

items.t: Instagram now testing videos up to 90 minutes long in major shift
items.x: ( KTLA ) Instagram is moving beyond its signature short-form videos, testing a new feature that allows creators to share content lasting up to 90 minutes, including podcasts, interviews and comedy shows. The Meta-owned platform announced Monday that it is testing a feature called "Features," which allows select creators to upload longer, horizontal videos that viewers can watch directly within the app. "For a long time, I have been against doing long-form video on Instagram," Instagram head Adam Mosseri said in a video posted Monday alongside Tessa Lyons, the company's vice president of product. "But we are actually gonna lean in for a bunch of different reasons." Lyons, who previously led product development for Instagram Reels, described the expansion as a new chapter for the platform. "It feels like a full-circle moment that we're here now talking about the beginning of our journey on long-form video," she said.
