items.t: Canned fruit sold at Walmart recalled in several states
items.x: (Gray News) - A voluntary recall over lead concerns has been issued for cans of Walmart fruit cocktail distributed to stores in at least seven states. The Food and Drug Administration said the recall applies to 15-ounce containers of Great Value Fruit Cocktail in Fruit Juice from Concentrate. Where the product was distributed More than 1,830 cases, or approximately 44,000 individual cans, were distributed to Walmart locations in Alabama, Arizona, Louisiana, New Mexico, Pennsylvania, Washington and Wyoming, the FDA said. How to identify the product The product is marked with lot number “6FCB 04 C2263” and a best if used by date of Sept. 1, 2027. Recall details The FDA initiated the recall for “potential contamination with elevated levels of lead” on Oct. 1. It was reclassified as a Class II recall on Oct. 20. According to the FDA, Class II recalls are issued when a product can cause temporary health effects with a remote possibility of serious issues. What customers should do Customers should throw the item away or return it to Walmart.

items.t: Wayne County Board of Education updates Buffalo K-8 school project
items.x: WAYNE COUNTY, W.Va. (WSAZ) - Tuesday night, the Wayne County Board of Education got an update on the new Buffalo K-through-8 school, including a first look at construction photos showing the concrete base is now complete. The estimated overall project cost is around $24 million. “We were fortunate enough to be able to get funding from the state,” Superintendent Todd Alexander said. “They realized the worthiness of that project, and we got a significant amount of funding from the state to make this happen,” the superintendent Todd Alexander said. The project adds a 66,000-square-foot wing to the existing Buffalo Middle School, which was built in 1980. Once complete, the wing will include new amenities for the school including a new cafeteria. The board said the project remains on track, with more updates to come as construction moves forward.

items.t: Commission tests election equipment ahead of Nov. 3
items.x: KANAWHA COUNTY, W.Va. (WSAZ) - Election preparations are underway in Kanawha County. The County Commission on Tuesday held a special meeting to test all equipment ahead of the midterms. The test, which was open to the public, makes sure machines and records are reset and ready to go, helping ensure a fair election, as required by state code. The general election is Tuesday, Nov. 3.

items.t: Halloween Hoedown haunts Nitro’s Living Memorial Park
items.x: NITRO, W.Va. (WSAZ) - The Halloween Hoedown haunted Nitro’s Living Memorial Park on Tuesday night. It started with a costume parade that began at the city’s library, before making its way to the park. The night featured DJ dances, costume contests, and a free trick-or-treat for the whole family. “You’re seeing smiles, you’re not hearing crying, you’re not seeing any trouble being had or anything like that. When we had the dance everybody’s up there dancing together; when we had the costume party everybody is just cheering everybody on,” said the City of Nitro’s Public Information Officer Joe Stevens. “It does bring the community together because there’s a lot of times you don’t see a lot of the folks until you do an event like this because everybody’s so busy these days.” A contest was held for costumes and dancing. Free hot dogs were also cooked up and served by the city council.

The law, that was signed by the president in July 2025, implemented several tax breaks for Americans and cut some social service programs. Derrick Van Ordern, R-Wis, at the GOP’s midterm convention in September. items.t: WSAZ’s own honored in 2026 class of West Virginia Broadcasting Hall of Fame
items.x: HUNTINGTON, W.Va. (WSAZ) - The West Virginia Broadcasting Hall of Fame held its 2026 induction ceremony at the Museum of Radio and Technology on Tuesday. WSAZ’s Susan Nicholas was honored, along with six other inductees. Joining Nicholas in the class of 2026 are: Alan Dye Jim Damron Will Shumate Dave Allen Michele Crist Randy Yohe The hall’s chairman, Thomas Resler, said those honored offer so much to the communities around them. “It’s important in the fact that we recognize the people that have such an effect on our lives,” Resler said. “They entertain us, they bring us the news, it connects our community.” Congratulations to everyone inducted this year!

items.t: Couple charged after 4 children removed from ‘deplorable conditions’, police say
items.x: MIDDLETOWN, Ohio ( WXIX /Gray News) - A couple is facing multiple charges of child endangerment and animal cruelty following a welfare check at their home in September, authorities said. Melanie and Christopher Todd were arrested after officers responded to their home on Cardinal Court to check on their children and animals, according to the criminal complaint. Police described the living conditions as “deplorable and unlivable.” Officers conducted the welfare check Sept. 29 after Middletown City Schools reported that two 10-year-old children appeared dirty and said they had no food to eat, police said. The children also said two cats were dead inside their home, the complaint said. During the check, officers found holes large enough to see outside in the walls and floors. One of the couple’s four children said the holes were caused by punching when Melanie and Christopher would get angry, the complaint said. items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — On this episode of Aging Untold, we examine the subtle, easily overlooked early warning signs of Parkinson’s disease and discuss when to talk with a physician. Then, we share how a grieving Michigan family turned heartbreak into hope by helping pair veterans and first responders with lifesaving service dogs. Parkinson’s doesn’t always start with a tremor — here’s what to watch for Parkinson’s disease can start long before a tremor and the subtle changes are easy to miss. items.t: ‘Amazed that she’s alive’: 18-year-old driver in ICU after hitting moose on icy road
items.x: ANCHORAGE, Alaska ( KTUU /Gray News) - A mother in Alaska said her 18-year-old daughter is lucky to be alive after hitting a moose Monday night while driving down an icy Anchorage road. “That’s what we’ve been hearing this entire ordeal, from the EMTs to the doctors; they are amazed that she’s alive,” Megan Stone said about her daughter’s crash. According to Stone, the collision occurred when her daughter Autumn was driving home and a moose appeared in the roadway. Stone said she does not believe her daughter had any time to brake. When firefighters arrived, they found a badly damaged vehicle with Autumn trapped inside. It took several crews to cut her out with the Jaws of Life hydraulic rescue tools. Anchorage firefighter Jason Dolph said moose are particularly dangerous when they are hit at highway speeds. “Typically when a car strikes a moose, that moose becomes suspended in the air,” Dolph said. “And when that moose then lands on the vehicle. items.t: General Motors to pay $220 million for selling drivers’ private data, Connecticut’s attorney general says
items.x: HARTFORD, Conn. (WFSB) - General Motors sold customers’ private driver behavior and location information to third parties, including data brokers who then sold it to insurance companies, according to Connecticut’s attorney general. Attorney General William Tong on Thursday announced that GM will pay $220 million as part of a settlement. Tong said the data was used by insurance companies to set insurance rates. He said the data collection impacted 123,143 people in Connecticut. Tong said he helped lead a coalition of 36 attorneys general in the case against GM, and that Connecticut will receive more than $6 million through the settlement. The settlement requires GM to obtain affirmative express consent from consumers before collecting or disclosing consumer driving and location data. According to the attorney general, Connecticut first began investigating GM and issued an initial notice of violation in 2024. items.t: Ukraine war continues despite Trump’s promise to end it
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - The war in Ukraine has lasted more than four-and-a-half years, and fighting continues despite repeated efforts by President Donald Trump to end the conflict. Trump made a pledge on the campaign trail dozens of times during the last presidential campaign. “Before I even arrive at the Oval Office shortly after I win the presidency, I will have the horrible war between Russia and Ukraine settled,” Trump said at a July 7, 2023, rally in Council Bluffs, Iowa. “Somebody said, are you on Russia’s side? Are you on Ukraine’s side? You know what? The side — I want people to stop dying. That’s the side I’m on.” That campaign promise has not been fulfilled. Trump has met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy twice at the White House. items.t: ‘She just lit up the room’: Toddler dies after being hit by car at a pumpkin patch, family says

The family of 21-month-old Nyxailia Hinton said they want answers after she died Tuesday. items.t: One transported to hospital following bed fire in Wethersfield, firefighters say
items.x: WETHERSFIELD, Conn. (WFSB) - A hospital bed fire closed a portion of Main Street in Wethersfield on Thursday morning. The Wethersfield Volunteer Fire Department said that it responded to a fire at 14 Main St. around 8:30 a.m. It closed the road in the vicinity. According to firefighters, they arrived to find that everyone who was in home made it outside, including the person who had been using the hospital bed. The bed was said to have been on the first floor. Crews encountered heavy smoke, but said they were able to quickly put the fire out. A female was transported to Hartford Hospital with burn injuries and smoke inhalation, the fire department said. Two other people suffered minor injuries. A cause for the fire remained under investigation as of Thursday afternoon. Main Street reopened to traffic around 9:45 a.m. Refresh this page and watch Eyewitness News for updates.

items.t: East Harford man dies in Route 2 crash, state police say
items.x: EAST HARTFORD, Conn. (WFSB) - A man from East Hartford was identified as the victim in a deadly crash that happened on Route 2 Wednesday night. State police said 67-year-old Richard Fusco was on the westbound side of the route just before the exit 2 off ramp in East Hartford. For an unknown reason, troopers said Fusco left his lane and hit a metal beam guardrail. His vehicle then continued across both travel lanes and crashed into a concrete barrier in the median. Fusco was pronounced dead at the scene, state police said. Route 3 northbound to Route 2 westbound was closed for the investigation. It has since reopened. State police sought dash camera footage and witnesses of the crash. Anyone with information was asked to contact Connecticut State Police at 860-534-1000.

items.t: ‘Breaking Away’ actress Barbara Barrie dies by medically assisted suicide, reports say
items.x: (Gray News) - Barbara Barrie, known for her 1979 role in “Breaking Away,” died Wednesday by medically assisted suicide, according to her daughter in a statement to The New York Times . Barrie was 95. Barrie had been diagnosed with terminal cancer and died in her New York City home, according to her daughter, Jane Harwick. Barrie’s agent, Gary Gersh, said her passing was “medically assisted in accordance with the New York State Medical Aid in Dying Law,” according to USA Today . In addition to “Breaking Away,” which earned her an Oscar nomination, Barrie also starred in several TV shows, including “Barney Miller” and “Suddenly Susan.” She also received a Tony nomination for her performance in the original production of “Company.”

items.t: Relocation offers on the rise as cities try big cash incentives to attract remote workers
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Remote work opportunities continue to thrive years after the COVID-19 pandemic made working from home mainstream. Now some communities across the U.S. are competing to attract new residents who are fully employed but can live anywhere, offering increasingly large cash incentives to lure remote workers. Cumberland, Maryland launched “Choose Cumberland,” a pilot program offering $20,000 to up to 10 people who agree to move to the city. The Appalachian Mountains community, located about 130 miles outside Washington D.C., saw its population decline from over 40,000 to less than 19,000 after several manufacturing companies and other large employers closed their doors starting in the 1970s. “At one time, the population of Cumberland was over 40,000 people,” said Mayor Ray Morriss. Program details and requirements The Cumberland incentive splits the money into two payments : $10,000 in relocation cash $10,000 for a down payment or approved home renovations Recipients must make Cumberland their primary residence for at least five years. “The people we are trying to entice are the people who are bringing their jobs with them,” Morriss said. items.t: Superstorm Sandy hit Connecticut 14 years ago
items.x: EAST HAVEN, Conn. (WFSB) - Superstorm Sandy hit Connecticut 14 years ago Thursday. The storm brought a 10-foot storm surge to the coast from Long Island Sound, wind gusts of 85 mph, and caused about $360 million in damage. Hundreds of thousands of customers were without power for about a week. In some cases, longer. Dozens of homes and businesses along the shore line, including Cosey Beach in East Haven, were destroyed or heavily damaged.

items.t: Gen Z has more debt than Millennials did at the same age

Ted Rossman, with nonprofit credit counseling agency Money Management International , said the agency has seen a 35% increase in demand from Gen Z clients in the past year. Their debt loads are about 12% higher than they were a year ago. Student loans, high rents and buy now, pay later plans are adding up and leaving many young adults living paycheck to paycheck with little savings. “That’s really showcasing a lot of these early career pressures,” Rossman said. “You have student loans, you have high housing costs. items.t: Antidepressants: What to know before you decide
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Feeling low, disconnected or not like yourself for weeks or months is different from a bad day. When it starts to affect sleep, energy or everyday life, it’s time to talk about support and treatment options. For some people, that could include an antidepressant. Start with a conversation with your provider Dr. Rhea Rogers, a board-certified physician, said the decision looks different for everyone. “Everybody is individualized so you can just talk with your provider,” Rogers said. Rogers said to recognize whether you’re feeling depressed and to look at signs such as loss of sleep, loss of energy or loss of motivation. Some people might also experience a triggering event that starts a downward spiral, which they can’t pull themself out of, she said. “When your quality of life is being affected, then you might want to look into antidepressant therapy,” Rogers said. Antidepressants are not “happy pills” Rogers cautioned that antidepressants do not take away sadness. “They’re not happy pills. items.t: The barbershop quartet tradition is alive in New Orleans
items.x: NEW ORLEANS ( InvestigateTV ) - On a Mid City evening, a four-part harmony rang out just off Canal Street. The group, Southern Tradition, has been around since 1999. The quartet is a place where a traditional American art form forges a friendship. “The main attribute to be a barbershop quartet singer is to not be embarrassed, just keep going,” said Karl Hansen. Four men with four different careers create one sound. Hansen is a doctor who sings bass. Hansen Eschette is a med tech singing tenor. Joe Jacquat is a civil engineer who sings baritone. Johnnie Oufnac is the only actual barber in this barbershop quartet, singing lead. “Being together for a long time helps us harmonize and understand where the other person is going,” Hansen said. Barbershop quartets have been around for more than a century. Though they can be found all over the world, ties to New Orleans are strong. “It really is the nexus of American music at its most basic level and a lot of it comes from New Orleans,” said Zachary Matherne. One of the city’s most famous native sons sang before he played. “Louis Armstrong was in a vocal quartet before he ever started playing a horn,” Matherne said. Matherne is an award-win

items.t: Nearly 11 million people in the U.S. could be living with undiagnosed diabetes
items.x: CHARLOTTE, N.C. ( InvestigateTV ) - Diabetes is the seventh leading cause of death in the United States, the No. 1 cause of kidney disease, and an estimated 40 million people are living with it nationwide. Despite decades of prevention education and major breakthroughs in treatment, doctors say diabetes continues to hit the South especially hard — including North Carolina. It can create serious long-term complications, including coronary artery disease, heart attacks, never damage, and amputations. But many people who have the disease may not know it. The CDC estimates around 11 million live with undiagnosed diabetes. “Every day, almost every hour” battle Andrew Tucker has lived with Type 2 diabetes for nearly two decades. He’s made major lifestyle changes but said managing the disease is still a daily fight. Tucker was diagnosed about 15 years ago, when he was 35. “Yes, for me, it is truly an everyday, almost every hour watching what I do,” Tucker said. Type 2 diabetes develops when the body doesn’t make enough insulin or doesn’t use insulin properly. Doctors say obesity is a major risk factor. items.t: This veteran is using his service dog to regain independence
items.x: ST. LOUIS, Mo. ( InvestigateTV ) - Veteran James Poggi served in the Marine Corps working in aviation. His time in the military led to a lifelong strain on his body, including five back surgeries and a below-the-knee amputation. “You go from being six foot three, 250 pounds and able to travel halfway across the world and do whatever they ask you to do, to being relying on wheelchairs, walkers, mobility devices, things like that, you become a vulnerable person that you never thought you’d be,” Poggi said. Poggi said he was in multiple accidents, hard landings, PT accidents and a car crash. He also developed spinal meningitis. “And that was all while I was active,” he said. To help ease some of the emotional toll, Poggi’s wife, who is also his caregiver, suggested he get a service dog. Service dog provides daily support Poggi got Teddy, a Goldendoodle, who serves as his service dog and daily lifeline. “You never went anywhere without your battle buddy. And he always, always better have your back. And that’s how it is. He’s always got my back,” Poggi said. The dog helped Poggi regain his independence by taking care of tasks many people take for granted. “His favorite thing is to retri

items.t: Man charged with murder, attempted murder in Westbrook, state police say
items.x: WESTBROOK, CT (WFSB) - A man faces murder and attempted murder charges following an incident in Westbrook, according to state police. They identified the suspect as 37-year-old John Bongiovanni. State police said they responded to a disturbance on East Pond Meadow Road on Wednesday around 5:25 p.m. Troopers said they arrived to find Bongiovanni outside of a home. Their investigation revealed two victims inside, both of whom suffered gunshot wounds, they said. LifeStar, an emergency medical helicopter, was called to the area. One victim was pronounced dead at the scene. The other was transported to Hartford Hospital in critical condition. Bongiovanni was charged with murder and criminal attempt to commit murder. He was held on a $3 million bond and given a court date of Thursday in Middletown. Troopers were on the scene until Thursday morning for the investigation. Jeff Miller, a resident, said the situation is unlike anything he has seen in the area. “Never, this has never happened around here. Kind of definitely threw me for a loop when I came down here,” Miller said. Watch Channel 3 and refresh this page for updates.

items.t: Crash causes backup on I-91 in Wethersfield
items.x: WETHERFSFIELD, Conn. (WFSB) - A crash led to a traffic backup on Interstate 91 northbound in Wethersfield on Thursday morning. According to the state Department of Transportation, the right lane was closed between exits 25 and 27. It has since reopened and the scene cleared. The two-vehicle crash was reported around 7:20 a.m. There’s no word on injuries or a cause. For real-time traffic updates, check the Channel 3 First Alert traffic map here .

items.t: 15 years ago, Winter Storm Alfred set Connecticut October snow record
items.x: CONNECTICUT (WFSB) - Thursday marked the 15th anniversary of Winter Storm Alfred, which brought enough snow to cancel Halloween in Connecticut. The storm set the all-time record for the biggest snowstorm in Connecticut in October. It dropped two feet of snow on some communities in 2011. Winter Storm Alfred led to more than 880,000 power outages. The outage total is a record that stands to this day.

items.t: Tennessee governor suspects Christa Pike’s sentence will stay the same after failed execution
items.x: NASHVILLE, Tenn. ( WSMV /Gray News) — Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee said he suspects Christa Pike’s sentence will remain the same following her failed execution last month, unless the courts determine otherwise. Lee’s comments on Pike Lee was asked Wednesday whether the state will try to execute Pike again or if he will commute her sentence to life in prison. “As it related to a particular individual like Christa Pike and her crime, she’s still incarcerated under the laws of the state of Tennessee,” Lee said. “I suspect her sentence will be the same as before unless determined otherwise by the courts.” Pike’s condition Pike was sentenced to death for the 1995 murder of Colleen Slemmer. In September, Pike survived two doses of the lethal injection drug. The execution attempt failed. Pike is back in prison after spending days in the hospital. She is now able to speak in full sentences and walk on her own. Pike survived two doses of the lethal injection drug.(DEPARTMENT OF EMERGENCY COMMUNICATIONS, TENNESSEE DEPARTMENT OF CORRECTION, ASSOCIATED PRESS) Executions paused, commissioner resigns Lee has paused executions through the end of the year to determine what went wrong in Pike’s attempt.

items.t: Connecticut DPH reports several flu deaths already this season
items.x: HARTFORD, Conn. (WFSB) - Six people have died from flu-related complications so far this seas, according to the Connecticut Department of Public Health. The department said flu season started in late September. The six were the state’s first flu deaths of the season. All of them were adults 55 and older, according to the department. Deaths reported earlier than last year State officials said the first flu death this season was reported about a month earlier than last year. Last year, the first reported death came the week of Oct. 25 . Health officials said the virus is already more active than usual for this time of year. Doctors urge vaccination Peak flu season is typically December to February. Doctors warned that late-October is the time to get vaccinated. State officials urged people to get a flu shot before cases pick up later this winter. Doctors said people 65 and older, infants and young children, and those with chronic health conditions are at higher risk for serious flu complications and should get vaccinated. They recommended that everyone who is able get the shot to protect the greater community. Paul Anthony, assistant director of infectious diseases at Hartford Hospit

items.t: Fire closes part of Route 32 in Willington
items.x: WILLINGTON, Conn. (WFSB) - A structure fire shut down part of Route 32 in Willington on Wednesday night. The state Department of Transportation reported the closure just before 10:30 p.m. near Plains Road. The CT DOT said the road reopened Thursday morning. Channel 3 have reached out to the Willington Fire Department to learn whether or not anyone was hurt. It has not yet responded.

items.t: Trial expected to begin for man accused of fatally hitting girlfriend with pickup truck
items.x: BURLINGTON, Conn. (WFSB) - A trial is expected to begin Thursday in a case against Cooper Oullette, who is accused of hitting and killing his girlfriend with his pickup truck after a night of underage drinking. Oullette is charged with manslaughter in the 2023 death of 17-year-old Sophie Ringquist. State police said Oullette and Ringquist were in an on-again, off-again relationship and had been arguing during a party . Oullette originally told troopers that Ringquist fell out of the truck. They said they later determined she was hit by a car. Ringquist’s family has sued Ouellette, a liquor store, and the party host for allegedly providing alcohol to Oullette.

items.t: Clinton police use drone to find juveniles accused of stealing car and fleeing into woods
items.x: CLINTON, Conn. (WFSB) - Police used drone technology to find five juveniles accused of stealing a car early Wednesday morning, according to the Clinton Police Department. Police said they responded to the area of Sols Point Road around 4 a.m. for suspicious activity. Officers said they found a stolen vehicle driving in the area and used stop sticks to blow out its tire. The vehicle proceeded to drive down East Main Street and pulled into the back parking lot of the Clinton Police Headquarters, according to the department. Police said five juveniles got out of the car and ran into the surrounding neighborhood and woods. A K-9 team tracked the driver on the ground while officers used a drone to track the juveniles from above, investigators said. All five juveniles were located and apprehended, according to police.

items.t: Border Patrol agent charged with murder in wife’s death
items.x: LAREDO, Texas ( KGNS /Gray News) — A U.S. Border Patrol agent in Texas has been charged in connection with the death of his wife. Abel Garza, 30, has been charged with murder, a first-degree felony, in the death of his wife, 28-year-old Mayra Alejandra Landeros, after a domestic disturbance in south Laredo. U.S. Customs and Border Protection confirmed in a statement that Garza is a Border Patrol agent. Garza also is charged with two counts of endangering a child and two counts of abandonment of a child. All four counts are second-degree felonies. He was transported to Webb County Jail, and his bond was set at $1 million. What police say happened The incident happened just before 3 a.m. Wednesday at a home near Texana Street and Nocona Street. Chief Miguel Rodriguez said police were initially called about a man knocking on doors asking for help. A police drone spotted a car leaving as officers arrived. Officers stopped the car and found Landeros in the back floorboard with critical stab wounds. A U.S. Border Patrol agent is charged with fatally stabbing his wife in Texas. items.t: Economist explains how the ‘K-shaped economy’ is impacting the midterms
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - As voters prepare to head to the polls for the midterm elections, a conflicting economic sentiment is once again emerging on the campaign trail. “Voters reflect the perception of the cost of living as they experienced, as opposed to what is in the data,” said Alessandro Rebucci, an economics professor at Johns Hopkins Carey Business School. “In the data, you have an economy that is very strong as a whole. How that pie is distributed affects how a large segment of the population and the voters are feeling about the economy right now.” The contradiction has been described by many economists recently, as the “k-shaped” economy, using a graph to depict how high-income earners and asset owners are doing compared to middle and lower-income earners. “To be concrete, the wealthiest households are presumed to spend much more than the lowest ones, not only in absolute terms, which is obvious, but also as a share of their income and in their wealth,” Rebucci said. In recent months on the campaign trail, President Donald Trump has said that the U.S. economy is doing well, often conflicting with what recent consumer surveys have found on voters’ economic opinions. “The ec

items.t: Bridgeport police investigating two shootings
items.x: BRIDGEPORT, CT. (WFSB) - Bridgeport police are investigating two shootings. Police say that the first incident happened at around 1:19 p.m. in the area of Reservoir Avenue and Alba Avenue. Officers located a 20-year-old man suffering from multiple gunshot wounds. He was taken to the hospital and is in critical condition. The second happened at around 4:00 p.m. A 17-year-old male walked into the hospital with a gunshot wound. He was listed in stable condition. No arrests have been made, and police say they have no reason to believe the two were connected. Anyone with information is asked to call Detective Timothy Leonard at (203) 581-5253, or Detective Albert Palatiello at (203) 581-5226.

items.t: High school student accused of trying to make bombs for ISIS, deputies say
items.x: GAINESVILLE, Fla. ( WCJB /Gray News) - A Florida high school student was arrested after an investigation into his contact with a terrorist organization revealed he was attempting to make bombs, authorities said. Alachua County sheriff’s deputies said the 15-year-old is a student at Buchholz High School. The sheriff’s office and FBI conducted a joint investigation on Friday at the teen’s home after investigators learned he was having online conversations with members and supporters of the Islamic State group, also known as ISIS. Investigators say the teen asked for help to build drones and explosives to attack people at an unknown location. Authorities spoke with the 15-year-old’s parents, who allowed them to search the boy’s phone. They reportedly found files containing instructions for making explosive devices and chemical compounds, as well as ISIS propaganda. On Monday, investigators searched the teen’s home with his parents’ consent after they revealed the information found on the phone. Inside, they found two jars in his bedroom. items.t: Fact check: Governor candidates’ claims on food taxes and electric bill charges
items.x: HARTFORD, Conn. (WFSB) - Two claims from the final debate between Gov. Ned Lamont, a Democrat, and Sen. Ryan Fazio, the Republican candidate for governor, were fact checked ahead of Tuesday’s election. A fact check found Fazio’s claim that Lamont raised taxes on food is misleading. Lamont did eliminate one public benefits charge on electric bills, but the change may not be permanent, the fact check found. Food tax claim Fazio criticized Lamont for raising taxes on the food people eat. The claim is misleading because only a small number of specific foods are taxed in Connecticut. “He has raised taxes on your food, on your paycheck, on online purchases, and more,” Fazio said during the debate. The statement is true, but not in the way people might expect, according to the fact check. Connecticut added a 1 percent surcharge on top of the regular 6.35 percent sales tax, but it applies only to prepared food and drinks. Restaurant meals, takeout and delivery are taxed at 7.35 percent in total. The same law requires supermarkets to charge that tax on prepared meals, such as deli sandwiches, hot foods and salad bars. items.t: ‘Pretty low individual’: Man scammed by fake life insurance agent shortly after sister’s death
items.x: CORINTH, Miss. ( WTVA /Gray News) — A Mississippi man says he was scammed shortly after the death of his sister. According to Tim Williams, he was called by a woman who identified herself as the life insurance agent for his sister, Stephanie Jeanine Williams Machado. The woman gave him account numbers and policy numbers, and requested $1,375 for the insurance company to release payment to the Corinthian Funeral Home. Williams said he entered a three-way phone call with the woman and the funeral home, and that it all seemed to be legitimate. All the money he had available at the time was $620, and the woman told him to send it. When Williams asked how the woman would like the funds sent, she said to get it to her however was easiest, either by going to the insurance office or via the Cash App. Williams said he sent the money to his nephew, who then sent it through the app. However, Williams said the funeral home told him it never received payment, so he looked up the number and found that it belonged to a man who lived in Alabama. items.t: College professor among 2 found dead in home; suspect in custody, police say
items.x: LORAIN COUNTY, Ohio. ( WOIO /Gray News) - An Ohio college professor and a woman were found shot to death in a home, and a suspect is in custody, according to authorities. Wednesday morning, police responded to the Oberlin College Conservatory lot at 77 E. College St. to assist firefighters with a vehicle smoking and possibly on fire. When crews arrived, they tried to find the registered vehicle owner, identified as Daniel Jones, 31, to conduct a welfare check. When officers arrived at Jones’ home to check on his family, they found the victims dead inside the home. Pipo Nguyen-Duy, a professor of studio art and photography at Oberlin College, was found dead on the first floor with an apparent gunshot wound. A woman found dead on the second floor was not immediately identified. She also had an apparent gunshot wound. Jones was located aat bout 10:20 a.m. and taken into custody. Charges are pending. The investigation is ongoing.

items.t: International fugitive sentenced for one of the largest health care fraud schemes in U.S. history
items.x: COLUMBIA, S.C. ( WIS /Gray News) - A man whom federal prosecutors called the architect of one of the largest health care fraud schemes in U.S. history was sentenced Monday. Herbert Kimble was sentenced to 20 years’ imprisonment with three years of court-ordered supervision. He was also ordered to pay more than $199 million in restitution to Medicare and forfeit more than $195 million in what prosecutors described as “ill-gotten gains.” Kimble pleaded guilty in 2019 to conspiring to commit health care fraud, violate the anti-kickback statute, and defraud the United States in connection with a telemedicine and durable medical equipment scheme involving back, shoulder, wrist, and knee braces. Prosecutors say Kimble ran offshore call centers that recruited elderly Medicare beneficiaries, paid kickbacks to telemedicine companies for signed prescriptions, then sold those orders to medical equipment companies that billed Medicare. Court filings put the intended loss at more than $400 million, with Kimble personally gaining more than $195 million. items.t: New Haven restricts ‘juice bars’ for minors ahead of Halloween weekend
items.x: NEW HAVEN, Conn. (WFSB) - New Haven passed two ordinances on so-called “juice bars,” where minors can buy nonalcoholic drinks during events at bars. New Haven police and Mayor Justin Elicker are expected to discuss a crackdown during a news conference Wednesday afternoon. City officials said juice bars often host under-age events in separate areas of bars and nightclubs; however, the city said some open alongside other events where alcohol is served. In an effort to protect teenagers, the city said it would not issue these businesses event permits Friday through Sunday ahead of Halloween weekend. New rules bring restrictions One ordinance prohibits new juice bars from opening. The other created a permit process for events at existing businesses. It was meant to make existing juice bars safer and hold repeat violators accountable. Businesses could face fines of $2,500 to $10,000 for offenses. City leaders also moved forward with objections to liquor permit renewals at three businesses following repeated public safety and quality of life concerns. items.t: 49 registered sex offenders live within a mile of new Norwich elementary school
items.x: NORWICH, Conn. (WFSB) - A new elementary school is being built in the Greeneville section of Norwich, and 49 registered sex offenders live within a mile of it. Connecticut has no laws on where sex offenders can live in relation to schools, and one lawmaker is pushing to change that. Greeneville Elementary, on Golden Street, is one of four new elementary schools going up in the city. It is expected to open in August 2027. Registry check Registered sex offender Joseph Dunion is still in custody weeks after police say he grabbed and kissed a 14-year-old girl near her bus stop on Boswell Avenue, not far from the school site. A check of the state’s sex offender registry found that Dunion lives within a mile of the school, along with 48 other registered sex offenders. Dunion has been a registered sex offender for close to 30 years. Norwich’s superintendent said the bus stop was moved after the incident. The superintendent said in a written statement that the location of one person’s home cannot determine where a school is built. “The presence or address of a particular individual at one point in time cannot provide a permanent or reliable basis for determining where a school should be bu

items.t: For politics, what is an October surprise?
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - An October surprise is an event that could shake up an election, but does it often make the difference? Matt Dallek, a professor of political management at George Washington University, described it as “an event that, at least in theory, has the potential to shake up an election, something that people did not foresee coming that upends the debate.” He said the term dates back to around the 1980 election, when President Jimmy Carter failed to secure the release of American hostages being held in Iran before November 4, 1980, election day. Carter lost to Republican rival Ronald Reagan. Several surprises have occurred in the years since. Surprises can be driven by a campaign or by news events. Examples include Iran-Contra-related indictments in 1992 and the global financial collapse in 2008. Dallek said those surprises likely did not change the outcome of the election that November. “There’s no evidence that they flip a dynamic that was already in place,” Dallek said. “What’s more typical is that an event occurs, it dominates the news cycle and the trend line starts to move further toward the candidate who was already doing well, who was already likely to prevai

items.t: Library says person threw box of cockroaches at a staff member, prompting closure
items.x: TOLEDO, Ohio ( WTVG /Gray News) - A cockroach attack forced the closure of a library in Ohio this week. Surveillance footage was released by the Toledo Lucas County Public Library, appearing to show a person throwing a box of cockroaches at a staff member on Tuesday at the Kent Branch Library. Surveillance footage apparently shows someone throwing a box of cockroaches at a library employee in Ohio. (Source: Toledo Lucas County Public Library) A library spokesperson confirmed the throwing of the box of cockroaches at the library worker on Collingwood Blvd. But it wasn’t immediately shared what led up to the cockroach attack. The library was said to have gone into restricted access before closing for the rest of the day for cleanup and remediation. The Kent Branch Library reopened Wednesday. Officials did not say whether anyone would be facing any charges.

items.t: Farmington’s Stanley-Whitman House is a stop on Connecticut’s Haunted Historic Trail
items.x: FARMINGTON, Conn. (WFSB) - The Stanley-Whitman House in Farmington, built between 1709 and 1720, is one of many stops on Connecticut’s Haunted Historic Trail. The house has changed hands over the years, and legends from the original Puritan settlers remain, including their praise of God and fear of Satan. The Smith family One of the first families to live in the house was the Smiths, who saw two young boys die there, according to the report. “Steel and Samuel. They died in about 1729. Really within weeks of each other. Early childhood death was common,” said Andy Verzosa, executive director of the Stanley-Whitman House. The house is laid out and furnished to recreate what it would have looked like three centuries ago. The cemetery The museum also offers programming in a nearby private cemetery named Memento Mori, which is Latin for “remember, you will die.” Thomas Barnes founded the cemetery in the 1600s. His wife, Mary, was one of the last Connecticut women hanged for witchcraft, according to the report. Verzosa told a story about Capt. Ebenezer Mix. “There was Captain Ebenezer Mix. items.t: Enfield voters weigh green lighting school construction project
items.x: ENFIELD, CT. (WFSB) - Enfield voters are weighing whether to green light a school construction project or not. The project, which is set to cost $511 million, would completely renovate four elementary schools, close one, and convert another into an academy. Bob Cressotti, who has spent 10 years on Enfield’s Town Council and previously served as mayor, says he is optimistic the proposal will go through. He called it generational and a historic opportunity for the town and its children. He also said it is necessary and that some of the schools, which were built 60-70 years ago, are in desperate need of renovations. “This project is definitely necessary. You look at the structures, the buildings are 50-60 years old. A lot of work is needed at the schools, roofs, windows and at this point, it’s not that they’ve been neglected, but it’s time for the buildings to get renovated,” he said. He added that there is bipartisan support on the town council and with state grants and reimbursements, taxpayers will be on the hook for a maximum of $89 million. However, that means property taxes will be going up. “It will solidify our school system and I just think facility wise and the new technolog

items.t: Heavy police presence seen on Cutler Street in New London
items.x: NEW LONDON, Conn. (WFSB) - Police are conducting an active investigation at a home on Cutler Street in New London on Wednesday afternoon. The mayor said the activity is not an emergency response and is an investigation. No further details were released. Eyewitness News will provide more details as soon as they become available.

items.t: Grandmother not indicted in baby’s death after police say she left her in hot car for 8 hours while she worked
items.x: MADISONVILLE, Ky. ( WFIE /Gray News) — A Kentucky doctor who accidentally left her grandchild unattended in a hot car for about eight hours will not be indicted for the baby’s death. Madisonville police said 10-month-old Scottie Crowell died in August . On Tuesday, a grand jury found there was insufficient probable cause for an indictment. Police said Scottie’s grandmother picked her up in the morning of Aug. 13 and was supposed to take her to daycare. She forgot the child was in the car and went to work, police said. She arrived at Owensboro Health Multi-Care, where she works as a doctor, around 8 a.m. The baby’s father called his wife after trying to pick up Scottie from daycare, but the child was not there. The baby’s mother called the grandmother at work, and the grandmother ran outside and saw Scottie was still in the vehicle around 4 p.m., police said. After 911 was called, first responders tried to administer lifesaving measures, but the baby died. “I would ask that you keep the infant’s parents and family in your thoughts and prayers as they continue to grieve and process this unimaginable loss,” said Commonwealth’s Attorney Hannah Kington-Jarvis.

items.t: Huskies end preseason in style with dominant win over Purdue
items.x: HARTFORD, Conn. (WFSB) - The UConn men’s basketball team ended its preseason with a dominant 76-53 win over the Purdue Boilermakers. The Huskies shot much better from the floor than Purdue, making 43.1% of their attempts and 28.6% of their shots from three point range. The Boilermakers only shot 32.8% from the floor and a poor 8% from behind the three point line. Colben Landrew led the team in scoring with 15 points. C.J. Cox was the top scorer for Purdue with 18. Nik Hamenia had the most rebounds for UConn with 11 and Silas Demary Jr. had the most assists with five. The Huskies now move into regular season play. Their first game will be against the Gardner-Webb Runnin’ Bulldogs at PeoplesBank Arena next Monday. items.t: Widow searches for lost wedding ring when husband dies 3 days after getting married in Las Vegas
items.x: LAS VEGAS ( KVVU /Gray News) — A South Dakota woman is asking for help finding the wedding ring her husband lost in Las Vegas the night they married. Tammy Bishop and Will Mulroy were married Oct. 20 at the Viva Las Vegas Chapel. Bishop said they celebrated on a party bus and toured the Strip. At a bar, though, she says Mulroy looked down and realized his ring was gone. “We got to a bar. He looked down and his band was gone. He lost it. He started crying,” Bishop said. According to Bishop, he told her the ring was two sizes too big because he had lost weight. She said the ring may have slid off on the bus or while he moved into his wheelchair. It may also have come off while he rolled down the Strip. “We backtracked our steps. We told the bus driver. We had everyone looking. We couldn’t find it,” she said. The next day, she joked with him: “You didn’t even have your ring on for 24 hours and you lost it.” Everyone laughed, she said. “I said it’s not a big deal; we will buy you a new one, but now that he is gone it is a big deal to me,” Bishop said. Sadly, Bishop said Mulroy died just three days after their wedding. She said he was in a lot of pain on the way home and mentioned going

items.t: Southbury student arrested after reportedly bringing BB gun to school, police say
items.x: SOUTHBURY, Conn. (WFSB) - A student at Pomperaug High School was arrested on Wednesday after bringing a BB gun to school in a backpack, according to the Southbury Police Department. Police said the school administration and the department resolved what they described as an isolated incident. The student did not have the BBs or CO2 cartridges needed to fire the item, officials said. The student cooperated with police and said they did not know the item was in the backpack until arriving at school, according to police. School administrators and the school resource officer addressed the situation within minutes of the discovery, police said. Officials said the BB gun was never displayed, no threats were made, and no students or staff were harmed or placed in danger. The student was arrested and is being charged with breach of peace and possession of a dangerous weapon. The student is scheduled to appear in Waterbury Juvenile Court. No further details were released. Eyewitness News will provide more details as soon as they become available.

items.t: Norwich water outage planned overnight Wednesday into Thursday
items.x: NORWICH, Conn. (WFSB) - Water service in the Fitchville neighborhood will be temporarily disrupted from 8 p.m. Wednesday, Oct. 28, to 6 a.m. Thursday, according to Norwich Public Utilities. The utility company said the work supports a Connecticut Department of Transportation culvert project at Bentley Brook and requires relocating a major water transmission line from the bridge. The utility is working overnight to limit the disruption to potentially thousands of customers. NPU will deliver bottled water and gallon jugs to affected customers Wednesday afternoon and recommends filling bathtubs or large containers ahead of the outage. After service returns, customers who see cloudy water should run their cold taps for five to 10 minutes, the utility said. NPU said a similar but shorter outage will likely be needed in the coming weeks. No further details were released. Eyewitness News will provide more details as soon as they become available.

items.t: Connecticut’s Beardsley Zoo sees higher animal activity in winter
items.x: BRIDGEPORT, Conn. (WFSB) - Winter offers a different view of the animals at Connecticut’s Beardsley Zoo, according to the zoo’s curator of education. Jim Knox, curator of education, said animal activity increases as temperatures drop. “As the mercury drops, the animal activity levels increase, so this is the best time to see animals. Their activity levels are high, they’re doing their thing,” Knox said. Many of the animals at the zoo are naturally adapted to colder climates. Some explore their habitats, move around and interact with their surroundings when temperatures drop. Visitors can see a baby spider monkey and a baby Chinese goral. The zoo also welcomed a red panda cub, Pabu, this year. Pabu will be on view in a few weeks. The zoo is continuing to care for the young animals as they grow. The zoo adjusts its care throughout the winter. It provides heated indoor spaces and other accommodations for animals when temperatures drop.

items.t: ‘I miss her like crazy’: Loved ones remembering post office worker hit and killed by car
items.x: FORT THOMAS, Ky. ( WXIX /Gray News) - Loved ones and a Kentucky community are mourning a post office worker who was hit and killed by a car while walking earlier this month. Marchelle Bertram worked at the front desk of the Fort Thomas Post Office for years, helping people who came in. Sadly, she lost her life in a collision in Bellevue on Oct. 15. Her daughter, Whitney Bertram, said she is remembering her mother while seeing a large amount of support from the community following her death. “There are so many people I don’t know whose lives she’s touched and affected,” Whitney Bertram said. The crash occurred while Marchelle Bertram was walking on Memorial Parkway near her home. Her daughter said she rushed to the hospital after learning her mother had been hit by a vehicle. “Given the grave amount of injuries she sustained, there was no way she was going to survive,” she said. Marchelle Bertram died at the hospital. Whitney Bertram said the driver stayed at the scene and believes the crash was an accident. “I miss her like crazy; I try not to think about it too hard because I’ll break down,” she said. According to Whitney Bertram, there has been an outpouring of support telling he

items.t: Ernie Johnson announces this will be his final season on ‘Inside The NBA’
items.x: (Gray News) - Ernie Johnson announced he will be stepping down as host of “Inside the NBA” at the end of the season. The Sports Broadcasting Hall of Famer took to social media on Wednesday to explain his decision to step away, saying, “It’s just time.” Johnson, 70, stated that he would not be retiring, but cutting back. “This is by no means the end. It’s just a turning of the page,” Johnson said. “And I’ll forever cherish every chapter we have written with ‘Inside the NBA.’” Johnson said he plans to continue to work, including covering the NCAA men’s basketball tournament for CBS and Turner Sports. The six-time Sports Emmy Award winner acknowledged that he has dealt with heart issues in recent years, but that isn’t the reason he’s stepping away from the show. “I just want to slow down a bit,” he added in his social media post. Johnson joined Turner Sports in 1989 and has hosted “Inside the NBA” since 1990. He thanked his TNT Sports and ESPN crews for their support over the years, as well as the viewers. “I just want to say thanks to you. Thanks for your loyalty, for your love, for your support. And on this day, for your understanding,” Johnson said.

items.t: Police department closes its investigation into Hayden Panettiere’s death
items.x: GREENVILLE, S.C. ( WHNS /Gray News) - The Greenville Police Department said it has officially closed its investigation into the death of Hayden Panettiere. Police said Panettiere’s death has been ruled accidental based on the medical examiner’s determination and the findings of the investigation. Panettiere, 36, died from an accidental overdose involving multiple prescription medications and fentanyl, according to findings previously released by the Greenville County Coroner’s Office. Toxicology testing determined the cause of death to be the toxic effects of fentanyl, 4-ANPP, alprazolam, methocarbamol and quetiapine. An autopsy showed no signs of contributing trauma. On Aug. 16, Panettiere was found unresponsive inside an apartment in Greenville, where she had been temporarily staying. Dispatchers received a 911 call reporting a woman in cardiac arrest at approximately 1:51 p.m. She was pronounced dead at 2:32 p.m. Her on-and-off boyfriend Brian Hickerson and his brother Zach Hickerson were at the apartment where she died. The coroner’s office had previously closed its case after the cause and manner were established. Police said at the time their independent investigation remaine

items.t: Trump says US will beat China in AI as technology emerges
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - Artificial intelligence has emerged as the critical sticking point between the U.S. and China. President Donald Trump, who has named it “super intelligence,” insists the U.S. will beat China in the AI competition. Trump said while campaigning for president that tariffs would form the crux of the bilateral relationship. The U.S. and China, the world’s two largest economies, have been engaged in a trade war during both of Trump’s terms. Speaking Sept. 13 in Ireland, Trump said the U.S. is leading China in AI. “We’re leading China in AI, we’re the most sophisticated country in the world, and frankly, I want to keep it that way because whoever wins AI, wins,” Trump said. During a state visit to Beijing in May, Trump praised Chinese President Xi Jinping. “And it’s to me an honor. We’ve had a fantastic relationship. We’ve gotten along. When they were difficulties, we worked it out,” Trump said. Trump hosted Xi at the White House in September for a state visit. He touted what he called “the tremendous strides” he and Xi had already made on national security, trade and technology. At the summit, the U.S. and China agreed to extend a trade truce until January. No agre

items.t: Norwalk police search for missing 36-year-old man with medical condition
items.x: NORWALK, Conn. (WFSB) - Police in Norwalk are seeking the public’s help in locating a missing man. 36-year-old Justin Beramendi has been reported missing and was last seen wearing a white hooded sweatshirt, gray or white sweatpants, and gray and white sneakers, according to the police department. Beramendi is 5 feet 6 inches tall and weighs 130 pounds, police said. He has short brown hair and brown eyes and now wears contacts. Officials said Beramendi needs medication for a medical condition. No further details were released. If anyone who has any information regarding his whereabouts or knows where he is, you are asked to call 911. Eyewitness News will provide more details as soon as they become available.

items.t: Man loses more than $4,000 after scammers spoof father’s number, claim parents are at gunpoint
items.x: SCOTTSDALE, Ariz. ( KPHO /Gray News) - A man lost thousands of dollars after getting a call that appeared to come from his father’s phone number, with a stranger claiming his parents were being held at gunpoint. Curtis Indyke was asleep around 11:30 p.m. on Oct. 21 when he got a call that appeared to be from his dad, who lives in Virginia. Indyke lives in Arizona. “I answer the phone and it’s not my dad. It’s some other male saying he has my parents basically at gunpoint,” Indyke said. The caller told him to pay or his parents would be shot. While still on the phone, Indyke said he texted 911 to report his parents were being held hostage in Virginia. The person who claimed to be holding Indyke’s parents hostage continued making threats. In a panic, Indyke sent more than $4,000 through Apple Pay to two separate phone numbers. “And they also wanted $1,000 worth of crypto gift cards, which I’ve never even heard of. I’m in IT and I’ve never even heard of them,” Indyke said. Indyke said his bank blocked that purchase. After the call ended, Indyke called his dad’s number back, but no one answered. “But then I got scared because, what if the guy had his phone still?” Indyke said. Police i

items.t: 8-month-old dies after left alone in running bathtub, police say
items.x: STERLING, Va. (Gray News) - A Virginia woman was arrested after her 8-month-old died after being left unattended in a bathtub, according to authorities. Rosellena Pisani, 30, was arrested and charged with homicide, two counts of child abuse and three counts of child endangerment, a press release said. On Sept. 12, emergency medical personnel and sheriff’s deputies responded to the residence after receiving a call about an unresponsive infant. Investigators determined the baby had been left unsupervised in a bathtub with the water running. Three children, ranging in age from 8 months to 8 years old, were at home during the incident, according to police. Loudoun County Sheriff Mike Chapman called the baby’s death heartbreaking, saying caregivers have a fundamental duty to protect children. He added investigators remain committed to seeking justice in the case.

items.t: Missing 7-year-old, pregnant mother both found safe
items.x: OVERLAND, Mo. ( KMOV /Gray News) — Officials in Missouri said a missing 7-year-old boy and his pregnant mother were found safe Wednesday. The Missouri State Highway Patrol previously issued an Endangered Person Advisory for Dylan Fernando Zendejas-Gonzalez, 7. Dylan was last seen leaving his home in Overland, near St. Louis, with his mother, Maria Guadalupe Gonzalez-Sanchez, 28. The two were last seen around 1:30 p.m. Sunday. Officials were concerned after personal belongings were left behind at their home. On Wednesday, the Overland Police Department said in a Facebook post that the two were found safe.

items.t: ‘She was screaming for her life’: Terrifying attempted kidnapping caught on video
items.x: HONOLULU ( KHNL /Gray News) — A terrifying kidnapping attempt in the middle of the afternoon on the Diamond Head Gold Coast in Honolulu was caught on video. Authorities said they were called to Kainalu condominiums on Coconut Avenue around noon on Monday about the reported kidnapping. Surveillance video from the area showed a truck parked outside the condominium complex that afternoon before a man was seen going inside the garage, appearing to confront two women and chasing one of them. A 77-year-old condo resident, who asked not to be identified, said the man picked up her 24-year-old friend. Police said the suspect elbowed the 77-year-old woman in the face. “He shoved me away from my friend and he picked her up,” she said. “He looked like a monster. Don’t do this.’” The 77-year-old said her friend was trying to fend off the kidnapper while she was hoping others would hear their screams for help. items.t: Man accused of threatening girl with a gun to get in his car later determined to have .292 BAC, deputies say
items.x: Salem, Ind. ( WDRB/WAVE /Gray News) — The sister of a man accused of threatening a girl with a gun to get in his car said that the whole thing was a “huge misunderstanding.” The incident happened on Friday in an Amish community in Salem, Indiana. Probable cause documents said 53-year-old Jeffrey Mauck went up to a girl outside her home and asked if her family sold any eggs. The girl told police that she said no and walked away. The Washington County Sheriff’s Department said Mauck then grabbed her and threatened her with a gun, telling her to get in his car. Officials said the girl’s family heard her screaming and came to the rescue. Court documents said that the girl’s father and his sons were able to restrain Mauck while waiting for the police to arrive. One of the responding officers said he found a pair of black handcuffs lying on the ground underneath Mauck and could smell what he believed to be the odor of alcohol coming from Mauck. Court documents said Mauck admitted to having been drinking. A chemical test determined that Mauck had a blood alcohol content of .292. items.t: Aging Untold: Fat-free doesn’t always mean healthy
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — On this episode of Aging Untold , we separate facts from fiction on “fat-free” foods to help you protect your heart and make healthier grocery choices. Then, National Alliance for Caregiving CEO Jason Resendez joins us to discuss the mounting pressures facing the sandwich generation and policy solutions offering caregiver relief. Plus, we meet the “Flower Buds,” an inspiring volunteer group in Kentucky that rescues discarded blooms to deliver hope and comfort across its community. Fat-free doesn’t always mean healthy: What to look for on food labels The “fat-free” option at the grocery store is not always the healthy option. Dr. Rhea Rogers, a board-certified physician, said the label can be misleading. “So if they’re removing the fat, they had to replace it with something else. So you have to look at the ingredients and look at the packaging,” she said. Rogers said she used to find all the fat categories confusing, so she created a simple way to sort them. items.t: The Hundred Club of CT holds sold-out luncheon for families of fallen first responders
items.x: HARTFORD, Conn. (WFSB) - The Hundred Club of Connecticut is holding its sold-out annual luncheon at the Aqua Turf in Southington, a fundraiser for the families of fallen police officers, firefighters and corrections officers. More than 30 of the families the group supports will have representatives at the event, according to Dale Hourigan, the club’s managing director. The club supports more than 100 families, he said. “Some organizations are there during the initial tragedy, but we’re with these families for life. We provide scholarships for the children, and we’re there for the ladies,” Dale Hourigan said. Membership costs $250 a year, a fee set in 1967 that has never risen, Haugen said. The club has given out more than $14 million since 1967. People who want to join can apply online at 100clubofct.org , he said.

items.t: Parents say students were forced to get off school bus and walk 3 miles home on dangerous roads
items.x: GUNTOWN, Miss. ( WTVA /Gray News) — Parents in Mississippi are demanding answers after they said their 11-year-old daughter’s school bus driver told her to get off the bus and walk miles home. James and Ann Lofton said their child and several other kids were forced to walk three miles to get home, though it’s unclear why. “You put your children out to catch the bus, you expect them to be safe on the bus,” Ann Lofton said. “You expect them to get to school safely, you expect them to get home safely, and then you get a phone call [saying] they’re walking down the side of the road. How is that keeping them safe?” The parents said they reported the incident to the Lee County School District. The Loftons said Superintendent Coke Magee suspended the driver for five days after the complaint. “We are aware of this, and it is being handled as a personnel issue,” the Lee County School District said in a statement. James Lofton said he wants everyone involved to lose their jobs. “That’s bull. It is bull crap. I think all their jobs, the superintendent, the one over the buses. I think they all need to be fired,” James Lofton said. “Because they’re hired to keep our kids safe. Instead, they put

items.t: Hartford launches HUSKY D coalition ahead of Jan. 1 eligibility changes
items.x: HARTFORD, Conn. (WFSB) - Hartford Mayor Arunan Arulampalam and other city leaders announced a new coalition to protect health care coverage for residents ahead of HUSKY D eligibility changes that take effect Jan. 1. The Hartford HUSKY D Coalition aims to give residents accurate information and a coordinated community response, according to a city official. Arulampalam said it brings together health care providers, federally qualified health centers, hospitals and community leaders. “If you rely on HUSKY D for your health care coverage, you may be losing it. You may be one of the 13,000 Hartford residents who will be losing it on January 1st,” Arulampalam said. He urged residents to visit the coalition’s website to check their status and learn about available resources.

items.t: Man arrested at Bradley Airport for fraudulently charging plane ticket, state police say

Troopers said Jainnier Ramos bought a ticket with the information for an Oct. 26 flight from Bradley International Airport to Puerto Rico. State police said a Tolland resident called them to make the complaint. The resident told them that while reviewing financial records, they discovered that one of their credit cards had been used without their knowledge. The records showed a charge of $700 to a national airline and another $200 charge to a business. The resident told troopers that they also received flight information to their email account. It identified the flight as going from Hartford to San Juan on the same evening the complaint was made. The email also said the name on the ticket was for a “Vera Jainnier Abniel Ramos.” The resident told troopers that they did not know anyone by that name. The victim also reportedly contacted Bradley Airport to advise it of the situation. Troopers said they initiated efforts to identify and find the suspect at the airport. items.t: Meet the volunteers who bring flowers from weddings and funerals to hospice patients
items.x: LOUISVILLE, Ky. ( Aging Untold ) — Inside Crescent Hill Baptist Church in Louisville, a group of volunteers gathers each week surrounded by color, creativity and collaboration. They call themselves the Flower Buds. From events to those in need The Flower Buds take donated flowers from weddings, funerals, wholesalers, supermarkets, florists, galas, banquets and other community events. They cut, clean and arrange the blooms into vases, then deliver them to nursing homes, the VA hospital, assisted living facilities and shelters. “Amazingly gifted with so many flowers from places like Kroger who have overbought and can’t sell them, and they allow us to pick them up and then bring them here, and then we cut them, clean them and vase them. Then we take them to nursing homes, the VA hospital, assisted living facilities,” Jodie Raible, a Flower Buds volunteer, said. The group sends out about 100 vases every week. “I take flowers to Up for Women and Children, it’s a day homeless shelter for women,” Stephanie Mullins, a Flower Buds volunteer, said. items.t: $5,000 reward offered after extremely neglected dog abandoned at CT State Park
items.x: DERBY, Conn. (WFSB) - A $5,000 reward is being offered for the arrest of the person responsible for the abandonment and extreme neglect of a dog at a Connecticut State Park. “Ozzy”, the small white-colored dog, was found dumped in in Osbornedale State Park on Tuesday, according to Shelton Animal Control. A passerby with her own dog spotted him curled up, his nails were also curled so badly he could barely walk, and being left in the park after dark would have been deadly, the animal advocacy group, Desmond’s Army Animal Law Advocates said. Ozzy is being cared for by staff at VCA Shoreline in Shelton. Desmond’s Army has reached out to Shelton Animal Control to help. No further details were released. Anyone with information is asked to call 203-924-2501. Eyewitness News will provide more details as soon as they become available.

items.t: Illegal moonshine distillery explodes, catches fire in mountains, officials say
items.x: WILKES COUNTY, N.C. ( WBTV /Gray News) - An explosion at an illegal moonshine distillery sparked a fire in the North Carolina mountains on Monday, according to authorities. Special agents from North Carolina’s Alcohol Law Enforcement Division were called to investigate the explosion in Wilkes County, North Carolina. Agents found an active 200-gallon illegal distillery. They seized about 1,800 gallons of mash, which is used to make moonshine, and 161 gallons of illegal moonshine. North Carolina officials shared photos showing the charred inside of a metal building. Distilling equipment was also damaged. Billy Ray Anderson, 69, was arrested and charged with manufacturing a non-taxpaid alcoholic beverage, possession for sale of a non-taxpaid alcoholic beverage, possession of a non-taxpaid alcoholic beverage, possession of distillery equipment, possession of distillery ingredients and allowing property to be used for the manufacture of a non-taxpaid alcoholic beverage. Moonshine is believed to have originated in North Carolina and was once an important source of income, particularly for rural residents.

items.t: Some packaged salads recalled for undeclared allergens
items.x: (Gray News) - Packaged salads produced by Taylor Farms have been recalled due to an undeclared allergen. According to the Food and Drug Administration, Taylor Farms is recalling its H-E-B Backyard BBQ Chop Salad because it may contain undeclared soy and tree nuts, specifically almonds. “People who have sensitivity or allergy to soy and tree nuts (almonds) may be at risk of a serious adverse reaction if they consume this product,” an FDA press release said. So far there have not been any illnesses or “adverse reactions” reported in connection with the recall. The salads were sold in H-E-B stores across Texas. They can be identified by their UPC code, 041220300457, and their best-by date, Oct. 30, 2026. Customers are asked not to eat the recalled salads and to throw them away or return them to the store for a refund.

items.t: How to spot fake crystals and avoid costly mistakes
items.x: SEDONA, Ariz. ( Aging Untold ) — The crystal and gemstone industry is booming, fueled in part by social media, but experts warn buyers to be cautious of fake products flooding the market. Jamie Inglett, who owns a crystal shop in Sedona, said consumers can find fake crystals in stores and at gem shows. “As a consumer you really kind of have to do your own research,” Inglett said. Growing popularity drives demand The crystal craze has exploded online, with #crystals generating 20 billion views on TikTok. Inglett has built up 215,106 Instagram followers and opened a physical storefront in Sedona after finding success online. “You don’t have to believe in crystal healing or crystal energy to appreciate their beauty,” Inglett said. What to know about fake crystals Shannon Wimberly, a crystal collector for several years, said she has encountered fake crystals and now scrutinizes purchases more carefully. “I absolutely know I’ve run into getting fake ones, so I started scrutinizing other things more and more,” Wimberly said. items.t: Caregiver advocate shares 3 policies that could help family caregivers
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — More than 60 million Americans are family caregivers, balancing work, kids and care for an aging parent or loved one. Jason Resendez, president and CEO of the National Alliance for Caregiving, recently testified before the U.S. Senate Special Committee on Aging. He joined gerontologist “Sam” Cradduck to talk through the solutions he presented. The three policies he brought to lawmakers Resendez said the National Alliance for Caregiving is championing changes “to address so many of the pain points that family caregivers face every day.” 1) Older Americans Act funding He said one priority is reauthorization and funding of the Older Americans Act. Resendez said the law provides dollars for state Area Agencies on Aging to deliver services for older adults, such as Meals on Wheels and caregiver support. “One of the only federal line items for caregiving comes through the Older Americans Act, and it’s called the National Family Caregiver Support Program,” Resendez said. He said the program funds respite, which gives caregivers the chance to take breaks. It also funds training, education and outreach, so family caregivers have peer support and someone to turn to when na

items.t: Long-term care costs rose about 50% in five years, report finds
items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — The cost of long-term care jumped nearly 50% in five years, while income for older households rose just 22%, according to a new AARP report . The report found long-term services and supports are becoming even less affordable for middle-class Americans. Alan Weil, senior vice president for public policy at AARP, said the gap is the most important finding. “Between 2019 and 2024, a five-year period, the cost of most long-term care services went up about 50%, but the incomes for older households only went up by about 22%,” Weil said. “So the gap between what people can afford and what it costs has grown.” The AARP also looked at what different types of care cost. Weil said the more skilled the service, the higher the price. “If you need someone to come in and help you prepare food, that’s less expensive than if you need someone to come in and provide nursing-level care,” Weil said. “Although I’ll also say that we’ve learned that a lot of caregivers are being forced to provide nursing care that they can’t afford to pay someone else to do, even though they’ve never been trained in nursing. So that’s where the burden falls back on the family.” The financial burden oft

items.t: Crash closes Route 8 south in Derby
items.x: DERBY, Conn. (WFSB) - Route 8 southbound in Derby was closed because of a crash, according to transportation officials. The highway has since reopened. Beforehand, the state Department of Transportation said the highway was closed between exits 13 and 12B. A vehicle overturned in the area around 8:15 a.m. on Wednesday. There’s no word on injuries or a cause. For real-time traffic updates, check the Channel 3 First Alert traffic map here .

items.t: FBI, bomb squad called to building in Windham after dead resident leaves chemicals behind
items.x: WINDHAM, Conn. (WFSB) - Environmental officials, the state police bomb squad, and the FBI were called to help with the disposal of chemicals left behind in a building by a dead resident. The state Department of Energy and Environmental Protection said they were first called to an address on Follett Road last week. “The DEEP Emergency Response Unit has been working with the state police bomb squad and the FBI on classification and disposal of chemicals that were left in a building by a deceased resident,” said James Fowler, CT DEEP. “We are classifying all non-explosive chemicals and removing them for proper disposal, and the bomb squad is handling anything that may be an energetic material.” Fowler said that work has been ongoing since last week and will continue for several more days. “From the DEEP perspective, there is no hazard to the public or the environment,” he said. No other details were released. Channel 3 has a crew headed to the scene.

items.t: Butter sold in 10 states recalled over possible yeast, mold and E. coli contamination
items.x: (Gray News) - Butter is being recalled because it might be contaminated with yeast, mold and E. coli, according to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. More than 1,300 cases of Miyoko’s Creamery European Style Salted Plant Milk Butter have been recalled in Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Iowa, Illinois, Indiana, Maryland, New Jersey, New Hampshire and Wisconsin. The recalled butter has lot code 07871 and a best-by date of Nov. 5, 2026. If you have the butter, you should not eat it, but the recall notice did not give further information about refunds.

items.t: She was born with eight fingers on one hand. Her family traveled to America for the surgery
items.x: ST. LOUIS, Mo. ( InvestigateTV ) - A family traveled from Turkey to St. Louis for their daughter’s surgery to treat a rare condition affecting fewer than 100 people worldwide. Elisa, an 18-month-old, was born with eight fingers on her left hand. She was diagnosed with Ulnar Dimelia, also known as Mirror Hand Syndrome. “Mirror Hand is incredibly uncommon, and even surgeons like myself who take care of a great deal of kids almost never see this in their career. So, it’s really uncommon. Numbers are hard to come by, but one in a million or less is probably about right,” said Dr. Charles Goldfarb, Chief of Orthopedic Surgery at St. Louis Children’s Hospital. The condition leaves patients without a radius bone. This means significant limitations in wrist and elbow motion and preserved shoulder movements. “From the very beginning, he was really warm, genuine, and gave us a lot of hope. Honestly, the trust and support he gave us played a huge role in our decision to come to St. Louis,” said Emircan Buga, Elisa’s father. They would have more time working with kids, more time working with families. Since then, the idea to reinvent systems that recruit and retain foster families has gained nationwide momentum. items.t: Connecticut leaders weigh tolls, other proposals to lower property taxes
items.x: HARTFORD, Conn. (WFSB) - State leaders are weighing new proposals to lower property taxes in Connecticut, including a recommendation to bring back highway tolls. Connecticut has some of the highest property taxes in the country. The state asked a panel of local residents, called the Citizens Assembly, to develop ways to bring them down. One recommendation is to bring back highway tolls to take pressure off car and property taxes. The panel also recommends that the state fully fund billions of dollars in special education costs. Those costs now fall heavily on cities and towns. Other proposals include adding a new tax on incomes over $1 million and having communities regionalize services.
