items.t: Valdosta firefighters launch free home safety initiative following two deadly house fires
items.x: VALDOSTA, Ga. (WCTV) - The Valdosta Fire Department has launched a community safety initiative “in light of the recent heartbreak and loss” the community has suffered, according to the fire department. To support residents, VFD is launching a free home safety program. The program includes smoke detector installation and home assessments, all for free. Under the program, firefighters are expected to conduct home assessments for fire hazards, safety equipment and help create an emergency escape plan, according to Fire Chief Marcus Haynes. VFD met with residents Wednesday to educate them on preventing tragedies such as a house fire that occurred Sunday on Stillwater Drive, which a Lowndes County coroner confirmed to WCTV claimed the lives of two children. Another is still recovering, according to the coroner. More News out of South Georgia Two weeks ago , a separate house fire occurred on West Park Avenue and claimed the life of a man and his 4-year-old grandson. Since then, a GoFundMe has been created for the family. With winter not too far away, the fire chief said they’re also inspecting space heaters and stovetops. items.t: DeSantis announces $100 million awarded to Florida water resource restoration, expansion projects
items.x: TALLAHASSEE, Fla. (WCTV) - Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis announced that $100 million in funds have been awarded to a number of state projects restoring and expanding state water resources. Funded through the Springs Restoration and Alternative Water Supply grant programs, $100 million has been awarded to 45 projects to restore Florida’s water resources, according to a press release. DeSantis shared the news at a press conference in Crystal River on Wednesday. More news out of the Big Bend: Of the grant funding, $50 million is going toward 23 projects aiming to restore Florida’s springs through wastewater upgrades and enhancements, according to the press release. This includes the Suwannee River. According to the press release, Suwannee River Water Management District was granted $3 million, which benefits the middle and lower Suwannee River Basin. “These strategic investments will build on the progress we’ve made in protecting our natural resources and improving water quality in communities across Florida, so that we can leave this state to God better than we found it,” DeSantis said in the press release. items.t: ‘They need to be honored’: Dream Flights honor Tallahassee veterans
items.x: TALLAHASSEE, Fla. (WCTV) - Local veterans took to the skies for an unforgettable tour overlooking parts of the capital city, all in a World War II airplane. Six veterans took off from Tallahassee International Airport Wednesday morning for a “Dream Flight” sponsored by the Florida Healthcare Association. For many of them, it is the first time getting up in the air since serving in the military. More Tallahassee news: The veterans from long-term care centers took exhilarating flights in open-cockpit biplanes used by World War II aviators. Charles Macdonald took part in the event. He served in the U. S. Marine Corps and Wednesday was his first time in an open-cockpit plane. “Awesome! That was a great flight, I mean, it’s been a while since I’ve been up there, I mean, being in an open-cockpit and everything with the air rushing by, it was just awesome,” Macdonald said. Macdonald was the first veteran to take flight. He said he had so much fun and would love to do it again if he’s able. The entire tarmac was full of joy, especially for veteran Roy Walker Jr., who had his nephew, Issac Williams, by his side cheering him on. “I’m very excited because I thought this day would never come.

items.t: ‘I miss her like crazy’: Loved ones remembering post office worker hit and killed by car
items.x: FORT THOMAS, Ky. ( WXIX /Gray News) - Loved ones and a Kentucky community are mourning a post office worker who was hit and killed by a car while walking earlier this month. Marchelle Bertram worked at the front desk of the Fort Thomas Post Office for years, helping people who came in. Sadly, she lost her life in a collision in Bellevue on Oct. 15. Her daughter, Whitney Bertram, said she is remembering her mother while seeing a large amount of support from the community following her death. “There are so many people I don’t know whose lives she’s touched and affected,” Whitney Bertram said. The crash occurred while Marchelle Bertram was walking on Memorial Parkway near her home. Her daughter said she rushed to the hospital after learning her mother had been hit by a vehicle. “Given the grave amount of injuries she sustained, there was no way she was going to survive,” she said. Marchelle Bertram died at the hospital. Whitney Bertram said the driver stayed at the scene and believes the crash was an accident. “I miss her like crazy; I try not to think about it too hard because I’ll break down,” she said. items.t: Ernie Johnson announces this will be his final season on ‘Inside The NBA’
items.x: (Gray News) - Ernie Johnson announced he will be stepping down as host of “Inside the NBA” at the end of the season. The Sports Broadcasting Hall of Famer took to social media on Wednesday to explain his decision to step away, saying, “It’s just time.” Johnson, 70, stated that he would not be retiring, but cutting back. “This is by no means the end. It’s just a turning of the page,” Johnson said. “And I’ll forever cherish every chapter we have written with ‘Inside the NBA.’” Johnson said he plans to continue to work, including covering the NCAA men’s basketball tournament for CBS and Turner Sports. The six-time Sports Emmy Award winner acknowledged that he has dealt with heart issues in recent years, but that isn’t the reason he’s stepping away from the show. “I just want to slow down a bit,” he added in his social media post. Johnson joined Turner Sports in 1989 and has hosted “Inside the NBA” since 1990. He thanked his TNT Sports and ESPN crews for their support over the years, as well as the viewers. “I just want to say thanks to you. Thanks for your loyalty, for your love, for your support. And on this day, for your understanding,” Johnson said.

items.t: Police department closes its investigation into Hayden Panettiere’s death
items.x: GREENVILLE, S.C. ( WHNS /Gray News) - The Greenville Police Department said it has officially closed its investigation into the death of Hayden Panettiere. Police said Panettiere’s death has been ruled accidental based on the medical examiner’s determination and the findings of the investigation. Panettiere, 36, died from an accidental overdose involving multiple prescription medications and fentanyl, according to findings previously released by the Greenville County Coroner’s Office. Toxicology testing determined the cause of death to be the toxic effects of fentanyl, 4-ANPP, alprazolam, methocarbamol and quetiapine. An autopsy showed no signs of contributing trauma. On Aug. 16, Panettiere was found unresponsive inside an apartment in Greenville, where she had been temporarily staying. Dispatchers received a 911 call reporting a woman in cardiac arrest at approximately 1:51 p.m. She was pronounced dead at 2:32 p.m. Her on-and-off boyfriend Brian Hickerson and his brother Zach Hickerson were at the apartment where she died. The city announced it received the 2026 Community Development Block Grant from the Georgia Department of Community Affairs (DCA) on Oct. 28. City officials say they applied for the grant as part of an agreement with Halcyon Home, Incorporated and the funding will be used to support the construction of the organization’s new domestic violence shelter. items.t: Trump says US will beat China in AI as technology emerges
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - Artificial intelligence has emerged as the critical sticking point between the U.S. and China. President Donald Trump, who has named it “super intelligence,” insists the U.S. will beat China in the AI competition. Trump said while campaigning for president that tariffs would form the crux of the bilateral relationship. The U.S. and China, the world’s two largest economies, have been engaged in a trade war during both of Trump’s terms. Speaking Sept. 13 in Ireland, Trump said the U.S. is leading China in AI. “We’re leading China in AI, we’re the most sophisticated country in the world, and frankly, I want to keep it that way because whoever wins AI, wins,” Trump said. During a state visit to Beijing in May, Trump praised Chinese President Xi Jinping. “And it’s to me an honor. We’ve had a fantastic relationship. We’ve gotten along. When they were difficulties, we worked it out,” Trump said. Trump hosted Xi at the White House in September for a state visit. He touted what he called “the tremendous strides” he and Xi had already made on national security, trade and technology. items.t: Man loses more than $4,000 after scammers spoof father’s number, claim parents are at gunpoint
items.x: SCOTTSDALE, Ariz. ( KPHO /Gray News) - A man lost thousands of dollars after getting a call that appeared to come from his father’s phone number, with a stranger claiming his parents were being held at gunpoint. Curtis Indyke was asleep around 11:30 p.m. on Oct. 21 when he got a call that appeared to be from his dad, who lives in Virginia. Indyke lives in Arizona. “I answer the phone and it’s not my dad. It’s some other male saying he has my parents basically at gunpoint,” Indyke said. The caller told him to pay or his parents would be shot. While still on the phone, Indyke said he texted 911 to report his parents were being held hostage in Virginia. The person who claimed to be holding Indyke’s parents hostage continued making threats. In a panic, Indyke sent more than $4,000 through Apple Pay to two separate phone numbers. “And they also wanted $1,000 worth of crypto gift cards, which I’ve never even heard of. I’m in IT and I’ve never even heard of them,” Indyke said. Indyke said his bank blocked that purchase. items.t: 8-month-old dies after left alone in running bathtub, police say
items.x: STERLING, Va. (Gray News) - A Virginia woman was arrested after her 8-month-old died after being left unattended in a bathtub, according to authorities. Rosellena Pisani, 30, was arrested and charged with homicide, two counts of child abuse and three counts of child endangerment, a press release said. On Sept. 12, emergency medical personnel and sheriff’s deputies responded to the residence after receiving a call about an unresponsive infant. Investigators determined the baby had been left unsupervised in a bathtub with the water running. Three children, ranging in age from 8 months to 8 years old, were at home during the incident, according to police. Loudoun County Sheriff Mike Chapman called the baby’s death heartbreaking, saying caregivers have a fundamental duty to protect children. He added investigators remain committed to seeking justice in the case.

items.t: How do FL’s top gubernatorial candidates plan to lead the state?

Among the rhetoric meant to fire up their own voters, both Republican Byron Donalds and Democrat David Jolly left hints of how they’d oversee the governor’s office. “If the rainy day fund can be expanded, then maybe we need to look at other people of our state actually having to pay less taxes as opposed to just expanding the state’s rainy day fund when it’s already statutorily full today,” Donalds said. Florida politics: “We’re going to exercise the powers of the office of governor very aggressively, just as the current governor has,” Jolly said. items.t: Missing 7-year-old, pregnant mother both found safe
items.x: OVERLAND, Mo. ( KMOV /Gray News) — Officials in Missouri said a missing 7-year-old boy and his pregnant mother were found safe Wednesday. The Missouri State Highway Patrol previously issued an Endangered Person Advisory for Dylan Fernando Zendejas-Gonzalez, 7. Dylan was last seen leaving his home in Overland, near St. Louis, with his mother, Maria Guadalupe Gonzalez-Sanchez, 28. The two were last seen around 1:30 p.m. Sunday. Officials were concerned after personal belongings were left behind at their home. On Wednesday, the Overland Police Department said in a Facebook post that the two were found safe.

items.x: HONOLULU ( KHNL /Gray News) — A terrifying kidnapping attempt in the middle of the afternoon on the Diamond Head Gold Coast in Honolulu was caught on video. Authorities said they were called to Kainalu condominiums on Coconut Avenue around noon on Monday about the reported kidnapping. Surveillance video from the area showed a truck parked outside the condominium complex that afternoon before a man was seen going inside the garage, appearing to confront two women and chasing one of them. A 77-year-old condo resident, who asked not to be identified, said the man picked up her 24-year-old friend. Police said the suspect elbowed the 77-year-old woman in the face. “He shoved me away from my friend and he picked her up,” she said. “He looked like a monster. Don’t do this.’” The 77-year-old said her friend was trying to fend off the kidnapper while she was hoping others would hear their screams for help. items.t: Man accused of threatening girl with a gun to get in his car later determined to have .292 BAC, deputies say
items.x: Salem, Ind. ( WDRB/WAVE /Gray News) — The sister of a man accused of threatening a girl with a gun to get in his car said that the whole thing was a “huge misunderstanding.” The incident happened on Friday in an Amish community in Salem, Indiana. Probable cause documents said 53-year-old Jeffrey Mauck went up to a girl outside her home and asked if her family sold any eggs. The girl told police that she said no and walked away. The Washington County Sheriff’s Department said Mauck then grabbed her and threatened her with a gun, telling her to get in his car. Officials said the girl’s family heard her screaming and came to the rescue. Court documents said that the girl’s father and his sons were able to restrain Mauck while waiting for the police to arrive. One of the responding officers said he found a pair of black handcuffs lying on the ground underneath Mauck and could smell what he believed to be the odor of alcohol coming from Mauck. Court documents said Mauck admitted to having been drinking. A chemical test determined that Mauck had a blood alcohol content of .292. items.t: Aging Untold: Fat-free doesn’t always mean healthy
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — On this episode of Aging Untold , we separate facts from fiction on “fat-free” foods to help you protect your heart and make healthier grocery choices. Then, National Alliance for Caregiving CEO Jason Resendez joins us to discuss the mounting pressures facing the sandwich generation and policy solutions offering caregiver relief. Plus, we meet the “Flower Buds,” an inspiring volunteer group in Kentucky that rescues discarded blooms to deliver hope and comfort across its community. Fat-free doesn’t always mean healthy: What to look for on food labels The “fat-free” option at the grocery store is not always the healthy option. Dr. Rhea Rogers, a board-certified physician, said the label can be misleading. “So if they’re removing the fat, they had to replace it with something else. items.t: Meet the volunteers who bring flowers from weddings and funerals to hospice patients
items.x: LOUISVILLE, Ky. ( Aging Untold ) — Inside Crescent Hill Baptist Church in Louisville, a group of volunteers gathers each week surrounded by color, creativity and collaboration. They call themselves the Flower Buds. From events to those in need The Flower Buds take donated flowers from weddings, funerals, wholesalers, supermarkets, florists, galas, banquets and other community events. They cut, clean and arrange the blooms into vases, then deliver them to nursing homes, the VA hospital, assisted living facilities and shelters. “Amazingly gifted with so many flowers from places like Kroger who have overbought and can’t sell them, and they allow us to pick them up and then bring them here, and then we cut them, clean them and vase them. Then we take them to nursing homes, the VA hospital, assisted living facilities,” Jodie Raible, a Flower Buds volunteer, said. The group sends out about 100 vases every week. “I take flowers to Up for Women and Children, it’s a day homeless shelter for women,” Stephanie Mullins, a Flower Buds volunteer, said. items.t: Man and 4-year-old boy die following West Park house fire in Valdosta
items.x: LOWNDES COUNTY, Ga. (WALB) — A Valdosta community is in mourning after a man and his 4-year-old grandson died in a recent house fire. On Oct. 15, Valdosta Fire Department (VFD) worked a blaze at a home on the 1300 block of West Park Avenue, that sent two people to the hospital and left multiple displaced. According to McLane Funeral and Cremation Services, 61-year-old Gary Lee Yoder and his 4-year-old grandson Grayson Jack Spires died from their injuries days later. A GoFundMe was created for the Yoder family as they mourn the deaths of their loved ones and work to recover everything they lost in fire. In light of the tragic incident, VFD is launching a community safety initiative designed to help locals establish an emergency plan for unexpected fires by providing free home safety assessments. “Our hearts and prayers are with the families who are grieving right now, and our primary goal is to stand beside our community and prevent further tragedy,” said Fire Chief Marcus Haynes. “We want to make it as simple as we can for every family to have peace of mind. items.t: Illegal moonshine distillery explodes, catches fire in mountains, officials say
items.x: WILKES COUNTY, N.C. ( WBTV /Gray News) - An explosion at an illegal moonshine distillery sparked a fire in the North Carolina mountains on Monday, according to authorities. Special agents from North Carolina’s Alcohol Law Enforcement Division were called to investigate the explosion in Wilkes County, North Carolina. Agents found an active 200-gallon illegal distillery. They seized about 1,800 gallons of mash, which is used to make moonshine, and 161 gallons of illegal moonshine. North Carolina officials shared photos showing the charred inside of a metal building. Distilling equipment was also damaged. Billy Ray Anderson, 69, was arrested and charged with manufacturing a non-taxpaid alcoholic beverage, possession for sale of a non-taxpaid alcoholic beverage, possession of a non-taxpaid alcoholic beverage, possession of distillery equipment, possession of distillery ingredients and allowing property to be used for the manufacture of a non-taxpaid alcoholic beverage. Moonshine is believed to have originated in North Carolina and was once an important source of income, particularly for rural residents.

items.t: Some packaged salads recalled for undeclared allergens
items.x: (Gray News) - Packaged salads produced by Taylor Farms have been recalled due to an undeclared allergen. According to the Food and Drug Administration, Taylor Farms is recalling its H-E-B Backyard BBQ Chop Salad because it may contain undeclared soy and tree nuts, specifically almonds. “People who have sensitivity or allergy to soy and tree nuts (almonds) may be at risk of a serious adverse reaction if they consume this product,” an FDA press release said. So far there have not been any illnesses or “adverse reactions” reported in connection with the recall. The salads were sold in H-E-B stores across Texas. They can be identified by their UPC code, 041220300457, and their best-by date, Oct. 30, 2026. Customers are asked not to eat the recalled salads and to throw them away or return them to the store for a refund.

Growing popularity drives demand The crystal craze has exploded online, with #crystals generating 20 billion views on TikTok. Inglett has built up 215,106 Instagram followers and opened a physical storefront in Sedona after finding success online. “You don’t have to believe in crystal healing or crystal energy to appreciate their beauty,” Inglett said. What to know about fake crystals Shannon Wimberly, a crystal collector for several years, said she has encountered fake crystals and now scrutinizes purchases more carefully. “I absolutely know I’ve run into getting fake ones, so I started scrutinizing other things more and more,” Wimberly said. items.t: Caregiver advocate shares 3 policies that could help family caregivers
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — More than 60 million Americans are family caregivers, balancing work, kids and care for an aging parent or loved one. Jason Resendez, president and CEO of the National Alliance for Caregiving, recently testified before the U.S. Senate Special Committee on Aging. He joined gerontologist “Sam” Cradduck to talk through the solutions he presented. The three policies he brought to lawmakers Resendez said the National Alliance for Caregiving is championing changes “to address so many of the pain points that family caregivers face every day.” 1) Older Americans Act funding He said one priority is reauthorization and funding of the Older Americans Act. Resendez said the law provides dollars for state Area Agencies on Aging to deliver services for older adults, such as Meals on Wheels and caregiver support. “One of the only federal line items for caregiving comes through the Older Americans Act, and it’s called the National Family Caregiver Support Program,” Resendez said. items.t: Long-term care costs rose about 50% in five years, report finds
items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — The cost of long-term care jumped nearly 50% in five years, while income for older households rose just 22%, according to a new AARP report . The report found long-term services and supports are becoming even less affordable for middle-class Americans. Alan Weil, senior vice president for public policy at AARP, said the gap is the most important finding. “Between 2019 and 2024, a five-year period, the cost of most long-term care services went up about 50%, but the incomes for older households only went up by about 22%,” Weil said. “So the gap between what people can afford and what it costs has grown.” The AARP also looked at what different types of care cost. Weil said the more skilled the service, the higher the price. “If you need someone to come in and help you prepare food, that’s less expensive than if you need someone to come in and provide nursing-level care,” Weil said. “Although I’ll also say that we’ve learned that a lot of caregivers are being forced to provide nursing care that they can’t afford to pay someone else to do, even though they’ve never been trained in nursing. items.t: West Virginia experiencing increase in Salmonella Typhimurium cases
items.x: CHARLESTON, W.Va. (WVVA) – The West Virginia Department of Health (WVDH) is investigating an outbreak of Salmonella Typhimurium. The outbreak started in early September, and 41 cases have been reported. Patients range in age from three to 54 years and five have been hospitalized. A common source has not been identified and exposures are under investigation. None of the cases outside West Virginia have been linked to this outbreak, indicating a localized event. To identify the source, timely reporting and specimen submission are essential. Collaboration between healthcare providers, laboratories and public health for Salmonella surveillance is vital in these cases. Salmonella Typhimurium is one of the most reported Salmonella serotypes in the U.S. It is acquired primarily through consuming contaminated food or water and encountering infected animals and their environments. Lab testing is essential for the diagnosis of salmonellosis. Most patients recover without antibiotics, but infections can progress to bacteremia or septicemia in young children, older adults and immunocompromised individuals.

McCuskey filed a lawsuit Thursday alleging TikTok violated several West Virginia consumer protection laws and ultimately harmed the state’s children. McCuskey said the app is designed to keep young teens engaged for as long as possible and doesn’t have safeguards for underage users. “West Virginia parents should not have to compete with an algorithm built to keep their kids scrolling, while targeting them with sexualized content,” McCuskey said in a news release. The lawsuit alleges that the platform’s features make children discoverable and reachable, exposing children to predators. The Consumer Protection Division of the Attorney General’s Office conducted testing using one account registered to an adult and another to a 13-year-old girl. The testing identified notable differences in the content delivered to each account: the child account repeatedly received sexually suggestive content while the adult account largely received content focused on ordinary interests like home improvement and local restaurants. “Parents have a responsibility t

items.t: West Virginia DMV unveils mysterious new “Cryptids” license plate
items.x: CHARLESTON, W.Va. (WVVA) – The West Virginia Division of Motor Vehicles is unveiling a new license plate, available for sale on Monday, Nov. 2, 2026. The plate was designed by Jesse Corlis and features nine different Cryptids from the mountain state: Flatwoods Monster, Mothman, Bigfoot, Sheepsquatch, Batboy, Veggie Man, Werewolf, Ogua and Grafton Monster. “First and foremost, I would like to pay tribute to Jesse Corlis, the talented graphic artist who designed the Cryptid license plate, along with several other license plates you see traveling the roads of West Virginia every day. One particularly popular design is the Pollinators plate, better known as the ‘Bee plate.” said DMV Commissioner Everett Frazier. Corlis developed the plate while working at the Kanawha City DMV headquarters. “Tragically, Jesse passed away in 2023 before he had the opportunity to see the Cryptid plate come to fruition,” said Frazier. “We recognize his creativity, talent and contributions to the West Virginia license plate program, and we are proud to see his work celebrated through this unique design.”

items.t: ‘Breaking Away’ actress Barbara Barrie dies by medically assisted suicide, reports say
items.x: (Gray News) - Barbara Barrie, known for her 1979 role in “Breaking Away,” died Wednesday by medically assisted suicide, according to her daughter in a statement to The New York Times . Barrie was 95. Barrie had been diagnosed with terminal cancer and died in her New York City home, according to her daughter, Jane Harwick. Barrie’s agent, Gary Gersh, said her passing was “medically assisted in accordance with the New York State Medical Aid in Dying Law,” according to USA Today . In addition to “Breaking Away,” which earned her an Oscar nomination, Barrie also starred in several TV shows, including “Barney Miller” and “Suddenly Susan.” She also received a Tony nomination for her performance in the original production of “Company.”

items.t: Relocation offers on the rise as cities try big cash incentives to attract remote workers
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Remote work opportunities continue to thrive years after the COVID-19 pandemic made working from home mainstream. Now some communities across the U.S. are competing to attract new residents who are fully employed but can live anywhere, offering increasingly large cash incentives to lure remote workers. Cumberland, Maryland launched “Choose Cumberland,” a pilot program offering $20,000 to up to 10 people who agree to move to the city. The Appalachian Mountains community, located about 130 miles outside Washington D.C., saw its population decline from over 40,000 to less than 19,000 after several manufacturing companies and other large employers closed their doors starting in the 1970s. “At one time, the population of Cumberland was over 40,000 people,” said Mayor Ray Morriss. Program details and requirements The Cumberland incentive splits the money into two payments : $10,000 in relocation cash $10,000 for a down payment or approved home renovations Recipients must make Cumberland their primary residence for at least five years. “The people we are trying to entice are the people who are bringing their jobs with them,” Morriss said. items.t: Hospice of Southern West Virginia to host lunch and tours for first responders
items.x: BECKLEY, W.Va. (WVVA) – Hospice of Southern West Virginia (HSWV) will welcome local first responders to its campus for a lunch and tours in recognition of National First Responders Day. The event will take place on Friday, Oct. 30, 2026, from 11:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. at Bowers Hospice House, located at 454 Cranberry Drive in Beckley. First Responders can enjoy lunch, connect with members of the Hospice of Southern West Virginia and learn more about the care that they provide to the region. Guests can also take an informal tour of the campus, including Bowers Hospice House, and see the environment where hospice care is provided. “There is no formal program,” said Tommy Redden, Chief Operating Officer, HSWV. “This is simply an opportunity to share a meal, have a conversation, see our facilities and build relationships with the first responders who serve our communities every day.”

items.t: Gen Z has more debt than Millennials did at the same age
items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — Gen Z carries more debt than Millennials did at the same age, even after adjusting for inflation, according to TransUnion data cited by a credit counseling expert. Ted Rossman, with nonprofit credit counseling agency Money Management International , said the agency has seen a 35% increase in demand from Gen Z clients in the past year. Their debt loads are about 12% higher than they were a year ago. Student loans, high rents and buy now, pay later plans are adding up and leaving many young adults living paycheck to paycheck with little savings. “That’s really showcasing a lot of these early career pressures,” Rossman said. “You have student loans, you have high housing costs. Those household formation years are very expensive, so GenZer’s actually have more debt than Millennials did at the same age, even adjusted for inflation according to TransUnion.” For Gen Z, Rossman said the starting point is the basics: knowing your budget and watching buy now, pay later spending. “It’s very popular among people in their 20’s, but it’s still debt,” Rossman said. “It can work in your favor. Sometimes you can get a good deal, but just be mindful that it’s not a free lunch. Ev

items.t: ‘He’s a monster’: Convicted Tennessee murderer still on the run as authorities investigate Wisconsin bank robbery
items.x: LAKE COUNTY, Tenn. ( WMC /Gray News) - The manhunt for escaped Tennessee inmate Jacob Allen Morley continues and authorities are investigating a possible link in Wisconsin after a man robbed a bank at gunpoint there on Tuesday. Dane County authorities said the Bank of Deerfield was robbed just before it closed. A gunman walked in, demanded money, restrained two employees and left with cash. Nobody was hurt during the robbery. The gunman stole a Lincoln MKZ from the parking lot to get away. The car was later found unoccupied. The Tennessee Bureau of Investigation said it is aware of the robbery in Wisconsin, but has not confirmed it is linked to Morley. Morley escaped from the Northwest Correctional Complex Monday. He stole a white 2008 Ford F-150 marked with Lindamood Planting Company. The truck was found abandoned early Tuesday in Marion, Illinois. Police said there is no evidence Morley is still in that area. Morley was serving a life sentence for the 2022 murder of Cody Birchfield. items.t: Antidepressants: What to know before you decide
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Feeling low, disconnected or not like yourself for weeks or months is different from a bad day. When it starts to affect sleep, energy or everyday life, it’s time to talk about support and treatment options. For some people, that could include an antidepressant. Start with a conversation with your provider Dr. Rhea Rogers, a board-certified physician, said the decision looks different for everyone. “Everybody is individualized so you can just talk with your provider,” Rogers said. Rogers said to recognize whether you’re feeling depressed and to look at signs such as loss of sleep, loss of energy or loss of motivation. Some people might also experience a triggering event that starts a downward spiral, which they can’t pull themself out of, she said. “When your quality of life is being affected, then you might want to look into antidepressant therapy,” Rogers said. Antidepressants are not “happy pills” Rogers cautioned that antidepressants do not take away sadness. “They’re not happy pills. They don’t take away the sadness, but they will be a way for you to work on how you got there or what else is going on,” Rogers said. She listed chronic stress, a thyroid imbala

items.t: The barbershop quartet tradition is alive in New Orleans
items.x: NEW ORLEANS ( InvestigateTV ) - On a Mid City evening, a four-part harmony rang out just off Canal Street. The group, Southern Tradition, has been around since 1999. The quartet is a place where a traditional American art form forges a friendship. “The main attribute to be a barbershop quartet singer is to not be embarrassed, just keep going,” said Karl Hansen. Four men with four different careers create one sound. Hansen is a doctor who sings bass. Hansen Eschette is a med tech singing tenor. Joe Jacquat is a civil engineer who sings baritone. Johnnie Oufnac is the only actual barber in this barbershop quartet, singing lead. “Being together for a long time helps us harmonize and understand where the other person is going,” Hansen said. Barbershop quartets have been around for more than a century. Though they can be found all over the world, ties to New Orleans are strong. “It really is the nexus of American music at its most basic level and a lot of it comes from New Orleans,” said Zachary Matherne. items.t: Nearly 11 million people in the U.S. could be living with undiagnosed diabetes
items.x: CHARLOTTE, N.C. ( InvestigateTV ) - Diabetes is the seventh leading cause of death in the United States, the No. 1 cause of kidney disease, and an estimated 40 million people are living with it nationwide. Despite decades of prevention education and major breakthroughs in treatment, doctors say diabetes continues to hit the South especially hard — including North Carolina. It can create serious long-term complications, including coronary artery disease, heart attacks, never damage, and amputations. But many people who have the disease may not know it. The CDC estimates around 11 million live with undiagnosed diabetes. “Every day, almost every hour” battle Andrew Tucker has lived with Type 2 diabetes for nearly two decades. He’s made major lifestyle changes but said managing the disease is still a daily fight. Tucker was diagnosed about 15 years ago, when he was 35. “Yes, for me, it is truly an everyday, almost every hour watching what I do,” Tucker said. Type 2 diabetes develops when the body doesn’t make enough insulin or doesn’t use insulin properly. Doctors say obesity is a major risk factor. items.t: This veteran is using his service dog to regain independence
items.x: ST. LOUIS, Mo. ( InvestigateTV ) - Veteran James Poggi served in the Marine Corps working in aviation. His time in the military led to a lifelong strain on his body, including five back surgeries and a below-the-knee amputation. “You go from being six foot three, 250 pounds and able to travel halfway across the world and do whatever they ask you to do, to being relying on wheelchairs, walkers, mobility devices, things like that, you become a vulnerable person that you never thought you’d be,” Poggi said. Poggi said he was in multiple accidents, hard landings, PT accidents and a car crash. He also developed spinal meningitis. “And that was all while I was active,” he said. To help ease some of the emotional toll, Poggi’s wife, who is also his caregiver, suggested he get a service dog. Service dog provides daily support Poggi got Teddy, a Goldendoodle, who serves as his service dog and daily lifeline. “You never went anywhere without your battle buddy. And he always, always better have your back. And that’s how it is. He’s always got my back,” Poggi said. The dog helped Poggi regain his independence by taking care of tasks many people take for granted. “His favorite thing is to retri

items.x: NASHVILLE, Tenn. ( WSMV /Gray News) — Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee said he suspects Christa Pike’s sentence will remain the same following her failed execution last month, unless the courts determine otherwise. Lee’s comments on Pike Lee was asked Wednesday whether the state will try to execute Pike again or if he will commute her sentence to life in prison. “As it related to a particular individual like Christa Pike and her crime, she’s still incarcerated under the laws of the state of Tennessee,” Lee said. “I suspect her sentence will be the same as before unless determined otherwise by the courts.” Pike’s condition Pike was sentenced to death for the 1995 murder of Colleen Slemmer. In September, Pike survived two doses of the lethal injection drug. The execution attempt failed. Pike is back in prison after spending days in the hospital. She is now able to speak in full sentences and walk on her own. items.t: Economist explains how the ‘K-shaped economy’ is impacting the midterms
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - As voters prepare to head to the polls for the midterm elections, a conflicting economic sentiment is once again emerging on the campaign trail. “Voters reflect the perception of the cost of living as they experienced, as opposed to what is in the data,” said Alessandro Rebucci, an economics professor at Johns Hopkins Carey Business School. “In the data, you have an economy that is very strong as a whole. How that pie is distributed affects how a large segment of the population and the voters are feeling about the economy right now.” The contradiction has been described by many economists recently, as the “k-shaped” economy, using a graph to depict how high-income earners and asset owners are doing compared to middle and lower-income earners. “To be concrete, the wealthiest households are presumed to spend much more than the lowest ones, not only in absolute terms, which is obvious, but also as a share of their income and in their wealth,” Rebucci said. In recent months on the campaign trail, President Donald Trump has said that the U.S. economy is doing well, often conflicting with what recent consumer surveys have found on voters’ economic opinions. “The ec

items.t: College professor among 2 found dead in home; suspect in custody, police say
items.x: LORAIN COUNTY, Ohio. ( WOIO /Gray News) - An Ohio college professor and a woman were found shot to death in a home, and a suspect is in custody, according to authorities. Wednesday morning, police responded to the Oberlin College Conservatory lot at 77 E. College St. to assist firefighters with a vehicle smoking and possibly on fire. items.t: Raleigh County board to hold final hearings Thursday on Cranberry-Prosperity closure
items.x: BECKLEY, W.Va. (WVVA) - Raleigh County education leaders say declining enrollment is forcing them to close schools, and parents have two more chances Thursday to be heard before the Board of Education votes on closing Cranberry-Prosperity Elementary. According to the district, Raleigh County Schools has lost more than 2,200 students in the last decade. On Tuesday night, the superintendent reported more than 300 fewer students this fall. “We have a total of 9,779 students enrolled in Raleigh County Schools. Last year, we had 10,090,” Superintendent Serena Starcher said. Closing Cranberry-Prosperity would cut nearly 10 positions and save about $1.1 million a year. Board of Education President Richard Snuffer said the closure will not be the last. “So, you know, we have to start looking at positions. And this is just the first of a bunch of painful cuts,” Snuffer said. Families and teachers pushed back at Monday’s hearings. The district’s numbers put Cranberry-Prosperity’s building utilization at 64%. items.t: Hometown Hero: David Blankenship
items.x: WYOMING COUNTY, W.Va. (WVVA) - David Blankenship, who leads five congregations in Pineville and Oceana, is October’s second Hometown Hero. In July 2022, a pastoral charge existed among the five churches. Blankenship now leads all five congregations. Answering a call to pastor Blankenship said his wife had a heart attack in May 2022. She had surgery in June and had a stroke during the procedure, he said. “In May, 2022, my wife had a heart attack. In June, she had surgery, and on the table, she had a stroke. She was on total life support. The hospital said it’s in God’s hands now, which I disagreed. It’s in God’s hands before you get there. I go outside, I pray to God, what would you have me do to bring my wife home in any condition? And it’s just a strong voice said, you will be pastoring the five churches. I said, okay, I will do it,” Blankenship said. For the past four years, Blankenship has used his role as pastor to spread the word of God and give back to his community. “I feel being behind the pulpit on Sunday is great, and I love it, and wonderful things have happened. items.t: Summers County kennel at double capacity, urging adoptions and fosters
items.x: SUMMERS COUNTY, W.Va. (WVVA) - The Summers County kennel is housing 12 dogs — double the six it is technically set up to hold, as staff scramble to find foster and forever homes. Animal Control Officer Alicia Ward with the Summers County Sheriff’s Department says some dogs, like Bluey, have been at the kennel for eight months, while others arrived as recently as yesterday. Seven of the 12 were removed from a home in a cruelty case. “All dogs are super sweet, each has their own personality,” Ward said. “We desperately need to find them some homes.” Ward said the dogs are receiving food, water, baths and daily care, but the crowded kennel environment takes a toll, with constant barking and close quarters stressing the animals. “If I get a call about that dog, I need to have somewhere to put that dog,” Ward said. “It breaks my heart, I want to save all the dogs. Where I’m at full capacity, I’m limited to how much I can help other dogs because I have no room. It’s heartbreaking to see such great dogs have to live their lives like this. items.t: For politics, what is an October surprise?
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - An October surprise is an event that could shake up an election, but does it often make the difference? Matt Dallek, a professor of political management at George Washington University, described it as “an event that, at least in theory, has the potential to shake up an election, something that people did not foresee coming that upends the debate.” He said the term dates back to around the 1980 election, when President Jimmy Carter failed to secure the release of American hostages being held in Iran before November 4, 1980, election day. Carter lost to Republican rival Ronald Reagan. Several surprises have occurred in the years since. Surprises can be driven by a campaign or by news events. Examples include Iran-Contra-related indictments in 1992 and the global financial collapse in 2008. Dallek said those surprises likely did not change the outcome of the election that November. “There’s no evidence that they flip a dynamic that was already in place,” Dallek said. “What’s more typical is that an event occurs, it dominates the news cycle and the trend line starts to move further toward the candidate who was already doing well, who was already likely to prevai

items.t: Library says person threw box of cockroaches at a staff member, prompting closure
items.x: TOLEDO, Ohio ( WTVG /Gray News) - A cockroach attack forced the closure of a library in Ohio this week. Surveillance footage was released by the Toledo Lucas County Public Library, appearing to show a person throwing a box of cockroaches at a staff member on Tuesday at the Kent Branch Library. Surveillance footage apparently shows someone throwing a box of cockroaches at a library employee in Ohio. (Source: Toledo Lucas County Public Library) A library spokesperson confirmed the throwing of the box of cockroaches at the library worker on Collingwood Blvd. But it wasn’t immediately shared what led up to the cockroach attack. The library was said to have gone into restricted access before closing for the rest of the day for cleanup and remediation. The Kent Branch Library reopened Wednesday. Officials did not say whether anyone would be facing any charges.

items.t: Grandmother not indicted in baby’s death after police say she left her in hot car for 8 hours while she worked
items.x: MADISONVILLE, Ky. ( WFIE /Gray News) — A Kentucky doctor who accidentally left her grandchild unattended in a hot car for about eight hours will not be indicted for the baby’s death. Madisonville police said 10-month-old Scottie Crowell died in August . On Tuesday, a grand jury found there was insufficient probable cause for an indictment. Police said Scottie’s grandmother picked her up in the morning of Aug. 13 and was supposed to take her to daycare. She forgot the child was in the car and went to work, police said. She arrived at Owensboro Health Multi-Care, where she works as a doctor, around 8 a.m. The baby’s father called his wife after trying to pick up Scottie from daycare, but the child was not there. The baby’s mother called the grandmother at work, and the grandmother ran outside and saw Scottie was still in the vehicle around 4 p.m., police said. After 911 was called, first responders tried to administer lifesaving measures, but the baby died. “I would ask that you keep the infant’s parents and family in your thoughts and prayers as they continue to grieve and process this unimaginable loss,” said Commonwealth’s Attorney Hannah Kington-Jarvis.

items.t: Widow searches for lost wedding ring when husband dies 3 days after getting married in Las Vegas
items.x: LAS VEGAS ( KVVU /Gray News) — A South Dakota woman is asking for help finding the wedding ring her husband lost in Las Vegas the night they married. Tammy Bishop and Will Mulroy were married Oct. 20 at the Viva Las Vegas Chapel. Bishop said they celebrated on a party bus and toured the Strip. At a bar, though, she says Mulroy looked down and realized his ring was gone. “We got to a bar. He looked down and his band was gone. He lost it. He started crying,” Bishop said. According to Bishop, he told her the ring was two sizes too big because he had lost weight. She said the ring may have slid off on the bus or while he moved into his wheelchair. It may also have come off while he rolled down the Strip. “We backtracked our steps. We told the bus driver. We had everyone looking. We couldn’t find it,” she said. The next day, she joked with him: “You didn’t even have your ring on for 24 hours and you lost it.” Everyone laughed, she said. “I said it’s not a big deal; we will buy you a new one, but now that he is gone it is a big deal to me,” Bishop said. items.t: Abundant sunshine returns on Thursday along with some warm temps
items.x: Temperatures will be hot throughout the rest of the work week, with highs reaching up near 70 degrees tomorrow and Friday. Temperatures will be cooling down to the low 60s for the start of the next week, but by the end of the week, temperatures could become seasonable. Overnight we’re going to see some of the cloud cover move out, which will allow our low temperatures to get a little bit cooler than we were last night. Lows will be bottoming out in the mid 40s, with mainly clear skies by Thursday morning. Thursday will see the return of high pressure, which means sunshine will be in abundance throughout the afternoon. Temperatures will be topping off in the upper 60s and low 70s, putting us ten degrees warmer than we’d usually be for this time of year. Winds will be light once again. Looking ahead to Halloween, we’re going to see a frontal system bring in some upper-level cloud cover, but the day should end up dry with temperatures topping off in the low 60s. Rain looks to arrive either at the end of the weekend or the start of next week. items.t: Princeton Police officer arrested on arson charge
items.x: PRINCETON, W.Va. (WVVA) - A Princeton Police Department officer has been arrested in connection to a structure fire in 2026. Lt. R.M. Combs has been charged with first-degree arson, according to a statement from the West Virginia Fire Marshal’s Office. The fire occurred on Aug. 4, 2026 in the 900 block of Harrison Street in Princeton. Combs, who has been employed by the department for 12 years, was taken to the Mercer County Magistrate’s Office for arraignment but bond information is not available at this time. An internal investigation by the Princeton Police Department and the criminal investigation are ongoing. Princeton Police Chief Ben Woodard said Combs has been suspended without pay pending further disciplinary action and all officers are subject to the highest standards of conduct. The West Virginia State Police also assisted with the arrest of Combs. The state Fire Marshal said the police department as well as the City of Princeton have been fully cooperative during the investigation.

items.t: ‘I miss her like crazy’: Loved ones remembering post office worker hit and killed by car
items.x: FORT THOMAS, Ky. ( WXIX /Gray News) - Loved ones and a Kentucky community are mourning a post office worker who was hit and killed by a car while walking earlier this month. Marchelle Bertram worked at the front desk of the Fort Thomas Post Office for years, helping people who came in. Sadly, she lost her life in a collision in Bellevue on Oct. 15. Her daughter, Whitney Bertram, said she is remembering her mother while seeing a large amount of support from the community following her death. “There are so many people I don’t know whose lives she’s touched and affected,” Whitney Bertram said. The crash occurred while Marchelle Bertram was walking on Memorial Parkway near her home. Her daughter said she rushed to the hospital after learning her mother had been hit by a vehicle. “Given the grave amount of injuries she sustained, there was no way she was going to survive,” she said. Marchelle Bertram died at the hospital. Whitney Bertram said the driver stayed at the scene and believes the crash was an accident. “I miss her like crazy; I try not to think about it too hard because I’ll break down,” she said. items.t: Ernie Johnson announces this will be his final season on ‘Inside The NBA’
items.x: (Gray News) - Ernie Johnson announced he will be stepping down as host of “Inside the NBA” at the end of the season. The Sports Broadcasting Hall of Famer took to social media on Wednesday to explain his decision to step away, saying, “It’s just time.” Johnson, 70, stated that he would not be retiring, but cutting back. “This is by no means the end. It’s just a turning of the page,” Johnson said. “And I’ll forever cherish every chapter we have written with ‘Inside the NBA.’” Johnson said he plans to continue to work, including covering the NCAA men’s basketball tournament for CBS and Turner Sports. The six-time Sports Emmy Award winner acknowledged that he has dealt with heart issues in recent years, but that isn’t the reason he’s stepping away from the show. “I just want to slow down a bit,” he added in his social media post. Johnson joined Turner Sports in 1989 and has hosted “Inside the NBA” since 1990. He thanked his TNT Sports and ESPN crews for their support over the years, as well as the viewers. “I just want to say thanks to you. Thanks for your loyalty, for your love, for your support. And on this day, for your understanding,” Johnson said.

items.t: Police department closes its investigation into Hayden Panettiere’s death
items.x: GREENVILLE, S.C. ( WHNS /Gray News) - The Greenville Police Department said it has officially closed its investigation into the death of Hayden Panettiere. Police said Panettiere’s death has been ruled accidental based on the medical examiner’s determination and the findings of the investigation. Panettiere, 36, died from an accidental overdose involving multiple prescription medications and fentanyl, according to findings previously released by the Greenville County Coroner’s Office. Toxicology testing determined the cause of death to be the toxic effects of fentanyl, 4-ANPP, alprazolam, methocarbamol and quetiapine. An autopsy showed no signs of contributing trauma. On Aug. 16, Panettiere was found unresponsive inside an apartment in Greenville, where she had been temporarily staying. Dispatchers received a 911 call reporting a woman in cardiac arrest at approximately 1:51 p.m. She was pronounced dead at 2:32 p.m. Her on-and-off boyfriend Brian Hickerson and his brother Zach Hickerson were at the apartment where she died. items.t: Trump says US will beat China in AI as technology emerges
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - Artificial intelligence has emerged as the critical sticking point between the U.S. and China. President Donald Trump, who has named it “super intelligence,” insists the U.S. will beat China in the AI competition. Trump said while campaigning for president that tariffs would form the crux of the bilateral relationship. The U.S. and China, the world’s two largest economies, have been engaged in a trade war during both of Trump’s terms. Speaking Sept. 13 in Ireland, Trump said the U.S. is leading China in AI. “We’re leading China in AI, we’re the most sophisticated country in the world, and frankly, I want to keep it that way because whoever wins AI, wins,” Trump said. During a state visit to Beijing in May, Trump praised Chinese President Xi Jinping. “And it’s to me an honor. We’ve had a fantastic relationship. We’ve gotten along. When they were difficulties, we worked it out,” Trump said. Trump hosted Xi at the White House in September for a state visit. He touted what he called “the tremendous strides” he and Xi had already made on national security, trade and technology. ( KPHO /Gray News) - A man lost thousands of dollars after getting a call that appeared to come from his father’s phone number, with a stranger claiming his parents were being held at gunpoint. Curtis Indyke was asleep around 11:30 p.m. on Oct. 21 when he got a call that appeared to be from his dad, who lives in Virginia. Indyke lives in Arizona. “I answer the phone and it’s not my dad. It’s some other male saying he has my parents basically at gunpoint,” Indyke said. The caller told him to pay or his parents would be shot. While still on the phone, Indyke said he texted 911 to report his parents were being held hostage in Virginia. The person who claimed to be holding Indyke’s parents hostage continued making threats. In a panic, Indyke sent more than $4,000 through Apple Pay to two separate phone numbers. “And they also wanted $1,000 worth of crypto gift cards, which I’ve never even heard of. I’m in IT and I’ve never even heard of them,” Indyke said. Indyke said his bank blocked that purchase. items.t: 8-month-old dies after left alone in running bathtub, police say
items.x: STERLING, Va. (Gray News) - A Virginia woman was arrested after her 8-month-old died after being left unattended in a bathtub, according to authorities. Rosellena Pisani, 30, was arrested and charged with homicide, two counts of child abuse and three counts of child endangerment, a press release said. On Sept. 12, emergency medical personnel and sheriff’s deputies responded to the residence after receiving a call about an unresponsive infant. Investigators determined the baby had been left unsupervised in a bathtub with the water running. Three children, ranging in age from 8 months to 8 years old, were at home during the incident, according to police. Loudoun County Sheriff Mike Chapman called the baby’s death heartbreaking, saying caregivers have a fundamental duty to protect children. He added investigators remain committed to seeking justice in the case.

items.t: Missing 7-year-old, pregnant mother both found safe
items.x: OVERLAND, Mo. ( KMOV /Gray News) — Officials in Missouri said a missing 7-year-old boy and his pregnant mother were found safe Wednesday. The Missouri State Highway Patrol previously issued an Endangered Person Advisory for Dylan Fernando Zendejas-Gonzalez, 7. Dylan was last seen leaving his home in Overland, near St. Louis, with his mother, Maria Guadalupe Gonzalez-Sanchez, 28. The two were last seen around 1:30 p.m. Sunday. Officials were concerned after personal belongings were left behind at their home. On Wednesday, the Overland Police Department said in a Facebook post that the two were found safe.

A 77-year-old condo resident, who asked not to be identified, said the man picked up her 24-year-old friend. Plus, we meet the “Flower Buds,” an inspiring volunteer group in Kentucky that rescues discarded blooms to deliver hope and comfort across its community. Fat-free doesn’t always mean healthy: What to look for on food labels The “fat-free” option at the grocery store is not always the healthy option. Dr. Rhea Rogers, a board-certified physician, said the label can be misleading. “So if they’re removing the fat, they had to replace it with something else. items.t: Some Monroe County schools placed on modified lockdown
items.x: PETERSTOWN, W.Va. (WVVA) - Some Monroe County schools have been partially locked down as the result of a situation in a neighboring county. Superintendent Jason Conaway said the district’s Peterstown complex and James Monroe High School have been placed on a modified lockdown due to a situation in neighboring Giles County. Conaway was unable to provide information about the situation in Giles County. WVVA reached out to Giles County schools and an official said the situation does not involve one of the district’s schools. WVVA also reached out to the Giles County Sheriff’s Office and an official declined to comment, citing a policy of not providing information to media members. This story is breaking news and will be updated as more information becomes available.

items.t: Meet the volunteers who bring flowers from weddings and funerals to hospice patients
items.x: LOUISVILLE, Ky. ( Aging Untold ) — Inside Crescent Hill Baptist Church in Louisville, a group of volunteers gathers each week surrounded by color, creativity and collaboration. They call themselves the Flower Buds. From events to those in need The Flower Buds take donated flowers from weddings, funerals, wholesalers, supermarkets, florists, galas, banquets and other community events. They cut, clean and arrange the blooms into vases, then deliver them to nursing homes, the VA hospital, assisted living facilities and shelters. “Amazingly gifted with so many flowers from places like Kroger who have overbought and can’t sell them, and they allow us to pick them up and then bring them here, and then we cut them, clean them and vase them. Then we take them to nursing homes, the VA hospital, assisted living facilities,” Jodie Raible, a Flower Buds volunteer, said. The group sends out about 100 vases every week. “I take flowers to Up for Women and Children, it’s a day homeless shelter for women,” Stephanie Mullins, a Flower Buds volunteer, said. items.t: Illegal moonshine distillery explodes, catches fire in mountains, officials say
items.x: WILKES COUNTY, N.C. ( WBTV /Gray News) - An explosion at an illegal moonshine distillery sparked a fire in the North Carolina mountains on Monday, according to authorities. Special agents from North Carolina’s Alcohol Law Enforcement Division were called to investigate the explosion in Wilkes County, North Carolina. Agents found an active 200-gallon illegal distillery. They seized about 1,800 gallons of mash, which is used to make moonshine, and 161 gallons of illegal moonshine. North Carolina officials shared photos showing the charred inside of a metal building. Distilling equipment was also damaged. Billy Ray Anderson, 69, was arrested and charged with manufacturing a non-taxpaid alcoholic beverage, possession for sale of a non-taxpaid alcoholic beverage, possession of a non-taxpaid alcoholic beverage, possession of distillery equipment, possession of distillery ingredients and allowing property to be used for the manufacture of a non-taxpaid alcoholic beverage. Moonshine is believed to have originated in North Carolina and was once an important source of income, particularly for rural residents.

items.t: Some packaged salads recalled for undeclared allergens
items.x: (Gray News) - Packaged salads produced by Taylor Farms have been recalled due to an undeclared allergen. According to the Food and Drug Administration, Taylor Farms is recalling its H-E-B Backyard BBQ Chop Salad because it may contain undeclared soy and tree nuts, specifically almonds. “People who have sensitivity or allergy to soy and tree nuts (almonds) may be at risk of a serious adverse reaction if they consume this product,” an FDA press release said. So far there have not been any illnesses or “adverse reactions” reported in connection with the recall. The salads were sold in H-E-B stores across Texas. They can be identified by their UPC code, 041220300457, and their best-by date, Oct. 30, 2026. Customers are asked not to eat the recalled salads and to throw them away or return them to the store for a refund.

Growing popularity drives demand The crystal craze has exploded online, with #crystals generating 20 billion views on TikTok. Inglett has built up 215,106 Instagram followers and opened a physical storefront in Sedona after finding success online. “You don’t have to believe in crystal healing or crystal energy to appreciate their beauty,” Inglett said. What to know about fake crystals Shannon Wimberly, a crystal collector for several years, said she has encountered fake crystals and now scrutinizes purchases more carefully. “I absolutely know I’ve run into getting fake ones, so I started scrutinizing other things more and more,” Wimberly said. items.t: Caregiver advocate shares 3 policies that could help family caregivers
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — More than 60 million Americans are family caregivers, balancing work, kids and care for an aging parent or loved one. Jason Resendez, president and CEO of the National Alliance for Caregiving, recently testified before the U.S. Senate Special Committee on Aging. He joined gerontologist “Sam” Cradduck to talk through the solutions he presented. The three policies he brought to lawmakers Resendez said the National Alliance for Caregiving is championing changes “to address so many of the pain points that family caregivers face every day.” 1) Older Americans Act funding He said one priority is reauthorization and funding of the Older Americans Act. Resendez said the law provides dollars for state Area Agencies on Aging to deliver services for older adults, such as Meals on Wheels and caregiver support. “One of the only federal line items for caregiving comes through the Older Americans Act, and it’s called the National Family Caregiver Support Program,” Resendez said. items.t: Long-term care costs rose about 50% in five years, report finds
items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — The cost of long-term care jumped nearly 50% in five years, while income for older households rose just 22%, according to a new AARP report . The report found long-term services and supports are becoming even less affordable for middle-class Americans. Alan Weil, senior vice president for public policy at AARP, said the gap is the most important finding. “Between 2019 and 2024, a five-year period, the cost of most long-term care services went up about 50%, but the incomes for older households only went up by about 22%,” Weil said. “So the gap between what people can afford and what it costs has grown.” The AARP also looked at what different types of care cost. Weil said the more skilled the service, the higher the price. “If you need someone to come in and help you prepare food, that’s less expensive than if you need someone to come in and provide nursing-level care,” Weil said. “Although I’ll also say that we’ve learned that a lot of caregivers are being forced to provide nursing care that they can’t afford to pay someone else to do, even though they’ve never been trained in nursing. So that’s where the burden falls back on the family.” The financial burden oft

items.t: She was born with eight fingers on one hand. Her family traveled to America for the surgery
items.x: ST. LOUIS, Mo. ( InvestigateTV ) - A family traveled from Turkey to St. Louis for their daughter’s surgery to treat a rare condition affecting fewer than 100 people worldwide. Elisa, an 18-month-old, was born with eight fingers on her left hand. She was diagnosed with Ulnar Dimelia, also known as Mirror Hand Syndrome. “Mirror Hand is incredibly uncommon, and even surgeons like myself who take care of a great deal of kids almost never see this in their career. So, it’s really uncommon. Numbers are hard to come by, but one in a million or less is probably about right,” said Dr. Charles Goldfarb, Chief of Orthopedic Surgery at St. Louis Children’s Hospital. The condition leaves patients without a radius bone. This means significant limitations in wrist and elbow motion and preserved shoulder movements. “From the very beginning, he was really warm, genuine, and gave us a lot of hope. Honestly, the trust and support he gave us played a huge role in our decision to come to St. Louis,” said Emircan Buga, Elisa’s father. items.t: Officials working to expand foster care for children in America, here’s how
items.x: NASHVILLE, Tenn. ( InvestigateTV ) - Kids sleeping in shelters, bussed between hotels, and overnights in office buildings. That’s the reality for many foster children in America. For every 100 children in foster care, federal data shows that only 57 licenses homes are available. In an effort to close that gap, the federal government launched a campaign in November 2025 called “A Home for Every Child.” “When we launched this, we offered states the choice: if they joined the Home for Every Child campaign, they would get administrative relief,” said Alex Adams, assistant secretary for the administration for children and families. “We would get them out of mountains of paperwork so that they could spend more time focused on things that actually improve child welfare outcomes. They would have more time working with kids, more time working with families. Since then, the idea to reinvent systems that recruit and retain foster families has gained nationwide momentum. items.t: Canned fruit sold at Walmart recalled in several states
items.x: (Gray News) - A voluntary recall over lead concerns has been issued for cans of Walmart fruit cocktail distributed to stores in at least seven states. The Food and Drug Administration said the recall applies to 15-ounce containers of Great Value Fruit Cocktail in Fruit Juice from Concentrate. Where the product was distributed More than 1,830 cases, or approximately 44,000 individual cans, were distributed to Walmart locations in Alabama, Arizona, Louisiana, New Mexico, Pennsylvania, Washington and Wyoming, the FDA said. How to identify the product The product is marked with lot number “6FCB 04 C2263” and a best if used by date of Sept. 1, 2027. Recall details The FDA initiated the recall for “potential contamination with elevated levels of lead” on Oct. 1. It was reclassified as a Class II recall on Oct. 20. According to the FDA, Class II recalls are issued when a product can cause temporary health effects with a remote possibility of serious issues. What customers should do Customers should throw the item away or return it to Walmart.

items.t: 24-year-old deputy killed in crash with coal truck while on duty, sheriff’s office says
items.x: LOGAN COUNTY, W. Va ( WSAZ /Gray News) - A 24-year-old sheriff’s deputy was killed in a crash while responding to a call, authorities said. The Logan County Sheriff’s Department identified the deputy as 24-year-old Caden Mullins. Deputy Mullins’ fiancée was airlifted from the scene of the crash to a hospital. Deputies say Mullins and his fiancée were at a truck-or-treat event on Saturday in the Man area when he received an emergency call from the sheriff’s department. The sheriff’s department says Deputy Caden Mullins, 24, died in the crash. Mullins was on his way to drop his fiancée off and head to the call when the crash occurred around 5 p.m., deputies say. Deputies say the crash happened at the intersection of Rum Creek Road and Route 10 when a coal truck pulled off the road and hit Mullins’ vehicle. Mullins worked for the Charleston Police Department for about a year before joining the Logan County Sheriff’s Department to be closer to family, the department said.

items.t: Woman arrested after 4-year-old found dead in Atlanta townhome
items.x: WASHINGTON, Ga. ( WRDW /Gray News) - A woman was arrested Tuesday morning after a 4-year-old boy was found dead more than an hour away in an Atlanta townhome, authorities said. Wilkes County Sheriff Darrell Powers said Jasmaine Smoak was arrested and booked into the Wilkes County Detention Center. According to WRDW’s sister station, Atlanta News First , Atlanta police responded to a gated community in the 3500 block of Cardinal Drive SW on Monday night for a welfare check. Officers forced their way into the home “based on information received during the welfare check,” Atlanta police said. Once inside, officers found the child dead. Emergency personnel attempted lifesaving measures but were unsuccessful, police said. Powers said deputies worked closely with Atlanta homicide detectives to locate Smoak using license plate reader technology. Smoak is charged with second-degree cruelty to children and concealing the death of another. Atlanta police said Smoak is a friend of the child’s mother. The circumstances surrounding the boy’s death remain unclear.

Organized events and home safety Hieatt suggested families attend organized events such as truck or treat, which he said are safer than approaching strangers’ houses. items.t: Bluefield could make Holiday of Lights changes
items.x: BLUEFIELD, W.Va. (WVVA) - Changes could be made to a Bluefield holiday tradition this year. The city is considering changes to the Holiday of Lights at Bluefield City Park, City Manager Cecil Marson told the Bluefield Board of Directors Tuesday. “The biggest thing is we want to be able to sustain it and keep it going for the long term and so we’re looking at different options this year,” Marson told WVVA after the meeting. The donation-based, month-long event takes in $0.96 per visitor, Marson added. But, it costs $4.22 per visitor to operate, he continued. Among the proposed changes are reducing the number of days per week to Thursday to Sunday and charging visitors except for the week after Christmas. Marson said no changes have been made yet and will require board approval.

items.t: Raleigh County SWA partners with Girl Scouts for flag retirement ceremony
items.x: BECKLEY, W.Va. (WVVA) – A special flag retirement ceremony will be held on Sunday, Nov. 1, 3:30 p.m. at the Raleigh County Solid Waste Authority’s Wooten Park. The Raleigh County Solid Waste Authority is partnering with the Girl Scouts to provide a dedicated space for the proper and respectful retirement of American flags that are no longer suitable for display. Any flag that is no longer suitable for display should not be thrown away; it should be retired in a dignified manner. A flag retirement ceremony provides an opportunity to respectfully dispose of the flag while recognizing what it represents: our country, its history and the people who have served and sacrificed to protect the freedoms represented by it. The Girl Scouts will learn about the significance of the flag and participate in a traditional retirement ceremony. The process will allow Scouts to understand that even when a flag can no longer be flown, it continues to deserve our respect. “This is about much more than properly retiring an old flag,” said Travis Kiblinger, Director of the Raleigh County Solid Waste Authority. “It is about teaching our young people respect — respect for our flag, respect for our country,

items.t: ‘Devastating’: Police department mourns death of officer in off-duty crash
items.x: AUTAUGA COUNTY, Ala. ( WSFA /Gray News) - A police officer in Alabama has died in an off-duty crash this week. According to the Prattville Police Department, Cpl. Dakota Lee Davis did not survive the injuries he sustained in a crash on Highway 31 on Monday afternoon. “The loss of CPL. Davis is devastating not only to the Prattville Police Department but to the city of Prattville. He will be missed by all,” Prattville Police Chief Mark Thompson said. Prattville Fire Chief Josh Bingham also remembers Davis as a hard worker and great officer. Bingham said those who want to honor Davis should do something nice for someone else. Law enforcement held a procession Tuesday morning as Davis’ body was transported from Montgomery to Millbrook. “We ask that you keep his wife, his family, and the PPD in your thoughts and prayers. We also ask for prayers for the first responders at the scene of the accident and the family of the vehicle involved,” Thompson continued. The crash remains under investigation by the Alabama Law Enforcement Agency. Further details regarding the collision were not immediately released.

items.t: Cheerios teams up with Ziploc to create resealable bags inside cereal boxes (finally)
items.x: (Gray News) — It’s been a long time coming: General Mills is introducing the first cereal box that includes a resealable bag. Say goodbye to folding, rolling or clipping the bag, or even transferring the cereal to an airtight container. Cheerios and Honey Nut Cheerios will be available with new packaging that includes a Ziploc PantrySeal™ bag. General Mills said this marks the first resealable bag inside a traditional cereal box, making it easier to pour and reseal while helping keep cereal fresh longer. “General Mills has received letters, emails and DMs asking for an easier way to reseal a cereal box, and we decided it was time to partner with the ultimate freshness brand: Ziploc®,” said Emilie Knox, Vice President and Business Unit Director for Cheerios at General Mills. “Cheerios with Ziploc PantrySeal™ takes a small, everyday cereal frustration and finally gives consumers the simple solution they’ve been asking for, making the whole routine easier and more enjoyable.” The new boxes will be available exclusively at Walmart.com beginning Oct. 27 and will be available at retailers nationwide in the coming months.

items.t: Woman dies after being hit by car in McDonald’s parking lot
items.x: WHITE OAK, Texas ( KLTV /Gray News) - A woman died after being hit by a vehicle in the parking lot of a fast-food restaurant, authorities said. White Oak police responded to the fatal crash around 4:35 p.m. Oct. 21 in the McDonald’s parking lot in the 600 block of East U.S. Highway 80. During the investigation, officers determined a woman walked out of the building, crouched in the driveway and began looking in her purse when a vehicle drove around the building and hit her, authorities said. Officers determined the woman was not visible to the driver due to rounding a blind corner and the woman being so low to the ground, according to a release. Paramedics took the woman to a hospital, where she later died, according to the release. Police determined the crash was an accident, and no criminal charges will be filed, according to the release. “Any incident involving the loss of life is a tragedy,” a department spokesperson wrote. “Our thoughts are with the family of the victim.”

items.t: Former Detroit Lions tight end Deon Butler to speak at Concord
items.x: ATHENS, W.Va. (WVVA) – Former Detroit Lions tight end Deon Butler will speak with high school and college students on Nov. 2 at Concord University. He was signed to an NFL team’s active roster before realizing that he couldn’t read the playbook. Butler has dyslexia, a learning disorder that disrupted how he processed and interpreted the written language, communicated and sensed direction. He travels the country sharing his experiences and encouraging students to believe in themselves, embrace their challenges and to never give up on their goals. Butler will speak inside the Carter Center’s gymnasium. The day’s agenda includes: 9:30 a.m. - 10:30 a.m.: Morning session with high school students; 11:30 a.m. - 12:30 p.m.: Lunch & networking with members of the Mountain Lion Success Network; 1 p.m. - 2:30 p.m.: Afternoon session with college students, offering perspectives and guidance relevant to their academic, personal and professional development.

items.t: We compared AI travel videos with real listings; here’s what we found
items.x: ATLANTA, Ga. ( InvestigateTV ) — A scroll through social media can make a mountain cabin, beachfront rental or luxury resort look like an easy escape. But some AI-generated travel videos may not accurately show the property a viewer would book or the price a viewer would pay. We reviewed TikTok posts promoting real hotels, resorts and vacation rentals. The posts included TikTok labels stating they were generated with artificial intelligence and that the creator earns commission. Several directed viewers to major booking services, including Expedia and Booking.com . In multiple examples, the apparently AI-generated video did not appear to match the property’s official listing or other photos. In others, the price promoted in the video was not a deal we could locate when we checked the listing. Using AI to create travel posts is not inherently illegal. The concern is whether commercial posts create a misleading impression about a real property, price, amenity, review or travel experience. items.t: Decatur mayor wants city to grow to 75,000 residents, plans more housing and apartments
items.x: HUNTSVILLE, Ala. ( WAFF ) - Decatur Mayor Kent Lawrence wants the city’s population to grow from about 59,000 to 75,000 residents. “Now, that’s not going to happen in my term, but that’s the goal that I’ve set that we’re working toward,” Lawrence said. Lawrence said the city would need to grow 2.5% each year for the next decade to reach this target. While the city has not grown at that rate in previous years, Lawrence said he expects the city to reach a 2.5% annual increase soon. “We haven’t grown as fast as other communities around us, but we’re on a clip now to do that,” he said. Lawrence said the city would need to build 600 to 700 housing units a year to reach that rate. So far, The city has permitted more than 50 houses a month in the past three months. Two new apartment complexes are under construction in Decatur. They will be the first new apartments built in the city since 1996. But Lawrence said he is also expecting commercial development to follow residential growth. “Rooftops drives commercial.
