items.t: The barbershop quartet tradition is alive in New Orleans
items.x: NEW ORLEANS ( InvestigateTV ) - On a Mid City evening, a four-part harmony rang out just off Canal Street. The group, Southern Tradition, has been around since 1999. The quartet is a place where a traditional American art form forges a friendship. “The main attribute to be a barbershop quartet singer is to not be embarrassed, just keep going,” said Karl Hansen. Four men with four different careers create one sound. Hansen is a doctor who sings bass. Hansen Eschette is a med tech singing tenor. Joe Jacquat is a civil engineer who sings baritone. Johnnie Oufnac is the only actual barber in this barbershop quartet, singing lead. “Being together for a long time helps us harmonize and understand where the other person is going,” Hansen said. Barbershop quartets have been around for more than a century. Though they can be found all over the world, ties to New Orleans are strong. “It really is the nexus of American music at its most basic level and a lot of it comes from New Orleans,” said Zachary Matherne. items.x: CHARLOTTE, N.C. ( InvestigateTV ) - Diabetes is the seventh leading cause of death in the United States, the No. 1 cause of kidney disease, and an estimated 40 million people are living with it nationwide. Despite decades of prevention education and major breakthroughs in treatment, doctors say diabetes continues to hit the South especially hard — including North Carolina. It can create serious long-term complications, including coronary artery disease, heart attacks, never damage, and amputations. But many people who have the disease may not know it. The CDC estimates around 11 million live with undiagnosed diabetes. “Every day, almost every hour” battle Andrew Tucker has lived with Type 2 diabetes for nearly two decades. He’s made major lifestyle changes but said managing the disease is still a daily fight. Tucker was diagnosed about 15 years ago, when he was 35. “Yes, for me, it is truly an everyday, almost every hour watching what I do,” Tucker said. Type 2 diabetes develops when the body doesn’t make enough insulin or doesn’t use insulin properly. Doctors say obesity is a major risk factor. items.t: This veteran is using his service dog to regain independence
items.x: ST. LOUIS, Mo. ( InvestigateTV ) - Veteran James Poggi served in the Marine Corps working in aviation. His time in the military led to a lifelong strain on his body, including five back surgeries and a below-the-knee amputation. “You go from being six foot three, 250 pounds and able to travel halfway across the world and do whatever they ask you to do, to being relying on wheelchairs, walkers, mobility devices, things like that, you become a vulnerable person that you never thought you’d be,” Poggi said. Poggi said he was in multiple accidents, hard landings, PT accidents and a car crash. He also developed spinal meningitis. “And that was all while I was active,” he said. To help ease some of the emotional toll, Poggi’s wife, who is also his caregiver, suggested he get a service dog. Service dog provides daily support Poggi got Teddy, a Goldendoodle, who serves as his service dog and daily lifeline. “You never went anywhere without your battle buddy. And he always, always better have your back. And that’s how it is. He’s always got my back,” Poggi said. items.t: Economist explains how the ‘K-shaped economy’ is impacting the midterms
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - As voters prepare to head to the polls for the midterm elections, a conflicting economic sentiment is once again emerging on the campaign trail. “Voters reflect the perception of the cost of living as they experienced, as opposed to what is in the data,” said Alessandro Rebucci, an economics professor at Johns Hopkins Carey Business School. “In the data, you have an economy that is very strong as a whole. How that pie is distributed affects how a large segment of the population and the voters are feeling about the economy right now.” The contradiction has been described by many economists recently, as the “k-shaped” economy, using a graph to depict how high-income earners and asset owners are doing compared to middle and lower-income earners. “To be concrete, the wealthiest households are presumed to spend much more than the lowest ones, not only in absolute terms, which is obvious, but also as a share of their income and in their wealth,” Rebucci said. items.t: College professor among 2 found dead in home; suspect in custody, police say
items.x: LORAIN COUNTY, Ohio. ( WOIO /Gray News) - An Ohio college professor and a woman were found shot to death in a home, and a suspect is in custody, according to authorities. When crews arrived, they tried to find the registered vehicle owner, identified as Daniel Jones, 31, to conduct a welfare check. Herbert Kimble was sentenced to 20 years’ imprisonment with three years of court-ordered supervision. items.t: For politics, what is an October surprise?
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - An October surprise is an event that could shake up an election, but does it often make the difference? Matt Dallek, a professor of political management at George Washington University, described it as “an event that, at least in theory, has the potential to shake up an election, something that people did not foresee coming that upends the debate.” He said the term dates back to around the 1980 election, when President Jimmy Carter failed to secure the release of American hostages being held in Iran before November 4, 1980, election day. Carter lost to Republican rival Ronald Reagan. Several surprises have occurred in the years since. Surprises can be driven by a campaign or by news events. Examples include Iran-Contra-related indictments in 1992 and the global financial collapse in 2008. Dallek said those surprises likely did not change the outcome of the election that November. “There’s no evidence that they flip a dynamic that was already in place,” Dallek said. “What’s more typical is that an event occurs, it dominates the news cycle and the trend line starts to move further toward the candidate who was already doing well, who was already likely to prevai

The final tally of early voting in Louisiana by the Louisiana Secretary of State’s office shows 520,942 people voted in this year’s midterm election. That is a 38% increase from the midterms in 2022, when 377,428 voters cast early ballots. An Orleans Parish election official said the turnout so far is impressive. “I think people are coming out in this big number because what is happening in our country is monumental, and people typically turn out more during midterms and presidential elections in general. So, everyone wants to exercise their right to vote,” said Chelsey Napoleon, Orleans Parish Clerk of Court. Dillard University political analyst Dr. Robert Collins said the early numbers seem to reflect a higher enthusiasm for this election, especially among Democrats and Black voters. “I think a lot of people feel that the Black voters in Louisiana feel under attack. When people feel under attack, that’s when they get more involved in the political process,” said Robert Collins, Ph.D., political analyst at Dillard University. Surveillance footage was released by the Toledo Lucas County Public Library, appearing to show a person throwing a box of cockroaches at a staff member on Tuesday at the Kent Branch Library. Surveillance footage apparently shows someone throwing a box of cockroaches at a library employee in Ohio. items.t: Grandmother not indicted in baby’s death after police say she left her in hot car for 8 hours while she worked
items.x: MADISONVILLE, Ky. ( WFIE /Gray News) — A Kentucky doctor who accidentally left her grandchild unattended in a hot car for about eight hours will not be indicted for the baby’s death. Madisonville police said 10-month-old Scottie Crowell died in August . On Tuesday, a grand jury found there was insufficient probable cause for an indictment. Police said Scottie’s grandmother picked her up in the morning of Aug. 13 and was supposed to take her to daycare. She forgot the child was in the car and went to work, police said. She arrived at Owensboro Health Multi-Care, where she works as a doctor, around 8 a.m. The baby’s father called his wife after trying to pick up Scottie from daycare, but the child was not there. The baby’s mother called the grandmother at work, and the grandmother ran outside and saw Scottie was still in the vehicle around 4 p.m., police said. After 911 was called, first responders tried to administer lifesaving measures, but the baby died. “I would ask that you keep the infant’s parents and family in your thoughts and prayers as they continue to grieve and process this unimaginable loss,” said Commonwealth’s Attorney Hannah Kington-Jarvis.

items.t: Ernie Johnson announces this will be his final season on ‘Inside The NBA’
items.x: (Gray News) - Ernie Johnson announced he will be stepping down as host of “Inside the NBA” at the end of the season. The Sports Broadcasting Hall of Famer took to social media on Wednesday to explain his decision to step away, saying, “It’s just time.” Johnson, 70, stated that he would not be retiring, but cutting back. “This is by no means the end. It’s just a turning of the page,” Johnson said. “And I’ll forever cherish every chapter we have written with ‘Inside the NBA.’” Johnson said he plans to continue to work, including covering the NCAA men’s basketball tournament for CBS and Turner Sports. The six-time Sports Emmy Award winner acknowledged that he has dealt with heart issues in recent years, but that isn’t the reason he’s stepping away from the show. “I just want to slow down a bit,” he added in his social media post. Johnson joined Turner Sports in 1989 and has hosted “Inside the NBA” since 1990. He thanked his TNT Sports and ESPN crews for their support over the years, as well as the viewers. “I just want to say thanks to you. Thanks for your loyalty, for your love, for your support. And on this day, for your understanding,” Johnson said.

items.t: Meet the volunteers who bring flowers from weddings and funerals to hospice patients
items.x: LOUISVILLE, Ky. ( Aging Untold ) — Inside Crescent Hill Baptist Church in Louisville, a group of volunteers gathers each week surrounded by color, creativity and collaboration. They call themselves the Flower Buds. From events to those in need The Flower Buds take donated flowers from weddings, funerals, wholesalers, supermarkets, florists, galas, banquets and other community events. They cut, clean and arrange the blooms into vases, then deliver them to nursing homes, the VA hospital, assisted living facilities and shelters. “Amazingly gifted with so many flowers from places like Kroger who have overbought and can’t sell them, and they allow us to pick them up and then bring them here, and then we cut them, clean them and vase them. Then we take them to nursing homes, the VA hospital, assisted living facilities,” Jodie Raible, a Flower Buds volunteer, said. The group sends out about 100 vases every week. “I take flowers to Up for Women and Children, it’s a day homeless shelter for women,” Stephanie Mullins, a Flower Buds volunteer, said. items.t: Illegal moonshine distillery explodes, catches fire in mountains, officials say
items.x: WILKES COUNTY, N.C. ( WBTV /Gray News) - An explosion at an illegal moonshine distillery sparked a fire in the North Carolina mountains on Monday, according to authorities. Special agents from North Carolina’s Alcohol Law Enforcement Division were called to investigate the explosion in Wilkes County, North Carolina. Agents found an active 200-gallon illegal distillery. They seized about 1,800 gallons of mash, which is used to make moonshine, and 161 gallons of illegal moonshine. North Carolina officials shared photos showing the charred inside of a metal building. Distilling equipment was also damaged. Billy Ray Anderson, 69, was arrested and charged with manufacturing a non-taxpaid alcoholic beverage, possession for sale of a non-taxpaid alcoholic beverage, possession of a non-taxpaid alcoholic beverage, possession of distillery equipment, possession of distillery ingredients and allowing property to be used for the manufacture of a non-taxpaid alcoholic beverage. Moonshine is believed to have originated in North Carolina and was once an important source of income, particularly for rural residents.

items.t: Some packaged salads recalled for undeclared allergens
items.x: (Gray News) - Packaged salads produced by Taylor Farms have been recalled due to an undeclared allergen. According to the Food and Drug Administration, Taylor Farms is recalling its H-E-B Backyard BBQ Chop Salad because it may contain undeclared soy and tree nuts, specifically almonds. “People who have sensitivity or allergy to soy and tree nuts (almonds) may be at risk of a serious adverse reaction if they consume this product,” an FDA press release said. So far there have not been any illnesses or “adverse reactions” reported in connection with the recall. The salads were sold in H-E-B stores across Texas. They can be identified by their UPC code, 041220300457, and their best-by date, Oct. 30, 2026. Customers are asked not to eat the recalled salads and to throw them away or return them to the store for a refund.

items.t: Judges hear arguments on whether case should stay open over Louisiana’s remaining majority-minority district
items.x: SHREVEPORT, La. (KSLA) - Federal judges in Shreveport heard arguments on whether a case related to Louisiana’s congressional maps should remain open. The Supreme Court previously ruled that a second majority-minority district drawn based on race was unconstitutional. The outcome does not affect the map used for this year’s midterm elections. Advocates say leaving the case open could lead to challenges against Louisiana’s remaining majority-minority district. What the hearing covered The arguments came during a motion to dismiss hearing in Callais v. Landry. Judges heard from lawyers representing voters who are considering a challenge to Louisiana’s current congressional map. The map has one majority-minority district. One side argued there could be room to explore whether violations exist in the remaining majority-minority district. The other side said the terms have already been satisfied and that a new claim should be filed in a separate lawsuit. Arguments for dismissal Attorneys from the Legal Defense Fund and the state of Louisiana argued there is no active violation. items.t: How to spot fake crystals and avoid costly mistakes
items.x: SEDONA, Ariz. ( Aging Untold ) — The crystal and gemstone industry is booming, fueled in part by social media, but experts warn buyers to be cautious of fake products flooding the market. Jamie Inglett, who owns a crystal shop in Sedona, said consumers can find fake crystals in stores and at gem shows. “As a consumer you really kind of have to do your own research,” Inglett said. Growing popularity drives demand The crystal craze has exploded online, with #crystals generating 20 billion views on TikTok. Inglett has built up 215,106 Instagram followers and opened a physical storefront in Sedona after finding success online. “You don’t have to believe in crystal healing or crystal energy to appreciate their beauty,” Inglett said. What to know about fake crystals Shannon Wimberly, a crystal collector for several years, said she has encountered fake crystals and now scrutinizes purchases more carefully. “I absolutely know I’ve run into getting fake ones, so I started scrutinizing other things more and more,” Wimberly said. items.t: Caregiver advocate shares 3 policies that could help family caregivers
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — More than 60 million Americans are family caregivers, balancing work, kids and care for an aging parent or loved one. Jason Resendez, president and CEO of the National Alliance for Caregiving, recently testified before the U.S. Senate Special Committee on Aging. He joined gerontologist “Sam” Cradduck to talk through the solutions he presented. The three policies he brought to lawmakers Resendez said the National Alliance for Caregiving is championing changes “to address so many of the pain points that family caregivers face every day.” 1) Older Americans Act funding He said one priority is reauthorization and funding of the Older Americans Act. Resendez said the law provides dollars for state Area Agencies on Aging to deliver services for older adults, such as Meals on Wheels and caregiver support. “One of the only federal line items for caregiving comes through the Older Americans Act, and it’s called the National Family Caregiver Support Program,” Resendez said. He said the program funds respite, which gives caregivers the chance to take breaks. items.t: Long-term care costs rose about 50% in five years, report finds
items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — The cost of long-term care jumped nearly 50% in five years, while income for older households rose just 22%, according to a new AARP report . The report found long-term services and supports are becoming even less affordable for middle-class Americans. Alan Weil, senior vice president for public policy at AARP, said the gap is the most important finding. “Between 2019 and 2024, a five-year period, the cost of most long-term care services went up about 50%, but the incomes for older households only went up by about 22%,” Weil said. “So the gap between what people can afford and what it costs has grown.” The AARP also looked at what different types of care cost. Weil said the more skilled the service, the higher the price. “If you need someone to come in and help you prepare food, that’s less expensive than if you need someone to come in and provide nursing-level care,” Weil said. “Although I’ll also say that we’ve learned that a lot of caregivers are being forced to provide nursing care that they can’t afford to pay someone else to do, even though they’ve never been trained in nursing. items.t: Butter sold in 10 states recalled over possible yeast, mold and E. coli contamination
items.x: (Gray News) - Butter is being recalled because it might be contaminated with yeast, mold and E. coli, according to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. More than 1,300 cases of Miyoko’s Creamery European Style Salted Plant Milk Butter have been recalled in Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Iowa, Illinois, Indiana, Maryland, New Jersey, New Hampshire and Wisconsin. The recalled butter has lot code 07871 and a best-by date of Nov. 5, 2026. If you have the butter, you should not eat it, but the recall notice did not give further information about refunds.

items.t: She was born with eight fingers on one hand. Her family traveled to America for the surgery
items.x: ST. LOUIS, Mo. ( InvestigateTV ) - A family traveled from Turkey to St. Louis for their daughter’s surgery to treat a rare condition affecting fewer than 100 people worldwide. Elisa, an 18-month-old, was born with eight fingers on her left hand. She was diagnosed with Ulnar Dimelia, also known as Mirror Hand Syndrome. “Mirror Hand is incredibly uncommon, and even surgeons like myself who take care of a great deal of kids almost never see this in their career. So, it’s really uncommon. Numbers are hard to come by, but one in a million or less is probably about right,” said Dr. Charles Goldfarb, Chief of Orthopedic Surgery at St. Louis Children’s Hospital. The condition leaves patients without a radius bone. This means significant limitations in wrist and elbow motion and preserved shoulder movements. “From the very beginning, he was really warm, genuine, and gave us a lot of hope. Honestly, the trust and support he gave us played a huge role in our decision to come to St. Louis,” said Emircan Buga, Elisa’s father. items.t: Officials working to expand foster care for children in America, here’s how
items.x: NASHVILLE, Tenn. ( InvestigateTV ) - Kids sleeping in shelters, bussed between hotels, and overnights in office buildings. That’s the reality for many foster children in America. For every 100 children in foster care, federal data shows that only 57 licenses homes are available. In an effort to close that gap, the federal government launched a campaign in November 2025 called “A Home for Every Child.” “When we launched this, we offered states the choice: if they joined the Home for Every Child campaign, they would get administrative relief,” said Alex Adams, assistant secretary for the administration for children and families. “We would get them out of mountains of paperwork so that they could spend more time focused on things that actually improve child welfare outcomes. They would have more time working with kids, more time working with families. Since then, the idea to reinvent systems that recruit and retain foster families has gained nationwide momentum. Jonathan Chad Simmons faces one count of manslaughter and one count of second-degree elder abuse in the death of his mother, according to Tuscaloosa County court documents obtained by WBRC. The court documents referred to the victim as Jonathan Chad Simmons’ mother, Brenda Hallman Simmons. Law enforcement found Brenda Hallman Simmons, 76, alive but unresponsive. Brenda Simmons died several days later while receiving medical care. The autopsy revealed she died from sepsis due to complications from multiple open bedsores. Joint investigation begins The Tuscaloosa Violent Crimes Unit and the state medical examiner’s office began a joint investigation after the family and health personnel suspected neglect. items.t: Canned fruit sold at Walmart recalled in several states
items.x: (Gray News) - A voluntary recall over lead concerns has been issued for cans of Walmart fruit cocktail distributed to stores in at least seven states. The Food and Drug Administration said the recall applies to 15-ounce containers of Great Value Fruit Cocktail in Fruit Juice from Concentrate. Where the product was distributed More than 1,830 cases, or approximately 44,000 individual cans, were distributed to Walmart locations in Alabama, Arizona, Louisiana, New Mexico, Pennsylvania, Washington and Wyoming, the FDA said. How to identify the product The product is marked with lot number “6FCB 04 C2263” and a best if used by date of Sept. 1, 2027. Recall details The FDA initiated the recall for “potential contamination with elevated levels of lead” on Oct. 1. It was reclassified as a Class II recall on Oct. 20. According to the FDA, Class II recalls are issued when a product can cause temporary health effects with a remote possibility of serious issues. What customers should do Customers should throw the item away or return it to Walmart.

items.t: 24-year-old deputy killed in crash with coal truck while on duty, sheriff’s office says
items.x: LOGAN COUNTY, W. Va ( WSAZ /Gray News) - A 24-year-old sheriff’s deputy was killed in a crash while responding to a call, authorities said. The Logan County Sheriff’s Department identified the deputy as 24-year-old Caden Mullins. Deputy Mullins’ fiancée was airlifted from the scene of the crash to a hospital. Deputies say Mullins and his fiancée were at a truck-or-treat event on Saturday in the Man area when he received an emergency call from the sheriff’s department. The sheriff’s department says Deputy Caden Mullins, 24, died in the crash. Mullins was on his way to drop his fiancée off and head to the call when the crash occurred around 5 p.m., deputies say. Deputies say the crash happened at the intersection of Rum Creek Road and Route 10 when a coal truck pulled off the road and hit Mullins’ vehicle. Mullins worked for the Charleston Police Department for about a year before joining the Logan County Sheriff’s Department to be closer to family, the department said.

items.t: Louisiana publishers raise copyright concerns as Madison Journal says it will stop using Facebook
items.x: MONROE, La. (KNOE) - The Madison Journal says it will stop using Facebook and pursue legal action, alleging its copyrighted content is being exploited by the social media company. Sam Hanna Jr., publisher of The Ouachita Citizen in West Monroe and president of the Louisiana Press Association, said he understands where the Madison Journal is coming from. Meta delays ad terms rollout Meta has delayed a rollout of its latest commercial and self-serve ad terms for Facebook and Instagram from Oct. 30 to Nov. 20. Publishers discuss content rights Hanna said the announcement raises questions about how social media companies use news content and what rights publishers have to protect their work. “As an owner and a publisher of community newspapers, I will not sign any agreement, user agreement that forfeits control or ownership of my content. And I can’t imagine any other media organization doing the same,” Hanna said. John Wyatt Emmerich, publisher of the Northside Sun and president of Emmerich Newspapers, said publishers have been trying to protect their copyrights for years. “This has been going on. items.t: Woman shot multiple times, man dead after attempted murder-suicide in Metairie
items.x: NEW ORLEANS (WVUE) - A woman is in critical condition Tuesday (Oct. 27) after a man shot her multiple times in Metairie, according to the Jefferson Parish Sheriff’s Office. Authorities said at about 5:45 p.m., the man shot the woman at 110 Veterans Memorial Boulevard in Metairie. They say he then drove to Oaklawn Drive and Toulouse Street and killed himself. The Jefferson Parish Coroner’s office identified the gunman Wednesday as Ahmad Alexander Rochon, a 27-year-old from Lafayette. Deputies on Tuesday night taped off the parking lot of an office building at the end of Veterans Boulevard as they investigated a car that was still running with its doors open. A witness who didn’t want to be identified said they heard multiple gunshots and saw an ambulance drive away with the woman, who had a bandage on her neck. Melanie and Christopher Todd were arrested after officers responded to their home on Cardinal Court to check on their children and animals, according to the criminal complaint. Police described the living conditions as “deplorable and unlivable.” Officers conducted the welfare check Sept. 29 after Middletown City Schools reported that two 10-year-old children appeared dirty and said they had no food to eat, police said. items.t: Entergy Louisiana offers $100 bill credits starting Oct. 28
items.x: LAKE CHARLES, La. (KPLC) - Struggling to keep up with higher household costs could get a little easier for thousands of Entergy Louisiana customers this week. Entergy Louisiana is launching a $2 million bill assistance program offering a one-time $100 bill credit, funded by shareholder dollars. Applications open Oct. 28 at 9 a.m. through United Way partners while funds last. The program covers customers living below the federal poverty level and ALICE households who earn above poverty level but below the cost of living in their parish. “This bill credit is one more way we’re stepping up to support the communities we serve during a time when everyday costs are on the rise,” said Nyka Scott, Entergy Louisiana customer service vice president. Customers can apply online through the United Way serving their parish. Applicants will need a photo ID and income documentation for each earner age 18 or older, such as a 2025 tax return first page, W-2, recent pay stub or Social Security benefit letter. For more information, click HERE.

items.t: Energy Department authorizes emergency oil exchange for Phillips 66 Lake Charles refinery
items.x: LAKE CHARLES, La. (KPLC) - A disruption at one of the area’s largest refineries prompted emergency federal action to keep fuel flowing. The U.S. Department of Energy authorized an emergency exchange of up to 400,000 barrels of crude oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve to the Phillips 66 Lake Charles Refinery. The oil will come from the West Hackberry site for immediate delivery to support production for Louisiana and surrounding markets. The refinery confirmed it received the crude, but would not elaborate on why it was needed. Under the exchange, Phillips 66 will return all borrowed oil plus additional premium barrels, helping replenish the reserve at no extra cost to taxpayers. “With this exchange, the Energy Department is taking definitive action to support refinery operations, maintain stable fuel supplies, and ensure all Americans continue to have access to the affordable, reliable, and secure energy they rely on every day,” said Under Secretary of Energy Kyle Haustveit.

items.t: Woman arrested after 4-year-old found dead in Atlanta townhome
items.x: WASHINGTON, Ga. ( WRDW /Gray News) - A woman was arrested Tuesday morning after a 4-year-old boy was found dead more than an hour away in an Atlanta townhome, authorities said. Wilkes County Sheriff Darrell Powers said Jasmaine Smoak was arrested and booked into the Wilkes County Detention Center. According to WRDW’s sister station, Atlanta News First , Atlanta police responded to a gated community in the 3500 block of Cardinal Drive SW on Monday night for a welfare check. Officers forced their way into the home “based on information received during the welfare check,” Atlanta police said. Once inside, officers found the child dead. Emergency personnel attempted lifesaving measures but were unsuccessful, police said. Powers said deputies worked closely with Atlanta homicide detectives to locate Smoak using license plate reader technology. Smoak is charged with second-degree cruelty to children and concealing the death of another. Atlanta police said Smoak is a friend of the child’s mother. The circumstances surrounding the boy’s death remain unclear.

items.t: Stained envelope disrupts last day of early voting at Yenni Building in Jefferson Parish

items.x: GREENVILLE COUNTY, S.C. ( WHNS /Gray News) - South Carolina authorities are asking for additional victims to come forward after a series of late-night burglaries targeting women home alone. Greenville County Sheriff Hobart Lewis said investigators were made aware on Oct. 16 of multiple burglaries that shared “some very concerning similarities.” In each burglary, a suspect entered or attempted to enter homes occupied by women who were alone at the time, Lewis said. Investigators identified the suspect as 25-year-old Terron Lamon Banks. Through their investigation, detectives said they linked Banks to four burglaries in September, including one where he entered an apartment through an unlocked window while a woman was sleeping. Banks’ charges include four counts of first-degree burglary, one count of grand larceny and one count of voyeurism. items.t: ‘Devastating’: Police department mourns death of officer in off-duty crash
items.x: AUTAUGA COUNTY, Ala. ( WSFA /Gray News) - A police officer in Alabama has died in an off-duty crash this week. According to the Prattville Police Department, Cpl. Dakota Lee Davis did not survive the injuries he sustained in a crash on Highway 31 on Monday afternoon. “The loss of CPL. Davis is devastating not only to the Prattville Police Department but to the city of Prattville. He will be missed by all,” Prattville Police Chief Mark Thompson said. Prattville Fire Chief Josh Bingham also remembers Davis as a hard worker and great officer. Bingham said those who want to honor Davis should do something nice for someone else. Law enforcement held a procession Tuesday morning as Davis’ body was transported from Montgomery to Millbrook. “We ask that you keep his wife, his family, and the PPD in your thoughts and prayers. We also ask for prayers for the first responders at the scene of the accident and the family of the vehicle involved,” Thompson continued. The crash remains under investigation by the Alabama Law Enforcement Agency. Further details regarding the collision were not immediately released.

items.t: Cheerios teams up with Ziploc to create resealable bags inside cereal boxes (finally)
items.x: (Gray News) — It’s been a long time coming: General Mills is introducing the first cereal box that includes a resealable bag. Say goodbye to folding, rolling or clipping the bag, or even transferring the cereal to an airtight container. Cheerios and Honey Nut Cheerios will be available with new packaging that includes a Ziploc PantrySeal™ bag. General Mills said this marks the first resealable bag inside a traditional cereal box, making it easier to pour and reseal while helping keep cereal fresh longer. “General Mills has received letters, emails and DMs asking for an easier way to reseal a cereal box, and we decided it was time to partner with the ultimate freshness brand: Ziploc®,” said Emilie Knox, Vice President and Business Unit Director for Cheerios at General Mills. “Cheerios with Ziploc PantrySeal™ takes a small, everyday cereal frustration and finally gives consumers the simple solution they’ve been asking for, making the whole routine easier and more enjoyable.” The new boxes will be available exclusively at Walmart.com beginning Oct. 27 and will be available at retailers nationwide in the coming months.

items.t: Woman dies after being hit by car in McDonald’s parking lot
items.x: WHITE OAK, Texas ( KLTV /Gray News) - A woman died after being hit by a vehicle in the parking lot of a fast-food restaurant, authorities said. White Oak police responded to the fatal crash around 4:35 p.m. Oct. 21 in the McDonald’s parking lot in the 600 block of East U.S. Highway 80. During the investigation, officers determined a woman walked out of the building, crouched in the driveway and began looking in her purse when a vehicle drove around the building and hit her, authorities said. Officers determined the woman was not visible to the driver due to rounding a blind corner and the woman being so low to the ground, according to a release. Paramedics took the woman to a hospital, where she later died, according to the release. Police determined the crash was an accident, and no criminal charges will be filed, according to the release. “Any incident involving the loss of life is a tragedy,” a department spokesperson wrote. “Our thoughts are with the family of the victim.”

items.t: We compared AI travel videos with real listings; here’s what we found
items.x: ATLANTA, Ga. ( InvestigateTV ) — A scroll through social media can make a mountain cabin, beachfront rental or luxury resort look like an easy escape. But some AI-generated travel videos may not accurately show the property a viewer would book or the price a viewer would pay. We reviewed TikTok posts promoting real hotels, resorts and vacation rentals. The posts included TikTok labels stating they were generated with artificial intelligence and that the creator earns commission. Several directed viewers to major booking services, including Expedia and Booking.com . In multiple examples, the apparently AI-generated video did not appear to match the property’s official listing or other photos. In others, the price promoted in the video was not a deal we could locate when we checked the listing. Using AI to create travel posts is not inherently illegal. The concern is whether commercial posts create a misleading impression about a real property, price, amenity, review or travel experience. items.t: Missing woman reportedly found alive in Mexico, but her family has doubts
items.x: PHOENIX ( KPHO /Gray News) — Mexican authorities said a missing Arizona woman was believed to have been found in Tijuana, but family members say they have doubts. Shayna Feinman, 35, was reported missing in March 2024. A Tijuana security force said Feinman was found on Oct. 23 after reports of a woman matching her description in an Encino neighborhood. The security force said the woman was confirmed to be Feinman, but Yavapai County Sheriff’s Office officials initially said they couldn’t independently confirm her identity because of “insufficient evidence.” Feinman’s sister Kara added that she did not recognize the person in Mexico and didn’t have hard evidence that the person was indeed her sister. Kara said this wasn’t the first time Feinman was reported to have been spotted. Feinman’s sister called these types of reports with little evidence from law enforcement agencies disheartening to the family. Tijuana officials said they took the woman in question to a safe location to await contact with the Feinman family and U.S. authorities. Details were not immediately shared about how Feinman may have ended up in Mexico. Yavapai County Sheriff’s deputies said Feinman vanished without

The arrest warrant said a girl walking to her bus stop was approached by a gray 2024 Kia Forte whose driver exposed himself. Police said Flock surveillance cameras tracked the car to Stafford, whom the victim identified in a photo lineup. Stafford is running for house district 42 in Smyrna, a seat held by Democrat Gabriel Sanchez. Stafford has been photographed with a number of prominent GOP officials, including state Sen. Mike Collins, seeking to unseat U.S. Sen. items.t: Special needs teacher accused of pouring hot sauce on student’s tongue as a punishment
items.x: HOUSTON COUNTY, Ala. ( WTVY /Gray News) - An Alabama special needs teacher is facing child abuse charges after deputies say she poured hot sauce on a student’s tongue. Heather Varner Hunter, a 46-year-old special needs teacher at Cottonwood Elementary School, allegedly used hot sauce to punish a student for sticking out their tongue in September. A Houston County Sheriff’s Office investigation followed. Jail records show Hunter was arrested Monday afternoon. She is no longer employed by the Houston County School System, according to Superintendent Brandy White. White said the school system cooperated fully with authorities, and all information has been turned over to the Alabama Department of Human Resources. Hunter was named Teacher of the Month in March, according to 95.5 WTVY-FM. She said she had taught at Cottonwood for eight years and spent 18 years as an educator. Hunter was released after posting a $2,500 bond.

items.t: Former true-crime producer accused of posing as aircraft heiress added to FBI most-wanted list
items.x: (Gray News) - A 75-year-old woman who allegedly posed as an heiress to steal more than $14 million has been added to the FBI’s Most Wanted list. According to the FBI, Mary Carole McDonnell is accused of posing as the heiress to the McDonnell Aircraft family with an $80 million secret trust. The McDonnell Aircraft Corporation was an aerospace manufacturer best known for its military aircrafts. The FBI said the alleged scheme began in July 2017 and lasted until May 2018. McDonnell allegedly obtained $14.7 million from Banc of California, as well as an additional $15 million from other financial institutions. On Dec. 12, 2018, a federal arrest warrant was issued for McDonnell. She faces charges of bank fraud and aggravated identity theft. McDonnell is described as 5-foot-7 with blond hair and blue eyes. She weighs about 145 pounds and has a scar on her right knee. Mary Carole McDonnell was the chief executive officer of Bellum Entertainment, LLC, a company based in Burbank, Calif., that produced and distributed several television shows, including true-crime programs like “It Takes a Killer” and “I Married a Murderer.” McDonnell has used several aliases, including Mary Carole Carroll,

items.t: Teenager charged in hit-and-run that killed 6-year-old getting off the bus

Police said Espinoza was taken to a hospital with life-threatening injuries and died there the following day. Doorbell camera footage obtained by WBTV on Monday shows the moments before Espinoza was hit. Court documents filed Monday allege that Finnie was driving the Mercedes-Benz that hit and killed Espinoza. Police had released a photo of the gray Mercedes-Benz, believed to be the car involved in the hit-and-run, Monday morning. By Monday evening, police said they identified Finnie as a suspect in the case after “conducting a traffic stop on the suspect vehicle.” The car had been seized as evidence. items.t: New Orleans named a finalist to host men’s, women’s NCAA Final Fours sometime between 2032-36
items.x: NEW ORLEANS (WVUE) - New Orleans has emerged as a finalist to host both a men’s and a women’s NCAA basketball tournament Final Four sometime between 2032-36, the organization announced Tuesday (Oct. 27). At the end of the NCAA’s fall meetings, seven finalist cities were revealed to be vying for the five men’s and women’s Final Fours during those years. items.t: Aging Untold: Hospice doesn’t have to happen at home
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — On this episode of Aging Untold, we explore compassionate hospice care options beyond the home, focusing on comfort, dignity and family support. Then, a breast cancer survivor opens up about the emotional toll of chemotherapy-induced hair loss and how she reclaimed her identity and strength. Hospice doesn’t have to happen at home Hospice care is about comfort, dignity and quality of life. It isn’t tied to one setting, the Aging Untold experts said. Hospice care can happen in a hospital, in independent living, assisted living, or in a private home. “For me, it’s whatever brings comfort to the family,” gerontologist “Sam” Cradduck said. “At this point, we’ve got to make sure that the person’s comfortable, that they’re being provided the care and the dignity they deserve.” Read the full article here. items.t: The Exoneree Band: How a group of wrongfully convicted men found their voice through music
items.x: ( Aging Untold )— They don’t have the fame of The Beatles or the fortune of The Rolling Stones, but the members of The Exoneree band share something far more profound. Now, as free men, they are using the power of music to heal, to tell their stories, and to build a brotherhood unlike any other. The band was born out of the Innocence Network’s annual conference, a gathering that brings together wrongfully convicted people from across the country. In 2011, this group of musically inclined exonerees found each other, and what started as a jam session quickly turned into something more. “It turned into a really nice brotherhood of guys who were not only musicians but had went through the same thing of being wrongfully convicted,” one band member recalls. Living in different parts of the country, they come together to create a sound that is both a celebration of their freedom and a testament to their resilience. Their music is a form of therapy, a way to process the unimaginable trauma of being stripped of their lives and liberty. “For me, it’s kind of like a therapy thing,” says one member. “Getting to share my story through music.” Each member carries the weight of a story that would

items.t: ‘McMillan & Wife’ actress Susan Saint James dies at 80
items.x: (Gray News) - Emmy-winning actress Susan Saint James has died. She was 80 years old. Saint James, who starred in “McMillan & Wife,” “Kate & Allie” and “The Name Game,” died Monday after being diagnosed with pancreatic cancer, according to People . Her family said she was “generous with her time and energy, which she valued more than money, and instinctively drawn to whoever needed lifting up,” in a statement to People. Saint James “never met a stranger” and “taught her children to pause, be kind and look out for other people,” her family said. “Every person she met became the most important person in the room at that moment, from a fellow board member to the clerk at the shoe store, who usually walked away knowing her entire life story,” her family said. After retiring from Hollywood in 1989, she made appearances on “Law & Order: Special Victims Unit” and “Suits.” She was married to longtime NBC executive Dick Ebersol for 45 years. In 2004, their 14-year-old son, Teddy, died in a plane crash in Colorado. Saint James received a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame in 2008.

items.t: Suspect arrested in Instagram sextortion investigation 3 years after teen’s death
items.x: Editor’s note: This story discusses suicide. If you or someone you know is struggling, call or text 988 to connect with the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. STREETSBORO, Ohio. ( WOIO/ Gray News) - An arrest has been made in connection to the death of an Ohio high school student who died by suicide after becoming a victim of sextortion. James, 17, died Nov. 19, 2022, after being targeted on Instagram. Streetsboro police, along with the Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force and Homeland Security Investigations, said a man in his early 20s is now in jail. In 2022, the 17-year-old thought he was exchanging photos with a 19-year-old girl who reached out to him on Instagram. James’ mother Tamia says after the encounter, in less than 24 hours her son received more than 200 text messages and dozens of calls from what she believes was a group of people saying they were going to ruin his life if he didn’t pay them thousands of dollars. Through the investigation, they tracked the IP address and were eventually able to connect him to the crime. Police said the suspect will stand trial and could face more than 10 years in prison.

The ad has drawn criticism from lawmakers in both parties, including Ohio’s Republican Gov. Mike DeWine. Ramaswamy, however, has defended the commercial, and argued that voters should be allowed to hear the allegations and make their own decisions. items.t: Mother who traveled to Las Vegas on a work trip arrested after unsupervised child was injured and hospitalized, deputies say
items.x: KISSIMMEE, Fla. (Gray News) - A mother who traveled to Las Vegas on a work trip was arrested after one of her children was injured and hospitalized, according to deputies. According to the Osceola County Sheriff’s Office , a child called 911 after a dumbbell fell on her 9-year-old brother’s head on Oct. 21. When deputies responded to the home, they found that four children, ages 14, 12, 11 and 9, were home unsupervised. Fire rescue took the 9-year-old child to the hospital. The responding deputy called the children’s mother, Irene Miller, 50. She told the deputy that she has been working in Las Vegas since Oct. 18, and would return on Oct. 23. Miller said she had a babysitter coming from Tampa every morning to get the children ready for school and to check on them after school, but she did not require her to stay at night. The 9-year-old returned home after being treated and discharged from the hospital. Authorities contacted the children’s father and agreed to take them to his home. Detectives met Miller when she got off her flight from Las Vegas on Oct. 23. Miller is charged with four counts of child neglect without great bodily harm. She was booked into the Orange County jail.

items.t: Breast cancer survivor faced hair loss during chemotherapy and reclaimed her identity
items.x: KANSAS CITY, Mo. ( Aging Untold ) — Hair loss is often the most common and visually striking side effect of chemotherapy, especially for women. Lisa Steinhauser, a breast cancer survivor, said she lost her hair and part of her identity during chemotherapy. Now she inspires patients to find strength during their own battle. Hair as part of her identity “So when I knew I was going to lose my hair, that was pretty hard because I had a lot of it,” she said. Hair has always been Steinhauser’s craft, artistry and expression. Diagnosis and treatment In December 2021, Steinhauser went in for a routine mammogram, and she said doctors found a spot they were concerned about. “I really was not expecting it to be anything at all, but it was,” she said. She was diagnosed with triple-negative breast cancer, an aggressive, invasive type of breast cancer. Treatment is intense. “It was not fun,” Steinhauser said. “I went every three weeks.” Shaving her head Steinhauser’s hair began to fall out during treatment. “Being in the shower and washing my hair and having those handfuls come out,” she said. items.t: How to use AI to budget for the holidays without overspending
items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — Holiday expenses often extend well beyond gifts and food, and those additional costs can add up quickly. Cherry Dale, vice president of financial education at Virginia Credit Union, said the first step to managing holiday spending is a simple list — before ever opening an AI tool like ChatGPT or Claude. Dale recommends listing everything planned for November and December spending, including travel, decorations, gifts and hosting costs. She said AI can help organize a budget, but personal information such as a name or banking details should never be entered. Dale said general, non-identifying details can still produce a useful, personalized budget. “You can put generic things like, ‘Hey, I’m hosting eight people for Thanksgiving, and I have six adults, two children. I would like to create a traditional Thanksgiving meal. Can you map out a budget for me with all of this information?’” Dale said. “And it will spit out approximate cost per person.” Dale said AI tools can suggest a menu and grocery list, or help identify gift ideas that fit a specific budget. “Use AI — put in, like, ‘I would like a gift for a child that’s interested in piano or theater, or maybe it’s

items.t: Manhunt underway for convicted murderer who escaped from prison, officials say
items.x: LAKE COUNTY, Tenn. ( WMC /Gray News) – A convicted murderer is on the run after escaping from a prison in Tennessee. Officers at the Northwest Correctional Complex in Lake County discovered inmate Jacob Morley was missing late Sunday night. Surveillance footage shows Morley breached a perimeter fence and left the facility in his prison uniform. Authorities released video of him allegedly stealing a white 2008 Ford F-350 during his escape around 1 a.m. Monday. The truck has a Tennessee license plate 138BBQV and is marked with Lindamood Planting Company on the side. TBI released new footage of escaped inmate Jacob Morley stealing a white 2008 Ford F-350 Morley is serving a life sentence for first-degree murder in the 2022 killing of Cody Birchfield in Carter County, officials said. According to the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation, Morley has now been added to the Tennessee Most Wanted List and should be considered dangerous. items.t: ‘The Pitt’ star Noah Wyle named People’s 2026 Sexiest Man Alive
items.x: (Gray News) — Actor Noah Wyle has been crowned People’s 2026 Sexiest Man Alive . Wyle, 55, is the star of the hit HBO show “The Pitt.” He broke onto the scene in the 1990s when he starred as the handsome young Dr. Carter on “ER” alongside George Clooney. In an interview with People, Wyle said he was shocked to find out he was named Sexiest Man Alive and thought it “sounded like a prank.” “Just not in a million years did I think that this would be an honor bestowed on me,” he told People. Wyle has three children : an 11-year-old daughter named Frances with his wife Sara, and 24-year-old Owen and 21-year-old Auden from a previous marriage. He had his chocolate lab, Lily, alongside him for many of the Sexiest Man Alive photos. Wyle described himself as a homebody who likes to “check out the books on the shelf in the library” or “pet the dog” at a party. On his days off, Wyle said he likes to make breakfast for his wife and daughter, journal, exercise, take Lily for a walk and read.

items.x: (Gray News) - Savannah Chrisley is expecting her first child with her fiancé, Jason. “I’ve prayed for this life. I’ve cried for this life. And there were moments I truly wondered if this life would ever be mine,” she said in an Instagram post. Chrisley, 29, shared the news on her podcast , Unlocked with Savannah Chrisley, and on Instagram. “The past few years have taken me through fires I never imagined I’d have to walk through. items.t: Hammond man arrested on alleged internet sex crimes, deputies say
items.x: HAMMOND, La. (WVUE) - Charles Stewart II, 52, arrested Tuesday (Oct. 27) over alleged internet sex crimes, Tangipahoa deputies said. The parish’s Internet Crimes Against Children (ICAC) Task Force arrested Stewart on 39 counts of pornography involving juveniles under the age of 13, deputies said. The investigation began last month, when investigators found the upload activity was coming from Tangipahoa Parish. The activity was traced to Stewart and a warrant for his arrest was obtained this morning, deputies said. items.t: ‘You can’t go any higher’: American Airlines’ most senior flight attendant retires
items.x: CHARLOTTE, N.C. (Gray News) - American Airlines’ most senior flight attendant is retiring after nearly 64 years with the company. Carol Fair has worked as a flight attendant for 63 years. At 83, she is retiring at the top of American Airlines’ seniority list. “It’s time. I’ve enjoyed every minute of it. I made No. 1 out of 30,000. You can’t go any higher, so I might as well hang it up,” Fair said in an interview with Forbes . Her last trip was on an American Airlines flight from London to Charlotte, North Carolina, on Monday. A crowd celebrated Fair when the plane landed at Charlotte Douglas International Airport. Fair is a 2008 inductee of the North Carolina Transportation Hall of Fame and is also a member of the Tennessee Aviation Hall of Fame. Her career is also featured in an exhibit at the Sullenberger Aviation Museum.

items.t: Dry end to the work week before weekend showers

Dry conditions will stick around through today, keeping fire danger elevated across Central Mississippi. While strong winds won’t be a factor, the combination of dry air and extremely dry ground ground means outdoor burning and any unattended fires could spread quickly. items.t: Aging Untold: How to spot the early signs of Parkinson’s and when to talk to a doctor
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — On this episode of Aging Untold, we examine the subtle, easily overlooked early warning signs of Parkinson’s disease and discuss when to talk with a physician. Plus, we explore what to consider when starting antidepressants, emphasizing the importance of setting realistic expectations and building a comprehensive support plan. Then, we share how a grieving Michigan family turned heartbreak into hope by helping pair veterans and first responders with lifesaving service dogs. Parkinson’s doesn’t always start with a tremor — here’s what to watch for Parkinson’s disease can start long before a tremor and the subtle changes are easy to miss. Dr. Rhea Rogers, a board-certified physician, said the loss of smell, constipation or changes in handwriting can be early signs. By the time tremors appear, Rogers said, significant damage has often already been done. Resources are available for people living with Parkinson’s. Read the full article here. items.t: ‘Amazed that she’s alive’: 18-year-old driver in ICU after hitting moose on icy road
items.x: ANCHORAGE, Alaska ( KTUU /Gray News) - A mother in Alaska said her 18-year-old daughter is lucky to be alive after hitting a moose Monday night while driving down an icy Anchorage road. “That’s what we’ve been hearing this entire ordeal, from the EMTs to the doctors; they are amazed that she’s alive,” Megan Stone said about her daughter’s crash. According to Stone, the collision occurred when her daughter Autumn was driving home and a moose appeared in the roadway. Stone said she does not believe her daughter had any time to brake. When firefighters arrived, they found a badly damaged vehicle with Autumn trapped inside. It took several crews to cut her out with the Jaws of Life hydraulic rescue tools. Anchorage firefighter Jason Dolph said moose are particularly dangerous when they are hit at highway speeds. “Typically when a car strikes a moose, that moose becomes suspended in the air,” Dolph said. “And when that moose then lands on the vehicle. In this case, it landed on the hood and kind of the windshield and roof area. We see forces of 30,000 to 40,000 pounds being put onto that car.” Fish and Game Biologist Cory Stantorf said there are usually about 100 moose-vehicle collision

items.t: Ukraine war continues despite Trump’s promise to end it
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - The war in Ukraine has lasted more than four-and-a-half years, and fighting continues despite repeated efforts by President Donald Trump to end the conflict. Trump made a pledge on the campaign trail dozens of times during the last presidential campaign. “Before I even arrive at the Oval Office shortly after I win the presidency, I will have the horrible war between Russia and Ukraine settled,” Trump said at a July 7, 2023, rally in Council Bluffs, Iowa. “Somebody said, are you on Russia’s side? Are you on Ukraine’s side? You know what? The side — I want people to stop dying. That’s the side I’m on.” That campaign promise has not been fulfilled. Trump has met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy twice at the White House. He met once with Russian President Vladimir Putin, in August 2025 in Anchorage, Alaska. “I will say that I believe we had a very productive meeting,” Trump said. “There were many, many points that we agreed on. Most of them, I would say. A couple of big ones that we haven’t quite got there, but we’ve made some headway. So, there’s no deal until there’s a deal.” On Sept. 18, Trump signed bipartisan legislation named after the late Sen.

items.t: We Walk the Line: Turning loss into a lifeline
items.x: (Editor’s note: This story discusses suicide. If you or a loved one needs help, call or text the Suicide Prevention Hotline at 988.) LANSING, Mich. ( Aging Untold ) — Members of the military and first responders run toward crisis and the repeated trauma can take a serious toll on mental health. A growing number of veterans and first responders are dying by suicide, struggling with the invisible wounds of service. The U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs estimates an average of 22 veterans take their own lives each day, and hundreds of first responders die by suicide annually. Two Michigan nonprofits are working together to help, providing free therapy and service dogs to veterans and first responders. For Tonya and Scott Shea, the mission is personal. Their son, Army Specialist Connor Shea, was a quiet, old soul with a passion for fishing and Johnny Cash. “His peaceful part of him was fishing. And he would just go on the lakes with his buddies or by himself, put in some headphones, listen to some Johnny Cash, cast some reels, and he was just simple,” Tonya Shea said. items.t: ‘She just lit up the room’: Toddler dies after being hit by car at a pumpkin patch, family says
items.x: SEVIERVILLE, Tenn. ( WVLT /Gray News) - A Tennessee toddler died after being hit by a car at a pumpkin patch, according to her family. The family of 21-month-old Nyxailia Hinton said they want answers after she died Tuesday. The Sevier County Sheriff’s Office said she fell and was hit by a car driven by a family friend at a pumpkin patch. However, details have not been given about how or where she fell. “She just lit up the room,” said Peandra Hinton, the child’s mother. “If you were having a bad day, you see Zayla, she’s gonna turn it all around.” Hinton said her daughter was with a babysitter who took her to the pumpkin patch without permission. She said her daughter was with a group of people she did not know. Hinton rushed to the hospital, where her daughter died from her injuries Tuesday, according to the sheriff’s office. Hinton said the past 48 hours have been a whirlwind, adding the hardest part has been waking up without her daughter. “The fact that I couldn’t wake up this morning to my baby, it really tore me up,” Hinton said. items.t: 13 former Shuckers help Brewers win first World Series
items.x: BILOXI, Miss. (WLOX) — Thirteen former Biloxi Shuckers helped the Milwaukee Brewers make franchise history Wednesday night, contributing to the team’s first World Series title. The Brewers finished the regular season with a 103-59 record before going 11-2 in the postseason, capped by a five-game World Series victory over the Tampa Bay Rays. Several former Shuckers played key roles in the championship run, including Jacob Misiorowski and Cooper Pratt, who stood out in Game 5. Pratt, who played for Biloxi from 2024-25, went 2-for-3 in the series-clinching game. Misiorowski, who played for the Shuckers from 2023-24, held the Rays scoreless for 5.2 innings and finished the postseason with a 1.89 ERA. Jackson Chourio, who played in Biloxi from 2022-23, also made an impact, finishing the World Series with a .458 batting average and two doubles. items.t: ‘Breaking Away’ actress Barbara Barrie dies by medically assisted suicide, reports say
items.x: (Gray News) - Barbara Barrie, known for her 1979 role in “Breaking Away,” died Wednesday by medically assisted suicide, according to her daughter in a statement to The New York Times . Barrie was 95. Barrie had been diagnosed with terminal cancer and died in her New York City home, according to her daughter, Jane Harwick. Barrie’s agent, Gary Gersh, said her passing was “medically assisted in accordance with the New York State Medical Aid in Dying Law,” according to USA Today . In addition to “Breaking Away,” which earned her an Oscar nomination, Barrie also starred in several TV shows, including “Barney Miller” and “Suddenly Susan.” She also received a Tony nomination for her performance in the original production of “Company.”

items.t: Relocation offers on the rise as cities try big cash incentives to attract remote workers
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Remote work opportunities continue to thrive years after the COVID-19 pandemic made working from home mainstream. Now some communities across the U.S. are competing to attract new residents who are fully employed but can live anywhere, offering increasingly large cash incentives to lure remote workers. Cumberland, Maryland launched “Choose Cumberland,” a pilot program offering $20,000 to up to 10 people who agree to move to the city. The Appalachian Mountains community, located about 130 miles outside Washington D.C., saw its population decline from over 40,000 to less than 19,000 after several manufacturing companies and other large employers closed their doors starting in the 1970s. “At one time, the population of Cumberland was over 40,000 people,” said Mayor Ray Morriss. Program details and requirements The Cumberland incentive splits the money into two payments : $10,000 in relocation cash $10,000 for a down payment or approved home renovations Recipients must make Cumberland their primary residence for at least five years. “The people we are trying to entice are the people who are bringing their jobs with them,” Morriss said. items.t: Gen Z has more debt than Millennials did at the same age
items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — Gen Z carries more debt than Millennials did at the same age, even after adjusting for inflation, according to TransUnion data cited by a credit counseling expert. Ted Rossman, with nonprofit credit counseling agency Money Management International , said the agency has seen a 35% increase in demand from Gen Z clients in the past year. Their debt loads are about 12% higher than they were a year ago. Student loans, high rents and buy now, pay later plans are adding up and leaving many young adults living paycheck to paycheck with little savings. “That’s really showcasing a lot of these early career pressures,” Rossman said. “You have student loans, you have high housing costs. Those household formation years are very expensive, so GenZer’s actually have more debt than Millennials did at the same age, even adjusted for inflation according to TransUnion.” For Gen Z, Rossman said the starting point is the basics: knowing your budget and watching buy now, pay later spending. “It’s very popular among people in their 20’s, but it’s still debt,” Rossman said. “It can work in your favor. items.t: ‘He’s a monster’: Convicted Tennessee murderer still on the run as authorities investigate Wisconsin bank robbery
items.x: LAKE COUNTY, Tenn. ( WMC /Gray News) - The manhunt for escaped Tennessee inmate Jacob Allen Morley continues and authorities are investigating a possible link in Wisconsin after a man robbed a bank at gunpoint there on Tuesday. Dane County authorities said the Bank of Deerfield was robbed just before it closed. A gunman walked in, demanded money, restrained two employees and left with cash. Nobody was hurt during the robbery. The gunman stole a Lincoln MKZ from the parking lot to get away. The car was later found unoccupied. The Tennessee Bureau of Investigation said it is aware of the robbery in Wisconsin, but has not confirmed it is linked to Morley. Morley escaped from the Northwest Correctional Complex Monday. He stole a white 2008 Ford F-150 marked with Lindamood Planting Company. The truck was found abandoned early Tuesday in Marion, Illinois. Police said there is no evidence Morley is still in that area. Morley was serving a life sentence for the 2022 murder of Cody Birchfield. Tyreece Miller, the U.S. marshal for the Western District of Tennessee, is asking for help in the search for Morley. items.t: Antidepressants: What to know before you decide
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Feeling low, disconnected or not like yourself for weeks or months is different from a bad day. When it starts to affect sleep, energy or everyday life, it’s time to talk about support and treatment options. For some people, that could include an antidepressant. Start with a conversation with your provider Dr. Rhea Rogers, a board-certified physician, said the decision looks different for everyone. “Everybody is individualized so you can just talk with your provider,” Rogers said. Rogers said to recognize whether you’re feeling depressed and to look at signs such as loss of sleep, loss of energy or loss of motivation. Some people might also experience a triggering event that starts a downward spiral, which they can’t pull themself out of, she said. “When your quality of life is being affected, then you might want to look into antidepressant therapy,” Rogers said. Antidepressants are not “happy pills” Rogers cautioned that antidepressants do not take away sadness. “They’re not happy pills. items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — As the number of cameras capturing vehicle information multiplies, so do concerns of privacy for everyday people. Plus, four-legged companions jump into action to help heal our heroes. We share the recent gift bringing military members support in the form of service animals. Tracking the trackers Flock Safety says its cameras don’t track people. But the company’s own training videos show police using the system to track suspects “from location to location to location.” And some of its cameras are designed to follow people as they walk. “And they quite literally use AI to zoom in and follow you around whether you’re a person of interest or not,” said Benn Jordan , a security researcher who found dozens of Flock cameras streaming openly online. items.t: The barbershop quartet tradition is alive in New Orleans
items.x: NEW ORLEANS ( InvestigateTV ) - On a Mid City evening, a four-part harmony rang out just off Canal Street. The group, Southern Tradition, has been around since 1999. The quartet is a place where a traditional American art form forges a friendship. “The main attribute to be a barbershop quartet singer is to not be embarrassed, just keep going,” said Karl Hansen. Four men with four different careers create one sound. Hansen is a doctor who sings bass. Hansen Eschette is a med tech singing tenor. Joe Jacquat is a civil engineer who sings baritone. Johnnie Oufnac is the only actual barber in this barbershop quartet, singing lead. “Being together for a long time helps us harmonize and understand where the other person is going,” Hansen said. Barbershop quartets have been around for more than a century. Though they can be found all over the world, ties to New Orleans are strong. “It really is the nexus of American music at its most basic level and a lot of it comes from New Orleans,” said Zachary Matherne. items.t: Nearly 11 million people in the U.S. could be living with undiagnosed diabetes
items.x: CHARLOTTE, N.C. ( InvestigateTV ) - Diabetes is the seventh leading cause of death in the United States, the No. 1 cause of kidney disease, and an estimated 40 million people are living with it nationwide. Despite decades of prevention education and major breakthroughs in treatment, doctors say diabetes continues to hit the South especially hard — including North Carolina. It can create serious long-term complications, including coronary artery disease, heart attacks, never damage, and amputations. But many people who have the disease may not know it. The CDC estimates around 11 million live with undiagnosed diabetes. “Every day, almost every hour” battle Andrew Tucker has lived with Type 2 diabetes for nearly two decades. He’s made major lifestyle changes but said managing the disease is still a daily fight. Tucker was diagnosed about 15 years ago, when he was 35. “Yes, for me, it is truly an everyday, almost every hour watching what I do,” Tucker said. Type 2 diabetes develops when the body doesn’t make enough insulin or doesn’t use insulin properly. Doctors say obesity is a major risk factor. items.t: This veteran is using his service dog to regain independence
items.x: ST. LOUIS, Mo. ( InvestigateTV ) - Veteran James Poggi served in the Marine Corps working in aviation. His time in the military led to a lifelong strain on his body, including five back surgeries and a below-the-knee amputation. “You go from being six foot three, 250 pounds and able to travel halfway across the world and do whatever they ask you to do, to being relying on wheelchairs, walkers, mobility devices, things like that, you become a vulnerable person that you never thought you’d be,” Poggi said. Poggi said he was in multiple accidents, hard landings, PT accidents and a car crash. He also developed spinal meningitis. “And that was all while I was active,” he said. To help ease some of the emotional toll, Poggi’s wife, who is also his caregiver, suggested he get a service dog. Service dog provides daily support Poggi got Teddy, a Goldendoodle, who serves as his service dog and daily lifeline. “You never went anywhere without your battle buddy. And he always, always better have your back. And that’s how it is. He’s always got my back,” Poggi said. items.t: Tennessee governor suspects Christa Pike’s sentence will stay the same after failed execution
items.x: NASHVILLE, Tenn. ( WSMV /Gray News) — Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee said he suspects Christa Pike’s sentence will remain the same following her failed execution last month, unless the courts determine otherwise. Lee’s comments on Pike Lee was asked Wednesday whether the state will try to execute Pike again or if he will commute her sentence to life in prison. “As it related to a particular individual like Christa Pike and her crime, she’s still incarcerated under the laws of the state of Tennessee,” Lee said. “I suspect her sentence will be the same as before unless determined otherwise by the courts.” Pike’s condition Pike was sentenced to death for the 1995 murder of Colleen Slemmer. In September, Pike survived two doses of the lethal injection drug. The execution attempt failed. Pike is back in prison after spending days in the hospital. She is now able to speak in full sentences and walk on her own. items.t: Border Patrol agent charged with murder in wife’s death
items.x: LAREDO, Texas ( KGNS /Gray News) — A U.S. Border Patrol agent in Texas has been charged in connection with the death of his wife. Abel Garza, 30, has been charged with murder, a first-degree felony, in the death of his wife, 28-year-old Mayra Alejandra Landeros, after a domestic disturbance in south Laredo. U.S. Customs and Border Protection confirmed in a statement that Garza is a Border Patrol agent. Garza also is charged with two counts of endangering a child and two counts of abandonment of a child. All four counts are second-degree felonies. He was transported to Webb County Jail, and his bond was set at $1 million. What police say happened The incident happened just before 3 a.m. Wednesday at a home near Texana Street and Nocona Street. Chief Miguel Rodriguez said police were initially called about a man knocking on doors asking for help. A police drone spotted a car leaving as officers arrived. items.t: Jackson museum seeks names of unidentified people in civil rights photographs
items.x: JACKSON, Miss. (WLBT) - Photographers who followed the civil rights movement through Mississippi shot thousands of frames. A handful of famous images made the history books. For 60 years, many of the people in the rest of those frames have gone unnamed. A new exhibit at the Smith Robertson Museum in Jackson is asking the public to help change that. “Proof Positive” opened Tuesday. It features 51 contact sheets, the full sets of frames photographers shot, not just the one picture that ran in a newspaper or magazine. Visitors are invited to look closely at the faces and say so if they recognize someone. “You could have been standing in a mass meeting or protest and the person next to you is the person that was featured,” said Theresa King, the museum’s manager. Visitors can identify someone at a kiosk in the gallery or on a paper card. They can explain who the person is or share the person’s story. When someone is identified, the museum sends a print of the photo to that person’s family as a gift. items.x: CANTON, Miss. items.t: Sleep specialist shares tips for adjusting to end of daylight saving time
items.x: GULFPORT, Miss. (WLOX) — Daylight saving time ends Sunday, Nov. 1, and clocks go back one hour this weekend. Some people see “falling back” as adding an hour of sleep. Memorial Hospital sleep specialist Dr. John Douglas said the extra hour could still affect sleep quality. Light affects circadian rhythm Douglas said light affects a person’s circadian rhythm the most. “I tell all my patients that it’s kind of like caveman days, you know, cave women days. You wake up with the sunrise, and you go to sleep when the sun goes down,” Douglas said. He said people should turn on every light, open the drapes and look at the reflected sunlight as soon as it comes up after waking at the new time. “So, that’ll set the clock in your brain as sunrise,” Douglas said. Douglas said it takes approximately three days for someone to adjust to the one-hour difference. Coast residents share opinions Coast residents gave mixed opinions on the time change. Some said the extra sleep is good. Others said it is too confusing to keep changing. “I think time change is a mess. It should stay the same all year long. items.t: Economist explains how the ‘K-shaped economy’ is impacting the midterms
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - As voters prepare to head to the polls for the midterm elections, a conflicting economic sentiment is once again emerging on the campaign trail. “Voters reflect the perception of the cost of living as they experienced, as opposed to what is in the data,” said Alessandro Rebucci, an economics professor at Johns Hopkins Carey Business School. “In the data, you have an economy that is very strong as a whole. How that pie is distributed affects how a large segment of the population and the voters are feeling about the economy right now.” The contradiction has been described by many economists recently, as the “k-shaped” economy, using a graph to depict how high-income earners and asset owners are doing compared to middle and lower-income earners. “To be concrete, the wealthiest households are presumed to spend much more than the lowest ones, not only in absolute terms, which is obvious, but also as a share of their income and in their wealth,” Rebucci said. items.t: For politics, what is an October surprise?
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - An October surprise is an event that could shake up an election, but does it often make the difference? Matt Dallek, a professor of political management at George Washington University, described it as “an event that, at least in theory, has the potential to shake up an election, something that people did not foresee coming that upends the debate.” He said the term dates back to around the 1980 election, when President Jimmy Carter failed to secure the release of American hostages being held in Iran before November 4, 1980, election day. Carter lost to Republican rival Ronald Reagan. Several surprises have occurred in the years since. Surprises can be driven by a campaign or by news events. Examples include Iran-Contra-related indictments in 1992 and the global financial collapse in 2008. Dallek said those surprises likely did not change the outcome of the election that November. “There’s no evidence that they flip a dynamic that was already in place,” Dallek said. “What’s more typical is that an event occurs, it dominates the news cycle and the trend line starts to move further toward the candidate who was already doing well, who was already likely to prevai

items.t: Grandmother not indicted in baby’s death after police say she left her in hot car for 8 hours while she worked
items.x: MADISONVILLE, Ky. ( WFIE /Gray News) — A Kentucky doctor who accidentally left her grandchild unattended in a hot car for about eight hours will not be indicted for the baby’s death. Madisonville police said 10-month-old Scottie Crowell died in August . On Tuesday, a grand jury found there was insufficient probable cause for an indictment. Police said Scottie’s grandmother picked her up in the morning of Aug. 13 and was supposed to take her to daycare. She forgot the child was in the car and went to work, police said. She arrived at Owensboro Health Multi-Care, where she works as a doctor, around 8 a.m. The baby’s father called his wife after trying to pick up Scottie from daycare, but the child was not there. The baby’s mother called the grandmother at work, and the grandmother ran outside and saw Scottie was still in the vehicle around 4 p.m., police said. After 911 was called, first responders tried to administer lifesaving measures, but the baby died. “I would ask that you keep the infant’s parents and family in your thoughts and prayers as they continue to grieve and process this unimaginable loss,” said Commonwealth’s Attorney Hannah Kington-Jarvis.

items.t: Ernie Johnson announces this will be his final season on ‘Inside The NBA’
items.x: (Gray News) - Ernie Johnson announced he will be stepping down as host of “Inside the NBA” at the end of the season. The Sports Broadcasting Hall of Famer took to social media on Wednesday to explain his decision to step away, saying, “It’s just time.” Johnson, 70, stated that he would not be retiring, but cutting back. “This is by no means the end. It’s just a turning of the page,” Johnson said. “And I’ll forever cherish every chapter we have written with ‘Inside the NBA.’” Johnson said he plans to continue to work, including covering the NCAA men’s basketball tournament for CBS and Turner Sports. The six-time Sports Emmy Award winner acknowledged that he has dealt with heart issues in recent years, but that isn’t the reason he’s stepping away from the show. “I just want to slow down a bit,” he added in his social media post. Johnson joined Turner Sports in 1989 and has hosted “Inside the NBA” since 1990. He thanked his TNT Sports and ESPN crews for their support over the years, as well as the viewers. “I just want to say thanks to you. Thanks for your loyalty, for your love, for your support.
