items.t: 8-month-old dies after left alone in running bathtub, police say
items.x: STERLING, Va. (Gray News) - A Virginia woman was arrested after her 8-month-old died after being left unattended in a bathtub, according to authorities. Rosellena Pisani, 30, was arrested and charged with homicide, two counts of child abuse and three counts of child endangerment, a press release said. On Sept. 12, emergency medical personnel and sheriff’s deputies responded to the residence after receiving a call about an unresponsive infant. Investigators determined the baby had been left unsupervised in a bathtub with the water running. Three children, ranging in age from 8 months to 8 years old, were at home during the incident, according to police. Loudoun County Sheriff Mike Chapman called the baby’s death heartbreaking, saying caregivers have a fundamental duty to protect children. He added investigators remain committed to seeking justice in the case.

items.t: Haunted Hangar brings alien encounter to Mississippi Aviation Heritage Museum
items.x: GULFPORT, Miss. (WLOX) — The Mississippi Aviation Heritage Museum is transforming one hall into a Haunted Hangar with an alien encounter theme. The event runs Wednesday through Saturday, Oct. 28-31. The Haunted Hangar is open from 4 to 6:30 p.m. each day. Admission is $10 per person and includes a hot dog, chips, and a drink. “We’re transforming one full hall of the museum into the haunted hangar,” board member Roger Kovacs said. The event is returning for its second year. “We had a great turnout last year. The kids had a lot of fun,” he said. Kovacs said some children were scared, but added that the Haunted Hangar was created with families in mind. “We really wanted to make it fun for the family. It’s just a little bit scary, but it’s not gory like some haunted houses. So it’s a family fun exhibit,” he said. During the event, the rest of the museum will remain available. Kovacs said visitors can go to the STEM area after they go through the Haunted Hangar. “The kids can play there. A lot of different things they can do there,” he said. items.t: Missing 7-year-old, pregnant mother both found safe
items.x: OVERLAND, Mo. ( KMOV /Gray News) — Officials in Missouri said a missing 7-year-old boy and his pregnant mother were found safe Wednesday. The Missouri State Highway Patrol previously issued an Endangered Person Advisory for Dylan Fernando Zendejas-Gonzalez, 7. With high pressure dominating the forecast, fire danger remains elevated through the start of the weekend. Rain chances return just in time for Halloween. Scattered showers are possible as early as Friday night, with heavier rain and thunderstorms most likely Saturday into Sunday. The caveat is that showers will me hit or miss meaning that many spots could stay dry all weekend while other areas see inches of rain. The bottom line for trick-or-treating is to monitor the forecast closely and have a backup plan in case of rain or storms. Another weather system is expected to move in mid way through next week. This system will bring more scattered showers and thunderstorms followed by a cold front that drops temperatures back into the low to mid-70s by the end of next week. They cut, clean and arrange the blooms into vases, then deliver them to nursing homes, the VA hospital, assisted living facilities and shelters. “Amazingly gifted with so many flowers from places like Kroger who have overbought and can’t sell them, and they allow us to pick them up and then bring them here, and then we cut them, clean them and vase them. The group sends out about 100 vases every week. “I take flowers to Up for Women and Children, it’s a day homeless shelter for women,” Stephanie Mullins, a Flower Buds volunteer, said. items.t: Jackson blindsided by JXN Water transition plan; now drawing up its own
items.x: JACKSON, Miss. (WLBT) - Jackson city officials say they were never consulted on a proposed transition plan for JXN Water and are gearing up to draw up a transition plan of their own. City Attorney Drew Martin shared the news at a Jackson City Council committee meeting Tuesday. He said the city was supposed to work on the plan with Interim Third-Party Manager Ted Henifin but only found out about that plan after the third-party manager submitted it to U.S. District Judge Henry Wingate. “He said, ‘Oh, I just wanted to let the judge look at it first, make sure it wasn’t going down any roads that weren’t worth going through,’” he said. “The next thing I knew, he was emailing everybody saying, ‘Here’s our plan.’” JXN Water releases transition plan. Here is what the third-party manager recommends Henifin released JXN Water’s transition plan Oct. 15. In it, he recommends JXN Water be converted from an S corporation to a public water authority, with its initial board of directors appointed by Wingate and subsequent board members elected by the utility’s ratepayers. items.t: Illegal moonshine distillery explodes, catches fire in mountains, officials say
items.x: WILKES COUNTY, N.C. ( WBTV /Gray News) - An explosion at an illegal moonshine distillery sparked a fire in the North Carolina mountains on Monday, according to authorities. Special agents from North Carolina’s Alcohol Law Enforcement Division were called to investigate the explosion in Wilkes County, North Carolina. Agents found an active 200-gallon illegal distillery. They seized about 1,800 gallons of mash, which is used to make moonshine, and 161 gallons of illegal moonshine. North Carolina officials shared photos showing the charred inside of a metal building. Distilling equipment was also damaged. Billy Ray Anderson, 69, was arrested and charged with manufacturing a non-taxpaid alcoholic beverage, possession for sale of a non-taxpaid alcoholic beverage, possession of a non-taxpaid alcoholic beverage, possession of distillery equipment, possession of distillery ingredients and allowing property to be used for the manufacture of a non-taxpaid alcoholic beverage. Moonshine is believed to have originated in North Carolina and was once an important source of income, particularly for rural residents.

items.t: Some packaged salads recalled for undeclared allergens
items.x: (Gray News) - Packaged salads produced by Taylor Farms have been recalled due to an undeclared allergen. According to the Food and Drug Administration, Taylor Farms is recalling its H-E-B Backyard BBQ Chop Salad because it may contain undeclared soy and tree nuts, specifically almonds. “People who have sensitivity or allergy to soy and tree nuts (almonds) may be at risk of a serious adverse reaction if they consume this product,” an FDA press release said. So far there have not been any illnesses or “adverse reactions” reported in connection with the recall. The salads were sold in H-E-B stores across Texas. They can be identified by their UPC code, 041220300457, and their best-by date, Oct. 30, 2026. Customers are asked not to eat the recalled salads and to throw them away or return them to the store for a refund.

items.t: Caregiver advocate shares 3 policies that could help family caregivers
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — More than 60 million Americans are family caregivers, balancing work, kids and care for an aging parent or loved one. Jason Resendez, president and CEO of the National Alliance for Caregiving, recently testified before the U.S. Senate Special Committee on Aging. He joined gerontologist “Sam” Cradduck to talk through the solutions he presented. The three policies he brought to lawmakers Resendez said the National Alliance for Caregiving is championing changes “to address so many of the pain points that family caregivers face every day.” 1) Older Americans Act funding He said one priority is reauthorization and funding of the Older Americans Act. Resendez said the law provides dollars for state Area Agencies on Aging to deliver services for older adults, such as Meals on Wheels and caregiver support. “One of the only federal line items for caregiving comes through the Older Americans Act, and it’s called the National Family Caregiver Support Program,” Resendez said. He said the program funds respite, which gives caregivers the chance to take breaks. items.t: Long-term care costs rose about 50% in five years, report finds
items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — The cost of long-term care jumped nearly 50% in five years, while income for older households rose just 22%, according to a new AARP report . The report found long-term services and supports are becoming even less affordable for middle-class Americans. Alan Weil, senior vice president for public policy at AARP, said the gap is the most important finding. “Between 2019 and 2024, a five-year period, the cost of most long-term care services went up about 50%, but the incomes for older households only went up by about 22%,” Weil said. “So the gap between what people can afford and what it costs has grown.” The AARP also looked at what different types of care cost. Weil said the more skilled the service, the higher the price. “If you need someone to come in and help you prepare food, that’s less expensive than if you need someone to come in and provide nursing-level care,” Weil said. “Although I’ll also say that we’ve learned that a lot of caregivers are being forced to provide nursing care that they can’t afford to pay someone else to do, even though they’ve never been trained in nursing. So that’s where the burden falls back on the family.” The financial burden oft

items.t: She was born with eight fingers on one hand. Her family traveled to America for the surgery
items.x: ST. LOUIS, Mo. ( InvestigateTV ) - A family traveled from Turkey to St. Louis for their daughter’s surgery to treat a rare condition affecting fewer than 100 people worldwide. Elisa, an 18-month-old, was born with eight fingers on her left hand. She was diagnosed with Ulnar Dimelia, also known as Mirror Hand Syndrome. “Mirror Hand is incredibly uncommon, and even surgeons like myself who take care of a great deal of kids almost never see this in their career. So, it’s really uncommon. Numbers are hard to come by, but one in a million or less is probably about right,” said Dr. Charles Goldfarb, Chief of Orthopedic Surgery at St. Louis Children’s Hospital. The condition leaves patients without a radius bone. This means significant limitations in wrist and elbow motion and preserved shoulder movements. “From the very beginning, he was really warm, genuine, and gave us a lot of hope. Honestly, the trust and support he gave us played a huge role in our decision to come to St. Louis,” said Emircan Buga, Elisa’s father. items.t: Canned fruit sold at Walmart recalled in several states
items.x: (Gray News) - A voluntary recall over lead concerns has been issued for cans of Walmart fruit cocktail distributed to stores in at least seven states. The Food and Drug Administration said the recall applies to 15-ounce containers of Great Value Fruit Cocktail in Fruit Juice from Concentrate. Where the product was distributed More than 1,830 cases, or approximately 44,000 individual cans, were distributed to Walmart locations in Alabama, Arizona, Louisiana, New Mexico, Pennsylvania, Washington and Wyoming, the FDA said. How to identify the product The product is marked with lot number “6FCB 04 C2263” and a best if used by date of Sept. 1, 2027. Recall details The FDA initiated the recall for “potential contamination with elevated levels of lead” on Oct. 1. It was reclassified as a Class II recall on Oct. 20. According to the FDA, Class II recalls are issued when a product can cause temporary health effects with a remote possibility of serious issues. What customers should do Customers should throw the item away or return it to Walmart.

(WLOX) — Democrat Scott Colom held a rally at St. John Community Center in Biloxi with former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg one week before the November general election. More than 1,000 people attended. Colom is challenging Republican incumbent Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith for a U.S. Senate seat from Mississippi. Local speakers open the rally Before Colom and Buttigieg spoke, attendees heard from Rep. Jeffrey Hulum III and Gulfport City Councilwoman Carissa Corbett. Hulum said: “For far too long, they told us to wait. Wait for better schools, wait for better bridges, wait for infrastructure, wait on leadership. items.t: 24-year-old deputy killed in crash with coal truck while on duty, sheriff’s office says
items.x: LOGAN COUNTY, W. Va ( WSAZ /Gray News) - A 24-year-old sheriff’s deputy was killed in a crash while responding to a call, authorities said. The Logan County Sheriff’s Department identified the deputy as 24-year-old Caden Mullins. Deputy Mullins’ fiancée was airlifted from the scene of the crash to a hospital. Deputies say Mullins and his fiancée were at a truck-or-treat event on Saturday in the Man area when he received an emergency call from the sheriff’s department. The sheriff’s department says Deputy Caden Mullins, 24, died in the crash. Mullins was on his way to drop his fiancée off and head to the call when the crash occurred around 5 p.m., deputies say. Deputies say the crash happened at the intersection of Rum Creek Road and Route 10 when a coal truck pulled off the road and hit Mullins’ vehicle. Mullins worked for the Charleston Police Department for about a year before joining the Logan County Sheriff’s Department to be closer to family, the department said.

The law, that was signed by the president in July 2025, implemented several tax breaks for Americans and cut some social service programs. items.t: Pearl High School moving down to 6A, but Pirates hope rivalries stay
items.x: PEARL, Miss. (WLBT) - Pearl High School is moving down to Class 6A, and the school’s athletic director said Pearl will work to keep the rivalry games Pirates fans circle on the calendar. The Mississippi High School Activities Association released its 2027-29 classifications Monday . Pearl competed in Class 7A during the 2025-27 cycle. For the next cycle, the school reported an adjusted enrollment of 864, which puts it at the top of the 24-school Class 6A field. That’s 25 students short of the 7A cutoff of 889, according to MHSAA data. Pearl will no longer be in the same class as 7A schools such as Brandon, Clinton and Northwest Rankin. Twenty-six schools statewide are changing classes. Athletic Director Ty Weems said the move wasn’t the school’s decision. Pearl reports its enrollment to the state, which verifies the numbers. “We just strictly pull our data and our enrollment that we report ... and we kind of let the numbers fall where they may,” Weems said. Classifications are based on enrollment in ninth through 11th grades, Weems said, because those are the students who will be competing when the new classes take effect. items.x: MIDDLETOWN, Ohio ( WXIX /Gray News) - A couple is facing multiple charges of child endangerment and animal cruelty following a welfare check at their home in September, authorities said. Melanie and Christopher Todd were arrested after officers responded to their home on Cardinal Court to check on their children and animals, according to the criminal complaint. Police described the living conditions as “deplorable and unlivable.” Officers conducted the welfare check Sept. 29 after Middletown City Schools reported that two 10-year-old children appeared dirty and said they had no food to eat, police said. The children also said two cats were dead inside their home, the complaint said. During the check, officers found holes large enough to see outside in the walls and floors. One of the couple’s four children said the holes were caused by punching when Melanie and Christopher would get angry, the complaint said. The home also had little to no edible food inside, officers said. According to the complaint, the floors were covered in dirty clothes, trash, animal feces, and debris. items.t: Trials for former Jackson officers in custody death set for 2027
items.x: JACKSON, Miss. (WLBT) - The trials of three former Jackson police officers charged in Keith Murriel’s death have been delayed more than 20 times since their indictments in 2023. Kenya McCarty and Avery Willis face second-degree murder charges. James Land faces a manslaughter charge. McCarty’s and Willis’ cases are scheduled for trial June 1, 2027. Court documents say officers tased Murriel more than 80 times while trying to restrain him. They then handcuffed him and placed him face-down in a patrol car. Body-camera video shows officers did not check on Murriel. When an ambulance arrived about an hour later, he was unresponsive. A 3 On Your Side investigation in 2023 found the officers may have violated department policies on force, Taser use and supervisor notification. JPD’s Taser policy requires officers to regularly monitor people in custody and use restraints that do not restrict breathing after Tasers are used. The video shows neither requirement was followed. The defense blames prosecutors for the latest delay. Court records show both sides have requested or contributed to delays over the life of the cases. All three defendants have pleaded not guilty. items.t: Woman arrested after 4-year-old found dead in Atlanta townhome
items.x: WASHINGTON, Ga. ( WRDW /Gray News) - A woman was arrested Tuesday morning after a 4-year-old boy was found dead more than an hour away in an Atlanta townhome, authorities said. Wilkes County Sheriff Darrell Powers said Jasmaine Smoak was arrested and booked into the Wilkes County Detention Center. According to WRDW’s sister station, Atlanta News First , Atlanta police responded to a gated community in the 3500 block of Cardinal Drive SW on Monday night for a welfare check. Officers forced their way into the home “based on information received during the welfare check,” Atlanta police said. Once inside, officers found the child dead. Emergency personnel attempted lifesaving measures but were unsuccessful, police said. Powers said deputies worked closely with Atlanta homicide detectives to locate Smoak using license plate reader technology. Smoak is charged with second-degree cruelty to children and concealing the death of another. Atlanta police said Smoak is a friend of the child’s mother. The circumstances surrounding the boy’s death remain unclear.

items.t: Gretna brothers died from suffocating on toxic gas at fishing plant, coroner says
items.x: NEW ORLEANS (WVUE) - The Plaquemines Parish Coroner’s Office said Thursday that two brothers died at a fishing plant in September from suffocating on hydrogen sulfide gas. The Coroner’s Office said Thursday their deaths were both accidents. Plaquemines Parish Coroner Dr. Neil Wolfson identified the men last month as Yesser and Elliott Rizo-Acevevo. Wolfson said the men lived in Gretna. The Plaquemines Parish Sheriff’s Office said the deadly incident on Sept. 4 involved hazardous material at Daybrook Fisheries in Empire, a commercial menhaden fish processing plant where the men worked. Wolfson said hydrogen sulfide is a byproduct of dead menhaden fish. Westbank Fishing, the fishing company partnered with Daybrook Fisheries which employed the brothers directly, said shortly after the incident that two of their employees died “during unloading operations.” “The site is secure, and there is no ongoing risk to employees or the surrounding community,” the company said at the time. It added that the incident was under investigation by both law enforcement and regulatory authorities and that it wouldn’t make any further comment while any investigation was active. items.t: Aging Untold: How to spot the early signs of Parkinson’s and when to talk to a doctor
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — On this episode of Aging Untold, we examine the subtle, easily overlooked early warning signs of Parkinson’s disease and discuss when to talk with a physician. Plus, we explore what to consider when starting antidepressants, emphasizing the importance of setting realistic expectations and building a comprehensive support plan. Then, we share how a grieving Michigan family turned heartbreak into hope by helping pair veterans and first responders with lifesaving service dogs. Parkinson’s doesn’t always start with a tremor — here’s what to watch for Parkinson’s disease can start long before a tremor and the subtle changes are easy to miss. Dr. Rhea Rogers, a board-certified physician, said the loss of smell, constipation or changes in handwriting can be early signs. By the time tremors appear, Rogers said, significant damage has often already been done. Resources are available for people living with Parkinson’s. Read the full article here. items.t: ‘Amazed that she’s alive’: 18-year-old driver in ICU after hitting moose on icy road
items.x: ANCHORAGE, Alaska ( KTUU /Gray News) - A mother in Alaska said her 18-year-old daughter is lucky to be alive after hitting a moose Monday night while driving down an icy Anchorage road. “That’s what we’ve been hearing this entire ordeal, from the EMTs to the doctors; they are amazed that she’s alive,” Megan Stone said about her daughter’s crash. According to Stone, the collision occurred when her daughter Autumn was driving home and a moose appeared in the roadway. Stone said she does not believe her daughter had any time to brake. When firefighters arrived, they found a badly damaged vehicle with Autumn trapped inside. It took several crews to cut her out with the Jaws of Life hydraulic rescue tools. Anchorage firefighter Jason Dolph said moose are particularly dangerous when they are hit at highway speeds. “Typically when a car strikes a moose, that moose becomes suspended in the air,” Dolph said. “And when that moose then lands on the vehicle. items.t: Ukraine war continues despite Trump’s promise to end it
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - The war in Ukraine has lasted more than four-and-a-half years, and fighting continues despite repeated efforts by President Donald Trump to end the conflict. Trump made a pledge on the campaign trail dozens of times during the last presidential campaign. “Before I even arrive at the Oval Office shortly after I win the presidency, I will have the horrible war between Russia and Ukraine settled,” Trump said at a July 7, 2023, rally in Council Bluffs, Iowa. “Somebody said, are you on Russia’s side? Are you on Ukraine’s side? You know what? The side — I want people to stop dying. That’s the side I’m on.” That campaign promise has not been fulfilled. Trump has met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy twice at the White House. He met once with Russian President Vladimir Putin, in August 2025 in Anchorage, Alaska. “I will say that I believe we had a very productive meeting,” Trump said. “There were many, many points that we agreed on. Most of them, I would say. A couple of big ones that we haven’t quite got there, but we’ve made some headway. ( Aging Untold ) — Members of the military and first responders run toward crisis and the repeated trauma can take a serious toll on mental health. A growing number of veterans and first responders are dying by suicide, struggling with the invisible wounds of service. The U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs estimates an average of 22 veterans take their own lives each day, and hundreds of first responders die by suicide annually. Two Michigan nonprofits are working together to help, providing free therapy and service dogs to veterans and first responders. For Tonya and Scott Shea, the mission is personal. Their son, Army Specialist Connor Shea, was a quiet, old soul with a passion for fishing and Johnny Cash. “His peaceful part of him was fishing. And he would just go on the lakes with his buddies or by himself, put in some headphones, listen to some Johnny Cash, cast some reels, and he was just simple,” Tonya Shea said. items.t: Dry and breezy this afternoon, but Halloween weekend rain is on the way
items.x: NEW ORLEANS (WVUE) - This afternoon is dry across southeast Louisiana and the Mississippi coast, but that dry stretch comes with a catch. Drought conditions, dry fuels, low humidity and light-to-moderate winds keep the fire danger elevated through the rest of today. Keep that in mind if you’re planning any outdoor burning, and obey all burn bans in place. Be extra careful with open flames even if your parish or county doesn’t have a ban. Thin cirrus clouds overhead are leftovers from Tropical Storm Vance out in the eastern Pacific, which is why fog struggled to form this morning. Where skies do clear tonight, patchy fog is possible as temperatures fall toward 52 degrees. Winds turn more easterly late today into Friday and stay that way through the weekend. That sets up a coastal flood concern. Combined with a king tide cycle, the east wind pushes water levels higher around high tide each day. Hancock County looks like the first spot to see minor nuisance flooding. A Coastal Flood Advisory is in effect from 1 AM to 5 AM Friday for the Mississippi coast. items.t: ‘She just lit up the room’: Toddler dies after being hit by car at a pumpkin patch, family says
items.x: SEVIERVILLE, Tenn. ( WVLT /Gray News) - A Tennessee toddler died after being hit by a car at a pumpkin patch, according to her family. The family of 21-month-old Nyxailia Hinton said they want answers after she died Tuesday. The Sevier County Sheriff’s Office said she fell and was hit by a car driven by a family friend at a pumpkin patch. However, details have not been given about how or where she fell. “She just lit up the room,” said Peandra Hinton, the child’s mother. “If you were having a bad day, you see Zayla, she’s gonna turn it all around.” Hinton said her daughter was with a babysitter who took her to the pumpkin patch without permission. She said her daughter was with a group of people she did not know. Hinton rushed to the hospital, where her daughter died from her injuries Tuesday, according to the sheriff’s office. Hinton said the past 48 hours have been a whirlwind, adding the hardest part has been waking up without her daughter. “The fact that I couldn’t wake up this morning to my baby, it really tore me up,” Hinton said. items.t: ‘Breaking Away’ actress Barbara Barrie dies by medically assisted suicide, reports say
items.x: (Gray News) - Barbara Barrie, known for her 1979 role in “Breaking Away,” died Wednesday by medically assisted suicide, according to her daughter in a statement to The New York Times . Barrie was 95. Barrie had been diagnosed with terminal cancer and died in her New York City home, according to her daughter, Jane Harwick. Barrie’s agent, Gary Gersh, said her passing was “medically assisted in accordance with the New York State Medical Aid in Dying Law,” according to USA Today . In addition to “Breaking Away,” which earned her an Oscar nomination, Barrie also starred in several TV shows, including “Barney Miller” and “Suddenly Susan.” She also received a Tony nomination for her performance in the original production of “Company.”

items.t: Relocation offers on the rise as cities try big cash incentives to attract remote workers
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Remote work opportunities continue to thrive years after the COVID-19 pandemic made working from home mainstream. Now some communities across the U.S. are competing to attract new residents who are fully employed but can live anywhere, offering increasingly large cash incentives to lure remote workers. Cumberland, Maryland launched “Choose Cumberland,” a pilot program offering $20,000 to up to 10 people who agree to move to the city. The Appalachian Mountains community, located about 130 miles outside Washington D.C., saw its population decline from over 40,000 to less than 19,000 after several manufacturing companies and other large employers closed their doors starting in the 1970s. “At one time, the population of Cumberland was over 40,000 people,” said Mayor Ray Morriss. Program details and requirements The Cumberland incentive splits the money into two payments : $10,000 in relocation cash $10,000 for a down payment or approved home renovations Recipients must make Cumberland their primary residence for at least five years. “The people we are trying to entice are the people who are bringing their jobs with them,” Morriss said. items.t: Gen Z has more debt than Millennials did at the same age
items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — Gen Z carries more debt than Millennials did at the same age, even after adjusting for inflation, according to TransUnion data cited by a credit counseling expert. Ted Rossman, with nonprofit credit counseling agency Money Management International , said the agency has seen a 35% increase in demand from Gen Z clients in the past year. Their debt loads are about 12% higher than they were a year ago. Student loans, high rents and buy now, pay later plans are adding up and leaving many young adults living paycheck to paycheck with little savings. “That’s really showcasing a lot of these early career pressures,” Rossman said. “You have student loans, you have high housing costs. Those household formation years are very expensive, so GenZer’s actually have more debt than Millennials did at the same age, even adjusted for inflation according to TransUnion.” For Gen Z, Rossman said the starting point is the basics: knowing your budget and watching buy now, pay later spending. “It’s very popular among people in their 20’s, but it’s still debt,” Rossman said. “It can work in your favor. items.t: Antidepressants: What to know before you decide
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Feeling low, disconnected or not like yourself for weeks or months is different from a bad day. When it starts to affect sleep, energy or everyday life, it’s time to talk about support and treatment options. For some people, that could include an antidepressant. Start with a conversation with your provider Dr. Rhea Rogers, a board-certified physician, said the decision looks different for everyone. “Everybody is individualized so you can just talk with your provider,” Rogers said. Rogers said to recognize whether you’re feeling depressed and to look at signs such as loss of sleep, loss of energy or loss of motivation. Some people might also experience a triggering event that starts a downward spiral, which they can’t pull themself out of, she said. “When your quality of life is being affected, then you might want to look into antidepressant therapy,” Rogers said. Antidepressants are not “happy pills” Rogers cautioned that antidepressants do not take away sadness. “They’re not happy pills. items.t: InvestigateTV+: Tracking the trackers
items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — As the number of cameras capturing vehicle information multiplies, so do concerns of privacy for everyday people. InvestigateTV+ explores what can happen when the tool is misused and meet one man on a mission to track every police camera in the country. Plus, four-legged companions jump into action to help heal our heroes. We share the recent gift bringing military members support in the form of service animals. Tracking the trackers Flock Safety says its cameras don’t track people. But the company’s own training videos show police using the system to track suspects “from location to location to location.” And some of its cameras are designed to follow people as they walk. “And they quite literally use AI to zoom in and follow you around whether you’re a person of interest or not,” said Benn Jordan , a security researcher who found dozens of Flock cameras streaming openly online. items.t: The barbershop quartet tradition is alive in New Orleans
items.x: NEW ORLEANS ( InvestigateTV ) - On a Mid City evening, a four-part harmony rang out just off Canal Street. The group, Southern Tradition, has been around since 1999. The quartet is a place where a traditional American art form forges a friendship. “The main attribute to be a barbershop quartet singer is to not be embarrassed, just keep going,” said Karl Hansen. Four men with four different careers create one sound. Hansen is a doctor who sings bass. Hansen Eschette is a med tech singing tenor. Joe Jacquat is a civil engineer who sings baritone. Johnnie Oufnac is the only actual barber in this barbershop quartet, singing lead. “Being together for a long time helps us harmonize and understand where the other person is going,” Hansen said. Barbershop quartets have been around for more than a century. Though they can be found all over the world, ties to New Orleans are strong. “It really is the nexus of American music at its most basic level and a lot of it comes from New Orleans,” said Zachary Matherne. items.t: Nearly 11 million people in the U.S. could be living with undiagnosed diabetes
items.x: CHARLOTTE, N.C. ( InvestigateTV ) - Diabetes is the seventh leading cause of death in the United States, the No. 1 cause of kidney disease, and an estimated 40 million people are living with it nationwide. Despite decades of prevention education and major breakthroughs in treatment, doctors say diabetes continues to hit the South especially hard — including North Carolina. It can create serious long-term complications, including coronary artery disease, heart attacks, never damage, and amputations. But many people who have the disease may not know it. The CDC estimates around 11 million live with undiagnosed diabetes. “Every day, almost every hour” battle Andrew Tucker has lived with Type 2 diabetes for nearly two decades. He’s made major lifestyle changes but said managing the disease is still a daily fight. Tucker was diagnosed about 15 years ago, when he was 35. “Yes, for me, it is truly an everyday, almost every hour watching what I do,” Tucker said. Type 2 diabetes develops when the body doesn’t make enough insulin or doesn’t use insulin properly. Doctors say obesity is a major risk factor. items.t: This veteran is using his service dog to regain independence
items.x: ST. LOUIS, Mo. ( InvestigateTV ) - Veteran James Poggi served in the Marine Corps working in aviation. His time in the military led to a lifelong strain on his body, including five back surgeries and a below-the-knee amputation. “You go from being six foot three, 250 pounds and able to travel halfway across the world and do whatever they ask you to do, to being relying on wheelchairs, walkers, mobility devices, things like that, you become a vulnerable person that you never thought you’d be,” Poggi said. Poggi said he was in multiple accidents, hard landings, PT accidents and a car crash. He also developed spinal meningitis. “And that was all while I was active,” he said. To help ease some of the emotional toll, Poggi’s wife, who is also his caregiver, suggested he get a service dog. Service dog provides daily support Poggi got Teddy, a Goldendoodle, who serves as his service dog and daily lifeline. “You never went anywhere without your battle buddy. And he always, always better have your back. And that’s how it is. He’s always got my back,” Poggi said. The dog helped Poggi regain his independence by taking care of tasks many people take for granted. “His favorite thing is to retri

items.t: Scattered Halloween storms remain
items.x: NEW ORLEANS (WVUE) - All eyes are on Halloween this year as our best chance for rain in several weeks arrives for the holiday. Weather changes start late this week as clouds move in and humidity begins to return. We still expect to remain dry through Friday, with only a spotty sprinkle shower possible by Friday evening. Highs stay around 80 even as the clouds increase. Halloween remains our focus as scattered storms begin to form through the day and into the evening/night. That means trick-or-treat times will have to pay attention to radar just in case one of those pop-ups forms over your neighborhood. The overall storm coverage will be around 60%, so this will not be a widespread storm day. Best advice is to pack the rain gear and hope for the best. I wouldn’t be canceling plans with this forecast. Into next week, we will be tracking a stronger front and a more widespread rain/storm signal. The timing brings that next storm into the forecast by Wednesday. It’ll turn sharply cooler behind that front! See a spelling or grammar error in our story? Click Here to report it. items.t: Teen arrested for alleged possession of child porn, deputies say
items.x: COVINGTON, La. (WVUE) - St. Tammany Parish Sheriff’s Office arrested Marcus Schech, 18, for possession of child sexual abuse material and bestiality, deputies said. The investigation began after the Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force (ICAC) received a tip from the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children. Investigators executed a search warrant at Schech’s residence in the 100 block of North Drive in Covington on Aug. 20, deputies said. There, investigators found five images of child sexual abuse material, which led to Schech’s initial arrest, deputies said. Several of Schech’s electronic devices were seized in that investigation and a forensic examination revealed an additional 373 images of CSAM and 25 bestiality images, deputies said. Schech was re-arrested on Oct. 20 by members of the U.S. Marshals Fugitive Task Force, deputies said. See a spelling or grammar error in our story? Click Here to report it. items.t: Tennessee governor suspects Christa Pike’s sentence will stay the same after failed execution
items.x: NASHVILLE, Tenn. ( WSMV /Gray News) — Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee said he suspects Christa Pike’s sentence will remain the same following her failed execution last month, unless the courts determine otherwise. Lee’s comments on Pike Lee was asked Wednesday whether the state will try to execute Pike again or if he will commute her sentence to life in prison. “As it related to a particular individual like Christa Pike and her crime, she’s still incarcerated under the laws of the state of Tennessee,” Lee said. “I suspect her sentence will be the same as before unless determined otherwise by the courts.” Pike’s condition Pike was sentenced to death for the 1995 murder of Colleen Slemmer. In September, Pike survived two doses of the lethal injection drug. The execution attempt failed. Pike is back in prison after spending days in the hospital. She is now able to speak in full sentences and walk on her own. Pike survived two doses of the lethal injection drug.(DEPARTMENT OF EMERGENCY COMMUNICATIONS, TENNESSEE DEPARTMENT OF CORRECTION, ASSOCIATED PRESS) Executions paused, commissioner resigns Lee has paused executions through the end of the year to determine what went wrong in Pike’s attempt.

items.t: Woman dead in Elysian Fields hit-and-run, NOPD says
items.x: NEW ORLEANS (WVUE) - A hit-and-run early Thursday (Oct. 29) left one woman dead, police said. NOPD is investigating a fatal hit-and-run crash in the 3100 block of Elysian Fields Avenue in the Third District. The incident happened at about 2:15 a.m. Officers found a woman who had sustained injuries and was later declared dead. Through investigation, officers learned the woman had purchased several items at the location before an unknown woman took the items from the top of the victim’s car. The victim allegedly confronted the woman and started banging on the hood of the suspect’s car, asking for her property back. The suspect allegedly then struck the victim twice with her vehicle and fled the scene, police said. The car is identified as a blue sedan with a spare tire on the front passenger side, police said. Police ask anyone with additional information to call NOPD at (504) 658-6205 or CrimeStoppers at (504) 822-1111. See a spelling or grammar error in our story? Click Here to report it. items.t: Border Patrol agent charged with murder in wife’s death
items.x: LAREDO, Texas ( KGNS /Gray News) — A U.S. Border Patrol agent in Texas has been charged in connection with the death of his wife. Abel Garza, 30, has been charged with murder, a first-degree felony, in the death of his wife, 28-year-old Mayra Alejandra Landeros, after a domestic disturbance in south Laredo. U.S. Customs and Border Protection confirmed in a statement that Garza is a Border Patrol agent. Garza also is charged with two counts of endangering a child and two counts of abandonment of a child. All four counts are second-degree felonies. He was transported to Webb County Jail, and his bond was set at $1 million. What police say happened The incident happened just before 3 a.m. Wednesday at a home near Texana Street and Nocona Street. Chief Miguel Rodriguez said police were initially called about a man knocking on doors asking for help. A police drone spotted a car leaving as officers arrived. Officers stopped the car and found Landeros in the back floorboard with critical stab wounds. A U.S. Border Patrol agent is charged with fatally stabbing his wife in Texas. items.t: Pelicans remain winless, fall to Nuggets 104-91
items.x: NEW ORLEANS (WVUE) - Nikola Jokic had 21 points, 13 rebounds and 10 assists for his 200th career triple-double in the regular season, and the Denver Nuggets never trailed in a 104-91 victory over the winless New Orleans Pelicans on Wednesday night. Jamal Murray scored 23 points, and Aaron Gordon added 15 points and 11 rebounds for the Nuggets, who swept a two-game, home-and-home series with New Orleans. After overcoming a 23-point deficit on to beat the Pelicans in Denver on Saturday, the Nuggets this time raced to a 22-point lead in the first half and maintained a comfortable margin most of the way. Zion Williamson scored 25 points for the Pelicans, hitting a fourth-quarter 3 that pulled New Orleans as close as 88-83. Murray responded with a 3 and a driving finger roll to push the Nuggets’ lead back to 10. Jokic needs 10 more regular season triple-doubles to supplant Russell Westbrook, who retired after last season, as the NBA leader. Christian Braun scored 15 points and Trevon Brazile added 11 points for Denver, which entered the game with several injuries and used just nine players. items.t: Economist explains how the ‘K-shaped economy’ is impacting the midterms
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - As voters prepare to head to the polls for the midterm elections, a conflicting economic sentiment is once again emerging on the campaign trail. “Voters reflect the perception of the cost of living as they experienced, as opposed to what is in the data,” said Alessandro Rebucci, an economics professor at Johns Hopkins Carey Business School. “In the data, you have an economy that is very strong as a whole. How that pie is distributed affects how a large segment of the population and the voters are feeling about the economy right now.” The contradiction has been described by many economists recently, as the “k-shaped” economy, using a graph to depict how high-income earners and asset owners are doing compared to middle and lower-income earners. “To be concrete, the wealthiest households are presumed to spend much more than the lowest ones, not only in absolute terms, which is obvious, but also as a share of their income and in their wealth,” Rebucci said. items.t: Members of 1961 Freedom Ride welcomed to New Orleans 65 years later
items.x: NEW ORLEANS (WVUE) - With a brass band and dancing Zulu members, a handful of civil rights icons from the 1961 Freedom Ridge were welcomed onto Xavier University of Louisiana’s campus 65 years after the initial trip. Back then, the group of young students took a bus from Washington D.C. through the Deep South as a way to test discriminations laws and Jim Crow policies. But the ride stopped in Alabama after violent, racial protests, instead of making it to New Orleans, the final destination. Wednesday evening, five riders got the homecoming they were hoping for 65 years ago after a two-week bus ride down the same routes and through the same towns as 1961. “It’s been quiet an expansive trip. I really enjoyed it,” Freedom Rider Kredelle Petway-Philips said. “It feels very gratifying... It’s about time,” Freedom Rider Stephen Thomas said. The five freedom riders took the 2026 trip with a total of 67 people; some were relatives of the original Freedom Riders, while others were community and faith leaders. items.t: High school student accused of trying to make bombs for ISIS, deputies say
items.x: GAINESVILLE, Fla. ( WCJB /Gray News) - A Florida high school student was arrested after an investigation into his contact with a terrorist organization revealed he was attempting to make bombs, authorities said. Alachua County sheriff’s deputies said the 15-year-old is a student at Buchholz High School. The sheriff’s office and FBI conducted a joint investigation on Friday at the teen’s home after investigators learned he was having online conversations with members and supporters of the Islamic State group, also known as ISIS. Investigators say the teen asked for help to build drones and explosives to attack people at an unknown location. Authorities spoke with the 15-year-old’s parents, who allowed them to search the boy’s phone. They reportedly found files containing instructions for making explosive devices and chemical compounds, as well as ISIS propaganda. On Monday, investigators searched the teen’s home with his parents’ consent after they revealed the information found on the phone. Inside, they found two jars in his bedroom. items.t: ‘Pretty low individual’: Man scammed by fake life insurance agent shortly after sister’s death
items.x: CORINTH, Miss. ( WTVA /Gray News) — A Mississippi man says he was scammed shortly after the death of his sister. According to Tim Williams, he was called by a woman who identified herself as the life insurance agent for his sister, Stephanie Jeanine Williams Machado. The woman gave him account numbers and policy numbers, and requested $1,375 for the insurance company to release payment to the Corinthian Funeral Home. Williams said he entered a three-way phone call with the woman and the funeral home, and that it all seemed to be legitimate. All the money he had available at the time was $620, and the woman told him to send it. When Williams asked how the woman would like the funds sent, she said to get it to her however was easiest, either by going to the insurance office or via the Cash App. Williams said he sent the money to his nephew, who then sent it through the app. However, Williams said the funeral home told him it never received payment, so he looked up the number and found that it belonged to a man who lived in Alabama. items.t: College professor among 2 found dead in home; suspect in custody, police say
items.x: LORAIN COUNTY, Ohio. ( WOIO /Gray News) - An Ohio college professor and a woman were found shot to death in a home, and a suspect is in custody, according to authorities. Wednesday morning, police responded to the Oberlin College Conservatory lot at 77 E. College St. to assist firefighters with a vehicle smoking and possibly on fire. When crews arrived, they tried to find the registered vehicle owner, identified as Daniel Jones, 31, to conduct a welfare check. When officers arrived at Jones’ home to check on his family, they found the victims dead inside the home. Pipo Nguyen-Duy, a professor of studio art and photography at Oberlin College, was found dead on the first floor with an apparent gunshot wound. A woman found dead on the second floor was not immediately identified. She also had an apparent gunshot wound. Jones was located aat bout 10:20 a.m. and taken into custody. Charges are pending. The investigation is ongoing.

items.t: International fugitive sentenced for one of the largest health care fraud schemes in U.S. history
items.x: COLUMBIA, S.C. ( WIS /Gray News) - A man whom federal prosecutors called the architect of one of the largest health care fraud schemes in U.S. history was sentenced Monday. Herbert Kimble was sentenced to 20 years’ imprisonment with three years of court-ordered supervision. He was also ordered to pay more than $199 million in restitution to Medicare and forfeit more than $195 million in what prosecutors described as “ill-gotten gains.” Kimble pleaded guilty in 2019 to conspiring to commit health care fraud, violate the anti-kickback statute, and defraud the United States in connection with a telemedicine and durable medical equipment scheme involving back, shoulder, wrist, and knee braces. Prosecutors say Kimble ran offshore call centers that recruited elderly Medicare beneficiaries, paid kickbacks to telemedicine companies for signed prescriptions, then sold those orders to medical equipment companies that billed Medicare. Court filings put the intended loss at more than $400 million, with Kimble personally gaining more than $195 million. items.t: For politics, what is an October surprise?
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - An October surprise is an event that could shake up an election, but does it often make the difference? Matt Dallek, a professor of political management at George Washington University, described it as “an event that, at least in theory, has the potential to shake up an election, something that people did not foresee coming that upends the debate.” He said the term dates back to around the 1980 election, when President Jimmy Carter failed to secure the release of American hostages being held in Iran before November 4, 1980, election day. Carter lost to Republican rival Ronald Reagan. Several surprises have occurred in the years since. Surprises can be driven by a campaign or by news events. Examples include Iran-Contra-related indictments in 1992 and the global financial collapse in 2008. Dallek said those surprises likely did not change the outcome of the election that November. “There’s no evidence that they flip a dynamic that was already in place,” Dallek said. “What’s more typical is that an event occurs, it dominates the news cycle and the trend line starts to move further toward the candidate who was already doing well, who was already likely to prevai

items.t: St. Bernard DA faces federal lawsuit over alleged use of office resources against citizen

He declined to elaborate on the alleged “information.” The lawsuit alleges that, less than an hour later, Nicosia sent an email from his government email address with the subject line “URGENT - Professional Misconduct of George Inbraguglio (sic) Jr.” Fox 8 obtained the email through a public records request. items.t: Louisiana early voting numbers surge, Democrats and independents see higher turnout
items.x: NEW ORLEANS (WVUE) - Data shows more than half a million voters participated in early voting in Louisiana. The final tally of early voting in Louisiana by the Louisiana Secretary of State’s office shows 520,942 people voted in this year’s midterm election. That is a 38% increase from the midterms in 2022, when 377,428 voters cast early ballots. An Orleans Parish election official said the turnout so far is impressive. “I think people are coming out in this big number because what is happening in our country is monumental, and people typically turn out more during midterms and presidential elections in general. So, everyone wants to exercise their right to vote,” said Chelsey Napoleon, Orleans Parish Clerk of Court. Dillard University political analyst Dr. Robert Collins said the early numbers seem to reflect a higher enthusiasm for this election, especially among Democrats and Black voters. “I think a lot of people feel that the Black voters in Louisiana feel under attack. When people feel under attack, that’s when they get more involved in the political process,” said Robert Collins, Ph.D., political analyst at Dillard University. items.t: Library says person threw box of cockroaches at a staff member, prompting closure
items.x: TOLEDO, Ohio ( WTVG /Gray News) - A cockroach attack forced the closure of a library in Ohio this week. Surveillance footage was released by the Toledo Lucas County Public Library, appearing to show a person throwing a box of cockroaches at a staff member on Tuesday at the Kent Branch Library. Surveillance footage apparently shows someone throwing a box of cockroaches at a library employee in Ohio. (Source: Toledo Lucas County Public Library) A library spokesperson confirmed the throwing of the box of cockroaches at the library worker on Collingwood Blvd. But it wasn’t immediately shared what led up to the cockroach attack. The library was said to have gone into restricted access before closing for the rest of the day for cleanup and remediation. The Kent Branch Library reopened Wednesday. Officials did not say whether anyone would be facing any charges.

items.t: Grandmother not indicted in baby’s death after police say she left her in hot car for 8 hours while she worked
items.x: MADISONVILLE, Ky. ( WFIE /Gray News) — A Kentucky doctor who accidentally left her grandchild unattended in a hot car for about eight hours will not be indicted for the baby’s death. Madisonville police said 10-month-old Scottie Crowell died in August . On Tuesday, a grand jury found there was insufficient probable cause for an indictment. Police said Scottie’s grandmother picked her up in the morning of Aug. 13 and was supposed to take her to daycare. She forgot the child was in the car and went to work, police said. She arrived at Owensboro Health Multi-Care, where she works as a doctor, around 8 a.m. The baby’s father called his wife after trying to pick up Scottie from daycare, but the child was not there. The baby’s mother called the grandmother at work, and the grandmother ran outside and saw Scottie was still in the vehicle around 4 p.m., police said. After 911 was called, first responders tried to administer lifesaving measures, but the baby died. “I would ask that you keep the infant’s parents and family in your thoughts and prayers as they continue to grieve and process this unimaginable loss,” said Commonwealth’s Attorney Hannah Kington-Jarvis.

items.t: St. Tammany DA fights proposed 60% budget cut he says could hurt prosecutions
items.x: NEW ORLEANS (WVUE) - The St. Tammany DA continues to fight against a proposed 60% cut to his budget, saying he and other Parish agencies are doing all they can to help right the ship. With St. Tammany facing a $22 million budget shortfall, DA Collin Sims has been asked to consider a budget that could slash prosecutions. “I can’t maintain that talent for less than $7 million a year for two parishes when I’m charging 1000 more defendants a year,” Sims told FOX 8. If parish voters fail to pass a quarter cent sales tax increase in December, Sims’ office would take a 60% cut, and he’s not alone. “The judiciary took a 60% cut. The coroner’s office runs out of money in 2027, the DNA lab which we’ve had for 10 years is gone, there’s no money for it,” Sims said. Parish officials are about to launch a limited media campaign for new taxes, with many pointing to millage rollbacks for several agencies including libraries and mosquito control. “You see our millage that we lowered from 2025 originally collecting 3.1%, it’s down to 2.27%,” said St. Tammany Mosquito Abatement Director Kevin Caillouet. items.t: Widow searches for lost wedding ring when husband dies 3 days after getting married in Las Vegas
items.x: LAS VEGAS ( KVVU /Gray News) — A South Dakota woman is asking for help finding the wedding ring her husband lost in Las Vegas the night they married. Tammy Bishop and Will Mulroy were married Oct. 20 at the Viva Las Vegas Chapel. Bishop said they celebrated on a party bus and toured the Strip. At a bar, though, she says Mulroy looked down and realized his ring was gone. “We got to a bar. He looked down and his band was gone. He lost it. He started crying,” Bishop said. According to Bishop, he told her the ring was two sizes too big because he had lost weight. She said the ring may have slid off on the bus or while he moved into his wheelchair. It may also have come off while he rolled down the Strip. “We backtracked our steps. We told the bus driver. We had everyone looking. We couldn’t find it,” she said. The next day, she joked with him: “You didn’t even have your ring on for 24 hours and you lost it.” Everyone laughed, she said. “I said it’s not a big deal; we will buy you a new one, but now that he is gone it is a big deal to me,” Bishop said. items.t: SWBNO expects to begin ‘major’ lead water line replacements in early 2027
items.x: NEW ORLEANS (WVUE) - In a statement, the Sewerage and Water Board of New Orleans (SWBNO) confirmed it plans to begin “major construction” on lead water line replacement in early 2027. The utility is currently under a federal 2037 deadline to replace all lead water lines in the city, both on public and private property. The CDC reports lead can damage the brains and development of children. SWBNO Executive Director Randy Hayman has estimated more than a half of the water lines in the city are made of lead. The utility offers an interactive map to show customers what it knows about water line composition near them. SWBNO Deputy General Supt. of Water Programs Becca Johnsey said the work will initially focus on areas where there’s a high density of lead and where residents are most vulnerable. She said that information will be made publicly available in contracts for the work in the coming weeks. “We’re finalizing (first locations),” she said. She said work on private property will require property owner approval, including through a right-of-entry form ( offered online ) to inspect the piping. items.t: Dry stretch remains through Friday, rain chances return for Halloween
items.x: NEW ORLEANS (WVUE) - Our dry stretch will continue through Friday. Rain chances return Saturday for Halloween lasting into midday Sunday. Drought conditions, dry brush and low humidity keep the fire danger elevated through at least Thursday. With some breezy conditions moving in, we will see some minor tide rises. A coastal flood advisory is in effect for Hancock County from 10 p.m. to 4 a.m. Thursday. Other parishes and counties could be added over the next few nights. Water levels should stay under a foot over normally dry ground, with the highest tides coming overnight. Changes are on the way by the end of the week. A system develops over Texas, and winds shift from east to southeast as moisture surges back in. That means clouds build Friday, with rain and a few storms arriving by Saturday for trick or treaters. Her daughter, Whitney Bertram, said she is remembering her mother while seeing a large amount of support from the community following her death. “There are so many people I don’t know whose lives she’s touched and affected,” Whitney Bertram said. The crash occurred while Marchelle Bertram was walking on Memorial Parkway near her home. Marchelle Bertram died at the hospital. items.t: Ernie Johnson announces this will be his final season on ‘Inside The NBA’
items.x: (Gray News) - Ernie Johnson announced he will be stepping down as host of “Inside the NBA” at the end of the season. The Sports Broadcasting Hall of Famer took to social media on Wednesday to explain his decision to step away, saying, “It’s just time.” Johnson, 70, stated that he would not be retiring, but cutting back. “This is by no means the end. It’s just a turning of the page,” Johnson said. “And I’ll forever cherish every chapter we have written with ‘Inside the NBA.’” Johnson said he plans to continue to work, including covering the NCAA men’s basketball tournament for CBS and Turner Sports. The six-time Sports Emmy Award winner acknowledged that he has dealt with heart issues in recent years, but that isn’t the reason he’s stepping away from the show. “I just want to slow down a bit,” he added in his social media post. Johnson joined Turner Sports in 1989 and has hosted “Inside the NBA” since 1990. He thanked his TNT Sports and ESPN crews for their support over the years, as well as the viewers. “I just want to say thanks to you. Thanks for your loyalty, for your love, for your support. And on this day, for your understanding,” Johnson said.

items.t: Police department closes its investigation into Hayden Panettiere’s death
items.x: GREENVILLE, S.C. ( WHNS /Gray News) - The Greenville Police Department said it has officially closed its investigation into the death of Hayden Panettiere. Police said Panettiere’s death has been ruled accidental based on the medical examiner’s determination and the findings of the investigation. Panettiere, 36, died from an accidental overdose involving multiple prescription medications and fentanyl, according to findings previously released by the Greenville County Coroner’s Office. Toxicology testing determined the cause of death to be the toxic effects of fentanyl, 4-ANPP, alprazolam, methocarbamol and quetiapine. An autopsy showed no signs of contributing trauma. On Aug. 16, Panettiere was found unresponsive inside an apartment in Greenville, where she had been temporarily staying. Dispatchers received a 911 call reporting a woman in cardiac arrest at approximately 1:51 p.m. She was pronounced dead at 2:32 p.m. Her on-and-off boyfriend Brian Hickerson and his brother Zach Hickerson were at the apartment where she died. President Donald Trump, who has named it “super intelligence,” insists the U.S. will beat China in the AI competition. Trump said while campaigning for president that tariffs would form the crux of the bilateral relationship. The U.S. and China, the world’s two largest economies, have been engaged in a trade war during both of Trump’s terms. Speaking Sept. 13 in Ireland, Trump said the U.S. is leading China in AI. “We’re leading China in AI, we’re the most sophisticated country in the world, and frankly, I want to keep it that way because whoever wins AI, wins,” Trump said. items.t: Kenner official sues council, alleges closed public meeting over aviation board
items.x: KENNER, La. (WVUE) - The City of Kenner’s deputy chief administrative officer and her husband have filed a lawsuit accusing the Kenner City Council of violating an open meetings law in August. Natalie and Richard Newton filed the lawsuit as private citizens this week, months after Kenner City Council members wrote a letter to New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno regarding the potential appointment of a new Kenner representative on the New Orleans Aviation Board. items.t: Man loses more than $4,000 after scammers spoof father’s number, claim parents are at gunpoint

items.t: 8-month-old dies after left alone in running bathtub, police say
items.x: STERLING, Va. (Gray News) - A Virginia woman was arrested after her 8-month-old died after being left unattended in a bathtub, according to authorities. Rosellena Pisani, 30, was arrested and charged with homicide, two counts of child abuse and three counts of child endangerment, a press release said. On Sept. 12, emergency medical personnel and sheriff’s deputies responded to the residence after receiving a call about an unresponsive infant. Investigators determined the baby had been left unsupervised in a bathtub with the water running. Three children, ranging in age from 8 months to 8 years old, were at home during the incident, according to police. Loudoun County Sheriff Mike Chapman called the baby’s death heartbreaking, saying caregivers have a fundamental duty to protect children. He added investigators remain committed to seeking justice in the case.

items.t: Missing 7-year-old, pregnant mother both found safe
items.x: OVERLAND, Mo. ( KMOV /Gray News) — Officials in Missouri said a missing 7-year-old boy and his pregnant mother were found safe Wednesday. The Missouri State Highway Patrol previously issued an Endangered Person Advisory for Dylan Fernando Zendejas-Gonzalez, 7. Dylan was last seen leaving his home in Overland, near St. Louis, with his mother, Maria Guadalupe Gonzalez-Sanchez, 28. The two were last seen around 1:30 p.m. Sunday. Officials were concerned after personal belongings were left behind at their home. On Wednesday, the Overland Police Department said in a Facebook post that the two were found safe.

items.t: “Litter Boom” installations aim to prevent trash from reaching critical waterways
items.x: NEW ORLEANS (WVUE) - Organizations in New Orleans teamed up Wednesday (Oct. 28) to install four Litter Booms across the city. Pontchartrain Conservancy partnered with the New Orleans Sewerage and Water Board and Osprey Initiative to install the Litter Booms, the Pontchartrain Conservancy organization said. With support from a 2025 award from the NOAA Marine Debris Program, the booms were installed to collect and remove trash floating on a canal’s surface, the organization said. This initiative is part of the Comprehensive Aquatic Litter Plan for Orleans Parish (CALPOP), which aims to install year-round litter booms and seasonal storm-drain debris interceptors across the city to prevent trash from reaching major waterways like Lake Pontchartrain and Bayou Bienvenue. So far, booms have been installed in three major stormwater canals: St. Charles, Lower 9th and Monticello, the organization said. “New Orleans is a city shaped by water, making the protection of our waterways essential to the health and resilience of our communities. items.t: Suspect in Houma stabbing spree indicted for four murders by Terrebonne grand jury
items.x: HOUMA, La. (WVUE) - The suspect in last month’s deadly Houma stabbing spree was indicted on four murder counts Tuesday (Oct. 27) by a Terrebonne Parish grand jury. items.t: Meet the volunteers who bring flowers from weddings and funerals to hospice patients
items.x: LOUISVILLE, Ky. ( Aging Untold ) — Inside Crescent Hill Baptist Church in Louisville, a group of volunteers gathers each week surrounded by color, creativity and collaboration. They call themselves the Flower Buds. From events to those in need The Flower Buds take donated flowers from weddings, funerals, wholesalers, supermarkets, florists, galas, banquets and other community events. They cut, clean and arrange the blooms into vases, then deliver them to nursing homes, the VA hospital, assisted living facilities and shelters. “Amazingly gifted with so many flowers from places like Kroger who have overbought and can’t sell them, and they allow us to pick them up and then bring them here, and then we cut them, clean them and vase them. Then we take them to nursing homes, the VA hospital, assisted living facilities,” Jodie Raible, a Flower Buds volunteer, said. The group sends out about 100 vases every week. “I take flowers to Up for Women and Children, it’s a day homeless shelter for women,” Stephanie Mullins, a Flower Buds volunteer, said. items.t: Illegal moonshine distillery explodes, catches fire in mountains, officials say
items.x: WILKES COUNTY, N.C. ( WBTV /Gray News) - An explosion at an illegal moonshine distillery sparked a fire in the North Carolina mountains on Monday, according to authorities. Special agents from North Carolina’s Alcohol Law Enforcement Division were called to investigate the explosion in Wilkes County, North Carolina. Agents found an active 200-gallon illegal distillery. They seized about 1,800 gallons of mash, which is used to make moonshine, and 161 gallons of illegal moonshine. North Carolina officials shared photos showing the charred inside of a metal building. Distilling equipment was also damaged. Billy Ray Anderson, 69, was arrested and charged with manufacturing a non-taxpaid alcoholic beverage, possession for sale of a non-taxpaid alcoholic beverage, possession of a non-taxpaid alcoholic beverage, possession of distillery equipment, possession of distillery ingredients and allowing property to be used for the manufacture of a non-taxpaid alcoholic beverage. Moonshine is believed to have originated in North Carolina and was once an important source of income, particularly for rural residents.

items.t: Some packaged salads recalled for undeclared allergens
items.x: (Gray News) - Packaged salads produced by Taylor Farms have been recalled due to an undeclared allergen. According to the Food and Drug Administration, Taylor Farms is recalling its H-E-B Backyard BBQ Chop Salad because it may contain undeclared soy and tree nuts, specifically almonds. “People who have sensitivity or allergy to soy and tree nuts (almonds) may be at risk of a serious adverse reaction if they consume this product,” an FDA press release said. So far there have not been any illnesses or “adverse reactions” reported in connection with the recall. The salads were sold in H-E-B stores across Texas. They can be identified by their UPC code, 041220300457, and their best-by date, Oct. 30, 2026. Customers are asked not to eat the recalled salads and to throw them away or return them to the store for a refund.

items.t: How to spot fake crystals and avoid costly mistakes
items.x: SEDONA, Ariz. ( Aging Untold ) — The crystal and gemstone industry is booming, fueled in part by social media, but experts warn buyers to be cautious of fake products flooding the market. Jamie Inglett, who owns a crystal shop in Sedona, said consumers can find fake crystals in stores and at gem shows. “As a consumer you really kind of have to do your own research,” Inglett said. items.t: Caregiver advocate shares 3 policies that could help family caregivers
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — More than 60 million Americans are family caregivers, balancing work, kids and care for an aging parent or loved one. Jason Resendez, president and CEO of the National Alliance for Caregiving, recently testified before the U.S. Senate Special Committee on Aging. He joined gerontologist “Sam” Cradduck to talk through the solutions he presented. The three policies he brought to lawmakers Resendez said the National Alliance for Caregiving is championing changes “to address so many of the pain points that family caregivers face every day.” 1) Older Americans Act funding He said one priority is reauthorization and funding of the Older Americans Act. Resendez said the law provides dollars for state Area Agencies on Aging to deliver services for older adults, such as Meals on Wheels and caregiver support. “One of the only federal line items for caregiving comes through the Older Americans Act, and it’s called the National Family Caregiver Support Program,” Resendez said. He said the program funds respite, which gives caregivers the chance to take breaks. items.t: Long-term care costs rose about 50% in five years, report finds
items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — The cost of long-term care jumped nearly 50% in five years, while income for older households rose just 22%, according to a new AARP report . The report found long-term services and supports are becoming even less affordable for middle-class Americans. Alan Weil, senior vice president for public policy at AARP, said the gap is the most important finding. “Between 2019 and 2024, a five-year period, the cost of most long-term care services went up about 50%, but the incomes for older households only went up by about 22%,” Weil said. “So the gap between what people can afford and what it costs has grown.” The AARP also looked at what different types of care cost. Weil said the more skilled the service, the higher the price. “If you need someone to come in and help you prepare food, that’s less expensive than if you need someone to come in and provide nursing-level care,” Weil said. “Although I’ll also say that we’ve learned that a lot of caregivers are being forced to provide nursing care that they can’t afford to pay someone else to do, even though they’ve never been trained in nursing. items.t: Butter sold in 10 states recalled over possible yeast, mold and E. coli contamination

items.x: ST. LOUIS, Mo. ( InvestigateTV ) - A family traveled from Turkey to St. Louis for their daughter’s surgery to treat a rare condition affecting fewer than 100 people worldwide. Elisa, an 18-month-old, was born with eight fingers on her left hand. She was diagnosed with Ulnar Dimelia, also known as Mirror Hand Syndrome. “Mirror Hand is incredibly uncommon, and even surgeons like myself who take care of a great deal of kids almost never see this in their career. So, it’s really uncommon. Numbers are hard to come by, but one in a million or less is probably about right,” said Dr. Charles Goldfarb, Chief of Orthopedic Surgery at St. Louis Children’s Hospital. The condition leaves patients without a radius bone. This means significant limitations in wrist and elbow motion and preserved shoulder movements. “From the very beginning, he was really warm, genuine, and gave us a lot of hope. items.t: Halloween storm threat looms
items.x: NEW ORLEANS (WVUE) - All eyes on Halloween as our highest rain chance in several weeks comes on the holiday. Currently, we’re seeing little day-to-day change, so it’s another cool start this morning with a warm finish expected. Highs should hit the 80s today and each day the rest of the week. Slowly, our humidity values are building back in, so it won’t feel as nice outside as it did last week. Rain and storm threats are up to 60% for Halloween. Chances are high we’ll be dodging downpours during the afternoon and continuing into the evening trick-or-treat hours. All plans should continue as is, but make sure you’re ready to pivot if that storm forms over you. As for temperatures, it’ll be a warm and humid Halloween. Highs should hit 80 and be in the 70s at sunset. Next week I’m already tracking a secondary system with a much higher impact. items.t: Canned fruit sold at Walmart recalled in several states
items.x: (Gray News) - A voluntary recall over lead concerns has been issued for cans of Walmart fruit cocktail distributed to stores in at least seven states. The Food and Drug Administration said the recall applies to 15-ounce containers of Great Value Fruit Cocktail in Fruit Juice from Concentrate. Where the product was distributed More than 1,830 cases, or approximately 44,000 individual cans, were distributed to Walmart locations in Alabama, Arizona, Louisiana, New Mexico, Pennsylvania, Washington and Wyoming, the FDA said. How to identify the product The product is marked with lot number “6FCB 04 C2263” and a best if used by date of Sept. 1, 2027. Recall details The FDA initiated the recall for “potential contamination with elevated levels of lead” on Oct. 1. It was reclassified as a Class II recall on Oct. 20. According to the FDA, Class II recalls are issued when a product can cause temporary health effects with a remote possibility of serious issues. What customers should do Customers should throw the item away or return it to Walmart.

items.t: 24-year-old deputy killed in crash with coal truck while on duty, sheriff’s office says
items.x: LOGAN COUNTY, W. Va ( WSAZ /Gray News) - A 24-year-old sheriff’s deputy was killed in a crash while responding to a call, authorities said. The Logan County Sheriff’s Department identified the deputy as 24-year-old Caden Mullins. Deputy Mullins’ fiancée was airlifted from the scene of the crash to a hospital. Deputies say Mullins and his fiancée were at a truck-or-treat event on Saturday in the Man area when he received an emergency call from the sheriff’s department. The sheriff’s department says Deputy Caden Mullins, 24, died in the crash. Mullins was on his way to drop his fiancée off and head to the call when the crash occurred around 5 p.m., deputies say. Deputies say the crash happened at the intersection of Rum Creek Road and Route 10 when a coal truck pulled off the road and hit Mullins’ vehicle. Mullins worked for the Charleston Police Department for about a year before joining the Logan County Sheriff’s Department to be closer to family, the department said.

items.t: Entergy Louisiana offers $100 bill credits starting Oct. 28
items.x: LAKE CHARLES, La. (KPLC) - Struggling to keep up with higher household costs could get a little easier for thousands of Entergy Louisiana customers this week. Entergy Louisiana is launching a $2 million bill assistance program offering a one-time $100 bill credit, funded by shareholder dollars. Applications open Oct. 28 at 9 a.m. through United Way partners while funds last. The program covers customers living below the federal poverty level and ALICE households who earn above poverty level but below the cost of living in their parish. “This bill credit is one more way we’re stepping up to support the communities we serve during a time when everyday costs are on the rise,” said Nyka Scott, Entergy Louisiana customer service vice president. Customers can apply online through the United Way serving their parish. Applicants will need a photo ID and income documentation for each earner age 18 or older, such as a 2025 tax return first page, W-2, recent pay stub or Social Security benefit letter. For more information, click HERE.

items.t: Planning commission approves new short-term rental rules, rejects expansion in French Quarter
items.x: NEW ORLEANS (WVUE) - The New Orleans City Planning Commission approved a new study on zoning rules for short-term rentals, but rejected a plan to allow their expansion on four blocks on Decatur and North Peters in the French Quarter on Oct. 27. The planning commission approved the new rules overwhelmingly, agreeing to remove the portion which would have allowed more short-term rentals on Decatur and Peters. The new rules limit short-term rentals to one per block and allow commercial short-term rentals to exist without an owner-manager present. The new rules now head to the city council for approval. Supporters and opponents spoke for three hours Tuesday afternoon, and while many opponents thought a French Quarter expansion might hurt the quarter’s residential quality, others said it is time to open up new areas for commercial development. Vieux Carre Property Owners, Residents and Associates (VCPORA) officials said the city is being overrun with often unregulated short-term rentals, and they do not want to see any more. items.t: Energy Department authorizes emergency oil exchange for Phillips 66 Lake Charles refinery
items.x: LAKE CHARLES, La. (KPLC) - A disruption at one of the area’s largest refineries prompted emergency federal action to keep fuel flowing. The U.S. Department of Energy authorized an emergency exchange of up to 400,000 barrels of crude oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve to the Phillips 66 Lake Charles Refinery. The oil will come from the West Hackberry site for immediate delivery to support production for Louisiana and surrounding markets. The refinery confirmed it received the crude, but would not elaborate on why it was needed. Under the exchange, Phillips 66 will return all borrowed oil plus additional premium barrels, helping replenish the reserve at no extra cost to taxpayers. “With this exchange, the Energy Department is taking definitive action to support refinery operations, maintain stable fuel supplies, and ensure all Americans continue to have access to the affordable, reliable, and secure energy they rely on every day,” said Under Secretary of Energy Kyle Haustveit.
