items.t: Ernie Johnson announces this will be his final season on ‘Inside The NBA’
items.x: (Gray News) - Ernie Johnson announced he will be stepping down as host of “Inside the NBA” at the end of the season. The Sports Broadcasting Hall of Famer took to social media on Wednesday to explain his decision to step away, saying, “It’s just time.” Johnson, 70, stated that he would not be retiring, but cutting back. “This is by no means the end. It’s just a turning of the page,” Johnson said. “And I’ll forever cherish every chapter we have written with ‘Inside the NBA.’” Johnson said he plans to continue to work, including covering the NCAA men’s basketball tournament for CBS and Turner Sports. The six-time Sports Emmy Award winner acknowledged that he has dealt with heart issues in recent years, but that isn’t the reason he’s stepping away from the show. “I just want to slow down a bit,” he added in his social media post. Johnson joined Turner Sports in 1989 and has hosted “Inside the NBA” since 1990. He thanked his TNT Sports and ESPN crews for their support over the years, as well as the viewers. “I just want to say thanks to you. Thanks for your loyalty, for your love, for your support. And on this day, for your understanding,” Johnson said.

items.t: 8-month-old dies after left alone in running bathtub, police say
items.x: STERLING, Va. (Gray News) - A Virginia woman was arrested after her 8-month-old died after being left unattended in a bathtub, according to authorities. Rosellena Pisani, 30, was arrested and charged with homicide, two counts of child abuse and three counts of child endangerment, a press release said. On Sept. 12, emergency medical personnel and sheriff’s deputies responded to the residence after receiving a call about an unresponsive infant. Investigators determined the baby had been left unsupervised in a bathtub with the water running. items.t: Illegal moonshine distillery explodes, catches fire in mountains, officials say
items.x: WILKES COUNTY, N.C. ( WBTV /Gray News) - An explosion at an illegal moonshine distillery sparked a fire in the North Carolina mountains on Monday, according to authorities. Special agents from North Carolina’s Alcohol Law Enforcement Division were called to investigate the explosion in Wilkes County, North Carolina. Agents found an active 200-gallon illegal distillery. They seized about 1,800 gallons of mash, which is used to make moonshine, and 161 gallons of illegal moonshine. North Carolina officials shared photos showing the charred inside of a metal building. Distilling equipment was also damaged. Billy Ray Anderson, 69, was arrested and charged with manufacturing a non-taxpaid alcoholic beverage, possession for sale of a non-taxpaid alcoholic beverage, possession of a non-taxpaid alcoholic beverage, possession of distillery equipment, possession of distillery ingredients and allowing property to be used for the manufacture of a non-taxpaid alcoholic beverage. Moonshine is believed to have originated in North Carolina and was once an important source of income, particularly for rural residents.

So far there have not been any illnesses or “adverse reactions” reported in connection with the recall. The salads were sold in H-E-B stores across Texas. They can be identified by their UPC code, 041220300457, and their best-by date, Oct. 30, 2026. Customers are asked not to eat the recalled salads and to throw them away or return them to the store for a refund.

Resendez said the law provides dollars for state Area Agencies on Aging to deliver services for older adults, such as Meals on Wheels and caregiver support. “One of the only federal line items for caregiving comes through the Older Americans Act, and it’s called the National Family Caregiver Support Program,” Resendez said. items.t: Long-term care costs rose about 50% in five years, report finds
items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — The cost of long-term care jumped nearly 50% in five years, while income for older households rose just 22%, according to a new AARP report . The report found long-term services and supports are becoming even less affordable for middle-class Americans. Alan Weil, senior vice president for public policy at AARP, said the gap is the most important finding. “Between 2019 and 2024, a five-year period, the cost of most long-term care services went up about 50%, but the incomes for older households only went up by about 22%,” Weil said. “So the gap between what people can afford and what it costs has grown.” The AARP also looked at what different types of care cost. Weil said the more skilled the service, the higher the price. “If you need someone to come in and help you prepare food, that’s less expensive than if you need someone to come in and provide nursing-level care,” Weil said. “Although I’ll also say that we’ve learned that a lot of caregivers are being forced to provide nursing care that they can’t afford to pay someone else to do, even though they’ve never been trained in nursing. items.t: She was born with eight fingers on one hand. Her family traveled to America for the surgery
items.x: ST. LOUIS, Mo. ( InvestigateTV ) - A family traveled from Turkey to St. Louis for their daughter’s surgery to treat a rare condition affecting fewer than 100 people worldwide. Elisa, an 18-month-old, was born with eight fingers on her left hand. She was diagnosed with Ulnar Dimelia, also known as Mirror Hand Syndrome. “Mirror Hand is incredibly uncommon, and even surgeons like myself who take care of a great deal of kids almost never see this in their career. So, it’s really uncommon. Numbers are hard to come by, but one in a million or less is probably about right,” said Dr. Charles Goldfarb, Chief of Orthopedic Surgery at St. Louis Children’s Hospital. The condition leaves patients without a radius bone. This means significant limitations in wrist and elbow motion and preserved shoulder movements. “From the very beginning, he was really warm, genuine, and gave us a lot of hope. items.t: Parenting Takes a Village: Teen Dating Violence. Warning signs every parent should know
items.x: COLUMBIA, S.C. (WIS) - How early should parents start talking to their children about healthy relationships? According to one survivor advocate, those conversations may need to happen sooner than many parents realize. In this week’s episode of Parenting Takes a Village , WIS News 10’s Billie Jean Shaw sits down with Dr. Vanessa Guyton, founder of HUSH No More, to discuss teen dating violence, the warning signs parents should recognize, and how to create a safe space for children to speak up. Guyton says she has seen children begin dating as early as elementary school, making it important for parents to start conversations about healthy relationships at a young age. Dating violence isn’t always physical. It can include emotional abuse, manipulation, excessive jealousy, and controlling behavior, including monitoring a partner’s phone or social media. During the conversation, Guyton shares advice on how parents can recognize potentially abusive relationships, respond if their child reveals they’re being abused, and balance their teenager’s privacy with their safety. items.x: (Gray News) - A voluntary recall over lead concerns has been issued for cans of Walmart fruit cocktail distributed to stores in at least seven states. The Food and Drug Administration said the recall applies to 15-ounce containers of Great Value Fruit Cocktail in Fruit Juice from Concentrate. Where the product was distributed More than 1,830 cases, or approximately 44,000 individual cans, were distributed to Walmart locations in Alabama, Arizona, Louisiana, New Mexico, Pennsylvania, Washington and Wyoming, the FDA said. How to identify the product The product is marked with lot number “6FCB 04 C2263” and a best if used by date of Sept. 1, 2027. Recall details The FDA initiated the recall for “potential contamination with elevated levels of lead” on Oct. 1. It was reclassified as a Class II recall on Oct. 20. According to the FDA, Class II recalls are issued when a product can cause temporary health effects with a remote possibility of serious issues. What customers should do Customers should throw the item away or return it to Walmart.

items.t: Kershaw County council blocks hate crime ordinance in first reading
items.x: CAMDEN, S.C. (WIS) - A proposal to add hate crime penalties in Kershaw County was shut down for now. The Kershaw County Council blocked the ordinance in its very first reading on Tuesday. Supporters said they never got a real debate. “It’s a lack of acknowledgement, a lack of respect and a lack of response,” one resident said following a council meeting that saw a community-supported ordinance shot down in just its first reading. Often referred to as a hate crime ordinance, the proposed measure appeared on the agenda as a first reading in title only. The ordinance was formally introduced to council just by its title or number — and read aloud rather than a multi-page document read to describe it. The lack of explanation frustrated activist Eve Carlin. “Our hope was that this would advance to some kind of discussion from the Kershaw County Council whether for or against,” Carlin said. The hate crime ordinance is in effect in only two South Carolina counties: Richland and Orangeburg. items.t: 24-year-old deputy killed in crash with coal truck while on duty, sheriff’s office says
items.x: LOGAN COUNTY, W. Va ( WSAZ /Gray News) - A 24-year-old sheriff’s deputy was killed in a crash while responding to a call, authorities said. The Logan County Sheriff’s Department identified the deputy as 24-year-old Caden Mullins. Deputy Mullins’ fiancée was airlifted from the scene of the crash to a hospital. Deputies say Mullins and his fiancée were at a truck-or-treat event on Saturday in the Man area when he received an emergency call from the sheriff’s department. The sheriff’s department says Deputy Caden Mullins, 24, died in the crash. Mullins was on his way to drop his fiancée off and head to the call when the crash occurred around 5 p.m., deputies say. Deputies say the crash happened at the intersection of Rum Creek Road and Route 10 when a coal truck pulled off the road and hit Mullins’ vehicle. Mullins worked for the Charleston Police Department for about a year before joining the Logan County Sheriff’s Department to be closer to family, the department said.

items.t: Volunteers, Lowe’s associates give former fosters new hope
items.x: WEST COLUMBIA, S.C. (WIS) - Community volunteers joined Lowe’s Red Vest associates to renovate and restore Growing Hope’s Supportive Transitional Living Apartments. The program helps young people who have aged out of the foster care system have a place to call home. Growing Hope received a $100,000 Lowe’s Community Impact Grant to continue providing stable housing, skill building and support to children and families. Volunteers met at 2815 Leaphart Rd. and turned the apartments into a new, clean and bright home for residents to enjoy. Growing Hope President and CEO Kate Hurt said the apartment project is essential to bringing independence to a group of people with no support system. “Foster Care is really a traumatic experience, and so when you’ve aged out and you don’t have a permanent connection, or an aunt to go to, or a friend to go to, and you’re pretty alone, nobody deserves that,” Hurt said. Projects with Lowe’s are selected from more than 5,000 nominations through Lowe’s Community Bucket List . The projects extend nationwide to those in need. Surveillance video from the area showed a truck parked outside the condominium complex that afternoon. items.t: Aging Untold: How to spot the early signs of Parkinson’s and when to talk to a doctor
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — On this episode of Aging Untold, we examine the subtle, easily overlooked early warning signs of Parkinson’s disease and discuss when to talk with a physician. Plus, we explore what to consider when starting antidepressants, emphasizing the importance of setting realistic expectations and building a comprehensive support plan. Then, we share how a grieving Michigan family turned heartbreak into hope by helping pair veterans and first responders with lifesaving service dogs. Parkinson’s doesn’t always start with a tremor — here’s what to watch for Parkinson’s disease can start long before a tremor and the subtle changes are easy to miss. Dr. Rhea Rogers, a board-certified physician, said the loss of smell, constipation or changes in handwriting can be early signs. By the time tremors appear, Rogers said, significant damage has often already been done. Resources are available for people living with Parkinson’s. Read the full article here. items.t: ‘Amazed that she’s alive’: 18-year-old driver in ICU after hitting moose on icy road
items.x: ANCHORAGE, Alaska ( KTUU /Gray News) - A mother in Alaska said her 18-year-old daughter is lucky to be alive after hitting a moose Monday night while driving down an icy Anchorage road. “That’s what we’ve been hearing this entire ordeal, from the EMTs to the doctors; they are amazed that she’s alive,” Megan Stone said about her daughter’s crash. According to Stone, the collision occurred when her daughter Autumn was driving home and a moose appeared in the roadway. Stone said she does not believe her daughter had any time to brake. When firefighters arrived, they found a badly damaged vehicle with Autumn trapped inside. It took several crews to cut her out with the Jaws of Life hydraulic rescue tools. Anchorage firefighter Jason Dolph said moose are particularly dangerous when they are hit at highway speeds. “Typically when a car strikes a moose, that moose becomes suspended in the air,” Dolph said. “And when that moose then lands on the vehicle. In this case, it landed on the hood and kind of the windshield and roof area. items.t: Ukraine war continues despite Trump’s promise to end it
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - The war in Ukraine has lasted more than four-and-a-half years, and fighting continues despite repeated efforts by President Donald Trump to end the conflict. Trump made a pledge on the campaign trail dozens of times during the last presidential campaign. “Before I even arrive at the Oval Office shortly after I win the presidency, I will have the horrible war between Russia and Ukraine settled,” Trump said at a July 7, 2023, rally in Council Bluffs, Iowa. “Somebody said, are you on Russia’s side? Are you on Ukraine’s side? You know what? The side — I want people to stop dying. That’s the side I’m on.” That campaign promise has not been fulfilled. Trump has met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy twice at the White House. He met once with Russian President Vladimir Putin, in August 2025 in Anchorage, Alaska. “I will say that I believe we had a very productive meeting,” Trump said. “There were many, many points that we agreed on. Most of them, I would say. A couple of big ones that we haven’t quite got there, but we’ve made some headway. items.t: DOJ asks Washington state to set aside 400 voter ballots
items.x: SEATTLE (KPTV) — Federal authorities are asking Washington election officials to set aside ballots from more than 400 voters they suspect registered without U.S. citizenship. At a news conference Monday at the federal courthouse in Seattle, the U.S. Attorney’s Office alleged it identified 400 people who voted illegally in state and federal elections, accounting for roughly 1,500 cast ballots. The Trump administration sent a formal request to the Washington Secretary of State’s Office asking election workers to sequester ballots cast by those individuals until their citizenship status can be verified. “We are asking the state to set aside those ballots until we can confirm they are legal voters,” Acting U.S. Attorney Neil Floyd said during the briefing. Federal prosecutors also alleged they suspect thousands more noncitizens may be registered to vote across Washington and said they plan to send state leaders an additional list before Election Day. Washington Secretary of State Steve Hobbs confirmed his office is reviewing the federal demand. items.t: Man gets stuck in storm drain while running from officers in Eugene
items.x: EUGENE, Ore. (KPTV) - A man became stuck in a storm drain while running from officers on Tuesday morning, according to the Eugene Police Department. Just before 10 a.m. on Oct. 27, officers were called to help city employees at Mattie Reynolds Park to remove a tent that was put up near Amazon Creek. The man inside the tent gave officers a fake name and pretended not to know how to get out of the tent, according to police. The man, identified by police as 32-year-old Tylor Robert Welty, then ripped a hole in the tent with his hands and dove into the creek. Officers followed Welty as he swam downstream. Police said he climbed out of the creek at one point and got into a storm drain under the pedestrian bridge at West 12th Avenue and Wallis Street. Police said Welty became stuck about 100 yards in the drain and was physically pulled out of the pipe. Welty was taken to a hospital and later booked into the Lane County Jail for escape from custody, two counts of violation of park rules, false information to police officer, and second-degree criminal trespass. Police said he also had a warrant for a parole violation and a park and open space restriction.

items.t: ‘Breaking Away’ actress Barbara Barrie dies by medically assisted suicide, reports say
items.x: (Gray News) - Barbara Barrie, known for her 1979 role in “Breaking Away,” died Wednesday by medically assisted suicide, according to her daughter in a statement to The New York Times . Barrie was 95. Barrie had been diagnosed with terminal cancer and died in her New York City home, according to her daughter, Jane Harwick. Barrie’s agent, Gary Gersh, said her passing was “medically assisted in accordance with the New York State Medical Aid in Dying Law,” according to USA Today . In addition to “Breaking Away,” which earned her an Oscar nomination, Barrie also starred in several TV shows, including “Barney Miller” and “Suddenly Susan.” She also received a Tony nomination for her performance in the original production of “Company.”

items.t: Relocation offers on the rise as cities try big cash incentives to attract remote workers
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Remote work opportunities continue to thrive years after the COVID-19 pandemic made working from home mainstream. Now some communities across the U.S. are competing to attract new residents who are fully employed but can live anywhere, offering increasingly large cash incentives to lure remote workers. Cumberland, Maryland launched “Choose Cumberland,” a pilot program offering $20,000 to up to 10 people who agree to move to the city. The Appalachian Mountains community, located about 130 miles outside Washington D.C., saw its population decline from over 40,000 to less than 19,000 after several manufacturing companies and other large employers closed their doors starting in the 1970s. “At one time, the population of Cumberland was over 40,000 people,” said Mayor Ray Morriss. Program details and requirements The Cumberland incentive splits the money into two payments : $10,000 in relocation cash $10,000 for a down payment or approved home renovations Recipients must make Cumberland their primary residence for at least five years. “The people we are trying to entice are the people who are bringing their jobs with them,” Morriss said. items.t: Gen Z has more debt than Millennials did at the same age
items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — Gen Z carries more debt than Millennials did at the same age, even after adjusting for inflation, according to TransUnion data cited by a credit counseling expert. Ted Rossman, with nonprofit credit counseling agency Money Management International , said the agency has seen a 35% increase in demand from Gen Z clients in the past year. Their debt loads are about 12% higher than they were a year ago. Student loans, high rents and buy now, pay later plans are adding up and leaving many young adults living paycheck to paycheck with little savings. “That’s really showcasing a lot of these early career pressures,” Rossman said. “You have student loans, you have high housing costs. Those household formation years are very expensive, so GenZer’s actually have more debt than Millennials did at the same age, even adjusted for inflation according to TransUnion.” For Gen Z, Rossman said the starting point is the basics: knowing your budget and watching buy now, pay later spending. “It’s very popular among people in their 20’s, but it’s still debt,” Rossman said. “It can work in your favor. He stole a white 2008 Ford F-150 marked with Lindamood Planting Company. The truck was found abandoned early Tuesday in Marion, Illinois. items.t: Providence Cancer Institute program supports breast cancer patients beyond treatment
items.x: PORTLAND Ore. (KPTV) - An emerging program at Providence Cancer Institute is supporting breast cancer patients through all aspects of their journey, with the aim of helping them live as full a life as possible. The program is called the Providence “Survivorship Program.” It is designed to help patients beyond surgery and treatment. One service offered through the program is a sound bath. The sound bath is a meditative experience that guides breast cancer patients away from fear and worry and into a less stressful space. “It helps create a soothing environment for the body that it’s like, oh, that’s what it feels like to feel grounded or settled,” said Michelle Ferretti, an oncology social worker. Ferretti described what patients may hear during a session. “There might be bigger, bolder sounds, or soft, you know, twinkling sounds, and it’s kind of moving you through a landscape of sound that supports your body. You know, relaxing,” Ferretti said. Oncologist Dr. Poorni Manohar is developing the program, which builds on existing services at Providence. items.t: Antidepressants: What to know before you decide
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — Feeling low, disconnected or not like yourself for weeks or months is different from a bad day. When it starts to affect sleep, energy or everyday life, it’s time to talk about support and treatment options. For some people, that could include an antidepressant. Start with a conversation with your provider Dr. Rhea Rogers, a board-certified physician, said the decision looks different for everyone. “Everybody is individualized so you can just talk with your provider,” Rogers said. Rogers said to recognize whether you’re feeling depressed and to look at signs such as loss of sleep, loss of energy or loss of motivation. Some people might also experience a triggering event that starts a downward spiral, which they can’t pull themself out of, she said. “When your quality of life is being affected, then you might want to look into antidepressant therapy,” Rogers said. Antidepressants are not “happy pills” Rogers cautioned that antidepressants do not take away sadness. “They’re not happy pills. They don’t take away the sadness, but they will be a way for you to work on how you got there or what else is going on,” Rogers said. She listed chronic stress, a thyroid imbala

items.t: The barbershop quartet tradition is alive in New Orleans
items.x: NEW ORLEANS ( InvestigateTV ) - On a Mid City evening, a four-part harmony rang out just off Canal Street. The group, Southern Tradition, has been around since 1999. The quartet is a place where a traditional American art form forges a friendship. “The main attribute to be a barbershop quartet singer is to not be embarrassed, just keep going,” said Karl Hansen. Four men with four different careers create one sound. Hansen is a doctor who sings bass. Hansen Eschette is a med tech singing tenor. Joe Jacquat is a civil engineer who sings baritone. Johnnie Oufnac is the only actual barber in this barbershop quartet, singing lead. “Being together for a long time helps us harmonize and understand where the other person is going,” Hansen said. Barbershop quartets have been around for more than a century. Though they can be found all over the world, ties to New Orleans are strong. “It really is the nexus of American music at its most basic level and a lot of it comes from New Orleans,” said Zachary Matherne. items.t: Nearly 11 million people in the U.S. could be living with undiagnosed diabetes
items.x: CHARLOTTE, N.C. ( InvestigateTV ) - Diabetes is the seventh leading cause of death in the United States, the No. 1 cause of kidney disease, and an estimated 40 million people are living with it nationwide. Despite decades of prevention education and major breakthroughs in treatment, doctors say diabetes continues to hit the South especially hard — including North Carolina. It can create serious long-term complications, including coronary artery disease, heart attacks, never damage, and amputations. But many people who have the disease may not know it. The CDC estimates around 11 million live with undiagnosed diabetes. “Every day, almost every hour” battle Andrew Tucker has lived with Type 2 diabetes for nearly two decades. He’s made major lifestyle changes but said managing the disease is still a daily fight. Tucker was diagnosed about 15 years ago, when he was 35. “Yes, for me, it is truly an everyday, almost every hour watching what I do,” Tucker said. Type 2 diabetes develops when the body doesn’t make enough insulin or doesn’t use insulin properly. Doctors say obesity is a major risk factor. items.t: This veteran is using his service dog to regain independence
items.x: ST. LOUIS, Mo. ( InvestigateTV ) - Veteran James Poggi served in the Marine Corps working in aviation. His time in the military led to a lifelong strain on his body, including five back surgeries and a below-the-knee amputation. “You go from being six foot three, 250 pounds and able to travel halfway across the world and do whatever they ask you to do, to being relying on wheelchairs, walkers, mobility devices, things like that, you become a vulnerable person that you never thought you’d be,” Poggi said. Poggi said he was in multiple accidents, hard landings, PT accidents and a car crash. He also developed spinal meningitis. “And that was all while I was active,” he said. To help ease some of the emotional toll, Poggi’s wife, who is also his caregiver, suggested he get a service dog. Service dog provides daily support Poggi got Teddy, a Goldendoodle, who serves as his service dog and daily lifeline. “You never went anywhere without your battle buddy. And he always, always better have your back. And that’s how it is. He’s always got my back,” Poggi said. All four counts are second-degree felonies. He was transported to Webb County Jail, and his bond was set at $1 million. Officers stopped the car and found Landeros in the back floorboard with critical stab wounds. A U.S. Border Patrol agent is charged with fatally stabbing his wife in Texas. items.t: Economist explains how the ‘K-shaped economy’ is impacting the midterms
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - As voters prepare to head to the polls for the midterm elections, a conflicting economic sentiment is once again emerging on the campaign trail. “Voters reflect the perception of the cost of living as they experienced, as opposed to what is in the data,” said Alessandro Rebucci, an economics professor at Johns Hopkins Carey Business School. “In the data, you have an economy that is very strong as a whole. How that pie is distributed affects how a large segment of the population and the voters are feeling about the economy right now.” The contradiction has been described by many economists recently, as the “k-shaped” economy, using a graph to depict how high-income earners and asset owners are doing compared to middle and lower-income earners. “To be concrete, the wealthiest households are presumed to spend much more than the lowest ones, not only in absolute terms, which is obvious, but also as a share of their income and in their wealth,” Rebucci said. The issues range from theft to sexual harassment. The Portland city ombudsman and city auditor conducted the survey of guests at the city’s alternative shelters. What guests reported Portland’s alternative shelters are funded by the city and run by various nonprofits. About half of the shelters are operated by the nonprofit Urban Alchemy. items.t: High school student accused of trying to make bombs for ISIS, deputies say
items.x: GAINESVILLE, Fla. ( WCJB /Gray News) - A Florida high school student was arrested after an investigation into his contact with a terrorist organization revealed he was attempting to make bombs, authorities said. Alachua County sheriff’s deputies said the 15-year-old is a student at Buchholz High School. The sheriff’s office and FBI conducted a joint investigation on Friday at the teen’s home after investigators learned he was having online conversations with members and supporters of the Islamic State group, also known as ISIS. Investigators say the teen asked for help to build drones and explosives to attack people at an unknown location. Authorities spoke with the 15-year-old’s parents, who allowed them to search the boy’s phone. They reportedly found files containing instructions for making explosive devices and chemical compounds, as well as ISIS propaganda. On Monday, investigators searched the teen’s home with his parents’ consent after they revealed the information found on the phone. Inside, they found two jars in his bedroom. items.t: 3 teens arrested in Vancouver for drive-by shooting in stolen car
items.x: VANCOUVER, Wash. (KPTV) - Three teens were arrested after Vancouver Police say they were involved in a drive-by shooting in a stolen car early Wednesday morning. Police say officers responded to a reported shooting at around 5:45 a.m. near W Evergreen Boulevard and Jefferson Street. No one was hurt during the shooting. Investigators found a shell casing in the street and identified the person they believed to be the intended target. After getting a description of the suspect car, officers say they received a report of a stolen car from a woman who said her teenage son returned home with two of his friends after stealing her car. The stolen car matched the suspect car involved in the drive-by shooting, according to police. Officers were able to track down the teens, ages 13, 16 and 17, who had run away from the house, and booked them into the Robert L. Harris Juvenile Justice Center on the following charges: First-degree attempted murder Drive-by shooting Second-degree taking a motor vehicle without permission Obstructing a law enforcement officer

items.t: College professor among 2 found dead in home; suspect in custody, police say
items.x: LORAIN COUNTY, Ohio. ( WOIO /Gray News) - An Ohio college professor and a woman were found shot to death in a home, and a suspect is in custody, according to authorities. Wednesday morning, police responded to the Oberlin College Conservatory lot at 77 E. College St. to assist firefighters with a vehicle smoking and possibly on fire. When crews arrived, they tried to find the registered vehicle owner, identified as Daniel Jones, 31, to conduct a welfare check. When officers arrived at Jones’ home to check on his family, they found the victims dead inside the home. Pipo Nguyen-Duy, a professor of studio art and photography at Oberlin College, was found dead on the first floor with an apparent gunshot wound. A woman found dead on the second floor was not immediately identified. She also had an apparent gunshot wound. Jones was located aat bout 10:20 a.m. and taken into custody. Charges are pending. The investigation is ongoing.

A few people were also arrested on outstanding warrants, including felony warrants, and one person was also accused of driving under the influence. items.t: International fugitive sentenced for one of the largest health care fraud schemes in U.S. history
items.x: COLUMBIA, S.C. ( WIS /Gray News) - A man whom federal prosecutors called the architect of one of the largest health care fraud schemes in U.S. history was sentenced Monday. Herbert Kimble was sentenced to 20 years’ imprisonment with three years of court-ordered supervision. He was also ordered to pay more than $199 million in restitution to Medicare and forfeit more than $195 million in what prosecutors described as “ill-gotten gains.” Kimble pleaded guilty in 2019 to conspiring to commit health care fraud, violate the anti-kickback statute, and defraud the United States in connection with a telemedicine and durable medical equipment scheme involving back, shoulder, wrist, and knee braces. Prosecutors say Kimble ran offshore call centers that recruited elderly Medicare beneficiaries, paid kickbacks to telemedicine companies for signed prescriptions, then sold those orders to medical equipment companies that billed Medicare. Court filings put the intended loss at more than $400 million, with Kimble personally gaining more than $195 million. items.t: Portland council bans concealed guns in certain city buildings
items.x: PORTLAND Ore. (KPTV) - The Portland City Council on Wednesday approved banning concealed carry handguns in city buildings with 12 votes in favor. The ordinance removes a state-law exception that let people with concealed handgun licenses bring guns into certain public buildings. Oregon lawmakers gave local governments authority to restrict that exception in 2025. The ban applies to three city-owned and managed buildings where official government meetings are held. The city administrator will identify the locations, post signs at entrances and publish the list online. The city will also set up an enforcement process that includes notice and a chance to comply before sending a violation to law enforcement. Supporters said limiting guns in meeting spaces will help protect city workers, officials and members of the public. The measure does not apply to every city building. The vote followed a second reading, the final legislative step before passage.

items.t: For politics, what is an October surprise?
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - An October surprise is an event that could shake up an election, but does it often make the difference? Matt Dallek, a professor of political management at George Washington University, described it as “an event that, at least in theory, has the potential to shake up an election, something that people did not foresee coming that upends the debate.” He said the term dates back to around the 1980 election, when President Jimmy Carter failed to secure the release of American hostages being held in Iran before November 4, 1980, election day. Carter lost to Republican rival Ronald Reagan. Several surprises have occurred in the years since. Surprises can be driven by a campaign or by news events. Examples include Iran-Contra-related indictments in 1992 and the global financial collapse in 2008. Dallek said those surprises likely did not change the outcome of the election that November. “There’s no evidence that they flip a dynamic that was already in place,” Dallek said. “What’s more typical is that an event occurs, it dominates the news cycle and the trend line starts to move further toward the candidate who was already doing well, who was already likely to prevai

items.t: Library says person threw box of cockroaches at a staff member, prompting closure
items.x: TOLEDO, Ohio ( WTVG /Gray News) - A cockroach attack forced the closure of a library in Ohio this week. Surveillance footage was released by the Toledo Lucas County Public Library, appearing to show a person throwing a box of cockroaches at a staff member on Tuesday at the Kent Branch Library. Surveillance footage apparently shows someone throwing a box of cockroaches at a library employee in Ohio. (Source: Toledo Lucas County Public Library) A library spokesperson confirmed the throwing of the box of cockroaches at the library worker on Collingwood Blvd. But it wasn’t immediately shared what led up to the cockroach attack. The library was said to have gone into restricted access before closing for the rest of the day for cleanup and remediation. The Kent Branch Library reopened Wednesday. Officials did not say whether anyone would be facing any charges.

items.t: Grandmother not indicted in baby’s death after police say she left her in hot car for 8 hours while she worked
items.x: MADISONVILLE, Ky. ( WFIE /Gray News) — A Kentucky doctor who accidentally left her grandchild unattended in a hot car for about eight hours will not be indicted for the baby’s death. Madisonville police said 10-month-old Scottie Crowell died in August . On Tuesday, a grand jury found there was insufficient probable cause for an indictment. Police said Scottie’s grandmother picked her up in the morning of Aug. 13 and was supposed to take her to daycare. She forgot the child was in the car and went to work, police said. She arrived at Owensboro Health Multi-Care, where she works as a doctor, around 8 a.m. The baby’s father called his wife after trying to pick up Scottie from daycare, but the child was not there. The baby’s mother called the grandmother at work, and the grandmother ran outside and saw Scottie was still in the vehicle around 4 p.m., police said. After 911 was called, first responders tried to administer lifesaving measures, but the baby died. “I would ask that you keep the infant’s parents and family in your thoughts and prayers as they continue to grieve and process this unimaginable loss,” said Commonwealth’s Attorney Hannah Kington-Jarvis.

items.t: 23-year-old sentenced for shooting at car in Salem and cocaine possession

items.t: Widow searches for lost wedding ring when husband dies 3 days after getting married in Las Vegas
items.x: LAS VEGAS ( KVVU /Gray News) — A South Dakota woman is asking for help finding the wedding ring her husband lost in Las Vegas the night they married. Tammy Bishop and Will Mulroy were married Oct. 20 at the Viva Las Vegas Chapel. Bishop said they celebrated on a party bus and toured the Strip. At a bar, though, she says Mulroy looked down and realized his ring was gone. “We got to a bar. He looked down and his band was gone. He lost it. He started crying,” Bishop said. According to Bishop, he told her the ring was two sizes too big because he had lost weight. She said the ring may have slid off on the bus or while he moved into his wheelchair. It may also have come off while he rolled down the Strip. “We backtracked our steps. We told the bus driver. We had everyone looking. We couldn’t find it,” she said. The next day, she joked with him: “You didn’t even have your ring on for 24 hours and you lost it.” Everyone laughed, she said. “I said it’s not a big deal; we will buy you a new one, but now that he is gone it is a big deal to me,” Bishop said. items.t: ‘I miss her like crazy’: Loved ones remembering post office worker hit and killed by car

Marchelle Bertram worked at the front desk of the Fort Thomas Post Office for years, helping people who came in. Sadly, she lost her life in a collision in Bellevue on Oct. 15. Marchelle Bertram died at the hospital. items.t: Ernie Johnson announces this will be his final season on ‘Inside The NBA’
items.x: (Gray News) - Ernie Johnson announced he will be stepping down as host of “Inside the NBA” at the end of the season. The Sports Broadcasting Hall of Famer took to social media on Wednesday to explain his decision to step away, saying, “It’s just time.” Johnson, 70, stated that he would not be retiring, but cutting back. “This is by no means the end. It’s just a turning of the page,” Johnson said. “And I’ll forever cherish every chapter we have written with ‘Inside the NBA.’” Johnson said he plans to continue to work, including covering the NCAA men’s basketball tournament for CBS and Turner Sports. The six-time Sports Emmy Award winner acknowledged that he has dealt with heart issues in recent years, but that isn’t the reason he’s stepping away from the show. “I just want to slow down a bit,” he added in his social media post. Johnson joined Turner Sports in 1989 and has hosted “Inside the NBA” since 1990. He thanked his TNT Sports and ESPN crews for their support over the years, as well as the viewers. “I just want to say thanks to you. Thanks for your loyalty, for your love, for your support. And on this day, for your understanding,” Johnson said.

items.t: Police department closes its investigation into Hayden Panettiere’s death
items.x: GREENVILLE, S.C. ( WHNS /Gray News) - The Greenville Police Department said it has officially closed its investigation into the death of Hayden Panettiere. Police said Panettiere’s death has been ruled accidental based on the medical examiner’s determination and the findings of the investigation. Panettiere, 36, died from an accidental overdose involving multiple prescription medications and fentanyl, according to findings previously released by the Greenville County Coroner’s Office. Toxicology testing determined the cause of death to be the toxic effects of fentanyl, 4-ANPP, alprazolam, methocarbamol and quetiapine. An autopsy showed no signs of contributing trauma. On Aug. 16, Panettiere was found unresponsive inside an apartment in Greenville, where she had been temporarily staying. Dispatchers received a 911 call reporting a woman in cardiac arrest at approximately 1:51 p.m. She was pronounced dead at 2:32 p.m. Her on-and-off boyfriend Brian Hickerson and his brother Zach Hickerson were at the apartment where she died. Trump said while campaigning for president that tariffs would form the crux of the bilateral relationship. The U.S. and China, the world’s two largest economies, have been engaged in a trade war during both of Trump’s terms. Speaking Sept. 13 in Ireland, Trump said the U.S. is leading China in AI. “We’re leading China in AI, we’re the most sophisticated country in the world, and frankly, I want to keep it that way because whoever wins AI, wins,” Trump said. When they were difficulties, we worked it out,” Trump said. Trump hosted Xi at the White House in September for a state visit. He touted what he called “the tremendous strides” he and Xi had already made on national security, trade and technology. items.t: 8-month-old dies after left alone in running bathtub, police say
items.x: STERLING, Va. (Gray News) - A Virginia woman was arrested after her 8-month-old died after being left unattended in a bathtub, according to authorities. Rosellena Pisani, 30, was arrested and charged with homicide, two counts of child abuse and three counts of child endangerment, a press release said. On Sept. 12, emergency medical personnel and sheriff’s deputies responded to the residence after receiving a call about an unresponsive infant. Investigators determined the baby had been left unsupervised in a bathtub with the water running. Three children, ranging in age from 8 months to 8 years old, were at home during the incident, according to police. Loudoun County Sheriff Mike Chapman called the baby’s death heartbreaking, saying caregivers have a fundamental duty to protect children. He added investigators remain committed to seeking justice in the case.

items.t: Missing 7-year-old, pregnant mother both found safe
items.x: OVERLAND, Mo. ( KMOV /Gray News) — Officials in Missouri said a missing 7-year-old boy and his pregnant mother were found safe Wednesday. The Missouri State Highway Patrol previously issued an Endangered Person Advisory for Dylan Fernando Zendejas-Gonzalez, 7. Dylan was last seen leaving his home in Overland, near St. Louis, with his mother, Maria Guadalupe Gonzalez-Sanchez, 28. The two were last seen around 1:30 p.m. Sunday. Officials were concerned after personal belongings were left behind at their home. On Wednesday, the Overland Police Department said in a Facebook post that the two were found safe.

items.t: ‘She was screaming for her life’: Terrifying attempted kidnapping caught on video
items.x: HONOLULU ( KHNL /Gray News) — A terrifying kidnapping attempt in the middle of the afternoon on the Diamond Head Gold Coast in Honolulu was caught on video. Authorities said they were called to Kainalu condominiums on Coconut Avenue around noon on Monday about the reported kidnapping. Surveillance video from the area showed a truck parked outside the condominium complex that afternoon before a man was seen going inside the garage, appearing to confront two women and chasing one of them. A 77-year-old condo resident, who asked not to be identified, said the man picked up her 24-year-old friend. Police said the suspect elbowed the 77-year-old woman in the face. “He shoved me away from my friend and he picked her up,” she said. “He looked like a monster. He just had so much hatred and craziness in his eyes.” The woman added, “I was yelling, ‘Help! Help!’ and she was yelling, too. She was saying, ‘You don’t want to do this. Don’t do this.’” The 77-year-old said her friend was trying to fend off the kidnapper while she was hoping others would hear their screams for help. items.t: Man accused of threatening girl with a gun to get in his car later determined to have .292 BAC, deputies say
items.x: Salem, Ind. ( WDRB/WAVE /Gray News) — The sister of a man accused of threatening a girl with a gun to get in his car said that the whole thing was a “huge misunderstanding.” The incident happened on Friday in an Amish community in Salem, Indiana. Probable cause documents said 53-year-old Jeffrey Mauck went up to a girl outside her home and asked if her family sold any eggs. The girl told police that she said no and walked away. The Washington County Sheriff’s Department said Mauck then grabbed her and threatened her with a gun, telling her to get in his car. Officials said the girl’s family heard her screaming and came to the rescue. Court documents said that the girl’s father and his sons were able to restrain Mauck while waiting for the police to arrive. One of the responding officers said he found a pair of black handcuffs lying on the ground underneath Mauck and could smell what he believed to be the odor of alcohol coming from Mauck. Court documents said Mauck admitted to having been drinking. A chemical test determined that Mauck had a blood alcohol content of .292. items.t: Aging Untold: Fat-free doesn’t always mean healthy
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — On this episode of Aging Untold , we separate facts from fiction on “fat-free” foods to help you protect your heart and make healthier grocery choices. Then, National Alliance for Caregiving CEO Jason Resendez joins us to discuss the mounting pressures facing the sandwich generation and policy solutions offering caregiver relief. Plus, we meet the “Flower Buds,” an inspiring volunteer group in Kentucky that rescues discarded blooms to deliver hope and comfort across its community. Fat-free doesn’t always mean healthy: What to look for on food labels The “fat-free” option at the grocery store is not always the healthy option. Dr. Rhea Rogers, a board-certified physician, said the label can be misleading. “So if they’re removing the fat, they had to replace it with something else. So you have to look at the ingredients and look at the packaging,” she said. Rogers said she used to find all the fat categories confusing, so she created a simple way to sort them. items.t: Parents say students were forced to get off school bus and walk 3 miles home on dangerous roads
items.x: GUNTOWN, Miss. ( WTVA /Gray News) — Parents in Mississippi are demanding answers after they said their 11-year-old daughter’s school bus driver told her to get off the bus and walk miles home. James and Ann Lofton said their child and several other kids were forced to walk three miles to get home, though it’s unclear why. “You put your children out to catch the bus, you expect them to be safe on the bus,” Ann Lofton said. “You expect them to get to school safely, you expect them to get home safely, and then you get a phone call [saying] they’re walking down the side of the road. How is that keeping them safe?” The parents said they reported the incident to the Lee County School District. The Loftons said Superintendent Coke Magee suspended the driver for five days after the complaint. “We are aware of this, and it is being handled as a personnel issue,” the Lee County School District said in a statement. James Lofton said he wants everyone involved to lose their jobs. “That’s bull. It is bull crap. I think all their jobs, the superintendent, the one over the buses. items.t: PDX to resume daily nonstop flights to Mexico City
items.x: PORTLAND, Ore. (KPTV) — Daily nonstop service between Portland International Airport and Mexico City will resume Jan. 21, 2027, through a partnership between Aeromexico and Delta Air Lines. Aeromexico will operate the year-round route, which the Port of Portland identified as a priority for expanding international service and supporting tourism and business travel. The route brings PDX to 11 nonstop international destinations, including five in Mexico, offered seasonally or year-round. Mexico City, the country’s largest city and the largest city in North America, offers connections throughout Mexico and Latin America, port officials said. Mexico accounted for 18% of Oregon’s goods exports, totaling $6.2 billion in 2024, according to the Port. Officials said international visitors typically stay longer and visit multiple destinations, increasing spending on lodging, dining and transportation. items.t: Meet the volunteers who bring flowers from weddings and funerals to hospice patients
items.x: LOUISVILLE, Ky. ( Aging Untold ) — Inside Crescent Hill Baptist Church in Louisville, a group of volunteers gathers each week surrounded by color, creativity and collaboration. They call themselves the Flower Buds. From events to those in need The Flower Buds take donated flowers from weddings, funerals, wholesalers, supermarkets, florists, galas, banquets and other community events. They cut, clean and arrange the blooms into vases, then deliver them to nursing homes, the VA hospital, assisted living facilities and shelters. “Amazingly gifted with so many flowers from places like Kroger who have overbought and can’t sell them, and they allow us to pick them up and then bring them here, and then we cut them, clean them and vase them. Then we take them to nursing homes, the VA hospital, assisted living facilities,” Jodie Raible, a Flower Buds volunteer, said. The group sends out about 100 vases every week. “I take flowers to Up for Women and Children, it’s a day homeless shelter for women,” Stephanie Mullins, a Flower Buds volunteer, said. items.t: Illegal moonshine distillery explodes, catches fire in mountains, officials say
items.x: WILKES COUNTY, N.C. ( WBTV /Gray News) - An explosion at an illegal moonshine distillery sparked a fire in the North Carolina mountains on Monday, according to authorities. Special agents from North Carolina’s Alcohol Law Enforcement Division were called to investigate the explosion in Wilkes County, North Carolina. Agents found an active 200-gallon illegal distillery. They seized about 1,800 gallons of mash, which is used to make moonshine, and 161 gallons of illegal moonshine. North Carolina officials shared photos showing the charred inside of a metal building. Distilling equipment was also damaged. Billy Ray Anderson, 69, was arrested and charged with manufacturing a non-taxpaid alcoholic beverage, possession for sale of a non-taxpaid alcoholic beverage, possession of a non-taxpaid alcoholic beverage, possession of distillery equipment, possession of distillery ingredients and allowing property to be used for the manufacture of a non-taxpaid alcoholic beverage. Moonshine is believed to have originated in North Carolina and was once an important source of income, particularly for rural residents.

items.t: Some packaged salads recalled for undeclared allergens
items.x: (Gray News) - Packaged salads produced by Taylor Farms have been recalled due to an undeclared allergen. According to the Food and Drug Administration, Taylor Farms is recalling its H-E-B Backyard BBQ Chop Salad because it may contain undeclared soy and tree nuts, specifically almonds. “People who have sensitivity or allergy to soy and tree nuts (almonds) may be at risk of a serious adverse reaction if they consume this product,” an FDA press release said. So far there have not been any illnesses or “adverse reactions” reported in connection with the recall. The salads were sold in H-E-B stores across Texas. They can be identified by their UPC code, 041220300457, and their best-by date, Oct. 30, 2026. Customers are asked not to eat the recalled salads and to throw them away or return them to the store for a refund.

items.t: How to spot fake crystals and avoid costly mistakes
items.x: SEDONA, Ariz. ( Aging Untold ) — The crystal and gemstone industry is booming, fueled in part by social media, but experts warn buyers to be cautious of fake products flooding the market. Jamie Inglett, who owns a crystal shop in Sedona, said consumers can find fake crystals in stores and at gem shows. “As a consumer you really kind of have to do your own research,” Inglett said. Growing popularity drives demand The crystal craze has exploded online, with #crystals generating 20 billion views on TikTok. Inglett has built up 215,106 Instagram followers and opened a physical storefront in Sedona after finding success online. “You don’t have to believe in crystal healing or crystal energy to appreciate their beauty,” Inglett said. What to know about fake crystals Shannon Wimberly, a crystal collector for several years, said she has encountered fake crystals and now scrutinizes purchases more carefully. “I absolutely know I’ve run into getting fake ones, so I started scrutinizing other things more and more,” Wimberly said. items.t: Caregiver advocate shares 3 policies that could help family caregivers
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — More than 60 million Americans are family caregivers, balancing work, kids and care for an aging parent or loved one. Jason Resendez, president and CEO of the National Alliance for Caregiving, recently testified before the U.S. Senate Special Committee on Aging. He joined gerontologist “Sam” Cradduck to talk through the solutions he presented. The three policies he brought to lawmakers Resendez said the National Alliance for Caregiving is championing changes “to address so many of the pain points that family caregivers face every day.” 1) Older Americans Act funding He said one priority is reauthorization and funding of the Older Americans Act. Resendez said the law provides dollars for state Area Agencies on Aging to deliver services for older adults, such as Meals on Wheels and caregiver support. “One of the only federal line items for caregiving comes through the Older Americans Act, and it’s called the National Family Caregiver Support Program,” Resendez said. He said the program funds respite, which gives caregivers the chance to take breaks. It also funds training, education and outreach, so family caregivers have peer support and someone to turn to when na

items.t: Long-term care costs rose about 50% in five years, report finds
items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — The cost of long-term care jumped nearly 50% in five years, while income for older households rose just 22%, according to a new AARP report . The report found long-term services and supports are becoming even less affordable for middle-class Americans. Alan Weil, senior vice president for public policy at AARP, said the gap is the most important finding. “Between 2019 and 2024, a five-year period, the cost of most long-term care services went up about 50%, but the incomes for older households only went up by about 22%,” Weil said. “So the gap between what people can afford and what it costs has grown.” The AARP also looked at what different types of care cost. Weil said the more skilled the service, the higher the price. “If you need someone to come in and help you prepare food, that’s less expensive than if you need someone to come in and provide nursing-level care,” Weil said. “Although I’ll also say that we’ve learned that a lot of caregivers are being forced to provide nursing care that they can’t afford to pay someone else to do, even though they’ve never been trained in nursing. So that’s where the burden falls back on the family.” The financial burden oft

items.t: Police arrest man accused of selling meth to homeless people in Salem
items.x: SALEM, Ore. (KPTV) - A 46-year-old man is facing several charges following an investigation into methamphetamine sales in downtown Salem, according to police. Police say Engels A. Marcelino sold meth to homeless people in Wallace Marine Park and the downtown area. Detectives learned he intended to sell meth at Riverfront Park as well. On Monday, Oct. 26, officers tried to stop Marcelino at the park, but he ran from them. He was taken into custody after a short foot pursuit. According to police, detectives found a loaded handgun, 59.7 grams of methamphetamine, and $233 in cash in Marcelino’s bag. Marcelino was booked into the Marion County Jail for unlawful delivery of methamphetamine, unlawful possession of methamphetamine, and felon in possession of a firearm. The investigation is ongoing, and no other details have been released at this time.

items.t: Butter sold in 10 states recalled over possible yeast, mold and E. coli contamination
items.x: (Gray News) - Butter is being recalled because it might be contaminated with yeast, mold and E. coli, according to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. More than 1,300 cases of Miyoko’s Creamery European Style Salted Plant Milk Butter have been recalled in Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Iowa, Illinois, Indiana, Maryland, New Jersey, New Hampshire and Wisconsin. The recalled butter has lot code 07871 and a best-by date of Nov. 5, 2026. If you have the butter, you should not eat it, but the recall notice did not give further information about refunds.

items.t: She was born with eight fingers on one hand. Her family traveled to America for the surgery
items.x: ST. LOUIS, Mo. ( InvestigateTV ) - A family traveled from Turkey to St. Louis for their daughter’s surgery to treat a rare condition affecting fewer than 100 people worldwide. Elisa, an 18-month-old, was born with eight fingers on her left hand. She was diagnosed with Ulnar Dimelia, also known as Mirror Hand Syndrome. “Mirror Hand is incredibly uncommon, and even surgeons like myself who take care of a great deal of kids almost never see this in their career. So, it’s really uncommon. Numbers are hard to come by, but one in a million or less is probably about right,” said Dr. Charles Goldfarb, Chief of Orthopedic Surgery at St. Louis Children’s Hospital. The condition leaves patients without a radius bone. This means significant limitations in wrist and elbow motion and preserved shoulder movements. “From the very beginning, he was really warm, genuine, and gave us a lot of hope. Honestly, the trust and support he gave us played a huge role in our decision to come to St. Louis,” said Emircan Buga, Elisa’s father. items.t: Officials working to expand foster care for children in America, here’s how
items.x: NASHVILLE, Tenn. ( InvestigateTV ) - Kids sleeping in shelters, bussed between hotels, and overnights in office buildings. That’s the reality for many foster children in America. For every 100 children in foster care, federal data shows that only 57 licenses homes are available. In an effort to close that gap, the federal government launched a campaign in November 2025 called “A Home for Every Child.” “When we launched this, we offered states the choice: if they joined the Home for Every Child campaign, they would get administrative relief,” said Alex Adams, assistant secretary for the administration for children and families. “We would get them out of mountains of paperwork so that they could spend more time focused on things that actually improve child welfare outcomes. They would have more time working with kids, more time working with families. Since then, the idea to reinvent systems that recruit and retain foster families has gained nationwide momentum. Millions of dollars in cash rewards are available to the state, territory, or tribal agency with the greatest improvement of its ratio of children to foster homes. items.t: Son indicted in mother’s death; medical staff say she had feces, insects in hair
items.x: TUSCALOOSA COUNTY, Ala. ( WBRC /Gray News) - A man has been indicted on charges related to the death of his mother in Alabama. Jonathan Chad Simmons faces one count of manslaughter and one count of second-degree elder abuse in the death of his mother, according to Tuscaloosa County court documents obtained by WBRC. The court documents referred to the victim as Jonathan Chad Simmons’ mother, Brenda Hallman Simmons. Deputies found woman unresponsive Tuscaloosa County deputies and medical personnel were called to the 13000 block of Alabama Highway 216 on May 16. Law enforcement found Brenda Hallman Simmons, 76, alive but unresponsive. Brenda Simmons died several days later while receiving medical care. The autopsy revealed she died from sepsis due to complications from multiple open bedsores. Joint investigation begins The Tuscaloosa Violent Crimes Unit and the state medical examiner’s office began a joint investigation after the family and health personnel suspected neglect. According to medical staff at the hospital, Simmons had multiple open wounds and sores on her body and showed signs of not being bathed. She had feces and insects in her hair. items.t: Portland seller dragged by car in Facebook Marketplace meetup robbery, records say
items.x: PORTLAND Ore. (KPTV) - A 20-year-old woman is accused of robbery and assault in connection with two Facebook Marketplace meetups in Northeast Portland. According to court records, both incidents happened Oct. 15. Portland police say a man arranged to meet a buyer who went by “Alexis Gray” on Facebook at the Cricket Wireless at Gateway Shopping Center that afternoon to sell a brand-new orange iPhone 17 Pro Max for $1,000. Police later identified the buyer as Fallon Penney. Court records say she was accompanied by an unnamed man described as 6-foot-2. The seller told police the man snatched the iPhone from his hands. As the pair ran toward a car with no license plates, the seller said he and his father chased after them. Penney then pepper-sprayed his father in the face, the seller said. Both suspects fled. That evening around 9:15 p.m., police believe the pair struck again at Heavenly Donuts on Northeast 102nd Avenue. According to court documents, a young woman met who she thought was “Alexis Gray” to sell her iPhone, also for $1,000. Like the other victim, she said the phone was taken from her hand. items.t: Canned fruit sold at Walmart recalled in several states
items.x: (Gray News) - A voluntary recall over lead concerns has been issued for cans of Walmart fruit cocktail distributed to stores in at least seven states. The Food and Drug Administration said the recall applies to 15-ounce containers of Great Value Fruit Cocktail in Fruit Juice from Concentrate. Where the product was distributed More than 1,830 cases, or approximately 44,000 individual cans, were distributed to Walmart locations in Alabama, Arizona, Louisiana, New Mexico, Pennsylvania, Washington and Wyoming, the FDA said. How to identify the product The product is marked with lot number “6FCB 04 C2263” and a best if used by date of Sept. 1, 2027. Recall details The FDA initiated the recall for “potential contamination with elevated levels of lead” on Oct. 1. It was reclassified as a Class II recall on Oct. 20. According to the FDA, Class II recalls are issued when a product can cause temporary health effects with a remote possibility of serious issues. What customers should do Customers should throw the item away or return it to Walmart.

items.t: 24-year-old deputy killed in crash with coal truck while on duty, sheriff’s office says
items.x: LOGAN COUNTY, W. Va ( WSAZ /Gray News) - A 24-year-old sheriff’s deputy was killed in a crash while responding to a call, authorities said. The Logan County Sheriff’s Department identified the deputy as 24-year-old Caden Mullins. Deputy Mullins’ fiancée was airlifted from the scene of the crash to a hospital. Deputies say Mullins and his fiancée were at a truck-or-treat event on Saturday in the Man area when he received an emergency call from the sheriff’s department. The sheriff’s department says Deputy Caden Mullins, 24, died in the crash. Mullins was on his way to drop his fiancée off and head to the call when the crash occurred around 5 p.m., deputies say. Deputies say the crash happened at the intersection of Rum Creek Road and Route 10 when a coal truck pulled off the road and hit Mullins’ vehicle. Mullins worked for the Charleston Police Department for about a year before joining the Logan County Sheriff’s Department to be closer to family, the department said.

items.t: How the One Big Beautiful Bill Act is impacting the midterms

The law, that was signed by the president in July 2025, implemented several tax breaks for Americans and cut some social service programs. Derrick Van Ordern, R-Wis, at the GOP’s midterm convention in September. items.t: Arborist dies after falling while working in tree in North Plains, authorities say
items.x: NORTH PLAINS Ore. (KPTV) - An arborist fell to their death while working in a tree Tuesday evening, authorities say. According to Tualatin Valley Fire & Rescue, the incident occurred around 5 p.m. in the area of Northwest Dixie Mountain Road and Northwest Northrup Road in North Plains. The Washington County Sheriff’s Office confirmed that the deceased was an arborist, but no other details regarding the circumstances surrounding the fall or the victim’s identity have been made available. An investigation is underway.

items.t: District releases details on Silver Rail Elementary reopening plan
items.x: BEND, Ore. (KPTV) - In a letter sent to families on Tuesday, Bend-La Pine Schools says they are taking steps to repair and reopen Silver Rail Elementary after the deadly school shooting on Oct. 15. The district says data from a survey sent to families shows around 86.2% would like to return to Silver Rail. While Silver Rail is expected to remain closed through Nov. 6 for repairs, the district says the return date for students and staff depends on when repairs are completed to meet all applicable safety codes. The district also plans to community engagement sessions next week to discuss safety and security in Bend-La Pine. The full letter and survey results can be found here .

Tina Kotek has warned her Republican opponent would be aligned with President Donald Trump. Republican challenger Christine Drazan says the race is not about Trump, but about what she calls the governor’s failure to deliver progress on key issues. items.t: New permanent homeless shelter pod village opens in Aloha
items.x: ALOHA Ore. (KPTV) - Washington County officials celebrated the official opening of a permanent homeless shelter pod village on Tuesday. Next Step Community features 60 pallet-style homes that can accommodate up to 70 people. The county purchased the site at 3390 Southwest 209th Avenue in Aloha last December, in order to relocate a temporary pod village into a permanent shelter. Construction began in March, and new residents will be moved in by the end of the year, according to Washington County and Metro officials. The village will be staffed around-the-clock with resources for housing navigation and employment support by Open Door HousingWorks, which was chosen to operate the facility. The development of the $3.7 million project was funded through the voter-approved Metro Supportive Housing Services measure, officials say.

items.t: Couple charged after 4 children removed from ‘deplorable conditions’, police say
items.x: MIDDLETOWN, Ohio ( WXIX /Gray News) - A couple is facing multiple charges of child endangerment and animal cruelty following a welfare check at their home in September, authorities said. Melanie and Christopher Todd were arrested after officers responded to their home on Cardinal Court to check on their children and animals, according to the criminal complaint. Police described the living conditions as “deplorable and unlivable.” Officers conducted the welfare check Sept. 29 after Middletown City Schools reported that two 10-year-old children appeared dirty and said they had no food to eat, police said. The children also said two cats were dead inside their home, the complaint said. During the check, officers found holes large enough to see outside in the walls and floors. One of the couple’s four children said the holes were caused by punching when Melanie and Christopher would get angry, the complaint said. The home also had little to no edible food inside, officers said. According to the complaint, the floors were covered in dirty clothes, trash, animal feces, and debris. items.t: Secret Service visits hundreds of Portland businesses in card skimming crackdown
items.x: PORTLAND Ore. (KPTV) - The U.S. Secret Service isn’t being so secret this week. Special agents visited 238 businesses that accept SNAP as part of Joint Operation Pacific Northwest to warn clerks about what they say are billion-dollar fraud schemes targeting benefit recipients. During the operation, agents inspected 377 point-of-sale terminals, 156 ATMs and 375 gas pumps. While no card skimmers were found, officials say they still consider the operation a success because of the large number of business owners and managers they were able to educate through outreach. “Sadly, we are facing an epidemic across our country and in our partner countries to where transactional organized crime groups are coming in specifically to steal from benefit recipients,” said Michael Peck, assistant special agent in charge of the operation. “They know that these programs have cash and they want to target them.” The Secret Service says it’s easy to steal EBT card data because the debit-style cards do not have chips built in, meaning any card that goes in a terminal could be at risk. “We’ve seen victims lose their money months after months after months,” Peck said. “You hear how they went to the grocery

items.t: Oregon election officials urge voters to submit ballots soon with week until Election Day
items.x: PORTLAND Ore. (KPTV) - Election Day is still one week away, but local election officials are reminding voters of the upcoming deadlines. The most important deadline to remember is that your ballot must be submitted no later than 8 p.m. on Election Day. In Oregon, voters have a couple of options when it comes to turning in your ballot. Oregon residents have been voting by mail since the 1980s. “It is so convenient,” said Hillsboro resident Betty Yen. Yen dropped off her ballot in Washington County on Monday and said the process was simple. “When you think about how other people have to struggle, have to take off work to line up, the setup they have here in Oregon is fantastic,” she said. In addition to visiting their local elections office in person, Oregonians also have the option to turn in their ballot at an official drop box or send it through the mail. But if you want to send your ballot through the mail, Tuesday, Oct. 27, is the recommended deadline, according to both Secretary of State Tobias Read and local elections officials. “That’s just so we can be sure that it gets here in time,” said Tim Scott, Director of Multnomah County Elections. “You can still mail it later, but w

items.t: U.S. 26 rolling slowdowns planned Tuesday night
items.x: PORTLAND, Ore. (KPTV) - There will be rolling slowdowns on U.S. 26 between OR 217 and Sylvan starting at 7 p.m. Tuesday so utility crews can finish replacing utility lines that cross the highway and were damaged in a pole fire on Monday. Officials do not have an estimated time for when the work will be finished. People driving on U.S. 26 Tuesday night should be prepared for slow traffic. The work follows a long closure of Highway 26 overnight Monday into Tuesday morning. Tualatin Valley Fire & Rescue said firefighters responded to a power pole fire on SW Barnes Road just after 11 p.m. Monday. The fire was quickly brought under control, but the pole was threatening nearby MAX train service and all lanes of Highway 26 in both directions near the OR 217 exit. items.t: Woman arrested after 4-year-old found dead in Atlanta townhome
items.x: WASHINGTON, Ga. ( WRDW /Gray News) - A woman was arrested Tuesday morning after a 4-year-old boy was found dead more than an hour away in an Atlanta townhome, authorities said. Wilkes County Sheriff Darrell Powers said Jasmaine Smoak was arrested and booked into the Wilkes County Detention Center. According to WRDW’s sister station, Atlanta News First , Atlanta police responded to a gated community in the 3500 block of Cardinal Drive SW on Monday night for a welfare check. Officers forced their way into the home “based on information received during the welfare check,” Atlanta police said. Once inside, officers found the child dead. Emergency personnel attempted lifesaving measures but were unsuccessful, police said. Powers said deputies worked closely with Atlanta homicide detectives to locate Smoak using license plate reader technology. Smoak is charged with second-degree cruelty to children and concealing the death of another. Atlanta police said Smoak is a friend of the child’s mother. The circumstances surrounding the boy’s death remain unclear.

The victim dropped his iPhone 16 during the attack and was able to get in his car while the taunts continued. The phone was later found smashed at the park. items.t: Multnomah Co. authorities warn of scammers posing as law enforcement to target victims
items.x: PORTLAND Ore. (KPTV) - The Multnomah County Sheriff’s Office (MCSO) is warning the public of scammers posing as law enforcement after a man was defrauded of $40,000 in a recent case. According to the MCSO, last month, a 79-year-old man was reported missing by his daughter after she received a concerning call from him and lost contact. items.t: Voters to weigh Trump’s record on 2024 campaign promises
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - President Donald Trump won a second term by making many promises to voters. Nearly two years after he was sworn in, those voters can judge whether he kept them, and they will decide in days how he has done. When Trump campaigned for president in 2024, he told voters he would turn around the U.S. economy and close America’s borders. items.t: Man arrested after series of late-night burglaries targeting women home alone, sheriff says
items.x: GREENVILLE COUNTY, S.C. ( WHNS /Gray News) - South Carolina authorities are asking for additional victims to come forward after a series of late-night burglaries targeting women home alone. Greenville County Sheriff Hobart Lewis said investigators were made aware on Oct. 16 of multiple burglaries that shared “some very concerning similarities.” In each burglary, a suspect entered or attempted to enter homes occupied by women who were alone at the time, Lewis said. Investigators identified the suspect as 25-year-old Terron Lamon Banks. Through their investigation, detectives said they linked Banks to four burglaries in September, including one where he entered an apartment through an unlocked window while a woman was sleeping. Banks’ charges include four counts of first-degree burglary, one count of grand larceny and one count of voyeurism. According to the sheriff’s office, Banks was able to be taken into custody at a bus station in Spartanburg County as he was trying to board a bus to Atlanta. “We have a great relationship [with] adjoining counties,” Lewis said. “Certainly relieved to have him in custody before he got out of the county and possibly harmed somebody else.” Deputies

items.t: ‘Devastating’: Police department mourns death of officer in off-duty crash
items.x: AUTAUGA COUNTY, Ala. ( WSFA /Gray News) - A police officer in Alabama has died in an off-duty crash this week. According to the Prattville Police Department, Cpl. Dakota Lee Davis did not survive the injuries he sustained in a crash on Highway 31 on Monday afternoon. “The loss of CPL. Davis is devastating not only to the Prattville Police Department but to the city of Prattville. He will be missed by all,” Prattville Police Chief Mark Thompson said. Prattville Fire Chief Josh Bingham also remembers Davis as a hard worker and great officer. Bingham said those who want to honor Davis should do something nice for someone else. Law enforcement held a procession Tuesday morning as Davis’ body was transported from Montgomery to Millbrook. “We ask that you keep his wife, his family, and the PPD in your thoughts and prayers. We also ask for prayers for the first responders at the scene of the accident and the family of the vehicle involved,” Thompson continued. The crash remains under investigation by the Alabama Law Enforcement Agency. Further details regarding the collision were not immediately released.

items.t: Cheerios teams up with Ziploc to create resealable bags inside cereal boxes (finally)
items.x: (Gray News) — It’s been a long time coming: General Mills is introducing the first cereal box that includes a resealable bag. Say goodbye to folding, rolling or clipping the bag, or even transferring the cereal to an airtight container. Cheerios and Honey Nut Cheerios will be available with new packaging that includes a Ziploc PantrySeal™ bag. General Mills said this marks the first resealable bag inside a traditional cereal box, making it easier to pour and reseal while helping keep cereal fresh longer. “General Mills has received letters, emails and DMs asking for an easier way to reseal a cereal box, and we decided it was time to partner with the ultimate freshness brand: Ziploc®,” said Emilie Knox, Vice President and Business Unit Director for Cheerios at General Mills. “Cheerios with Ziploc PantrySeal™ takes a small, everyday cereal frustration and finally gives consumers the simple solution they’ve been asking for, making the whole routine easier and more enjoyable.” The new boxes will be available exclusively at Walmart.com beginning Oct. 27 and will be available at retailers nationwide in the coming months.

items.t: Woman dies after being hit by car in McDonald’s parking lot
items.x: WHITE OAK, Texas ( KLTV /Gray News) - A woman died after being hit by a vehicle in the parking lot of a fast-food restaurant, authorities said. White Oak police responded to the fatal crash around 4:35 p.m. Oct. 21 in the McDonald’s parking lot in the 600 block of East U.S. Highway 80. During the investigation, officers determined a woman walked out of the building, crouched in the driveway and began looking in her purse when a vehicle drove around the building and hit her, authorities said. Officers determined the woman was not visible to the driver due to rounding a blind corner and the woman being so low to the ground, according to a release. Paramedics took the woman to a hospital, where she later died, according to the release. Police determined the crash was an accident, and no criminal charges will be filed, according to the release. “Any incident involving the loss of life is a tragedy,” a department spokesperson wrote. “Our thoughts are with the family of the victim.”

We reviewed TikTok posts promoting real hotels, resorts and vacation rentals.
